Figure 3 shows the same seasonal swing at all 5 long-history Primaries, with D10 swinging furthest. The grey band is the fixed lockdown window. The figure does not isolate the shared month-to-month level that the correlations above describe, because the seasonal cycle dominates the figure.

Centre the residual quantiles of a replica fit before adding them to a forecast's mean. The raw quantiles carry the replica year's mean bias, so adding them shifts every quantile of the scored year by that bias. In experiment 104 the shift moved the median forecast by -21.3 to +3.6 points at the six long-history Primaries and reversed the sign of two contrasts (all years against 12 months, and drift against no drift) (experiment 104, Correction). Applies to experiments and to production. Confidence: high, because the centred and uncentred sets differ only in this shift.

For the convex demand model, tie a joint fit through a level-tracking filter to the two-stage coefficients (provisional). In a fit that minimises the error after a Kalman filter that tracks a level, the filter absorbs a constant shift of each slow term (the weekly profile, the tent, and the harmonics), so the loss leaves those terms to the penalty alone. The untied joint fit's weekly profile moved by a median of 19 points of capacity (up to 95) when the training cut-off moved back by 7 days, against 1 point for the two-stage fit, and its quantile score at 12 to 36 hours was 5.4 points of capacity worse (experiment 135). A ridge tie to the two-stage coefficients cut the weekly-profile movement to 1 point and left the score within 0.013 points of the two-stage fit. Applies to experiments. Evidence: five decision substations, the scored year, one model family. Confidence: medium, because the explanation was not tested by a variant of the loss.

Give a capacity increment only to a season-year with enough training rows (provisional). A fit whose cut is 2024-07-01 includes the half-hour that ends exactly at the cut, which belongs to season-year 2024, so that season-year has only 2 rows at D5. A free capacity increment for those 2 rows reached -56 points in an unconstrained fit. The N5 scripts drop any season-year with fewer than 1,000 training rows from the capacity columns, so the rows count towards the previous season-year's capacity (experiment 113). Applies to experiments that fit the convex model's capacity. Evidence: D5 at the 2024-07-01 cut. Confidence: high.

docs.title: Timestamps and availability
docs.text:
Treat ERA5 as available about 5 days after the event, so ERA5 at lag times is a ceiling and not an input that a live service can have. ERA5 is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) estimate of past weather. Name the weather source used at lag times in every write-up. Applies to experiments. Evidence: experiment 37 and experiment 38 both state the delay and call their numbers retrospective.

Treat an ECMWF ensemble run as usable 9 hours after its init_time, and derive power_fcst_init_time from the run. The constant NWP_PUBLICATION_DELAY_HOURS in packages/ml_core/src/ml_core/features/_nwp.py is 9. A 00Z run reaches our disk at about 10:30 UTC, which is 10.5 hours after its init_time, so the 9 hours is not the time the run arrives. The delay is the earliest usable time of a slot: any delay above 6 hours and up to 12 hours selects the same run at each of the four 6-hourly slots, and 9 hours gives each slot the run that a healthy ingest has landed by that slot. Bulk-mode training uses the same constant to derive power_fcst_init_time, so changing the constant changes the training features. A replay of a past init_time must apply the delay, because joining a run that landed afterwards is lookahead bias. Applies to experiments and production. Source: the constant's docstring in that file.

Join power and CAMS timestamps on (time - 1 µs).truncate("1h") + 1h (medium to high confidence). A power timestamp marks the end of its half-hour, and a CAMS timestamp marks the end of its hour. A naive join on equal timestamps drops or misassigns half the rows, and shifting the join by 30 minutes earlier weakens the correlation between hourly power and irradiance by 0.04 (experiment 103, figure 10). Applies to experiments and production.

Do not shift power timestamps: the time column of the cleaned power table marks the end of the half-hour (high confidence that no 30-minute error exists). Power timestamps show no 30-minute error on either side of NGED's fix of 2026-03-26 08:30 UTC, and the ingest's correction of the earlier late stamps goes the right way by the right amount. The test used clear days and the change in net power against a sun-height predictor at sunrise and sunset, with an offset search from -120 to +120 minutes and 95% intervals from resampling days, on the aggregate of the 6 metered solar farms. Before the fix, the corrected stamps read 0.9 minutes late (series from -0.2 to +2.9), so the raw feed was about 31 minutes late and the 30-minute ingest correction is right to within about 3 minutes. After the fix, from April to 2026-09-10, the median is +4.7 minutes (+1.5 to +13.3). The same months before the fix read +2.0 (-3.3 to +5.4), so the two sides do not differ. Primaries metered in MW are a weaker test, because demand ramps bias the fit: only D5 and D18 gave usable fits (+7 to +18 minutes). A correlation-peak test on summer middays is uninformative, because the correlation is flat near -0.18 with peaks at +/-60 to 90 minutes, so use sunrise and sunset ramps on clear days (experiment 103, figure 13). Applies to experiments and production. Scope: all power series, 2019 to 2026. The limits are that the metered solar farms lie within one 25 km area, the side after the fix has under 50 clear days, and the only known-answer check is the 30-minute sign test.

Assume a power reading reaches the forecast 3.5 hours after the half-hour it covers, and treat the number as an assumption. The recent-level filter of experiment 106 sees only the residuals whose half-hour ended at least 3.5 hours before the 09:00 UTC initialisation, the delay that experiments 87 and 104 use for lagged power (3 hours plus the half-hour a reading covers). No experiment has measured the delay of the live telemetry. Readings 0 hours old instead of 3.5 lowered the score by 0.035 points (95% interval -0.060 to -0.016). Readings 9 hours old raised it by 0.026 (0.000 to 0.046), and readings 24 hours old raised it by 0.099 (0.059 to 0.142), on five Primaries in the scored year. Experiment 115 repeated the sweep on ensemble weather at day D+1 (scored year, five Primaries, difference of mean scores without an interval): readings 0 hours old lowered the score by 0.016 points, readings 24 hours old raised it by 0.088, and readings 33 hours old raised it by 0.120. Applies to experiments and production. Provisional: the delay was not measured on live telemetry. Confidence: low for the delay, medium for the size of its effect.

When power readings are missing, let the Kalman filter coast and widen the quantile bands; do not fall back to the convex demand model with no correction (provisional, low to medium confidence). Coasting means running the Kalman filter, which estimates the recent error of the demand model's forecast, without feeding it new readings, so its short-lived error component decays and its slowly varying error component holds steady. After injected gaps of 3 to 72 hours, coasting scored 0.245 to 0.439 points of quantile score better (in percent of effective capacity, lower is better) than the demand model with no correction, over leads of 0.5 to 168 hours. Widening each quantile's offset from the mean by the filter's variance growth since the last reading reduced the share of readings below the predicted 5% quantile from 7.7% to 5.5% after a 24-hour gap (the target is 5%), without worsening the quantile score. The data could not show whether, after about 72 hours, it would be better to drop the filter but keep the winter night offset and recipe R. Applies to production. Evidence: experiment 205, at five Primary substations (up to 56 injected gaps each, made by hiding readings in clean data).

docs.title: Weather products
docs.text:
Train each model on the history of the weather product that will serve it, and do not train on the Centre for Environmental Data Analysis (CEDA) archive of the Met Office's UKV forecast and then serve the live UKV. UKV is the Met Office's UK Variable-resolution forecast, on a 2 km grid. The CEDA archive and the live product are statistically different, and the archive is licensed for non-commercial use (experiment 53). Applies to experiments and production.

Calibrate the ECMWF ensemble's temperature and irradiance before it drives a model trained on ERA5 and CAMS, and expect shifts of up to about 2 K in temperature and 20% in irradiance (medium confidence). Per substation, season, lead band, and hour band, the ensemble-mean temperature needed a shift of -1.15 to +2.05 K (mean +0.20) and the daylight irradiance a ratio of 0.80 to 1.11 (mean 0.95) at five Primary substations, fitted on the odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06. Shrinking the forecast solar anomaly towards CAMS's month-by-half-hour climatology did not help in any lead band (experiment 111). Applies to experiments, and to production if a model trained on past weather serves ensemble forecasts.

Drop an ensemble member that has a missing weather value from its run at that substation, and refuse a run whose control member is incomplete (medium confidence). Member 36 of the run of 2025-06-04 has 12 missing shortwave values at two Primaries, which would fail every half-hour of the run at those substations; the ensemble mixture then pools the remaining 50 members' forecasts (experiment 111). Applies to experiments and production.

Treat the ECMWF ensemble's shortwave radiation as a 6-hour mean after lead 144 hours. Applies to: experiments and production. "Lead" is the hours after the ensemble run's start time. The ensemble store's stamps are 3-hourly up to lead 144 hours and 6-hourly from lead 150 to 360 hours, and each downward shortwave value is a mean over the period that ends at the stamp. A pipeline that assumes 3-hour periods misplaces the daily peak after lead 144 hours (experiment 310). The evidence is a build for six solar farms in the trial area at leads of 12 to 252 hours. The confidence is moderate, and the entry is provisional until the experiment has had its reviews.

Drop observations that were not known at run time when building the manual_heuristic and climatology references. Applies to: experiments and production. manual_heuristic takes the quantiles of 13 earlier observed powers, 1 to 6 weeks and 49 to 55 weeks before the half-hour. When the lead exceeds 7 days, the observation 1 week before the half-hour is not yet known at run time. Drop that observation at those leads (experiment 310). The confidence is moderate, and the entry is provisional until the experiment has had its reviews.

Do not assume the unit PV shape rises with irradiance at low sun. Applies to: experiments. SunGeometry.pv_shape_and_ghi returned a unit PV shape that fell from 0.124 to 0.090 as half-hourly irradiance rose from 150 to 227 W/m2 at an elevation of about 14 degrees, in a fake ensemble that scaled the irradiance of one substation by 0.6 to 1.4. The response of the T-all fit to member irradiance was therefore not monotone on 1.8% of the daylight rows with a physical clear-sky index, all at elevations of 14 to 16 degrees (experiment 184). The scored contrast did not change when rows under 17 degrees were dropped. The confidence is moderate, and the entry is provisional until the experiment has had its reviews.

docs.title: Wind farms
docs.text:
Do not compute air density from the ECMWF ensemble's surface pressure for a model trained on ERA5 surface pressure (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments and production. The ensemble's surface pressure at the three metered wind farms is 0.7 to 7.0 hPa above ERA5's in the monthly mean (about +2.7 hPa on average, because the two products use different terrain heights), and a density column built from the ensemble pressure scored 0.049 points worse than temperature alone (95% interval 0.015 to 0.091). Evidence: experiment 256, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026.

Drop the rows in mask.parquet of experiment 210 before training or scoring on the three metered wind farms, and do not expect ERA5 wind speed alone to find idle rows (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. The idle floor is a set of near-zero readings with repeated values (W1 and W3 in MVA) or small negative readings (W2 in MW, down to -0.071 MW). At ERA5 100 m wind of 5 to 8 m/s, 11% to 50% of half-hours are in the idle band, and a wind-speed threshold that keeps false drops under 5% misses 51% to 69% of idle-band half-hours out of sample. The mask adds runs of at least 12 hours in the idle band at high ERA5 wind (suspected outages), which total 160 hours at W1, 428 at W2, and 2,742 at W3. W3's idle share at wind above 10 m/s is 6.2% over all years and 1.5% from 2021, so its first 2 years differ from the later ones. Evidence: experiment 210, three farms, 2019-09 to 2026-09. The mask is built on ERA5, which arrives about 5 days late, so it is for training and evaluation rows and not for live use. Removing the mask's rows from training lowered the quantile score of both the physics core and the XGBoost model when the weather was the 51 ensemble members (by 0.075 and 0.062 points on the kept rows, intervals excluding zero), and worsened it by under 0.015 points when the weather was ERA5 (experiment 276, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026).

Treat the low_wind_idle flag of experiment 210's mask as an ERA5 wind rule, not as a finding that the farm was idle (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. The flag marks every half-hour with ERA5 100 m wind below the fitted threshold that lies outside an outage run, and it does not look at power. Of the 9,787 flagged half-hours in the scored year, 914 (9.3%) had power above the farm's idle band. To score idle half-hours as zero output, set the target to 0 only where the reading is also in the idle band, and drop the outage_suspected half-hours. Dropping the mask's rows raises the default's score by 0.515 points because the dropped half-hours are easy; random drops that match the wind-speed bin give the same rise, and random drops that match only farm, month, and hour give 0.12. Evidence: experiment 432, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026.

Do not check a wind farm's capacity from half-hours at strong ERA5 wind alone (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. The half-hours with ERA5 100 m speed at least 2 m/s above the speed where the fitted power curve saturates hold 0.31% (W1), 1.12% (W2), and 0.18% (W3) of half-hours, so 28-day blocks rarely hold the 20 half-hours that a stable high quantile needs. The ratio of observed to expected power over every half-hour at 20% of scale or more found a loss of half the capacity within 60 days at 91% to 93% of start dates at all three farms, and a loss of a quarter at 26% to 77%. Evidence: experiment 341, three farms, 2019-09 to 2026-06. The real records show repaired episodes of 2 weeks to 3 months and no permanent step.

Do not zero the wind forecast, or the training target, where the wind speed is below the turbines' cut-in speed (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments and production. The cut- in speeds fitted by the physics core are 2.69 m/s (W1), 2.85 m/s (W2), and 3.38 m/s (W3). The ERA5 100 m speed falls below cut-in on 5.4% of scored half-hours, and 99.9% of those half-hours are already in experiment 210's mask. That ERA5 rule finds only 54% of the mask's rows. The ensemble- mean speed falls below cut-in on 0.77% of half-hours. Setting the forecast to zero on those half- hours raised the kept-row quantile score by 0.004 points (99.67% interval 0.000 to 0.012) and raised the score on the zeroed rows from 2.39 to 3.92, because the farms still produce small real output there. Setting the training target to zero changed the score by 0.001 points (-0.010 to 0.012). Evidence: experiment 336, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026.

Build the ensemble hindcast member rows with the production feature engineer, and expect a table of offsets per lead day, quantile, and farm to lower the wind forecast's quantile score (provisional, low confidence). Applies to: experiments. The production TabularFeatureEngineer reproduced the stored scored-year frames of experiment 230 exactly and built 442 daily runs (April 2024 to June 2025) for the three metered wind farms in a few minutes. On the scored year, a table of offsets fitted on those runs lowered the quantile score of the physics-core forecast by 0.60 points, and a neural head given the ensemble's wind summaries did no better. The observed power was below the physics-core forecast's median on 31% to 40% of rows in every scored quarter and 33% in the first hindcast quarter, so the offsets correct a stable low bias in the ensemble mixture's median, whose cause the experiment did not identify. Evidence: experiment 259, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026.

Do not fit a wind-forecast correction to the single year of ensemble hindcast runs without checking that the speed-to-power relation of the hindcast year matches the scored year (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments and production. At the three metered wind farms, observed power at the same ensemble-mean 100 m wind speed was higher in the scored year (July 2025 to June 2026) than in the hindcast runs (April 2024 to June 2025) in most speed bins, and the mean observed fraction of capacity rose from 0.20 to 0.25 at W1, from 0.25 to 0.28 at W2, and from 0.21 to 0.25 at W3, while the ensemble-mean speed rose by 0.3 m/s. A neural adapter fitted to the hindcast runs scored 0.21 to 1.04 points worse than the same adapter fitted to ERA5 and then given an offset table, and an offset table fitted to the hindcast runs still helped. Evidence: experiment 303, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026; the cause of the shift is not identified. In experiment 344, a correction keyed by the ensemble-mean wind speed and fitted to the hindcast gained 0.021 points on the kept rows (99.67% interval -0.126 to +0.077), and the same correction fitted to January to June 2025 gained 0.146 points (-0.257 to -0.038).

Judge a wind forecast's harm at low winds on rows grouped by the forecast-time ensemble-mean speed, not by ERA5 speed (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. The rows whose ERA5 100 m speed is below cut-in are chosen by the observed wind, so they collect the half-hours where the forecast was too high, and every upward correction worsens them: a constant shift by 0.51 points and a speed-dependent curve by 0.65 points (both fitted to January to June 2025), while the rows whose forecast speed is below cut-in improved by 0.17 points under the curve and worsened by 0.08 under the shift. Evidence: experiment 344, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026.

Correct the ECMWF ensemble's 10 m and 100 m wind speeds before a wind-power model fitted to ERA5 reads them, and expect the uncorrected input to lower the median forecast by about 10 points of capacity (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments and production. At the three metered wind farms the ensemble-mean 100 m wind was 1.0 m/s slower than ERA5's in July 2025 to June 2026 (0.7 m/s in the hindcast), growing from 0.4 m/s at days 0 to 2 to 1.3 m/s from day 7, and 1.5 m/s slower at ERA5 speeds of 8 to 12 m/s. The 10 m wind was 1.3 m/s slower at those speeds. A physics-based wind-power model fitted to ERA5 had 52.8% of rows below its median when fed ERA5 wind (after dropping the idle rows of experiment 210's mask), and 36.6% when fed the ensemble-mean wind. The swap lowered the median by 10.2 points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity), and the 10 m and 100 m speeds each explained about 7 points alone. Evidence: experiment 261, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026.

Do not drop half-hours when the final physical notification exceeds metered output by more than 5% of capacity, when cleaning public wind farms' Elexon output (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. A wind farm's physical notification is the operator's own forecast. It correlates with metered output at only 0.7 to 0.8, and exceeds metered output in 35% of half-hours at the median of the 40 kept farms. The rule therefore removed 20% to 83% of the kept farms' half-hours, and kept the half-hours where the farm outproduced its forecast. Dropping only the half-hours with a bid-offer acceptance removed 3.6% of half-hours at the median kept farm and at most 10.4%. Evidence: experiment 288, 65 candidate Elexon wind units, of which 40 were kept, 2019-09 to 2026-06.

Leave capacity, turbine rating, and hub height out of a correction head trained on a pool of farms (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. Each of the 40 kept public wind farms has a distinct combination of those three values. A head given 3 random numbers per farm fitted the training farms as well as one given the real values. With the real values, a head trained on four fifths of the farms scored 12.8% worse on the held-out fifth than the head trained on all 40 farms, and beat the XGBoost forecast (R0) on 11 of 40 held-out farms. Without them, the held-out head scored 4.4% worse and beat R0 on 24 of 40. Evidence: experiment 288, 39 Scottish and 1 English wind farms, July 2025 to June 2026. Covers the pooled correction head only.

Score a wind-farm head on the idle half-hours before using it (provisional). The idle half-hours are the ones experiment 210's idle-band mask removes, where wind is near zero and the metered series holds a reactive-power floor. Where it applies: experiments that train a head on wind-farm rows after dropping those half-hours. Evidence: in experiment 324, a mixture-density head trained without the idle half-hours scored 0.27 points better than XGBoost plus the offset table on the other half-hours and 2.1 points worse on the 10,642 idle half-hours, so on all rows the gain was 0.04 points (95% interval -0.12 to 0.05). We did not test training with the idle half-hours included. Covers the three metered wind farms, July 2025 to June 2026. Confidence: medium.

Do not train a wind farm with no history on public wind farms alone (provisional, low confidence). Applies to: experiments. A mixture-density network trained on 40 public onshore wind farms (hourly ERA5 weather from 2019-09 to 2024-03, no temperature) and applied to the three metered wind farms scored 17.7% worse at day 1 and 17.9% worse at day 2 than a network trained on the other two metered wind farms, with equal scores from day 4. Evidence: experiment 345, three farms, July 2025 to June 2026, ensemble weather. The cause is untested: the public farms' target, their missing temperature, and their different turbines are all candidates.

docs.title: Embedded solar capacity
docs.text:
Hold embedded-solar capacity as one value per Primary per season-year, and do not estimate it weekly. In experiment 45, no pair of penalties on the grid was both quiet on noise and responsive to a real fall. The frozen weekly fit had a path error of 0.040 against 0.027 for the season-year constant on the semi-synthetic baseline, and gave 0.66 false steps per Primary-year against a limit of 0.5. Refreshing the table once per season-year captured almost all of the gain from a current capacity in experiment 78, which lowered the quantile score by 0.018 points of capacity (98.75% interval -0.036 to -0.004, where a negative value means a lower error). Applies to experiments and production. Scope: 8 Primaries metered in MW.

Feed the forecast a capacity built only from data before the run, keyed by the run's date. A capacity fitted on all the data leaks the future. The latest week of a real-time capacity had 3.63 times the path error of the same week in the final fit (experiment 45), so do not read the newest week as a measurement. Applies to experiments and production.

Mask the weeks with no usable observation, and never read them as zero capacity. One Primary (Mount Bridge Boston) has 198 unobserved weeks of 354, and its season-year constant falls to about 0 MW from 2023-09-04 to 2025-08-25, all in unobserved weeks (experiment 45). Applies to any capacity table.

Exclude the MVA-only Primaries from capacity fits. The MVA reading folds the solar output into positive demand, and experiment 39 fitted a negative capacity at Stickney in every year. A fit that unfolds the sign recovered capacity with a median error of 0.09 against 0.29 for the fit that ignores the sign. The unfolding fit found the direction of flow with a balanced accuracy of 0.78, where 0.5 is a guess, and the 75% to 87% reverse flow at Stickney from 2021 cannot be checked without signed power (experiment 79). Applies to experiments. Confidence: medium.

Drive the solar shape with CAMS irradiance, and report capacity as the 99th percentile of the half-hourly output in AC power. CAMS irradiance recovered an injected 99th-percentile capacity in experiment 39, and experiment 45 defines capacity the same way. Applies to experiments and capacity tables.

Compare each Primary's pinned capacity with a curve of irradiance fitted on the same window before trusting it (provisional; medium-low confidence). In experiment 350, a learned curve with no capacity estimate scored 0.969 points better than the pinned capacity at D5 on sunny daylight half-hours (24 to 240 hours), and 0.025 worse over the other five Primaries together. At D5 the pinned capacity forecast demand too low by 5.9 points above 550 W/m2, against 2.8 for the curve, which points to a pin that is too high, though the experiment did not separate that from a wrong unit solar shape. Applies to experiments. Scope: 6 Primaries, one scored year.

Treat Wrangle T1 and Wrangle T2 as one area for any outside solar count, and use the Primary's polygon and not its point. The two share one polygon, and one Primary's point lies 95 m outside its own polygon (experiment 45). Applies to experiments and production.

Flag the Primaries whose capacity is confounded, and carry the error bound of each unflagged one. Kirton is flagged in 6 of 7 season-years. A day-long cloud-driven load is detected in only 0.35 of simulated trials, so the bound on the capacity at the seven unflagged Primaries is 0.18 to 0.71 and not 0.10 (experiment 40). In experiment 39, 6 of the 8 Primaries passed all four real-data checks, and the placebo-sky check failed at Wrangle T1. Applies to experiments.

Do not fit the panel orientation mix or the ratio of direct-current to alternating-current rating from a Primary's power, and use a fixed menu instead. The orientation mix is not identified on injected mixes (experiment 73). A fitted east-south-west shape lowered the held-out fit error by 1.3% in experiment 73, but gave no forecast gain in experiment 77, which keeps the all-south shape. Applies to experiments.

Shrink the forecast solar anomaly, and do not rely on the anomaly beyond about 2 days. The residual of the ensemble-based median has a slope of -0.42 to -0.69 on the oracle shift in every month and hour bin (experiment 51), and -0.771 overall in experiment 46, so a coefficient of 1 is too large. The ensemble forecast of the solar anomaly carries skill only to about 2 days ahead (experiment 46). Shifting the ensemble mean scored 0.129 points (0.057 to 0.212) better than shifting each member (experiment 51). Applies to experiments, in summer daylight hours.

Remove the logged switching, padded by 24 hours, from every capacity fit. A transfer moves the donor substation's solar output and looks like a capacity step (experiment 45 applies this mask). Applies to experiments. Confidence: medium, because the write-up states the rule and does not test the rule.

Do not treat the real-time frozen capacity vintage as the season-year constant. The vintage is experiment 45's weekly capacity estimate made with data up to each origin date. Over the weeks that it and the hindsight season-year constant share, the two differ in every week, by a ratio of 0.30 to 1.48 in the early weeks of 2020 and 2021 and by up to about 10% in the weeks near the end of the data (experiment 104). Each origin lists weekly capacities back to 2019-09, but the first origin is 2023-08, so a training cut before then has no real-time capacity. Take the latest origin on or before the cut, hold its last week afterwards, and hold the last observed value through unobserved weeks. Applies to experiments. Scope: six MW Primaries. Confidence: high for the difference, which was measured week by week; medium for the size near the cut, which comes from five Primaries.

Pin the capacity in a model to the real-time vintage. A capacity fitted together with the other terms moves with the optimiser's starting point (experiment 105's pooled model reached different capacities at nearly the same fit). Experiment 106 therefore takes the weekly capacity from the latest frozen vintage whose origin is on or before the cut, holds the median of the last 13 weeks up to the cut afterwards, and holds the last observed value through unobserved weeks. The latest week's capacity has 3.63 times the path error of the final fit's capacity for the same week (experiment 45), which is why the median of 13 weeks is held and not the last week. Applies to experiments. Scope: the six MW Primaries and D18. Confidence: medium. The fitted capacity scored 0.04 points better in the scored year and 0.16 worse in the replicate year, so the two choices are not separable on this evidence.

A cut before the first real-time origin uses hindsight, and the amount differs by substation. The first origin is 2023-08-07 at the five long-history Primaries. A cut up to 6 weeks before an origin uses that vintage as it is (5 weeks at the tuning cut of 2023-07-01). A cut more than 6 weeks before the first origin takes the median of the vintage's last 13 weeks and scales it back at 5% a year, the median of 12 season-year (1 July to 30 June) increments at five Primaries. That level is hindsight: D9 at 2024-07-01 looks 9.5 months ahead, D15 at 2025-07-01 370 days, D18 at every cut up to the whole scored year, and every Primary at the tuning year's replica (2022-07-01) 13 months. D14's vintage stops at 2023-04-17 at every origin, so its capacity is held from then.

Leave a substation out of a joint (pooled) fit at any cut where its pinned capacity is a late vintage (provisional). A hindsight capacity in one substation's target would move the fleet mean and so every other substation's forecast. In experiment 158, D9's capacity is a late vintage at every cut before 2025-04, so D9 was fitted alone at those cuts and joined the fleet from 2025-04. Applies to experiments and production. Confidence: medium; the rule follows studies.dp_gam_pooled's refusal, and no experiment measured the size of the effect.

With the capacity pinned, a drift term absorbs an injected solar farm in the hours the farm produces. The morning, midday, and evening bands move, and the night band does not (0.004 to 0.011 points in experiment 106's test). Applies to experiments.

Do not count a season-year as trained because a few half-hours of it precede the cut. A season-year runs from 1 July to 30 June. A training cut at 1 July 00:00 UTC leaves two night-time half-hours of the next season-year in the training data, because local time is an hour ahead in summer, so a model would count a whole extra season-year as trained and give it a capacity and a centring mean from those two rows. Count a season-year as trained only when it holds enough rows (experiment 104 uses 30 days of half-hours for centring, and any solar signal for capacity). Applies to experiments. Confidence: high, because a test of the training rows shows it.

Treat the ERA5 half-hourly file's :30 values as interpolated. Each :30 value is the mean of the hourly values either side of it, so it contains the reading from the hour after the half-hour it labels. Treat it as interpolated, not as a separate measurement (experiment 104). Applies to experiments. Confidence: high, because the mean absolute difference from the neighbours' average is zero.

Do not read the PV capacity of a pooled demand model as a measurement, and do not expect a prior to hold it near the vintages. In the pooled differentiable-physics model, the inferred capacity of a substation changed by up to 20 points of capacity with another start or with the network off (D5 50 or 30, D9 12 or 23, in season-year 2023), and a prior centred on the vintage with scale 5 changed nothing, because the prior is a few nats against about 340,000 rows of data. A swap of the fitted capacity paths among substations still worsened the summer-midday error at 6 of 6 (experiment 105). Applies to experiments that fit capacity inside a demand model. Confidence: medium. A capacity profile shows the free fit's loss is 4,563 nats above a fit with the capacities pinned at the convex model's, so the optimiser is the weak point; why it is slow is not tested.

Skip the solar-offset arms at D18, which has no capacity vintage before 2025-07-01. Its first usable data begin in February 2025, so an origin on or before the cut does not exist (experiment 105). Applies to experiments. Confidence: high.

Rebuild a new substation's effective capacity from its own rows before a model pools it in points, and fit its solar capacity from the same rows. A power series is divided by its effective capacity, the 99th percentile of its absolute power over its history, and a substation with 4 weeks of history has only that window to take the percentile from. In experiment 109 the whole-history capacity was 1.29 to 2.04 times the capacity rebuilt from June 4-week windows, 1.09 to 1.66 times the one rebuilt from April-to-June 3-month windows, and 0.91 to 0.98 times the one rebuilt from January 4-week windows, so a model that pools coefficients in points sees a June substation as larger than it is. A vintage capacity that is fitted after the cut holds the future, so a model that reads it for a short window leaks it. The same applies to a pooled substation that holds only part of its window (D18 in experiment 109): its scale is rebuilt from the rows it holds. Applies to experiments that pool a substation with a short history, and to onboarding in production. Evidence: experiment 109 (scored year, six held-out Primaries; provisional: one experiment, gate not passed under its pre-registered definition). The rule is motivated by leakage. Pooling D18 on its whole-history scale instead moves three contrasts by 0.03 to 0.05 points.

Do not pool a capacity read from a vintage fitted long after the cut. In a joint fit such a capacity moves the fleet mean, and so every other substation's forecast. Give the substation a capacity fitted from its own rows before the cut instead (D9 at the 2024-07-01 cut and D18 at the 2025-07-01 cut, experiment 109; provisional: not measured, and the experiment's gate did not pass under its pre-registered definition).

Do not rely on the farm series behind a disaggregated Primary's reading. For D8 (Marsh Lane), the metadata table names two farms whose output was added back, and the raw power table holds 1 reading for one farm and 4,643 for the other (441 above zero, none after 2026-01-26). The notes in the information field are a July 2026 snapshot, so the files carry no history of when an analogue failed (experiment 182).

Clip the solar term at D5 at 60% of the held capacity (medium confidence, provisional). D5 is the one substation with the export-clip flag in the series table, and its sunny-daylight forecast error against BG2 falls from +0.202 MW to +0.069 MW when the solar output the GAM subtracts from demand is capped at 60% of the capacity held after the cut. The same clip at D10 and D16, which show no plateau in clear-sky net power, leaves their sunny error unchanged and raises their error over all half-hours by 0.005 to 0.006 MW, so apply it only where the limit exists. A ceiling of 100% clips nothing. The evidence is one substation and one scored year, with the ceiling chosen on the tuning months (experiment 180; applies to experiments and production).

docs.title: Switching and the switching log
docs.text:
Mask switching with the 66 hand-filtered real transfers, and with nothing else. The transfers run from January 2022, and the raw log holds many events too small to matter (experiment 101, filtering the labelled set of experiment 41). Applies to experiments, and to production once a detector runs there.

Do not rely on a training mask for switching transfers to improve the convex GAM. Training the 24-month convex GAM with no mask worsened the score by 0.002 points on clean rows and 0.003 points after a logged transfer, and 476 simulated transfers worsened it by 0.009 points, because the hand mask is at most 7% of the training half-hours (experiment 212). Applies to experiments and production at D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16. Confidence: moderate, with a provisional status until the experiment's review is merged.

Expect D10 to carry unlabelled jumps of 15 to 20 points. D10's night-time floor rose from 25 to 45 points on 8 November 2024 and stayed high to about 1 December, and its residuals rose by 15 to 20 points from 17 November to 14 December 2025. Neither window is in the hand-filtered labels, and both are probably unlabelled switching. Dropping the 2025 window lowered D10's scores by 0.09 to 0.53 points and moved the five-site contrasts by under 0.08 points (experiment 104, Correction). Masking both windows in the quarterly refits of experiment 107 moved the quantile score contrast of all years with drift minus all years without drift from -0.451 to -0.512 points (a larger drift gain) and left every label unchanged. Applies to experiments scoring D10. Confidence: medium, because the cause is not confirmed.

Do not conclude that a logged closure moved no load because no detector flagged the closure. Of 381,830 logged half-hours on 16 series, 80.5% lie in closures over 60 days that no label covers, and only 2.6% lie inside labelled transfers of 25% or more of the receiving load (experiment 101). Applies to experiments and production.

Treat a logged closure of 2 to 6 hours as unconfirmed, and treat unexplained alarms as an upper bound on false alarms. An unexplained alarm is a detector alarm with no logged closure near it. Nine one-sided confirmations of 2 to 6 hour closures appeared against about 6 on shifted logs, while longer closures gave 28 against 0.4 (experiment 37). The log misses real steps, so an alarm with no logged cause is not necessarily false. Applies to experiments.

Add the substation pair 14-25 to the interconnection list before attributing closures to the pair. The detector of experiment 37 could not attribute those closures. Applies to experiments and production.

Treat the labelled set as reliable only for transfers of 25% or more of the receiving load that last over 1 day. Only that band reached labeller recall of 0.80 in experiment 41, so mark smaller, shorter, and unmetered-receiver cases as not scored. Applies to experiments.

Recompute moved_share_of_receiver from the events, and never read the stored column. The stored value is missing for 62 of the 81 visible events that touch a Primary series, because the labeller wrote some series identifiers as strings and 20 events name no metered receiver (experiment 44). Applies to experiments.

Report the 21 of 66 real transfers that have no metered receiver separately. Their receiving-load share is blank, and their megawatts are the labeller's estimate (experiment 101). Applies to experiments, and to production once a detector runs there.

Do not read the lower recall at injected transfers without a metered receiver as a property of the detector alone. The gap comes mostly from small injected steps: 211 of 274 such transfers step by less than the alarm threshold (experiment 58, experiment 55). Applies to experiments that inject transfers.

Restore the missing residual readings at series 12 and 13, or count the affected events as unobserved, before scoring on real transfers. Of the 35 real transfers over 1 day, 6 (11.5 MW) have no readings in the stored residual panel (experiment 101). Series 12 and 13 have residuals only from 2026-02 (experiment 37). Applies to experiments.

Do not mask with the labels of the refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC). RO-NC marks 9% to 16% of half-hours per year from 2022, and masking on the labels raised the error (experiment 89). The detector labels were also not shown to help on rows outside switching in experiment 86. Applies to experiments and production.

Do not set lagged power inside an ARA to missing. Masking those lags raised the error by 0.409 points of capacity (98.33% interval +0.281 to +0.517) on the rows with such a lag (experiment 89). Applies to experiments, for the Primary demand model.

Do not remove the detected intervals from the history of the error correction. The threshold-weighted error rose 57% on half-hours outside logged switching (experiment 38). Applies to production, with the caveat that the detector of that experiment is an early version.

Count overlapping detected intervals once when summing the megawatts, and end each interval when the transfer ends. Of the cases where the detector marked a transfer, 21% held two or more overlapping intervals, whose megawatts were added together, and the detector kept reporting megawatts for a median of 48 hours (90th percentile 96 hours) after a transfer ended, because it alarmed the return step as a new transfer of opposite sign (experiment 88). Applies to experiments and production.

Expect the end of a found transfer to be known 19 to 24 hours late, and expect the detector's score to separate poorly in the first 24 hours after an onset. The 24-hour blocks delay the end (experiment 43). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve is 0.60 in the first 24 hours (experiment 91). Applies to production.

Do not suppress detector alarms near the monthly refit of the residual model. Suppression lost about 5% of the moved megawatts, all in the 13% of headline-band transfers that start or end within 24 hours of a refit (experiment 71). The headline band is the injected transfers that move 25% to 40% of the receiving load for over 1 day. Applies to experiments and production.

Treat D8's multi-day drops as events, and do not read them as transfers to its metered neighbours or expect RO-NC to find them. D8 has 29 runs of 2 days or longer in which its power sits about 2.7 MW (range 1.2 to 5.4) below the convex demand model, 28 of them since July 2023. A metered neighbour steps up with them at a rate not clearly above random times (8 of 29 against 0.21), and 10 of the 52 RO-NC alarms on D8 fall within 6 hours of a drop's start or end (experiment 159). Applies to experiments and to production, for D8. The scope is one series and one residual model, the cause is unknown, the count depends on the threshold (15 to 48 for -2.5 to -1.0 MW), and the entry is provisional until NGED has said what moved.

Mask the rows of every known load transfer out of the training data of a forecast that uses no recent power. The evidence is provisional and the confidence medium, and masking itself was not tested. A generalised additive model (GAM) with a 24-month training window, refitted every month, learned injected transfers of 25% of a substation's power lasting 7, 30, and 90 days as 8.5%, 19%, and 32% of their size in the 48 hours after each transfer ended, and learned a permanent step to one half after about 12 months (experiment 274; 10 Primary substations, 4 onset dates, the ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather). No tested duration kept the bias under 0.1 points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of the substation's capacity). Applies to experiments and production.

Treat the Kalman filter's correction as undefined, not zero, before a series' first reading. The filter's correction of a series is exactly zero until its first reading, so the difference between the forecast with recent power and the forecast without it is zero there too. Series 13 has no reading for 67% of the grid and series 7 for 37%; their standard deviation of that difference was zero until those rows were set to missing (experiment 308; 15 Primary series). Applies to experiments and to production, for any score built on the filter's correction. Provisional until the experiment's reviews are merged.

Give every detector alarm a closing rule that works when no end is known, and mask the alarm to that close. Applies to: experiments and any pipeline that masks detected load shifts. An alarm with no close masks the series to its end, so a rule such as a 14-day cap has to close the alarm. With the cap closing the alarm, a label-free detect-and-mask pipeline scores 0.016 points of capacity better than no mask on ordinary rows, on the 95% pinball loss (experiment 327). Confidence: provisional, 15 Primaries, one record.

docs.title: Forecast tails and curtailment cost
docs.text:
Count the half-hours beyond a limit before ranking forecasts on curtailment cost. Two bulk supply points have only 19 half-hours beyond a limit of 0.9 times their earlier maximum export, which cannot rank forecasts (experiment 84). Applies to experiments.

Label every curtailment cost "calibration to history, not a saving". The experiment's headline cost, £571,823 at a scaled limit of 0.9 times the maximum, is a calibration to history and not a saving (experiment 84). Applies to experiments.

Read tail coverage month by month, and expect the coverage to swing. The q95 tail coverage of the stored best-guess quantiles at Primaries swung from 0.88 to 0.97 across months, and a recalibration fitted on earlier months did not move coverage by more than its own interval (experiment 97). Applies to experiments, for the 12 to 36 hour lead band.

Re-fit a residual detector's noise for D8 before and after 2025-03, and label D8's engine only up to 2025-02 (provisional). Applies to: experiments. D8's residual noise (the median absolute step-to-step error of the residual) is 0.17 to 0.27 MW in clean months and 0.35 to 0.75 MW from 2024-05, rising most after 8.91 MW of 11 kV solar was connected on 2025-03-24. A detector with its noise fitted on 2022 to 2023 flags 40% to 45% of D8's half-hours from 2025-03 onward, even in April to June 2026, when 2% of half-hours are below -2.5 MW (experiment 196). The flags are not solar noise alone: the same detector flags 29% to 36% of D8's night half-hours from 2025-03, and neither night-only evidence, an edge test, nor a price gate removes them (experiment 199). The scope is one Primary; the confidence is moderate, and the entry is provisional until the experiment has had its reviews.

Sort the stored quantiles of a farm forecast before reading its median (provisional). Applies to: experiments, and production if a stored quantile set is ever read column by column. In the stored solar-farm forecasts that experiment 255 read from experiments 224 and 243, 26,344 of 77,897 rows (34%) had quantile columns that were not in increasing order, in every forecast arm, so q50 is not always the middle value of the forecast's own quantiles. Scoring the curtailment cost with the quantiles sorted per row moved the avoidable cost of the forecast arms by up to 3.7% and left every contrast's sign and 95% interval verdict unchanged (experiment 268). studies.node_curtailment sorts each row by default and counts the rows that crossed. The scope is the six trial solar farms (labelled A to F) in experiments 224 and 243; the confidence is high for the count and moderate for the size of the effect.

Do not read a metered solar farm's coverage at the 0.01 quantile as calibration without checking for exact zeros (provisional, medium confidence). Applies to: experiments. Coverage at the 0.01 quantile is the share of half-hours with output at or below that quantile. Farm D's metered output is exactly zero in 11.7% of the half-hours scored in 2025-09 to 2026-08 (7% in September, 24% to 26% in October and November, 44% in December, 49% in January, 0% from April), so the 0.01 quantile of every arm tested sits at about zero and its coverage equals the zero share. The pinball loss on those rows is about zero for every arm, so they add nothing to any contrast but dilute the percentage differences; report 0.01 contrasts with and without farm D. The cause of the zeros (outage, curtailment, or an export limit) is not established. Evidence: experiment 284, farm D, 2025-09 to 2026-08.

Take climatology and the manual heuristic from experiment 87's stored references when a scorer needs eleven quantiles (provisional). Applies to: experiments. The stored climatology and manual-heuristic forecasts of experiment 48 hold nine quantiles (q05 to q95), so code that pads the missing q01 and q99 fills them with either the capacity or a copy of q05 and q95, and the padded tails are wrong. The versions in experiment 87's ref_climatology and ref_manual_heuristic hold all eleven. Both experiments store power as a fraction of capacity, not in percentage points of capacity (experiment 277). The scope is the six Primary substations (which step 33 kV down to 11 kV) and the two bulk supply points D13 and D17 (which step 132 kV down to 33 kV); the confidence is high, because we read the stored files.

Report a tail's coverage as the share strictly below the quantile, beside the share at or below it and the share of exact zeros, wherever the actual output can sit on a point mass. For the six metered solar farms, 3.0% of daylight half-hours read exactly zero. The share at or below the 0.01 quantile is 3.3% to 3.5% for Metered solar farms research default 1, and the share strictly below it is 1.2% to 1.4%, so the "at or below" figure overstates the lower-tail miss by the zeros (experiment 321). Applies to experiments, for the 12 to 252 hour lead range. Confidence: provisional, six farms, one scored year.

docs.title: Privacy and anonymisation
docs.text:
Never publish the name, the identifier, or the time series of an NGED metered generator, and label each generator (for example "Solar farm A"). Substations are not covered by this rule. Public data, such as the settled output of Balancing Mechanism Units in Elexon's published data, may be named. Applies to experiments, studies, and production reports.

Give a bulk supply point's relation its own coefficients before using it. Applies to: experiments. A bulk supply point (BSP) reading is import-positive, the generator series are export-positive, and the Primaries' apparent-power series are positive. At the one BSP that closes, the reading equals 1.01 to 1.16 times the MW Primaries plus 1.03 to 1.10 times the MVA Primaries minus 0.85 to 0.90 times the metered generation, plus unmetered solar and a level (the closure audit of experiment 124). The scope is two BSPs, of which one closed; the confidence is moderate, and the entry is provisional until the experiment has had its reviews.

Average several network seed sets before scoring a small contrast. Applies to: experiments. Experiment 201's median-correction network, retrained with 6 different seed sets, moves the pooled score at 0.5 to 168 hours between 2.5787 and 2.6038, so one seed set carries 0.01 to 0.02 points of noise (experiment 325). Confidence: provisional, one family, one scored year.

Score the pooled mixture density network only on valid times from 2025-07-01. Applies to: experiments. The stored ensemble demand frames and summaries that experiments 397 to 409 read begin with the scored period, so test months before 2025-07 have no inputs and a fit for them stops before writing a forecast (experiment 416; the months 2025-05 and 2025-06 failed). The 12 months from 2025-07 to 2026-06 are the full set. Confidence: provisional, one family.

Compute a gate or threshold that needs one weather value per valid time from the shortest-lead forecast row, not the first row (high confidence). Applies to: experiments and production. With recorded weather every forecast row of one valid time carries the same value, so "keep the first row per valid time" is harmless. With ensemble forecasts each row carries its own run's value, and the first row of the sorted frame is the longest-lead one (mean lead 333 hours at D5), whose irradiance is a blurred 6-hour mean. Experiment 417's Primary-level gate did this and shut at D8 and D12; on the shortest-lead row it opens at both, as with recorded weather (experiment 424). The entry is provisional until the experiment has had its reviews.

docs.title: Evaluation protocol for Primary demand, version 2
docs.text:
This page fixes how every experiment on Primary substation demand is scored, so that results from different experiments can be compared. An experiment records protocol: demand-v2 in its front matter. A change to any metric, fold, series list, slice, interval, tolerance, or adoption condition on this page makes a new version. The superseded text moves to evaluation-protocol-archive/, where demand-v1.md already holds version 1, and the table of versions below gains a row. An experiment whose plan was written before version 2 merged finishes under demand-v1. The protocols for solar and wind have their own version numbers, so a change here does not move theirs. The research default rule defines the research default and the log of its versions. This page defines how a change to it is scored and when the change is adopted.

Version Date Change demand-v1 2026-10-28 First version demand-v2 2026-10-29 Per-Primary floor against the benchmarks, stop rule for blind alleys, and the replicate rule for ENS-trained arms

docs.title: What is scored
docs.text:
The series are the 16 Primaries, in three groups that are always reported separately. The three groups answer different questions, so no headline pools them.

Group Primaries What the group tests Signed-MW D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16 The demand model, because the meter records the sign of the flow MVA-only D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22 The demand model plus the effect of hidden reverse flow, because the meter records apparent power with no sign Short-history D15, D18 Report-only: no adoption rests on this group. No experiment we found fitted the GAM stack at D15

D8 is a labelled exception. D8 has no tuning month and borrows the second-stage spread of six donor Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22). D8 is scored in two labelled arms: one with donor spread, and one with own-residual bands fitted on earlier folds. The own-residual arm is the D8 row in the per-Primary table, because the donor-spread arm is known to be the weaker one and would make D8 the worst Primary for a reason that is already understood. Donor spread is fitted before D8 is scored, so D8 is fitted last.

Every number for the MVA-only group carries the label "reactive power assumed zero". The rule that picks the fit fails at a power factor of 0.97, and the reactive power of the real MVA-only meters is unknown.

The forecasts compared are the forecast under test, the current research default, and three fixed references. The references are BG2 (the XGBoost-based production-style forecast), manual_heuristic, and climatology. The current research default and each reference are regenerated on the folds and Primaries of this protocol, under new stored-forecast names, because the existing stored forecasts cover six Primaries on another row set and are never overwritten. Each reference is never retuned. Earlier scores of the references, which stop at 168 hours and use other row sets, are not comparable with scores under this protocol.

The lead range is 0.5 to 240 hours, and every experiment scores all of it. NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days. Days 11 to 14 are reported only for the arms that have forecasts at those leads, and a table lists which arms are covered.

The first run under this protocol produces the forecasts for 168 to 240 hours that the references lack. The stored demand forecasts stop at 168 hours, so BG2 has never been scored past 168 hours, and BG2, the GAM stack, manual_heuristic, and climatology need new runs at those leads. The ML MANAGER schedules this run. Until it has finished, no experiment scores the 168 to 240 hour leads, and the days 8 to 10 and 11 to 14 slices are empty.

docs.title: The three fixed benchmarks
docs.text:
Each family keeps three benchmarks whose recipes never change: manual_heuristic, climatology, and one frozen XGBoost-based reference. The rows grow as months arrive, and the benchmarks are extended with the same recipe and never retuned. Every change page reports the research default's absolute score against the three benchmarks, with intervals, because a chain of small contrasts can hide a drift in absolute skill. Diagnostic pages need not report them.

For Primary demand the frozen reference is BG2. BG2 is the stored arm p_s6_bg2 of experiment 87. BG2 is a quantile blend of five forecasts, with an explicit solar offset at the 5 of 16 Primaries that have a clean solar capacity estimate. The five forecasts are a weekly-refitted XGBoost model, a monthly-refitted XGBoost model, an analogue model (the experiment 87 page does not state its type), an XGBoost model pooled by substation type, and the frozen stack of experiment 48. For the bulk and grid supply points, BG2 is the weekly-refitted XGBoost model alone (b_weekly).

Production does not run BG2. Production serves a much weaker XGBoost model, stored as xgboost_baseline. Experiment 87 scored it at 10.536 points on the Primary quantile score, against 5.260 for BG2. A page that names BG2 as a benchmark says that production does not run BG2.

The GAM stack trails BG2 on sunny April-to-June half-hours. Experiment 251 found the stack worse than BG2 in April, May, and June (+0.162, +0.220, and +0.054 points), and at D5 on sunny half-hours. Every Primary-demand change page reports this finding until a version of the research default closes the gap.

docs.title: Folds
docs.text:
Folds are contiguous months with a training window that ends before the first forecast origin of the scored month. Fold k trains on data up to the end of month M(k), then scores every daily forecast run whose origin date falls in month M(k)+1, at every lead up to 240 hours. The publication lag of the power data counts as part of the training cut. The row set is every daily ensemble run, at the 00:00 UTC origin, in the scored period. It includes the runs that fold_a_every5d_v1 holds, and it gets a new row_set_id when the first experiment under this protocol stores its forecasts. The publication lag of the power data is the lag in production, and studies.eval_protocol states its value.

The experimenter chooses the training regime and states it in the plan. An expanding window and a sliding window (for example, the last 24 months) are both allowed. The regime must be the same for the forecast under test and for its comparison arm, unless the regime is the change under test.

A fold needs at least 12 months of training history before it is scored. The GAM has seasonal terms, and a fold that has never seen a winter measures extrapolation, not the change under test. Each Primary's report says which months were excluded by this rule.

The scored period is 2025-07 to 2026-06, with a replicate period of 2024-07 to 2025-06 for the Primaries that have one. The ENS archive starts on 2024-04-01 at every Primary, so an arm trained on ENS forecasts has a replicate of 2025-04 to 2025-06 only, at 13 Primaries, and none at D8, D15, and D18. Only a Primary with at least 12 months of history before the replicate period has a replicate, and an adoption that needs a replicate cannot rest on the others. Rows inside hand-filtered events are excluded, as in the research default's row set, except that a detected step day at a Primary like D8 is never excluded.

Every Primary in a group is scored over the same months, so that a pooled group score averages the same rows. A Primary whose history is too short for a month is left out of that month for its whole group, or the pooled score is labelled with the months it covers. D15 and D18 are scored from the first month that studies.eval_protocol.fold_plan returns for each of them, with no replicate. The module governs the first scorable month at every Primary, and the scored months are a few. A 95% month bootstrap on four months under-covers, so their numbers are reported only and do not count in the tally of Primaries where the forecast under test wins. D9's history starts on 2023-10-01, so it has no replicate months before 2024-10.

The months that the 12-month rule excludes are reported as their own labelled slice. Cold-start months are where a longer fit history helps most, and a gain there is otherwise invisible.

Stage-2 and filter forecasts for the tuning period are stored for every fold, except at D8. The GAM stack's second stage and the Kalman filter need forecasts from before each scored month, and a missing store blocks a rescore. Every experiment stores its per-run forecasts and its stage columns.

No experiment scores a valid time on or after 2026-07-01. This is an honour-system rule. A replicate that scores later valid times is labelled "tuning-adjacent" and is not read as held-out evidence. The rule truncates the last June origins, whose leads run past 2026-07-01. A physical lock on the held-out data is a separate, later piece of work.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The three scored metrics are the mean absolute error of the median, the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), and the tail-weighted CRPS (twCRPS). CRPS is estimated as the quantile score over 11 levels, which is the headline metric of every family. The ensemble CRPS of studies.ensemble_scores is a different estimator and is not used here. Pass or fail is judged in points of effective capacity, where a point is 1% of a Primary's capacity, and every table shows megawatts beside it, as the substation cards do. The headline metric is CRPS.

Four tail measures and the curtailment cost are reported and have no pass or fail. The tail measures are pinball loss and coverage at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles, per group and per Primary. The curtailment cost is the avoidable-curtailment-cost measure of studies.eval_protocol. It is read only for the signed-MW group. The MVA-only meters record unsigned apparent power, which hides reverse flow, so the cost is not defined there and carries the label "reactive power assumed zero".

The implementing code is the package studies.eval_protocol. The package lives in src/studies/eval_protocol/, with the modules metrics.py and slices.py, and a separate pull request adds it. Slice masks and the twCRPS threshold are defined there. The definitions are those of the substation cards (sunny by clear-sky index, sunny by unit shape, cold nights at 3 °C or below, and bank holidays). The twCRPS threshold is fixed per Primary and named in studies.eval_protocol. The docstrings of the package are the definition, and a change to a mask or a threshold makes a new version of this protocol. The package defines the slices with the ERA5 2 m temperature at each series' location, and the ENS forecasts are scored over those slices. The slice of a half-hour is therefore the same for every forecast, because it depends on an estimate of the weather that happened and not on any forecast. ERA5 is an estimate of past weather, so a half-hour near a threshold can sit in the wrong slice, equally for every arm.

Experiment code must import the metric definitions from studies.eval_protocol. A hard-coded copy of a metric is a defect, because copies are how a changed definition stops applying to some experiments.

docs.title: Slices
docs.text:
Each metric is reported over the slices below, and every slice row shows its half-hour count. A slice with few half-hours is labelled "thin", as the substation cards do.

Kind Slices Lead time Day 1 (0 to 24 hours), day 2, days 3 to 4, days 5 to 7, days 8 to 10, days 11 to 14. Days 1 to 10 is the headline band Time of day Night, morning, midday, and evening, in local time, with the hour boundaries stated in studies.eval_protocol Condition All days; sunny by clear-sky index; sunny by unit shape; sunny April to June; the months excluded by the 12-month rule; winter (December to February); winter nights; cold nights (3 °C or below); Economy 7 step hours; Christmas (24 December to 1 January); bank holidays Load-shift events During each hand-labelled load-shift event; in the 7 days after each event ends Group Signed-MW, MVA-only, and short-history, each separately Series Every Primary on its own row, and every Primary in each lead band (at least the day 1 band beside days 1 to 10)

The two load-shift slices have no pass or fail. The row set of the main score excludes the rows inside hand-filtered events, so the scores during the events and in the 7 days after each event ends are reported separately. Seven logged transfers are too few for an interval, per experiment 277. The length of 7 days is a choice of demand-v2, which the maintainer may change in a later version. The event list is the hand-filtered list and never the output of a detector.

The tolerance for "sunny daylight half-hours" applies to the sunny-by-clear-sky-index slice. The first run passes the realised clear-sky index (global horizontal irradiance over the Haurwitz clear-sky irradiance). The other sunny slices are reported.

The verdict names the lead band it rests on. A verdict that rests on days 1 to 2 says so, because NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days.

docs.title: Reporting in every write-up
docs.text:
The twCRPS threshold and the curtailment limit need at least 12 months of readings before the scored period. A series with fewer readings gets a null value and a status, not a threshold from a short history.

An arm that is missing at a Primary is reported as "not fitted", never dropped. The tally of Primaries where the forecast under test wins states its denominator, which is the number of Primaries scored for both arms, and the number of Primaries not fitted.

For each pre-registered contrast, the write-up states the 99% interval of the adoption condition and the 95% interval of the reported contrast, with the direction, the lead band, and the pooling decided before scoring. The 99% interval undercovers on short periods (96.5% at 12 months), and the write-up says so beside it. The first run states, for each Primary, whether it has a replicate and which Primaries have hand-labelled events, since an empty event list gives an empty slice.

Each write-up reports the load-shift slices beside the main score. The write-up shows the score during the events and the score in the 7 days after each event ends, for the forecast under test and for the current research default, with the half-hour count of each slice. The write-up draws no pass or fail from them.

Each write-up carries a per-Primary table, the worst Primary, and a leave-one-out contrast. The table lists every Primary's paired difference and its 95% interval, sorted by gap. Beside the pooled score the write-up shows the worst Primary and the number of Primaries where the forecast under test wins. For each pooled group contrast, it also shows two leave-one-out contrasts: without the Primary with the largest absolute paired difference, and without the Primary with the worst score. The sign of a pooled contrast can change when one Primary is left out.

Intervals are 95% intervals from the paired bootstrap that resamples whole calendar months. Any statistic across Primaries states the number of Primaries, because a correlation across 14 or 16 sites is weak evidence.

The write-up names the research default's version and the protocol version. For example, "default plus x versus Primary demand research default 3, scored under demand-v2". The result.md take-home stays at one or two paragraphs with figures, and the full metric table sits in a collapsed section.

A change aimed at one series or slice names at least two placebo Primaries in its plan. A placebo fails when it moves in the same direction as the target, beyond its own 95% interval. A change with a failed placebo cannot be adopted as a general change.

docs.title: When a change is adopted
docs.text:
These conditions apply only when an experiment asks to adopt a change. Most experiments do not ask. A change is adopted only when all six conditions hold. A change aimed at named Primaries follows the targeted path below, and the other conditions still apply to it.

  1. Gain. The 99% month-block interval of the contrast (default plus x, minus default) on the CRPS of days 1 to 10 lies wholly on the better side of zero, and the point estimate is at least the minimum gain for the change's tier. The contrast is read for the signed-MW group and for the MVA-only group separately, and each group's verdict is stated on its own. With k pre-registered arms, the interval is read at the level 1 − 0.01/k. The short-history group takes no part.
  2. No harm to a group. The signed-MW group passes the gain condition. The MVA-only group stays within the tolerance of its headline, with D8 and without D8, and is not required to show a gain. Each protected slice stays within its tolerance in each group, judged by a one-sided 95% non-inferiority bound. A breach at a group makes the verdict rejected.
  3. No harm to a Primary, and a floor against the benchmarks. A Primary whose point estimate is more than 0.05 points worse than the previous default makes the verdict needs-human, with the Primary named. The floor applies to the 14 Primaries of the signed-MW and MVA-only groups. The candidate's CRPS over days 1 to 10 must be less than or equal to the CRPS of manual_heuristic at each of them, and no more than 1.10 times the CRPS of BG2 (both scores are non-negative, in points of effective capacity, on the same Primaries, folds, and leads, and a BG2 score of zero is a breach). D8 is judged with its own-residual arm, against the one D8 row of each benchmark. Both comparisons use the point estimate. A Primary at which the previous default already breaches the floor does not block a candidate, provided the candidate's ratio there is no higher than the previous default's. A breach gives the verdict needs-human, with the worst Primary named. The floor is not a tolerance. The interval is not tested at each Primary, because 16 one-sided tests would breach by chance more often than not. The ratio of 1.10 is a starting value read from one table of experiment 378, where default 3 passed at 13 of 14 Primaries, and the maintainer may revise it.
  4. Replication. An arm trained on ENS forecasts can be replicated only over 2025-04 to 2025-06, at 13 Primaries. That replicate is reported and labelled "weak replicate", and the weak replicate alone does not make the verdict needs-human. A release is judged on the one scored year plus the holdout (July to October 2026), which the release-model skill reads once, and the holdout confirms the sign only. The gain has the same sign in the replicate period at the Primaries that have one, and the replicate estimate is at least half of the smaller of the main estimate and the minimum gain. If that test fails, the verdict is needs-human. Where the minimum gain is zero, the condition reduces to the same sign. Leaving out one series at a time is a check for changes tuned on one series and does not stand in for a second period: a change with no second period stays a candidate. A change that fails replication is not retried on the same replicate period with a changed x, unless the change is pre-registered as a new experiment and the failed attempt is counted. A change that meets this condition satisfies audit trigger 7, and a candidate that fails it never becomes a base for later work.
  5. Controls. The experiment's own controls passed, the placebos did not fail, and no audit trigger in the ml-experiment skill is unresolved. The audit's findings are triaged in the pull request before the adoption.
  6. Serving. The change uses only inputs available at forecast time. If the change would need a serving-path change to port, the page says so.

A change aimed at named Primaries has a targeted path. The gain is judged on the named Primaries instead of the group, because a gain at one Primary is diluted by 8 or 16 in a pooled score. The placebos must stay non-inferior, and the change is adopted only as an automatic per-substation choice. The choice follows a rule fixed at training time from earlier out-of-sample scores alone, and the experiment scores the rule's output, never the better arm at each Primary in hindsight.

The tolerances and minimum gains are fixed here and tweaked only by a new version. A tolerance is the harm a protected group may suffer before an adoption fails.

Protected group Tolerance, in points Headline of each group (CRPS, days 1 to 10), including the MVA-only group with and without D8 0.02 The 0.01 and 0.99 pinball tails, the worse end scored 0.05 Cold winter nights 0.05 Sunny daylight half-hours 0.05 twCRPS 2% relative Each lead band 0.05 Each Primary, on the point estimate 0.05 Per-Primary coverage at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles Flagged when the 95% month-resampled interval of the coverage excludes the nominal level; a flag does not fail the change Tier of the change Minimum gain, in points A changed setting, an added column, or a changed loss 0 A new fitted step, a new input, or a new data source 0.02 A new head 0.03

The adoption outcome is adopted, rejected, or needs-human. adopted sets promoted_to in the front matter, and the outcomes rejected and needs-human appear in the first line of result.md beside the existing verdict, with production_status: candidate.

A neutral change passes a group's harm test with probability Φ(τ/SE − 1.645), where τ is the tolerance and SE is the standard error. A tolerance of 2 standard errors passes a neutral change 64% of the time, and a change that truly harms the group by exactly the tolerance passes 5% of the time. The per-Primary rule is a flag because 16 such tests would breach by chance far more often than not.

When the metrics disagree, the verdict is decided in this order. A breach of condition 2 makes the verdict rejected, unless the change targets a different slice and the maintainer overrules. A Primary breach or a floor breach of condition 3 makes the verdict needs-human, naming the worst Primary. A CRPS gain with the median error moving the other way beyond tolerance gives needs-human. needs-human is also the fallback for any case this list does not cover.

The first experiment under this protocol rescoring the references. Experiments 374 and 376 used one fixed fit and a tuning month, not monthly folds, so their scores are not comparable with scores under this protocol.

A screening arm is allowed. Monthly retraining of 16 Primaries over 12 scored months costs about 384 stack fits per change for two arms. An experiment's plan may screen with fewer folds or Primaries, and says so. Only a full run under this protocol supports an adoption.

The cumulative harm budget is 2 times the group's tolerance, measured against the family's first version. The no-harm condition compares each adoption only with the previous version, so n adoptions that each cost up to the tolerance could cost n times the tolerance in total. At each adoption, the current research default must also stay within the budget against the first version, using the first version's stored forecasts. The retest rules of the research default rule still apply.

A change that wins on the gain condition but fails another condition is recorded as a candidate, not adopted. Candidates are retested when the missing evidence arrives, or when a rebase run is available, as the research default rule describes.

A targeted adoption on a subgroup uses a short list of admissible subgroups, set in advance. The list is cold nights, the Economy 7 step, and sunny daylight. A targeted adoption on a subgroup also needs no harm on the family headline.

An experiment may hold several default-plus-x arms, and at most one of them is adopted. Each arm is read at the level 1 − 0.01/k, and the others become candidates that rebase on the new version. A bundle of two components is adopted as one change only when it was pre-registered as one change and its leave-one-out arms show neither component harmful.

Only a pre-registered arm can be adopted. A post hoc arm becomes a candidate that needs a fresh experiment. When an experiment tests k variants of one change (tilt 20 and tilt 27, for example), the best variant needs replication on its own after the Bonferroni read.

An experiment that evaluates a blend reports each constituent model family alone beside the blend. The single-family table comes first, and the page states the blend's added value over the best single family, with an interval. A blend is adopted into the research default only with that table present. The first production update is a relatively simple model implemented as one model family, for example XGBoost only, while blends stay of interest.

The default plus x is produced on the research default's full row set. Its stored forecasts then serve as the next version without a separate regeneration job.

The ablation that follows every fifth adoption drops a component only on evidence. A component is dropped only when the interval of its removal lies wholly on the better side, or when its removal is non-inferior within the tolerance and the component sits in a higher complexity tier.

The nominal 99% interval covers less than 99% on short periods. A percentile bootstrap that resampled independent normal months with a nominal 99% interval covered 96.5% of the time at 12 months, 92.0% at 6 months, and 83.7% at 4 months (1,500 trials of 2,000 resamples each). The real procedure also resamples seeds and has autocorrelated months, so the figures are indicative. For periods under 12 months, add a t test on the monthly paired differences or use a studentised bootstrap. Adoption contrasts use 99% whatever the number of arms, as a stated exception to the interval-level convention, and a change page says "the 99% interval lies wholly on the better side of zero" in place of the study skill's "statistically significant at the 5% level".

The recorded gain of each version is an upper bound. Winners are selected on the scored year, so the recorded estimate overstates the true gain. In a simulation, a true gain of 2 standard errors was recorded on average as 2.7. The log therefore also reports the cumulative gain on the replicate period, which carries no selection bias, beside the scored-year sum.

docs.title: The holdout
docs.text:
The frozen period is the existing holdout: valid times on or after 2026-07-01. No experiment scores those valid times, which are kept for a finalist. The release-model skill scores the holdout once per release, on the sign of the effect only, and a month may confirm one release only.

The holdout holds under four months and no winter on 2026-10-23. It covers July to October 2026, and the months from November to February arrive by about March 2027. Until then, a change that acts in winter (the heating curve, cold nights, the Economy 7 step) is adopted on the scored year alone, and its log entry reads "winter-unconfirmed". The holdout confirms its sign in March 2027 or later.
