Every fitted series, including each with no step, appears in the unpooled table. This replaces the earlier draft, in which the verdict rested on D5, D10, and D16.

The selected subset is expected to look larger than the pool, and the gap is the selection effect. Experiment 121 read winter 2025-26 and found a step at 01:00 of 4.3, 7.1, and 5.3 points in the residuals of the day-ahead model at D5, D10, and D16, and 1.9 to 3.4 points at D11, D14, and D9. The choice of those three series came from that winter, so winter 2025-26 is labelled the selection winter.

docs.title: Pre-fit clarification 2: the unit is points of effective capacity (written before any fit)
docs.text:
Every size in this plan is in points of effective capacity, and the first draft mislabelled the unit as megawatts. One point is 1% of the series' effective capacity, which is the series' own 99th percentile of cleaned demand and not an electrical rating. Experiment 121's step figures (4.3, 7.1, and 5.3 at D5, D10, and D16) are in points: its quantile scores are in points, and a 7.1 MW step at D10 would exceed the series' 5.4 MW effective capacity. The wrong label was found in test 1, which showed D10's night difference to be about 0.4 MW (about 8 points). Every number in the plan (the predictions, the injected shapes S of 4 and 7, the bias bound of 0.5, the trigger thresholds of 4, 8, and 15, and the 1.7 summer step) keeps its value and now reads in points. Each series' night difference d is converted to points before any fit, so the pooled steps average comparable quantities, and the page also prints each series' step in MW (one point at D10 is 0.054 MW). Test 1 printed raw night differences for one series in the design winters and a per-series mean d over all nights of winters 2021-22 to 2025-26; no estimate, interval, or fit was computed before this clarification.

Units clarification: what "effective capacity" is, and the raw step in MW. The table's effective capacity is a scale taken from the demand itself: it matches each series' 99th percentile of cleaned half-hourly demand (D10: 5.398 MW against a 99th percentile of 5.413 MW; D5: 5.723 against 5.734; D16: 9.115 against 9.143). It is neither the electrical rating of the substation nor a PV capacity. A point is therefore 1% of that near-peak demand. Computed from the stored cleaned power on cold GMT nights (daily mean at most 3 C) of winters 2023-24 and 2024-25 (printed in report.txt under raw_cold_step), the half-hour ending at 01:00 minus the mean of the 22:00 to 23:30 half-hours is 0.27 MW (4.8 points) at D5, 0.44 MW (8.2 points) at D10, and 0.87 MW (9.5 points) at D16. The raw step is therefore a few tenths of a megawatt, and the figures of 1.9 to 10.7 "MW" in the earlier descriptive check of the night step are points: that check divided by a proxy capacity of about 100, which is the scale of points.

docs.title: Pre-fit clarification 3: actual demand against the baseline forecast on cold nights (written before the figure was computed)
docs.text: A figure on the substation cards shows actual demand and experiment 114's baseline forecast (B0) on cold winter nights, so that a visible miss at 01:00 shows up. The maintainer asked for it after the first fits. The rule is fixed here, before any residual is computed: cold winter nights are the cold-snap nights of the plan (the evenings whose next day lies in the coldest 10% of days of its July-to-June year by the mean ERA5 temperature across the six decision series, on Greenwich Mean Time nights that are not excluded), for winters 2023-24 and 2024-25, the winters with stored B0 predictions before the scored winter is unlocked. Each panel shows the median across nights, with the 25th to 75th percentile band, of actual demand and of the B0 median forecast (day D+1), for the half-hours starting 22:00 to 07:30, in points. The eight E7-X series have no stored B0 forecast, so they appear with actual demand only. A one-line list of other visible misses follows, from the median B0 residual per half-hour: the half-hour with the largest median residual, and the half-hour of the largest 30-minute rise between 05:00 and 08:00 in the actual and in the forecast. The figure is descriptive: it adds no contrast and no verdict. Winter 2025-26 enters only after PR 1397 has merged.

docs.title: The question, and what earlier experiments already say
docs.text:
The night step is real in one winter and unmeasured across winters. Experiment 121 tried to detect the step through quantile scores over all 20 night half-hours, where a step of 4 points is diluted to about one noise standard deviation, and its fourth gate had to be redefined twice.

E7 changes the instrument. E7 compares five window half-hours with four baseline half-hours of the same night, so the dilution disappears and a slow level error cancels. The estimator is a regression of the night difference on cold, in the spirit of the degree-day regressions used for load, and the pooling is the random-effects meta-analysis of DerSimonian and Laird (1986) with the Hartung and Knapp (2001) interval. The block bootstrap follows Künsch (1989). The earlier experiments this plan builds on are 111, 113, 114, 120, 121 (PR 1413), and 122. One targeted search for a DOI on Economy 7 or storage-heating load found none on temperature dependence. The nearest sources are Elexon CP1058A, which describes the Economy 7 profile class, and a statistical review of UK residential electrical loads; neither was checked for a temperature-dependent night step. Elexon's Radio Teleswitch guidance note states that teleswitch times are in UTC and that Settlement converts them to clock time in British Summer Time where a GMT indicator is set; which value of the indicator means fixed to GMT is unresolved in the documents read, so "UTC-fixed" on this page is a reading of the data only.

docs.title: Estimand
docs.text:
• Window rows: the five half-hours starting 00:30, 01:00, 01:30, 02:00, and 02:30. Test 1 prints the timestamp convention of the observed file against experiment 121's code, and the window follows the documented convention only. It is fixed in test 1, before any estimate, and never moved. Sensitivity (descriptive): the three-row window 00:30 to 01:30.
  • Baseline rows: the four half-hours starting 22:00 to 23:30 of the same night, on the same clock as the window. A night is labelled by its evening's local date, and its day type (weekday, Saturday, Sunday) is that date's.
  • Night difference d: the mean of the window rows minus the mean of the baseline rows, in points.
  • Cold c: max(0, 15.5 - T) degrees, where T is the daily mean of hourly ERA5 temperature at the substation's cell over the local calendar day containing the window rows. The daily mean is a proxy for the temperature that sets storage-heater charging, and it includes the afternoon after the step. Its correlation with the mean temperature from 18:00 to 08:00 is printed, and a night-temperature c is a descriptive sensitivity.
  • Primary rows (GMT nights): nights between the October and March clock changes, when the local and UTC clocks agree. Clock-change nights, bank-holiday nights, and the Christmas to New Year run are dropped from every fit.
  • Summer reference d_summer: the mean of d over June to August nights on the local clock. Experiment 121's one summer pair found a step of 1.7 points or less; the page states the assumption that the summer night has no step.
  • Slope b: the points change in d per degree of c, from d = a_w + b*c + day-type terms + noise on GMT nights, with a separate intercept a_w for each winter w and a common b across winters. The slope needs no summer assumption.
  • Step at a stated cold night: step = a_hat + b*c_ref - d_summer, with c_ref = 12.5 degrees (daily mean 3 C, inside experiment 122's cold-snap range of -2.0 to 3.1 C), where a_hat is the mean of the winter intercepts. The step is the full cold-dependent and flat step, with no demand model removed. The flat part is a_hat - d_summer, so reading the step at c = 0 is an extrapolation, because few GMT nights are warmer than 15.5 C. The flat part is reported separately from b.
  • Excess over B0 (cross-check R): the same regression on experiment 114's stored B0 residuals measures only the part of the step that B0's free daily profile and its 00:00 to 04:00 heating band do not already absorb. R is a different, smaller quantity, expected at 30 to 60% of D, and is compared with D only as a measure of the absorption, never as an error.

docs.title: Substations and histories
docs.text:
Fitted series: the six decision series, which are DP Primaries, and the eight E7-X Primaries. The rule-based flag of nged_data.cleaning is applied to all 14 series, so E7-X needs no hand-filtered switching list. The six decision series are also run with their hand-filtered list as a sensitivity. E7-X has its own row set, e7_nights_v1, outside dp_mw_v1. D12 reports apparent power in MVA, so its night difference is an apparent-power step, converted to points in the same way.

Series Observed from Winters (2021-22 to 2025-26) Role D5, D10, D11 2019-09-17 5 decision series; D5 and D10 prompted the study D14 2019-10-21 5 decision series D16 2020-12-22 5 (the history covers 2021-07 onwards) decision series; prompted the study D9 2023-08-23 3 (2023-24 to 2025-26) decision series D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22 2019-09-17 5 E7-X: not chosen for any step D15, D18 n/a n/a generator-linked, shown only as G-c, not fitted

Winters 2021-22 to 2025-26 only. Winter 2019-20 is not added: its window would leave about 6 months after the lockdown months go out, with no summer and no pinned-capacity vintage.

Winter roles. Winter 2023-24 (tuning) and winter 2024-25 (replicate) are used for design checks (block length). Winters 2021-22 and 2022-23 are not opened for any design choice, and their estimates are read only after the gate has run. Winter 2025-26 is the selection winter, and the maintainer ruled that it is fitted only after PR 1397 (experiment 114) has merged. Headline winters are 2021-22 to 2024-25 (the winters that did not choose the three series), and winter 2025-26 is reported beside them. There are at most four headline winters and five in all, from one weather product and one set of substations, so the winters are separate years and not independent experiments. The page prints the winter count at every estimate.

docs.title: Estimators
docs.text:
• D (primary): the direct per-night regression above. Intervals come from a 14-day-block bootstrap of nights stratified by winter, 1,000 draws, the same count in the real fits and in the gate. A bounded (non-negative) b is fitted only as a descriptive variant, never in the gate.
  • R (cross-check): the same regression on stored B0 residuals (predictions/{tuning,replicate, scored}_b0, median, day D+1), for winters 2023-24 to 2025-26 only, at the six decision series. Experiment 114 stores no earlier residuals. R is not injected into the gate, because injected data would need B0 refitted per draw. R reads winter 2025-26 only after PR 1397 has merged, and the run pins the merge commit's SHA in decisions.json.
  • E7-K (descriptive): R on the stored *_b0_k and *_t_all_k predictions, which shows how much of the step the Kalman filter removes.
  • Cold-snap subset (winter-first rule): the coldest 10% of days of a winter by the mean ERA5 temperature averaged across the six decision series (experiment 122's rule). The day count is stated, and too few days where under 5. On the subset the page prints the raw mean of d minus d_summer. November to March is reported beside November to February.
  • Event-day rule: not applicable, because E7 has no scored contrast across calendar events.

docs.title: Pooling
docs.text:
The pool is a random effect across series, with limits. With k series the pooled mean has a Hartung-Knapp interval (t with k - 1 degrees of freedom) and, beside it, a percentile interval from resampling whole series. The between-series standard deviation tau is printed with a profile- likelihood interval. The pooled mean is marked cannot tell if the two intervals disagree on whether 0 lies inside. With fewer than 5 series in a set, the page prints the plain mean and range, with no tau. Neighbouring cells share one ERA5 product, so the series are not independent, and the page says the pooled intervals are optimistic.

Pooled sets, side by side:

  1. the six decision series (headline);
  2. D5, D10, and D16 (selected for showing the step);
  3. D11, D14, and D9 (not selected);
  4. the eight E7-X series;
  5. all 14 series.

The gap between sets 2 and 3 shows the selection effect.

docs.title: Known-answer test and gate
docs.text:
Order: test 0, test 1, the rank check, design checks, the gate, and only then the estimates of winters 2021-22 and 2022-23, and winter 2025-26 after PR 1397 has merged. The gate can fail by design. A failed gate is recorded as it stands and is not redefined, and it removes the detectable label, so the raw means carry the page.

  1. Feasibility. Each fitted series has the rule-based flag, at least two winters, and a night table with every window and baseline row present on at least 90% of its nights. Failures are named and dropped.
  2. Reproduction (blocking). The night table's d equals a hand-computed d on 20 printed nights; the timestamp convention and window rows are printed; no row on or after 2026-07-01; R's stored residuals reproduce experiment 114's stored B0 quantile score for the tuning year to 1e-4.
  3. Known-answer injection (can fail). Noise: real nights of the same series with D's fitted cold-dependent part removed from the five window rows, resampled in 14-day blocks within winter, with the real covariates. Injected shapes, in points at c_ref, scaled by c / 12.5, for S in {4, 7} plus a placebo S = 0:
    • matched: an equal amount on the five window rows (the fitted form);
    • ramp-plateau: weights 0, 0.5, 1, 1, 1 on the five window rows, continuing at weight 1 until 07:00. The truth is the mean weight over the window times S;
    • flat: S on the window rows of every GMT night, not scaled with cold (truth b = 0, step = S);
    • night-temperature: the matched shape driven by the 18:00 to 08:00 mean temperature instead of the daily mean (descriptive: its bias is reported, and no coverage target is set).

There are 200 draws per cell per series, at all fitted series. - Target (the label rests on these rows): coverage of the truth by the 90% interval of the step at c_ref, for the matched, ramp-plateau, and flat shapes and the placebo, is 85 to 95% pooled over series and 80 to 98% for each series. With 200 draws the Monte Carlo standard error is about 2.1 points per series and about 0.9 points pooled over 14. Block resampling makes the draws less independent, so these errors are lower bounds. - Bias: the mean estimate lies within 0.5 points of the truth for the matched and flat shapes at 4 and 7. - Power (descriptive): the share of draws with the 90% interval above 0, at 4 and 7 points, per series. A series under 80% at 4 points is marked "weak". - Pooled interval: S is drawn per series from {0, 0, 4, 4, 7, 7} across the six decision series, and the pooled mean's Hartung-Knapp interval covers its true mean in 85 to 95% of 200 draws. 3. Rank check (blocking). The design matrix (1, c, day-type terms, winter intercepts) has full rank, its smallest singular value and the variance inflation of c are printed per series, and a series with a variance inflation above 10 is dropped.

Gate result: the table says interval coverage within 85 to 95% or names the failing cell. The page does not say the estimate is right, because the gate tests the estimator on shapes this plan chose.

docs.title: Timing (descriptive)
docs.text: The gate cannot calibrate timing, because cold British Summer Time (BST) nights are few. A cold BST night is a night in BST with a daily mean below 8 C. Per series and per winter-pair, the page prints the count and says cannot tell where it is under 10. Where it is 10 or more, the estimator is delta, the mean over those nights of d measured with the local-clock window minus d measured with the UTC-clock window (the baseline on the matching clock). A step fixed to the local clock makes delta positive, and a step fixed to UTC makes it negative. A 90% block-bootstrap interval is printed and the label (local, UTC, unresolved) is marked uncalibrated.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text:
• Table 1 (unpooled, first): per series, b, the flat part, and the step at c_ref, each with 90% intervals, the winters used, the raw cold-night mean of d minus d_summer, R and its ratio to D, and the detectable flag. Every fitted series appears, including those with no step.
  • Table 2 (winters): the step at c_ref per winter per series, the selection winter marked.
  • Table 3 (pooled): the five sets above, with both intervals, tau, and cannot tell where it applies. The first set is the headline.
  • Table 4 (timing): counts, delta, and the label.
  • detectable: the 90% interval of the step at c_ref lies wholly above 0, and the gate row for that series is within its band. No multiplicity correction is made: with 14 series, about 0.7 false positives are expected under no step (5% one-sided each), and the page says so.
  • Winter breakdown: every estimate is shown per winter, with the count of winters.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
Written before any estimate; each line can fail.

  • Headline pooled step at c_ref, six decision series, headline winters: between 2 and 6 points, with the Hartung-Knapp interval wholly above 0.
  • Selected subset (D5, D10, D16): 5 to 10 points, above the pooled step of D11, D14, and D9, which is 1 to 3.5 points and may include 0. The selected subset's larger value is the selection effect.
  • E7-X: each series 0 to 3 points, and the E7-X pooled step 0.5 to 2 points, below the pooled step of the decision series.
  • Slope b: positive at D5, D10, and D16, between 0.4 and 0.8 points per degree.
  • Flat part: a_hat - d_summer within +-2 points at every series. A series whose 90% interval lies wholly outside +-2 points fails the line.
  • R against D: 30 to 60% at D5, D10, and D16.
  • Raw contrast: the raw cold-night mean of d minus d_summer lies within 2 points of D's step at the mean c of those nights (about 8 to 10 degrees), not at c_ref.
  • Timing: cannot tell at most series; if a label is printed, local.
  • Gate: coverage within the bands. The chance of a failing cell is judged about one in three, because the ramp-plateau shape changes the window mean.
  • Run time: under 1.5 hours of wall clock on CPU.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
There is no win-or-lose verdict on a hypothesis about a model. The verdict word summarises the estimates and the gate:

  • supported: the gate rows are within their bands for all six decision series, the headline pooled step over the six decision series has a Hartung-Knapp interval wholly above 0 in the headline winters, and the percentile interval agrees.
  • partly supported: the gate is within its bands and the pooled step is positive but cannot tell, or positive only in the selection winter.
  • inconclusive: a gate row for a decision series fails, or fewer than 2 headline winters are available at those series. invalid: a leak (a row on or after 2026-07-01). failed: test 1 or the rank check cannot pass.
  • The estimate does not choose between models and does not change the production forecast. A supported result feeds the substation cards and a calibrated b can serve as a prior for experiment 121's night arms; neither is part of this plan.

docs.title: Audit before merge: the seven triggers
docs.text:
The seven triggers are those of briefs/common.md and briefs/dp_cal.md, applied to these results.

  1. A control fails: test 1, the rank check, or the placebo coverage outside its band.
  2. Contradiction: a pooled step above 15 points, a negative step at a series whose raw cold- night mean exceeds 4 points, or an E7-X pooled step above that of the decision series.
  3. Estimate and raw contrast disagree in sign at a series.
  4. Leaving one series out moves the pooled mean outside the all-series pooled interval.
  5. A null control moves: the unbounded and bounded D disagree at a series with b far from 0.
  6. Interval width: D's interval at c_ref is wider than 8 points at a decision series.
  7. A later design depends on it: the cards and experiment 121's night arms use the numbers, so trigger 7 fires. The manager runs the Opus review of the estimator and the gate after the quota resets (01:00 UTC on 2026-10-21); this session runs one Sonnet code review for leakage (the cut at train_end) and one Sonnet write-up review.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: D-labels only, with dates, for the Primaries; no substation names, no topology. D15 and D18 are generator-linked and appear only as G-c, normalised, with no dates, and are not fitted. Fitted steps in points are acceptable for Primaries, which are not generators. Per-series slopes are shown only where the rank check passes and the gate row is within its band, because experiment 121 forbade per- site slopes from weakly identified fits.

docs.title: Substation cards in the plan
docs.text:
Section label: "Provisional: fitted to past weather, estimation only". One card per fitted series shows:

  • the step at a stated cold night (daily mean 3 C), in points, with its 90% interval, the slope in points per degree, and the winter-versus-summer contrast;
  • the flat part and the summer reference;
  • the start time: the first half-hour whose mean (observed minus baseline), on cold GMT nights minus the summer mean, exceeds half of its value at 02:30, with a bootstrap interval in half- hours;
  • the timing label (local or UTC, where estimable) or cannot tell, with the count of cold BST nights;
  • R's ratio to D and the Kalman filter's removal (E7-K);
  • an example forecast week, where the series has one in dp_series.md's selection rule, drawn from stored predictions.

docs.title: Comparison with experiments 121 and 120
docs.text: Experiment 121 (MH). Its night-arm estimates are compared with D's step per series, with both intervals and their overlap. Experiment 120 (SH) learns an unsupervised daily-shape library with a 01:00 shape. When SH reports, the comparison per series is SH's integrated 01:00 jump over the five window rows, in points at the same cold night, beside D's step. A series where SH shows no jump and D's interval lies wholly above 0 is a case the learned library misses, and the card says so. The plan does not decide which is right.

docs.title: Run order, reuse, compute, and time
docs.text:
Scripts import only their own folder, studies.*, and reviewed packages. The scripts read the series' power through studies.power.scan_power (cleaned readings), ERA5 temperature from the stage 1 pilot's era5_features.parquet, and the copy of experiment 114's and experiment 121's window and block-resampling conventions. D needs no demand model.

Order: night table and tests 0, 1, and 3; design checks on winters 2023-24 and 2024-25 (block length); the gate; then winters 2021-22 and 2022-23; then winter 2025-26 after PR 1397 has merged; tables, cards, write-up.

CPU only, 6 cores, with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 in every worker (one process per series). The run pauses when the 1-minute load average is above about 35. The budget is 1.5 hours of wall clock, no GPU.

docs.title: What the write-up must contain
docs.text:
The take-home says how large the full night step is at a daily mean of 3 C, pooled over the six decision series and per series, whether it grows with cold, what the selection effect is, how much of the step B0 already absorbs, and that the clock is not identified where cold BST nights are few. The page is figure-led: raw first (the mean of d against c with the fitted line and the summer reference), then the step per series with intervals, the same per winter with the selection winter marked, known-answer recovery per shape, the pooled forest plot with the five sets, and cold BST night counts.

Caveats: the three large series were chosen on the selection winter; the five winters share one weather product; the summer reference may hold a step of up to 1.7 points; the flat part is an extrapolation; the step has the pattern of storage heating and NGED has not confirmed the cause (daylight, lighting, and switching schedules also change at night); the daily mean temperature is a proxy for the temperature that sets charging; the gate tests only the shapes this plan chose.

docs.title: Size: the five triggers
docs.text: 1. Stored: private estimates and figures under data/ml-experiments/, and the write-up under docs/ml-experiments/; nothing in Delta. 2. Serving path: not touched. 3. Degradation rule: not touched. 4. More than one defensible design: yes (window, cold variable, estimator); this plan pre-registers D. 5. Callers not nameable without searching: none. Size: medium.

docs.title: Review triage
docs.text: The plan was reviewed once by a Sonnet agent (30 findings), and the manager and maintainer rulings were applied: D replaces the earlier joint estimator; the bound is removed from the gated estimator; the gate tests the used estimator on misspecified shapes; the pooled estimate is reported after the unpooled table; E7-X runs on the rule-based flag; no winter 2019-20. The full review is private. A second change, the pre-fit clarification at the top of this page, makes the six decision series the headline.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, H: does a bulk supply point reading limit the damage from a Primary's metering error?
docs.text:
Adding the bulk supply point reading to the Primary substations' fit halved the damage from a scale error in one Primary's history, but it made forecasts on clean data worse at every weight above zero, so the reading should not go into the Primaries' loss. The smallest clean-data loss was 0.385 points, about 17 times the 0.023-point limit. An exactly specified synthetic system lost clean accuracy the same way, so the loss does not come mainly from a wrong multiplier. The cause is untested. The next thing to try is the bulk supply point reading as a separate monitor, outside the Primaries' fit. The verdict is not supported, for this joint fit with the multipliers on the Primaries' and generation sums fixed at 1.

Why not supported and not inconclusive. The pre-registered tuning rule allows a clean-forecast rise of at most 0.023 points, the limit on extra clean error fixed before any fit. That rule failed at every weight tried, so the result stands on its own. Arm B was an extra arm that stopped at its plumbing check, and it does not change the verdict.

A Primary substation is a substation that takes power from a bulk supply point. A bulk supply point (BSP) is where the distribution network takes power from the transmission network. The BSP reading is roughly the sum of the Primaries' power minus the power of the metered generators beneath it. We fitted each Primary's forecast together with the BSP reading. The weight says how closely the fit must match that reading, and weight 0 means separate fits. We then injected metering errors into one Primary's history (gaps, stuck values, and scale errors) and measured the damage, which is the rise in that Primary's forecast error, with and without the BSP reading. A point is 1% of a Primary's effective capacity, and every error below is a mean absolute error in points. The data come from experiment 103, and experiment 36 had found that summing the Primary forecasts added little at the BSPs. The plan was committed before any fit, and the commit order proves it.

Figure 1 shows two runs of the same tuning. The tuning cut is 2023-07-01: the fit reads only earlier data, and the tuning year is the 12 months after it. The first run set the BSP row's scale to 1.2 MW, from a regression on the Primaries' readings. Arm B's plumbing check showed that the joint fit's BSP row carries the Primaries' fitted variation, 2.9 MW, so the re-run used 2.9 MW and a grid reaching lower weights. A given weight then acts about 6 times weaker (2.9 over 1.2, squared). Both runs use the same 200 injected errors. The re-run came after seeing the first run, so it is post hoc, and it changes the numbers and not the verdict.

Figure 2 shows the closure audit's multipliers. The audit fits, per BSP, how much of each Primary's reading and of the generation enters the BSP reading.

Figure 3 shows arm B's plumbing check. Synthetic systems built exactly as the fit assumes still lose clean accuracy at every weight.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Hint fit (the pilot). One BSP, the one that closes in the audit, with a joint fit of its Primaries and one remainder step penalty. Each Primary's demand has a smooth drift, and the fit is made once before each scored year with no Kalman filter re-learning the level. The plan caps a pilot at partly supported.
  • Arm B (plumbing check only). It asked whether the hint stops hurting clean forecasts once its multipliers are fixed at the closure audit's fit. The check used 20 synthetic systems built exactly as the fit assumes, plus a control with the multipliers 15% wrong. The stop rule was that a failed check ends the arm, and the check failed twice (see the findings below), so arm B's tuning grid was never run.
  • Row set. dp_mw_v1 and dp_mva_dark_v1 from experiment 103. Tuning year 2023-24, replicate year 2024-25, scored year 2025-26. Only the clean-error grid was fitted at the replicate and scored cuts.
  • Injections. 200 errors at two Primaries (60 gaps, 60 stuck runs, 80 scale errors of 20%), 10 seeds per cell and Primary.
  • Not produced. The score is the mean absolute error of a point forecast, so there are no quantile scores, tail rows, climatology or manual_heuristic rows, BSP-forecast arms, or intervals. The known-answer gate was not run, because the tuning rule chose weight 0.

docs.title: Headline numbers
docs.text:
• The BSP reading halves the damage from scale errors. The summed extra error from scale errors fell from 33.0 points at weight 0 to 16.3 at weight 30 in the first run and to 16.8 in the re-run (51% and 49% of the damage left), about 0.2 points per injection. Pooling all 200 injections gives a 41% cut in the first run (32.8 to 19.4 points) and 40% in the re-run.
  • The BSP reading does nothing for gaps and stuck runs. Neither did measurable damage at weight 0 (summed -0.1 points each), and weight 30 added 1.2 to 1.8 points in both runs.
  • The BSP reading makes clean forecasts worse. The tuning-year clean mean absolute error rose against separate fits as follows, with a limit of 0.023 points (the replicate and scored years are in tuning_report.txt):
Weight First run (1.2 MW), points Re-run (2.9 MW), points 0.003 not tried 0.385 0.03 not tried 0.765 0.1 2.355 1.083 1 4.222 2.989 30 4.652 4.564
  • The tuning rule chooses weight 0 in both runs, so the damage-reduction gate (a cut of at least 0.30) cannot pass. No interval was computed.
  • The BSP reading is a weak monitor. At the tuning cut a 30-day 25% scale error is found in 0% of injections when the fit includes the injected series, and in 50% when the fit is trained only on earlier rows (2% and 29% at the replicate cut). The earlier-rows fit raises a false alarm on 1.2% of windows in the data it was fitted to and on 61% of windows in the year after the cut.

docs.title: Closure-audit findings
docs.text:
• One BSP closes in the training years, and the other does not. At the pilot BSP the in-sample residual is 2.2 to 3.2 points (1.2 to 1.8 MW) at the three cuts, over six winters with a median residual within 1 MW.
  • The fitted multipliers are 1.01 to 1.16 on the Primaries and 0.85 to 0.90 on the generation.
  • Out of sample, the frozen fit drifts. The residual scale is 5.5 points with a +3.7 MW median offset. The other BSP has an in-sample residual of 11 points.
  • The full numbers are in audit_report.txt (first run: audit_report_first_run.txt).

docs.title: Arm B plumbing check
docs.text:
• First run (before the BSP-row scale correction). The exact synthetic systems rose by 13.0 points at weight 0.1, and the control with multipliers 15% wrong rose by 12.0, so the check could not tell them apart. The check exposed the 1.2 MW scale fault described under Figure 1.
  • Second run (after the correction). The exact systems still rose by 6.0 points at weight 0.1 and by 0.05 points at the smallest weight, 0.0003, above the 0.023 limit. The control rose by about the same, so the check cannot detect a wrong multiplier. Numbers are medians of the 20 systems (armb_plumbing_first_run.json, armb_plumbing.json).
  • Cause of the loss (untested). We hypothesise that the BSP reading carries the sum of the Primaries' own autocorrelated noise, and the fit bends to explain it. We did not run a control without that noise.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Mean and median forecasts, and quantile scores, do not apply, because the pilot scores a point forecast by its mean absolute error.
  • Trigger 1 (a control fails) fired: arm B's plumbing check failed twice.
  • Trigger 2 (a contradiction) fired. The result contradicts the prediction that clean error would change by no more than 0.02 points, and it contradicts the finding of experiment 36 that bottom-up children add 0.04 to 0.19 points at the BSPs. The cause was not tested.
  • Trigger 7 (dependence) also applies, because a possible follow-on experiment depends on this result.
  • Triggers 3 to 6 do not apply or were not run: the score is a mean absolute error (trigger 3), no leave-one-out was run (4), no arm is nested in another (5), and no interval was computed (6).
  • Predictions that failed: the chosen weight W* was predicted at 0.3 to 3 and came out at 0, and the extra clean error at W* was predicted within +/-0.02 points. The extra clean error at weight 30 was predicted 0.05 to 0.15 points worse than at W*, and it came out at 4.564 points.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• A coding fault is not excluded, because the known-answer gate was not run.
  • The filter-on reading, the production-relevant one, was not produced.
  • Only one BSP was fitted, so the finding may not carry to a BSP with different Primaries.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Keep the BSP reading out of the Primaries' loss, and use its residual against the Primaries' fitted values as a monitoring signal, scored for detection and false alarms in the year after the cut. Whether to run it is the maintainer's decision.
  • Test the cause directly: a synthetic control with no autocorrelated noise in the BSP reading.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, N8: do the 51 ENS members and GAM-K's residual table count weather error twice?
docs.text: This experiment asked whether the weather forecast error is counted twice in the uncertainty bands of our demand forecast, and tested a fix. The forecast comes from GAM-K, a generalised additive model with a convex heating response that forecasts a substation's demand (from experiment 111). GAM-K runs on each of the 51 members of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble, where each member is a separate simulation of the weather. It then puts a table of past forecast errors, as quantiles by lead time and time of day, around every member's demand forecast. The table was measured as observed demand minus the ensemble's average forecast, so it already contains the weather error that the 51 members' spread also carries. The weather error is therefore counted twice: once in the spread of the members and once in the table. We refitted the table on forecasts driven by the weather model's best estimate of the true weather (almost no weather error), placed it around each member, and compared the bands with today's bands and with today's bands after re-tuning their width factors on the same grid. The test used the same rows at five Primary substations. Refitting the table did not improve the tails. The weather members' variance is 4 to 19 (percentage points of the substation's effective capacity, squared) against 27 to 53 for the table, so the double count exists in the code and is too small to matter. The verdict is inconclusive, because no arm reached 14 of 16 calibration checks (four tail quantiles in each of four lead-time bands), which the decision rule needs. On cold winter nights (days at or below each site's 10th percentile of winter temperature, in runs of two or more), every arm's 95% quantile covered only 73% to 78% of the observed values, so demand exceeded it about a quarter of the time.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Take-home message. Placing a table of forecast errors around each of the 51 weather members, fitted so that it holds no weather error, scored 0.007 points of tail pinball worse than today's table re-tuned on the same grid in the scored year (98.3% interval −0.001 to +0.013, five substations, 291 runs). The replicate months agree in sign (+0.004, −0.006 to +0.017). The reason is in the variance accounting: demand error is dominated by the model's own error, and the weather members carry little of it. The larger finding is on cold winter nights, where the 95% quantile of every arm sits too low. The verdict is inconclusive: MP had 6 of 16 calibration cells in band in the scored year and 12 in the replicate months, and K0-w had 5 and 11.

The known-answer gate passed every blocking test. The synthetic twin recovered the injected weather variance within 5% per lead band, the analytic double-count ratio of K0's variance to MP's within 4%, and a halved member spread as an s of 2.0 in 3 of 4 lead bands (the second lead band chose 1.0 against a true factor near 2.0). K0 rebuilt from the cache reproduced experiment 111's stored tuning quantiles to 8e-6 (float32 rounding). A positive control confirmed that the causality test detects a changed reading before the filter's cutoff. The twin's numbers are in work/gate.json, printed by e00125_gate.py. The twin confirms the arithmetic and the code, and does not show that the real ensemble behaves like the twin.

Figure 1 shows that MP does not beat K0-w on any measure (C1), the decision contrast. The key to the arms: K0 is today's table with its stored factors, K0-w is today's table with factors re-tuned, MP is the analysis-proxy table placed around each member, MP-s is MP with the members rescaled, MM centres on the ensemble mean, and MO uses the members alone.

  • C1, MP minus K0-w (decision): quantile score +0.0077 (95% interval +0.0006 to +0.0133) and tail pinball +0.0070 (−0.0013 to +0.0134) in the scored year; +0.0006 (−0.0092 to +0.0121) and +0.0035 (−0.0056 to +0.0173) in the replicate months. MP improved tail pinball at 1 of 5 substations in the scored year and 2 of 5 in the replicate months.
  • MP minus the stored K0: the same within 0.0005, so re-tuning K0's factors on the wide grid (K0-w minus K0: +0.0001, −0.0008 to +0.0013) changed the scores by under 0.001 and cut the cells in band from 9 to 5.
  • C2, MP minus MM (two designs compared): −0.0254 in quantile score (−0.0379 to −0.0139) and −0.0086 in tail pinball (−0.0189 to −0.0010) in the scored year. Pooling the members as a mixture with the proxy table beats the ensemble-mean design, but the contrast changes the centres and the table together, so it does not isolate the members.
  • C4, MP-s minus MP: −0.0005 (−0.0009 to −0.0001). Rescaling the members about their mean by an s chosen on the tuning months (1.25 at 0 to 24 hours, 1.0 elsewhere) is a gain of no practical size.
  • Absolute scores, scored year, leads 0.5 to 168 hours (points of capacity; smaller is better):
Arm Quantile score Tail pinball Cells in band (of 16) Mean absolute error of the median K0 (today's table, stored factors) 2.800 0.4685 9 4.907 K0-w (today's table, factors re-tuned) 2.801 0.4689 5 4.907 MP (analysis-proxy table) 2.808 0.4759 6 4.904 MP-s (members rescaled) 2.808 0.4756 8 4.904 MP-1 (MP, every factor 1) 2.808 0.4753 12 4.904 MM (ensemble mean, today's table) 2.834 0.4845 8 4.912 MO (members only) 3.747 1.3508 0 4.910

K0's 2.800 is experiment 111's score, reproduced. The replicate months give the same ordering, except that K0-w and K0, and MP-s and MP-1, swap places by under 0.001. The day-ahead (D+1) score was not computed separately; the lead bands are in e00125_tables.py.

Figure 2 shows that the cold winter nights are the main miss, and no arm fixes it. A cold day is a local day whose ERA5 mean temperature is at or below the 10th percentile of the site's winter days in 2019 to 2024; a cold snap is two or more such days in a row. The rule was fixed in work/decisions.json (hash 019a763a…) before any score was read. On the 36 substation-days of the scored winter's cold snaps, K0's q95 covered 77.7%, K0-w's 72.9%, MP's 73.7%, and MM's 77.9% of the observed night half-hours at day-ahead leads (the target is 95%); the q99 covered 91% to 94%. The lower tail is also off, in the other direction: the q05 covered 7.3% (nominal 5%) in every arm. In the four arms tested, which share GAM-K's centre, the miss therefore lies in the centre or the width of the day-ahead forecast on cold nights, and not in the residual-table variants tried.

Figure 3 shows all four arms with a table slightly too narrow, and the tuned factor of 0.9 makes it worse on calibration cells. Coverage lies within 2.4 points of the level at every level and lead band. The calibration rule is stricter than that (a half-width of 2.5 standard errors with one effective case per substation-day), so MP-1 with every factor at 1 had 12 cells in band while MP, with factors of 0.9 to 1.0 tuned on the odd months, had 6. The factors tuned on the tuning months narrowed bands that were already slightly too narrow out of period.

Figure 4 shows why the fix cannot matter: the table's variance is several times the members'. The members' variance (σ_w², the variance of the 51 corrected member forecasts) is 4.1, 6.1, 12.7, and 18.6 points squared in the four lead bands, against 27 to 53 for the table's 11 atoms and 34 to 61 for the squared error of the ensemble mean. The total variance of K0-w's mixture over MP's is 0.98, 1.01, 0.95, and 1.05, not the 1.05 to 1.8 predicted. The residual table fitted on ensemble-mean residuals and the one fitted on analysis-driven residuals have nearly the same width, which suggests the ensemble mean's error is mostly model error and filter error, if the members' spread is a fair measure of weather error. The rank histogram of ERA5 temperature that would test this was not drawn.

Figure 5 shows that the 51 members alone are far too narrow for demand. The observed value fell outside the range of all 51 members in 74%, 71%, 62%, and 55% of rows in the four lead bands (a flat histogram would put 4% there). The fair CRPS of the members is 3.69 to 4.46 points (Ferro (2014)). The threshold-weighted CRPS of the two mixtures (Gneiting and Ranjan (2011)) differs between K0-w and MP by at most 0.005 in any band (upper tail 0.2975 against 0.2976 at 0 to 24 hours).

Predictions and what happened. The prediction that K0's variance was 1.05 to 1.8 times MP's failed (0.95 to 1.05). The prediction that K0-w moves its factor to 0.7 to 0.8 at long leads failed (K0-w's factors are 0.9 in every band). MP's factors are 0.9 to 1.0, as predicted, but MP was in band in fewer than 14 cells (6 and 12). The predicted gain on cold nights (MP's night q95 within 1 to 3 points of K0-w's) holds in the sense that MP is within 1 point of K0-w, and both are 21 to 22 points from nominal. The decision rule gave inconclusive, not refuted, because the quantile-score interval of C1 does not lie wholly above +0.02.

Checks.

  • Median minus mean forecast per site (scored year, points): MP's median lies 0.14 below the ensemble mean at D5, 0.05 below at D11, 0.02 below at D10 and D16, and 0.02 above at D14. K0-w's are −0.10, −0.04, −0.04, +0.00, and +0.01 at D5, D11, D10, D16, and D14. MM has zero by construction.
  • Mean absolute error of the median beside C1: MP is 0.003 points better (4.904 against 4.907) while its quantile score is 0.0077 worse.
  • Triggers fired: triggers 2, 3, 4, and 6. Every explanation below is post hoc, written after the scores were read, and none was tested by a further run except where stated.
    • Trigger 2: the variance-ratio and C1 predictions failed. The variance accounting above is the post hoc explanation, and it is a calculation on the stored predictions, not a new test.
    • Trigger 3: the error of the median and the quantile score point in different directions, by 0.0025 points, and MP's median at D5 sits 0.04 points below K0-w's, above the plan's 0.01 threshold. No explanation was tested.
    • Trigger 4: leaving out D5 or D16 flips the sign of C1's replicate quantile-score estimate, which is within 0.001 of zero and has an interval spanning zero. The scored-year sign and the verdict do not change.
    • Trigger 6: C1's 95% score interval has a half-width of 0.0064, under half of experiment 111's sister contrast at 0.016. The post hoc explanation is that the two arms differ only in the width of the table.
    • No Opus audit was run, because the verdict is inconclusive and two Sonnet reviews were applied.

Caveats.

  • K0's scored-year tails were read before the plan, so the scored year is not blind for K0.
  • The analysis proxy is a control member of the ensemble and not an independent analysis.
  • The replicate months are interleaved with the tuning months and are not out of time.
  • The scored year has 291 runs (the 2026-06-30 run is excluded, as in experiment 111), and one winter. The cold-snap read rests on 36 substation-days.
  • The 11-atom mixture caps q01 and q99, for every arm alike.
  • The substation cards of the plan were not produced.
  • The rank histogram is of demand among the members. The plan's rank histogram of ERA5 temperature was not drawn, because the cache holds demand forecasts and not member weather.
  • The cold-night coverage finding (73% to 78% at the 95% quantile) is descriptive, not a tested contrast. It rests on 36 substation-days at 5 substations in one winter.
  • The cold-snap rule was written after the predictions were stored and before any score was read.
  • The known-answer gate has limits. On the twin, K0 also reaches 16 of 16 calibration cells, so that check alone cannot tell the double count from its absence. The variance-ratio check (2b) does, but only in the two longest lead bands. The members-only arm under-covers more than the analytic formula predicts (shortfall 0.60 to 0.80 against 0.41 to 0.76), and the gate does not explain the gap. No known-answer test covers the analysis-proxy centre built from the real cache.
  • The tables for K0, K0-w, and MM come from experiment 111's stored fit, which includes a few replicate-month rows near month ends. That favours those arms over MP in the replicate months.
  • The replicate-month bootstrap uses two month blocks, so its intervals are rough. The bootstrap uses one random seed, not the three the plan asked for.
  • Not computed, though the plan listed them: the all-rows score beside the switching-filtered score, the share of rows beyond the most extreme atom, and the 80% and 90% coverage by lead band.
  • The night band and the month blocks take local hours and dates from the half-hour's end time, so the 23:30 to 00:00 half-hour falls in the next day.

Lessons for later experiments. In this experiment the cold-night shortfall is the clearer target of the two we measured: a quantile of demand on cold nights, conditioned on temperature, is one option. A factor tuned on alternate months was not reliable out of period here (6 of 16 cells against 12, with no detectable difference in tail pinball). At five substations in one scored year, the members did better as a mixture (C2) than alone (MO).

docs.title: What N8 asks, and why it starts from the code
docs.text:
GAM-K already runs the 51 members, so the question is whether the weather error is counted twice. studies.dp_ens.forecast_run drives the monthly GAM-K fit with each usable ENS member's weather, adds the filter's correction to each member's mean, puts a residual table around every corrected member, and pools the members with mixture_quantiles. The residual table (LeadHourSpread: one table per lead band, hour band, and quarter, times a factor per lead band) is fitted by fit_spread_from_frame (e00111_ens.py:243-255) on observed minus the corrected ensemble mean. That residual already contains the weather-forecast error that the 51 members carry, so the scored distribution counts it twice.

The evidence for the double count is mild, so the effect size to expect is small. Experiment 111's tuned factors are [1.0, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9] (0.9 is the floor of its grid in the three bands from 24 hours up), and moving them changed the score by 0.003 to 0.013 points. A factor of 0.9 is a variance of 0.81 of the table, whereas a double count of half the table's variance would force about 0.7. So the double count is real in the code and probably modest in the numbers.

Literature. Ensemble model output statistics (Gneiting et al. (2005)) fit a predictive variance that is an affine function of the ensemble variance. Bayesian model averaging (Raftery et al. (2005); Fraley et al. (2010) for exchangeable members) and kernel dressing (Bröcker and Smith (2008)) centre one kernel on each member. The dressing paper fits the kernel width on the errors of the individual members, not of the ensemble mean, for the reason N8 tests: the mean's error holds the spread already. Arm MP is that dressing, with the proxy-driven residual table as the kernel. Rasp and Lerch (2018) is the neural form, not used here.

Why members help a demand forecast in particular. GAM-K's heating response has a hinge near 15.5 °C, so equal temperature spread gives a large demand spread on a cold night and almost none in mild weather. Passing members through GAM-K captures that heteroscedasticity, which one residual table cannot.

Overlap with CAL. The tail-calibration plan (CAL, postponed on 2026-10-20) listed arms MP, MO, and MM as its fourth method. N8 owns those arms, and CAL's plan has dropped them, which leaves CAL four planned contrasts. CAL's arm KE (ENS spread as a width input) is a rival way to use the same spread and stays CAL's. N8 does not depend on CAL, and CAL's step of tuning a passing MP further depends on N8.

Builds on experiments 111 (GAM-K, tuned factors, ENS store), 114 (T-all-K), and 115 (W1). N8 changes only the spread; the median-defining mean, the filter, and the fits are experiment 111's. The Kalman filter is the level-and-anomaly filter as it stands on main, which experiment 118 kept over its 14-weight filter. N8 does not redesign the filter, and the Kalman-on-ensemble-residuals arm uses it unchanged.

Experiment 119 asks for a plain recalibration of GAM-K's quantiles. Arm K0-w (the stored table re-tuned on the wider factor grid) is that recalibration, so N8 also answers 119's next step.

docs.title: Data on local disk, and the periods
docs.text:
Only data already on the workstation is read. No fetch, no AWS.

  • ENS store: experiment 111's work/ens_store/<site>.npz holds 821 daily 00:00 UTC runs (2024-04-01 to 2026-06-30), 51 members, 702 half-hours, for D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16, and D18 (centre box only). Extraction counts usable members per run (usable_members()) and prints any run under 51 (experiment 111 dropped member 36 where its shortwave value was missing). Every statistic uses the usable members of that run. The longer Source Cooperative ENS history is not used.
  • Nothing on or after 2026-07-01 is read. Rows whose valid time falls on or after 2026-07-01 are dropped, which removes the far leads of the last runs, and the 2026-06-30 run is excluded, as experiment 111 excluded it.
  • Sites: the decision sites D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 (all five are needed for the gate; the verdict counts sites improving at 4 of 5); D9 beside them. D15, D18, and the MVA Primaries are out.
Period Role Odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06 tuning: the proxy residual table, factors, and s Even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06 replicate: never used to choose a setting 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29, the 292 runs scored: the verdict

A tuning or replicate row needs both its origin and its valid time in the period's months. The replicate months are interleaved with the tuning months, not out of time: the residual table for August to December 2024 is fitted partly on data from 2025, so a replicate agreement shows robustness to which months were held out, not a forecast made with only past data. The scored year is out of time, but its table is up to two years stale. The verdict rule treats the scored year as the test and the replicate months as a second, weaker check. The same holds for K0 and K0-w.

The data holds two independent winters, and neither period holds a whole one. The replicate months hold December and February of 2024-25, the tuning months hold November, January, and March, and the scored year holds all of 2025-26. Experiment 111's scored-year tails were read before this plan, so the scored year is not blind for K0; every setting of every other arm is chosen on the tuning months.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Screening tier: no new GAM fit and no refit. Every arm reuses experiment 111's monthly GAM-K fits, pinned capacity, ENS calibration, solar shrink, filter hyperparameters, and ENS store. The 51 member means and the filter's level and anomaly are cached once per run, and every arm is a post-processing step on the cache. One seed (the fits are deterministic).

Arm Centres Residual table around each centre Role K0 51 corrected members ensemble-mean residuals, 111's factors, mixture benchmark, reproduced K0-w 51 corrected members as K0, factor re-tuned on MP's grid fair control: is the double count only a scale error? MP 51 corrected members proxy-driven residuals, factor on the wide grid, mixture decision arm MP-s members rescaled about their mean by s as MP spread-scaled variant MM corrected ensemble mean K0's table, factor re-tuned, no mixture exploratory MO 51 corrected members none exploratory: weather error only MP-1 as MP every factor 1 exploratory: MP with no tuned factor
  • The wide factor grid is {0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5}, used for K0-w, MP, MM, and MP-s. K0 keeps 111's grid {0.9, 1.0, 1.15, 1.3} only as the stored benchmark. C1 is MP minus K0-w. If K0-w matches MP, the double count is a scale error and no member-aware residual table is needed.
  • MP's residual table. Per tuning-month origin, the proxy cache (the control member of the latest run, NWP lead 9 to 33 hours) supplies the weather, and the forecast is made with the filter's level and anomaly at each lead, through forecast_frame with a zero-spread frame, not through proxy_residual_stream (which has no filter and no lead dependence). The residual is observed minus that forecast; its centred quantiles per hour band, quarter, and lead band form the table. Lead bands are experiment 111's four, in hours from the origin (0–24, 24–48, 48–144, 144–168).
  • MP-s replaces each member's mean μ_m by μ̄ + s·(μ_m − μ̄), with s per lead band from {0.8, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0}. The ensemble mean does not move. s is chosen first, with the factor held at MP's value, by the mean pinball at q05, q95, q01, and q99 on the tuning months; the factor is then re-tuned given s. The two trade off along a flat ridge, so the report prints the score surface for each lead band, and a tie goes to the smaller s. s above 1 means the member spread is too small for demand at that lead band, a hypothesis here and not a finding.

Operational definitions. σ_w² is the variance across members of the corrected member means at a target. σ_m² is the variance of the residual table's 11 atoms, weighted by their probability masses (the 11 levels are unevenly spaced, so the weights are the mass each atom carries under mixture_quantiles). Every variance and coverage statement below is computed on the same 11-atom mixture that is scored, never on an analytic mixture.

Mixture tails. The mixture of 11-atom members is a distribution whose lowest and highest atoms carry 3% mass each, and the mixture's q01 and q99 cannot lie beyond the members' own q01 and q99 atoms. So q01 and q99 coverage is capped for every arm alike, including K0. The tail rows therefore compare arms under the same definition and are not a claim about the 99% tail of the true distribution. The report prints the fraction of rows whose actual lies beyond the most extreme atom of the whole mixture, for each arm.

docs.title: Known-answer gate (blocking, on the tuning months, before any replicate or scored row)
docs.text:
A failed blocking test stops scoring; if it cannot be fixed inside the experiment, the verdict is inconclusive. Tests 1 and 2 use a synthetic twin of each decision site's tuning-month runs.

The twin. The truth weather W is ERA5 temperature and CAMS irradiance. Member weather is W_m = W̄ + e_m with e_m zero-mean, standard deviation σ_w(lead) known (temperature 0.6 K at 12 hours rising to 2.0 K at 7 days; irradiance ratio 0.04 rising to 0.20), and W = W̄ + e_0 is a fresh draw, so truth and members are exchangeable by construction. The twin's analysis proxy is W plus an error of 0.1 K. Fake demand is GAM-K's prediction on W plus AR(1) noise η with known σ_m (the fitted φ and σ_z). Because the twin is exchangeable by construction, it confirms the arithmetic and the code, and not that the real ECMWF ensemble behaves so. The exact predictive distribution is simulated by 500 further draws of W, and the 11-atom mixture of the 500 draws' fake members is the reference.

  1. Variance transfer (blocking). The mixture's σ_w², pooled over all tuning-month runs of a site (a 51-member sd is only about 10% accurate on one run), is within 10% of the 500-draw variance of GAM-K(W) per lead band, in every cell with Monte-Carlo sd above 0.5 points. Pass at all five sites. The ratio is also printed for cold-night cells (ERA5 temperature below 3 °C), where the hinge makes the transfer largest.
  2. Known σ_w and σ_m are recovered, and the double count appears at the predicted size (blocking). (a) The operational σ_w² and σ_m² are within 10% of the injected values per lead band. (b) K0's total variance divided by MP's total variance equals the analytic ratio (2σ_w² + σ_m²)/(σ_w² + σ_m²), computed from the injected values and the 11-atom mixture, within 10% per lead band; the twin's analytic ratio is printed before the real arms run, and the central 90% interval's over-coverage that follows is the expected value, not a fixed 3 points. (c) MP's coverage is in band in at least 14 of 16 cells. (d) MO under-covers at q05 and q95 by more than the analytic amount minus 2 points. (e) With the members' weather spread halved against the truth, the true demand-space factor s* is computed from the 500-draw reference (it is not 2, because the hinge is non-linear), s* must lie inside the s grid, and MP-s recovers s* within 25% in at least 3 of 4 lead bands.
  3. Reproduction. Rebuilding K0 from the cache reproduces experiment 111's stored gamk_tuning_<site>.parquet quantiles to 1e-4. mixture_quantiles of 51 identical members equals a single member's quantiles. MP with a zero residual table equals MO. MP-s with s = 1 equals MP. MP's table fitted on an all-zero residual stream is exactly zero.
  4. Causality. Changing any actual from a half-hour that ended after τ minus 3.5 hours, or any ENS run issued after τ, leaves every arm's forecast at τ unchanged. The cache records the fit's cut per run, and the pinned-capacity vintage date is printed against each origin. The residual table, factors, and s use the tuning months; for the replicate rows that is not past-only data (see "Data on local disk, and the periods").
  5. Mean and order. The mean over members of each arm's centre equals the cached corrected ensemble mean to 1e-9 (for MP-s with s = 1 and for MP); quantiles are non-decreasing after every transformation, at every row.

Reported, not blocking: the rank histogram of ERA5 temperature (and irradiance) among the calibrated members per lead band, as a diagnostic of under-dispersion. It is new code (below).

docs.title: What counts as calibrated
docs.text:
A cell is calibrated if its coverage lies within nominal ± 2.5·√(p(1 − p)/n_eff), with n_eff the number of distinct (site, local valid date) pairs in the cell, the rule of the CAL plan. A cell is one of four tail levels in one of four lead bands, 16 in all. A calibrated forecast passes all 16 cells only about 80% of the time per period (CAL plan), so "all 16" is not the target. The target is at least 14 of 16 cells in band, and no more failing cells than K0-w. The gate measures the pass rate on the twin (test 2c) and the report prints it.

Variance accounting (reported). Per arm, site, lead band, and season, the variance of the mixture splits into σ_w² and σ_m², beside the variance of the actual error of the ensemble mean. The report prints whether K0's total follows 2σ_w² + σ_m² and MP's σ_w² + σ_m² on the real data.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Per arm and period, on rows shared across a contrast's arms, outside the hand-filtered switching events, with the all-rows score beside; the four lead bands, 12–36 hours, and D+1 (15.5 to 39 hours from the 09:00 UTC origin):

  • Quantile score over the 11 levels (points). It approximates the CRPS by a sum over unevenly spaced levels, so it is called the quantile score, never "the CRPS".
  • Coverage of the central 80% and 90% intervals and at q01, q05, q95, and q99, with the band above, from studies.tail_calibration's coverage and pinball tables.
  • Tail pinball at q01, q05, q95, and q99 (same module), and the mean over the four.
  • The mean absolute error of the median beside each contrast.
  • New metric code, in a separate module PR to packages/studies, with tests and a mutation pass: the rank histogram, the fair CRPS of the 51 members (MO only, reported in its own table, not beside the quantile score), and the tail-weighted CRPS of the quantile mixtures (the upper and lower tail weights of Gneiting and Ranjan (2011)). Scores are proper (Gneiting and Raftery (2007)), so a sharper calibrated arm wins. studies.tail_calibration has none of these today. The module PR gets one Sonnet code review and does not merge before the Opus review. Tuning and the known-answer gate run before it merges, and no replicate-year or scored-year fit runs until its Sonnet review is triaged.
  • No curtailment cost (experiment 87 found no event that could rank forecasts).

docs.title: Winter and the operator's cold nights
docs.text:
Winter is November to March, local time, and comes first in the write-up. It is five month blocks in the scored year and two in the replicate months (December, February). Month-block bootstrap on two non-adjacent blocks is empty, so the replicate-months winter rows have no interval. The scored winter's intervals resample days within months, in blocks of 7 days, and are descriptive. The decision is on the full year.

The cold-snap rule is fixed now, before any score is read. A cold day is a local calendar day whose ERA5 daily-mean 2 m temperature at the site's grid box is at or below the 10th percentile of that site's November to March daily means over 2019-09-01 to 2024-06-30. A cold snap is a run of two or more consecutive cold days. The thresholds and episode lists are computed from ERA5 alone and hashed into decisions.json before any arm is scored. With about two winters the count is probably 3 to 8 episodes per site, so cold-snap rows carry no interval.

Which direction the cold nights should move. Experiment 111's night band (00:00 to 05:59 local) under-covered at q95 (92.3% in the planner's read of experiment 111's stored predictions) and D5 in winter more so (89.0%), while the pooled tails are near nominal. Removing the double count narrows the general band, which would worsen those cells. The members' own heteroscedastic spread widens the band on cold nights, because the hinge turns their temperature spread into a large demand spread. So MP is expected to be narrower than K0 in mild weather and at least as wide on cold nights. The cold-night figure includes K0-w, to separate this from a scale change.

The operator-visible figure shows, for each decision site, the cold nights of the scored winter: actual demand (in points of effective capacity) against the D+1 median and 90% band of K0-w and MP, with the nights outside each band marked and the Economy 7 step visible at D5, D10, and D16, plus a table of night-band tail coverage per arm. The nights shown are fixed by the cold-snap rule, never by an arm's score.

docs.title: Planned contrasts and margins
docs.text:
Three planned contrasts: C1, C2, and C4, each in the replicate months and the scored year. The quantile-score non-inferiority test uses 95% month-resampled intervals (studies.bootstrap, paired across arms, 3 seeds), because the +0.02 margin was set against a 95% half-width of about 0.016 (experiment 111's sister contrast). The tail-pinball and calibration reads use 98.3% intervals (Bonferroni over three contrasts), each period separately.

  • C1 (decision), the double count: MP minus K0-w. MP minus the stored K0 is reported beside it.
  • C2, two coherent designs compared: MP minus MM changes the centres (members against their mean) and the residual table (proxy against ensemble-mean) together, so it compares designs and does not isolate the members.
  • C4, the spread-scaled variant: MP-s minus MP.

Exploratory at 95%: MP minus MO (the model-error spread is needed; its size is too large to inform a decision), MP-1 minus MP, D9, 12–36 hours, the best arm against Xlag-d, X-nl+K, and BG2, and the winter and cold-snap rows.

Non-inferiority margin +0.02 points on the quantile score over 0.5 to 168 hours: above the sister contrast's noise (−0.008, half-width about 0.016) and below the 0.03 that W1 and N3 + N4 treat as the smallest gain worth porting.

Power. At a 95% half-width of about 0.016 on the quantile score, a score change under 0.02 cannot be told from zero, and the double count's expected effect (a factor of 0.9 against 1.0, a 0.003 to 0.013 points change in experiment 111) is below that. So the verdict will rest on calibration cells and tail pinball, and a small gain is the likeliest positive outcome. The report states the detectable tail-pinball effect from the bootstrap half-width before reading the contrast.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
Written before any fit; each line can fail, and none overrides the decision rule.

  • Variance ratio. Weather error grows with lead, so K0's total variance divided by MP's is near 1 at 0–24 hours (1.05 to 1.2) and approaches 2 at 144–168 hours (1.4 to 1.8), if σ_w² is large against σ_m² there. MP's central 90% interval is 2 to 6% narrower than K0-w's at 0–48 hours and 10 to 25% narrower at 144–168 hours.
  • K0-w. The wide grid moves K0's factor to 0.7 to 0.8 at 144–168 hours and 0.8 to 0.9 elsewhere; K0-w captures most of MP's narrowing at long leads, and MP differs from K0-w mainly in cold weather and at long leads.
  • C1. MP has its factor at 0.9 to 1.15 and is in band in 14 or more of 16 cells; tail pinball falls by 0.002 to 0.01 against K0-w; the quantile score is within ±0.01 of K0-w.
  • C2. MP minus MM is −0.01 to −0.04 in the quantile score, mostly in the tails and in winter.
  • C4. s is 1.0 to 1.25 at 0–48 hours and 1.0 elsewhere; MP-s minus MP within ±0.01, no lead band at a grid edge.
  • Cold nights. MP's night-band q95 coverage is within 1 to 3 points of K0-w's, closer to 95%.
  • Gate. Test 1's ratio is 0.9 to 1.1 in every cell, with the largest departure on cold nights.
  • Run time. 2 to 3 hours on 6 cores.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
The verdict reads C1, because the question is whether the member-aware residual table beats a re-scaled version of today's. An arm passes in a period if it has at least 14 of 16 cells in band and no more failing cells than K0-w, the upper end of its 95% quantile-score interval against K0-w is at most +0.02 points, and its mean tail pinball against K0-w is below zero.

  • supported: the gate passed; MP passes in the scored year and in the replicate months; the 98.3% interval of MP's tail pinball minus K0-w's lies wholly below zero in the scored year; and 4 of 5 decision sites improve in the scored year.
  • small gain: MP passes in both periods and the tail-pinball interval includes zero.
  • partly supported: MP passes in the scored year only; or MP passes pooled but its night-band q95 coverage is further from nominal than K0-w's; or MP beats the stored K0 but not K0-w.
  • refuted: MP's quantile-score interval against K0-w lies wholly above +0.02 in either period.
  • not supported: both periods' tail-pinball intervals lie within ±0.002 of zero and MP and K0-w have the same number of cells in band.
  • inconclusive: anything else, including K0-w already at 14 or more cells in both periods with MP indistinguishable (the double count is then a scale error, reported as the finding), or a gate test that cannot be fixed.

The best arm is the passing arm with the lowest scored-year tail pinball; ties within 0.002 go to the simplest (K0-w, MP, MP-s). Handed on: a passing MP becomes GAM-K's spread candidate, and CAL (if restarted) tunes it further.

docs.title: Audit before merge: the seven triggers
docs.text:
"Checks" bullets: median minus mean forecast per site and arm; mean error beside each contrast.

  1. A control fails: any gate test, K0's reproduction of 2.800, the nesting identities.
  2. A contradiction: the variance accounting against 2σ_w² + σ_m²; MP's factor far above 1 (the proxy table too narrow, because the proxy is a control member and not an analysis); C1 against a later CAL run of the same arm.
  3. Quantile score and mean error of the median disagree in sign, or the median moves by over 0.01 points.
  4. Leaving one site out flips a calibration pass, a sign, or the verdict.
  5. A nested arm beats its container: MP-s losing to MP at s = 1 after tuning; MO beating MP.
  6. Interval width: C1's score interval more than twice or under half as wide as the sister's.
  7. A later design depends on an unreplicated result: MP adopted from one period.

docs.title: Substation cards (Provisional: fitted to past weather and forecast on ENS, screening run)
docs.text: One card per decision site (D9 beside), showing only what experiment 111's cards cannot: the proxy table's width against the ensemble-mean table's width per hour band (the double count made visible); the members' spread by lead band, winter against summer; s and the factor by lead band; tail coverage for K0-w and MP; and example D+1 forecasts for the second Monday of July, October, January, and April (weeks beginning 2025-07-14, 2025-10-13, 2026-01-12, and 2026-04-13, fixed now, before any score is read), median and 80% and 90% bands against the observed series. The demand panels are experiment 111's cards, linked.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: D-labels only, with dates, for D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16. D15 and D18 are not used. Never name or guess D15's generator, and show no topology or substation name.

docs.title: What the write-up must contain
docs.text:
The take-home says whether the weather error was counted twice, how much of the fix is a scale change that K0-w also gets, and what happens on cold winter nights.

  • Order: the winter analysis and the cold-night figure first, then the tails table (coverage and pinball at q01, q05, q95, and q99, every arm, per lead band, both periods, cells outside the band in bold), then the headline chart (cells in band and mean tail pinball, with intervals).
  • Figures, raw data first: a winter and a summer week per site; the variance accounting; reliability diagrams per lead band; the rank histograms; the gate (twin coverage for K0, K0-w, MP, MO); conditional coverage by site, season, and hour band.
  • Absolute scores of every arm and reference at D+1 and over 0.5 to 168 hours, on shared rows.
  • Caveats: K0's scored-year tails were read before the plan; the proxy is a control member and not an analysis; interleaved months; a stale table in the scored year; two winters; five substations; the capped q01 and q99; the assumed 3.5-hour delay; hindsight masks; the ENS calibration shifts the ensemble mean and not each member; the twin's weather error is simulated.

docs.title: Compute and module
docs.text:
CPU only, 6 cores, under 8 GB per script (one site at a time; mixtures in chunks of 20,000 cases; the member-mean cache is about 20 MB per site and period). GAM-K's hinge basis is not a linear sum, but 51 members per run is a few milliseconds of numpy, so a GPU gains nothing. Estimate: the member-mean cache about 10 minutes per period; the proxy pass over the tuning months about 10 minutes; the factor and s grids are the slow step, since each pair re-sorts 51×11 atoms per case over roughly 170,000 tuning cases, so 20 to 40 minutes per arm; the gate's twin about 20 minutes. Total 2 to 3 hours. Cut first: MP-1, MM, D9.

One new module, no change to a reviewed one. studies.dp_ens, ens_members.mixture_quantiles, tail_calibration, and bootstrap are on origin/main, and the experiment's scripts import them. The rank histogram, the fair CRPS, and the tail-weighted CRPS go into a new module in packages/studies (the separate PR above). The member rescaling and the twin live in the experiment folder, which has no tests of its own scripts, so the gate's own checks (tests 3 to 5) cover them. If MP is adopted, forecast_run needs a way to take a proxy-fitted table, which is a further module PR.

docs.title: Size: the five triggers
docs.text:
• Changes what gets stored: no (private files only).
  • Touches the production serving path: no.
  • Touches a degradation rule: no.
  • Admits more than one defensible design: yes, narrowly (the residual table's fit, the member rescaling), each pre-registered, every arm a post-processing step.
  • Spans code whose callers could not be named without searching: no.

Medium. One Sonnet plan review (done), one Sonnet code review of the experiment's scripts for leakage (every fit and table cut at the origin's training end), one Sonnet write-up review, and the module PR's own Sonnet review; the Opus reviews run later. The mutation pass covers the new metric module.

docs.title: Run order
docs.text: Code; gate tests 3 to 5; member-mean cache and the proxy pass on the tuning months; tuning (K0-w, MP, MP-s); gate tests 1 and 2; replicate months; scored year; variance accounting; write-up and cards.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, S1: do cheap additions to GAM-K lower the day-ahead score?
docs.text:
Take-home: no cheap addition showed a gain we can trust. Of thirteen screens (nine in the first family, four exploratory), none earned the label gain. Seven were undecidable (the interval was wider than the margin, or too few calendar months were available to resample), two were tie (A-free and D-sch), two were not powered (S-ewma and S-mm, whose gate failed), one was worse (W-basis), and G-skf is inconclusive. The result narrows the search to E-sol on a larger row set and rules out a learned year cycle as a forecast term. Past weather was used throughout, so every number is a ceiling for ENS weather. Verdict: inconclusive.

The question was whether adding one cheap term to T-all-K (experiment 114's day-ahead model with the Kalman filter) lowers the quantile score on November-to-March rows. The scored year is 2025-07 to 2026-06 on five decision substations, with the penalty weight (1.0) taken from experiment 114 and the filter re-tuned per arm on the tuning year.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (T-all-K, per site): 0.0 at all five substations, because the residual spread is centred.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast: the sign of the mean absolute error of the mean forecast matches the sign of the quantile-score contrast for all thirteen screens.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 1 (a control failed): G-skf's power gate failed (it recovered the regime on 98% of half-hours but its state error was 0.38 above the plain filter's, interval -1.9 to +6.1), and W-basis's injected-effect gate moved the wrong way. Trigger 2: F-mix predicted tails moving towards nominal and the cold-snap score within noise, and got +0.078 points. An Opus audit ran (a fresh Opus agent, findings below). Triggers 3 to 7 did not fire (no leave-one-out run was needed, because no contrast is a gain).
  • Reproduction: B0 equals fit_gam to 3e-13, T-all equals experiment 114's stored scored-year forecast to 1e-4 points, and every appending arm with zeroed columns equals T-all to 1e-11 points.

docs.title: Audit findings and triage
docs.text:
• Intervals resample only 3 to 6 calendar months, so at 99.44% the bounds are close to the smallest and largest month means. Accepted: X9 (F-mix) and X13 (W-stn) are relabelled undecidable (too few month blocks), and F-mix's +0.078 rests on January 2026 and on D11 (+0.29; the other four sites range from -0.06 to +0.09).
  • X3 and X4 were labelled tie though gate 3 said not powered. Accepted: both are now not powered, and the report applies the gate downgrade.
  • W-basis's gate-3 failure is a fault in the gate. The truth blends T-all and W-basis with a weight s of 0.30 to 0.92, but W-basis replaces T-all's harmonics, so it can fit that truth only at s = 1. C-hw (and C-wind) replace columns too, so C-hw's "not powered" label is suspect. Accepted as a caveat, not re-run.
  • G-skf has no coding error. On its own model it beat the plain filter in 98 of 100 draws (median -1.85); two blow-up draws (+186, +33) fail the mean-based gate, and the fitted matrix reads level shifts as outliers, which freezes the state. The cap at inconclusive stands.
  • Confirmed: X2, X8, X9, and X11 re-derived from the stored predictions match to 4 decimals; the spread is median-centred with no previous-year bias; F-mix and G-skf feed the filter the same replica residuals; no leakage found.
  • Minor: W-basis's basis cache is keyed by cut, so within a gate-3 worker the 2022-07 basis comes from its first synthetic draw. Left as is.
