    • Noted, no change: the detector's timestamps sit one half-hour later than the site's grid timestamps. The forecast-error series and the scored actual shift together, so no number moves.

  • Leakage review (one Sonnet reviewer, code only). It found no way for a deployable arm to see data later than its forecast time. The filter runs forward, the 96-half-hour onset lag matches the alarm statistic's window, known_from is the stamp at which the end statistic is computable, and tuning reads only the tuning months. Its other findings and their triage:

    • Accepted, as a limit on the controls (not re-run): the placebo prior is shifted by whole weeks, so it seldom falls on the scored rows, which sit around events. "Matches the placebo" therefore shows that a late alarm has no measurable gain over an unrelated prior, and the page's claim stays at that. The variance-inflation control also differs from S-KF in both alarm times and the likelihood update, so it does not isolate the update alone.
    • Accepted, as a limit on the rows (not re-run): the "after a causal alarm" rows count any alarm within 2 hours of a transfer, including repeat and return-step alarms, so they describe cases where the detector fired near a real transfer. They exclude the cost of false alarms.
    • Accepted, code only: the unused step_points and age_days arrays are removed. They fed no arm, so no number moves.
    • Noted: the scored-score files are reused if they exist, so a re-tune needs them deleted first; the chosen settings (prior 0.5, multiplier 4) were the ones used for the scored files. The multiplier 4 sits at the lower edge of the grid (4 to 256), so a smaller multiplier was not tried.
    • Not checked by the reviewer: where experiment 138's classifier and threshold were fitted.

docs.title: Departures from the plan
docs.text:
• S-KF's prior is binary (0.5 while an alarm is active, 0 otherwise), not a logistic function of the detector's score. S-F (plain features) was not built, and the real year was not scored (C3 and C5 have no number), because the stop rule fired on the tuning months. The placebo and variance-inflation controls were run on the simulated data only.
  • The causal alarm is known from 96 half-hours (48 hours) after the step starts, a conservative stand-in for the statistic's 24-hour window plus the 24-hour peak test. The planned unit test (truncating the forecast-error series and checking the score is unchanged) was not written, so the claim that the alarm time is causal rests on this lag and on the end rule's own known_from. A leak would favour the detector, which makes the negative result stronger, not weaker.
  • Intervals are 95%, not the planned family-wise level, because only one contrast carries a verdict. The simulated data use the ERA5-driven residuals of experiment 130 (cleaner than live residuals), the fast-path injection, and K0's uncertainty bands, which were not refitted per arm.
  • "Within 48 hours of an alarm" means target valid time from the stamp at which the alarm is known. The detector and the moved megawatts are those of experiment 147's headline draw. The two longer-prior arms are post hoc.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: A filter that holds the transfer's step flat at every lead is wrong once the transfer ends. An experiment could test a correction for a detected transfer that decays toward zero over the typical transfer duration (from the logged operations), on the same simulated data, with the true-interval arm as its ceiling and the causal alarm as the deployable arm. It could also test the alarm at the shorter lag that a 24-hour step statistic allows if the peak test is dropped.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit)
docs.text:
Question. How much does the switching detector help when its output is fed into the forecast itself? Earlier results measured the ceiling only: a perfect detector lowers the best guess's score by 0.42% (experiment 44), and true moved megawatts close 83% of the gap that the refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC) closes 16% of (experiment 88). RO-NC is the detector of experiment 130. Lab conditions are allowed (maintainer, 2026-10-18); every shortcut is named in the write-up.

Base forecast. GAM-K member forecasts and the K0 filter as experiment 134 stores them (monthly refits from experiment 111). The best-guess assembly of experiment 136 is not merged; if it is ready before the real-year scoring, the same arms are re-run on it, labelled post hoc.

Arms.

  • K0 — GAM-K's filter with no detector input (control).
  • S-KF — the filter becomes a two-regime mixture per hour band. Regime N ("normal running arrangement") uses the fitted level variance q; regime S ("switched") uses q times a multiplier chosen on the tuning months. The prior probability of S per half-hour is a logistic function of the causal RO-NC score, and the filter's likelihood updates it. The correction is the posterior-weighted mean of the two regimes' corrections.
  • S-F — K0 plus a regression of the residual on two causal features: event age (hours since the causal onset, capped at 7 days) and signed step size. Fitted on the tuning months.
  • S-HE — S-KF with the detector's hindsight end (the interval end from experiment 130's end rule). NOT DEPLOYABLE. It is the ceiling for the causal arms.
  • S-ORACLE — S-KF whose prior is 1 inside the true transfer interval and 0 outside, from the injected truth (and from the logged events in the real year). NOT DEPLOYABLE. Upper bound.
  • Causal onset-only signal is the deployable input. The harness takes the signal as a table of (series, half-hour, score, signed step), so the causal live end rule of experiment 140 can be swapped in later without changing the arms.

Causal score. RO-NC's step statistic compares the mean of the residual after a stamp with the mean before it, so a score stamped at the onset has seen up to 24 hours of the future. The deployable score is therefore re-indexed: the score at stamp s uses only residuals ending no later than s minus 3.5 hours (the telemetry delay), the alarm is stamped when the "after" window is full and not at the onset, and the peak, partner, and veto tests use the same cut. A unit test truncates the residual stream at s minus 3.5 hours and requires the score at s to be unchanged. Only S-HE and S-ORACLE may read onset-stamped scores.

New filter core (a deliverable). Experiment 134's filter is single-regime, so S-KF needs a two-regime core in this folder: a per-stamp prior input, a level-variance multiplier for regime S, a posterior update from the two regimes' likelihoods, and moment-matched mixing of state and covariance. Gate: S-KF with the prior fixed at 0 reproduces K0 to numerical tolerance. The regime-S multiplier grid is 4, 16, 64, and 256 times q, chosen on the tuning months.

Known answer first (injected world). Draw transfers of known size and timing in the real residual stream using experiment 130's injection harness (headline band: moved load 25% or more of the receiving load, lasting over 1 day; other bands descriptively), with injection seeds disjoint from the tuning months. The frozen GAM-K forecast is not refitted, so adding the moved megawatts to the stream (experiment 130's fast path) is valid for the filters. Scoring uses actuals plus the signed moved megawatts at the donor and each receiver, never the original actuals, normalised by the same effective capacity as the score. The spread is shared across arms (K0's), so every contrast is a location-only difference. The scorable mask is recomputed on the injected world: injected rows stay in, and logged events overlapping an injection window are dropped. Two gates: an injected event of size zero reproduces K0 exactly, and check (a): S-KF's posterior probability of S passes 0.5 within 24 hours of the causal alarm for at least 60% of detected headline-band events.

Controls.

  • Placebo. S-KF with the causal score shifted by a random whole number of weeks within each series, which keeps the alarm rate, durations, and hour-of-day structure. Predicted gain: about zero.
  • Variance-inflation control. K0 with regime S's multiplier applied at the same fraction of stamps but unrelated to events (the placebo prior, with no likelihood update), to separate knowing when from simply adapting faster.
  • False alarms. Report the alarm rate per series per year, the detection-delay distribution, and alarms on Economy 7 winter mornings and evenings.
  • S-F is fitted on the injected tuning world (disjoint seeds), because the real tuning months hold few events; the number of events is stated.

Real year. The same arms on the real scored year. The real year can support only "no harm" (C3) and a descriptive gain near events (C5), because experiment 44 bounds the whole-year gain at about 0.42%. Logged events are used only descriptively. The expected whole-year change is computed from the injected-world gain and experiment 44's event frequency and compared with C3's interval width before the verdict.

Rows and scoring. fold_a_daily_gap_v1; the five decision substations of experiment 134 plus D9 beside them; leads 0.5 to 168 h with D+1 (15.5 to 39 h) beside, and the gain by lead band; winter (November to March) and cold nights (daily mean under about 3 C) separately; tail calibration, with q95 and q99 coverage and pinball loss on cold nights reported separately (q95 coverage was 73% to 78% in experiment 125); intervals resample whole calendar months; absolute scores for K0, climatology, the manual heuristic, and (when ready) the best guess shown beside every contrast. "Within 48 hours of an onset" means the target valid time. A pooled figure weights the six sites equally. Labels for the sites follow experiment 134; no metered-generator series is used.

Contrasts (family-wise level 5%, Bonferroni across C1, C2, C3, and C5).

  • C1: S-KF minus K0, injected world, target rows within 48 hours of a causal alarm on a headline-band transfer.
  • C2: S-F minus K0, same rows.
  • C3: S-KF minus K0, real scored year, all rows outside logged events (non-inferiority).
  • C4: share of the K0-to-S-ORACLE gap closed by S-KF, injected world (descriptive).
  • C5: S-KF minus K0, real scored year, rows within 48 hours of a causal alarm or of a logged event.
  • Placebo minus K0 and variance-inflation control minus K0 are descriptive, and S-KF must beat both on C1 for supported.

Decision rule. The threshold is set by the cost of porting: a two-regime filter plus a detector pipeline step is a new component. Before the verdict, the plan fixes the minimum detectable effect as the half-width of C3's month-resampled interval.

  • supported: C1's interval is wholly below zero, S-KF beats the placebo and the variance-inflation control on C1, C3's upper end is at most +0.005 points, and the q95 and q99 coverage on cold nights is within 2 points of K0's.
  • not supported: C1's interval includes zero or lies above it, or S-KF fails to beat the placebo.
  • inconclusive: otherwise, including a C3 interval wider than +0.005 points.

C1 is an easy test by construction (large injected steps). A supported verdict therefore means the mechanism works in the lab, and the write-up says plainly that the real-year benefit is bounded by experiment 44 and judged by C3 and C5.

Stop rule. If check (a) fails, or C1's point estimate is above zero on the tuning months, stop before scoring the real year, record not supported or inconclusive, and write up what the failure rules out. Compute cap: 6 cores at one thread each, 16 GB per job.

Compute. CPU only (the corrections are small filters on cached forecasts). systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue, 6 workers, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.

Lab shortcuts, named. ERA5-driven residuals in the detector (as in experiment 130), which are cleaner than live ENS-driven residuals and so inflate C1; hindsight end in S-HE; true megawatts in S-ORACLE; fast-path injection.

Data processing. Reads cleaned_power_time_series with the substation_zero flags treated as kept, as experiment 132 did.

docs.title: Reviews planned
docs.text: A Sonnet review of the plan is triaged above (leakage of the score, the new filter core, scoring of injected actuals, the vacuous verdict rule, and the missing controls were accepted). Sonnet then reviews the code for leakage (the detector score at a half-hour may use residuals ending no later than that half-hour minus the 3.5-hour telemetry delay), then the write-up. One Opus review only with the maintainer's approval.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: a small sequence model on GAM-K's recent residuals
docs.text: Take-home: a small neural network trained on one year of GAM-K's forecast errors did not learn to adapt when those errors change, so we did not score it. GAM-K is our demand model with a Kalman filter (a method that updates a forecast from its recent errors). We added a known change to real errors, either a +3-point step for 8 weeks or a +3-point shift on Saturday evenings, and checked whether the network, trained on unchanged errors, corrected for the change. It recovered none of it, in two architectures, and the sign was wrong for the step. The experiment therefore stops at this check, and the verdict is inconclusive: the day-ahead forecast score was not measured, and the comparison with the Kalman filter and recipe R (subtract 0.75 times the last 14 days' mean error) was not made. Whether more history would help is untested.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Can a small neural network, trained on the stored residuals of GAM-K, do the job of the Kalman filter and recipe R, and does it give better tails? GAM-K is the convex demand model with a Kalman filter on ECMWF ensemble weather (experiment 111). Recipe R subtracts 0.75 times the mean of the last 14 days' errors by half-hour (experiment 115); the same-weekday profile added only 0.011 points. The network pools the substations with a substation embedding, so patterns shared between substations can be learned. Sequence models of recent errors follow Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (1997) and Cho et al. (2014) (the gated recurrent unit used here); the pinball loss is the standard training loss of quantile regression (Koenker and Bassett, 1978).

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
This section is the plan as pre-registered; the gate failed, so only the samples, the gate fits, and the tuning-month fits ran (see Results).

  • Substations. The six substations whose member forecasts experiment 111 stored (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16, and D9). Experiment 111's ensemble store holds seven series (those six and D18), so the other DP series have no stored GAM-K member forecasts, and no demand model is refitted. D9 is trained on but reported beside the five decision substations.
  • One sample per (substation, run). 810 runs per substation, of which about 530 precede the scored year: about 3,200 training samples, and about 1,100 for the odd-months-only fit. Consecutive samples share 13 of 14 input days, so the independent information is about one year of days per substation. Target: the 48 half-hours of day D+1 (leads 15.5 to 39 hours), as actual minus K0's median forecast.
  • Clock. Every day, the day type, the holiday flag, and the output index use the UTC day and the UTC half-hour (0 to 47), the day D+1 being a UTC day. No local clock enters.
  • Input. The 14 UTC days before the origin's day, plus a 15th partial day, as vectors of 48 half-hour residuals from SiteData.stream (observed minus the chained GAM fit, driven by the analysis proxy, ending at the origin's latest usable reading, 3.5 hours before the 09:00 UTC origin) with a reading mask; each day carries its day type (five types, as in experiment 134) and a holiday-like flag. Missing readings are zero with mask zero. The target day enters through its day type, holiday-like flag, Christmas-window flag, and the calibrated ECMWF ensemble-mean temperature and irradiance at its 48 half-hours (published by the origin, so available at forecast time; past days use the analysis proxy, as in experiment 111). The target day's actuals are never an input.
  • Network. A one-layer gated recurrent unit (32 hidden units) over the 15 day vectors, a substation embedding (4 dimensions), and a two-layer head (64 units) producing 144 numbers per sample: a median correction per half-hour, and a lower and an upper log-scale per half-hour that stretch K0's own quantile offsets (the distance of each K0 quantile from K0's median), so the 11 quantiles cannot cross. About 35,000 parameters (about 42,000 with the linear skip layer added after the first gate run). AdamW, weight decay, dropout 0.1. Early stopping uses month-block validation folds, purged by 15 days either side of the held-out block; the early-stopped model is the one used (no refit).
  • Arms. K0; R; SEQ-ridge (a ridge regression of the same median correction on the same inputs, the linear reference; if the neural network does not beat it, a neural network is not needed); SEQ-blind (the SEQ-quantile network with the residual input zeroed, so that any gain from the weather and day-type scale heads alone can be told apart from reading the residuals); SEQ-median (median correction trained on absolute error; the spread is rebuilt by experiment 111's routine as for every other arm); SEQ-quantile (the correction and the two scales trained with the pinball loss at the 11 quantiles).
  • Training sets. Replicate comparison: train on the odd (tuning) months only and score the even months. Scored-year comparison: train on all runs whose valid times fall before 2025-07-01 (embargoing the last 2 days), early stopping on a month-block fold held out of those. The final forecast averages the fold models (3 folds for the replicate fit, 5 for the scored-year fit) and 2 seeds each; the seed is fixed per job.
  • Compute. About 3,000 samples and 35,000 parameters: seconds per fit, on the GPU if it is free and on the CPU otherwise, far inside the 2 GPU-hour cap. Every script runs under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue with one thread per worker.
  • Other leads. The network outputs day D+1 only. Every arm built on it equals K0 at other leads, so the all-lead columns show R's lead-band behaviour against K0 and SEQ's equal to K0.
  • Reuse. Rows, periods, scoring, bootstrap, breakdowns, and charts are experiment 134's, copied into this folder with the prefix e00142_. No change to src/ or packages/.

docs.title: Planned contrasts (99% month-resampled paired intervals; D-labels only)
docs.text:
• C0. SEQ-quantile minus SEQ-blind (does reading the residuals help beyond the weather and day-type scale heads).
  • C1. SEQ-median minus R at D+1, scored year (decides the verdict), and replicate months.
  • C2. SEQ-quantile minus R at D+1, scored year, and replicate months.
  • C3. SEQ-quantile minus SEQ-median at D+1 (does the quantile loss help the tails).
  • C4. SEQ-median minus K0, SEQ-quantile minus K0, and SEQ-median minus SEQ-ridge.
  • Beside them: all lead bands, winter, winter evening peaks (16:00 to 20:00), cold nights (daily mean under about 3 degrees C) with q95 coverage, holidays and the days after them, and Christmas; tail coverage and pinball at q01, q05, q95, q99; the training-versus-validation gap.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1. SEQ-median minus R is between -0.03 and +0.05 points at D+1 in the scored year, with a 99% interval about 0.03 wide; the most likely outcome is a null.
  • P2. SEQ-quantile minus SEQ-median is between -0.05 and +0.02, and SEQ-quantile minus R is between -0.05 and +0.03.
  • P3. Cold-night q95 coverage of SEQ-quantile is between 74% and 82% (K0: 73 to 78%); it does not reach 90%.
  • P4. SEQ-quantile minus SEQ-blind is between -0.03 and 0.00: most of any tail gain comes from the weather and day-type heads, not from the residual history.
  • P5. SEQ-ridge scores within 0.02 points of SEQ-median.
  • P6. The validation pinball loss exceeds the training loss by 10% or more in the replicate fit and by less than that in the scored-year fit.
  • P7. Holidays and Christmas have too few rows (about 400 and 100 per substation-year) for any contrast to exclude zero.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text: The threshold is 0.02 points at D+1, applied to the point estimate; the 99% interval must also exclude zero. A serving-path model is a new component that has to be trained, versioned, and monitored, so a smaller gain does not justify it. The primary arm for the verdict is SEQ-median against R (C1); SEQ-quantile against SEQ-median (C3) decides the tail claim only. SEQ-median is supported if C1 is at most -0.02 with the interval excluding zero in the scored year, the replicate months agree in sign, and SEQ-median beats SEQ-ridge. It is small gain if the interval excludes zero but the estimate is above -0.02. A tail gain is supported if C3 excludes zero below zero and cold-night q95 coverage moves at least 5 points towards 95% without SEQ-blind doing the same. Otherwise the verdict is not supported, and a clean negative is a fine result. A failed gate caps the verdict at inconclusive. The scored-year network trains on all pre-scored months while R's kappa was tuned on the odd months only; this asymmetry favours the network and is a caveat.

docs.title: Known-answer gate on real residuals (before any scored fit)
docs.text:
Two injections are added to the real residual inputs of April to June 2024 (before every tuning month) and targets of the validation folds, and the network was trained on clean data. (a) A level step of +3 points for eight weeks: the network must recover at least 30% of the step from the third day on and more than R does. (b) A +3-point shift on Saturdays 17:00 to 21:00 UTC for eight weeks: it must recover at least 15% of the shift from the third injected Saturday on, as experiment 134's gate required of RB. The networks are scored on the validation folds that they did not train on, and the gate tests the architecture's ability to adapt on real residuals, not its usefulness.

The absorption test. A second network is trained with the injection present in the training weeks A (the first four of the eight), and is evaluated on the later held-out weeks B twice, with the injection present and absent. It passes if, on the clean held-out weeks, its correction at the injected half-hours is under 25% of the shift: it must adapt from the residual inputs and not memorise the calendar position. A failed gate stops the experiment before any replicate or scored forecast is read. The gate ran twice, and the absorption test was redefined after the first run (see Results).

docs.title: What this experiment will not say
docs.text: Six substations, five of them decision substations, and one independent winter; the network is trained on GAM-K's residuals on ensemble-driven weather, not on the production XGBoost blend; the result bears on a research engine, not on a model release.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Gate, first architecture (gated recurrent unit alone). Level step of +3 points for eight weeks (April to June 2024, before every tuning month): the network recovered -5% of it from the third day (gate: at least 30% and more than R); R recovered 0%, because recipe R removes each day's mean. Saturday-evening shift of +3 points: the network recovered 0.04% (gate: 15%). The absorption test was ill-defined as first written (it compared against zero and not against the clean-trained network, and returned -54%), so that number is not used.
  • Gate, second architecture (post hoc revision before any replicate or scored read). A linear skip from the 14-day mean residual by half-hour, the previous day, and the partial current day was added, which can represent recipe R exactly. The neural network recovered -10% of the level step and -0.1% of the Saturday shift; R recovered 0% and -9%. The absorption test (training with the shift in four of the eight weeks, evaluating the other four on clean inputs, correction minus the clean-trained network's) gave 2.2% on clean weeks, below the 25% limit and 2.6% on injected weeks, so the network did not memorise the calendar, but it did not adapt either.
  • Fit quality on the tuning months. Day-ahead mean absolute error of the median on three held-out month blocks (purged by 15 days): network 3.97, 4.07, 4.43 against K0 4.02, 4.06, 4.57 points, a reduction of 0% to 3% (the mean of two seeds per block; the second block's reduction is about 0%). Over the two seeds, the validation error exceeds the training error by -0.2%, 12%, and 31% on the three blocks; the three blocks have about 700 training samples each.
  • Arms and rows not run. SEQ-median, SEQ-quantile, SEQ-ridge, and SEQ-blind were not scored in the replicate months or the scored year, as the plan requires after a failed gate. The code for the fits and frames is in the folder but was not run.
  • Predictions. P1 to P5 and P7 were not tested. P6 held for the replicate-type fit (the validation error exceeded the training error by more than 10% in two of three blocks).
  • Checks. No audit trigger fired except trigger 1 (a failed control), whose explanation is the small training set and whose investigation is the first-architecture and second-architecture comparison above.
  • Caveats. The gate period (April to June 2024) is spring, not winter. The skip path could represent recipe R, so a failure to recover the shift means the optimiser found no use for it in about 1,100 noisy samples, not that the architecture could not express it.
  • What to try next. Train on longer history (the 2021 to 2024 ensemble backfill, if the maintainer approves its use) or on simulated residuals, and re-run this gate before any score.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: keeping holiday readings out of the GAM-K filter's update
docs.text: Take-home: leaving holiday readings out of the filter's update did not reliably help, so these two Christmases give no reason to change the filter. The filter corrects the day-ahead demand forecast using the forecast's recent errors. A holiday cluster is a bank holiday or a run of holidays close together, such as 24 December to 2 January. After Christmas 2025 the quantile score (lower is better; 1 point is 1% of a substation's capacity) improved by 0.456 points when the filter ignored holiday readings, and after Christmas 2024 it worsened by 0.194. Over the 5 holiday clusters of the scored year (2 July 2025 to 29 June 2026) the score fell by 0.089 points on the 5 days after each cluster (99% interval from resampling clusters -0.309 to +0.036). Over the 5 clusters of July 2024 to June 2025 it rose by 0.063 (+0.022 to +0.160). In 10 of 12 clusters, the filter's error on the holiday days had the same sign as on the following days, so the holiday readings are not usually contamination. Zeroing the correction on holiday days is harmful (+0.62 points there). Experiment 118 did that and ignored the readings together. The verdict is not supported.

docs.title: What was asked, and the answer in plain terms
docs.text:
The question was whether Christmas Day and other holidays teach the filter a wrong level that spoils the days after the holidays. The filter is the Kalman filter on the recent errors of the physics-based demand model driven by ensemble weather forecasts (GAM-K; its unchanged form is arm K0, see "Background and credit" below). We changed only which readings the filter learns from and left the demand model, the filter settings, and the spread alone. K-skip ignores every reading on a bank holiday and on 24 December to 2 January. K-skip-core ignores bank holidays (including 1 January) and 24 to 26 December only. K-skip+1 also ignores the day after a holiday. K-zero ignores holiday readings and sets the correction to zero on holiday days. Scores are quantile scores in points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of a substation's capacity; lower is better) at day D+1 (leads 15.5 to 39 hours from the 09:00 UTC forecast time) over five Primary substations (stations stepping power down from 33 kV to 11 kV), outside the hand-filtered switching events (periods when demand was moved to or from another substation, marked by hand). An arm is one variant of the filter. Leakage days are the 5 days after the last day of a holiday cluster.

Answer. On the 25 leakage days of the scored year (5 days after each of 5 holiday clusters), K-skip scored 0.089 points better than K0, but the interval includes zero and the sign reverses in 2024-25. K-skip does no harm elsewhere (+0.002 on the 324 days that are neither holiday nor leakage days; -0.005 over all 66,844 rows, interval -0.017 to +0.005). The decision rule needed an interval wholly below zero for the leakage days, so the verdict is not supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and rows. K0, K-skip, K-skip-core, K-skip+1, K-zero; all share K0's filter settings and spread. K0 reproduces experiment 115's frame exactly (largest quantile difference 0 points at 6 substations; frames.txt). No demand model was refitted and nothing was tuned. "2024-25" pools the tuning and replicate months of July 2024 to June 2025 (each alone holds 1 to 3 holiday clusters, so the pooling is post hoc); the scored year has 292 runs, 66,844 D+1 rows. Day categories hold 5 holiday dates (bank holidays outside Christmas), 10 Christmas-window dates, 25 leakage dates, and 324 other dates in the scored year.
  • Absolute D+1 scores. Scored year: K0 2.524, K-skip 2.519, K-skip-core 2.525, K-skip+1 2.522, K-zero 2.541. 2024-25: K0 2.425, K-skip 2.429, K-skip-core 2.429, K-skip+1 2.437, K-zero 2.442.
  • The two periods disagree on the days after a holiday (C1, K-skip minus K0). Scored -0.0887 (-0.3090 to +0.0355, 5 clusters, 3 of 5 substations better); 2024-25 +0.0626 (+0.0222 to +0.1604, 5 clusters, 1 of 5); replicate months alone +0.0376 (2 bank-holiday clusters; the days after Christmas 2024 fall in the tuning months, so the replicate sign check did not test Christmas). Leaving out one substation never changes the scored sign (-0.044 to -0.117).
  • K-skip did no harm on holiday days (C2, margin +0.10). Scored -0.0301 (-0.0625 to +0.0003); 2024-25 +0.0004 (-0.0041 to +0.0103). Passed.
  • K-skip did no harm on other days (C3, margin +0.01). Scored +0.0022 (-0.0009 to +0.0080); 2024-25 -0.0001 (-0.0011 to +0.0005). Passed.
  • The net effect over all rows is within the interval around zero (C6). Scored -0.0049 (-0.0166 to +0.0050); 2024-25 +0.0044 (-0.0016 to +0.0142).
  • Skipping the day after a holiday as well did not help (C4). Scored +0.0607 (-0.0537 to +0.1486); 2024-25 +0.0911 (+0.0090 to +0.2635). Skipping the day after a holiday does not help.
  • Zeroing the correction on holiday days hurt (C5). Scored +0.6190 (+0.0637 to +1.8134); 2024-25 +0.3045 (+0.1258 to +0.8079). K-zero's bank-holiday days cost +0.847 against K0 in the scored year.
  • Christmas. K-skip minus K0 on the Christmas window: 2025 -0.033, 2024 -0.002; on the 5 days after: 2025 -0.456 (2 of the 3 substations with rows on those days better), 2024 +0.194 (1 of 5). On 27 to 30 December, K-skip-core minus K0: 2025 -0.082, 2024 +0.132; K-skip-core minus K-skip: +0.240 in 2025 and +0.127 in 2024, so ignoring Christmas Day alone is not what helped in 2025, and ignoring 27 December to 2 January as well helped. Each Christmas is one cluster, so no interval is meaningful.
  • Other holidays (scored year). Easter 2026 -0.099 on the holiday days and +0.043 after; Late Summer 2025 +0.025 after; early and late May 2026 -0.077 and -0.125 after. In 2024-25 every cluster's days after were worse with K-skip (+0.019 to +0.194).
  • Winter (scored year, K-skip minus K0). November to March -0.0099 (-0.0258 to -0.0000); winter evenings 16:00 to 20:00 -0.0233 (-0.0754 to -0.0000); cold-snap nights -0.0696 (-0.2011 to -0.0000; 19 dates). The upper ends round to zero because 4 to 5 month blocks resample poorly. In 2024-25 the same breakdowns were +0.006, +0.005, and +0.029.
  • Cold-snap nights, q95 coverage (scored year, 895 rows; nominal 0.95). K0 0.840, K-skip 0.869, K-skip-core 0.828, K-skip+1 0.878, K-zero 0.850; 2024-25 K0 0.888, K-skip 0.892. All arms under-cover on cold nights.
  • Tails, D+1, scored year (coverage gap in points, pinball loss). K0: q01 +1.31 (0.1912), q05 +1.75 (0.6362), q95 -1.57 (0.6613), q99 -1.21 (0.2090). K-skip: +1.28 (0.1909), +1.73 (0.6355), -1.51 (0.6600), -1.23 (0.2086). K-zero is worse at q95 (-2.08) and q99 (-1.61).
  • Lead bands. K-skip minus K0 on days after a holiday is negative at every lead band in the scored year (-0.025 to -0.100), all with intervals that include zero.
  • Predictions. P1 failed (its scored-year size held, -0.089, but the replicate and 2024-25 signs are positive); P2 failed (-0.082 and +0.132, not at most -0.10 in both); P3 held (-0.030, +0.000); P4 held (upper +0.008, +0.0005); P5 failed (+0.061 and +0.091, outside 0.03); P6 held (+0.619, +0.305).

docs.title: A step added to one day is carried forward by K0 and by no skip arm
docs.text: The known-answer gate passed before any scored fit. A +3-point step added to every reading of one day was carried by K0 into the following days (share of the step at days 1 to 5 after 1 January 2025: 0.06, 0.23, 0.17, 0.12, 0.08, the median of 5 substations; 5 May and 26 May 2025 give 0.08, 0.23, 0.17, 0.12, 0.08), and carried by K-skip, K-skip+1, and K-zero not at all (largest absolute share 0, 6 substations). On the control day, 15 January 2025, K-skip matched K0 to within 0.002. A step on 3 January 2025 was carried by K-skip (at least 0.10 on the second day) and not by K-skip+1. Each holiday day with readings had 48 readings skipped, and K-skip equalled K0 exactly before the first skipped reading. Most of these conditions are true by construction of the mask; the informative result is that K0 carries a step at all. The calendar assigns each half-hour to its local start date, which studies.dp_calendar documents.

docs.title: Whether holiday readings usually carry the same level error as the days after
docs.text: The holiday readings' residual usually has the same sign as the residual on the days after, so carrying it forward is usually not wrong. The filter's residual (observed minus the fitted forecast) averaged +0.7 points on Christmas 2024's holiday days and +5.6 on the 5 days after, and +4.3 and +7.7 in 2025. The sign differs in 2 of the 12 clusters (early May 2024 and Late Summer 2025). The magnitudes differ (+0.73 against +5.59 in 2024), and the 12 clusters include two from May 2024 outside every scored period. The result makes "holidays teach a wrong level" unlikely as the general case in these 12 clusters. The residual does not explain why ignoring 27 December to 2 January helped in 2025, because both Christmases have the same sign and opposite effects. That remains unexplained, with one Christmas for each sign.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site (scored year, D+1, points). K0 and K-skip: D10 +0.003, D11 -0.022, D14 +0.014, D16 -0.014, D5 -0.097. The arms share K0's spread, so the values are the same to 3 places.
  • Error of the median and of the mean forecast beside each contrast (scored year, D+1). C1 -0.141 and -0.142 (quantile score -0.089); C2 -0.040 and -0.037; C3 +0.004 and +0.004; C6 -0.007 and -0.007. All point the same way as the quantile score.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction) applies to P1, P2, and P5; the explanation tested above is recorded and does not settle P2. Triggers 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire: the gate passed; the quantile score and the errors agree; leaving out one substation never flips C1's scored sign; no nested arm beats the arm that contains it; no sister experiment on these rows; no later experiment that we found depends on this result. No audit was run, and no Opus review, as the brief asked.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Two Christmases and about 5 holiday clusters per period. Intervals from resampling 5 clusters are wide and unstable, and the Christmas contrasts are single clusters.
  • The spread is K0's. It slightly favours K0 on days where K-skip's residuals differ.
  • The substations' holiday days are not independent; the per-substation counts (3 of 5) reflect the same weather.
  • The early winters of experiment 122 were not added: that experiment stored quantile predictions only, not residual streams.
  • Gate thresholds were set before the gate was run, and the plan was amended once after its review (K-skip-core, cluster bootstrap, extra gate checks), before any score was read.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Keep K0 for this Christmas. The filter's holiday behaviour is not shown to be a defect.
  • If a holiday term is revisited, test it over more than two Christmases, for example by running GAM-K's filter on past weather for 2019 to 2024, which needs residual streams that no stored experiment holds.
  • Test ignoring only 27 December to 2 January's readings (not 24 to 26 December) as a Christmas-specific rule, since K-skip-core and K-skip separate there.

Every number above is printed by ml-experiments/00143-*/e00143_report.py and e00143_gate.py; the report's output is report.txt.

docs.title: Plan, committed before any fit
docs.text: The plan below was committed before any fit and amended once, after its review and before any score was read: K-skip-core, the cluster bootstrap, C6 in the decision rule, and extra gate checks were added. Section headings are one level lower than in the plan's commit.

docs.title: Background and credit
docs.text: GAM-K is the physics-based demand model (a generalised additive model) with the Kalman filter on its recent errors, as built in experiment 111, following the Kalman-on-additive-model idea of de Vilmarest and Goude (2022). This experiment reuses experiment 111's stored fits, calibrations, and filter settings; experiment 115's cached ensemble member forecasts, K0 spread, and scoring rows; and the scoring and breakdown code of experiment 134. Experiment 118 tried two holiday actions at once in a different filter (KEZ-DT): it dropped holiday readings from the update and zeroed the correction on holiday targets, and it scored +1.24 points worse on 17 holiday days (+0.62 to +1.83). Halving the correction (KEZ-DTs) was +0.09 on those days. Of the two actions, only the second is shown to hurt in these experiments. We found no GAM-K breakdown of Christmas in the earlier experiments. Experiment 134 found that the holiday rule on the recent-error profile raised the score by 0.004 points (an interval including zero), and that its Christmas-window contrast was +0.07; the holiday rule's own effect in those windows was not printed.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All four arms are K0's member forecasts plus a correction, with K0's filter hyperparameters, spread tables, and spread factors (experiment 115's stored values), so the arms differ only in the correction.

  • K0 (control). GAM-K's filter reads every reading, as in experiment 111.
  • K-skip. A reading on a holiday day is treated as missing for the update only. A holiday target still gets the carried level and transient.
  • K-skip-core. K-skip, but only bank holidays and 24 to 26 December are skipped. K-skip also skips 27 December to 2 January, so its 27 to 30 December targets differ from K0 for two reasons (Christmas Day not learned, and four more days not learned). K-skip-core separates them: on 27 to 30 December it ignores Christmas Day but reads the readings of the 27th onwards.
  • K-skip+1. K-skip, and also the first non-holiday day after each holiday day is skipped, to test slow recovery.
  • K-zero (reference only). K-skip's filter, and the level and transient are set to zero on holiday targets. This is experiment 118's drop-and-zero idea on GAM-K.

The holiday set is fixed here before any fit: every England and Wales bank holiday in the holidays package's list for England (including the substitute days it marks as observed), and every day from 24 December to 2 January. Days are Europe/London dates; a reading belongs to the date of its half-hour's start.

Day categories (disjoint, by the target's local date). Christmas window (24 December to 2 January); bank holiday (a bank holiday outside that window); after Christmas and after bank holiday (days 1 to 5 after the last day of a holiday cluster, where a cluster joins holiday days at most 3 days apart, so Good Friday and Easter Monday are one cluster); other (everything else). "Leakage days" are the two "after" categories. A day that follows two clusters takes the later cluster's label, and 1 and 2 January belong to the Christmas window even where New Year's Day is also a bank holiday. 27 to 30 December lie inside the Christmas window and are also scored on their own, as K-skip-core against K-skip and against K0. After Christmas the leakage days are 3 to 7 January, by which time K-skip has ignored 10 days of readings; a null C1 there could therefore be a stale level rather than no contamination, and the K-skip-core contrast on 27 to 30 December is the cleaner test of Christmas Day's contamination.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: No setting is fitted. The filter hyperparameters, spread tables, and spread factors are those of K0 as experiment 111 and 115 tuned them. The odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06 (tuning months) are therefore a first read, with the known-answer gate run on them; the even months (replicate months) and the scored year (2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29) are read after the predictions are fixed. Christmas 2024 lies in the replicate months and Christmas 2025 in the scored year. The past-weather winters of experiment 122 cannot be added cheaply: that experiment stored quantile predictions only, not residual streams, so rerunning the filter on earlier Christmases would need new past-weather fits and is left to a later experiment.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
All at day D+1, quantile score in points of effective capacity, K-arm minus K0 unless stated (negative favours the first-named arm), pooled over the five decision substations, with 99% intervals from a day-block bootstrap (below).

  • C1 (decides). K-skip minus K0 on the leakage days.
  • C2 (non-inferiority). K-skip minus K0 on holiday days (Christmas window and bank holidays).
  • C3 (non-inferiority). K-skip minus K0 on the other days.
  • C4. K-skip+1 minus K-skip on the leakage days.
  • C5 (reference). K-zero minus K-skip on holiday days.
  • C6 (non-inferiority). K-skip minus K0 over all D+1 rows (month-block bootstrap, studies.bootstrap).
  • C7. K-skip-core minus K0 on 27 to 30 December, and K-skip-core minus K-skip on the same days.

Required breakdowns for C1 to C3 (K-skip against K0, and K-skip+1 against K0): winter (November to March); winter evening 16:00 to 20:00; cold nights (days with a daily mean under 3 C, local 22:00 to 06:00), with q95 coverage; each holiday cluster separately, with a figure per Christmas (20 December to 5 January, daily mean D+1 score per arm); 27 to 30 December; every lead band beside D+1. Tail calibration (coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, q99) is reported for each arm.

Cluster bootstrap. Days of one holiday cluster share filter state, so they are not independent. A block is one holiday cluster with its holiday days and its 5 following days, over all decision substations. Clusters are resampled with replacement within the period, 5,000 resamples, a fixed seed, percentile interval; for C3 and C6 the blocks are calendar months. The write-up states how many clusters and dates each period holds, and a conclusion resting on few clusters says so. Christmas occurs once a year, so the Christmas findings rest on two Christmases (2024 and 2025) and are not generalised.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1. C1 is between -0.05 and -0.30 in the scored year, and negative in the replicate months.
  • P2. On 27 to 30 December, K-skip-core minus K0 is at most -0.10 in each of the two Christmases (point estimates; two Christmases give no interval worth a rule). Where the largest gain sits is read from this contrast, not from C1.
  • P3. C2 is between -0.05 and +0.10.
  • P4. C3 is within ±0.01, and its upper interval end is at most +0.01.
  • P5. C4 is within ±0.03 (skipping the day after a holiday adds nothing measurable).
  • P6. C5 is above +0.30 (zeroing the correction on holiday targets hurts), the direction of experiment 118.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
The verdict follows C1, C2, and C3 in the scored year, and the replicate months must agree in the sign of C1. Skipping holiday readings costs nothing in production, because it is a mask on the update, so the threshold for a gain is zero.

  • supported: C1's interval lies wholly below zero; C2's upper end is at most +0.10 (about 4% of the score; holiday days are about 5% of the year); C3's upper end is at most +0.01; and C1 is negative in the replicate months; and C6's upper end is at most 0.00 (the net annual effect does not lose).
  • partly supported: C1's interval lies wholly below zero but C2 or C3 fails its margin.
  • not supported: C1's interval includes zero or lies above it.
  • A failed known-answer gate caps the verdict at inconclusive.

docs.title: Known-answer gate (before any scored fit)
docs.text:
On real tuning-month residuals, add +3 points to every reading of one holiday day, run each arm's filter on the changed stream, and measure how much of the step reaches the correction on the following days. The holiday days injected are 1 January 2025, 5 May 2025, and 26 May 2025 (all in tuning months); the control day is Wednesday 15 January 2025 (not a holiday, not adjacent to one). The change in the correction (changed stream minus real stream) is averaged over D+1 rows whose target is 1 to 5 days after the injected day, as a share of 3 points.

  • Pass conditions. On each holiday day, K0 carries a share of at least 0.10 into the second day after the injected day (the first day whose forecast sees the whole injected day), and K-skip and K-skip+1 carry 0.00 (to 1e-9). On the control day, K-skip's share is within 0.02 of K0's, so that skipping holidays does not damage the filter elsewhere. K-zero's change on the holiday targets themselves is exactly zero.
  • Further checks, all run before any scored fit. Every holiday day with readings has 46 to 50 readings skipped; K-skip equals K0 exactly on every row whose cutoff precedes the first skipped reading; a step injected on 3 January is carried by K-skip (share at least 0.10 on the second day) and not by K-skip+1. Most of these checks are true by construction of the mask. The gate's informative parts are that K0 carries a step (the bar is 0.10) and that the masks hit the dates intended (the local date of the half-hour's start, as studies.dp_calendar defines it).
  • K0 reproduces experiment 115. The K0 frame's q01, q05, q50, q95, and q99 match experiment 115's stored K0 frame to 1e-3 points at every site.
  • A failed condition is reported and capped as stated in the decision rule.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text: The spread tables and factors are K0's, tuned for K0's residuals, so they slightly favour K0 on leakage days where K-skip's residuals are smaller. The effect is conservative for K-skip.

docs.title: Compute and process
docs.text: CPU only, at most 4 cores. Each filter run over a site's grid takes about 1 second, and a frame build for four arms and six substations takes a few minutes. Every script runs under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue. Reviews: one Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review, one Sonnet numbers review, and one Sonnet prose review. No Opus review unless the ML manager asks.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: does the weather-forecast error persist from day to day?
docs.text:
Take-home: in this test, the day-ahead weather forecast did not repeat its errors from one day to the next, so there is nothing to feed a demand correction. The brief set a stop rule at a lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.2 (the correlation between one day's error and the next day's). Every season's value is under 0.2, so no demand forecast was fitted. Two caveats apply: wind was not tested, because experiment 111's ensemble store does not hold it, and the reference was a later forecast, not observed weather.

We asked whether an ECMWF ensemble forecast that was too cold or too cloudy yesterday tends to be too cold or too cloudy today. For each day we took the ensemble mean forecast published the morning before. We subtracted a reference for that day that a live service could build afterwards: the control forecast from each of the following runs, joined end to end. We call this reference the "analysis proxy". It is a later forecast, not an observation. We then correlated each day's error with the error 1 to 7 days later, at seven substations over 820 days.

The lag-1 correlation is at most +0.11, so a correction based on it has no signal to use. A search of docs/ml-experiments found no earlier experiment that tested this directly. The closest earlier result we found is experiment 111's, where ERA5 (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis) residuals in the GAM-K filter (the convex demand model with a Kalman filter) did not change the score (GAM-K-era5 minus GAM-K: -0.008, interval -0.024 to +0.008). That agrees with this experiment's result.

docs.title: Weather-forecast errors are barely correlated from one day to the next
docs.text:
Each cell is the Pearson correlation averaged over seven substations (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16, D18), with about 200 days per season. The raw and anomaly versions are both in the JSON file; "anomaly" removes each calendar month's mean error first.

Variable Season Lag 1 Lag 2 Lag 3 Lag 7 Temperature December to February +0.11 +0.07 -0.06 -0.05 Temperature March to May +0.03 +0.02 -0.04 +0.06 Temperature June to August +0.02 +0.02 -0.02 +0.08 Temperature September to November +0.10 0.00 -0.04 +0.03 Irradiance December to February +0.03 -0.13 -0.02 -0.02 Irradiance March to May -0.01 -0.09 -0.01 +0.02 Irradiance June to August +0.04 +0.04 +0.08 +0.06 Irradiance September to November +0.05 +0.02 -0.10 -0.11
  • The anomaly version gives similar values (lag 1 from -0.01 to +0.09).
  • e00144_autocorr.py prints lags 1 to 7 for both versions and writes work/autocorrelation.json.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Wind was not tested. Experiment 111's ensemble store holds temperature and shortwave irradiance only. GAM-K takes no wind input.
  • The reference is a later forecast. The error is the revision between the day-ahead ensemble mean and the next run's control forecast, which is 9.5 to 33 hours old when subtracted.
  • The errors are small. At D5 the daily temperature error has a standard deviation of about 0.3 degrees Celsius, and the daily irradiance error about 14 W/m².
  • A bias against observed weather could still persist. ERA5 is published about 5 days after the date, too late to use at forecast time. Experiment 111's ERA5 result found no gain, which points the same way.
  • No demand forecast was fitted, so there are no scores, tail calibration, or breakdowns.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: correcting GAM-K with the errors of the most similar past days
docs.text: Take-home: averaging the errors of the 20 most similar past days gave a small, real gain over recipe R at day D+1 (0.041 points, about 1.7% of recipe R's score of 2.436), and the part of the idea that was about weather and holidays did not help. Recipe R is the baseline correction: it subtracts 0.75 times the mean of the last 14 days' errors by half-hour from the forecast of GAM-K, the physics-based demand model (a generalised additive model with a Kalman filter that updates it using ensemble weather forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, ECMWF). One point is 1% of a substation's capacity, and lower scores are better. The gain comes from using many same-day-type days over a 13-week season window, including last year's days. Ranking days by forecast temperature helped by only 0.005 points. Using the same holiday of the year before made holidays worse. The verdict is small gain, not a stronger one. The 99% interval for the difference from R lies wholly below zero, but the upper end of that interval (-0.017) is above the -0.02 threshold written into the plan before any fit.

docs.title: What was asked, and the answer in plain terms
docs.text:
The question was whether the day-ahead correction should average the errors of the past days that look most like the day being forecast, instead of the most recent days. The quantity forecast is the electricity demand at five Primary substations (the stations that step power down from 33 kV to 11 kV). Each forecast covers day D+1, the calendar day after the 09:00 UTC forecast origin, which is 15.5 to 39 hours ahead. Experiment 115 found recipe R, and experiment 134 found that a weekday term added only 0.011 points. This experiment looked for the most similar past days instead: same day type (Monday, Tuesday to Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday), within a season window of the same date, and closest in forecast daily mean temperature, with the same holiday for holidays. It is a nearest-neighbour ("analog") correction as in Delle Monache et al. (2013), applied to forecast errors.

Answer. The best arm, ANALOG+R, scored 2.395 points at day D+1 in the scored year (2 July 2025 to 29 June 2026, 292 daily forecast runs) against 2.436 for R. Rows inside the hand-filtered switching events are left out. The settings were chosen on the odd months of July 2024 to June 2025; the even months are the replicate months.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and settings. Kappa is the fraction of the mean error subtracted, k is the number of similar days averaged, the season window is the number of weeks either side of the date from which days are drawn, and lambda is the weight of the analog profile against R's 14-day profile. K0 (GAM-K); R (recipe R, kappa 0.75); ANALOG-k (kappa 0.75, k 20 days, 8 weeks); ANALOG+R (kappa 1.0, k 20, 13 weeks, lambda 0.5, the weight of the analog profile against R's profile); ANALOG-holiday (R, with the analog profile at weight 0.5 on holiday-like days only; fixed settings); ANALOG+R-notemp (no temperature ranking; k 20, 8 weeks); ANALOG+R-recent (post hoc: ANALOG+R without days older than 300 days). Settings are fleet-wide, chosen by the tuning rows' mean absolute error of the median at D+1; k reached its largest value on the grid (20) for all three tuned arms. Tuning rows' error: K0 4.299, R 4.131, ANALOG+R 4.053. No demand model was refitted, so no retraining schedule applies and the contrasts do not depend on a retraining schedule.
  • Rows. 66,844 D+1 rows in the scored year and 41,126 in the replicate months at the five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16), D9 beside them.
  • Absolute scores, scored year, D+1 (all leads). K0 2.524 (2.812), R 2.436 (2.744), RB 2.424 (2.750), RB-day-types 2.414 (2.756), ANALOG-k 2.422 (2.793), ANALOG+R 2.395 (2.750), ANALOG-holiday 2.438 (2.746), ANALOG+R-notemp 2.400 (2.757), ANALOG+R-recent 2.411 (2.760). D9 beside them: R 2.123, ANALOG+R 2.107.
  • C1 ANALOG+R minus R (decides the verdict, 99%). Scored year -0.0405 (-0.0572 to -0.0169), 4 of 5 substations; replicate months -0.0330 (-0.0558 to -0.0045), 4 of 5. Winter (November to March) -0.0526 (-0.0676 to -0.0259); leaving out any one substation keeps the estimate between -0.027 and -0.052 with the interval below zero. Over all leads +0.0067 (-0.0048 to +0.0187); at 48 to 144 hours +0.0182 (+0.0079 to +0.0295).
  • C2 ANALOG-k minus R. -0.0138 (-0.0471 to +0.0295), 2 of 5; replicate +0.0002. C3 ANALOG+R minus RB-day-types. -0.0185 (-0.0315 to -0.0052), 5 of 5; replicate -0.0051 (-0.0171 to +0.0127). C5 ANALOG+R minus K0. -0.1291 (-0.1765 to -0.0899), 5 of 5.
  • Where C1 gains (scored year, D+1). Monday -0.0928 and Friday -0.1375 (both 5 of 5), Saturday -0.0296, Sunday -0.0363, Tuesday -0.0251, Wednesday and Thursday within noise. Winter evening 16:00 to 20:00 -0.1095 (-0.1625 to -0.0375), 4 of 5. Cold-snap days (forecast daily mean under 3 degrees C, 80 site-days) -0.1092 (-0.2264 to -0.0593), 5 of 5 substations; cold-snap nights (22:00 to 06:00, 900 rows) -0.0442 (-0.1664 to +0.0362), 4 of 5, with an interval that includes zero. Against RB-day-types the cold-snap days score -0.0738 (-0.3648 to +0.0501). Non-winter -0.0325 (-0.0557 to +0.0009).
  • Temperature. ANALOG+R-notemp minus ANALOG+R is +0.0046 (-0.0012 to +0.0110) in the scored year and +0.0029 in the replicate months: ranking by temperature gains 0.005 points, too little to justify the lookup under the plan's 0.02 rule. The gain is larger where weather matters: winter evenings +0.0174 (-0.0165 to +0.0450) scored and +0.0160 (+0.0076 to +0.0253) replicate, and all leads +0.0066 (+0.0018 to +0.0117) scored. On cold days the chosen analogs differ from the target by 3.0 degrees C on average (site D10), against 1.3 on other days, probably because few cold days exist.
  • Last year's days. In the scored year the mean pool of candidates at D10 is 80, of which 51 are from the previous year; in the tuning and replicate months it is 34, of which 8 are. ANALOG+R-recent minus ANALOG+R is +0.0162 (+0.0107 to +0.0224) in the scored year and +0.0016 in the replicate months, which have few days from the previous year (8 on average). About 40% of the gain over R (roughly 26 to 55% from the interval of the difference) therefore comes from last year's days (recent-only minus R: -0.0243, -0.0375 to -0.0072). The tuned settings were chosen on a pool with little previous-year history, so they may under-use last year's days.
  • Holidays. C4 (ANALOG-holiday minus R) on holiday-like days is +0.0713 (+0.0192 to +0.1424), 1 of 5 substations better; Christmas window +0.0053; Easter +0.1161 (one set of 720 rows). ANALOG+R minus R on holiday-like days is +0.1595 (+0.0441 to +0.2851). All 16 holiday-like targets of the scored year (D10) used their own holiday's earlier occurrence (identity path); none needed the fallback. One earlier occurrence is a worse correction than R's 14-day profile. Non-holiday rows carry the whole gain (-0.0486, 5 of 5). The days 1 to 3 after a holiday-like day gain -0.0279 (-0.0620 to +0.1369) against R, and -0.0672 (5 of 5) against RB-day-types. About 13 holiday-like days fall on scored runs, so the intervals are coarse. Christmas window (4 substations): C1 +0.0133 (-0.0050 to +0.0181), C3 -0.0647 (-0.0702 to -0.0437), C5 -0.1242 (-0.1442 to -0.0477). Easter: C1 +0.2786, 0 of 5 substations better. Holiday-like days: C2 +0.3747 (+0.2352 to +0.5498). Replicate months, which test the fallback path only because no holiday there has an earlier occurrence: C4 on holiday-like days +0.0663 (-0.1248 to +0.0845), 1 of 5 substations better. Holiday verdict: ANALOG-holiday is not a candidate, because C4 is positive on holiday-like days and in the Christmas window, and only 1 of 5 substations is better.
  • Tails (scored year, D+1; coverage gap, observed minus nominal coverage in percentage points, then pinball loss). ANALOG+R: q01 +1.27 (0.1843), q05 +1.65 (0.5910), q95 -0.94 (0.6570), q99 -1.16 (0.2130); R: +1.39 (0.1875), +1.76 (0.6138), -1.01 (0.6573), -1.16 (0.2124). On cold-snap nights (900 rows; nominal levels 0.95 and 0.99, so every arm under-covers) the share of readings at or below q95 is 0.839 for K0, 0.888 for R, and 0.891 for ANALOG+R; below q99 it is 0.953, 0.976, and 0.978. In the replicate months the 468 cold-night rows show 0.998 and 1.000 for R and ANALOG+R, so cold-night coverage differs between periods.
  • Not computed. The curtailment-cost metric was not scored, because the experiment changes only the day-ahead mean correction. The q95 and q99 pinball losses barely move (0.6573 to 0.6570 and 0.2124 to 0.2130), and the upper tail is the one that matters for curtailment; q05 improves by 0.023.
  • Predictions. Held: P4 (temperature adds 0.00 to +0.02: +0.005), P7 (the gain reverses beyond 48 hours), P8 (tuned k at least 5), and P6's first half (the gain is largest on winter evenings among the season and time-of-day cuts; Friday is larger). Failed: P1 (C1 was -0.041, below the predicted -0.005 to -0.03), P2 (the pure analog arm was not worse than R), P3 (ANALOG+R beat RB-day-types by 0.0185, not within 0.01), P5 (the holiday arm was worse than R, not better, in the Christmas window too, and the interval lay wholly above zero), and P6's second half (the non-winter estimate was -0.033, not within 0.005 of zero).

docs.title: Gate
docs.text:
The known-answer gates G0, G1, and G2 passed, and they ran on the tuning months before any replicate or scored forecast was read. The recovered shares (the fraction of an injected shift that each arm's correction picks up) agree with the expected values in the plan.

  • G0, no lookahead. Injecting +3 points on the target day and on the origin's own day changed no arm's profile at all (largest change 0.0).
  • G1, Saturday evenings. Share of the +3-point shift recovered, median of five substations: R 0.089, ANALOG-k 0.352, ANALOG+R 0.220 (twice R is 0.178), the placebo (the day type of 3 days later) 0.045 for ANALOG+R and 0.000 for ANALOG-k. G1b at k 3 and 4 weeks: 0.556 with temperature ranking and 0.590 without.
  • G2, a recurring holiday. The Spring Bank Holiday of 26 May 2025 recovered 0.3125 of a shift injected on 27 May 2024 for ANALOG-holiday (the plan's expected value) and 0.000 for R.
  • G3, a recurring weather state (informative, did not cap the verdict). On cold days ANALOG+R recovered 0.300 and ANALOG+R-notemp 0.265. The difference, 0.035, is below the 0.05 the plan asked for. Together with the null result for temperature above, the temperature part of the hypothesis is untested in the gate and only weakly supported in the scores. The verdict for that part is inconclusive, not refuted.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site (scored year, D+1, points). ANALOG+R: D10 +0.011, D11 -0.018, D14 +0.007, D16 -0.021, D5 -0.060. R: +0.009, -0.019, +0.002, -0.015, -0.037. K0 at D5 is -0.097.
  • Error of the median and of the mean forecast beside each contrast (scored year, D+1). C1: -0.0675 and -0.0689. C2: -0.0109 and -0.0128. C3: -0.0320 and -0.0323. C4: +0.0036 and +0.0038. C5: -0.2447 and -0.2482. The quantile score and both errors point the same way.
  • Triggers. Four of the plan's seven audit triggers fired, and none led to an audit: the ML manager decided against one to save usage quota (a message to this session on 2026-10-21, not committed). The Opus audit is the step the manager skipped. Trigger 1: G3, a known-answer gate that failed, reported as informative above. Trigger 2: the C1 gain is larger than predicted (P1), the pure analog arm did not lose to R (P2), and ANALOG+R beat RB-day-types by more than predicted (P3); the recent-only ablation explains part of P1 (last year's days carry about 40% of the gain) and nothing explains P2 and P3. Trigger 4: C2 (ANALOG-k minus R, -0.0138) flips sign when D14 is left out (+0.0017); C1, C3, C4, and C5 keep their sign when any one substation is left out. Trigger 5: R, which the holiday arm contains as a special case, beats the holiday arm on holiday-like days (+0.0713); the cause is the one-sample holiday profile. Trigger 3 did not fire. Trigger 6 did not fire: experiment 134's C1 interval is 0.026 wide and this one is 0.040 wide. Trigger 7 did not fire: no later experiment depends on this result yet.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Five substations and one independent winter; about 13 holiday-like days in the scored year.
  • k stopped at the largest grid value, so a larger k may do better. The tuning screen used the median's absolute error, 135 settings per arm against one fixed setting of R, and the replicate months (-0.033) guard against that optimism.
  • The tuned settings come from a pool with little history from the previous year; the scored year's pool is larger.
  • The shift applies at every lead as R does; the gain reverses beyond 48 hours, so a serving version would apply it at day D+1 only.
  • ANALOG+R-recent is post hoc and was not re-tuned. Its cap of 300 days leaves out days older than 300 days; with the tuned 13-week window, days 274 to 300 days old are still allowed, so it leaves out most but not all of the previous year.
  • The tuned arms' spread is fitted on the tuning rows after the settings were chosen on the same rows, so the spread is slightly too narrow out of sample, and R, which was not tuned, does not have this bias. Quantile-score and tail contrasts against R are therefore slightly biased against the analog arms.
  • The gate's shares are fractions of the raw +3-point shift. Removing each day's mean and the kappa shrink put the ceiling near 0.62 at kappa 0.75, and the plan's expected values already include that.
  • The report's cold-snap rows use the observed daily mean below 3 degrees C in winter months, while the gate's cold days use the forecast daily mean below 5 degrees C in the tuning months, so they are different sets of days.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test a day-type profile with k 20 or more and a 13-week season window, applied at day D+1 only, with lambda tuned on the quantile score. The gain over RB-day-types (0.0185) says the larger pool and last year's days matter more than the choice of similarity.
  • Leave holiday-like days on R's 14-day profile and test a pooled holiday profile (several holidays of one kind together) instead of one earlier occurrence.

Every number above is printed by ml-experiments/00145-*/e00145_report.py; its output is report.txt.

docs.title: Plan, committed before any fit
docs.text: This experiment asked whether the day-ahead forecast's recent-error correction should average the errors of the most similar past days instead of the most recent days. The forecast is the electricity demand of five Primary substations (the stations that step power down from 33 kV to 11 kV) for the day after the 09:00 UTC forecast origin, from the physics-based demand model with a Kalman filter on ECMWF ensemble weather (GAM-K, arm K0; experiment 111). Recipe R subtracts 0.75 times the mean of the last 14 days' errors by half-hour (experiment 115). A weekday term gave only 0.011 points more (experiment 134). This experiment picks, from all the past days of the same day type within a season window, the ones whose forecast temperature was closest to the target day's, and averages their errors. It is a nearest-neighbour ("analog") correction of the kind forecasters use for load on holidays and extreme weather, as in the analog ensemble of Delle Monache et al. (2013), applied to the error of a forecast and not to the weather. A clean negative result is a fine outcome. Experiment 143 (in progress) tests a different holiday idea (keeping holiday readings out of the Kalman filter's update); the two do not overlap in mechanism.

docs.title: Read before planning
docs.text:
• Earlier advice followed. Experiment 134's advice is to use day types and not seven weekdays, and to apply the term at D+1 only. This plan uses day types, and applies the analog shift at every lead as recipe R does, so the lead bands show whether the loss beyond 48 hours that experiment 134 found also appears here.
  • Experiment 115's KW-pl52 arm (the diurnal shape from 52 weeks earlier) scored -0.034 against K0, against -0.075 for the current shape (KW), so last year's shape gains about half as much as the current one. That means demand errors have a seasonal repeat but the pattern drifts within a year. The season window of this plan therefore starts narrow (2 to 13 weeks either side), and the most-recent days stay in the pool, so the arm can use last year's days where they match and the recent days elsewhere.
  • Residual history. GAM-K's D+1 errors exist for runs from 2024-04-02, so the first scored target has about 15 months of history and the last has about 27 months. The same-holiday- last-year arm can show whether one earlier occurrence of a holiday, at one substation, predicts the next one: all 16 holiday-like days of the scored year (the Late Summer Bank Holiday, 24 to 31 December, New Year's Day, the Easter weekend, Easter Monday, May Day, and the Spring Bank Holiday) have an earlier occurrence in the history, and the scoring script prints that check. The arm cannot show anything about the tuning or replicate months: of their holiday-like days only the two May 2025 bank holidays have an earlier occurrence, so Christmas 2024 and Easter 2025 use the fallback to any earlier holiday-like day. The holiday arm's setting is therefore fixed before any fit and not tuned, and one earlier occurrence is one noisy sample. The holiday result rests on 16 days at each of 5 substations.
  • What the tuning rows cannot exercise. A tuning target has at most 15 months of history, so its pool holds recent same-class days and almost no days of the previous year; the scored year's pool also holds last year's days. The tuned k and N are therefore tuned on a recency-dominated pool, and the write-up reports the number of candidates and of previous-year candidates by period. The plan does not predict the tuned N.
  • Warm-up runs. The history before 2024-07 comes from warm-up runs, whose Kalman errors may not have converged; the write-up prints the usable-block count and the mean absolute error by month.
  • Past weather at lag times. The similarity uses the ENS ensemble-mean temperature that each past day's forecast run saw for that day, so it exists at forecast time. The target day's forecast temperature is from the run being corrected. No ERA5 enters.
  • No data-processing entry is expected. Read docs/ml-experiments/data-processing.md; the plan adds no new processing step.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• K0. GAM-K as stored (control; linked from experiment 115).
  • R. Recipe R as experiment 115 stored it (linked): K0 minus 0.75 times the mean of the last 14 UTC days' D+1 errors by local half-hour, each day's mean removed, no holiday rule. Call its 14-day profile A.
  • ANALOG-k. K0 minus kappa times the mean error of the k most similar past days (below); where no analog set exists the arm falls back to A. A pure analog correction.
  • ANALOG+R. K0 plus the shift -kappa x (A + lambda x (the analog profile minus A)). Lambda 0 is R, so R is nested. Lambda is the weight of the analog profile in the correction.
  • ANALOG-holiday. R on every non-holiday-like day; on a holiday-like target day, K0 minus 0.75 times A plus 0.5 times (the same-holiday profile minus A). The weights are fixed, because the tuning months hold too few repeated holidays to tune them.
  • ANALOG+R-notemp (exploratory ablation). As ANALOG+R, with the k most recent days of the same class inside the season window replacing the k closest in temperature, so the contrast with ANALOG+R isolates the weather similarity.
  • References from earlier experiments (read only). Experiment 134's RB and RB-day-types.

What is similar. A source day S is a candidate for target day T (both UTC days of the D+1 block; the target's run has origin on T-1) when all of the following hold.

  • S is at most T-2, so its block came from the run of day S-1 and S ended before the origin, as in experiment 134.
  • S has a usable error block (at least 40 of 48 half-hours with a reading) and a forecast temperature.
  • Class. For a non-holiday T, S is a non-holiday-like day of T's day type (Monday, Tuesday to Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday). For a holiday-like T (an English bank holiday, Easter Saturday or Sunday, 24 December, or 27 to 31 December), S has T's holiday identity: a bank holiday's name (Good Friday, Easter Monday, Christmas Day, ...), Easter Saturday, Easter Sunday, or the month and day for 24 and 27 to 31 December. If T has no earlier occurrence, S is any holiday-like day, and if fewer than 2 of those exist the arm falls back to A.
  • Season. For a non-holiday T, S lies within N weeks either side of T's day of year (circular). A holiday T uses no season window, since its class is already narrow.
  • Nearest. The k candidates with the smallest absolute difference between S's forecast daily mean temperature (the ENS ensemble-mean temperature, mean of the 48 half-hours of the D+1 block, from the run of S-1) and T's. Ties go to the more recent day. A non-holiday T needs at least 3 candidates, otherwise the arm falls back to A.

No lookahead. Every input to a correction at origin O is an error block of a day that ended before O, or a forecast temperature from a run that started before O.

docs.title: Settings and how they are chosen
docs.text:
• Grids. kappa from 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25; k from 3, 5, 8, 12, 20; N from 4, 8, 13 weeks (kappa 1.25 and k 20 were added after a first screen on the tuning rows put the tuned kappa and k at the old grid edge; no replicate or scored row had been read); lambda from 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 (ANALOG+R and its ablation; ANALOG-k is lambda 1).
  • Rule. Fleet-wide settings, one set for all five decision substations, chosen by the lowest pooled mean absolute error of the corrected median at D+1 on the tuning rows (the odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06), as in experiment 134. Each arm's spread is then refitted on the tuning rows and one factor per lead band is chosen, as for every arm of experiment 115.
  • R's kappa is tuned on the same rows too. The tuning screen prints R's mean absolute error at kappa 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, and 1.25, so a reader can see whether R at 0.75 was a handicap.
  • Lead scope. Every arm applies its shift at every lead, as R does, so that R is nested; experiment 134 found such a shift loses beyond 48 hours, and the lead bands show it here too. The verdict metric is D+1 either way.
  • Tuning uses the median's absolute error, not the quantile score, for the speed of a screen of about 150 settings; the contrasts are on the quantile score.

docs.title: Known-answer gate (reported before any score)
docs.text:
On real tuning-month residuals, inject a repeated pattern, run every arm's full profile code on the changed readings, and measure the share of the pattern each correction recovers. Each injection goes through the same reading filter, class rule, and fallback as the real scoring, so the gate can fail for a real reason.

  • G1, a recurring day type. +3 points on Saturdays 17:00 to 21:00 local for 8 Saturdays (2 November to 21 December 2024), read at the third to eighth Saturday, as in experiment 134. Pass at the reference setting (kappa 0.75, k 8, N 8, lambda 1 for ANALOG-k and 0.5 for ANALOG+R): each analog arm recovers at least 0.15 of the shift and at least twice what R recovers, and the placebo (the class is the day type of the date 3 days after the target; same settings) recovers at most what R recovers plus 0.05.
  • G2, a recurring holiday. +3 points on the evening (17:00 to 21:00 local) of the Spring Bank Holiday of 27 May 2024, read at the Spring Bank Holiday of 26 May 2025 (a tuning row). Pass: ANALOG-holiday recovers at least 0.15 of the shift (expected 0.75 x 0.5 x 0.83, about 0.31), and R recovers none, since the earlier occurrence is a year before R's 14 days.
  • G3, a recurring weather state (informative). +3 points on 17:00 to 21:00 local on every day of November 2024 to January 2025 whose forecast daily mean temperature is below 5 degrees C, read at the injected days from the sixth on. ANALOG+R should recover at least 0.05 more than ANALOG+R-notemp. This gate is reported and does not cap the verdict.
  • G1b, the temperature ranking. The G1 injection at k 3 and N 4, where the pool of Saturdays holds more than 3 candidates, read at the same Saturdays; ANALOG-k with temperature and without are reported side by side (informative).
  • G0, no lookahead. +3 points on the readings of the target day T and of T-1, the origin's own day, at the injected Saturday runs: every arm's profile at T must be unchanged to the last digit. Failing G0 invalidates the experiment.
  • Expected values, so that a bug is distinguishable from a pass. Removing each day's mean costs a factor of 5/6 (8 injected half-hours of 48 raise the block mean by 0.5). At the G1 reference the pool of Saturday n holds the 8 Saturdays T-7 to T-56, so k 8 takes all of them, n-1 injected, and the mean share is 0.5625: ANALOG-k about 0.75 x 0.5625 x 0.83 = 0.35, R about 0.089, ANALOG+R about 0.22 (the margin over twice R, 0.178, is 0.04), and the placebo about 0.
  • A failure of G1 or G2 caps every verdict at inconclusive. The gate runs before any replicate or scored forecast is read.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1. ANALOG+R minus R at D+1 in the scored year: -0.005 to -0.03 points.
  • P2. ANALOG-k minus R: 0.00 to +0.05 (a pure mean of at most 12 days is noisier than the 14-day mean).
  • P3. ANALOG+R minus RB-day-types is within 0.01 (day types carry most of the same information).
  • P4. ANALOG+R-notemp minus ANALOG+R is 0.00 to +0.02 (temperature similarity adds little at D+1, because GAM-K already models temperature).
  • P5. On holiday-like days ANALOG-holiday minus R is -0.05 to -0.3 at D+1, with an interval that includes zero, so the predicted outcome is "cannot tell"; in the Christmas window the sign is the same.
  • P6. The gain is largest in winter evenings (16:00 to 20:00 from November to March), and the non-winter estimate lies within 0.005 of zero.
  • P7. Beyond 48 hours the analog arms lose against R, as experiment 134's profile did.
  • P8. The tuned k is 5 or more.
  • Expected verdict. P1's range straddles the 0.02 bar, so small gain or not supported is the expected verdict, and supported would be a surprise.

docs.title: Contrasts and decision rule
docs.text:
• C1 ANALOG+R minus R (decides the verdict), C2 ANALOG-k minus R, C3 ANALOG+R minus RB-day-types, C4 ANALOG-holiday minus R on holiday-like days, C5 ANALOG+R minus K0. Diagnostics: ANALOG+R-notemp minus ANALOG+R, ANALOG-holiday minus R on all rows.
  • Supported if C1's scored-year 99% interval has its upper end at most -0.02; the replicate months have the same sign and an estimate at least half the scored estimate; at least 3 of 5 substations improve in both periods; the winter C1 estimate is at most 0 with its upper end under +0.02; and the gate passes. Small gain if the scored interval lies wholly below zero but its upper end is above -0.02. Not supported if the interval includes zero. Refuted if the interval lies wholly above zero. A gate failure caps every verdict at inconclusive.
  • Holiday verdict, separately, descriptive. Only about 13 holiday-like days fall on scored runs, 8 of them in December, so a month-block interval is very coarse. C4 is reported with its interval, the count of scored holiday-like days, the split between the identity path and the fallback path (and how often the fallback fires), and the number of substations that improve. The arm is a candidate for holidays only when C4's estimate is negative at 4 of 5 substations, both inside and outside the Christmas window, and its 95% interval lies wholly below zero. The replicate months hold no holiday with an earlier occurrence, so they check the fallback path only.
  • Threshold, with the reason. 0.02 points (about 1% of the score), because the change adds a history lookup keyed on day type, holiday identity, and forecast temperature to the serving path, and because experiment 134's day-type arm gained 0.022 over R without such a lookup.
  • Intervals. 99% intervals for the five planned contrasts and 95% for the rest, month blocks resampled, paired across arms (studies.bootstrap.bootstrap_difference_at_level).

docs.title: Breakdowns and checks
