GAM-K's level and the NRA level are the same state: two random-walk levels observed only through their sum cannot be told apart, so a separate fourth state would add nothing. This differs from the brief's wording ("two extra states") on that point only.

Intervals come from the merged causal RO-NC alarm with experiment 147's R2 rule (the onset is known 96 half-hours after the step, the end is known 60 half-hours after the true end, the 6-hour lookahead of experiment 148). When an alarm becomes known at a forecast origin, the filter is re-run from the interval's onset with x switched on over [onset, now], so the step is not left in n. The filter is re-run once per distinct set of known intervals, as experiment 151 does for subtraction.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• K0: GAM-K's filter on the stream, no correction.
  • S-KF: experiment 141's two-regime filter, with 141's chosen prior and multiplier, fed the detected intervals.
  • NEW-DET: the new filter fed the detected intervals.
  • NEW-ORACLE: the new filter fed the true transfer intervals with no delay (the ceiling).
  • CLEAN: GAM-K's filter on the stream without the injected transfers (reported beside, not the denominator of C1).
  • GAM-ONLY, MASK, NEW-DETNOCAP, NEW-DET96, NEW-TRUEEND: see the design changes below.
  • Placebo: see the design changes below (real alarms on the recorded power).

The ratio of x's process noise to n's is set on the tuning months (the odd months) from {10, 100, 1000, 10000}, scored by quantile score on NEW-DET's pre-registered post-alarm rows against the true NRA, as 141 tuned its multiplier; the scored months are not used to choose it.

docs.title: Design changes made before any score was read
docs.text:
The changes below were agreed before any arm was scored. The first run was stopped and discarded.

  • Two denominators. Every share is reported against NEW-ORACLE (the pre-registered C1) and against CLEAN, so the verdict is comparable with experiment 151's.
  • Two floors. GAM-ONLY ignores power (the GAM-K member forecasts with no correction). MASK is K0 with the readings inside every known interval missing, re-run from the onset. If NEW-DET is about as good as MASK, masking is the far smaller production change.
  • End rule. The detected arms use the detected end plus 60 half-hours (the 6-hour lookahead rule's median call lag). A sensitivity arm (NEW-DET96) uses 96 half-hours, the 90th percentile. NEW-TRUEEND keeps the detected alarm but ends the offset at the true end, so the post-end loss from a late end is visible. The offset decays by a factor of 0.5 per reading after its end (one reading per hour band per day), a time constant of 1.4 days, and it is not carried into the forecast.
  • Interval cap. An interval still open 14 days after its onset has its offset folded into the NRA level, because a step with no return would otherwise hold the level frozen. NEW-DETNOCAP shows the effect of the cap.
  • Row sets are not pooled in a headline. Scores are reported separately inside the transfer, in the 48 hours after the true end, and in the remaining rows (detection lag, after the detected end), and by transfer duration (1 to 3 days, 3 to 7 days, over 7 days). C1 stays the pooled post-alarm rows for the decision rule only.
  • Placebo uses real alarms. The placebo is experiment 148's real causal alarms (6-hour lookahead) on the recorded power, with the new filter, MASK, and K0 scored against the recorded series outside the logged switching periods. Intervals shifted by whole weeks are not used.
  • No circular real check. The labelled MW is the detector's own step, so observed power plus labelled MW is not used as the NRA. The real-transfer check is descriptive: forecasts issued inside logged transfers with targets after the logged end, scored against observed power.

docs.title: Rows and windows
docs.text: Experiment 151's: rows of experiment 141's worlds whose origin is after the alarm, with targets inside the transfer or in the 48 hours after its true end; the detection lag (onset to alarm) and the 48 hours after the detected end are reported separately. The first test uses sites D11 and D16 (the two sites with the most injected transfers, 333 and 372 across 141's 44 worlds), the first eight worlds. Widen to the six sites only if C1 passes.

docs.title: Pre-registered checks and risks
docs.text:
• Ceiling identity: with no alarm intervals the new filter equals K0 to 1e-9; checked in the run script.
  • Leakage: a forecast at origin c uses only intervals known at c, and stream values up to c minus the 3.5-hour telemetry delay.
  • Oracle gap: a gap whose own interval includes zero reports no share.
  • Past weather: the residual stream is on the frozen GAM-K, which uses past weather at lag times only through experiment 130's stored panels; the lab shortcut (ERA5 in the residual model) is the same as experiments 141 and 151, and the new filter adds no weather input.
  • Sharing: the scoring harness is a copy of experiment 151's scripts at the time of writing; its session is asked to commit them so they can be diffed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• C1 (pre-registered). NEW-DET closes 78% of the K0-to-NEW-ORACLE gap (99% interval 5% to 107%; 7,579 rows, 35 events, D11 and D16, 8 worlds). Against CLEAN (the filter on the stream without the injected transfer) it closes 69% (95% interval 41% to 96%). The prediction was 40% to 70%.
  • Mean quantile score on those rows (percentage points of effective capacity; smaller is better): K0 4.72, GAM-ONLY 2.89, MASK 2.84, S-KF 5.02, NEW-DET 2.91, NEW-DET96 2.78, NEW-DETNOCAP 2.88, NEW-TRUEEND 2.89, NEW-ORACLE 2.41, CLEAN 2.09.
  • Row sets, NEW-DET minus K0, not pooled. Inside the transfer −1.56 (−2.42 to −1.07). In the 48 hours after the true end −2.13 (−3.37 to +0.01). Before the alarm is known +0.39 (+0.01 to +0.68), MASK loses by a similar +0.35 on these rows. A likely cause is that the filter acts on alarms unrelated to the scored target; this was not tested.
  • Experiment 141's two-regime filter (S-KF) is worse than K0 by +0.30 (+0.13 to +0.36). Its level follows the transfer, as predicted.
  • Offset time constant. The offset decays by a factor of 0.5 per reading after its end is called, one reading per hour band per day, a time constant of 1.4 days. A late end (60 half-hours) costs little: NEW-TRUEEND and NEW-DET differ by 0.02.
  • Interval cap. The 14-day cap with re-absorption changes the score by 0.03 (NEW-DET 2.91 against NEW-DETNOCAP 2.88). The cap has no visible effect.
  • Placebo on real alarms (experiment 148's causal alarms on recorded power, 21,648 rows): NEW-DET minus K0 is +0.58 (−0.79 to +1.71), with a mean median-forecast shift of 4.07 points. MASK gives +0.41 (−1.22 to +1.66). The rule (95% interval within ±0.01) fails.

docs.title: Checks run after scoring
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast error (NEW-DET, C1 rows). D11: median −0.34, mean −0.29. D16: median +3.78, mean +3.76. The median and mean errors are almost equal at each site, so the forecast distribution is roughly symmetric.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile score. Mean absolute error of the mean forecast: K0 7.59, NEW-DET 4.94, NEW-ORACLE 4.29. The mean forecast's error points the same way as the quantile score.
  • Tail calibration on the C1 rows (coverage at the quantile, target in brackets): NEW-DET 0.058 (0.01) at q01, 0.103 (0.05) at q05, 0.961 (0.95) at q95, 0.990 (0.99) at q99. K0: 0.001, 0.006, 0.570, 0.731. NEW-DET's lower quantiles sit too high (5.8% of targets fall below its q01 forecast, against the 1% intended); K0's tails are far worse.
  • Triggers fired: 1 (a control, the placebo, failed), 4 (leaving out D11 gives −119% and leaving out D16 gives 103%), and 5 (GAM-ONLY, a nested arm with less input, beats K0). A Sonnet audit ran ; the audit's findings are triaged below.

docs.title: Audit findings and triage
docs.text:
• NEW-DET is effectively MASK. NEW-DET minus MASK is +0.071 (−0.001 to +0.115), and NEW-DET never beats MASK by more than 0.05 in any event or duration stratum. At offset-noise ratio 10^12 the filter reproduces the plain filter on a masked stream. We accept this finding; it is the main finding.
  • The oracle gap is mostly "stop reading the corrupted power". K0's mean absolute median error grows from 5.3 to 9.9 points as the step ages. We accept this finding; the verdict is unchanged.
  • A few events dominate. Two D11 events and one D16 event hold 94% of the summed gap. Weighting each event equally gives 63%, and each site equally 66% (D11 alone 103%, D16 alone −119%). Dropping the three largest events by gap gives −322%. We accept this finding; the pooled share is not robust.
  • The oracle is not a clean ceiling at D16. Real alarms there overlap injected events, so masking arms lose against recorded power that holds real shifts. We accept this as a caveat.
  • The placebo rule is not a fair test. The 12 real alarms with scored rows last 1 to 16 days. Ten of them show a mean level shift of 4 to 21 points, and none is a zero or a bank holiday, so K0 follows the real level and any arm that acts is penalised. A usable placebo needs known false alarms (experiment 151's list of unexplained alarms is the candidate). We accept this finding; the plan's week-shifted placebo was replaced on the manager's request and is not run.
  • The tuned ratio is weak. It was tuned on 401 rows from 4 events, all at D11, and 10000 is the edge of the grid. Ratio 10 scores a higher C1 share (84.5%) on the scored rows. We accept this finding; the verdict is unchanged.
  • Leakage and algebra. No leakage found; the filter matches the plain filter to 1e-14 with no open interval. The end-call lag at 96 half-hours gives 84%. No change to the verdict.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lab conditions: ERA5-based residuals and true injected megawatts, as in experiments 141 and 151.
  • The real-transfer check the manager asked for (forecasts issued inside logged real transfers, scored after the logged end) was not run; the placebo on real alarms was meant to cover the no-harm part but cannot, so no-harm on real transfers is untested.
  • Six-site widening was not run, because C1 did not pass.
  • What the next experiment should answer: whether any transfer-aware filter beats MASK on transfers that mask handles badly, such as short transfers (1 to 3 days) and real level shifts that do not return, scored per event and against known false alarms.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, N0 gate 2: the partly pooled convex model's heating error against the injected truth
docs.text:
On synthetic substations with a known heating curve, a partly pooled regression model estimated the heating response of a substation with only 4 winter weeks of data better than fitting that substation alone or copying the fleet's curve, but no method recovered the sign of the substation's own deviation from the fleet's curve on most seeds. The fleet's shared heating curve was recovered as well as the average of separate per-substation fits recovers it. In this synthetic test, sharing the heating curve across substations therefore worked, and a substation's own offset from that curve was not learnable from 4 weeks. The next experiment, which fits a partly pooled generalised additive model (GAM, a demand model built from smooth curves), should not rely on offsets learned from 4 weeks. The verdict is partly supported: three of the four pass-or-fail lines written down before the run hold (listed under "Pre-registered lines").

The method is the convex regression model of experiment 109. The model gives each substation the fleet's shared coefficients plus a penalised deviation of its own ("partial pooling"; the model is convex, so its fit has one optimum). Experiment 150 could not tell whether the method shrinks a substation's own coefficients correctly, because in 4 weeks of June the heating signal is weak.

Each synthetic substation has a known heating curve: one shared by the fleet plus its own offset. The eight synthetic substations use the real calendar and weather of real substations. Each synthetic substation in turn keeps only the 4 weeks before 2025-02-01, when heating dominates demand, and the other seven keep 2 years. The experiment repeats this procedure on five random draws of the injected coefficients ("seeds"). The injected fleet coefficients and the noise level are the same as in experiment 150.

Terms used below. The "fleet" is the eight synthetic substations. The "heating error" is the root mean square of the fitted heating contribution to demand minus the injected one. It is taken over the November to March rows of the substation's 2 years of calendar and weather, and is stated in points of effective capacity (percentage points of the substation's capacity). The "offset" is the substation's mean heating contribution minus the fleet curve's. The "fair oracle" is a reference estimator that is told the fleet mean, the true spread of each coefficient, and the noise variance, and then estimates every coefficient from the same 4 weeks. The two "controls" are the pooled fit run with no pooling (penalty 0 rows of evidence) and with complete pooling (penalty 1,000,000 rows). The "pooled fit" uses the penalty experiment 150 tuned on each seed (300 to 1,000 rows).

docs.title: Pre-registered lines
docs.text:
• W1, the shared curve. W1 holds on a seed when the fleet curve's error is at most 1.1 times the per-site average's error. The fleet curve's error is measured against the injected fleet mean and averaged over the eight turns. The per-site average is the average of the penalty-0 fits.
  • W2, close to the fair oracle. The pooled fit's heating error is at most 1.1 times the fair oracle's.
  • W2b, better than both controls. The pooled fit's heating error is below no pooling's and below complete pooling's.
  • W3, the offset's sign. The pooled fit's offset has the injected sign at 6 or more of the 8 substations, and the slope of the fitted offsets on the injected offsets, through the origin, is positive.
  • Decision. A line holds when it passes on at least 4 of 5 seeds; the verdict rule is in the front matter.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Every number below is printed in report.txt. Errors are in points of effective capacity.

Line (pre-registered) Seeds passed Detail W1, shared curve within 10% of per-site fits 5 of 5 Fleet-curve error 0.52 to 1.31, against 0.62 to 1.28 for the per-site average. W2, pooled error within 10% of the fair oracle 4 of 5 Seed 2 missed: 3.61 against the oracle's 2.80. W2b, pooled error below both controls 5 of 5 Complete pooling came closest, 0.10 behind the pooled fit on seed 3. W3, own offset has the injected sign 2 of 5 Signs right at 4, 6, 3, 6, and 4 of 8 substations.
  • The pooled fit's heating error is below complete pooling's and no pooling's on every seed. Pooled fit: 2.84, 3.61, 3.28, 3.08, and 3.39. Complete pooling: 3.72, 4.63, 3.38, 3.57, and 3.93. No pooling: 8.34, 5.89, 8.36, 11.52, and 4.13. Fair oracle: 3.37, 2.80, 3.91, 4.07, and 4.00.
  • Three of the four lines hold, including W2b, so the verdict is partly supported.
  • Most of the pooled fit's gain over no pooling comes from sharing the curve, not from the substation's own offset. The pooled fit's margin over complete pooling is 0.10 points on seed 3 and 0.48 to 1.02 points on the other four seeds.
  • Even the fair oracle reached 6 of 8 correct offset signs on only two seeds. This comparison was added after the run. The fair oracle got the sign right at 3, 8, 5, 7, and 5 of 8 substations, the pooled fit at 4, 6, 3, 6, and 4, and no pooling at 4, 3, 4, 3, and 3. The oracle reached 6 or more on seeds 2 and 4, the same two seeds as the pooled fit. The pooled offsets' slope on the injected offsets was 0.50, 0.53, -0.06, 0.67, and 0.27, against the oracle's 0.35, 1.00, 0.26, 1.47, and 0.66.
  • The error of the fitted coefficients themselves (root mean square of fitted minus injected coefficient) is lowest for the pooled fit on 4 of 5 seeds. The pooled fit's 1.87 to 2.46 beat the oracle's 2.30 to 4.06 on every seed and complete pooling's 2.10 to 2.63 on every seed except seed 4, where complete pooling's 2.20 is just below the pooled fit's 2.26.

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text:
• Predicted: heating error below both controls on 4 or 5 of 5 seeds. Observed 5 of 5.
  • Predicted: within 10% of the fair oracle on 5 of 5 seeds. Observed 4 of 5; seed 2 is the miss.
  • Predicted: own-offset sign right at 6 or more of 8 on 3 or 4 of 5 seeds. Observed 2 of 5. A prediction of 3 seeds was already a predicted failure of W3, which needs 4. The fair oracle also reached 6 of 8 on only 2 seeds, which points to the information in 4 weeks, and the oracle's edge on some seeds has an explanation in its extra knowledge (see the caveats).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, per site. Not applicable: the gate scores coefficients and noise-free truth, not forecasts.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each contrast. Not applicable for the same reason; the contrasts here are errors against the injected truth.
  • Audit triggers that fired. Trigger 1 (a known-answer line, W3, fails) and trigger 7 (a later experiment's design, the partly pooled GAM, depends on this gate). Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fires only for W3's sign count. Triggers 3 to 6 do not apply. One Sonnet reviewer re-derived the numbers from the stored runs and read the code. No Opus audit ran. The next experiment should treat the offset result as unreplicated beyond one January and five seeds.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The fleets share the real calendar, weather, and noise weeks, and differ only in the injected coefficients, so the 5 seeds are not independent replicates of the noise. The held weeks are one January.
  • The oracle's offset is measured against the true fleet mean, and the pooled fit's against its fitted fleet mean. The oracle's prior mean also includes the held-out substation's own truth (1 of 8). Both choices flatter the oracle and hurt the pooled fit on the offset's sign.
  • The penalty is experiment 150's, tuned on June and not retuned for January.
  • The injection is into the synthetic series, not into the residuals of a fitted real substation. Truth for every coefficient is therefore known, and the fleet's heating curve is the six real Primaries' fitted curve with injected spread.
  • The pooled fit is given the true capacity of the seven full-history substations (inherited from experiments 109 and 150).
  • Each model is fitted once, at the 2025-02-01 cut, so the contrasts do not depend on a retraining schedule.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: Plan the partly pooled GAM shapes experiment so that the shared curve is pooled and the substation's offset comes from its full history, not from 4 weeks. Use at least a winter's rows for any substation whose own offset is scored, because the sign of the offset was not found from 4 weeks by any method tried.

docs.title: Experiment 155: recipe R improves the stage 1 forecast; the night offset adds nothing
docs.text:
Subtracting recipe R's error profile from the stage 1 forecast lowers its score by about 0.04 points, and the winter night offset adds nothing once R is in. The stage 1 forecast (arm A) is the convex demand model with a Kalman filter on recent errors, driven by the ensemble-mean weather forecast, from experiment 136. The score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of a substation's effective capacity (lower is better), over forecasts 0.5 to 168 hours ahead at five Primary substations in the year from July 2025 (the scored year).

Recipe R (experiment 115) subtracts 0.75 times the mean error of the last 14 days, by half-hour of the day. The winter night offset is a ridge-fitted correction for the half-hours from 21:30 to 09:00 UTC that depends on whether it is winter (November to March) and on the weekend; it comes from the audit of experiment 137. Arm A scored 2.791. Adding R gave 2.754 (contrast C2, -0.037; 99% interval from resampling calendar months -0.062 to -0.016). Adding the offset alone gave 2.774 (C1, -0.017; -0.033 to -0.002). Adding both gave 2.756 (C3, -0.035; -0.061 to -0.014), and the offset on top of R changed the score by +0.002 (C4; -0.004 to +0.009).

The best arm is therefore arm C, R alone. It scores 0.026 points below BG2 (2.780), the production recipe, with an interval too wide to rank the two. The verdict is inconclusive because a placebo planned in advance (the offset with its winter indicator moved six months) gained as much as the real offset, and the plan caps the verdict when that happens. The audit showed the placebo could not tell the two apart, so the cap does not change the choice of arm C. Without the cap the verdict would be partly supported, because C3's upper bound (-0.014) is above the -0.02 threshold. The next experiments start from arm C.

We added each correction to experiment 136's stored forecasts, alone and together, refitted each arm's spread, and scored every arm on the same half-hourly rows. The analog correction of experiment 145 is an extra arm.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and schedule. A is experiment 136's A2 as stored. B adds the winter night offset. C adds R at every lead. D adds R to B (R on B's own past errors). C48 and D48 limit R to leads of 48 hours or less. E adds experiment 145's tuned analog correction to B. B0 is the offset without the winter indicator (ablation). The fits are experiment 136's monthly refits on a 24-month window, so every contrast is within that schedule.
  • Rows. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29, five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16; D9 beside them), outside the hand-filtered switching events. The headline rows (464,228 at the five decision substations) are those that every arm and BG2, climatology, and the manual heuristic share. The store holds 291 scored runs per substation, not the 292 the plan names. Five outage rows at D16 (actual 0) leave the headline because BG2 has no actual there.
  • Absolute skill, all leads (points of effective capacity). A 2.791, B 2.774, C 2.754, D 2.756, C48 2.777, D48 2.766, E 2.757, B0 2.788, experiment 111's GAM-K 2.800, BG2 2.780, manual heuristic 3.497, climatology 3.804. Day D+1: A 2.489, B 2.462, C 2.436, D 2.432, E 2.393, BG2 2.535, GAM-K 2.521. Replicate months (even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06), all leads: A 2.710, B 2.719, C 2.664, D 2.688, E 2.711.
  • C1, B minus A (offset). -0.017 (-0.033 to -0.002), 5 of 5 substations, 11 of 12 months; replicate +0.009 (-0.022 to +0.048). Cold nights (daily mean below 2 °C, 5,395 rows) -0.058.
  • C2, C minus A (R). -0.037 (-0.062 to -0.016), 5 of 5 substations, 12 of 12 months; D+1 -0.053 (-0.087 to -0.022); replicate -0.047 (-0.106 to -0.001). Leaving out any one substation gives -0.029 to -0.042.
  • C3, D minus A. -0.035 (-0.061 to -0.014); replicate -0.022 (-0.079 to +0.030). It lies 0.019 from the sum of C1 and C2, inside the predicted 0.02.
  • C4, D minus C. +0.002 (-0.004 to +0.009); replicate +0.024 (0.000 to +0.067). C5, D minus B. -0.018 (-0.034 to -0.004).
  • C6, D minus BG2. -0.024 (-0.220 to +0.153), D+1 -0.103 (-0.306 to +0.093). C14, A minus BG2 +0.010 (-0.164 to +0.174), as experiment 136 found; C13 is A minus experiment 111's GAM-K, -0.009. The intervals are 0.3 to 0.4 points wide, so no arm can be ranked against BG2.
  • C7, E minus D. +0.001 (-0.010 to +0.014) over all leads, -0.039 (-0.056 to -0.010) at D+1; E scores 0.08 worse than D (interval -0.008 to +0.177) and 0.12 worse than A on bank holidays other than Christmas.
  • C8 and C9, limiting R to 48 hours. C48 minus C +0.023 (+0.007 to +0.041); D48 minus D +0.010 (-0.001 to +0.021). R helps beyond 48 hours as well.
  • Spread refit (post hoc). Using arm A's spread table for the corrected means scores 0.002 to 0.005 better than each arm's own refit (B 2.771, C 2.750, D 2.751), so refitting the spread on tuning months that start with little history costs a little.
  • Predictions against outcome. C1 -0.017 against -0.02 to -0.04 (a little short; cold nights (daily mean below 2 °C) -0.058 against -0.10 to -0.30, a miss; on experiment 136's 3 °C definition -0.098, at the edge of the range). C2 -0.037 inside -0.03 to -0.08; at D+1 -0.053 against -0.07 to -0.12 (a miss). C3 inside 0.02 of the sum. C48 and D48 worse by 0.023 and 0.010 (inside 0.00 to 0.03). E minus D at D+1 -0.039 (inside), all leads +0.001 (inside). The best arm scored 2.754 against 2.67 to 2.75 (just outside), and minus BG2 -0.026 against -0.03 to -0.11 (just outside). The cold-night q95 coverage rose by 1.1 percentage points at most (predicted 2 to 6).
  • Verdict by the pre-registered rule. The placebo control failed, so the verdict is capped at inconclusive. The winning arm is C: its all-lead score is the lowest, D (2.756) and E (2.757) are within 0.005 points, and C comes first in the tie order.

Christmas rows only (7,775 rows): B -0.035, C -0.054, D -0.054, BG2 -0.921. Bank holidays without Christmas (11,138 rows): B +0.041, C +0.015, D +0.037, E +0.119, BG2 +0.653.

Against A, B's difference is +0.003 (+0.001 to +0.005, passes the +0.02 bound) and the R arms' is -0.048 (-0.139 to +0.032, fails the bound by its upper end and shows no growth in the point estimate). The production cadence is not tested.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per substation: 0.000 for arms A, B, and D at all six substations, because the residual table is centred, so this check exposes nothing here.
  • Mean forecast's error beside each contrast (mean absolute error): C1 -0.035, C2 -0.090, C3 -0.087, C4 +0.003, C7 +0.009. Every contrast moves in the direction of its quantile score.
  • Leave-one-out: removing any one substation leaves C1 at -0.015 to -0.019, C2 at -0.029 to -0.042, and C3 at -0.028 to -0.041, so the leave-one-out reversal check (trigger 4) did not fire.
  • Controls. Reproduction: arm A rescored on experiment 136's rows gives 2.791 (passed). Spread refit with a zero shift reproduces A's quantiles to 1.5e-5 (passed). Leakage: corrupting actual by 100 points from each cut (offset) and from the origin's own day (R) changed no applied shift (maximum change 0.0, passed). Injected known answer: the winter-night step of 6 points is recovered as 5.60 points at every substation (93%), and R's shift on an injected daily shape of 3 points is +2.06 (0.75 times the day-mean-corrected 2.75), inside 25% of +2.25 (passed). Placebo: failed. The offset with the winter indicator moved six months scored 2.774, the same as B (difference +0.00002), against a pass rule of at most half of C1.
  • Zero-shift runs. R's shift is zero for 4 of 184 tuning runs and none of the replicate or scored runs at each substation.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 1 (the placebo) and trigger 2 (predictions missed on cold nights and at D+1). Trigger 5 did not fire, because C4's interval includes zero, although arm C scores 0.002 below arm D. Triggers 3, 4, and 6 did not fire. The independent audit (Opus) is in the private briefs folder (e155_audit_report.md) and is triaged below.

docs.title: Audit and triage
docs.text:
• Finding 1, placebo (accepted). The placebo was degenerate: with per-slot constants, a May to September indicator spans nearly the same space as a November to March indicator. A scan of 55 month sets found that a five-month window gains about -0.017 only when it splits the year into winter and summer halves, and 40 random five-month sets gained -0.003 on average (none as much as the real flag). The gain therefore needs a seasonal split, and the real flag is the best one. The cap stays because the rule was pre-registered, and the scan is reported as a labelled post hoc control.
  • Finding 2, the two corrections overlap (accepted). R fitted on B's errors removes about 58% of the offset at night, and R's day-mean removal moves the offset's level onto daytime half-hours, so D is worse than C by +0.005 (+0.002 to +0.008) in daytime. No order of the two beats C. The offset is dropped from the winning arm.
  • Finding 3, Christmas (accepted). Rows and units match; BG2's advantage is real for one event. It is reported as one event, with no ranking.
  • Findings 4 and 5, no leakage and row-set details (accepted). The row-set details are stated in the Results.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One scored year. The offset is fitted on one earlier winter, and the replicate months show the offset's sign reversed (+0.009), so the offset's evidence is thin. The selection of arm C uses the scored year, and the replicate months agree on R (-0.047).
  • The intervals against BG2 are 0.3 to 0.4 points wide, so the ranking of the corrected arms against BG2 is open.
  • Analog source days. Arm E has fewer source days than experiment 145 had, because the stored forecasts omit the every-fifth-day stride runs and the runs before 2024-07.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Calibrate the tails of arm C on cold nights, where the q95 covers 82.7% of rows.
  • Test a run-day term for 27 to 31 December (the audit's candidate) and the winter offset again at a second winter, with a placebo made of random month sets, only if R's daytime effect is solved.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
Question. Experiment 136 assembled a GAM-K with the heating split (T-all), one shared filter noise setting (POOL), the pinned solar capacity, and the ensemble mean as its weather input, and could not rank it against BG2. Two later experiments found corrections that act on the finished forecast: a winter night offset (the audit of experiment 137) and the 14-day error profile of recipe R (experiment 115). This experiment adds them to experiment 136's A2 one at a time and together, scores every arm on the same rows, and picks the winning arm that the calibration experiments start from. No new modelling: every piece exists, and the code is copied from experiments 136, 137, and 145.

Arms. All arms share the rows and the weather of experiment 136's A2, the pinned capacity of experiment 139 (which found that replacing the pin does not help, so the pin is kept), and the filter noise of experiment 136.

Arm Built from Added piece A Experiment 136's A2 forecasts as stored none: GAM-K, T-all, POOL, pinned capacity, ensemble mean B A winter night offset C A recipe R at every lead D B recipe R at every lead, fitted on B's own past errors C48 A recipe R at leads of 48 hours or less (variant) D48 B recipe R at leads of 48 hours or less (variant) E B the analog correction of experiment 145 (ANALOG+R, tuned values) at every lead, in place of R B0 A the offset's per-slot constants and weekend flag only, without the winter indicator (ablation, no verdict)

Reference arms. BG2, experiment 111's GAM-K, ref_climatology, and ref_manual_heuristic, as stored and read as experiment 136 reads them.

The winter night offset (arm B). For each of the 24 half-hours that end between 21:30 and 09:00 UTC, the offset is a[h] + w[h] * winter + c[h] * weekend, where winter is 1 when the evening's date (the UTC date 21:30 before the half-hour ends, so post-midnight half-hours take the previous date) falls from November to March, and 0 otherwise, and weekend flags Saturday and Sunday evenings. The coefficients are a ridge regression of arm A's own past errors (actual minus mean forecast) on those 72 columns. They are fitted per substation on all rows whose run origin and valid time are both before the first day of the month being forecast (an expanding window, refitted monthly, starting from 2024-07), as in experiment 137, with experiment 137's ridge penalty of 100. The offset replaces experiment 137's temperature term because the audit of that experiment found a winter indicator matched it and so the data show a winter night bias and not a step that grows with cold. The offset shifts every quantile and the mean.

Recipe R (arms C, D, C48, D48). For a run with origin on UTC day O, the target day is T = O + 1. The profile is the mean over the source days T - 15 to T - 2 (at least 3 of them usable) of each source day's D+1 error block, by local half-hour with the day's mean removed. A source day's block is the error of the pre-R forecast of the run issued on the day before it, over its leads of 15.5 to 39 hours. The shift added to every row of the run is minus 0.75 times the profile at the row's local half-hour. The code is e00145_analog.py's recipe R, copied. In arm D the pre-R forecast is B, so R is fitted on the errors that remain after the offset and the two corrections do not count the same error twice. The 48-hour variants zero the shift on rows with a lead above 48 hours.

The analog correction (arm E). Experiment 145's ANALOG+R with its tuned values (20 source days of the same day type within 13 weeks of the target's day of the year, weight 0.5 of the analog profile against R's 14-day profile, kappa 1.0), added to B at every lead. The values are not retuned here. The loss beyond 48 hours that experiment 145 found is why the variants exist, and arm E is read at D+1 and at every lead.

Spread. Each arm's quantiles are its corrected mean plus a residual table (hour band by calendar quarter by lead band) fitted on that arm's own corrected forecasts in the tuning months (the odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06), every spread factor 1, as experiment 136 and experiment 145 do. Experiment 137 left the spread unchanged instead. The spread's width is therefore not a second thing the arms differ in, and the comparison with the residual table of arm A's uncorrected forecast (a post hoc sensitivity row for each of B, C, and D: the arm's corrected mean with arm A's residual table) shows how much the refit matters, because the correction arms' tuning-year forecasts start from an empty or thin history and may give wider tables than the scored year needs. Experiment 125 found factors tuned on alternate months scored worse out of period, so no factor is tuned. The comparison spread (the pooled quantile model with factor 1.15 of the BG2 recipe) is the stored BG2 and is not recomputed.

Rows and periods. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, 09:00 UTC power_fcst_init_time, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, rows outside the hand-filtered switching events. The scored year is the 292 runs from 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29. The tuning months are the odd months and the replicate months the even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, as in experiment 136. D-labels only. The error stream that R and the offset read is the corrected forecasts of the stored tuning, replicate, and scored runs. The every-fifth-day stride runs of the scored year are in no stored forecast, so R's 14-day profile has about 11 source days there, and the minimum of 3 is met. A run with fewer than 3 usable source days gets a shift of zero, and the count of such runs per arm and period is reported. The corrections use every row with a reading, switching-masked rows included, because switching information is not used in this pass; the scores and the spread tables exclude the masked rows. The ridge penalty of 100 and experiment 145's tuned values are reused without retuning.

Weather and what exists at forecast time. The weather is the calibrated ensemble mean of experiment 136, and the filter uses an analysis proxy built from earlier runs. The offset uses the calendar only, and R and the analog correction use errors of days that ended before the origin. Every input exists at forecast time.

Scoring. The headline is the quantile score over leads 0.5 to 168 hours at the five decision substations in the scored year. Beside it:

  • lead bands (under 24 hours, 24 to 72 hours, 72 to 168 hours) and day D+1;
  • cold nights: night and evening half-hours (the night and evening hour bands of experiment 136) of the winter days whose ERA5 daily mean 2 m temperature at the substation's grid box is below 2 °C, at all leads; experiment 136's definition (an ERA5 half-hourly temperature of 3 °C or below) is reported as well so that the two experiments can be compared, and q95 coverage is the second headline for the cold-night rows because experiment 125 found it was 73% to 78%;
  • holiday and Christmas rows: rows on a bank holiday or in the Christmas run days (the holiday_period of the calendar), with the Christmas rows reported alone;
  • tail calibration at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles, overall, on cold nights, and by hour band (night, evening, morning, and day, as in experiment 136);
  • the quantile score by UTC half-hour from 21:00 to 09:00 on winter nights, for A, B, and D, to show whether the offset worsens the 22:00 to 23:00 half-hours as experiment 137's term did;
  • the quantile score by lead hour for leads up to 24 hours, and the score at leads of 0.5 to 3.5 hours, 3.5 to 9.5 hours, and 9.5 to 24 hours, for each arm. The production service will refresh its forecast every 6 hours with an input that is 3.5 hours old, so a forecast used in production is up to 9.5 hours older than its origin. The check is whether an arm's error grows between those lead bands by more than arm A's, which would make the corrections fragile under that cadence. The production cadence itself is not tested here;
  • absolute scores for every arm and for the reference arms, and the mean absolute error of the mean forecast beside every quantile-score contrast.

Planned contrasts. C1 B minus A (the offset), C2 C minus A (R), C3 D minus A (both: the headline), C4 D minus C (the offset on top of R), C5 D minus B (R on top of the offset), C6 D minus BG2, C7 E minus D (the analog correction in place of R), C8 C48 minus C (limiting R to 48 hours), C9 D48 minus D, C10 C48 minus A, C11 D48 minus A, and C12 E minus A. Each is read at the 99% level. The replicate months give the sign.

Controls, run before any contrast is read.

  • Reproduction. Arm A, rescored from the stored forecasts of experiment 136 on the same common rows, scores 2.791 over leads 0.5 to 168 hours, within 0.001.
  • Leakage. Add 100 points to actual at every valid time on or after each month's cut, in a copy of the frames, and rebuild every correction. Pass: no correction applied to the month changes (a maximum change of 0.0), for the offset and for R. For R the control also corrupts actual from the origin's own day and checks that the run's shift is unchanged, because the newest source day is T - 2.
  • Injected known answer. In a control copy of the frames, add a winter-night step of known size (6 points on the half-hours from 01:00 to 08:30 UTC, November to March) and a daily shape error of known size (3 points on the half-hours ending 17:00 to 19:00 local time, every day) to the actual of every row, the scored year included, and rebuild the corrections. Pass: the fitted winter-night offset minus the clean fit's offset, averaged over the injected half-hours at the cuts of 2025-11 onward, is within 25% of 6 points at 5 of 6 substations, and R's shift on the injected half-hours minus the clean shift has a mean within 25% of +2.25 points (0.75 times the injected 3 points; error is actual minus forecast in this sentence, and the code's forecast minus actual sign is the opposite, so the shift is plus 0.75 times the mean actual minus forecast).
  • Placebo. Shift the winter indicator by six months (so winter is 1 from May to September) and refit. Pass: the placebo's all-lead score change against A in the scored year is at most half of C1's, read only if C1's interval lies wholly below zero (otherwise the placebo is reported and not read). The offset's per-slot constants carry about a third of its gain (experiment 137's audit), so the placebo is not expected to be zero, and the ablation B0 shows how much the constants carry.

Five triggers (size). Stored: private files only. Serving path: not touched. Degradation rule: not touched. More than one design defensible: yes, three, each pre-registered above. Callers not nameable without searching: no, the scripts copy experiments 136, 137, and 145.

Audit triggers to watch. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) and trigger 5 (a nested arm beating the arm that contains it, which could be arm D against arm B and arm C) are the likely ones. The write-up lists which fired and tells the manager if any did.

Resources. Central processing unit (CPU) only, at most 8 cores with one thread per worker, each job under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue. No GPU. The jobs read stored forecasts, so a full run is expected to take minutes.

Outputs. Predictions for every arm in the dp_preds layout (q01 to q99, actual, switching_mask, 09:00 UTC origins, leads up to 168 hours) for D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, under data/ml-experiments/00155-dp-bg-stage2-assembly-night-offset-and-error-correction/work/dp_preds/, so that the substation cards can be rebuilt from the winning arm.

Advice followed and departures. From experiment 136: keep T-all; check POOL's cold-night tails (the tail table reports them). From experiment 137: test a seasonal offset and judge on cold winter nights and also on the 22:00 to 23:00 half-hours (the by-hour figure shows them). From experiment 145: apply the analog and weekday terms at D+1 only (the C48 and D48 variants test whether R itself should be limited; the brief's recipe applies it at every lead) and leave holiday-like days on R's 14-day profile. From experiment 139: keep the pinned capacity. Provisional: the offset, because experiment 137 failed its placebo and its readability rule; this experiment is a second winter of evidence only in the sense that the scored year is the same year, so it adds no independent winter.

docs.title: A faster onset alarm from simultaneous opposite steps at a metered neighbour, feeding a mask forecast
docs.text:
Take-home message. A load transfer is an operator moving demand from one substation to a neighbour by switching. The refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC) learns of a transfer about 48 hours after the step, because it waits 24 hours for the step and 24 more for the peak. An alarm that fires when one metered substation steps by several noise units (multiples of its usual half-hour-to-half-hour variation) and a connected metered substation steps the opposite way is known 3 to 9 hours after the step, depending on the window (2, 4, or 6 hours). On the transfers the alarm finds, masking the readings from it closes 95% of the forecast-error gap to the true series, against 40% for RO-NC's mask. The alarm finds few transfers: 38% of the simulated transfers, counted one by one (RO-NC 69%), and 5 of 35 real ones (RO-NC 20). Pooled over all forecasts, masking from either alarm scores 0.119 points of capacity better than masking from RO-NC alone, and, on all rows after a transfer begins, no mask beats the weather-model-only forecast.

We asked whether a much earlier alarm would let the mask forecast of experiment 151 start masking days before RO-NC raises its alarm. A transfer moves power from one substation to its neighbours, so the two substations step in opposite directions at the same time, while weather and holidays move neighbours the same way. We built an alarm on that pair of steps over windows of 2, 4, and 6 hours, and set its threshold so that its real alarms in odd months that no logged switching explains number at most 80, as RO-NC's do. We then added simulated transfers (from experiment 141 and experiment 147) to the recorded half-hourly power of six Primary substations, in 44 simulated copies of the record (worlds), and scored two measures: how soon each alarm is known (the lag from the step), and the forecast error of a mask driven by each alarm. The mask sets the readings missing from the alarm's start until its end is called. The forecast is a weather-driven generalised additive model (GAM) whose Kalman filter corrects it with recent power, scored against the true series without the simulated transfers, in points of effective capacity (percent of the substation's capacity; smaller is better).

By the pre-registered rule the verdict is partly supported. The speed test (C1) is supported. The forecast test (C4) is not: masking from either alarm scores 0.119 points better than masking from RO-NC (negative is better), but the upper end of the 99% interval is -0.025, above the required -0.10. The no-harm test on real rows (C5) is not supported either. The pair alarm adds almost no recall to RO-NC, because 223 of the 231 even-month transfers it finds (4-hour window) are also found by RO-NC.

  • Arms. RO-NC (alarm known 48 hours after the step), the pair alarm NEW (known 1.5 windows after the step: a peak test of half a window, then the window itself), and UNION (the intervals of either alarm, merged within 24 hours). An interval is the span the mask treats as a transfer. The mask arms are MASK-RONC, MASK-NEW, and MASK-UNION, beside no correction (K0), the forecast fed the true series (CLEAN), and the weather model alone (GAM-only). The end of every interval uses RO-NC's offline end rule, called as in experiment 148, so the onset alarm is the only difference. Weather in the filter's residual is ERA5, as in experiments 141 and 151 (past weather standing in for the forecast, which flatters every arm equally); no refit runs.
  • Tuning. Matched thresholds k: 4.5 (2 h), 3.75 (4 h), and 3.5 (6 h), giving 68, 66, and 57 real unexplained alarms in odd months. The 4-hour window had the highest share of moved MW found on odd-month transfers (0.760, against 0.736 and 0.752) and is the headline.
  • Detection, even-month transfers (611 of the 1,160 in the 44 worlds). Median lag from the step to the alarm being known: 6 hours against 48. Share of moved MW found 0.749 for the pair alarm, 0.901 for RO-NC, and 0.902 for the union (shares of moved MW, not of transfers); C2 is -0.152 (95% -0.226 to -0.097) and C3 is +0.001 (95% -0.022 to +0.031). Of the 1,160 simulated transfers, 43% have a metered receiver. Those carry 89% of the moved MW (the coverage). The window sets the lag, so the lag does not vary between transfers and its interval has zero width.
  • C4, all 277,056 forecast rows after a transfer began (12 months of target time). Mean quantile score in points of capacity: K0 3.549, CLEAN 2.416, GAM-only 3.025, MASK-RONC 3.338, MASK-NEW 3.233, MASK-UNION 3.219. MASK-UNION minus MASK-RONC -0.119 (95% -0.215 to -0.052; 99% -0.244 to -0.025); MASK-NEW minus MASK-RONC -0.105 (95% -0.355 to +0.099); MASK-NEW minus GAM-only +0.209 (95% +0.069 to +0.281). Share of the K0-to-CLEAN gap closed: MASK-RONC 19%, MASK-NEW 28%, MASK-UNION 29%, GAM-only 46%.
  • Where the mask helps. On the 29,582 rows of transfers the pair alarm finds, MASK-NEW closes 95% of the gap (95% interval 91% to 97%), MASK-RONC 40%, and MASK-UNION 72%. After RO-NC's alarm is known, MASK-RONC closes 79% and MASK-NEW 28%. Before RO-NC's alarm, MASK-NEW closes 28% (16% to 58%) and MASK-RONC -5% (worse than no correction).
  • Each transfer weighted equally (475 transfers). MASK-UNION minus MASK-RONC -0.133 (95% -0.225 to -0.043). Without D11, which supplies 48% of rows: -0.213 (95% -0.310 to -0.107). Leaving out any one of the six substations keeps the sign of the union contrast.
  • C5, real stream (874,369 rows outside logged transfers), minus no correction. MASK-RONC +0.228 (95% +0.086 to +0.403), MASK-UNION +0.140 (+0.033 to +0.265), MASK-NEW +0.064 (-0.002 to +0.135), GAM-only +0.297 (+0.216 to +0.387); positive is worse. Forecasts issued inside a logged real transfer and scored after its end (9 pairs of a logged transfer and a substation): K0 9.843, MASK-RONC 5.018, MASK-UNION 4.496, MASK-NEW 5.824, GAM-only 4.713.
  • False alarms by substation (all months, no logged closure within 24 hours, 4-hour window). The pair alarm raises 9 at substation D8 and 0 at D9. RO-NC raises 28 at D8 and 33 at D9. The 2-hour window raises 23 at D8 and 1 at D9.
  • Real transfers over a day (35). The pair alarm finds 6, 5, and 7 at the 2, 4, and 6-hour windows (median lag 3.2, 6.5, and 9.5 hours); RO-NC finds 20.
  • Tail calibration after onset (share of actuals at or below the quantile; pinball loss). K0: q01 0.024 (0.280), q05 0.049 (0.851), q95 0.814 (1.104), q99 0.906 (0.460). MASK-RONC: 0.029 (0.329), 0.060 (0.880), 0.858 (0.949), 0.931 (0.365). MASK-UNION: 0.024 (0.293), 0.053 (0.824), 0.868 (0.938), 0.936 (0.369). GAM-only: 0.002 (0.185), 0.012 (0.694), 0.822 (0.855), 0.921 (0.311). All arms use the same uncertainty width, so these are contrasts in the forecast's location. The masks move the upper tail (q95 and q99) towards the nominal 0.95 and 0.99.
  • Post hoc arms (labelled; the pre-registered verdict is unchanged). MASK-NEW at the 2-hour and 6-hour windows: 3.212 and 3.256. MASK-NEW with the alarm series only (no partner): 3.333. The pair alarm plus only those RO-NC intervals that match an injected transfer (an oracle, because it uses the truth): 3.086, which is 0.215 below the union's 3.301 for the same construction without the filter, so RO-NC's alarms that match no injected transfer worsen the score by about 0.2 points.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast by substation: D10 -0.076, D11 -0.044, D14 +0.084, D16 +0.040, D5 -0.347, D9 -0.091 points of capacity, identical for every arm.
  • Mean-forecast contrast has the same sign as the quantile score: MASK-UNION minus MASK-RONC -0.204 (95% -0.312 to -0.103) in the error of the mean forecast and -0.204 in the error of the median forecast.
  • Triggers. The audit trigger for a contradicted prediction fired: the share of transfers with a metered receiver (43%) is below the predicted 60% to 85%, and the union found the same moved MW as RO-NC (+0.001) instead of +0.05 to +0.15 more. The explanation, tested: 223 of the 231 transfers the pair alarm finds are also found by RO-NC, so the pair alarm cannot add recall. The 89% coverage by moved MW is the figure that matters, because the forecast error follows the megawatts moved. The trigger for a nested arm beating the arm that contains it fired in the first run and not after the fix described below. A language-model reviewer audited the first run and re-derived its headline numbers. The fix changed the pair-alarm forecast scores, and that reviewer did not repeat the re-derivation, so the fixed numbers have one independent code review and no independent re-derivation. The session's brief allowed no Opus audit.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Lab conditions. Injected steps are exactly balanced between metered neighbours and the weather residual uses ERA5, so the 0.75 share of moved MW found is a ceiling. The 5 of 35 real transfers are the counterweight.
  • The mask arms lose to ignoring recent power. GAM-only scores 3.025 on the same rows and is not part of the pre-registered contrasts; on real rows outside transfers it is worse than no correction (+0.297 points of capacity).
  • Few months. The all-row contrasts rest on 12 calendar months, and the by-transfer contrasts on 475 transfers from six substations.
  • The pair alarm's first threshold choice used real odd months only, and the 4-hour window was chosen on odd-month injected transfers; the even-month share of moved MW found is 0.011 higher for the 2-hour window.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next question is whether a forecast that drops recent power while any alarm is active, and otherwise keeps it, beats the weather model alone. The weather model alone scores 0.52 points better than no correction on rows after a transfer began (3.025 against 3.549) but 0.30 points worse on real rows outside transfers (3.000 against 2.703), so switching between the two could capture the gain of each.

docs.title: Changes to the pre-registered plan
docs.text:
The plan, decision rule, and arms were committed before any run. Three changes followed:

  • Peak test (before any run). The plan's first-crossing alarm was replaced by a peak test of W/2, because a first crossing dates the onset up to W early.
  • Causal partners (after the code review). The first run kept a partner interval only when the partner's own next 24 hours kept half the step, which a live service cannot see. Partners now copy their alarm's interval. This changed MASK-NEW from 2.955 to 3.233 and MASK-UNION minus MASK-RONC from -0.294 to -0.119.
  • Post hoc arms. The alarm-series-only, other-window, and match-filtered arms, and the leave-one-site-out and weather-model-only contrasts, were added after the audit and the review.

docs.title: Experiment 157: does fitting the solar capacity jointly with the demand terms recover an injected farm?
docs.text:
Take-home message: in this test, letting the solar capacity change month by month did not find more of an injected solar farm than a capacity that changes once a year, so the forecast stage is not worth running. We added the recorded output of five real solar farms, one at a time, to the power of six Primary substations (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16). We then measured the recovery: the share of the added farm's capacity that the fitted solar capacity found, where 1.0 means the farm was found exactly. The two-stage method fits one capacity for each July-to-June season-year, as in experiment 129. Fitted again here on the same rows, it recovered 0.75 to 0.87 (median over the five farms, one figure per Primary), where experiment 129 reported 0.78 to 0.88 on its own rows. The monthly method recovered 0.67 to 0.78, averaged over July 2024 to June 2025. At the five Primaries that decide the verdict (all but D9), none reached the recovery of 0.95 to 1.05 that we fixed before running any fit. One scale of the assumed solar-output curve, the same for every site, fits a median of 0.92 to 0.94 of the five farms, because the farms' output curves differ from it (figure 1). The hypothesis is not supported.

Net power is linear in solar capacity, so the capacity can be fitted inside the demand model of studies.dp_gam instead of in a second stage. The joint arm gives the capacity a non-negative level for each calendar month and penalises its change from month to month. The two-stage arm and the joint arm both trained on the same rows before 2025-07-01. The Kalman filter is not involved, because this stage fits capacity and never forecasts. The idea of a joint fit comes from the PV design session; the convex demand model and the injection come from experiments 110 and 129.

Terms. Recovery is the capacity fitted with a farm injected, minus the capacity fitted without it, divided by the injected capacity. Each farm's output is scaled so that its own 99th percentile equals 50% of the Primary's pinned capacity (the capacity that experiment 45's frozen vintage holds), and that 50% is the injected capacity. D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 are the five decision Primaries, and D9 is shown beside them. A season-year runs from July to June and is labelled by the year of the July, so season-year 2024 is July 2024 to June 2025. Capacity is the 99th percentile of alternating-current output over daylight half-hours, in MW.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Verdict by the pre-registered rule: stop. Over the five farms, the median recovery of the joint fit (its fitted path averaged over season-year 2024) is 0.754 (D5), 0.696 (D10), 0.685 (D11), 0.776 (D14), 0.730 (D16), and 0.668 (D9). None lies in 0.95 to 1.05, and none exceeds 0.88. The joint fit recovered less than the predicted 0.78 to 0.92 at every Primary.
  • Two-stage benchmark, same rows: 0.840 (D5), 0.825 (D10), 0.785 (D11), 0.865 (D14), 0.823 (D16), 0.746 (D9). The two-stage arm beats the joint arm's year mean at all six Primaries.
  • The two-stage pin recovers none of an injection. It does not refit, so its recovery is 0 by construction, and an injection appears whole in the forecast error.
  • Farm-to-farm spread. The five farms' recoveries span 0.55 to 0.80 for the joint year mean and 0.67 to 0.88 for the two-stage arm (the lines in figure 1).
  • Growth-penalty sensitivity (labelled, cannot change the verdict). The year-mean median is 0.65 to 0.75 at a penalty share of 0.01 and 0.71 to 0.83 at 1.0. A stiffer penalty moves the joint arm towards the two-stage arm, and at penalty share 1.0 it still sits below the two-stage arm at every Primary.
  • Post hoc read-outs. The joint fit's last month (June 2025, which is what a forecast would hold) recovers 0.85 to 0.92, with the farm maximum between 0.93 and 0.99. June is a month of strong sun, so the figure is not comparable with a year mean. A single month can also exceed a farm's year-wide shape ceiling, because the path may rescale each month. Weighting the months by the squared solar shape gives 0.76 to 0.89, close to the two-stage figures.
  • Shape ceiling. The least-squares scale of a farm's output on the derated unit shape of studies.dp_gam, over the training rows of season-year 2024, is 0.92 to 0.94 as a median over farms (0.77 to 0.97 for single farms). The ceiling is the most that a single capacity scale of the fixed shape finds in that season-year if the demand terms absorb nothing. It bounds the two-stage arm's one scale per season-year, and a monthly path can exceed it, so the 0.95 gate was out of reach for most farms under one scale per season-year. The cause of the farm's shape differing from the fleet shape (tilt, azimuth, inverter clipping, or irradiance error) was not tested.
  • Winter months are barely identified. The monthly recovery is 0.84 to 0.96 from April to August and 0.2 to 0.35 in December (figure 2). A likely cause is that the demand terms absorb the small winter signal. We did not test this.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Wiring check passed. With no injection, the two-stage fit built from the month design's Gram matrix reproduces fit_gam at D10 to 1e-6 (46.062283 against 46.062283 points of effective capacity). The check covers the two-stage arm with no injection only, so the joint arm has no independent check.
  • Triggers of the ml-experiment skill's "Audit before merge": none fired. The wiring check passed. The result agrees with the prediction that fewer than 4 of 5 Primaries reach the gate, and it disagrees with the predicted range of 0.78 to 0.92, because the joint fit recovered less. That contradiction does not change the verdict, and the likely cause is the winter months in the unweighted year mean.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One origin. The fits use rows before 2025-07-01 and read season-year 2024 only.
  • Intervals are ranges over five farms, not confidence intervals. Each Primary has one real power series, and the fit is nearly linear in the injected farm, so the variation across farms is the main source of uncertainty.
  • Only five farms, each injected at 50% of the Primary's pinned capacity, were tested. Experiment 129 also tested synthetic plants and a cloud-driven load, and this experiment did not.
  • Compute. CPU, 1 core, 25 seconds for the grid of six Primaries, five farms, two arms, and three growth penalties. Pre-registered penalty share: 0.1 of the mean Gram diagonal over the month columns that have rows.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• A fixed-shape capacity probably cannot reach 1.0, so test a different shape first. A fitted tilt and azimuth per Primary, or a fitted peak-to-capacity ratio, would raise the ceiling. A joint capacity fit is worth planning only once the ceiling is above the 0.95 gate.
  • No forecast arms are run, because the pre-registered decision rule says to stop.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit)
docs.text:
Question. Experiment 129 found a capacity per season-year from each Primary's own power and recovered an injected real farm's output at 0.78 to 0.88. Experiment 139 found the as-of capacity no better than the pin, and the hindsight capacity equal to it. Net power is linear in capacity, so the capacity can instead be fitted inside the GAM-K fit as a monthly path. Does fitting the capacity as a monthly path recover the injection near 1.0? This experiment runs only the known-answer stage, as the maintainer asked, because the expected forecast gain is under 0.05 points of the quantile score.

Arms, all on the same rows. Every arm trains on rows before the origin 2025-07-01 and has the same demand terms, so that only the capacity differs.

Arm Capacity Role 1. Pin Experiment 45's frozen vintage, held Reference. It does not refit, so it recovers none of the injection 2. Two-stage as-of Experiment 129's arm 2: non-negative increments per season-year, ridge 0.1 on the cumulative capacity Benchmark 3. Joint A non-negative level for each calendar month (the derated unit shape times the level), a penalty on the squared change of the level from month to month, and a near-zero ridge on the level The arm under test

The joint fit's growth penalty is fixed in advance. It is 0.1 times the mean diagonal of the Gram matrix over the capacity columns, the share experiment 129's arm 4 used. Two values, 0.01 and 1.0, run as labelled sensitivity checks that cannot change the verdict. The shape parameters (tilt 35 degrees, south-facing, ratio of direct-current to alternating-current rating 1.15, inverter clip at the alternating-current capacity, and 0.4% per kelvin de-rating) stay as in studies.dp_gam. The Kalman filter acts on residuals only in the forecast stage, so it is not involved here: this stage fits capacity and never forecasts.

Injection. Each of the five real farms of experiment 129 (labels A, B, C, D, F; anonymised) is added to the Primary's power over all training rows at 50% of the Primary's pinned capacity, as a farm's output divided by its 99th percentile. Rows where the farm's reading is missing or a dropout are removed from both the injected and the matching base fit, so a difference of fits never mixes two row sets. Recovery is read per Primary and farm, then summarised by the median over farms. The base fit has no injection.

Recovery read-out. The raw recovery averages the fitted path over season-year 2024, the latest complete season-year before the origin. The joint fit's last-month value, which is what a forecast would hold, is reported beside it. The divisor that experiment 129 applied (the median recovery of other farms) is not applied to the pre-registered gate, because the question is whether the joint fit needs no divisor. The divided two-stage recovery is shown for context.

Primaries and checks. D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 count for the decision. D9 is reported beside them. The tables show every farm at every Primary, plus the unmodified base capacity of each arm in MW, so that a reader can see the joint path's level against the two-stage steps. As a wiring check, a fit with zero injection must reproduce arm 2's published capacity for the same cut to three decimal places.

Five triggers. Stored: private files only. Serving path: not touched. Degradation rule: not touched. More than one defensible design: no, because the maintainer fixed the arms and the stop rule. Callers not nameable without searching: no.

Compute. CPU only, at most 4 cores, thread caps all 1, each job under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue. The first Primary is timed before the full grid.

Reviews. One Sonnet code review (leakage first: no row at or after the origin may train) and one Sonnet prose review. No Opus review.

Advice followed. From experiment 129, count only season-years with at least 12,000 training half-hours when reading a capacity, and use an as-of capacity and never a hindsight capacity in a forecast test. Departs from none.

docs.title: Experiment 158: do partly pooled GAM shapes beat per-site GAM fits?
docs.text:
In this test on six Primary substations, fitting a demand model's shared curves jointly across the six let a substation with only 3 months of history forecast almost as well as one with 24 months, but it did not help a substation that already had 24 months. Scores are quantile scores, the mean over 11 quantiles of twice the pinball loss, in points of capacity (1% of a substation's capacity), and lower is better. A substation with 3 months of history scored 3.01 points with the shared curves and 3.64 points fitted alone (difference -0.629, 99% interval -1.639 to -0.091), against 2.84 for a substation fitted alone on 24 months. The gain held at all five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16) and in all 12 months of the scored year (2025-07 to 2026-06), and it was largest in winter and on Christmas rows. At 24 months, pooling changed the score by +0.004 points (-0.006 to +0.014). Pooling at 24 months is safe, but it makes each substation's forecast depend on the other five substations' data and on one joint monthly refit, for no measurable gain. The arm that pooled only the heating curve scored worse than the per-site fit at 3 months, but the two arms also differed in ridge, so this test cannot say whether the other shared curves carry the gain. The verdict is partly supported.

We asked whether a demand forecast improves when each substation's heating curve, lighting curve, daily profile, holiday effects, and Christmas shape are the fleet's average curve plus a deviation of the substation's own that a penalty shrinks towards zero ("partial pooling"). The fleet is the six Primary substations D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16. The forecast is GAM-K (a generalised additive model with a Kalman filter on recent errors) of experiment 111, a convex demand model driven by the ensemble-mean weather forecast as in experiment 136. The partly pooled fit is the convex model of experiment 109, which applies the multilevel-model idea of Gelman and Hill to the coefficients. Experiment 154 had found on synthetic data that a shared heating curve is recovered better than separate fits recover it and that a substation's own offset cannot be read from 4 weeks. We kept every level, capacity, and offset per substation. We scored monthly refits over the scored year at the five decision substations, with the even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06 as a replicate. A row is one substation's forecast for one half-hour at one lead time. Holiday rows are bank holidays and the Christmas run, and Christmas rows are those within a few days of Christmas Day.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Every number is in report.json, which e00158_report.py writes. Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity, lower is better.

  • Arms and settings. K0 (no pooling), PH (heating curve pooled, penalty 300 rows of evidence), PS (all shared families pooled, 300 rows on the heating curve and 3000 on the others), and complete pooling (also called tied) as a reference, each for a target with 24 months and with 3 months of history (the other five substations keep 24). A penalty of 300 rows against about 35,000 training rows at 24 months, or 4,300 at 3 months, shrinks lightly. The penalty pair was chosen on the odd tuning months from three values per family, the same for both histories. Monthly refits, no weekly refits.
  • Absolute scores over the scored year and all lead times. K0 2.839, PH 2.839, PS 2.843, complete pooling 3.133, K0-3m 3.638, PS-3m 3.009, PH-3m 4.145. References: experiment 136's A2 (per-site T-all) 2.791, BG2 2.780, manual heuristic 3.497, climatology 3.804.
  • L1 (heating pooled gains at 24 months) fails: C1, PH minus K0, is -0.000 (-0.002 to +0.001). The threshold was a gain below -0.02 points. C3, PS minus PH, is +0.004 (-0.005 to +0.014).
  • L2 (non-inferior at 24 months) holds: C2, PS minus K0, is +0.004 (-0.006 to +0.014) and C8 (ordinary rows) is +0.006 (-0.002 to +0.015). Both upper bounds are below +0.02. The replicate months agree (+0.007 and +0.006).
  • L3 (short-history gain) holds: C4, PS-3m minus K0-3m, is -0.629 (-1.639 to -0.091), at 5 of 5 substations and 12 of 12 months. The replicate months give -1.051 (-3.236 to -0.117). The gain is the same at every lead band (-0.61 to -0.66). Leaving each decision substation out in turn leaves it between -0.59 and -0.69.
  • C5, PH-3m minus K0-3m, is +0.507 (-0.073 to +1.024). The scored-year interval includes zero. The replicate months give +0.601 (+0.339 to +0.852). The arms differ in ridge (see the caveats). Two post hoc heating-only arms with penalties of 3000 and 30000 rows scored 4.126 and 4.142 in the scored year, no better than PH-3m's 4.145, so a stronger heating penalty did not close the gap to K0-3m (3.638).
  • C6, PS-3m minus K0, is +0.169 (+0.053 to +0.327). A 3-month substation with pooling is within 0.17 points of a 24-month substation fitted alone, and still worse.
  • L4 (events) fails: C7, PS minus K0 on holiday and Christmas rows at 24 months, is -0.024 (-0.049 to +0.028). The sign is negative at 3 of the 4 decision substations with Christmas rows in the scored Christmas, and at 1 of 5 in the replicate Christmas. C9 (Christmas rows alone) is -0.032 in the scored year and +0.019 in the replicate months, each from one Christmas, so neither has a usable interval. On cold nights at 24 months PS scored 2.599 against K0's 2.645.
  • With a 3-month history, pooling helped most on holiday and Christmas rows. Christmas rows scored 4.32 against 9.39 for the per-site fit, holiday rows 3.98 against 9.58, winter (December to February) 3.41 against 4.91, and cold nights 3.43 against 4.49 (scored year).
  • The 24-month arm tuned on its own (penalties of 300 and 300) scored 2.839, the same as K0.
  • Tail calibration, scored year, all leads (coverage of q01, q05, q95, q99; pinball loss at q01 and q99). K0: 2.2%, 6.3%, 94.7%, 98.3%; 0.225 and 0.231. PS: 2.1%, 6.4%, 94.5%, 98.3%; 0.223 and 0.229. K0-3m: 3.4%, 8.2%, 93.6%, 97.3%; 0.326 and 0.542. PS-3m: 2.6%, 7.1%, 94.4%, 98.1%; 0.245 and 0.246.

docs.title: Predictions against outcome and checks
docs.text:
• C1 to C3 and C8 predicted within about +/-0.03; observed within +0.006. C7 predicted -0.2 to -1.5; observed -0.024. C4 predicted -3 to -12 and revised to -0.5 to +0.3 after the tuning months showed K0-3m scoring 3.05; observed -0.629, just outside the revised range. Complete pooling scored worse than PS at 24 months by 0.29, as predicted (0.05 to 0.30).
  • Controls. The per-site fits at penalty 0 reproduce experiment 111's stored fits to within 7.2e-11 over 162 fits (27 monthly cuts and 6 substations; reproduction.txt). K0's score (2.839) equals experiment 136's A0. The fit refuses any training row after the cut. Complete pooling scoring worse than PS passes the shrinkage check at 24 months and at 3 months. Experiment 154 is the known-answer gate and was not repeated here.
  • Median forecast minus mean forecast, per site. 0.000 at every site for K0, PS, and PS-3m, at 12 to 36 hours. This is zero by construction, because both forecasts are built from the same corrected mean.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast. The mean absolute error has the same sign as the quantile score for C1 to C9 (for example C2 +0.010, C4 -0.833, C7 -0.033).
  • Audit trigger 2 fired for C7 and C4, and the explanations were tested. Two post hoc arms with a penalty of 30000 rows on the non-heating families scored worse than K0 at 24 months on Christmas rows (3.052 and 3.050 against 3.012 in the scored year, 3.603 and 3.586 against 3.376 in the replicate), so at 24 months the fleet's Christmas shape is worse than a substation's own two Christmases. K0-3m scored 3.64, not the 6 to 17 predicted, because the filter corrects most of a poorly fitted level.
  • Audit triggers 5 and 7. Trigger 5 (a nested arm beating the arm containing it) does not apply, because PH-3m is not nested in K0-3m. Trigger 7 holds in principle, because a later onboarding design could rest on C4, and C4 is replicated in the even months. No Opus audit ran.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• PH-3m and K0-3m differ in ridge. K0-3m uses experiment 109's ridge of 10 on every coefficient, and the pooled arms use 0.1, because a ridge of 10 would also pull a pooled heating curve to zero. C5 therefore mixes pooling with ridge, and this test cannot say which shared curves carry the gain of PS-3m.
  • K0-3m's ridge was not tuned on these tuning months, while PS-3m's penalty pair was. The sign of C4 holds in the replicate months, at all five decision substations, and in 12 of 12 months, but its size is not a like-for-like gain.
  • Six substations, 3 months, one scored year. D9 is fitted alone before 2025-04 because its pinned capacity is a late vintage, and D18 is out of the fleet. D5 has no scored Christmas rows after the switching mask.
  • K0 is experiment 136's A0, not experiment 155's arm, because experiment 155 has not run, and the pooled design shares B0's columns, not T-all's.
  • The switching terms of experiments 141 and 147 are not in the fit. The detector's alarm arrives about 48 hours after a step.
  • The penalty pair was tuned on the odd months of one year, and the plan was amended once after the first tuning scores were read (see "Plan"). The 3-month history is a window of 3 months, not a new substation's first 3 months.
  • No curtailment-cost metric was scored. The question is the fit, not a headline model.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: A follow-up could give the heating curve and the calendar families separate penalties, pool T-all's split columns, and test the pooled fit on a real substation that joins with 3 months of history. Separate penalties need a change to the reviewed module studies.dp_gam_pooled, in its own pull request. Pooling did not improve Christmas rows at 24 months, and this experiment did not test whether more years of history would.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
Question. Experiments 105, 109, and 112 pooled raw demand, so the shared shape had to absorb each substation's solar output and switching. Solar capacity is now a pinned term, the filter of GAM-K handles recent level shifts, and experiment 154 showed, on synthetic fleets with a known answer, that sharing the heating curve across substations recovers it better than fitting each substation alone, and that a substation's own heating offset is not learnable from 4 weeks. This experiment asks whether the same sharing helps the real forecast, at 24 months of history, at 3 months, and on holidays.

Method. The partly pooled convex fit of experiment 109 (studies.dp_gam_pooled.fit_pooled) gives each substation the fleet's coefficients plus a ridge-penalised deviation of its own. The fit is GAM-K's design with a pinned capacity and no drift. With a penalty of 0 the fit is the per-site fit, and the folder's reproduction control checks that it matches experiment 111's stored fits to 1e-8. The forecast engine (ensemble mean input, per-substation Kalman filter, residual table fitted on the tuning months) is copied from experiment 136, so the arms differ only in their monthly fits. The partly pooled fit is the idea of Gelman and Hill (multilevel models) applied to the coefficients of a generalised additive model.

Fleet. D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16. D18 is left out because its capacity is a late vintage. D9's pinned capacity is a late vintage (growth_prior) at the cuts before 2025-04, and the pooled fit refuses such a capacity, so D9 is fitted alone in every arm at those cuts and joins the fleet from 2025-04.

Arms. All arms refit monthly from 2024-04.

Arm Pooled families History of the target K0 none (penalty 0) 24 months PH heating curve 24 months PS heating, lighting, daily profile, holiday periods, Christmas tent, harmonics 24 months tied the families of PS, completely pooled (reference) 24 months K0-3m, PH-3m, PS-3m as K0, PH, and PS 3 months for the target, 24 for the other five

The 3-month arms take each substation in turn as the target, so the other five keep 24 months. Capacity, level (the band means of the profile), and the filter stay per substation in every arm. studies.dp_gam_pooled pools the holiday periods and the Christmas tent with the other non-heating families under one penalty, so PS cannot pool the heating curve and the profile at different strengths from the calendar families. Splitting them would change the reviewed module and is left for a follow-up if PS gains.

The penalty (amended 2026-10-21, after the tuning-month scores of K0 and PH were read and before any replicate-month or scored-year score). The deviation penalty is in rows of evidence (a substation with far more training rows keeps its own curve). The first plan tuned PH's heating penalty over 100 to 10000 and each history separately. The tuning months showed that at 24 months every penalty up to 10000 scored the same as K0 within 0.002 points (a substation has about 35,000 training rows, so a penalty of 10000 rows barely pools), and that the tie rule would then pick the penalty that pools least, which makes C1 and C2 uninformative. The amended rule is one penalty pair for both histories, as in experiment 109, because a joint fit in production serves a mature substation and a new one with the same penalty. PS is tuned over the heating penalty h and the penalty o of the other families, each in 300, 3000, and 30000 rows (nine pairs), on the odd tuning months of 2024-07 to 2025-06. The chosen pair is the one with the lowest all-lead score at the decision substations of the 3-month arm, among the pairs whose 24-month score is at most 0.02 points above K0's on the same months; a tie within 0.005 points goes to the smaller h + o. PH takes the chosen h with o = 0. The 24-month arm tuned separately (the first plan) is reported as a labelled variant. The tuned penalties are therefore the same for both histories.

Prediction check after reading the tuning months. K0-3m scored 3.05 points on the tuning months, against a predicted 6 to 17, because the Kalman filter corrects most of a poorly fitted level within days. The predicted size of C4 (-3 to -12 points) cannot hold. The written prediction above is left as it was, and the revised expectation, written before any scored-year score is read, is C4 between -0.5 and +0.3 points and C6 between +0.1 and +0.6 points. The decision rule is unchanged.

Switching. The switching terms of experiments 141 and 147 are not part of this fit. Experiment 141 found that feeding the detector's causal alarm to the filter did no better than a random placebo, because the alarm arrives about 48 hours after the step, and experiment 147 found a live end rule inconclusive. The fit therefore does not take the hand-filtered switching events as ground truth, and the rows inside those events are excluded from scoring, as in every experiment on fold_a_daily_gap_v1.

Per-site baseline. The brief names the best-guess GAM-K components of experiment 155 as the per-site baseline. Experiment 155 has not run, so K0 is experiment 136's A0 (GAM-K on the ensemble mean, pinned capacity, per-substation filter), and experiment 136's A2 (per-site T-all and shared filter noise) is an absolute reference. The pooled design shares B0's columns, not T-all's split columns, because studies.dp_gam_pooled pools B0's design. Pooling T-all is a follow-up.

Rows and periods. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, 09:00 UTC power_fcst_init_time, leads 0.5 to 168 hours. The tuning months are the odd months and the replicate months are the even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, and the scored year is 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29 (292 runs), as in experiment 136. D-labels only. The replicate months hold the Christmas of 2024 and the scored year the Christmas of 2025. The weather is the calibrated ensemble mean of experiment 136 and the filter uses its analysis proxy built from earlier runs, so every input exists at forecast time. Each monthly fit trains on rows that end before its cut.

Rows for events. Holiday rows are those on a bank holiday or in the Christmas run (holiday_period >= 0), and Christmas rows are those within the Christmas tent's window of Christmas Day. Ordinary rows are all others.
