The farms are A, B, C, D, and F, the farms with data from 2019-09. The curve is the mean over the farms of the monthly scales, divided by the mean of its own 12 values so that the curve has mean 1.
  • No leakage from the injected farm. For an injected farm X, the curve uses the other four farms only. The farm-only fit of X also uses that curve.
  • Applying the curve. The Primary's derated shape is multiplied by the factor of the half-hour's calendar month. The temperature derating is then divided out again (the fixed-point step of experiment 238), so that the fit does not apply the derating a second time.
  • Arms. The satellite shape without the curve, and the satellite shape with the curve, on the same rows and the same injections at D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16.
  • Intervals. A month-block bootstrap, 200 resamples, stratified as in experiment 231, over the fits of the Primary's injected farms; the curve is held fixed in each resample, which understates the uncertainty of the curve. The spread of the factors over the farms is reported beside it.
  • Reading a flat curve. If every factor lies within 3% of the others, the fall of the flat top is not a seasonal efficiency effect, and the write-up says so.

docs.title: Plan: checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction: the arm without the curve reproduces experiment 231's rung 4 to within 1e-6, and a curve of 12 factors equal to 1 reproduces the arm without the curve.
  • Derating: the shape returned for the fit, derated by the fit's own formula, equals the satellite shape times the factor to within 1e-6.
  • Review: one Sonnet review of this plan, one of the code, one of the write-up.

docs.title: Can small XGBoost components inside the XGBoost-free solar and wind forecasts close the gap to a full XGBoost forecast?
docs.text:
Take-home. For solar farms, XGBoost helps most when it predicts the spread around the mean forecast of a physics-based solar plant model (a model that turns weather forecasts into farm output). The solar forecast with XGBoost spread scores 4.3% better than the plant model alone and 1.6% better than full XGBoost on the quantile score (lower is better; defined below), for forecasts made 12 to 36 hours ahead. It also scores 0.361 against full XGBoost's 0.478 in pinball loss at the 0.99 quantile (the 99th-percentile, high-output forecast), which is the tail that matters for curtailment, when generation is switched off. Correcting the plant model's mean with XGBoost made the quantile score worse, by about as much as a placebo model trained on shuffled residuals, so the placebo test fails. For wind, an XGBoost stage on the physics-based wind model (from experiment 230) closes 71% of the gap to full XGBoost at 12 to 36 hours. The gap is the difference between the XGBoost-free forecast and full XGBoost.

Experiment 234 found that forecasts with no XGBoost (a gradient-boosted decision-tree model, which production uses today), score 2.8% worse for metered solar farms and 5.0% worse for metered wind farms at 12 to 36 hours ahead. We asked whether adding a small XGBoost model inside the XGBoost-free forecast closes at least half of that gap. For solar we fitted three small XGBoost models on top of the plant forecast of experiment 224: one corrects the plant's mean (R), one predicts the spread, meaning 11 quantile offsets added to the plant's mean (S), and one does both (RS). For wind we scored the three small models that experiment 230 already built on the wind physics model (two XGBoost models and one neural network), without refitting them. Each score uses forecasts made 12 to 36 hours ahead, on half-hourly forecast targets. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in percentage points of the farm's capacity. Intervals come from resampling whole months and the three random seeds, at the 98.3% level (a 95% interval widened for three comparisons). A negative difference means the first arm is better. The scored year is 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31 and the replicate half-year is 2025-03-01 to 2025-08-31.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• No arm is kept under the rule as written. An arm that adds an XGBoost model is kept when it closes half the gap to full XGBoost and the placebo scores within 0.01 of the plant alone. Solar S closes more than half the gap (change -0.238 against the needed -0.076, upper interval end -0.125). The placebo PR scored +0.154, so by the rule as written nothing is kept. PR is the placebo of the mean-correction arm, and S has no placebo of its own. Wind B5 closes more than half the gap (-0.179 against -0.126, the threshold recomputed from the corrected gap of 0.251; the plan quoted -0.121 from a gap of 0.242), and no wind placebo was run.
  • Solar beats the plant alone at 12 to 36 hours (scored year, 41,676 half-hourly forecast targets at six farms, quantile score).
    • Plant alone (A3) 5.598; full XGBoost (A5) 5.446; the plant re-run in this code (A3r) 5.598.
    • S 5.360, which is -0.238 from A3 (98.3% interval -0.362 to -0.125) and -0.086 from A5 (-0.165 to +0.004). S beats A3 at 5 of 6 farms.
    • R 5.780 (+0.182, +0.007 to +0.319); RS 5.659 (+0.061, -0.110 to +0.245); R0 (R without hour and month) 5.737 (+0.139); PR (placebo) 5.752 (+0.154, +0.002 to +0.306).
    • Replicate half-year (26,600 rows): S is -0.435 from A3 (-0.658 to -0.179) and -0.720 from A5 (-1.100 to -0.332), because A5 scores 6.700 there against A3's 6.415.
  • Post hoc arms, run after the first scores were read. These arms test why R and the placebo lost and why S won; the verdict does not depend on them.
    • A regularised mean correction (depth 2, at least 300 rows per leaf, 100 rounds at rate 0.05) Rg scores 5.595 (-0.003 from A3, -0.124 to +0.097), and its placebo PRg +0.043 (-0.072 to +0.163). The default XGBoost settings overfit the noisy residual.
    • RSg 5.503 (-0.095, -0.269 to +0.101): no better than S.
    • SQ (S without the plant's error 48 hours earlier) is 0.025 worse than S (+0.001 to +0.057). SC (S without hour and month) scores 5.327, which is 0.033 better than S (-0.079 to -0.003) and 0.119 below A5.
    • X5r (direct XGBoost on experiment 224's arm-5 inputs, under this protocol) scores 5.429, -0.017 from A5 (-0.063 to +0.035). S is -0.069 from X5r (-0.118 to -0.010), so using the plant mean as the centre improves the score by about 0.07 points.
  • Solar tails, 12 to 36 hours (pinball loss / coverage), A3, A5, S. q01 0.374 / 0.032, 0.352 / 0.034, 0.367 / 0.033; q05 1.433 / 0.055, 1.365 / 0.068, 1.329 / 0.066; q95 1.367 / 0.963, 1.214 / 0.956, 1.177 / 0.946; q99 0.386 / 0.991, 0.478 / 0.996, 0.361 / 0.990. MAE of the median 9.918, 9.810, 9.732.
  • Wind, 12 to 36 hours (22,788 half-hourly forecast targets at three farms, with the three seeds of experiment 230's XGBoost arms). Physics model alone (B1) scores 5.112 and full XGBoost (A0r) 4.861, a gap of 0.251.
    • B5 (XGBoost starting from the physics model's expected power, with 11 quantile outputs) scores 4.933. That is -0.179 from B1 (-0.287 to -0.062), 71% of the gap, and +0.072 from A0r (+0.049 to +0.099).
    • B14 (A0r with the physics model's outputs added as inputs) scores 4.857, -0.255 from B1 and -0.004 from A0r, so it is full XGBoost with extra inputs.
    • B9 (a small neural network that calibrates the physics model) scores 5.111, no change.
    • Over all leads (321,363 targets) the gap is 0.077. B5 is -0.034 from B1 (-0.073 to +0.011), 44% of the gap and not separable from zero.
  • Wind source and revision. Experiment 230 corrected its spread step. The wind arms are its stored forecasts after that correction, read before experiment 230 merged, so the numbers are provisional. With the corrected spread the 12 to 36 hour gap is 5.2% (5.112 against 4.861); experiment 234 quoted 5.0% from the earlier spread.
  • Schedule and settings. Solar: XGBoost with three seeds, colsample_bytree 1.0, trained once on all ensemble months before the fold start (no weekly refits), 12 to 36 hour rows only. The plant scale, ceiling, and offset factors come from tuning months only. The ensemble members are the only weather source (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts ensemble, available at forecast time).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per farm (points of capacity, 11-level mean). A3 +0.27 to +0.48, A5 -0.48 to +0.02, S -0.12 to +0.83. None exceeds 1 point.
  • Mean absolute error (MAE) of the median beside the quantile score. The MAE of the median moves with the quantile score for S (-0.186 from A3, -0.402 to -0.000), SQ, SC, and X5r, and for R (+0.324).
  • Audit triggers and audit. Two triggers fired: the placebo PR scored 0.154 points worse than the plant alone where the rule required at most 0.01, and PR's loss is about as large as R's. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the result (the brief for this experiment excludes Opus). It re-derived S minus A3 (-0.238, 95% interval from its own month resampling -0.337 to -0.144), S minus A5 (-0.086, -0.149 to -0.014), R minus A3 (+0.182), and PR minus A3 (+0.154) from the stored predictions, and found no leakage, no misaligned rows, and no effect of the zero floor. It explained the R and PR losses as a bias, not a width problem: the median forecast of R and PR sits below the actuals (0.469 and 0.450 of actuals at or below it, against 0.49 for the plant alone) because the mean residual changes between the tuning months (2024-04 to 2025-08) and the scored year. PR keeps each month-and-hour mean residual by construction, so it is not a clean noise control. We also tested the over-flexible-model explanation: regularising removes most of the loss (PRg +0.043).
  • Leave one farm out. S has a lower quantile score than A3 at 5 of 6 farms in the scored year and 5 of 6 in the replicate (farm A is the exception), and S minus A3 keeps its sign when any one farm is left out. S minus A5 is fragile: it shrinks by about 40% without farm A and is near zero at two farms, so the lead over full XGBoost is a small gain.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• One fold and one weather source per type. The solar result rests on one scored year and one replicate half-year at six farms. S has no seed-to-seed variation beyond the three seeds.
  • S has the plant's error 48 hours earlier as an input, which full XGBoost (A5) lacks. SQ shows that input is worth 0.025 points, so that input does not explain S's 0.086-point lead over A5.
  • Nested out-of-fold residuals are second-order leaky at month boundaries. The error 48 hours earlier of a training row can include a held-out target at the edge of a block of months.
  • Wind placebo and the all-leads band were not part of the solar-style check. Wind uses experiment 230's own training, which differs from this experiment's protocol.
  • Next: port S's idea to the wind physics model under this experiment's protocol (plant mean as the centre, an offsets model without the hour and month, and a regularised mean correction as an ablation), and test S on the 60 to 84 and 108 to 132 hour bands.

The code is in ml-experiments/00240-no-xgboost-forecast-sprinkle-part-2/.

docs.title: PV capacity: how well does a calibrated interval cover?
docs.text:
Take-home message: dividing the capacity found by the median recovery of other real farms removes most of the bias, and the interval built from the same recoveries is too narrow to call an 80% interval. The corrected estimate is within 10% of the injected capacity at all five decision Primaries when the calibration uses the same season-year. The interval covers 58.7% of held-out injections with that calibration and 78.7% with the all-years calibration. The interval covers 0% to 2% when a cloud-driven load is added to the Primary's demand.

What was done. The experiment fits nothing. It reads the recoveries that experiment 129 measured when it added the recorded output of a real solar farm (the five farms A, B, C, D, and F are metered generators and are never named) to a Primary substation's power at 20%, 50%, and 100% of the Primary's pinned capacity, for season-years 2019 to 2024. For each held-out farm at a Primary, the capacity found is divided by the median recovery of the other four farms at the same Primary, and the 80% interval runs from the capacity found divided by the 90th percentile of those recoveries to the capacity found divided by the 10th percentile. The calibration set is either the other farms in the same season-year (12 recoveries) or the other farms in every season-year (up to 72 recoveries). D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 are the five decision Primaries (the substations whose capacity is judged). The recovery is the capacity found with the farm added, minus the capacity found without it, divided by the injected capacity, in the capacity unit of experiment 129 (the 99th percentile of alternating-current output over daylight half-hours, in MW). The stored fits stop at 2026-07-01, so the maintainer's labelled exception for capacity experiments (data to 2026-07-31) is not used, and no forecast is scored.

Figure 1. The corrected estimate is within 10% of the injected capacity for 63 of 75 held-out injections at the five decision Primaries (same-year calibration, season-year 2024).

Figure 2. The 80% interval covers 59% to 79% of held-out injections, and 0% to 2% when a cloud-driven load is added.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• The accuracy condition is met with same-year calibration. The median absolute error of the corrected estimate is 0.032 to 0.094 of the injected capacity at the five Primaries (0.056 over all 75 held-out injections at season-year 2024), against 0.145 to 0.220 uncorrected (0.193 pooled). The corrected estimate is within 10% for 84% of those injections.
  • The accuracy condition fails at 2 of 5 Primaries with all-years calibration. The median absolute error is 0.104 at D5 and 0.103 at D16, and 0.031 to 0.056 at the other three. The corrected estimate is within 10% for 73% of the injections.
  • The coverage depends on the calibration set. At season-year 2024 the interval covers 58.7% of the 75 held-out injections with same-year calibration and 78.7% with all-years calibration. Over all season-years (six at three Primaries, four at D14 and D16) the coverage is 60.8% and 71.8% (390 injections). The target is 70% to 90%.
  • The two conditions are met by different calibration sets, so neither set meets both. Same-year calibration meets the accuracy condition and misses the coverage range. All-years calibration is in the coverage range and misses the 4-of-5 accuracy requirement (3 of 5 Primaries pass). The plan did not say which calibration set decides, and the decision rule is not met by either.
  • A cloud-driven load breaks the calibration. With experiment 129's cloud-driven load added to the held-out injection, the median corrected estimate is 26% to 30% too high (a median ratio of 1.26 to 1.30 at season-year 2024) and the interval covers 0% to 1.3% of injections (2.3% over all seasons with all-years calibration).
  • The sample is smaller than it looks. The 3 injected fractions at each farm give nearly the same recovery, so the 75 injections at season-year 2024 are about 25 distinct farm and Primary pairs, and the Primaries share the same weather. With about 25 pairs, a coverage of 79% has a standard error of about 0.08.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Row counts: every Primary holds 15 injections without load and 15 with load per season-year, except D14 and D16, which start at season-year 2021.
  • Reproduction: the stored recovery equals the capacity found with the farm minus the capacity found without it, divided by the injected capacity, to within 1e-9, as the script checks.
  • Median forecast minus mean forecast, and the mean-forecast error: not applicable, because the experiment scores no forecast.
  • Audit triggers (the seven triggers in the ml-experiment skill's "Audit before merge"): none of triggers 1 to 6 applies, because the experiment has no control, no sister experiment, and no nested arm. Trigger 7 may apply, because a later design may depend on the finding that the interval is not an 80% interval. The maintainer's decision on an audit is pending.
  • Review: one Sonnet review of the code and the page.
  • No Opus audit was run. The ML manager decided that quota did not allow an Opus review of any of this series' experiments, so every audit trigger listed above stays unaudited and a Sonnet reviewer read the code and the page instead.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The injections zero the farm's output when the sun is under 15 degrees above the horizon. Experiment 239 found that keeping that output raises the recovery by 0.033, so the recoveries here understate a farm that produces in winter. Dividing a real farm's estimate by them would overstate its capacity by about 4%.
  • The calibration uses four farms, so the 10th and 90th percentiles sit close to the smallest and largest recovery, and a fifth farm falls outside that range at least 2 times in 5.
  • The farms sit tens of kilometres from the Primaries, so a real unmetered farm near the Primary may differ in orientation and size from the five farms.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does a wider interval cover 80% of new farms? Widening the interval to the full range of the four recoveries, or taking the 90% interval from the all-years calibration, would test the coverage without changing the correction. The prediction that could fail is a coverage of 70% to 90% at 4 of 5 Primaries.
  • How large is the shift from a cloud-driven load in real demand? The correction is 26% too high in that case. A measured demand response to cloud would show whether the shift is realistic.

docs.title: Plan: design
docs.text:
• Held-out injection. One Primary, one farm, one fraction (20%, 50%, or 100% of the pinned capacity), and one season-year. The calibration set holds the same Primary's injections of the four other farms, without cloud-driven load. The held-out farm never enters its own calibration.
  • Corrected estimate. The capacity found divided by the median recovery of the calibration set. Its ratio to the injected capacity is the held-out recovery divided by that median.
  • Interval. The capacity found divided by the 90th percentile of the calibration recoveries (lower end), and by the 10th percentile (upper end).
  • Two calibration sets. The four other farms at the same season-year as the held-out injection (12 recoveries), and the four other farms over all six season-years (72 recoveries).
  • Reading. The decision reads season-year 2024, the last complete season-year, over 15 held-out injections per Primary (5 farms by 3 fractions). Coverage over all six season-years is reported beside it.
  • Shift. The same intervals applied to injections with a cloud-driven load added (experiment 129's cloud_load rows) show whether the calibration survives demand that follows cloud.
  • Limit to state. The injections of experiment 129 set the farm's output to zero when the sun is lower than 15 degrees above the horizon, so the recoveries understate a farm that produces in winter.

docs.title: Plan: checks
docs.text:
• Row counts: every Primary and season-year holds 15 injections without load, and 15 with load.
  • Reproduction: the stored recoveries equal the capacity found with the farm minus the capacity found without it, divided by the injected capacity.

docs.title: Does running all 51 ensemble members through the wind model give better 1% and 99% quantiles for the three metered wind farms than running the ensemble mean once?
docs.text:
Take-home: keep running all 51 ensemble members through the wind model. Running the wind model once on the ensemble mean of the weather instead raises the tail score (the mean of the 0.01 and 0.99 pinball losses, in points of capacity) from 0.47 to 0.83 for the physics core and to 1.23 for XGBoost, and the change comes entirely from the 0.99 quantile. The likely cause, which this experiment did not test directly, is that averaging the members removes the high winds that give full output, so the upper tail comes out too low. The single spread factor tried here, which widens the forecast about its median, did not repair that. The physics core and XGBoost differ by under 0.01 points on the tails, so the choice between them does not matter for the tails.

This experiment asks whether the 1% and 99% quantiles of three metered wind farms (labelled W1 to W3) are better when each of the 51 ensemble weather members (ECMWF ENS) goes through a wind model and the 51 forecasts are combined into one distribution, or when the wind model runs once on the average weather. A wind model here turns weather inputs into power, trained on ERA5, the past-weather estimate. We refitted experiment 230's two wind models, a physics-based power curve (the core) and an XGBoost model, and ran each both ways on its 53 Tuesday forecast runs. Running the members scored better in every comparison. At days 1 and 2 the physics core's gap includes zero, and the gap grows with lead time. This result narrows the tail question to "run the members, whichever wind model", and leaves open whether a cheaper route can keep the tails.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are in points of capacity (smaller is better), on the rows that experiment 210's mask keeps, for W1, W2, and W3 over 53 Tuesday runs from July 2025 to June 2026. The tail score T is the mean of the 0.01 and 0.99 pinball losses. Intervals resample whole months and the three seeds, not farms, so they describe these three farms. The decisive intervals, including the by-band ones, are corrected to 98.75% across the four contrasts. Experiment 210's mask drops rows where the observed power is an idle-band measurement artefact. The schedule was one fit per farm, on valid times before 2025-06-17, with no later refitting.

  • C1, physics core, members minus mean: -0.361 (interval -0.612 to -0.157). By lead band: days 1 and 2 -0.043 (-0.131 to 0.008), days 3 to 6 -0.193 (-0.491 to -0.028), days 7 and later -0.554 (-0.906 to -0.235).
  • C2, XGBoost, members minus mean: -0.760 (-1.079 to -0.450). Days 1 and 2 -0.106 (-0.217 to -0.023), days 3 to 6 -0.396 (-0.807 to -0.128), days 7 and later -1.168 (-1.667 to -0.683).
  • C3, core with minus without residual quantiles: -0.056 (-0.162 to -0.005). The residual quantiles help, slightly.
  • C4, members, core minus XGBoost: +0.001 (-0.007 to 0.008). The tail scores differ by under 0.01 points.
  • All of the change in T comes from the 0.99 quantile. The 0.99 pinball loss is 1.378 for the core on the mean against 0.658 on members, and the 0.01 loss is 0.289 against 0.288.
  • Quantile score (nine levels): core members 11.79, core mean 12.20, XGBoost members 11.66, XGBoost mean 12.34, core members without residuals 12.02. The members results reproduce experiment 230's B1 (11.79) and A0r (11.66).
Arm T, all leads T, days 1 and 2 Coverage, all leads (%) Coverage before the spread factor (%) XGBoost, 51 members 0.472 0.329 91.6 90.7 Core, 51 members 0.473 0.343 91.6 90.9 Core, members, no residuals 0.529 0.431 90.3 78.9 Core, ensemble mean 0.833 0.386 84.0 67.2 XGBoost, ensemble mean 1.232 0.435 81.3 62.6

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per farm (points): the members route sits 5.4, 5.6, and 4.7 points below the mean at W1, W2, and W3 for the core, and the mean route 1.7, 2.4, and 2.1. The members' median lies further below the mean because the mixture has a long upper tail, so the skew is real and not a shifted spread.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each quantile contrast: the mean absolute error contrast has the same sign: C1 -0.182 (-0.318 to -0.025) and C2 -0.308 (-0.516 to -0.068), 95% intervals.
  • Leave one farm out (95% intervals): C1 and C2 stay negative without any one farm (C1 -0.29 to -0.48, C2 -0.62 to -1.00). C3's interval includes zero without W2.
  • Audit triggers (the seven in the ml-experiment skill): trigger 2, a result contradicting its prediction, fired on size and not on direction. The prediction was 0.02 to 0.08 points, and C1 and C2 are about 7 and 15 times the middle of that range. The explanation was tested, and the Results bullets give it: the 0.01 loss does not move and all of the change in T comes from the 0.99 loss. The prediction also named days 3 to 6 as the largest gap, and the largest gap is at days 7 and later. No other trigger fired, and no Opus audit was run.
  • Prediction record: the mean route's raw coverage at days 1 and 2 was 85.3% (core) and 82.0% (XGBoost), under 88% as predicted. The members route's raw coverage there was 94.9% and 94.1%, above the predicted 88% to 92%.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The pre-registered text is unchanged. The hypothesis, prediction, and decision rule in the front matter are as committed before any fit.

  • Weather source: ERA5 (training, about 5 days late) and ENS members (inference, available at forecast time).

  • Ensemble mean of direction: the mean route averages the direction sine and cosine columns, so the pair is no longer a unit vector when members disagree. The unit-vector error affects XGBoost's mean route only, because the physics core ignores direction.
  • Ensemble mean: the mean route averages the inputs. Averaging the 51 outputs is the members route's centre and was not run separately.
  • Not scored: the curtailment-cost metric (it needs a node with its generators). The tail score is the proxy.
  • Three farms: W1 to W3 only, and one year.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• A cheaper route that keeps the tails: a small neural network, or a quantile regression, that maps the ensemble mean and the ensemble standard deviation of the weather to the 11 quantiles. Pre-register a gain over the members route of at least 0 on T and a cost saving; the prediction that could fail is that it stays 0.1 points worse than members on T beyond day 6.
  • Separate spread factors per tail: the factor scales about the median and is fitted on the 5% to 95% band, so a factor for each tail would test whether the upper tail of the mean route can be repaired.

docs.title: Does a physics plant with a small neural head forecast a metered solar farm better than a plant, XGBoost, or a neural network alone?
docs.text:
A small neural network on top of the solar-farm power model ties XGBoost and beats the power model alone when it outputs all 11 quantile offsets, though the power model was not given the lagged power and ensemble spread that the neural network saw. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters the output of six solar farms in its trial area, which this page labels A to F. The "plant" is a solar-farm power model: south-facing panels at 35 degrees tilt, a heat loss of 0.4% per kelvin, and one fitted scale and ceiling per farm, driven by the mean of the 51 members of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble forecast, as in experiment 224. We compared the plant alone, XGBoost (Chen and Guestrin, 2016), a neural network with no physics, and six hybrids, at 12 to 36 hours ahead on daylight half-hours in 2025-09 to 2026-08. The score is the quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity.

The prediction partly holds. The numbers in this paragraph are for the own-history setting: each farm's neural networks and plant scale are fitted on that farm's own months before 2025-09. The quantile score is 5.48 for H5 (the plant forecast plus 11 quantile offsets, which a neural network outputs as amounts added to the plant forecast), 5.49 for XGBoost, 5.54 for the neural network with no physics, 5.73 for the plant alone, and 8.64 and 8.69 for the climatology and manual-heuristic floors. H5 beats the plant by 4.4% (95% interval 3.2% to 5.9%) and ties XGBoost (-0.3%, -1.2% to +0.8%). The neural network with no physics does not beat XGBoost (+0.9%, +0.2% to +1.9%), as predicted. Against XGBoost, H5's pinball loss is 29% lower at the 0.99 quantile and 9.5% lower at the 0.01 quantile, which meets the 5% target at both tails. The 3% gain in the mean absolute error (MAE) of the median fails: H5's MAE of the median is only 0.5% lower than XGBoost's, with an interval from -1.5% to +0.6%. The hybrids' gain is larger on cloudy half-hours, as predicted (Figure 4).

The one-number hybrids barely help. H1 (the plant times a neural network's scale), H2 (the plant plus a neural network's correction), H3 (a neural network adjusts the irradiance and cell temperature before the plant), and H4 (H3 followed by H1) lower the score by 0.06% to 0.6% against the plant, and every interval includes zero. The stop rule (stop if no hybrid beats the plant by at least 2% at 2 of the first 3 farms) does not fire, because H5 beats the plant by at least 2% at all six farms; H1 to H4 would have fired the stop rule.

Zero history keeps the order. When the networks and XGBoost are fitted on the other five farms and the plant scale is the median of those farms' scales, XGBoost and H5 tie at 5.61, the neural network with no physics scores 5.65, and the plant alone 5.87. H5 beats the plant by 4.5% (3.5% to 5.6%). In this setting H1 and H2 do lower the score by 1.3%, with intervals below zero, The pooled plant scale is about 2.5% worse than a per-farm scale, and the neural networks may partly repair it.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Rows. 41,654 daylight half-hours (sun more than 5 degrees above the horizon) at 12 to 36 hour leads in 2025-09 to 2026-08, six farms, the rows of experiment 224. Each farm has equal weight, and the 95% intervals come from resampling the 12 scored months 20,000 times. The networks' scores are means over five seeds.
  • Weather and forecast time. ECMWF ensemble, 00 UTC run, nearest 0.25 degree cell: mean and spread of the members' irradiance, and the mean temperature. All exist at forecast time. Lagged power is the farm's own observed power one day earlier (two days when the lead is over 24 hours), which exists at forecast time. The plant arm sees neither the lagged power nor the spread; the neural arms and XGBoost see both.
  • Quantile score, own history (95% interval): H5 5.48 (4.95 to 5.92); XGBoost 5.49 (4.94 to 5.95); neural network 5.54 (5.00 to 6.01); H2 5.69; H1 5.70; H4 5.72; H3 5.72; plant 5.73 (5.21 to 6.17); H6 5.75; climatology 8.64; manual heuristic 8.69.
  • Quantile score, zero history: XGBoost 5.61; H5 5.61; neural network 5.65; H2 5.79; H1 5.80; H4 5.84; H3 5.86; H6 5.86; plant 5.87.
  • Contrasts, own history, quantile score: C1 H5 minus plant -4.39% (-5.90 to -3.18); C2 H5 minus XGBoost -0.27% (-1.17 to +0.83); neural network minus plant -3.23% (-5.03 to -1.83); neural network minus XGBoost +0.94% (+0.25 to +1.86). Cloudy half-hours (clear-sky index under 0.5): H5 minus plant -5.1%, H2 minus plant -2.6%; clear half-hours: H5 -4.3%.
  • MAE of the median, own history (points of capacity): H5 9.85; XGBoost 9.90; plant 9.95; neural network 10.06. H5 minus XGBoost -0.49% (-1.53 to +0.64); the neural network is 1.7% worse than XGBoost (+0.8% to +2.9%).
  • Pinball loss at the tails, own history (points of capacity): 0.01 quantile: H5 0.334, XGBoost 0.369, plant 0.373, neural network 0.400; 0.99 quantile: neural network 0.328, H5 0.344, plant 0.418, XGBoost 0.485. In zero history H5 is 1.6% worse than XGBoost at the 0.01 quantile (interval -3.3% to +5.3%), so the 5% target holds only in the own-history setting there.
  • Per farm, H5 minus plant in quantile score: A -2.4%, B -5.4%, C -5.3%, D -5.4%, E -2.7%, F -5.3%. Leaving one farm out keeps H5 minus plant between -4.2% and -4.8%, and H5 minus XGBoost within 0.5% of zero.
  • Seeds. The standard deviation of the score across five seeds is 0.007 for H5 and 0.021 for the neural network.
  • Tail calibration. Coverage at the 0.99 level is 99.35% for XGBoost (over-covered) and 98.0% to 98.5% for the other arms.
  • Curtailment value. Not scored, because experiment 224 found that its pilot set of grid nodes cannot rank forecasts by curtailment value.
  • Departures from the brief. The experiment's brief (the written specification it was set up from) asks for weekly refits, day of year as an input, and a violation count for monotonicity in irradiance. We ran one fit on the tuning months, left day of year out (it lets a network memorise the date), and did not count violations. Outputs are non-negative, at most the farm's ceiling, and non-crossing by construction. The interpretability plots for H1 and H3 were not drawn. Part (B), which adds the Met Office's UKV weather-model variables as inputs, was not run.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (points of capacity, own history): H5 +0.52, plant +0.89, neural network +0.18, XGBoost -0.51. The mean forecast is the weighted mean of the 11 quantiles.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each quantile contrast. The MAE of the mean forecast is 9.93 for H5, 10.19 for the plant, 10.17 for the neural network, and 10.17 for XGBoost. H5's gain against the plant in the quantile score (4.4%) is matched by a 2.6% gain in the MAE of the mean forecast, so the gain is both in location and in width.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 3 (a quantile contrast and the median MAE disagree) fires for the neural network: its quantile score is 3.2% better than the plant's, while its MAE of the median is 1.1% worse. The neural network is better at the 0.99 quantile (-21.6%) and worse at the 0.01 quantile (+7.3%), so the quantile score hides opposite tail effects. Trigger 4 (a nested arm worse than the arm it contains) fires weakly: H4 scores 0.5% worse than H1, within the seed spread. The blind control H6 scores 1% worse than H2, which suggests the plant carries only a small part of the gain. Trigger 7 (a later part builds on these results) fires, because part (B) builds on these results. No Opus audit was run, because the ML manager ruled one out to save quota. A Sonnet reviewer read the code for leakage and found no scored-year row in any fit: the plant scale, ceiling, offsets, normalisation, and epoch choice, and the XGBoost fit, use rows before 2025-09-01 only, and the zero-history fits never see the scored farm's training rows.
  • Caveat: zero history still reads recent power. In the zero-history setting the scored farm's own power from one or two days earlier is an input (lagged power), so "zero history" means no training history, not no live observations.
  • Caveat: lead of exactly 24 hours. A lead of exactly 24 hours uses the observation at the forecast time, which assumes no telemetry delay.
  • Caveat: the plant arm lacks two inputs. The plant arm has no lagged power and no spread, so part of H5's gain over the plant may come from those inputs and not from the neural network's capacity. A follow-up could give the plant the same inputs.
  • Caveat: XGBoost is not handicapped. XGBoost sees the same 12 raw columns as the neural network (including lagged power and spread) plus the plant forecast.
  • Caveat: one fit, 12 months. The scored year uses one fit on the tuning months, with no refit, and has 12 months, so the intervals are wide. The floors are re-implemented from their definitions.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether the 4.4% gain of H5 survives when the plant arm is given the same lagged power and ensemble spread as inputs, and whether UKV variables (part B) improve H5 and the neural network at 12 to 36 hours.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
• Weather and forecast time. ECMWF ensemble (51 members), 00 UTC run, at the nearest 0.25 degree cell, 12 to 36 hours ahead, as in experiment 224: ensemble-mean irradiance, beam, diffuse, and temperature, and the members' standard deviation of irradiance. All exist at forecast time. Lagged power is the farm's own observed power one day earlier (two days earlier when the lead is over 24 hours), which exists at forecast time. This is part (A); part (B) adds UKV variables.
  • Plant. The fleet-shape plant of experiment 224 (tilt 35 degrees, south, 0.4% loss per kelvin of cell temperature), with a scale and a ceiling per farm. Its quantiles are the plant forecast plus 11 residual quantiles of the tuning months in four bins of the forecast ("the offsets").
  • Arms. References: the two floors and the plant alone and XGBoost. Pure neural network: a multilayer perceptron on the raw weather, sun geometry, lead, and lagged power. H1: the plant times a bounded scale factor from a network. H2: the plant plus an additive correction from a network. H3: a network adjusts the irradiance and temperature, which then go through the unchanged plant (trained end to end). H4: H3 followed by H1. H5: the plant plus a network that outputs all 11 quantile offsets. H6: H2 without the plant forecast as input (the blind control).
  • Settings. (i) Own history: each farm's network and plant scale are fitted on its own tuning months (before 2025-09). (ii) Zero history, leave-one-farm-out: the networks and XGBoost are fitted on the other five farms' tuning months, and the plant scale and ceiling are the median over those five farms, so the scored farm contributes no data. The two are reported separately.
  • Inputs left out on purpose. Day of year is not an input, because a calendar column lets a network memorise the date; solar elevation and azimuth carry the season. The hybrids see no farm label, so setting (ii) is possible.
  • Schedule. One fit per arm, seed, and setting on the tuning months; no refit in the scored year (the screening schedule; the weekly refits the brief asks for the headline are not run). Five seeds per neural arm; the last two tuning months select the training epoch. Pinball loss at the 11 levels is the training loss; outputs are non-negative and capped at the farm's ceiling by construction, and the quantiles are non-crossing by construction.

docs.title: Data-processing note
docs.text: Experiment 268 found crossing quantiles in 26,344 of its 77,897 generator-forecast rows (34%), but all of them belong to three generators that are not solar farms, so none is on this page. Experiment 273 counted 0 crossing rows in every arm here, because the fit scripts sorted the 11 quantiles before writing them, so sorting does not change the scores on this page.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: does the disagreement between independently trained correction networks set the width of the cold-night bands?
docs.text:
Take-home: the spread of 20 independently trained neural networks does not predict how wrong the substation demand forecast is on cold nights, so it cannot set the width of the cold-night prediction bands. On cold nights the 95% quantile of E0's bands (the combined bands of experiment 169) covers 0.8875 of the readings, against a nominal 0.95. Scaling the bands by the spread raises that coverage to 0.8939, and scaling by a randomly shuffled spread, a control, raises it to 0.8951. The registered check that the spread reacts to an unusual input failed, so the verdict is inconclusive, although every contrast points the same way as refuted. The experiment cannot rule out other uses of the spread.

The question. We asked whether the demand forecast's cold-night errors reflect information that the correction network lacks, which the disagreement between independently trained copies of the network would show. Experiment 192 found that the 51 ensemble weather members differ too little to signal the error. A cold night is a winter night (November to March, evening or night hours) whose ERA5 day-mean temperature (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' estimate of past weather) is below 2 C.

The method. We trained 20 copies of the pooled correction network of experiment 200 and experiment 211, once without and once with recent-error inputs, with different random seeds, or on bootstrap resamples of whole months. The error inputs are the forecast's recent errors. The correction network is a small neural network that shifts and rescales the quantiles of arm D, the best day-ahead forecast of experiment 155. Deep ensembles are the method of Lakshminarayanan et al. (2017). The spread of the 20 corrections scaled the bands of E0, the combined bands of experiment 169 (arm D with experiment 160's smooth table and experiment 164's widening). Scores are quantile scores in points of effective capacity, lower is better, on experiment 211's rows: scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29, leads 15.5 to 39 h, five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16). A row is one substation's forecast for one half-hour from one run.

The caveat. The scored year holds 782 cold-night rows on 10 days, so every cold-night number is noisy.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Gate (failed). The registered shift (4 C times the substation's cold-night slope, applied to the forecast-level input) lowered the spread of the network without error inputs from 0.426 to 0.393 on the 18 injected rows (ratio 0.92, 95% interval 0.87 to 0.99) and from 0.387 to 0.360 on all 894 cold-night rows (the 782 rows of the decision substations plus D9's 112). The rule needed a ratio of at least 1.1, so the verdict is capped at inconclusive. The failure comes from the gate's design: cold-night inputs already sit at the 70th to 95th percentile of each substation's training levels, so the registered shift moves them towards the middle. A shift of 25 times the size raised the spread 6.4-fold, and the opposite sign gave 1.10 (the audit's post hoc check).
  • Prediction 1 (fails). Cold-night Spearman correlation of the seed-ensemble spread with the absolute error of E0's median: 0.00 (95% day-resampled interval -0.19 to +0.18) in the scored year, -0.16 (-0.50 to +0.34) in the replicate even months on 257 rows over 4 days, -0.07 in the odd (tuning) months. Over all rows it is 0.27 (0.25 to 0.29). The error-input networks reach 0.29 (0.05 to 0.41) in the scored year and -0.01 in the replicate months. Pre-registered rule: at least 0.2 with a lower bound above 0.1 in both years.
  • Prediction 2 (fails). E0's cold-night q95 coverage is 0.8875 on these rows (0.896 in experiment 169 over leads to 168 h). E3 reaches 0.8939 (+0.0064, 0.0014 to 0.0116), below 0.90. The placebo P (20 shuffles within substation, month, and hour band) reaches 0.8951, E3 minus P is -0.0012 (-0.0036 to 0.0000), and the shuffle across substations gives +0.0077. E3's q95 scale is 1.017 plus 0.024 per unit of spread above the 90th percentile; the intercept alone gives the whole lift.
  • Prediction 3 (passes). The 20 single-network gains over arm D range from 0.083 to 0.100 (mean 0.090, standard deviation 0.0052) without error inputs and from 0.076 to 0.128 (mean 0.107, standard deviation 0.0147) with them (figure 3).
  • Arms, scored year, five decision substations. Arm D 2.4317, E0 2.4302, E1 (mean of the 20 corrections, arm D's offsets) 2.3315 without and 2.2920 with error inputs, E1 bagged 2.3328 and 2.3095, E3 2.4307 (E3 minus E0 +0.0005, -0.0021 to +0.0030). Replicate even months: E3 minus E0 +0.0009 (-0.0023 to +0.0042). E3 on the error-input spread scores 0.007 lower than E0 (-0.0124 to -0.0021), post hoc and descriptive: it was not the registered arm and the placebo was run on the reference spread only.
  • Tail calibration, scored year (coverage / pinball loss; nominal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99). All rows, E0: q01 0.022 / 0.386, q05 0.064 / 1.265, q95 0.948 / 1.320, q99 0.981 / 0.416. All rows, E3: 0.022 / 0.387, 0.072 / 1.273, 0.950 / 1.319, 0.984 / 0.410. Cold nights, E0: 0.042 / 0.751, 0.088 / 1.752, 0.887 / 1.491, 0.962 / 0.420. Cold nights, E3: 0.043 / 0.754, 0.091 / 1.764, 0.894 / 1.475, 0.972 / 0.397. Cold nights, E1 without error inputs: 0.038 / 0.629, 0.086 / 1.594, 0.797 / 1.859, 0.910 / 0.661; the network head moves the cold-night upper tail further from nominal than E0.
  • Checks.
    • Median minus mean forecast: E0's median equals its mean at every substation (difference 0.0); E1's centre minus the mean is -0.52, 0.01, -0.35, 0.19, and -0.04 at D10, D11, D14, D16, and D5.
    • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts: E3 shares E0's centre, so its centre error is E0's (mean error -0.32, absolute error 4.19). E1's centre scores 4.06 absolute error against 4.19, the same direction as its score gain. On cold nights E1's mean error is +1.78 against E0's +1.22 and its absolute error 5.10 against 5.14.
    • Leave one substation out: E3's cold-night coverage lift stays positive at all five substations (+0.004 to +0.009); the all-row score contrast changes sign (D11 -0.0014, D10 +0.0023), inside its interval.
    • Triggers: the failed gate (a known-answer test) fired trigger 1 of the skill's seven audit triggers (a control fails), so a fresh Opus audit re-derived every headline from the stored files and found no error that changes a number or the verdict (the report is in the private briefs folder). Its points: row alignment and out-of-sample head sets correct, no leakage in the training masks, the gate wired correctly and failing by design, E3's lift from its intercept alone. Trigger 6 (a headline interval under half as wide as a sister experiment's) is not met on like rows: experiment 169's interval covers leads to 168 h and resamples months, this experiment's covers 15.5 to 39 h and resamples days.
  • Caveats. The gate injects through the forecast-level input because the networks have no temperature input, and its slope uses ERA5 temperature rather than the ensemble-mean temperature. The replicate year uses two cross-fit network sets trained on 3 to 5 months of ensemble-weather rows each, so it is not like-for-like with the scored year. D9's training data starts in 2024. Schedule: one fit per network, no retraining cadence; the contrasts do not depend on it.
  • What to try next. (1) An input-distance score (the forecast level's distance from its training range) as the band-width covariate, since the spread tracks it at 0.50 on cold nights. (2) A bias correction of the mean forecast at ensemble-mean temperatures near 0 C, as experiment 169 proposed. (3) A small neural layer is not indicated by this result; the prediction that could fail is that a learned scale on the cold-night residual beats the constant 1.017 widening on 3 winters.

docs.title: Pre-registration amendments (made before any score or spread was read)
docs.text:
• Early stopping and purge. The full and cfx sets stop on 2025-04-28 to 2025-06-24; cfy stops on 2024-10-01 to 2024-11-10, because its held-out half contains the usual block. All early-stopping blocks come from the training half. A 15-day purge sits on both sides of each held-out half and each early-stopping block. The cross-fit networks see 3 to 5 months of ensemble weather rows, fewer than the full set's 12, so the replicate-year numbers are not like-for-like with the scored year.
  • Normalisation and knots. The spread z is divided by the median spread of the tuning months of the same head set, and the knots are the 50th and 90th percentiles of the tuning months. The scored year is divided by the full set's own tuning-month median. The tuning-month spread distributions of the cross-fit and the full sets are plotted side by side.
  • Months. E3 is fitted on all rows of the odd months (tuning) of 2024-07 to 2025-06, never on cold nights alone. The replicate-year test of prediction 1 uses the even months; the odd months are reported beside it. Cold-night row and day counts of each period are printed; if the tuning months hold fewer than 300 cold-night rows, the cold-night result is read from the scored year and the replicate even months alone.
  • Intervals. Spearman correlations and coverages carry 95% intervals resampled by valid day. Prediction 1 passes when the point estimate is at least 0.2 and the interval's lower bound is above 0.1. E3 passes prediction 2 on a point estimate of 0.90 or more, and the write-up states whether the lift over E0 exceeds its interval.
  • Placebo. Primary P shuffles z among rows of the same substation, valid month, and hour band, 20 times (seeds 0 to 19); the reported lift is the mean over shuffles. A second placebo shuffles among all substations (descriptive). P is read as a difference from E3 in cold-night q95 coverage over resampled days. E3 must lift coverage by at least 0.005 for the "P's lift under half of E3's" clause to apply.
  • Gate. The forecast level (mean, divided by 100) is one of the network's inputs, so the injection reaches the networks. The cold-night slope of the forecast level on ensemble-mean temperature is fitted on the training months (2020 to 2025-06) of each substation. The rows are picked with seed 244, the spread is computed twice on the same rows (clean and injected), and the number of injected rows and days is printed. The gate reads spread only, no coverage or score.
  • Prediction 3. The seed-to-seed spread is the standard deviation, across the 20 seeds, of each single network's scored-year all-row quantile-score gain over arm D, using the network's own bands (arm D offsets), in points of effective capacity.
  • Extra arms and reports. E1's own score (ensemble-mean centre, arm D offsets) is reported so the change of centre is separate from the band scaling; E3's centre is E0's mean. E3 fits the levels 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, and 0.99 as experiment 169 did; the middle three levels (0.40, 0.50, 0.60) keep E0's offsets. The spread of the log scales is reported as a second covariate (Spearman only). E3 on the bagged spread (E2) is fitted too and reported as descriptive. The coverage by spread decile is the first figure, and the 20 seed gains and the placebo follow. Experiment 201's three stored corrections are not used. Experiments 160, 164, 169, 192, 200, 201, 209, and 211 are cited in the write-up.

docs.title: Are the false steps in the meter-regime test load shifts between Primaries?
docs.text:
The false steps in experiment 207 are not load moved between connected Primary substations, and the load-shift alarms do not explain them. A Primary substation is one that feeds homes and businesses. Experiment 207 fitted one solar capacity (in MW) for each month to a Primary's power. In a year with no change at the site, the fit still jumped by more than 0.5 MW between two months at some Primaries. We call such a jump a false step. Experiment 207's test requires fewer than 1 false step per year, and the test failed at the anonymised Primaries D10 and D11.

We asked whether the false steps are real transfers of load between neighbouring Primaries, which would also show as a step in the Primary's demand forecast error. We took the 7 false steps at D10 and D11 that fall between two summer months, so that the month of the step is known. For each, we looked for an explanation within a 30-day window around the month boundary. An explanation is either a step of the opposite sign at a metered neighbouring Primary, 0.4 to 2.5 times the size of the Primary's own largest step and at least 2 noise units (a noise unit is the spread of that Primary's one-day steps in odd-numbered months), within 6 hours of the own step; or an alarm within 24 hours of the own step from one of three load-shift alarms. The alarms are RO-NC (the refit-offset neighbour-count detector of experiment 130), the pair alarm (opposite steps at a connected metered neighbour, experiment 156), and the learned score (a logistic regression on the detector features, experiment 195).

We repeated the check on random 30-day windows at the same Primary and calendar month, with a step of similar size and no false step within 31 days. These matched windows give the base rate: how often an explanation appears when no false step is present. This experiment reads stored results and fits nothing. The result narrows the search: the false steps and the load-shift detectors are separate problems, and the first check at the false steps is the cleaning rule's zero readings.

The prediction fails: 3 of 7 false steps have an explanation (0.43), below the matched base rate of 0.66, where the prediction needed at least twice that rate. The 95% interval for the ratio is 0.19 to 1.0 (bootstrap over the 7 false steps). No false step has a balanced opposite neighbour step (0 of 7, base rate 0.51). Verdict not supported.

The recount of experiment 207's test shows nothing about cause. With the explained false steps removed, the test passes at D10 (0.80 false steps per year, from 1.73) and still fails at D11 (1.00). Matched random windows are explained more often (0.66) than the false steps are (0.43), so removing "explained" steps removes steps at random. This is a diagnostic, and the verdict on experiment 207 stands as it was.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The false steps are explained no more often than matched windows, whichever explanation is counted. Each row gives the share of the 7 false steps, then the base rate in brackets:

  • Balanced opposite neighbour step: 0 of 7 (0.00; 0.51).
  • RO-NC alarm: 2 of 7 (0.29; 0.48).
  • Pair alarm: 1 of 7 (0.14; 0.00). The one pair alarm is at D11, August 2022, where no matched window had one, so one event decides this row.
  • Learned score alarm: 4 of 7 (0.57; 0.50).
  • Any alarm: 3 of 7 (0.43; 0.50).
  • Any explanation: 3 of 7 (0.43; 0.66).

An explanation counts only where the Primary's largest residual step in the window reaches 3 noise units. At D11, August 2022, the step is 2.7 noise units, so its pair and learned alarms are not counted. Counting them would give 4 of 7 explained (0.57), still under the base rate of 0.66.

The ratio to the base rate is 0.65 (0.19 to 1.0) at D10 and D11 together. It is 0.75 at D10 alone (5 false steps) and 0.00 at D11 alone (2 false steps). Across the four Primaries that have matched windows, the ratio is 0.71 (0.26 to 1.0) for 8 of the 10 false steps; D14 has no matched window. An alarm anywhere in the 30-day window occurs at 4 of 7 false steps (0.57), against 0.55 of matched windows.

Three false steps sit within a day of readings of 0 MW that the cleaning rule flags, and no matched window does. These are D11 August 2022, D11 May 2023, and D14 August 2022, each with 1 to 7 half-hourly readings flagged substation_zero, against none of the 241 matched windows. The model sees a flagged zero as an ordinary reading, so the zeros may cause the step; this experiment does not test that. No false step is within a day of a bank holiday (share of matched windows: 0.11). The largest residual step has the same sign as the capacity step in 4 of the 10 false steps and the opposite sign in 6, so the two steps do not share a direction.

No audit trigger of the ml-experiment skill fired. The failed prediction was pre-registered as a possible outcome. No control or nested arm exists. D10 alone and D11 alone give the same verdict (0.60 against 0.80 at D10, 0.00 against 0.30 at D11, observed share against base rate). No later experiment depends on the result. No forecast is scored, so the forecast-error checks do not apply.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Row definition: the false steps are the step path of experiment 207 at weight 0.3 (its pre-registered penalty on month-to-month jumps), fitted with no injected farm, on summer rows of 2022 to 2024. Experiment 207 fitted 5 row sets per Primary, one for each solar farm it injected in other tests, and the same step in several row sets counts once. A false step between two summer months is dated to a 30-day window centred on the first day of the later month, because the fit gives one capacity per month, so a step can be dated only to a month.
  • Gate recount: false steps per year before and after removing the explained ones: D5 0.00 and 0.00, D10 1.73 and 0.80, D11 1.00 and 1.00, D14 0.93 and 0.67, D16 0.60 and 0.27. The August-to-April net change makes up 10 of D10's 26 false-step counts and 5 of D11's 15, where a count is a false step in one row set in one year, and the recount keeps it because it cannot be dated. A post hoc recount without it, before any removal, gives D10 1.07 and D11 0.67.
  • The Primary's own step: the largest one-day level shift of the demand model's forecast error in the window, from the convex model of experiment 130 (arm B), needing 3 noise units. The step of D10 in August 2022 falls at the window's edge (Figure 2), so a window of this width can pick a step from the neighbouring month.
  • Alarms: RO-NC from experiment 130, and the pair alarm and the logistic learned score from experiment 195. The learned score counts an alarm from any of experiment 195's three cross-validation folds, so it covers more alarms than one fold would.
  • Matched windows: 241 windows over the 8 false steps that have any (10 to 62 per false step; both D14 false steps have none and drop out of the ratios). The size match is on the Primary's own largest residual step in MW, within 30% of the false step's, not on the size of the capacity step. The windows come from 2022 to 2025 (16, 10, 85, and 130 windows in each year in turn). The alarm tables cover every year to mid-2026.
  • Caveats: 7 false steps at the two failing Primaries cannot show a small effect, and the ratio's interval is 0.19 to 1.0. A capacity fitted once per month cannot show cause. The residual uses ERA5 past weather, not forecasts, and the alarm tables are built with hindsight, so the check favours the detectors more than live use would.

docs.title: What the next experiment could answer
docs.text: One option is whether the 3 readings flagged substation_zero beside false steps cause the steps. A fit that masks flagged zero readings, and keeps the August-to-April net change out of the false-step count, would show how many of the 26 and 15 false-step counts remain at D10 and D11.

docs.title: Does adding the DWD ICON-D2 weather forecast to the ensemble plus UKV lower a metered solar farm's day-ahead error?
docs.text:
Adding the German ICON-D2 weather forecast to the ECMWF ensemble and the Met Office UKV lowers the day-ahead error of a metered solar farm by 1.0%, which is under the 1.5% we set as worth a fourth weather source. ICON-D2 is the Deutscher Wetterdienst's regional weather model (2 km grid, run every 3 hours). The error is the quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity. The tree with ICON-D2 columns is 0.3% lower than the tree without them, with an interval that includes zero. The UKV used here is the research archive on the Centre for Environmental Data Analysis (CEDA), which differs statistically from the live UKV, so any gain is an upper limit for production.

We asked whether a metered solar farm's output is forecast better from ensemble, UKV, and ICON-D2 together than from ensemble and UKV. For each of six farms, A to F, we compared the plant model on a blend of the three products' irradiance (arm B3) with the blend of ensemble and UKV (arm R3), and a second-stage tree with ICON-D2 columns (B4) with the tree without them (R5). R3 and R5 are experiment 229's arms A3 and A5, re-run on these rows. The verdict is a small gain. The pre-registered prediction was a gain under 1.5% with an interval including zero; the B3 interval excludes zero by a small margin (-1.8% to -0.1%).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. B2 is the plant model on a convex blend of the ensemble and ICON-D2 plant forecasts, with weights by UKV cloud band, so B2 also uses UKV's cloud forecast. B3 is the same on ensemble, UKV, and ICON-D2, with weights in steps of 0.1 by UKV cloud band, fitted on the other farms. B4 is the second-stage tree on ensemble columns, UKV shortwave, cloud, and plant-forecast columns, and six ICON-D2 columns (shortwave, direct radiation, air temperature, wind speed, the plant response to ICON-D2, and the plant forecast). B4x is the tree on ensemble and ICON-D2 columns only. The placebos are B3 and B4 with ICON-D2 taken from a random row of the same month, hour band, and cloud band.
  • Rows. The rows are 19,225 daylight half-hours (sun more than 5 degrees above the horizon) of six farms that have a complete UKV run and an ICON-D2 value, valid 12 to 29 hours after the ensemble run's 00 UTC start. The folds, the tuning months, and the 10 scored months are those of experiment 229. ICON-D2 enters through Open-Meteo's Previous Runs file (previous_day1, the run Open-Meteo labels as made about 24 hours before), assumed published 3 hours after the run starts, so the latest valid time available at an 08 UTC forecast origin is 29 hours out. The ICON-D2 tables hold no usable rows before 2024-04, so each fold is tuned on the months from 2024-04 to just before it.
  • The quantile score at 12 to 29 hours (mean over farms, 95% interval) is 5.75 (4.86 to 6.71) points of capacity for B4, 5.77 (4.85 to 6.76) for R5, 5.84 (4.99 to 6.73) for B3, 5.87 (4.96 to 6.87) for B4x, 5.89 (5.05 to 6.79) for R3, 6.05 (5.14 to 7.00) for B2, and 6.19 (5.33 to 7.15) for the ensemble plant A1. The placebos score 5.88 (B4) and 5.97 (B3), climatology 9.25, and the manual heuristic 9.62.
  • The planned contrasts are the median over six farms of the percentage change, with 99% intervals (the Bonferroni level for five contrasts). D1, B3 against R3, is -1.0% (-1.8 to -0.1). D2, B4 against R5, is -0.3% (-1.0 to +0.4). D3, B2 against A1, is -2.7% (-4.8 to -0.1). D4, B3 against its placebo, is -2.4% (-3.4 to -1.3), and D5, B4 against its placebo, is -2.6% (-3.7 to -1.1). The hypothesis needed D1 or D2 at least 1.5% lower, and neither is. D1's interval excludes zero at 2 of 6 farms (A and F), D2's at 2 (B and D).
  • Shuffling ICON-D2 raises the error by more than adding ICON-D2 lowers it. D4 and D5 are larger than D1 and D2 because the blend weights and the tree are fitted on the real ICON-D2, so a shuffled column breaks the fit. The placebo contrasts show that ICON-D2 carries information about the day; D1 and D2 show how little it adds to the other two products.
  • ICON-D2 is weaker than the ensemble and highly correlated with it. On sunny half-hours the correlation of plant-forecast errors is 0.76 between ICON-D2 and the ensemble, 0.60 between ICON-D2 and UKV, and 0.59 between UKV and the ensemble. B3's weights, averaged over the farms and both folds, are 0.44 ensemble, 0.36 UKV, and 0.20 ICON-D2 in the clearest cloud band (UKV cloud under 30%), 0.60, 0.22, and 0.18 in the middle band, and 0.70, 0.20, and 0.10 in the cloudiest. In B2 ICON-D2 receives 0.42, 0.27, and 0.20 in the same bands. Ensemble plus UKV (X1) is 5.0% better than the ensemble alone on these rows (-7.6 to -2.3), nearly twice B2's 2.7%. The shuffle placebo draws a random row of the same farm, month, hour band, and cloud band, which may be the row itself.
  • On sunny half-hours the plant fit rises by 0.008. The fraction of output fitted (clear-sky irradiance above 650 W/m², median over farms) is 0.931 for A1, 0.935 for B2, 0.938 for R3, and 0.939 for B3. The gap to 0.973 (experiment 218's fit with observed weather, on other rows) is 0.042 for A1, and B3 closes 19% of that gap, compared with 17% for R3.
  • The tails are not calibrated at the lowest levels for any arm, nor at q05 and q95 for the trees. Pooled over farms, the coverage at q01 is 0.041 for A1, 0.040 for R3, and 0.040 for B3, against 0.01 nominal. At q99 it is 0.993 for all three. The trees are worse at q05 (0.123 for B4 and 0.122 for R5 against 0.05) and at q95 (0.917 and 0.919 against 0.95). B3 beats the manual heuristic's quantile score by 41% (X3, -49.6 to -31.5). The curtailment value is not scored.
  • The checks show no spread shifting the forecast. The mean forecast's absolute error points the same way as the quantile score (10.25 for B4, 10.31 for R5, 10.37 for B3, 10.46 for R3, and 11.13 for A1, in points of capacity). B3's gain over R3 is negative at 5 of 6 farms (not at E, +0.05%), and both folds agree: B3 scores 5.22 against R3's 5.26 on the scored fold, and 6.38 against 6.42 on the replicate.
  • The data gate passed. ICON-D2 shortwave peaks in the same hour as the clear-sky curve at all six farms. The plant fed ICON-D2 shortwave has a held-out mean absolute error of 10.5 to 12.9 points of capacity, against 16.2 to 18.9 for the cloudless sky. Coverage is 99% to 100% of half-hours in every month from 2024-04, except 94% in 2026-04 and the partial 2026-09, and none before 2024-04. The stop rule's 18 months of overlap is met (2024-04 to 2026-08). The monthly ratio of ICON-D2 to clear-sky shortwave on sunny rows is 0.52 to 0.84. The ratio is defined only for April to September, the months with sunny half-hours.
  • Audit triggers. The trigger for a nested arm beating the arm that contains it did not fire in the planned pairs, but B4x, without UKV, scores worse than R5 (X2, +1.4%, 0.06 to 3.6), as expected. The trigger for a result contradicting its prediction fires only for the interval of D1, which excludes zero by 0.07 percentage points. No audit was run, because the size of the contradiction (1.0% against a predicted under 1.5%) does not change the next step. The ICON-D2 ensemble arm was not run: D1 and D2 are below the 1.5% that the plan sets for a gain.
  • The scope is narrow. The 12 to 29 hour band is the first 17 hours of the day-ahead forecast, and no row has a lead over 29 hours. The scored months are 10, of which 4 are autumn and winter, and the UKV era from 2026-02 is not scored. ICON-D2's publication delay of 3 hours is an assumption. The weather is read at each farm's nearest grid cell, and the schedule is one refit per fold, as in experiment 229.
  • What to try next. A weather product of a different kind from a regional deterministic forecast, such as a satellite-derived cloud nowcast for the early hours of the day, and a small learned irradiance-response component fed by the three products.

docs.title: Data-processing note
docs.text: Experiment 268 found crossing quantiles in 26,344 of its 77,897 generator-forecast rows (34%), but all of them belong to three generators that are not solar farms, so none is on this page. Experiment 273 counted 0 crossing rows in every arm here, because the fit scripts sorted the 11 quantiles before writing them, so sorting does not change the scores on this page.

docs.title: Can the export cap of the solar clip be learned from the metered series instead of set to 60%?
docs.text:
The profile fit learns a ceiling that closes most of the hand-set clip's gain, but one year of data cannot show it reaches 80%. The profile fit refits the demand model for ceilings of 40% to 100% of held capacity on the 12 months before each cut and keeps the ceiling with the lowest training objective. At D5 the learned ceiling stays between 55% and 70%, close to the hand-set 60% (figure 2).

Figure 1. The arms against the unclipped fit at D5 and D9.

What already exists. Experiment 214 picks the clip ceiling as-of from a grid of shares by out- of-sample error, and experiment 110's profile_clip fits the ceiling in sample. Neither experiment learns the cap from the series alone without scoring a grid of candidate shares on forecast error. The as-of choice of experiment 214 scores about the same as the profile fit at D5 (0.129 MW).

Closure at the decision site. Closure is an arm's gain over the unclipped fit divided by the hand-set clip's gain, on D5's sunniest third of daylight half-hours, months resampled as whole blocks in pairs.

Arm D5 closure (95% interval) D9 closure (95% interval) Profile fit (learned) 96% (62% to 104%) 93% (70% to 189%) Clear-sky envelope (learned) 60% (22% to 79%) 23% (5% to 32%) 60% clip, softer edge 100% (99% to 100%) 104% (98% to 134%)

The profile fit passes the pre-registered 80% as a point estimate at both sites. The profile fit's interval reaches below 80%, so the verdict is partly supported. The envelope arm fails: the quantile of implied clear-sky export sits at 67% to 86% of held capacity at D5 and 84% to 100% at D9 (figure 2), above the ceilings that help.

Figure 2. The ceiling each learned arm picked at each monthly cut.

The placebos do not move. The arms change D10's and D16's sunny-daylight error by between -0.009 and +0.003 MW (figure 3), inside the 0.02 MW limit.

Figure 3. The arms against the unclipped fit at D10 and D16.

The clip's edge is not the active ingredient. A softer edge (smoothing 0.5 per point of capacity instead of 2.0) gives the same gain as the hand-set clip: 0.132 MW at D5 against 0.133 MW.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Each cut's ceiling uses only rows before that cut. The envelope arm's window ends at the cut, and the profile fit's training rows end there.
  • The arms read the same rows as experiment 178's cut, and the row counts match the control's.
  • The scoring script raises when an arm's row count differs from the control's after the join.
  • Held capacity can come from an early vintage newer than the cut when no vintage predates it; all arms share that choice.
  • Closure ratios are unstable when the hand-set clip's own gain is small, as at D9 (the interval reaches 189%).

docs.title: Which clip form the final assembly should use
docs.text: Use the hand-set 60% ceiling. Its gain is close to the profile fit's, and it needs no fitting step at each cut. The softer edge changes nothing, so the experiment-180 form stays. Where a site has no hand-set value, the profile fit is the better of the two learned choices.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment takes the clip and the profile-fit cap as inputs. The small monotone neural network of the brief's experiment 4 receives either ceiling as one of its inputs.

docs.title: Do UKV irradiance and cloud inputs improve the two best neural heads on the plant for a metered solar farm?
docs.text:
Giving the neural heads UKV irradiance and cloud columns lowers a metered solar farm's quantile score by about 1%, and XGBoost gains as much, so UKV is a small gain, below the 3% threshold. Experiment 248 is part (B) of the architecture comparison in experiment 243, which compared a solar-farm power model (the "plant"), XGBoost, a neural network, and six hybrids at six metered solar farms labelled A to F. We gave H5 (the plant forecast plus 11 quantile offsets from a neural network) and H2 (the plant forecast plus a correction from a neural network) six columns from UKV, the Met Office's UK high-resolution weather model: shortwave irradiance and the total, low, medium, high, and very low cloud fractions. Experiment 229 found that these columns lower the score by 1.8% when blended into the plant's irradiance. We scored 12 to 36 hour leads on daylight half-hours in 2025-03 to 2025-12, in two folds of 6 and 4 months. The score is the quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity.

The prediction fails: no arm gains 3%. Over the 10 scored months, H5 with UKV columns scores 5.96 against 6.02 for H5 with ensemble inputs only, a change of -1.1% (95% interval -2.2% to -0.1%). H2 gains 1.5% (0.2% to 2.5%) and XGBoost gains 1.4% (0.6% to 2.2%), so XGBoost gains at least as much as H5, against the prediction. The control, which takes the UKV columns from another day of the same farm, month, half-hour, and ensemble clear-sky band, changes the score by -0.07% (-0.44% to +0.29%). H5 with UKV beats the control by 1.0% (0.2% to 2.0%). The gain is smaller than 3%. H5 with UKV scores 0.5% below XGBoost with UKV, but the interval (-2.9% to +2.2%) spans zero.

The gain is similar in the two folds and differs across farms. H5's score falls 1.5% in 2025-09 to 2025-12 (interval -2.0% to -1.0%) and 1.4% in 2025-03 to 2025-08 (interval -2.8% to +0.9%). At farm A, UKV makes H5 3.0% worse, and at farm D 0.3% worse; at farms B, C, E, and F it makes H5 1.3% to 3.6% better.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Rows. The scored rows are 34,147 daylight half-hours (sun more than 5 degrees above the horizon) at 12 to 36 hour leads with a usable UKV run: 10,470 in 2025-09 to 2025-12 and 23,677 in 2025-03 to 2025-08. Each farm has equal weight, and the 95% intervals come from resampling the 10 scored months 20,000 times. Neural scores are means over five seeds; XGBoost and the plant have one fit each.
  • Weather and forecast time. European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble inputs as in experiment 243. UKV from the Centre for Environmental Data Analysis (CEDA) archive at the farm's nearest cell, from the freshest complete run published 4 hours before the forecast time (the delay experiment 229 assumed). Both the ensemble run and the UKV run exist at forecast time. Lagged power is the farm's own observed power one day earlier (two days when the lead is over 24 hours).
  • Quantile score, both folds (95% interval): H5 with UKV 5.96 (5.00 to 6.91); XGBoost with UKV 5.99 (4.93 to 7.07); H5 with UKV from another day 6.02; H5 6.02 (5.07 to 6.98); XGBoost 6.08 (5.00 to 7.19); H2 with UKV 6.12; H2 6.22; plant 6.34 (5.36 to 7.34); climatology 9.19; manual heuristic 9.68.
  • Quantile score by fold: in 2025-09 to 2025-12, XGBoost with UKV 5.46, XGBoost 5.59, H5 with UKV 5.61, H5 5.69, plant 5.94, climatology 7.87, manual heuristic 8.50; in 2025-03 to 2025-08, H5 with UKV 6.38, H5 6.47, XGBoost with UKV 6.64, XGBoost 6.74, plant 6.88.
  • Contrasts, both folds, quantile score: H5 with UKV minus H5 -1.10% (-2.24 to -0.07); H2 with UKV minus H2 -1.48% (-2.47 to -0.20); XGBoost with UKV minus XGBoost -1.44% (-2.24 to -0.56); H5 with UKV minus the control -1.03% (-1.96 to -0.23); control minus H5 -0.07% (-0.44 to +0.29); H5 with UKV minus XGBoost with UKV -0.53% (-2.87 to +2.17); H5 with UKV minus the plant -6.07% (-8.13 to -4.09).
  • By fold, H5 with UKV minus H5: 2025-09 to 2025-12 -1.53% (-1.97 to -1.05); 2025-03 to 2025-08 -1.44% (-2.76 to +0.90). In the 2025-09 to 2025-12 fold, XGBoost with UKV minus XGBoost is -2.33% (-4.18 to -1.34), larger than H5's gain.
  • Cloudy half-hours (clear-sky index under 0.5) and clear half-hours (0.5 or more), both folds; the clear-sky index is the ensemble-mean irradiance over the clear-sky irradiance: H5's gain is -1.3% (-5.2 to +4.1) on cloudy half-hours and -1.2% (-2.3 to 0.0) on clear half-hours, so the gain is not concentrated in cloud.
  • Per farm, change in quantile score from UKV columns, both folds (farms A to F): H5 +3.0%, -1.3%, -2.2%, +0.3%, -3.6%, -2.6%; XGBoost +0.2%, -1.4%, -1.2%, -0.8%, -3.0%, -2.3%; H2 +1.3%, -0.9%, -1.7%, -0.1%, -5.1%, -1.9%.
  • Mean absolute error (MAE) of the median, both folds (points of capacity): H5 with UKV 10.57; H5 10.71; XGBoost with UKV 10.57; XGBoost 10.78; plant 11.06. H5 with UKV minus H5 is -1.33% (-2.46 to +0.02).
  • Tails, both folds: pinball at the 0.99 quantile is 0.493 for H5 with and without UKV and 0.634 for XGBoost with and without UKV, so UKV does not change the upper tail for either forecaster. H5 with UKV is 22% lower than XGBoost with UKV at that quantile (interval -35% to -16%). At the 0.01 quantile, pinball loss is 2.5% higher with UKV, but the interval (-1.3% to +7.2%) spans zero.
  • Seeds. The standard deviation of the farm-mean score across five seeds is 0.01 to 0.07 for H5 and H2, with and without UKV.
  • Not measured. This experiment did not measure the curtailment value, ICON-D2 (a German weather service regional weather model) inputs (experiment 229's ICON-D2 follow-on has not reported that they helped), the zero-history setting, and the 22-variable UKV set (experiment 229 found it no better than the 6 used here).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (points of capacity, 2025-09 to 2025-12): H5 -0.10, H5 with UKV -0.29, plant -0.07, XGBoost -1.44, XGBoost with UKV -1.28. In 2025-03 to 2025-08: H5 +1.14, H5 with UKV +1.25, XGBoost +0.41. The mean forecast is the weighted mean of the 11 quantiles. In 2025-09 to 2025-12 the median of the neural heads sits close to their mean forecast, and UKV moves H5's median 0.2 points below its mean, so UKV shifts the centre of the forecast slightly more than its middle quantile.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each quantile contrast. The MAE of the mean forecast falls from 10.24 to 10.02 points of capacity for H5 in 2025-09 to 2025-12 (-2.2%) and from 11.50 to 11.09 in 2025-03 to 2025-08 (-3.6%), larger than the 1.5% and 1.4% quantile-score gains. For XGBoost it falls from 10.50 to 10.29 and from 11.84 to 11.63. UKV therefore improves the forecast's location at least as much as its spread.
  • Triggers fired. No trigger fired in a way that changes the verdict: the control behaves (it gives no gain), the averages without any one farm keep the sign of H5's gain at every farm left out (-0.1% to -2.6% across both folds), and the quantile score and the MAE point the same way. Trigger 7 does not apply. No Opus audit was run, because the ML manager ruled one out to save quota. A Sonnet reviewer has not read this experiment's code; the code is a copy of experiment 243's code, which a Sonnet reviewer read for leakage, with the folds, the UKV columns, and the control added.
  • Caveats. The CEDA UKV archive is a research archive and differs statistically from the live UKV, so any gain is an upper limit for production. Each fold tunes on the months before it, and the replicate fold's farm E has 1,063 tuning rows, so its fit there rests on little data. The share of observations below the 0.01 quantile forecast is 7% in 2025-09 to 2025-12 and about 3% in 2025-03 to 2025-08, against a nominal 1%, so the lower tail is under-covered in both folds for the neural heads, XGBoost, and the plant. The pooled intervals come from 10 months, and the leave-one-farm-out check refits nothing: it drops one farm from the average. The neural heads' inputs also include the lagged power and the ensemble spread, which the plant arm does not have.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should test whether a weather product of a different kind, such as a satellite-derived irradiance estimate at forecast time, lifts a metered solar farm's forecast by more than the 1% that UKV does, and whether the under-covered lower tail in autumn and winter can be fixed by recalibrating the offsets on recent months.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
• Why. Experiment 243 found that a neural head that outputs all 11 quantile offsets on the plant (H5) ties XGBoost, and that the best one-number hybrid is H2. Experiment 229 found that UKV adds 1.8% when blended into the plant's irradiance. This experiment asks whether a neural head extracts more from UKV than a blend does.
  • Weather and forecast time. ECMWF ensemble inputs as in experiment 243. UKV: the six irradiance and cloud variables of experiment 229 (shortwave down, and total, low, medium, high, and very low cloud) at the farm's nearest cell, from the freshest complete run published 4 hours before the forecast time, plus UKV shortwave over clear-sky irradiance. Both exist at forecast time. The UKV-CEDA archive is a research archive and differs from the live UKV, so every gain is an upper limit for production.
  • Arms. Ensemble only: the plant, XGBoost, H2, H5. With UKV columns: XGBoost, H2, H5. Control: H5 with UKV columns taken from another day of the same farm, month, half-hour, and ensemble clear-sky band. Five seeds per neural arm, one fit on the tuning months per fold, no refit. Experiment 229 found 22 UKV variables no better than 6, so only the six are used.
  • Folds. Scored fold 2025-09 to 2025-12, tuned on 2024-04 to 2025-08; replicate 2025-03 to 2025-08, tuned on 2024-04 to 2025-02. The last two tuning months of each fold select the training epoch. Both folds lie in the second UKV era, so no fit and score straddle a UKV physics change. Own-history setting only; the zero-history setting is not repeated.

docs.title: Data-processing note
