  • Position in the window. The position of the transfer in the 24-month training window is the same at every date, because every fit is cut at the end of the transfer, so the transfer is always the last 30 days of the window. This design cannot explain the spread.
  • Season. A seasonal shape explains the spread only weakly. The lowest share is in mid-January (8.6%) and the highest in late April (29.2%), but the same calendar month differs by up to 7.4 points between years: April is 29.2% in 2023 and 21.8% in 2024, and June is 24.5% in 2023 and 20.0% in 2024. The two extreme dates have mean transfers of 14.8 and 13.7 points, near the middle of the 10.9 to 16.1 range, so the size of the transfer is unlikely to explain them. The cause is not located.
  • Winter. The 2023-12-20 end date has a normal 48-hour share (21.8%), but the share over days 3 to 10 after the end is 2.0% and over days 10 to 17 is -8.6%. Christmas and the New Year fall in those windows. We did not test whether the holidays cause this.
  • Substations. The share, with the fit cut at the end of the transfer, runs from 19.9% (D12) to 24.0% (D10), and the bias from 1.51 (D12) to 3.48 (D11) points.
  • Later windows. Over days 3 to 10 the mean share is 19.3%, over days 10 to 17 it is 16.7%, and over days 3 to 33 it is 16.6%.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Cut offset. Moving the cut from the end date to 72 hours later lowers the mean share over days 3 to 10 from 19.3% to 18.8%. Across all 120 jobs, a cut 12 hours later changes the bias over days 10 to 17 by at most 0.04 points.
  • Experiment 274's jump. e00290_diagnose.py (output in diagnose_report.txt) refits D3 with a transfer ending on 1 July 2023. A cut at the end gives 2.13 points and a cut 12 hours later gives 0.88, as in experiment 274. A transfer ending on 2 July falls from 3.52 to 2.81, and one ending on 20 June barely changes (2.25 to 2.24). The jump appears at two of three D3 end dates around the start of July and in none of the 120 jobs here, which avoid the first of a month. We did not find its mechanism, so we cannot say whether other substations show it at those dates.
  • Median minus mean. GAM_ONLY forecasts the mean, so there is no median-minus-mean gap to report.
  • Audit. No Opus audit run; trigger 2 fired (agreed with the ML manager, to save quota).
  • Audit triggers. One of the seven fired: the result contradicts the prediction written here (a share within 15% to 25% at every date). The explanation we tested, the position of the transfer in the training window, is excluded by the design, and the cause remains open. No Opus audit was run, because this session was limited to Sonnet models. The spread matters most to later experiments that quote the 19% of experiment 274 as a single figure.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The cut is always at the end of the transfer, so the position of the shift in the 24-month window is fixed. Experiment 274 scored fits cut months after the end.
  • One shape (a share of the substation's own power), one size (25%), one window (24 months), and one injection per date.
  • The 95% t interval is from the 12 date means, not a bootstrap over substations as well.
  • The spread is not explained. Testing the holiday explanation needs end dates in matched holiday and non-holiday weeks.
  • Later experiments that report the share learned as normal could quote a range and use several end dates.

docs.title: Are D8's multi-day drops generator-engine spells?
docs.text:
D8's multi-day drops coincide with the engine detector's running states, which is consistent with one gas engine running, but this experiment cannot prove it. D8 is one of the 16 Primary substations of the trial. In 27 of its 28 drops that began after 2023-08-15, the engine detector flags at least half of the half-hours. The detector flags the same share in only about one in five matched windows of D8, and in none of the drops' dates at three other Primaries (D5, D10, and D11). The depths of the drops do not stand at whole multiples of one engine unit, so the second part of the prediction failed, and the verdict is partly supported: one of the two tests in the decision rule held.

We asked whether D8's drops coincide with a gas engine running. A drop is a stretch of 2 to 19 days in which D8's metered power sat about 2.7 MW below the power that the fitted expected-power model of experiment 159 predicted. That experiment found 29 drops. The first, in 2022, predates the engine's disappearance from D8's reading (experiments 194 and 196), so 28 drops are scored. The engine has up to three units of about 2 MW each. The detector of experiments 196 and 199 gives, for each half-hour, the probability that one or more units run. We call a half-hour "flagged" when that probability exceeds 0.5, and a drop "overlapping" when at least half of its half-hours are flagged. We compared the number of overlapping drops with the same number in 5,000 draws of placebo windows. A placebo window has the length of a drop, lies a whole number of weeks away, and avoids every drop. We also checked whether the drops' depths are whole numbers of one unit (1.97 MW), and whether the load-shift alarms of D8 fall inside the engine's spells.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. The detector flags at least half of the half-hours in 0.96 of D8's drops, in 0.19 of matched placebo windows, and in none of the drops' dates at D5, D10, and D11.

Figure 2. The depths spread across 0.6 to 2.7 units, with the most drops between 1.0 and 1.25 units.

Figure 3. D8's shortfall fades from March 2026 and no drop starts, but the detector still flags 39% to 48% of half-hours.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The detector flags most drops and few matched windows.

  • Overlap (arm v1, all half-hours of each drop): 27 of 28 drops (0.96; Wilson 95% interval 0.82 to 0.99). In the placebo windows 0.19 overlap, so 5.2 drops are expected (95% of draws 2 to 9; one-sided p 0.0002). On average 0.70 of a drop's half-hours are flagged.
  • Two periods: from 2023-08-15 to 2025-02-28, 10 of 11 drops overlap (placebo 0.12). From 2025-03-01, 17 of 17 overlap (placebo 0.23). Experiment 196 found that the detector over-flags D8 from March 2025, and outside the drops the detector flags 0.46 of D8's half-hours from then, against 0.31 before.
  • Night half-hours only (arm N, which does not decide the verdict): 14 of 28 drops overlap (0.50; 0.33 to 0.67), against a placebo of 0.05 (p 0.0002). The direction agrees with arm v1.
  • Controls: at D5, D10, and D11, 0 of 28 drops' dates have at least half of their half-hours flagged (placebo windows 0.00 to 0.01). A regional cause such as shared weather therefore does not explain the overlap.

The depths of the drops do not stand at whole units.

  • Unit: the unit estimated from the engine's recorded output is 1.93 MW (95% interval 1.91 to 1.95). The plan fixed 1.97 MW.
  • Depths: the mean distance of the 28 depths from the nearest multiple of one unit is 0.287 units (0.233 to 0.342) at 1.97 MW, 0.277 at 1.93 MW, and 0.230 at 1.75 MW. A uniform spread gives 0.25, and the prediction needed the interval wholly below 0.25. Depths from 2023-08-15 to 2025-02-28 (11 drops, median 3.6 MW) give 0.319, and depths from 2025-03 (17 drops, median 2.4 MW) give 0.266.
  • Steps at the drops' edges: the onset steps give 0.214 (0.159 to 0.273, p 0.046) at 1.97 MW but 0.222 at 1.75 MW (p 0.24). The end steps give 0.258 (0.207 to 0.307).
  • Possible reason: the 24-hour median of D8's residual outside the drops (metered power minus expected power) has a standard deviation of 1.20 MW before March 2025 and 0.91 MW after, about half of one unit. The test may therefore be unable to resolve whole units at this noise. We have not tested that explanation, so the failed prediction neither supports nor refutes the engine.

The drops sit in dearer half-hours, and none began after January 2026.

  • Timing: onsets fall in the 6-hour blocks 0 to 6, 6 to 12, 12 to 18, and 18 to 24 UTC 11, 3, 4, and 10 times (chi-squared p 0.067), and ends 6, 4, 6, and 12 times. No weekday stands out (onsets p 0.48).
  • Price: the mean system-price fifth across a drop is 3.45, against 3.03 in matched placebo windows (paired Wilcoxon p 0.001). The engine runs in 26% of the dearest fifth and 9% of the cheapest (experiment 194). The onsets themselves do not rise with price: by fifth, cheapest to dearest, they number 6, 8, 7, 2, and 5.
  • After March 2026: no drop starts from 2026-03-01 to 2026-06-24, against 5.4 expected at the rate of the previous 12 months (17 drops; Poisson probability of none 0.0045). The share of D8's half-hours with power 2.5 MW or more below expected falls from 0.17 in February 2026 to 0.008 in April, but the detector's flag share stays at 0.39 to 0.48.

Most of D8's load-shift alarms lie inside engine spells, but spells cover most of the time.

  • Spells: the detector's flagged runs, joined across gaps of up to 3 hours and widened by 3 hours either side, cover 0.73 of D8's half-hours from 2023-08-15. Every share of alarms inside spells has to be read against 0.73.
  • RO-NC alarms: of the 27 unexplained alarms of the refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC) from 2023-08-15, 26 lie inside a spell (expected 19.8, p 0.002), and 21 lie within 3 hours of a spell's start or end (expected 13.8, p 0.004). Five lie inside a drop (3.5 expected).
  • Experiment 195 alarms: the pair alarm, the learned score, and the re-ranker of experiment 195 have all of their 60, 36, and 36 alarms inside a spell (expected 44.0, 26.4, and 26.4).
  • Share of unexplained alarms at D8 and D9: the two Primaries supply 61 of the 148 unexplained alarms in the false-alarm analysis of the alarms of experiment 130 (0.41). The 26 alarms inside spells exceed the random-time expectation by 6.2 alarms. Counting only that excess leaves D8's and D9's share at 0.37 (0.39 if the 6.2 alarms also leave the total of 148). Counting all 26 gives 0.24 (0.29), an upper bound that mostly restates the 0.73.
  • Neighbours: among the 27 drops that overlap, 9, 6, and 3 have a neighbour step-up at onset of at least 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 times the depth (0.33, 0.22, and 0.11). Experiment 159's placebo shares are 0.344, 0.214, and 0.124. The one drop without overlap has a step-up above all three, so the comparison cannot separate the two groups.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• No audit has run: this result has not been replicated, and the brief for a D8 forecast that is told when the engine is running depends on its headline. The manager decides whether an audit of the method runs. The failed depth prediction has only the noise measurement above as an explanation.
  • No forecast is scored: the median-minus-mean and mean-forecast checks of the experiment skill therefore do not apply.
  • Circularity: the drops and the detector both read D8's residual, so some overlap is built in. The controls rule out a shared regional cause, and the placebo rules out a detector that flags everything (0.19), but neither tests the engine directly. D8's own record of the engine after 2023-08-15 is zeros or absent (experiment 194), so we found no independent record. The engine's recorded output exists only for the 44 days from 2023-07-03 to 2023-08-15, and no drop falls in them (the first drop after the 2022 one starts on 2023-10-21), so that check cannot be run. Experiment 196 also fitted D8's detector parameters and noise on 2023-09 to 2025-12, a window that contains most of the drops, whereas the three controls fit their own noise on their own history.
  • Detector reliability: experiment 196 judged the detector not supported after March 2025, and 17 of the 28 drops lie there. The period before March 2025, where the detector's known-answer test applies, gives 10 of 11 against 0.12.
  • Reproduction: arm v1 agrees with the stored probabilities of experiment 196 on every half-hour, and the 29 drops are those of experiment 159.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: A forecast for D8 that is told when the engine is running is justified, and its first test is whether the drops' half-hours are forecast better with that information than without it. NGED could confirm the engine's running hours in the drops, which would settle the circularity.

docs.title: Does the ensemble's irradiance on the cells around a metered solar farm lift the day-ahead forecast?
docs.text:
At the six metered solar farms tested, the ensemble's irradiance on the cells around a farm adds almost nothing to the day-ahead forecast. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters the output of six solar farms in its trial area, which this page labels A to F. A day-ahead cloud field can be right in shape and wrong in position by tens of kilometres, so we asked whether the weather forecast on the cells around a farm lowers the error of the farm's day-ahead power forecast. The weather forecast is the 51-member ensemble of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), stored on hexagonal cells about 15 km apart. The power forecast, called H5 (from experiment 243), is a physical solar-farm power model plus a neural network that adds a correction to each of 11 quantile levels of the forecast. We gave H5 11 extra inputs per half-hour, computed over the 7 hexagons (the farm's own hexagon and its 6 neighbours) and the 19 hexagons (two rings of neighbours) around the farm: the mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum of the ensemble-mean irradiance; the share of member- hexagon pairs with a clear-sky index above 0.8 (the ratio of irradiance to clear-sky irradiance); and the irradiance at the neighbouring hexagon that the 10 m wind comes from. We scored the forecast 12 to 36 hours ahead on daylight half-hours in 2025-09 to 2026-08, with the quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity (percentage points of the farm's capacity).

The prediction fails. The summaries lower the quantile score by 0.36% (98.75% interval 0.70% to 0.05%) against H5 on the farm's own hexagon, and the plan required 2%. The plan's stop rule (stop if the gain is under 1% at 4 or more of the 6 farms) fired, because the gain is under 1% at 5 of the 6 farms, so the arm with a convolution over the 19 hexagons (N2) was not fitted. The 0.36% is also fragile: leaving out farm B, C, or E puts zero inside the interval. Neighbouring hexagons differ from the farm's own hexagon by only about 8 to 10 W/m² (about 3% of the mean daylight irradiance of 310 W/m²). In this store and at this scale, the ensemble mean is therefore too smooth between neighbours to show where a cloud edge falls.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Arms. N0: H5 on the own cell (refitted here; its scores equal experiment 243's stored H5 to every digit). N1: N0 plus the 11 summaries. Placebo: N1 with the summary vector of another day of the same farm, split, month, hour, and own-cell clear-sky band. X0 and X1: XGBoost (Chen and Guestrin, 2016) without and with the summaries. N2 was not fitted (stop rule).
  • Rows. The 41,654 daylight half-hours (sun more than 5 degrees above the horizon) at 12 to 36 hour leads of experiment 243, six farms, equal weight per farm, 98.75% intervals for the planned contrasts and 95% elsewhere, from resampling the 12 scored months 20,000 times. Neural arms are means over five seeds.
  • Quantile score (95% interval). N1 5.455 (4.93 to 5.91); N0 5.475 (4.95 to 5.93); X1 5.479 (4.93 to 5.94); placebo 5.491 (4.97 to 5.94); X0 5.493 (4.95 to 5.95); climatology 8.64; manual heuristic 8.69.
  • Contrasts, quantile score (98.75%). C1 N1 minus N0 -0.36% (-0.70 to -0.05). C2 N1 minus placebo -0.65% (-0.89 to -0.40). C3 N1 minus X1 -0.43% (-1.46 to +0.96). C4 N2 minus N0 not run. Outside the plan (95%): X1 minus X0 -0.27% (-0.45 to -0.09); N0 minus X0 -0.34% (-1.30 to +0.81).
  • Per farm, N1 minus N0. A +0.27%, B -0.23%, C -0.77%, D -0.07%, E -1.35%, F +0.14%. Leaving one farm out of C1 gives -0.48% (A), -0.38% (B), -0.29% (C), -0.42% (D), -0.12% (E), -0.45% (F); the interval includes zero when B, C, or E is left out.
  • Clear and cloudy half-hours (own-cell clear-sky index at least 0.5 is clear, under 0.5 is cloudy), N1 minus N0: clear -0.39% (-0.78 to -0.02); cloudy -0.28% (-0.58 to +0.21).
  • Error of the median and of the mean forecast (points of capacity). MAE of the median: N0 9.85, N1 9.80 (-0.44%, -0.95 to +0.22). MAE of the mean forecast: N0 9.96, N1 9.94 (-0.21%, -0.40 to +0.07).
Tail (N1 minus N0) Pinball change (98.75%) Coverage N0 Coverage N1 Nominal 0.01 quantile -1.6% (-3.1 to -0.5) 3.3% 3.2% 1% 0.05 quantile -0.7% (-1.6 to +0.1) 6.0% 6.1% 5% 0.95 quantile 0.0% (-0.9 to +1.1) 94.5% 94.5% 95% 0.99 quantile -0.4% (-1.7 to +1.0) 98.5% 98.5% 99%
  • Tail calibration. The neighbourhood lowers the pinball loss at the 0.01 quantile by 1.6%, the one tail result whose interval excludes zero, and leaves the 0.99 quantile unchanged (-0.4%, interval spans zero). Both arms over-cover the 0.01 quantile (3.2% to 3.3% of observations fall below it, against 1% nominal) and under-cover the 0.99 quantile (98.5% against 99%), so the summaries do not fix the tail calibration.
  • Fraction of output fitted by the median forecast (1 minus the sum of squared errors over the sum of squared output, median over farms): 0.912 for N0 and 0.911 for N1 on all scored half-hours, and 0.944 and 0.944 on sunny half-hours (clear-sky index at least 0.8). These are out-of-sample forecasts, so they are not comparable with experiment 218's in-sample 0.91 (ensemble mean) and 0.973 (observed weather), which use a different set of half-hours.
  • Curtailment value. Not scored: the median forecast moves by only 0.44% (interval spans zero), and experiment 224 found that its pilot set of grid nodes cannot rank forecasts.

docs.title: Neighbourhood data check
docs.text:
• Store. The ensemble store holds H3 resolution-5 hexagons (about 15 km between centres) for the whole of Great Britain, not a 0.25 degree lattice, so the brief's "3 by 3" block is ring 1 (7 hexagons) and its "5 by 5" block is rings 1 and 2 (19 hexagons). Every farm has 6 of 6 ring-1 hexagons and 18 or 19 of 19 hexagons (a missing hexagon is open sea), so no farm was dropped.
  • Variables. Downward shortwave radiation, 2 m temperature, and 10 m wind exist for all 51 members. Cloud cover (total or low) is not in the store, so the share of member-hexagon pairs with clear-sky index above 0.8 stands in for it, with the farm's clear-sky irradiance applied to every hexagon.
  • Orientation. The farm's own hexagon reproduces experiment 224's ensemble-mean irradiance to within 0.5 W/m² on every row, and the mean absolute difference from the own hexagon grows from 8.0 to 10.4 W/m² in ring 1 to 14.1 to 17.0 W/m² in ring 2 at every farm, which is the pattern expected if the hexagons sit where H3 places them. The upwind hexagon is the ring-1 hexagon whose direction is closest to the direction the ensemble-mean 10 m wind comes from.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (points of capacity). N0 +0.54, N1 +0.52, placebo +0.55, X0 -0.70, X1 -0.73. The neighbourhood does not shift either forecast.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile contrast. C1's MAE of the mean forecast is -0.21% (interval includes zero) against -0.36% in the quantile score, so both point the same way (trigger 3 does not fire).
  • Triggers fired. The ml-experiment skill lists seven audit triggers. Trigger 4 (leaving one farm out changes the verdict of a planned contrast) fires: C1's interval includes zero without B, C, or E. Trigger 5 fires weakly: the placebo scores 0.29% worse than N0 (95% interval +0.07% to +0.55%), a shift larger than the half-width of the placebo's interval (0.24 percentage points). The 11 extra inputs, each carrying another day's summary, are enough to worsen the score by that much, which also means N1's gain against the placebo (C2, -0.65%) overstates the value of the real summaries, and C1 is the cleaner reading. No Opus audit was run, because the result is a null that no later design depends on, and the ML manager's brief reserves Opus for a result that changes the next step. Triggers 1, 2, 3, 6, and 7 do not fire.
  • Caveat: one fit. One fit on the months before 2025-09 (the screening schedule of experiment 243, own history only), 12 scored months, and one set of five seeds, so the intervals are wide.
  • Caveat: placebo donors. The placebo's donor days come from the same split (tuning or scored) as the row, so a scored row's placebo uses another scored day's forecast weather, which exists at forecast time. No power values leak.
  • Caveat: coarse neighbours. The hexagons are about 15 km apart, so a cloud-position error smaller than that would not show in them, and the ensemble's native grid resolution is not recoverable from the store.
  • Caveat: not run. N2 (convolution), a zero-history setting, and weekly refits were not run.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a weather input of a different kind, such as satellite-derived cloud for the first hours of the day-ahead window, lowers the quantile score where more views of the ECMWF ensemble do not.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
• Neighbourhood and variables. See "Neighbourhood data check" above. A farm needs 5 of 6 ring-1 hexagons and 15 of 19 hexagons in the store, or it is dropped from every arm.
  • Weather and forecast time. ECMWF ensemble, 00 UTC run, 51 members, available at forecast time. Lagged power is the farm's own power one day earlier (two when the lead exceeds 24 hours).
  • Arms. N0: H5 on the own cell, as in experiment 243. N1: N0 plus 11 summaries per half-hour (mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum of the member-mean irradiance over the ring-1 and rings-1-2 blocks; the share of member-cell pairs with clear-sky index above 0.8 in each block; the member-mean irradiance at the ring-1 cell nearest the direction the 10 m wind blows from). N2: N0 plus a small convolution over the 19 cells' member mean and member spread (run only if the stop rule does not fire). X0 and X1: XGBoost without and with the summaries. Placebo: N1 with the summary vector taken from another day of the same farm, month, hour, and own-cell clear-sky band.
  • Schedule. One fit per arm and seed on the months before 2025-09, five seeds per neural arm, the last two tuning months select the epoch (the screening schedule of experiment 243; own history only).
  • Advice followed. Let the neural network output all 11 offsets (H5), leave day of year out, give every arm the lagged power and the spread (experiment 243).

docs.title: Does a 20 degree panel tilt and a higher, softer clip improve the spread-binned solar-farm power model?
docs.text:
Changing the plant's panel tilt from 35 to 20 degrees fixes most of its winter over-prediction on clear half-hours, but the forecast band as a whole does not improve, and a higher or softer power cap does nothing, so the plant's shape is not what limits the upper tail of the band. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters six solar farms, labelled A to F here. The "plant" is the physical power model of experiment 224, and "P2" is the version from experiment 270 that stores residual quantiles for each cell of 6 bins of the plant's forecast crossed with 3 bins of the spread of its 51 ensemble members. Experiment 282 found that the farms fit best at a tilt of 15 to 20 degrees, so we recomputed the 51 members' responses at 20 degrees, tried a higher cap and a soft cap, and scored the result on experiment 287's rows. A "hard cap" stops the plant's forecast abruptly at a fixed level, and a "soft cap" approaches that level smoothly. The premise tested is that the best-guess demand stack under-predicts clear-sky solar output by 5 to 8% from April to July (experiment 282). "Own history" means the forecast uses the farm's own earlier months, "zero history" means it uses only the other five farms, and "arm c" is defined under Arms.

The pre-registered pair of tests failed. The quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 levels, in points of capacity; lower is better) moved by under 1% as predicted. But with tilt 20 and a soft cap (arm c), the 0.99 pinball loss fell by 1.4% (98.75% interval from resampling the 12 scored months, -5.2% to +2.1%) against the 3% bar, and the April to July under-prediction did not shrink: P2 had none to shrink, so the bar of a 3-point shrink was unreachable (P2's median absolute bias was 1.5% before any change). Arm c's median absolute bias on clear half-hours in those months is 2.7%, against 1.5% for P2. The stop rule did not apply, because the 0.99 gain of 1.4% exceeds 1%, so the result falls in the rule's middle zone; the interval includes zero, and arm c is not carried to the stack.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
The arms are P2 with a different plant. Only the tilt and the cap differ between arms. Every arm fits its scale by the same unclipped least-squares rule as P2, every cap level comes from tuning rows (the months before 2025-09) only, and each arm's member responses are recomputed with its own tilt. The tilt of 20 degrees comes from experiment 282's fits, which used the scored year, so arms a, c, and f are slightly optimistic.

  • P2: tilt 35, hard cap at the tuning 0.995 quantile of output. The rebuilt control matches experiment 287's stored P2 exactly (own history 5.5483, zero history 5.7112).
  • (a) tilt 20. (b) soft cap (p-norm minimum, exponent 6) at the tuning 0.999 quantile. (c) both. (d) experiment 282's pooled leave-one-farm-out shape, own history only. (e) and (f) are P2 and arm (a) with a hard cap at the tuning 0.999 quantile, added after the plan review and before any score was read, to separate a higher cap from a soft one.
  • Row set and schedule. Experiment 287's scored-year daylight rows at 12 to 36 hour leads, one fit on the months before 2025-09 with no refits. Weather is the ECMWF ensemble 00 UTC run, available at forecast time; no past weather is used.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Quantile score (own history, points of capacity; interval over 12 months). P2 5.55 (4.94 to 6.09), (a) 5.54, (b) 5.56, (c) 5.54 (4.81 to 6.16), (d) 6.15, (e) 5.55, (f) 5.54; experiment 287's GAM 5.47, MDN 5.39, blend 5.36. Zero history: P2 5.71, (a) 5.69, (b) 5.72, (c) 5.69, (e) 5.71, (f) 5.69. The floors are 8.69 (manual_heuristic) and 8.64 (climatology).
  • Score contrasts against P2 (own history, 98.75% interval). (a) -0.18% (-3.8 to +1.5); (b) +0.19% (-0.08 to +0.41); (c) -0.11% (-3.8 to +1.6); (d) +10.9% (7.7 to 14.2); (e) -0.006% (-0.06 to +0.03); (f) -0.17% (-3.8 to +1.5). Zero history: (a) -0.35% (-3.7 to +1.1), (b) +0.11%, (c) -0.33%.
  • 0.99 pinball loss against P2 (own history). (a) -0.6% (-4.4 to +2.6); (b) -0.8% (-2.8 to +0.3); (c) -1.4% (-5.2 to +2.1); (d) +13.6% (3.5 to 23.9); (e) -0.7% (-2.6 to +0.3). Experiment 287's blend is 7.9% below P2 (-11.2 to -3.4) and its GAM 5.2% below, so the plant's shape closes at most about a fifth of the gap.
  • Where tilt 20 helps and hurts (arm c against P2, own history). December to February score -9.0% (-22.3 to +0.5); March to May +0.8% (-0.6 to +2.0); June to August +1.7% (0.6 to 3.1); September to November +0.6% (-1.1 to +1.2); March to June +0.8% (-0.2 to +1.7). Tail pinball loss: 0.01 quantile -4.3% (-9.7 to -1.9), 0.05 quantile -2.2% (-6.1 to -0.1), 0.95 quantile +0.9% (-2.9 to +3.7).
  • Soft against hard cap at the same level. (b) minus (e): score +0.20% (-0.02 to +0.41), 0.99 pinball loss -0.06% (-0.25 to +0.04). (c) minus (f): score +0.06% (-0.08 to +0.18), 0.99 pinball loss -0.05% (-0.14 to +0.03). The form of the cap does not matter.
  • Tail coverage (own history, nominal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99). P2 0.034, 0.063, 0.951, 0.986; arm c 0.034, 0.063, 0.945, 0.987; experiment 287's blend 0.034, 0.068, 0.959, 0.992. The 0.01 quantile covers 3.4% of rows, 3.4 times its nominal 1%, for every arm.
  • Bias of the mean forecast on clear half-hours (own history, actual over forecast minus 1). April to July, P2 per farm A to F: -0.2%, +2.7%, +0.3%, +7.0%, +0.3%, +3.6% (951 to 1,546 rows each); arm c: -3.2%, -0.3%, -2.6%, +2.8%, -4.2%, +0.7%. The rows are the scored set of the score tables. Median absolute bias 1.54% for P2 and 2.69% for arm c, a shrink of -1.14 points (98.75% interval -1.14 to +4.32 from resampling 4 months, too coarse to rank). Pooled over farms, P2's bias is -19% in November, -33% in December, and -26% in January against 0%, -8%, and -7% for arm c (figure 4).
  • Curtailment cost. Not scored: these six farms are single series, and the curtailment-cost metric needs a substation node plus its generators.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per farm (own history, points of capacity). P2 0.16 to 0.46, (a) 0.01 to 0.51, (b) 0.15 to 0.49, (c) 0.03 to 0.53; none of P2, (a), (b), (c), (e), and (f) has a median more than 0.6 points from its mean forecast (arm (d) reaches -1.2).
  • Mean-forecast error beside the score contrast. Arm c: mean-forecast absolute error -0.6% (-3.9 to +1.5) against a score change of -0.1%, the same direction. Arm (b): +0.22% (0.07 to 0.36) against +0.19%.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired: the result contradicts the premise that P2 under-predicts in April to July. The explanation tested is that P2 refits its scale on each farm's own tuning months, while the stack's capacity is pinned; the April to July bias results above support this explanation. Trigger 4 fired for the score contrast only: dropping one farm in turn moves arm c's score change between -0.57% and +0.46%, around zero. The 0.99 change stays between -0.3% and -3.1%, and the bias criterion fails whichever farm is dropped, so the verdict does not depend on which farm is dropped. The other triggers did not fire. No Opus audit was run, because no contrast that decides the verdict changes sign.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet plan review changed the plan (same scale rule for every arm, arms e and f, the stop-rule middle zone, the bias definition). A Sonnet code review found no leakage and led to a bias row-set fix, two added contrasts, and two caveats. A Sonnet write-up review led to the clarifications in this page. No Opus review was run.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Scale not refitted through the soft cap. Arms b and c keep the unclipped least-squares scale, so the soft cap lowers their forecast near the cap by up to 11%; arms e and f, which share the cap level with a hard cap, show the cap form changes the score by under 0.2%.
  • Arm d mixes weather products. The pooled table is fitted to CAMS irradiance (estimated past weather) and applied to ensemble irradiance, which may explain part of its 10.9% loss; it was not refitted on ensemble rows.
  • One fit per arm, no refits. A weekly refit could change the absolute scores and possibly the contrasts, which this experiment did not test.
  • The 20-degree tilt was chosen on the scored year (experiment 282), so the gains of arms a, c, and f are optimistic, and they are still small.
  • Next. Tilt 20 lowers winter error and raises summer error, which suggests that a tilt between 20 and 35 degrees, or a seasonal term (a different diffuse-sky split in winter), would do better than either 20 or 35 degrees. The upper tail's remaining gap to experiment 287's blend comes from the heads' inputs, not the plant.

docs.title: Does a regime-aware model beat a single model at a Primary with a persistent generator regime?
docs.text:
Telling the forecast when D8's gas engine runs would help a lot, but only when the state is read at the half-hour being forecast, and that state is built from the reading being forecast. D8 is one of the 16 Primary substations of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) in the trial. Its meter stopped including the output of a gas engine of up to three units of about 2 MW each on 2023-08-15, so we take D8's multi-day drops in power (2 to 19 days, about 2.7 MW) to be the engine running (experiment 194, experiment 291). We asked whether a forecast with an extra term for the half-hours when the engine runs beats a forecast without it. Both forecasts are the same generalised additive model with a Kalman filter on recent errors, trained on all of D8's history. The engine's running state is estimated by a detector, not observed. We tested five ways of giving the term its state. The one usable at forecast time, the state of the last day whose readings had arrived, made the quantile score 10.3% worse than the forecast without the term. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, our stand-in for the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), and smaller is better.

The term's gain on D8 is partly circular, because the engine states and the drops come from the same residual. The states are the probabilities of the detector of experiment 196, as run in experiment 291 (PR 1594, "Experiment 291: are D8's multi-day drops generator-engine spells?"). Experiment 291 found the drops in the residual that this detector reads, so the states cannot confirm that the drops are an engine. The detector's filtered probability uses readings only up to each half-hour, but its inputs are not causal: the expected-power series it reads is centred on a 30-day window, so a state can carry up to 15 days of later readings. That flatters every arm that uses a state, which makes arm 3's loss conservative and leaves the post hoc gain at risk.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Rows. The 292 daily runs of experiment 191, scored from 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, outside the hand-filtered events, seed 0: 97,012 rows at D8, 84,137 at D5, 96,370 at D10, 97,046 at D11. Every arm is refitted monthly, as in experiment 191, so no contrast depends on weekly refits.
  • Arm 1, the single-model arm. Experiment 191's generalised additive model with a Kalman filter (GAM-K), no 24-month window, D8's whole history, its own tuning months for the spread.
  • Arm 2. Experiment 191's reference rows (D8 from 2025-04-01, donor spread). Arm 2 reproduces experiment 191's stored forecasts exactly (largest difference 0.0). Arm 2 differs from arm 1 in both the history and the source of the spread.
  • Arm 3, deciding. Arm 1 plus a break indicator (1 from 2023-08-15) and the filtered probability of one or more running units, with a non-negative coefficient, read from the same half-hour of the last settled day at forecast time.
  • Other arms. Break indicator only. Engine state at the target half-hour from the smoothed posterior, which uses the reading (leaky ceiling). Post hoc: expected number of units (arm 3-units), and arm 3 trained on the filtered probability lagged 1 to 7 days (matched). Arm 3-window is arm 3's engine term on arm 2's rows.
  • Arm 4. Experiment 264's stored arm_emp (the median plus the past 365 days' residual quantiles) and arm2b.
  • Lab shortcuts. The detector's parameters were fitted on 2023-09 to 2026-01 and its expected power comes from a model fitted with hindsight. The filtered probability uses only readings up to the half-hour, and the last-day state ignores the 3.5-hour delivery delay of readings, so about 15% of target half-hours read a state built from readings not yet delivered.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. Only the arm that sees the state at the target half-hour (24% better) gains more than the post hoc arm trained on the lagged state (3% better). The last-day state, arm 3, is 10% worse.

Figure 2. The offset per half-hour with the engine on is 3.5 to 3.6 MW at every refit; per running unit it is 1.4 to 1.5 MW, against the recorded unit of 1.97 MW. Trained on a day-old state, the offset is 0.9 to 1.0 MW.

Figure 3. The single model reads 1.1 MW below its forecast while the engine runs and 0.8 MW above it otherwise. Only the target-state arm removes both gaps.

Figure 4. In December 2025 the forecast that sees the engine state at the target follows the readings down during the shaded spells; the others barely move.

Figure 5. At the three Primaries without an engine, the arms move the quantile score by -0.9% to +2.0%.

The slope of arm 1's error on the state of the last settled day, fitted with an intercept, is 0.15 MW per unit of probability (95% interval -0.06 to 0.32), against 3.6 MW fitted, so it cannot be told from zero. On the state at the target it is 2.20 MW (1.72 to 2.65), close to one engine unit but circular.
