Audit trigger 4 (leaving one Primary out changes a verdict) fired: leaving out D16 or D10 turns the verdict of C1 from refuted into inconclusive (+0.036, -0.006 to +0.091; +0.041, -0.016 to +0.111), although the sign holds. Audit trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction) is borderline: C1 misses its predicted bound by 0.015 points. One explanation was tested: P sits 5 to 13% above B, and arm R, which has no divisor, is nearer to the pin but has a wide interval. The explanation is not confirmed.
  • Audit (Sonnet, as the manager directed). An independent re-derivation from the stored forecasts, with its own scoring and bootstrap code, reproduced every figure above to three decimals (interval ends differ in the third decimal because of resampling). Leaving out both D16 and D10 gives -0.001 (-0.044 to +0.059). In the replicate year, leaving out D16 gives +0.036 (-0.032 to +0.067). D16 is worse in 10 of 12 months and D10 in 11 of 12, so the harm is not from a few months, although the 10 worst days carry 41% of D16's total and 32% of D10's. The audit found no row-alignment or quantile-score flaw. The verdict is therefore not supported: no gain, and probably slightly worse, with the harm carried by D16 and D10.

docs.title: Caveats and simplifications
docs.text:
• The plant-response table of arm B is not as-of. Arm B reads experiment 349's table, which was fitted once to the six farms' history to 2026-06-30. Arm P uses no plant-response table: only the capacity fit and its injection recoveries are used, both with rows before each origin.
  • The first stage only. The neural-network head, the solar summary, the blend, and the 168 to 240 hour range were not rerun.
  • Divisor choice. P divides by the injection recovery, which makes its capacity larger than the physical-shape units imply; R is the unit-consistent version, with a wide interval.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the capacity's effect on cold winter nights and the darkest daylight third, where P scored better than the pin, in the full stack.
  • Read the capacity out in the empirical shape and apply it in the empirical shape, in the first stage and in the ensemble's solar response, if the mismatch is still suspected.

docs.title: How much does the score of Primary demand research default 3 on sunny half-hours depend on the solar capacity it is given, with and without the Kalman filter?
Take-home message
docs.text:
The sunny-half-hour score of the demand forecast moved by only 0.010 points (interval -0.104 to +0.088) when the assumed solar capacity was 20% too low, but rose by 0.124 points when it was 20% too high, and the Kalman filter halves that rise. The forecast of demand at six Primary substations (anonymised D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) subtracts the output of unmetered rooftop solar from each substation's demand, and the size of that solar (its capacity) is fixed to the weekly capacity estimates of experiment 45, which this page calls the pin. Experiment 349 and experiment 350 found no reliable gain from a different capacity. We asked how much the score depends on the capacity at all.

We refitted the first stage of Primary demand research default 3 (a convex demand model, with a Kalman filter that corrects the forecast using the latest readings; the later stages add a neural-network head, a summary of the solar term, and a blend with a manual heuristic) five times, with the pinned capacity multiplied by 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, and 1.4, and forecast each with and without the filter. The arm at scale 1.0 with the filter (arm A of experiment 349) reproduces experiment 349's stored default exactly. On the sunniest third of each substation's daylight half-hours, with the filter, the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of the substation's effective capacity, smaller is better) is 4.361 at 0.8, 4.371 at 1.0, and 4.495 at 1.2. Verdict: partly supported (one of the two predictions held). We predicted that, with the filter, the sunny score would differ by under 0.1 points between any two scales from 0.8 to 1.2 (largest minus smallest). That failed: the difference was 0.134 (95% interval 0.054 to 0.321). We also predicted a difference of over 0.3 without the filter. That held: 0.367 (0.129 to 0.614). The curve is flat from 0.8 to 1.0 times the pin and rises above 1.0. The later stages of the stack (neural-network head, solar summary, blend) and the 168 to 240 hour range were not refitted.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 2: with the filter, the sunny score is flat from 0.8 to 1.0 and rises above 1.0.

Figure 3: D5 and D9 prefer a lower capacity and the other four Primaries prefer the pin.

Figure 4: on all half-hours the filter helps and the pin is the best of the five scales.

Figure 1a: experiment 349's loss came from D16 and D10 at every lead band.

Figure 1b: the loss concentrates in January to March at D5 and D16.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and schedule. Scale s in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4} times experiment 45's pinned weekly capacity path, in the first stage of experiment 349's code (the code imports that folder without changing it), with monthly refits on a 24-month window as in that experiment, each arm forecast with the filter and without it (fitted mean plus a spread table fitted on the same arm's tuning months). Every arm uses the same refit dates and training window, so the schedule does not differ between arms.
  • Row set. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, six Primaries, rows outside the hand-filtered events, 0.5 to 168 hours (24 to 168 hours in logs/score.log).
  • Sunny score, pooled, 0.5 to 168 hours (95% month-resampled intervals in logs/score.log).
Scale With filter Without filter 0.6 4.465 4.179 0.8 4.361 4.144 1.0 4.371 4.253 1.2 4.495 4.511 1.4 4.728 4.881
  • Planned contrasts, sunny, 0.5 to 168 hours. C1 (filter, 0.8 minus 1.0): -0.010 (-0.104 to +0.088). C2 (filter, 1.2 minus 1.0): +0.124 (+0.030 to +0.219). C3 (no filter, 0.8 minus 1.0): -0.110 (-0.228 to -0.003). C4 (no filter, 1.2 minus 1.0): +0.258 (+0.122 to +0.388). C5 (no filter minus filter at 1.0): -0.118 (-0.451 to +0.191). At 24 to 168 hours: C1 -0.024, C2 +0.130 (+0.032 to +0.232), C3 -0.103, C4 +0.242 (+0.111 to +0.373), C5 -0.186.
  • Beyond the planned range. With the filter, 0.6 minus 1.0 is +0.094 (-0.091 to +0.295) and 1.4 minus 1.0 is +0.358 (+0.160 to +0.554). The predicted +0.10 to +0.25 at 0.6 was just missed on the low side, with an interval that includes it.
  • By Primary (with the filter, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2). D5 6.410, 6.646, 7.038; D9 3.862, 3.979, 4.178; D10 4.934, 4.818, 4.865; D11 3.338, 3.281, 3.329; D14 3.548, 3.519, 3.548; D16 4.236, 4.161, 4.208. D5 and D9 improve at 0.8, as predicted for D5; the other four are best at the pin. D16 at 0.8 is 0.075 worse, in line with experiment 349's estimate sitting 28% below the pin there and scoring 0.218 worse.
  • Leave one Primary out (sunny, with the filter, C2). Without D5: +0.074 (-0.019 to +0.162). Without any other Primary: +0.108 to +0.143, all intervals above zero. The no-filter range falls from 0.367 to 0.179 without D5 and stays 0.342 to 0.441 without any other Primary.
  • Experiment 349's contrast (its arm B, which used a different capacity, minus its arm A, the pin), read from stored forecasts. Pooled +0.047, as in experiment 349. By lead band: +0.067 (0 to 24 h), +0.051 (24 to 72 h), +0.040 (72 to 168 h). By Primary: D16 +0.356, +0.310, +0.138 across the three bands, D10 +0.12 to +0.16 everywhere, D11 about +0.04, and D5, D9, and D14 negative (-0.03 to -0.07) at short leads. By month the loss concentrates in January to March (+0.15 to +0.29) and the gain in May (-0.145). Figures 1a and 1b show the cells.
  • No-harm groups, 0.5 to 168 hours, with the filter. All half-hours: 2.858, 2.793, 2.773, 2.797, and 2.868 at scales 0.6 to 1.4, so the pin is the best scale of the five; C1 +0.020 (+0.004 to +0.036), C2 +0.025 (+0.003 to +0.049). Removing the filter at the pin worsens the score by +0.330 (+0.181 to +0.484) on all half-hours and +0.509 (-0.159 to +1.030) on winter nights.
  • Tails, all rows, at scale 1.0 (filter, then no filter). Coverage below q01 2.20% and 1.10%; below q05 6.68% and 3.81%; below q95 94.74% and 85.90%; below q99 98.35% and 94.04%. Pinball loss at q95 0.720 and 0.902, at q99 0.220 and 0.316. Across scales with the filter no tail moves by more than 0.03 points. Without the filter the upper tail is under-covered, so the no-filter arm's better sunny score does not carry to the tails.
  • Reference rows. The first stage alone is not the research default, so no manual-heuristic or climatology row is given; the default's own scores are in the research default log. The experiment changes no production behaviour, so no curtailment-cost row is given.
  • Model family and range. One model family, no blend, first stage only, 0.5 to 168 hours, which covers 7 of the 10 forecast days that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), the distribution network operator, needs.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate. Scale 1.0 with the filter equals experiment 349's stored arm A in every period at all six Primaries (largest gap 0.0 in q01, q05, q25, q50, q75, q95, q99, mean, and actual; logs/gate.log).
  • Median minus mean forecast, per Primary and arm: 0.000 for all ten arms.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast (sunny, 0.5 to 168 hours): C1 +0.008, C2 +0.205, C3 -0.139, C4 +0.406, C5 -0.298, the same signs as the quantile score except C1, where both values are within 0.01 of zero.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fired: the with-filter range (0.134) missed the prediction (under 0.1). The explanation, tested by the leave-one-out run and the audit, is that D5's export limit gives D5 a steep response; without D5 the with-filter range is 0.074. Trigger 4 (leaving one site out flips a contrast) fired: leaving D5 out moves C2's interval from above zero to across zero, and the no-filter range from 0.367 to 0.179, which changes which planned conditions hold. The audit confirmed this (next section). Trigger 5 (a nested arm beating the arm that contains it) did not fire as a failure: the no-filter arm scores 0.118 better on sunny half-hours at the pin, but the interval includes zero, and the filter wins on all half-hours.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet auditor (the brief limited the session to Sonnet; the audit rule names Opus) re-derived the headline numbers from the stored forecasts with its own code. Each finding is triaged here.

  • Pooled sunny scores reproduce to three decimals (accepted).
  • Pin scaling, fit dates, spread fitting, and leakage checks passed (accepted). The scale multiplies the weekly path and the held value, the fits and the prediction use the same scaled capacity, and no fit sees data past its cut.
  • The no-filter arm's better sunny score is a real mechanism, with caveats (accepted). On sunny rows the filter adds about 2.1 points to the forecast at every lead. The filter helps up to 24 hours (sunny score 3.53 against 3.82 without it) and hurts at 72 to 168 hours (4.75 against 4.47). C5's interval includes zero (-0.118, -0.451 to +0.191), so the sentence "no filter is better on sunny half-hours" is not supported.
  • The verdict depends on D5 (accepted). With D5 the rule gives partly supported. Without D5, C1 (+0.031, -0.055 to +0.130) and C2 (+0.074, -0.019 to +0.162) both reach the upper edge of the planned band, and the no-filter range falls to 0.179, which would read as inconclusive. C1's lower edge with D5 (-0.104) is also just outside the band. The verdict word stays as pre-registered, and the headline carries the leave-out-D5 numbers.
  • D5's export limit explains most of its steepness (accepted, not measured directly). The fit has no clip, and D5's error at the top decile of the solar shape grows almost linearly with scale (+9.2, +13.7, and +18.3 points at 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2), which a saturated output produces. The clip level itself was not tested.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• First stage only. The neural-network head, solar summary, and blend were not refitted, so a response that the later stages create or remove is not measured.
  • Scale multiplies the pin at every week. It does not change the unit shape or the pin's growth path, so it tests the level and not the shape of the solar term.
  • 12 months to resample. Intervals resample the 12 calendar months of one year, so they are wide and the ranking of arms inside 0.1 points is not resolved.
  • Heterogeneity. The pooled curve mixes D5 and D9, which prefer a lower capacity, with four Primaries that prefer the pin.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Keep the pin for the demand stack and do not spend effort on a more exact capacity inside 0.8 to 1.0 times the pin; the harm is above the pin.
  • If a capacity estimate is used, test capping it at the pin, because the harm sits above the pin.
  • Test whether a per-Primary export clip at D5 and D9 removes their preference for a lower capacity.

docs.title: How well does Primary demand research default 3's stack forecast D8 when the MVA meter's fold is modelled?
docs.text:
This experiment found no evidence that the fold in D8's meter explains D8's poor forecast score. Fitting D8's demand model through the fold changes the quantile score by -0.23 points (95% bootstrap interval -0.83 to +0.21), and the interval includes zero. The verdict is not supported. D8's score stays about 3.5 points worse than BG2 whichever way the fold is treated. The larger problem is the width of the forecast's uncertainty bands, which the stack calculates from the forecast errors of six other Primaries. A band fitted on D8's own earlier months (an arm added after the main comparison was scored, so it is exploratory) lowers the score by 2.22 points, to 1.32 points above BG2. The evidence therefore favours trying that band change before any further work on the meter model.

D8 (Marsh Lane) is a primary substation (Primary) whose meter reports apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA). Apparent power has no sign, so a flow back into the electricity network, the fold, appears as a positive reading. BG2 is the production-style forecast. On the quantile score, one point is 1% of D8's effective capacity (10.38 MW), and lower is better. The stack is the current research-default model for Primary demand (version 3): a convex demand model with a Kalman filter, plus a night offset and a correction called recipe R.

We rescored stored forecasts and did not refit anything. We took the stored ensemble forecasts of experiment 152: one fit that models the fold (the meter operator of experiment 110) and one that treats the folded readings as ordinary signed demand. We added the night offset and recipe R of experiment 252 to each, and scored them against the card's forecast (experiment 252's arm A1), BG2, the manual heuristic, and climatology. The stack was not refitted through the meter, because studies.dp_meter fits only the basic design, not the stack's T-all design and 60% solar clip. The arms are A (the card's forecast), B (fold-modelling fit plus night offset and recipe R), and C (signed-demand fit plus the same two corrections).

Figure 1: the fold effect is a few tenths of a point, and its sign changes with the slice of rows.

Figure 2: the borrowed band keeps every arm 2 to 4 points above BG2; D8's own band closes most of the gap.

Figure 3: every stack arm scores about 3 points above BG2 in absolute terms.

Figure 4: D8's readings jump between levels that the day-ahead forecast smooths over.

Figure 5: the fitted negative flow sits mostly in two months, and about half of it is at night.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. A is experiment 252's arm A1 (stage-2 arm d) as stored. B is experiment 152's arm A (meter fit, symmetric quantiles) plus the night offset and recipe R. B-fold is experiment 152's arm F (quantiles folded at zero) with the same shift added to its quantiles; it keeps arm F's own band and has no refitted band, so B-fold minus B mixes the fold with a change of band and only B-fold minus C is quoted. C is experiment 152's arm N plus the same stage 2. The fits are monthly on 3 to 14 months of data from 2025-04-01. This excludes the change in what D8's series measures in April 2025. The width of the uncertainty band comes from the forecast errors of six other Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22) on a tuning period.
  • Rows. 96,986 half-hourly rows, one per forecast run and valid time (97,012 before the join to BG2, climatology, and the manual heuristic drops 26), in the scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours. The stored ensemble forecasts stop at 168 hours, so the 168 to 240 hour blend of Primary demand research default 3 is not applied.
  • The control gate passed. The script reproduces experiment 252's stored D8 scores: A1 11.433 and BG2 7.593. Experiment 152's F minus N at D8 is -0.190 here (-0.189 on its page).
  • C1, B minus C (the verdict). All rows -0.234 (-0.827 to +0.205); sunny daylight -0.229 (-0.661 to +0.037). With folded quantiles (B-fold minus C) all rows -0.350 (-0.941 to +0.098) and sunny daylight -0.287 (-0.676 to -0.032). In winter nights B is worse than C by +0.337 (+0.084 to +0.740). The interval over all rows includes zero, so the fold does not meet the -0.10 threshold. Post hoc: in the first half of the scored year B minus C is -0.487 (-1.676 to +0.439) and in the second half +0.018 (-0.015 to +0.054).
  • Absolute scores, all rows. B 11.132, B-fold 11.016, C 11.366, A 11.433, experiment 152's arms without stage 2: fold-aware 10.739, signed-demand 10.951. BG2 7.593, manual heuristic 8.469, climatology 9.757. On sunny daylight rows B 10.076, C 10.306, A 10.471, BG2 8.223, manual heuristic 10.735, climatology 15.806.
  • C2, B minus A (descriptive). All rows -0.301 (-0.916 to +0.144); sunny daylight -0.395 (-0.893 to -0.087). B has no T-all design or solar clip, so the contrast mixes the fold with those pieces.
  • C3, against BG2 (descriptive). B minus BG2 is +3.539 (+2.493 to +4.615) over all rows and +1.853 (+1.182 to +2.703) on sunny daylight rows. A minus BG2 is +3.840 (+2.458 to +5.378) and C minus BG2 is +3.773 (+2.416 to +5.271).
  • A band from D8's own history closes most of the gap (post hoc, reference arm). Arm B with each month's uncertainty band fitted on D8's own earlier months (valid times before the month; July 2025 keeps the band from other Primaries) scores 8.914 over all rows and 8.462 on sunny daylight rows. B with own band minus B is -2.218 (-2.901 to -1.558); minus BG2 it is +1.321 (+0.570 to +2.168) over all rows, +0.239 (-0.421 to +0.773) on sunny daylight rows, and +0.804 (+0.581 to +1.043) in the second half of the year alone. The own-history arm's tail shares are 4.4%, 9.1%, 92.8%, and 96.6% at q01, q05, q95, and q99, against 21.4%, 31.0%, 72.0%, and 83.0% for B. The mean forecast is unchanged, so only the band moved. A band fitted on the scored rows themselves, which uses information a live forecast would not have and so is a best case, scores 8.443.
  • High-level and low-level readings. Rows are split by whether D8's reading, as a 24-hour centred median, is at or above 4.5 MW (37,477 rows) or below it (59,509 rows). B minus C is -0.005 (-0.567 to +0.375) at the high level and -0.379 (-1.025 to +0.098) at the low level. The gap to BG2 is +3.95 at the high level and +3.28 at the low level, with overlapping intervals. Climatology (7.70) and the manual heuristic (7.85) score about as well as BG2 at the high level, so the stack arms with the borrowed band lose there (Figure 4).
  • Reverse flow. The fitted signed flow is below zero on 1.8% of scored rows (2.9% of sunny daylight rows; 410 of 17,441 distinct valid times), down to -57% of effective capacity. 362 of those distinct valid times are in August and September 2025, and 188 are between 00:00 and 05:30 UTC, mostly before sunrise. About 198 are between 10:00 and 17:30 UTC, where solar export is possible. The readings are below 5% of effective capacity on 1.7% of rows. The night-time negative flow therefore marks drops in the readings. The daytime half could be export or drops, and the sign is not observable in an MVA meter.
  • The night offset and recipe R scored worse than the fits they correct. They raise the score (higher is worse) by 0.39 (fold-aware: 10.739 to 11.132) and 0.42 (signed-demand: 10.951 to 11.366) over all rows, and by about 0.4 in the second half of the year alone (9.758 to 10.174). The offset alone is 11.067 and recipe R alone is 10.962 for the fold-aware arm. No interval was computed, and the step also replaces experiment 152's own band with the band from other Primaries.
  • The stack arms leave far too many readings below q01. Share of readings at or below each quantile, all rows (nominal 1%, 5%, 95%, 99%): B 21.4%, 31.0%, 72.0%, 83.0%; C 21.6%, 31.1%, 72.2%, 82.9%; A 21.7%, 31.2%, 72.3%, 83.0%; BG2 0.2%, 4.0%, 94.4%, 99.8%. All stack arms put 21% of readings below q01.
  • Not done. The curtailment-cost metric is not computed, because D8 is one series and the metric needs a node with its generators. The sign of D8's flow cannot be checked without signed megawatts.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean (points, all rows). B 0.00, C 0.00, A 0.00, B-fold -0.22 (the fold moves the median by design).
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts. Mean absolute error of the mean forecast: B 15.21, C 15.42, A 15.48, BG2's median 13.88. B is below C and A, the same direction as C1 and C2.
  • Trigger 5 (a stage-2 arm scoring worse than the fit it corrects) fired: the stage-2 arms score worse than the fit they correct (B against experiment 152's arm A, and C against arm N). The first-year warm-up of the offset's expanding window explains part of the gap (B scores 12.093 against 11.722 for the unshifted fit in the first half of the scored year), but the gap remains in the second half (10.174 against 9.758). The Opus audit was waived by the manager; a Sonnet audit ran instead (next bullet). The fold verdict does not depend on it, because C1's interval includes zero with or without stage 2 (experiment 152's own N, A, F arms: -0.19 for F minus N).
  • Sonnet audit of trigger 5. It re-scored the raw stored forecasts of experiment 152 and found no bug and no leakage (adding 500 to every later reading changed no earlier shift). It reproduced the three headline contrasts: B minus C -0.234 (-0.796 to +0.196), B minus unshifted fit +0.393 (+0.187 to +0.612), and own-history band minus B -2.218 (-2.899 to -1.559). Of the +0.393, +0.243 comes from the shifts (night offset +0.254, recipe R +0.073) and +0.150 from replacing experiment 152's band with the band of other Primaries. D8's level steps explain the harm: the realised night error regressed on the offset has slope -1.10. The audit did not re-run the donor Primaries or check how the own-history band behaves in the first quarter of 2026.
  • Triggers 3, 4, 6, and 7 did not fire: the quantile score and the mean-forecast error agree in direction, there is one site so no leave-one-site-out check exists, no sister experiment has the same rows at D8, and no later design depends on this result.

docs.title: Prediction against outcome
docs.text:
• (1) B minus C -0.30 to 0.00. Got -0.234. Held.
  • (2) Reverse flow on 0 to 2% of half-hours. Got 1.8% of rows but 2.35% of distinct valid times (410 of 17,441). Partly held, and 188 of the 410 are at night, which the prediction did not expect.
  • (3) B at least 1.5 points above BG2. Got +3.539. Held.
  • (4) B within 0.5 points of A. Got -0.301. Held.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Fit the band on D8's own history. Arm B is 3.5 points above BG2 at D8, and the own-history band removes 2.2 of those points. The remaining 1.3 points sit in the high-level rows (+1.402, +0.989 to +2.010) and in winter nights. A term for D8's switching between two levels could address them; the D8 analysis of 2026-10-26 (a private brief) discusses it.
  • Leave the night offset and recipe R off at D8 until D8 has more than 15 months of history.
  • The stack's T-all design could be fitted through the meter at a Primary with strong reverse flow, such as D12; D8 does not need it.

docs.title: Do a forecast band fitted on D8's own residuals, and a longer fit history with a level step, close D8's gap to BG2?
docs.text:
A forecast band built from D8's own recent errors closes about 60% of D8's gap to BG2 without changing the median forecast.

The same rule raises the score by 1% to 6% at two of three Primaries with no engine, so it suits D8 and not yet the whole fleet. A longer fit history helps only in the first months, when the stored fits held 3 to 5 months of data. The verdict is partly supported: the own-residual band (fix 1) clears its threshold, and the longer fit history (fix 3) does not.

D8 (Marsh Lane) is a primary substation (Primary) whose forecast band the stack borrows from six other Primaries. We asked whether a band fitted on D8's own past errors, and a fit history that starts in September 2023 instead of April 2025, bring D8's forecast closer to BG2, the production-style forecast. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of D8's effective capacity (1 point is 1% of 10.38 MW, about 0.1 MW), and lower is better. The stack is a generalised additive model (GAM) of demand with a Kalman filter on recent errors, recipe R (subtract 0.75 times the last 14 days' mean error by half-hour), and a winter night offset. We rebuilt the band from D8's residuals of the previous 365 days with the methods of experiment 264 and experiment 265, tested the rule at D2, D3, and D4 (Primaries with no gas engine), and refitted D8's monthly stack with the longer history. The stack and its stored forecasts come from experiment 252. The D8 trial in experiment 353 (not yet merged) first found that a band from D8's own earlier months helps, and this experiment tests that finding against placebo Primaries.

Figure 1: the own-residual band closes about 60% of D8's gap to BG2.

Figure 2: the longer history helps in August and September 2025 only.

Figure 3: at Primaries with no engine, arm 2 raises the score by 1% to 6%, and arm 3 by up to 7%.

Figure 4: coverage is 0.90 to 0.96 after the first quarter.

Figure 5: from October 2025 on, the longer history lowers the score by 0.11 points.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms (fix 1, stored forecasts). Arm 1 is experiment 252's stage-2 arm d with the donated spread. Arm 2 is arm 1's median plus the as-of quantiles of D8's own residuals (365-day window, 28-day minimum, 6-hour reporting lag, refreshed every 7 origins). Arm 3 is arm 2 with the residual quantiles taken separately for each hour block and season. Arm 4 is arm 2 shrunk towards BG2's own residual quantiles. Arm A2 is arm 2's band on the stage-2 arm a (no night offset, no recipe R). The method code is from experiments 252 and 264, folders ml-experiments/00252-* and ml-experiments/00264-*.
  • Arms (fix 3, new monthly fits at D8). (a) Fit from 2025-04, as stored. (b) Fit from 2023-09 with an unpenalised level step per hour band at 2025-04-01. (c) Fit from 2023-09 with no step. Arm (d), the neighbours' profile as a prior, was not run, because studies.dp_gam has no prior hook. The fits are monthly, at the cuts of the stored fits. Every fit arm is scored with arm 3's band (the best on all rows in fix 1) and the stage-2 steps; the choice of arm 3 and of the stage-2 steps as the primary was made after fix 1's scores and before the fit arms' scores, and is post hoc.
  • Rows. 96,986 half-hourly rows at D8 in the scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours (the stored ensemble forecasts stop at 168 hours), fold_a_daily_gap_v1. Intervals resample whole months; the 99% level is the Bonferroni level for five planned contrasts.
  • Gate. The script reproduces experiment 252's stored D8 scores (arm 1 11.433, BG2 7.593), and fit arm (a) reproduces the stored forecasts exactly (largest difference 0.0 on every quantile and the mean).
  • Absolute scores, all rows. Arm 1 11.433, arm 2 9.161, arm 3 9.084, arm 4 9.195, A2 8.921, BG2 7.593, manual heuristic 8.469, climatology 9.757. On sunny daylight rows arm 2 scores 8.641 and BG2 8.223 (arm 2 minus BG2 +0.42, interval -0.72 to +1.15). On cold nights arm 2 scores 8.079 and BG2 8.878. In 2026 arm 2 is 0.91 points above BG2 (+0.54 to +1.28).
  • C1, arm 2 minus arm 1 (fix 1's verdict contrast). -2.27 (99% -3.37 to -1.35), so 59% of arm 1's 3.84-point gap to BG2. The interval lies wholly below the -1.0 threshold. Post hoc, on the 87,578 rows after the first as-of fit (the first fit is at the origin of 2025-08-06), the contrast is -2.52 (-3.69 to -1.61).
  • C2 and C3. Arm 3 minus arm 2 -0.08 (-0.14 to +0.00), and arm 4 minus arm 2 +0.03 (-0.04 to +0.18). The cell rule and the BG2 prior add nothing measurable to the plain own-residual band.
  • Stage-2 steps. A2 minus arm 2 is -0.24 (-0.50 to -0.06): with the own-residual band, dropping the night offset and recipe R scores better, as experiment 353 advised. Most of it sits in the first three months, when the stage-2 steps have the least history.
  • Pre-registered conditions for arm 2. Three of the four failed, and the fourth held. The share of the gap closed is at least 60% in 7 of 12 months; it falls short in July (0%), August (39%), September (58%), and May 2026 (55%), and December has a gap of 0.12 points, too small to divide by. The share of readings inside q05 to q95 is 0.917, 0.901, and 0.960 in the three quarters after the first, so the last one is above 0.95. Arm 2 beats BG2 in one month (December), within the allowed two, so that condition held.
  • Tails at D8, all rows. Share of readings below q01: arm 1 21.7%, arm 2 3.9%, arm 3 4.3%, arm 4 3.9%, BG2 0.2%. Below q05: 31.2%, 7.8%, 8.7%, 7.7%, and 4.0%. Above q99: 17.0%, 3.2%, 3.5%, 3.4%, and 0.2%. Inside q05 to q95: 0.411, 0.848, 0.838, 0.839, and 0.904. The own-residual bands still leave 4% of readings below q01, which matters because the lower tail is the curtailment-relevant one.
  • Placebos. Arm 2 minus arm 1 is +0.114 points at D2 (+5.5% of arm 1's score, 99% interval +2.2% to +9.1%), +0.019 at D3 (+1.3%, -4.7% to +6.8%), and +0.139 at D4 (+6.1%, +0.2% to +12.9%). The limit was +3%, so D2 and D4 fail. Arm 3 raises the score by 1.7% at D2, -0.9% at D3, and +7.0% at D4. The share of readings below q01 at D2, D3, and D4 is 2.5%, 3.2%, and 4.3% with arm 1 and 2.1%, 2.9%, and 4.5% with arm 2, so the lower tail does not worsen materially. The rise comes from the band ignoring lead time. The band takes residuals at the shortest lead and applies them at every lead to 168 hours. Coverage falls from 0.854 at 0 to 24 hours to 0.835 at 120 to 168 hours.
  • C4, fit (b) minus (a). All rows -0.70 (99% -1.86 to -0.02), July to September 2025 -2.55 (-4.11 to +0.01), and 2026 -0.13 (-0.35 to +0.06). The all-rows interval is not wholly below the -0.5 threshold, so C4 does not clear it. Fit (b) scores 8.382 against fit (a)'s 9.084, and is 0.79 points above BG2.
  • Where the gain sits. Monthly scores with arm 3's band, (a) against (b): July 12.70 and 12.71, August 11.55 and 7.44, September 12.21 and 8.97. Fit (a) rests on 3 to 5 months of data at those cuts, and the audit traced the gain to its cold-start error (fit (a)'s mean-forecast bias in August is +9.5 points against -2.1 for (b)). Post hoc, from October 2025 to June 2026 (73,331 rows), (b) minus (a) is -0.11 (-0.27 to +0.03).
  • C5, fit (c) minus (a) in 2026. +0.01 (-0.33 to +0.42). The prediction that (c) is worse than (a) in 2026 failed, so the data give no sign that the step is needed. (b) minus (c) is -0.09 (-0.24 to +0.04) on all rows.
  • Level step. The fitted steps at 2025-04-01 are negative at every hour band and cut: about -0.4 to -0.7 MW at night, -1.4 to -1.6 MW and -1.9 to -2.3 MW in the two daytime bands, and -0.8 to -0.9 MW in the evening from September 2025. Fit (c) without a step scores no worse, so the GAM's other terms may absorb the drop.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean, points of capacity. Arm 1 0.00 (its mean equals its median), arm 2 -0.03, arm 3 -0.38, A2 -0.75, fit (b) with arm 3's band -1.44. Arm 3's median sits 0.38 points below its mean, and fit (b)'s sits 1.44 points below. The band rule therefore moves the median by up to 0.15 MW.
  • Error of the median forecast, MW. Arm 1 1.607, arm 2 1.610, arm 3 1.613, BG2 1.440, so the own-residual band leaves the median error unchanged while the quantile score falls by 2.27 points. Fit (a) scores 1.613, fit (b) 1.509, and fit (c) 1.527.
  • Triggers that fired. Three checks failed: a placebo Primary exceeded the +3% limit (D2 and D4), two predictions failed without a tested explanation (fit (c) worse than fit (a) in 2026, and the monthly 60% closure), and a nested arm beat the arm that contains it (stage-2 arm a beat arm d).
  • Audit. A Sonnet audit re-derived arm 2's band, the placebos, and the fit arms from the stored forecasts with its own code. It confirmed every printed headline number and found no lookahead.
  • Audit findings, triaged.
    • The fit-history gain sits in the cold-start months, so the page reports it that way, and a post hoc October-to-June contrast was added.
    • The step date 2025-04-01 was chosen with hindsight, so the experiment tests whether a step is available, not whether a forecaster would find one.
    • The band's lead-independence probably explains the placebo rise, and it is the next experiment.
    • The December closure share has no meaning, because arm 1 is within 0.2 points of BG2 that month.
    • Origins are not daily, so "every 7 origins" is 8 to 9 days. The difference is harmless.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Lead range. The stored forecasts cover 0.5 to 168 hours; National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) needs forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead, so the 168 to 240 hour range is untested here.
  • Lab shortcuts. The reporting lag of 6 hours is an assumption about NGED's delivery of readings. The first 8 to 35 days of the scored year keep the donated band, because 28 days of resolved residuals do not exist yet; the shortcut understates the gain.
  • One site. D8 is one Primary, and the 12 scored months give wide intervals. The first-three-month intervals rest on three months, and the resampling cannot give them a meaningful lower bound.
  • Post hoc. These choices were made post hoc: the choice of arm 3's band and the stage-2 primary for fix 3, the October-to-June contrast, and the after-first-fit contrast.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• A band that widens with lead time. Take the as-of residuals by lead band as well as by hour and season, and re-test at D2, D3, and D4 against the +3% limit. That would show whether the placebo cost is the lead-independence the audit suspects.
  • Apply the own-residual band at D8 only. The score gain is larger than that of the other D8 fixes tested in experiments 252, 264, and 353, and a version that costs nothing at other Primaries is the condition for using it fleet-wide.
  • Leave the longer history and the level step. Neither earned its complexity in steady state.

docs.title: Does refitting D8's stack weekly close its gap to BG2, and how much of the gap is the median rather than the band?
docs.text:
Refitting D8's forecast weekly instead of monthly barely changes its score, so BG2's weekly refit is not why it beats our model at D8, and the remaining gap does not come from the median or the band alone. D8 is the Marsh Lane electricity substation. BG2 is the XGBoost model that is our current best reference forecast, and "the stack" is our additive-model forecast, which we compare against it. We refitted the stack (the version of experiment 354: fitted from 2023-09 with a step in its level at 2025-04-01, and a forecast band taken from D8's own past errors) monthly, weekly, and quarterly. We also put BG2's median forecast, and separately BG2's band (the spread of its quantile forecasts around the median), into the stack's forecast on the same 96,986 half-hours. The score is the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of D8's capacity (1 point is 0.1 MW), and a lower score is better. Weekly minus monthly is -0.045 points (99% interval -0.118 to +0.001). BG2 stays 0.79 points better than the monthly stack, and neither swap closes most of that gap.

  • Arms. (M) monthly refit, 12 cuts, the stored fit b of experiment 354 with its own-residual band by hour block and season (arm 3 there). (W) weekly, 52 cuts. (Q) quarterly, 4 cuts. Swaps on arm M's rows: (S1) M's median with BG2's spread, (S2) BG2's median with M's own-residual spread, (S3) BG2's median with the donated spread of experiment 252. Reuses the code of experiments 252, 264, and 354.
  • Gate. M scores 8.382 and BG2 7.593, as stored in experiment 354.
  • Absolute scores (all rows, quantile score). M 8.382, W 8.338, Q 8.416, S1 8.271, S2 8.171, S3 9.995, BG2 7.593, manual_heuristic 8.469, climatology 9.757.
  • Cadence contrasts (99% intervals, 20,000 month resamples). W minus M -0.045 (-0.118 to +0.001); Q minus M +0.034 (+0.003 to +0.082). W minus M in July to September 2025 is -0.148 (-0.309 to 0.000), in 2026 -0.013 (-0.033 to +0.008), on sunny half-hours -0.077 (-0.285 to +0.080).
  • Swap contrasts against M. S1 -0.111 (-0.999 to +0.325), which closes 14% of the 0.79-point gap to BG2. S2 -0.212 (-0.618 to +0.232), which closes 27%. S3 +1.613 (+0.602 to +2.624), so the donated spread is the worst part (the finding of experiment 354). In July to September 2025 S1 scores 8.454 against M's 9.585 (-1.131, -3.421 to +0.066), so the band difference is concentrated in the first three months.
  • Median error and coverage. Median absolute error is 1.509 MW for M, 1.503 for W, 1.514 for Q, and 1.440 for BG2. The share of readings inside q05 to q95 is 84.6% for M, 84.7% for W, 84.6% for Q, and 90.4% for BG2. Share below q01: M 3.9%, W 3.8%, BG2 0.2%. Share above q99: M 2.9%, BG2 0.2%.
  • Pre-registered predictions. H1 held: W minus M is under 0.2 points and Q minus M under 0.3. H2 failed: S1 closes 14%, not more than half, though S2 closes 27%, under a third as predicted. Verdict partly supported: the cadence is not the cause, but the gap does not split into a band part and a median part.
  • Reading of H2 (post hoc). The two swaps together close 41% of the gap. BG2's spread is fitted to BG2's own median errors, so swapping either part alone breaks the pairing. The pairing explanation is a hypothesis, not a tested result.
  • Not run. The placebo cadence contrast at D2, D3, and D4 failed in the forecast step (a lead band had no tuning residual to fit the spread on, ValueError in studies.dp_ens). The brief made the placebos optional ("if cheap"), so they were dropped, and the cadence result rests on D8 only. The cadence result therefore may not carry to other Primaries; experiment 278 found weekly equal to monthly at six other Primaries.
  • Lab shortcuts. The own-residual band uses only errors known when the forecast is made, and assumes a reading arrives 6 hours after its valid time. Horizon is 0.5 to 168 hours, not NGED's 1 to 10 days. Weather at forecast time is the ensemble forecast, as in experiment 252.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast (points of capacity): M -1.44, W -1.37, Q -1.71, which is the own-residual band's shift of the median from the filter's mean, as in experiment 354. Error of the mean forecast beside the median's: M 1.505 against 1.509 MW, W 1.500 against 1.503 MW, so the cadence contrast has the same sign on the mean forecast. Audit triggers (the ml-experiment skill's seven conditions): none fired. The reproduction gate held, no result contradicts its prediction, and only one site was scored.
  • What to try next. Fit BG2's median and spread jointly on the stack's residuals at D8 (for example a model of the stack's error on BG2's error), rather than swapping parts. Test weekly against monthly again at a Primary with long history before adopting weekly refits anywhere.

docs.title: Plan as registered before any score was read
docs.text:
• Question. D8 (Marsh Lane) scores 8.38 with the best stack of experiment 354 against BG2's 7.59. BG2 refits weekly and the stack refits monthly. The maintainer asked, on 2026-10-26, whether weekly refits close the gap, and how the gap splits between the median and the band.
  • Cadence arms (fits at D8). The stack of experiment 354's fit b (from 2023-09 with a level step per hour band at 2025-04-01, stage-2 arm D, own-residual band by hour block and season): (M) monthly cuts as stored, (W) a cut every 7 days, (Q) every third monthly cut. Only data available at each cut is used.
  • Swap arms (no fit). On arm M's rows: (S1) arm M's median with BG2's spread (BG2 quantile minus BG2 median, added to arm M's median); (S2) BG2's median with arm M's own-residual band; (S3) BG2's median with the stack's donated spread; M and BG2 as stored. Report the score, median error in MW, and q05 to q95 coverage.
  • Placebos. The cadence contrast at D2, D3, and D4 (stored default window, no level step).
  • Slices. Sunny daylight half-hours and the first three scored months, separately.
  • Scoring. Scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, the 96,986 rows of experiment 354, month-resampled 95% and 99% intervals.
  • Weather at forecast time. Same ensemble forecast weather and past-weather proxy as experiment 252, so every input exists at forecast time.
  • Earlier advice followed. Experiment 354: fit b with the own-residual band. Experiment 278: weekly equalled monthly on six other Primaries, so a null is the prior.
  • Compute. CPU only, 6 spawned workers, one thread each, MemoryMax=16G.

docs.title: Does blending with Wind farms research default 1, or refitting every month, fix the upper tail of Wind farms research default 2?
docs.text:
Take-home: blending Wind farms research default 2 (a physics model plus a neural-network head) with Wind farms research default 1 (an XGBoost model), or refitting default 2 every month, does not fix its upper tail. Of the half-hourly observations at 24 to 240 hours' lead, 2.15% fall above default 2's 0.99 quantile (q99), against the 1% a calibrated q99 gives. The best arm leaves 1.77%, and no arm clearly beats default 2. The blend's small gain is the same with shuffled weights, so it comes from averaging two forecasts and not from learning weights. The top quantile probably needs new information, and the monthly retrained head is the one arm worth a longer retest. Verdict: not supported, meaning no arm fixed the tail while keeping the gain.

We asked whether four cheap changes would fix the upper tail of Wind farms research default 2 (a physics model of each farm run on the 51 weather-ensemble members, then a mixture head) while keeping its 0.23-point gain over Wind farms research default 1 (an XGBoost model plus a table of quantile offsets). The four changes were: a per-quantile blend of the two defaults whose weights are refitted each month (u2); experiment 348's blend of the physics model's residual band with default 1 (u1, the recipe of experiments 270, 287, and 300); a monthly offset layer on default 2 (u4, experiment 346's recipe); and retraining default 2's head every month (u3). Scores are in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity). W1 to W3 are the three metered wind farms, whose names are withheld. W1 to W3 are the three metered wind farms, whose names are withheld. Scored at true days 1 to 10 (lead 24 to 240 hours), kept half-hours, on the 53 Tuesday runs of fold_a_tuesdays_v1 (the scored year) and, once, on the Tuesday runs of 2026-07 to 2026-10 (the replicate, about 16 runs).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and window. Default 2 is experiment 347's y2, refitted here (five seeds). u2 and u4 refit on the first day of each month on kept daily runs from 2025-04-16 whose valid times end at least 3.5 hours before that day (earlier runs are in-sample for default 2's head, so a start in 2024-04 would measure the head's training fit). u3 retrains on all finished runs from 2024-04, stopping early on the last 2 months. Kept rows end at 2026-09-13, so the refits of 2026-10 use runs to that date. Default 1 has 3 seeds and is paired with seed s mod 3. Code reuse: experiments 230, 259, 303, 310, 326, 336, 346, 347, and 348.
  • Schedule. Monthly refits on a growing window for every arm; the scored year and the replicate use the same refits. The contrast could depend on schedule for u3 and u4 only.
  • Absolute scores, true days 1 to 10 (scored year; replicate). Default 1 10.751 (7.231); default 2 10.518 (7.122); u1 10.604 (7.237); u2 10.470 (7.082); u2 placebo 10.465 (7.088); u3 10.480 (7.002); u4 10.495 (7.206). Frozen XGBoost reference 11.102 and climatology 13.860 (from experiment 347, scored year). Seed sd of the headline: default 2 0.026, u2 0.013, u3 0.019, u4 0.029.
  • Gate. Default 2 reproduces experiment 347 (10.518 and 11.081 over every lead), default 1 reproduces 10.752 to within 0.001, and u1 reproduces experiment 348's z5 (10.604 against 10.605).
  • Gain over default 2, true days 1 to 10 (scored year, 99.75% month-block interval; replicate, 95% run-block interval). u2 -0.048 (-0.178 to +0.045; replicate -0.040, -0.118 to +0.041); u1 +0.086 (-0.151 to +0.289; replicate +0.116, -0.036 to +0.274); u4 -0.023 (-0.145 to +0.108; replicate +0.084, -0.012 to +0.173); u3 -0.038 (-0.104 to +0.024; replicate -0.120, -0.206 to -0.022). At days 1 to 2 u2 gains 0.166 (-0.374 to -0.023); at days 3 to 10 no arm's interval excludes zero.
  • Gain over default 1 (cumulative harm budget). u2 -0.280 (-0.471 to -0.115); u1 -0.147 (-0.272 to -0.059); u4 -0.255 (-0.620 to +0.058); u3 -0.270 (-0.567 to -0.002). No arm is worse than default 1; the one-sided 95% harm bound against default 1 is at most -0.078 on the headline and +0.044 at the 0.99 pinball loss.
  • Added value of the blend over the best single family. The best single family is default 2 (10.518, against 10.751 and 11.102). u2 adds -0.048 (-0.178 to +0.045); u1 adds +0.086.
  • Controls. The shuffled-weights placebo gains 0.053 and u2 gains 0.048; u2 minus placebo is +0.005 (-0.021 to +0.035), so the placebo keeps the whole gain. Leakage check: every refit's latest valid time is at or before the month start minus 3.5 hours (arms/leakage.json, 32 refits, no violation).
Arm (scored year, true days 1 to 10) Below q01 (%) Below q05 (%) Above q95 (%) Above q99 (%) p01 p05 p95 p99 5 to 95 coverage (%) default 1 0.55 1.36 6.62 1.66 0.285 1.347 2.414 0.603 92.0 default 2 0.81 4.43 6.69 2.15 0.283 1.302 2.382 0.626 88.9 u1 0.67 2.54 6.65 1.78 0.287 1.335 2.407 0.602 90.8 u2 0.69 4.19 6.51 1.86 0.283 1.303 2.348 0.599 89.3 u2 placebo 0.70 4.19 6.48 1.86 0.283 1.303 2.350 0.601 89.3 u3 0.80 4.76 6.36 2.04 0.283 1.302 2.360 0.617 88.9 u4 0.78 4.78 5.71 1.77 0.283 1.301 2.359 0.614 89.5
  • Tails. u2 lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by 4.3% (0.626 to 0.599) and leaves 1.86% above q99. u4 lowers the share to 1.77% but raises the 0.99 pinball loss against default 1 (0.614 against 0.603). On the replicate runs every arm has under 0.7% above q99 (default 2 0.48%, u4 0.29%, u3 0.38%), so the replicate cannot judge the upper tail.
  • Adoption (order u2, u1, u4, u3). No arm passes condition 1: every scored-year interval of (arm minus default 2) includes zero, and u1 is worse than default 2. Nothing is adopted and no arm is a candidate for a later version of the research default.
  • Pre-registered predictions.
    • u2 lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by at least 10% (fails, 4.3%) and puts the share above q99 under 1.6% (fails, 1.86%). u2 gains at least 0.05 points (fails by 0.002, 0.048).
    • u1 matches experiment 348's gain over default 1 (holds, 0.147) and its gain over default 2 is smaller than u2's (holds, since u1 loses 0.086).
    • u4 gains under 0.05 (holds, 0.023) and the share above q99 stays above 2% (fails, 1.77%).
    • u3 gains under 0.05 (holds, 0.038) and has a wider interval than u4 (fails, 0.129 against 0.253 wide).
  • Serving. u1 and u2 need the plant plus head and the XGBoost default both running, and a monthly job to refit weights (u1 also needs the stored residual-band table). u4 needs a monthly offset job. u3 needs a monthly job that retrains the head.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per farm (true days 1 to 10): default 2 -3.3, -3.5, -3.1 points for W1 to W3; u2 -3.6, -4.0, -3.4; u3 -3.3, -3.8, -3.0; u4 -3.5, -4.2, -3.5; default 1 -4.2, -4.5, -3.3. The mean-forecast absolute error moves with the quantile score for u1, u2, and u3, and against it for u4 (15.161 against 15.028 for default 2, while its score improves by 0.023). Leaving W3 out turns u2's gain into a loss (+0.017); leaving out W1 or W2 keeps it. Triggers fired: 1 (the placebo kept the gain), 3 (u4), and 4 (u2 without W3). The weights differ between months by a standard deviation of 0.12 on average, so a shuffle moves them modestly; why that leaves the score unchanged is explained by the audit below. The audit was run by a Sonnet agent, not Opus (the manager waived Opus while credits are low); the auditor re-derived the contrasts from the stored arrays and found no method fault. Its findings: the arrays are sorted, in range, and aligned (median correlation with default 2 of 0.92 to 0.99); u2 reproduces from its stored weights to 3e-8; a fixed weight of 0.75 on default 2 (no learning) gives -0.047, the same as u2, so the placebo behaves as designed and the gain is averaging; u4's opposite movement of mean-forecast error comes from lifting only the upper quantiles (+1.7 to +2.5 points from q75 to q99); u2's pooled gain is one farm (W3 -0.186, W1 +0.026, W2 +0.007), and default 1 is competitive with default 2 only at W3; default 1 has only 3 independent seeds, so the seed sds of the arms that use it are optimistic; and on every lead u4 leaves 1.84% above q99, not 1.77% (the headline-scope figure). The auditor's own advice: u2's gain rests on W3, and only u3 and u4 keep their sign without it, both within noise.
  • Caveats. Scored at true days 1 to 10 only; three farms give wide intervals. The replicate is about 16 runs and its kept rows end at 2026-09-13. Intervals resample the seed mean of each row's score, so seed variation is reported separately. The runs 2025-04-16 to 2025-06-16 that stopped default 2's head early feed u2 and u4's first windows, a small optimism for those arms. u1's blend weights come from earlier Tuesday runs selected by the month of the run, so a run from late in a month contributes outcomes up to about 10 days into the next month, which breaks the 3.5-hour rule that u2, u3, and u4 obey; this lookahead (also present in experiment 348's z5) can only flatter u1, which already loses. The u1 and u3 refits are not in arms/leakage.json (u3's check is printed in the heads log). The curtailment metric is not scored: it needs a node's export and its generators' forecasts together.
  • What to try next. (1) Retest u3 on a longer out-of-time period. (2) Give the top quantile new information: a point mass fitted with a likelihood (experiment 348's advice), or a monthly recalibration of q99 on its own. (3) Use a fixed 0.75:0.25 mix of the two defaults, which the audit found equals u2.

docs.title: Does retraining Wind farms research default 2's mixture head every month still beat default 2 on many more runs?
docs.text:
Take-home: retraining the mixture head of Wind farms research default 2 every month improves the quantile score slightly, by about 0.04 to 0.05 points over one year and about 0.10 points over the latest 2.5 months, but the one-year 99% interval still touches zero, so the change is a candidate and is not adopted. The upper tail is not fixed. Verdict: partly supported.

Wind farms research default 2 is this project's current wind forecast: a physics model of each farm is run on each of the 51 members of the ECMWF ensemble weather forecast, and a mixture head (a small neural network that turns the 51 power forecasts into 11 quantiles) produces the final forecast. Wind farms research default 1 is the earlier recipe, an XGBoost model plus a table of quantile offsets. We asked again whether retraining the mixture head on the first day of every month beats keeping the head fixed. Experiment 356 tested this (its arm u3) on 53 Tuesday runs, meaning forecasts issued on Tuesdays, and on 10 Tuesday runs of 2026-07 onwards. This experiment scores the same five seeds of retrained heads on every kept daily run: 439 runs from 2025-07-01 to 2026-09-13, using the data already fetched for experiment 356. "Kept" means the rows that pass experiment 210's data-cleaning mask. The scored year is the 12 months 2025-07 to 2026-06, and the replicate is the 74 runs of 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-13. Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity), where a lower score is better, at true days 1 to 10 (lead 24 to 240 hours). W1 to W3 are the three metered wind farms, whose names are withheld.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scope u3 minus default 2 Interval Stale-head placebo minus default 2 53 Tuesday runs, scored year (primary) -0.038 -0.094 to +0.016 (99%, months) -0.006 Every run, scored year (365) -0.044 -0.082 to +0.002 (99%, months) -0.005 Every run, 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-13 (74, replicate) -0.096 -0.127 to -0.066 (95%, runs) -0.058 Tuesday runs of 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-13 (10) -0.120 -0.207 to -0.021 (95%, runs) -0.054 Every run (439) -0.052 -0.088 to -0.009 (99%, months) -0.013
  • Arms and schedule. Default 2 is experiment 347's y2. u3 retrains the head monthly on all finished runs from 2024-04 (valid times at least 3.5 hours before the month starts), as in experiment 356, whose case table, default 1 and default 2 forecasts and code this experiment reuses (folders 356, 348, 347, 346, 336, 326, 310, 303, 259, and 230). The window of training runs grows by one month at each refit.
  • Absolute scores (headline). Default 2: 10.518 (53 Tuesday runs), 10.399 (scored year, 365 runs), 7.261 (74 runs of 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-13), 9.929 (all 439 runs). u3: 10.480, 10.355, 7.165, 9.877. Default 1: 10.751, 10.574, 7.429, 10.103. Standard deviation across seeds of the headline: 0.026 for default 2 and 0.019 for u3 (Tuesdays).
  • Gate. Default 2 reproduces 10.518, default 1 reproduces 10.751, and u3 reproduces experiment 356's 10.480 on the 53 Tuesday runs.
  • Gain over default 2, headline (negative is better). The table above has each scope. Relative to default 2's score, the gain of u3 is 0.4% on the Tuesday runs, 0.4% over the scored year, 1.3% on the replicate, and 0.5% on all runs. Over all runs, days 1 to 2 gain -0.032 (-0.080 to +0.015) and days 3 to 10 gain -0.057 (-0.098 to -0.005). A t interval over the 15 monthly differences (2025-07 to 2026-09), which suits few months better than a percentile bootstrap, is -0.095 to +0.005 (99%); u3 beat default 2 in 11 of 15 months.
  • Placebo. Each month takes the head fitted at a random earlier month at least 3 months before (the first 3 months take the first head; one draw). Over the scored year the stale head gains only 0.005. The score of u3 minus that of the stale head is -0.039 (-0.079 to +0.006). From 2026-07 onwards the stale head still gains 0.058, probably because even a head 3 or more months old holds newer data than default 2. So the placebo separates recency within the scored year but not in the latest months, and the replicate gain may partly reflect a change in the farms or weather during 2026.
  • Tails (true days 1 to 10). Share of observations above q99, default 2 against u3: 2.15% and 2.04% (53 Tuesday runs), 1.83% and 1.70% (all runs), 0.68% and 0.63% (replicate). The 0.99 pinball loss falls from 0.626 to 0.617 (Tuesdays) and from 0.594 to 0.583 (all runs). The share stays above the 1% intended. The share below q01 is unchanged (0.81% and 0.80% on Tuesdays). The share below q05 rises slightly (4.43% to 4.76% on Tuesdays).
  • Harm (one-sided 95% upper bound of u3 minus default 2). Headline -0.003 (Tuesdays) and -0.015 (scored year); 0.01 pinball loss +0.001 and 0.99 pinball loss 0.000 and -0.005. All are within the tolerances (0.02 and 0.05).
  • By farm (all runs, u3 minus default 2). W1 -0.063, W2 -0.012, W3 -0.081. Leaving out any one farm keeps the sign (-0.046, -0.072, -0.038).
  • Adoption conditions. (1) Gain: not met on the pre-registered scopes; the 99% intervals of the Tuesday runs and the scored year include zero (the scored-year interval by 0.002), and the interval over all runs excludes zero (-0.088 to -0.009) with the month-block interval but not with the t interval. (2) No harm: met. (3) Replication: met, same sign, -0.096. (4) Controls: reproduction gate and leakage check passed; the placebo is partly informative (above). (5) Serving: the change needs a monthly job that retrains the head on the finished runs. Nothing is adopted without the maintainer's decision, and the change stays a candidate.
  • Pre-registered predictions. The gain is between 0.03 and 0.10 (holds, 0.038 to 0.096) but the interval excludes zero on only one of the scopes (partly holds). The placebo gains under half of u3's gain (holds over the scored year, fails on the replicate). At least 1.8% above q99 (holds on Tuesdays, 2.04%; fails on all runs, 1.70%). The gain is larger from 2026-07 on (holds).
  • Median and mean forecast. The median forecast sits below the mean forecast, per farm (all runs, W1 to W3), by 3.19, 3.57, and 3.04 points for default 2 and by 3.26, 3.84, and 2.93 points for u3. The absolute error of the mean forecast moves the other way from the quantile score over the scored year (+0.011 on Tuesdays, +0.017 over the year, -0.003 over all runs). That fires audit trigger 3 of the ml-experiment skill (the mean forecast's error and the quantile score point in different directions). No other audit trigger fired: the placebo and the gate pass, and no leave-one-farm-out check flips a sign.
  • Audit. A Sonnet agent (the usual Opus audit was waived while credits are low) re-derived the contrasts from the stored arrays with its own code and reproduced them exactly. It found no leakage, because every head's training and stopping rows end at least 3.5 hours before its month starts, and no invalid quantile. It read trigger 3 as a difference in loss: the head is fitted to quantiles, the squared error of the mean forecast falls (root mean squared error 20.23 to 20.17), and the gain sits at the 0.5 to 0.95 levels. Per seed, the all-run contrast is negative for all five seeds, from -0.007 to -0.087.
  • Caveats. Three farms, kept rows, true days 1 to 10 only; farm names withheld. Daily runs of one month are strongly correlated, so 15 months are the effective sample, and 99% month-block intervals from so few months can cover less than 99%. The placebo is a single draw. The curtailment metric is not scored.
  • What to try next. Options are to retest after about 6 more months of runs, and to give the upper tail new information (for example a second weather forecast), since retraining leaves it unchanged.

docs.title: MVA fold: known-answer test at folded signed Primaries
docs.text:
The model fitted through the meter recovers the flow direction and the solar capacity about as well as a model that sees the signed power, while reactive power is zero. The model also invented reverse flow at the one Primary substation with none (D5), and it failed when the data carried reactive power at power factor 0.97. Verdict: partly supported. The sequence stops here, because the pre-registered pass rule fails as written.

We asked whether the direction of the power flow at a Primary substation can be recovered from a meter that reports only apparent power (the size of the flow in MVA, with no direction). We took five Primaries whose signed power is known and subtracted the output of a real solar farm at two sizes: 1.0 times and 2.0 times the site's median absolute midday power. Those are injection levels 1.0 and 2.0, and "natural" means no injection. We then replaced each reading with its magnitude, which is what folding means here.

We fitted three models. L0 is the convex demand-plus-solar model fitted through the meter, as in experiment 110. S is the same model fitted to the signed series, which is the ceiling. N is the same model fitted to the magnitude as if it were signed power. Fits were frozen at 2025-07-01 (the scored cut) and scored on the following year with past weather; the replicate cut is 2024-07-01. "Sunny half-hours" are April to September, starting 10:00 to 13:30 UTC, with irradiance of at least 500 W/m².

docs.title: Results (scored cut, zero reactive power in the data, point forecasts)
docs.text:
• Direction, sunny half-hours. L0's accuracy is within 0.01 of S's at every site and level except D5 at the natural level. At level 1.0 it is 0.82 to 0.94 against N's 0.26 to 0.70. At level 2.0 it is 0.94 to 0.99 against N's 0.01 to 0.06. The replicate cut agrees (L0 within 0.01 of S).
  • Pre-registered rule. At level 1.0, 4 of 5 sites reach balanced accuracy 0.80 on sunny half-hours (D5 is 0.69, and S is 0.66 there too). At level 2.0, balanced accuracy is 0.5 at every site, because 92% to 99% of the sunny half-hours are reverse flow. The rule fails as written, and the metric cannot tell the arms apart there. Plain accuracy, post hoc, passes at 5 of 5 sites.
  • Capacity. L0's fitted capacity is within 15% of S's at 5 of 5 sites at both levels. The rise from the natural fit is about 75% to 80% of the injected capacity for both L0 and S (D10: 0.80), so the capacity shortfall appears in the signed fit too and the folding does not cause it.
  • Reading error. L0's mean absolute error on the magnitude is below N's at every level-1.0 and level-2.0 cell, by 1 to 15 points on sunny half-hours (for example D10 at level 2.0: 10.4 against 25.3).
  • Placebo fails at D5. With no injection, L0 gets the direction right on 35% of sunny half-hours at D5 (S and N: 98%). Its fitted capacity is 1.30 times S's. The six starting points of the fit disagree by 45 percentage points of capacity. The lowest-loss start has a solar term that is large and negative at midday, a mirror image that a loss on the magnitude cannot tell from the right answer.
  • Reactive power breaks it. With power factor 0.97 in the data and Q = 0 in the fit, L0 collapses to N at D11, D14, and D16 at level 1.0 (accuracy 0.31 to 0.63, capacity 0.70 to 0.77 of S). The design brief's measurement puts the reactive floor at Stickney (D12) below 1% of capacity, so the zero-reactive case is the relevant one there.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers. Audit trigger 1 (a failed control) fired: the D5 placebo. A fresh Sonnet auditor found no leakage, confirmed the D5 result is a mirror-basin weakness and not a bug, traced the Q1 collapse to the Q = 0 assumption, and confirmed the sunny mask. It also flagged that the claim "L0 matches S" excludes D5 at the natural level, which this page states.
  • Median against mean forecast. Not applicable: these are point forecasts from frozen fits.
  • Departures from the plan. Plain accuracy is added post hoc beside balanced accuracy. The audit used Sonnet because the series brief requires it, not Opus.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Frozen fits on past weather, no ensemble, no Kalman filter, no quantiles: sign recovery only.
  • One farm (A) supplies the injected output, so the result is for one farm shape.
  • At the natural level, D11, D14, and D16 have no reverse flow, so balanced accuracy cannot be computed.
  • Step 2 should read L0's reverse flow only after a check that rejects the D5-type mirror basin (for example, require the lowest-loss start to agree with the start nearest zero reverse flow).

docs.title: Does averaging the GAM stack's quantiles with BG2's beat BG2 alone at D8?
docs.text:
At D8 the GAM stack adds little to BG2, so a blend of the GAM stack and BG2 does not beat BG2 by a margin that would justify running a second stack.

Giving the stack and BG2 weight 0.5 each scores 0.041 points above BG2 on the second half of the scored year (95% interval -0.082 to +0.170). A weight of 0.25 on the stack scores 0.060 points below BG2 on that half, with an interval that includes zero. The verdict is not supported. The stop rule ends the planned contrasts, so the placebos, tails, and slices below are descriptive.

D8 (Marsh Lane) is a primary substation, which this page calls a Primary. At D8, BG2 (best guess 2, the production-style forecast) scores below the GAM stack. The GAM stack is a generalised additive model (GAM) of demand with a Kalman filter on recent errors and a band fitted on D8's own past errors (Primary demand research default 1 refitted weekly; see experiment 355 and experiment 354).

We asked whether the stack adds information that BG2 lacks. We used stored forecasts and no new fits, averaging each of the 11 quantiles of the two forecasts at stack weights 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75. The first half of the scored year (July to December 2025) chose the weight, and the second half (January to June 2026) judged it.

The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantiles, in points of D8's effective capacity (10.38 MW, so 1 point is about 0.1 MW). Lower is better. This experiment is interim: one substation, one scored year, and weights chosen on a half-year.

Figure 1: at D8 no blend scores below BG2 by an interval wholly below zero on the second half.

Figure 2: the 0.5 blend scores below BG2 in 8 of 12 months, and December 2025 is the largest gap.

Figure 3: at three Primaries with no gas engine, the 0.5 blend scores below BG2, and below the stack at D2 and D4.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. BG2; the GAM stack (experiment 355's weekly-refit arm W); and blends with weight 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 on the stack. Code reuses experiments 252, 264, 354, and 355 (folders ml-experiments/00252-*, 00264-*, 00354-*, and 00355-*) for the stored forecasts and scoring helpers.
  • Rows. The scored set has 96,986 half-hourly rows at D8, 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, forecast lead times of 0.5 to 168 hours, fold_a_daily_gap_v1. Intervals resample whole months (20,000 resamples). Intervals below are 95%, the level the plan set; the 99% Bonferroni intervals for the four planned contrasts are in blend_scores.json.
  • Gate. The script reproduces 8.338 (stack, printed 8.3376) and 7.593 (BG2) before any blend is read.

  • Absolute scores at D8 (quantile score, points of capacity):

    Arm Whole year First half Second half GAM stack 8.338 8.861 7.816 Blend, 0.25 on the stack 7.438 7.789 7.087 Blend, 0.5 on the stack 7.511 7.836 7.188 Blend, 0.75 on the stack 7.809 8.186 7.434 BG2 7.593 8.040 7.147 Manual heuristic 8.469 9.324 7.617 Climatology 9.757 11.324 8.195

  • Weight choice. The first half selects 0.25 (7.789, against 7.836 for 0.5). The choice is a minimum over first-half scores alone, so no second-half score enters it.

  • C1, 0.5 blend minus BG2, second half (the verdict contrast). +0.041 (-0.082 to +0.170). The interval is not wholly below zero, so the stop rule applies and the prediction fails.
  • C2, 0.5 blend minus BG2, whole year. -0.082 (-0.362 to +0.122).
  • C3, 0.25 blend minus BG2, second half. -0.060 (-0.132 to +0.006). Over the whole year the 0.25 blend is -0.155 (-0.307 to -0.057), and the whole-year figure includes the half-year the weight was chosen on.
  • C4, 0.5 blend minus the stack, second half. -0.628 (-0.794 to -0.455). The stack alone is +0.669 (+0.434 to +0.928) above BG2 on that half.
  • Lead bands, whole year (scores of the 0.5 blend, the 0.25 blend, and BG2). In the 0 to 24 hour band they are 7.415, 7.290, and 7.436; in the 24 to 72 hour band 7.415, 7.337, and 7.489; in the 72 to 168 hour band 7.584, 7.525, and 7.685. The 0.5 blend minus BG2 is -0.021, -0.074, and -0.101, each with an interval that includes zero. The 0.25 blend minus BG2 is -0.146, -0.152, and -0.160, each with an interval wholly below zero.
  • Months. The 0.5 blend beats BG2 in 8 of 12 months and loses in July, February, May, and June. December 2025 alone is 7.84 against 9.20.
  • Sunny April-to-June half-hours (2026), the sunniest third of daylight half-hours. Stack 7.178, blend 0.25 6.468, blend 0.5 6.574, BG2 6.501. The 0.5 blend minus BG2 is +0.073 (-0.215 to +0.394). On cold nights (below 2 °C) the stack scores 8.003, blend 0.5 7.856, and BG2 8.878.
  • Tails (whole year). Share of readings inside q05 to q95: stack 0.847, blend 0.25 0.919, blend 0.5 0.908, blend 0.75 0.883, BG2 0.904. Share below q01: 3.8%, 0.5%, 1.2%, 2.3%, and 0.2%. Share above q99: 2.9%, 0.3%, 0.7%, 1.5%, and 0.2%. Averaging the quantiles with BG2's cuts the stack's share below q01 from 3.8% to 0.5% at weight 0.25. BG2 has the smallest share beyond q01 and q99 (0.2% each, against a nominal 1%), so its outer quantiles sit wider than nominal.
  • Placebos (whole year, 0.5 blend). The stack scores below BG2 at D2, D3, and D4 already (-0.100, -0.209, -0.099; only D3's 95% interval, -0.335 to -0.099, excludes zero). The 0.5 blend minus BG2 is -0.198 (-0.267 to -0.130) at D2, -0.234 (-0.296 to -0.178) at D3, and -0.221 (-0.347 to -0.108) at D4. The 0.5 blend minus the stack is -0.097 (-0.174 to -0.017) at D2, -0.025 (-0.099 to +0.047) at D3, and -0.122 (-0.196 to -0.051) at D4. The first half selects weights 0.75, 0.75, and 0.5 at D2, D3, and D4.
  • How the stack builds its band. The stack averages the 51 ensemble members into one mean run and forecasts one corrected mean from it, so no per-member forecasts exist to pool. The band is that median plus the as-of empirical quantiles of the stack's own past residuals (reading minus median at the shortest lead of each valid time), by six-hour block and season, over the trailing 365 days, refreshed about every 7 origins: one residual width on one median.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, D8. The stack's median is 1.37 points (about 0.14 MW) below its mean. BG2's median is 2.49 points above the stack's median, on average. Blend rows have no mean column.
  • Error of the median forecast beside each score contrast. Median absolute error is about 1.50 MW for the stack, 1.42 MW for the 0.25 blend, 1.43 MW for the 0.5 blend, 1.45 MW for the 0.75 blend, and 1.44 MW for BG2. The ordering matches the quantile-score ordering, so trigger 3 did not fire. The correlation between the stack's and BG2's median errors is 0.86.
  • Triggers that fired. Trigger 2 fired in a weak form: the 0.5 blend failed its prediction, and the monthly scores are consistent with the first half carrying the 0.5 blend's gain, December 2025 above all, but no test confirmed that. No Opus audit ran, because this experiment's plan allowed Sonnet only. Triggers 1, 3, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire, and trigger 4 (leave one site out) does not apply to one site.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Lead range. The stored forecasts cover 0.5 to 168 hours. NGED needs forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead, so the 168 to 240 hour range is untested.
  • Stack definition. The D8 stack is the weekly-refit arm with its own-residual band. A stack with the donated band, or a different refit cadence, may blend differently. At D2, D3, and D4 the stack is experiment 354's arm 1, because the own-residual band raised the score there.
  • Weights. A grid of three weights on a half-year of data is coarse, and the first half carries the stack's cold-start months.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Leave the blend out at D8. The stack adds too little to BG2 to justify the effort of two stacks.
  • Test a blend at the Primaries where the stack beats BG2. D2 and D4 score 0.10 to 0.12 points below the stack alone, so a blend with BG2 may help there. Choose the weights on a separate half-year.

docs.title: Which of BG2's five members explains its lower score than the GAM stack at substation D8?
docs.text:
Take-home message: BG2's lower score at substation D8 is not a gain from blending. BG2 is the second "best guess" forecast for Primary substations (the substations that step 33 kV or 66 kV down to 11 kV): a blend of five forecasts. D8 is the Primary substation at Marsh Lane. The GAM stack is the generalised additive model forecast of Primary demand research default 1, refitted weekly (experiment 355). Scores are the quantile score, twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points (percent of effective capacity; lower is better). Four of BG2's five members score 7.47 to 7.69 alone, against 8.338 for the GAM stack. Dropping any one member moves the blend's 7.593 by at most 0.09 points. The XGBoost stack member alone scores 8.562, so the lower score comes from the other four members' own forecasts. The prediction written before any score was read held: no drop moved D8's score by 0.2 points or more.

What we did. We rebuilt BG2's blend from experiment 87's stored member forecasts, with no new fits. The five members are weekly-refitted XGBoost, monthly-refitted XGBoost, an analogue model, a model pooled by substation type, and the XGBoost stack (the N1 model with a 14-day error correction). We re-blended the members with one dropped, re-choosing the blend's monthly weights from earlier months each time, and scored each member alone. Experiment 87 reports drop-one ablations for the Primary substations as a group and none for D8 on its own. The rows are the 96,986 half-hourly forecast rows of experiments 353 to 355 at D8. D8's effective capacity is 10.4 MW, so one point is 0.104 MW. The re-blended five-member arm reproduces BG2's stored 7.593.

Caveat. The result is interim: one substation and one scored year. The experiment cannot show why one member scores best.
