docs.title: Control check at three other Primary substations (D2, D3, D4)
docs.text:
Each substation has 121,492 half-hourly rows: all stored rows with a lead of up to 168 hours and an observed power value.

  • D2: five-member blend 2.181; drops move it by -0.003 to +0.053 points (largest: without the XGBoost stack, interval +0.026 to +0.081); the best single member (weekly XGBoost) scores 2.221.
  • D3: blend 1.661; drops move it by -0.002 to +0.020; the best single member scores 1.673.
  • D4: blend 2.403; drops move it by -0.020 to +0.021, all intervals include zero; the best single member (weekly XGBoost) scores 2.374, 0.029 better than the blend.
  • The blend is within 0.03 points of the best single member at D3 and D4, and 0.04 points better at D2. The pooled-by-type member alone is the worst of the five at each of the three.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Mean forecast. The stored member forecasts hold quantiles only, so there is no mean forecast to compare with the median. The mean absolute error of the median in the table ranks the arms in the same order as the quantile score for the arms with the lowest scores (analogue alone, 1.408 MW; the blend without the XGBoost stack, 1.419 MW).
  • A member beats the blend that contains it (audit trigger 5). The analogue member alone scores 0.121 points better than the five-member blend (interval -0.255 to -0.013). A Sonnet agent (not Opus, because this result does not decide a model release) audited the method by re-deriving the scores from the stored D8 frame with its own code, and found no error. There were no duplicate row keys, no missing values, and no crossing quantiles in any arm. The analogue member's advantage comes from a lower median error and better coverage at the same interval width. The analogue member beats the blend in 8 of 12 months, and about half of the total gain comes from January 2026, October 2025, and December 2025 together. In November to January the blend puts weight 0.5 on the XGBoost stack member, the worst member alone, because the weights are chosen on earlier months across all 16 Primary substations. The audit calls the analogue member modestly better, on one substation over 12 months. The control check at D2, D3, and D4 shows no member beating the blend by more than 0.03 points.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Blend weights. Each arm's weights are re-chosen over all 16 Primary substations, so the D8 numbers also reflect the other 15 substations.
  • Actual values. D8 uses experiment 355's observed power, which models the meter's fold at the MVA level. The control check uses the raw observed series.
  • Scorer. The 11 quantile levels are averaged without weights, as in experiments 252 to 355. Experiment 87's mass-weighted scorer gives 9.6 for the same BG2 rows, so the two scores are not comparable.
  • One way to look further. Compare the inputs of the four non-stack members with the GAM stack's at D8.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00360-bg2-member-drop-one-at-d8/ imports experiment 87's folder (e00087_assemble.py, e00087_common.py).

docs.title: Can a plain step detector separate generator-like steps from D8's demand, and does removing them from the training target improve the GAM stack?
docs.text:
A plain step detector separates 3 MW and 4 MW generator-like spells from D8's demand most of the time, but removing the steps it finds from the training target does not improve D8's forecast.

The test does not support building a particle filter on the evidence of this detector. A detector that rejects ordinary demand swings is one option, since the rule flags nearly as many rises as falls. The verdict is not supported.

Figure A: the detector's falls and drops at D8 cover the long dips in demand in two winter weeks, and nothing in a week with no detected falls.

The three weeks start on 12 January 2026, 26 January 2026, and 22 December 2025. The first two are the non-overlapping weeks with the most detected hours (121 and 140) in the 12 months over which the forecasts are scored (2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30). The third is the week with no detected hours closest to the middle of those 12 months. The residual-median rule for choosing weeks was fixed before any chart was drawn. Detection here uses the whole record, including data after each monthly refit date. Orange shading marks falls of 6 hours or more. Purple shading marks multi-day drops. Where the two overlap, the colour is pink.

Figure B: with 2 MW and 4 MW spells injected into D2, the detector misses some spells and flags some segments that match no injected spell.

The spells are simulated and added to the power readings of D2, a primary substation (Primary) with no known generator: one random set of on/off spells for each size, spread over July 2024 to June 2025. Each panel shows 8 days. Each "missed" panel shows the earliest injected spell (orange) that has no detected half-hours, and the first 2 MW panel also shows a second spell that was only partly found. Each "false alarm" panel shows the earliest detected segment (purple) that overlaps no injected spell, on 5 July 2024. In these panels, pink marks an injected spell that was also detected.

Figure C: removing the detected steps from the training target changes D8's median forecast by under 1 MW in the weeks shown, and the score does not improve.

The lines are the median forecast, made 12 to 36 hours ahead, for the same three weeks as Figure A, from three variants of the GAM stack: the control (raw target), the variant with the detected levels added back to the training target, and the variant with the detected rows masked. The black line is the actual demand. Gaps are half-hours with no stored forecast. The lower panels show each variant's forecast minus the control forecast. In the week starting 22 December 2025, all three variants forecast negative demand on 25 and 26 December, while the readings stay positive.

Figure A and Figure C show only D8, and Figure B shows only D2. These figures illustrate the result. They do not test it. The study is interim: a detector that rejects ordinary demand swings has not been tried.

D8 is a primary substation (Primary) whose power seems to include a dispatchable generator that switches on and off. We asked whether a simple rule can find such steps in D8's power, and whether taking them out of the training target helps the forecast. We added simulated on/off spells of 2, 3, and 4 MW to three Primaries with no known generator, D2, D3, and D4, and counted how many spells the rule found again. We then refitted D8's generalised additive model (GAM) stack with the detected steps removed. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of D8's capacity (1 point is about 0.1 MW), and lower is better. The residual-median rule extends experiment 159's rule for multi-day drops (experiment 159). The stack, its refits, and the own-residual band come from experiment 354, and the gas-engine background from experiment 264, experiment 265, and experiment 291.

Figure 1: the detector finds 4 MW spells 91% of the time and 2 MW spells 55% of the time.

Figure 2: neither removal arm moves the score by more than 0.1 points.

Figure 3: the rule finds falls in every month.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Detector. The baseline of each half-hour is the median of the same half-hour on the 2 to 8 days before and after. A fall is a run of at least 6 hours in which the 6-hour centred median of the residual is at or below -1.5 MW, with gaps under 6 hours merged. A multi-day drop uses experiment 159's rule (24-hour median, gaps under 12 hours merged, at least 2 days). At a fit cut only data before the cut is seen. The drop pass was added after the first catalogue run found only 4 drops of 2 days or longer with the 6-hour rule, and before any forecast was scored.
  • Catalogue at D8 since 2023-08-15. 193 falls of at least 6 hours (median level -3.0 MW, median dwell 0.38 days) and 171 rises of the same size; 6 multi-day drops (median level -2.7 MW, median dwell 2.5 days). At 1.0 MW the counts are 273 falls and 11 drops; at 2.0 MW, 126 falls and 1 drop. Prediction P2 (25 to 40 falls and 20 to 30 drops) failed on both counts: experiment 159 found 29 drops with a different baseline.
  • Injection test. 20 draws on each of D2, D3, and D4, 2024-07 to 2025-06, with spells and gaps resampled from D8's catalogue. A spell is recovered when detected segments cover at least half of it and the segment's level is within 30% of the injected total. One component at a time: 75% (3,986 spells; 95% Wilson interval 73% to 76%); 2 MW 55%, 3 MW 83%, 4 MW 91%. Two at once: 70%. Three at once: 59%, and 43% at 2 MW. Two simultaneous 4 MW spells still reach 83%, and two simultaneous 3 MW spells reach 75%. The median start error is 0 to 1 hour (0.5 in most cells) and the median level error is within 6% of the injected level in every cell. On the uninjected hosts the same windows are recovered by chance 0.4% of the time, and the rule finds 29, 5, and 6 falls a year at D2, D3, and D4. P1 failed on its first half (75% against 80%) and held on its second.
  • Rows. 96,986 half-hourly rows at D8 in 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours (the stored ensemble forecasts stop at 168 hours), fold_a_daily_gap_v1. Intervals resample whole months at the 99% level, the Bonferroni level for two planned contrasts.
  • Arms. Monthly refits (12 fits) from 2023-09 with a level step per hour band at 2025-04-01, arm 3's own-residual band by hour block and season, the night offset and recipe R. Control: the raw target. T1: each detected segment's level added back to its rows. T0: the segment's rows masked from the fit. The detector flags 9% to 13% of training rows at the cuts checked (2024-09 and 2026-06), at a mean level of about -3.0 MW. Fit code is copied from experiment 354's e00354_fit.py with the target edit; the scripts import experiments 252, 264, and 354.
  • Gate. The control scores 8.382, as in experiment 354's fit (b).
  • Absolute scores, all rows. Control 8.382, T1 8.375, T0 8.384, BG2 7.593, manual heuristic 8.469, climatology 9.757. All three arms trail BG2.
  • C1, T1 minus control. -0.007 (99% -0.097 to +0.053), so P3 (at least -0.2) failed.
  • C2, T0 minus control. +0.001 (-0.071 to +0.054). P4 held only because masking moved the score by +0.001.
  • Post hoc slices, descriptive. On sunny daylight half-hours, T1 minus control is -0.197 (-0.699 to -0.015) and T0 minus control -0.105 (-0.526 to +0.079). On cold nights, T1 minus control is -0.100 (-0.206 to +0.274). These slices were not planned, so they do not change the verdict.
  • Tail calibration, arm 3 band. q05 to q95 coverage 0.846 (control), 0.847 (T1), 0.845 (T0). Share of readings below q01 0.039, 0.040, 0.040. Share above q99 0.029 in all three.
  • Scope. Dispatchable on/off components only; solar and wind follow the weather. Only the sum of demand and generators is observed, so components of similar size may be unidentifiable. The generator behind D8 is unproven (experiments 264, 265, 291). The result is for D8 at leads of 0.5 to 168 hours, shorter than the 10-day horizon the network operator (NGED) needs.
  • Not run. A particle filter, a production port, and a mixture band with an explicit on-probability. The removed component re-enters through the own-residual band, which is fitted on the actual power.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, points of capacity. Control -1.44, T1 -1.31, T0 -1.30.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. Mean absolute error 1.505 MW (control), 1.499 MW (T1), 1.502 MW (T0), so both measures point the same way and the difference is small.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired in part: C1 contradicts its prediction of -0.2. The explanation test shows the edit moved the median forecast by 1.17 points (0.12 MW) on average for T1, and by 1.03 points for T0, so the fit changed without improving. That pattern fits a detector whose falls are partly ordinary demand swings (171 rises for 193 falls). No Opus audit was run, because the brief excludes Opus, and no later experiment depends on this result's sign. Triggers 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Reject ordinary demand swings by requiring a fall to be matched by a rise of similar size at the end of its dwell, then repeat the injection test with that rule.
  • Test the 6 multi-day drops alone as a mask on the training target, since they are the segments most likely to be the generator.

docs.title: MVA fold: gated fit through the meter, known-answer test
docs.text:
A gate that checks fitted reverse flow against an independent solar forecast does not stop the fit through the meter from inventing reverse flow. At the registered setting the gate rejected no fit in any of 60 cases. At a stricter post hoc setting it fixed D5, the one of the five substations with no reverse flow, at the 2025 cut only, and it rejected the correct fits at four of five substations when reverse flow was heavy. Verdict: refuted. The sequence stops here.

Experiment 358 found that the model fitted through an apparent-power meter invents reverse flow at D5 when no solar output is injected. This experiment tested a gate. The fit tries six starting points. The gate rejects a start when more than 0.5% of its training half-hours have negative fitted power while the independent solar output is under a set multiple (the ratio) of the fitted demand. The independent solar output is the pinned capacity times the solar shape plus, in this lab test, the injected farm's true output. We tested the registered ratio of 0.75 and, post hoc, the ratios 1.0 and 1.25. Everything else follows experiment 358. The ungated fit (L0) reproduces experiment 358's numbers.

docs.title: Results (reactive power zero; scored cut unless stated)
docs.text:
• Registered gate (ratio 0.75) rejects nothing. It rejects 0 of 6 starts in all 60 cases, so it gives the ungated fit's answer everywhere. D5 with no injection stays at 0.35 against the signed fit's 0.98. The decision rule fails on one criterion: the gate matches the signed fit within 0.02 at 5 of 5 substations at both injection levels, but misses D5 at the natural level by 0.63.
  • Why it rejects nothing. On training half-hours the mirror fit's negative power falls where the independent solar output is at least 0.75 times the fitted demand, because true flow at midday is near zero and the independent forecast cannot tell a small positive flow from a small negative one. The invented reverse flow at D5 appears mostly on the following year's half-hours.
  • Post hoc ratio 1.0. At the scored cut it fixes D5 with no injection (accuracy 0.96, capacity 1.02 times the signed fit's) and matches the signed fit at level 1.0. It breaks level 2.0 at D11, D14, and D16 (accuracy 0.05 to 0.06 against 0.94 to 0.96, capacity 0.18 to 0.26 times the signed fit's), because the correct starts are rejected. At the 2024 cut it does not fix D5 (0.49, with every start rejected) and also breaks level 2.0 at D10, D14, and D16.
  • Ratio 1.25. It breaks level 1.0 at D11, D14, and D5 and level 2.0 at all but D11 at the scored cut.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers. Audit trigger 1 (a control fails: the D5 placebo) and trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction) fired. The explanation tested is that the invented reverse flow appears on half-hours after the fit was made, not on its training half-hours. A fresh Sonnet auditor found the gate code a faithful copy of the ungated fit apart from the rejection step, found the units right, and reproduced experiment 358's D5 numbers. It found no bug behind the null at 0.75: a start is rejected only when its fitted solar exceeds about 1.33 times the independent solar, and the wrong D5 starts overshoot by only about 1.2 times. It also noted that clipping the forecast power at zero cannot change a sign accuracy, so the clip is inert here.
  • Median against mean forecast. Not applicable: the forecasts are single values from frozen fits.
  • Departures. Ratios 1.0 and 1.25 are post hoc. The audit used Sonnet because the series brief requires Sonnet only.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The gate reads the injected farm's true output, an advantage a real substation lacks, and it still failed.
  • One farm shape (A) supplies the injected output.
  • Try a rule on the meter readings alone: accept reverse flow only if the training readings come within a few percent of capacity of zero at midday. The brief's measurement says only Stickney (D12), Langrick (D22), and Marsh Lane (D8) do.

docs.title: Can a penalised level term for each stretch between detected steps let the GAM stack explain D8's steps instead of masking them?
docs.text:
Giving the forecast for D8 a separate level for each stretch between detected steps made the quantile score worse, from 8.382 to 8.674 points at the middle penalty strength.

D8 is a primary substation (Primary) whose power seems to include a dispatchable generator that switches on and off. A step is a rise or fall of at least 1.5 MW in D8's power found by experiment 361's detector, and a stretch is the run of half-hours between two such steps. We gave each stretch its own level, shrunk towards zero by a ridge penalty, and tried three penalty strengths. The weakest penalty scored worst (8.800) and the strongest scored nearest to the control (8.545), where the control is experiment 354's forecast without the stretch levels. Of the three strengths tried, none beat the control. The verdict is not supported. The criterion was a fall of at least 0.2 points with a 99% interval wholly below zero, and a stop rule ended the experiment if the middle penalty did not beat masking the steps.

Experiment 361 removed or masked the steps in the training target, and the score did not move. We asked a different question: if every training row is kept and each stretch gets its own level, can the weather and calendar terms be estimated inside stretches? We refitted experiment 354's best generalised additive model (GAM) stack monthly with the new columns and scored one year of forecasts. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of D8's capacity (1 point is about 0.1 MW), and lower is better. The penalised level for each group of rows is a random-effect design, and the step detector is experiment 361's.

Figure 1: every segment-term arm scores worse than the control, and the masking arm scores the same.

Figure 2: the segment term is worse in every lead band and on days with and without detected steps.

Figure 3: the segment term raises the score at both Primaries that have no engine.

Figure 4: the segment term changes the fitted solar-capacity and seasonal terms most at D8.

Figure 5: in the fortnight with the most detected steps, the median forecasts of the control and of the middle-penalty segment term follow the same shape.

Headline caveat for every number: interim, one substation plus two placebo Primaries, one scored year; the detector recovers 55% of 2 MW and 91% of 4 MW injections and flags ordinary demand swings; the generator behind D8 is unproven. Lead range: 0 to 168 hours, not the full 1 to 10 days NGED care about.

  • Arms. C: experiment 354's fit (b) (monthly refit at 12 stored cuts, history from 2023-09, one level step per hour band at 2025-04-01), refitted here. M: experiment 361's masking arm, read from its stored forecasts. S: C plus one ridge-penalised level for each stretch between the starts and ends of segments found by experiment 361's step and multi-day-drop rules on power up to the cut, with the ridge at 0.1, 1, and 10 times the interaction penalty's scale (weak, middle, strong). At forecast time every row after a cut takes the latest stretch's level, so no future data enter; the level can be one refit period old. All frames are stage d with experiment 354's arm-3 band.
  • Row set. 96,986 rows (fold_a_daily_gap_v1, the rows of experiment 354). Gate passed: C scores 8.382. Stage 2 and the filter are experiment 252's, unchanged.
  • Scores (all rows). C 8.382, M 8.384, S weak 8.800, S middle 8.674, S strong 8.545; BG2 7.593, manual_heuristic 8.469, climatology 9.757.
  • C1 (S middle minus C). +0.291 points (99% interval +0.096 to +0.538); the pre-registered threshold was at most -0.2. 2026 only: +0.188 (-0.003 to +0.385).
  • C2 (S middle minus M). +0.290 points (99% interval +0.118 to +0.510). S does not beat M, so the stop rule fired.
  • By lead band (S middle minus C). Up to 12 h +0.162 (-0.010 to +0.333); 12 to 36 h +0.187 (+0.012 to +0.373); 36 to 72 h +0.318 (+0.109 to +0.572); over 72 h +0.324 (+0.113 to +0.605).
  • By day type (S middle minus C). Days with a detected step (hindsight detection, 16,350 rows) +0.486 (-0.125 to +1.157); days without (80,636 rows) +0.252 (+0.012 to +0.474).
  • MAE, correlation, bias (mean forecast). MAE 1.505 MW (C), 1.502 (M), 1.551 (S middle); correlation with readings 0.459, 0.460, 0.436; bias +0.035, +0.041, +0.048 MW.
  • Placebos (S middle minus C). D2 2.114 to 2.248, +0.134 points (+6.3%; 99% interval +0.038 to +0.243); D4 2.457 to 2.618, +0.161 points (+6.6%; +0.044 to +0.322). Both exceed the +3% limit.
  • Tail calibration (D8, all rows). Readings below q01: C 3.9%, S middle 4.4%; above q99: C 2.9%, S middle 3.4%; inside q05 to q95: C 84.6%, S middle 83.7%.
  • S+ (arm S widened in the upper quantiles by the chance that the generator switches back) was not tested. The stop rule applies. In addition, S+ could never have applied: the detector cannot see a fall still in progress at the cut, so the latest stretch before each of the 12 cuts always counted as a normal stretch and the widening reached 0 rows. The share of training rows inside detected falls was 9.2% to 9.8% (median depth 28.5 points, about 2.9 MW).
  • Clean-Primary check. At D2 (345 stretches, level standard deviation 1.7 points) the middle penalty changes the fitted heating coefficients by 16%, the solar-capacity coefficients by 23%, and the seasonal harmonics by 31% (relative norm of the difference); at D8 (380 stretches, standard deviation 12.7 points) by 29%, 74%, and 67%. So the segment term takes over work from the weather terms, including at a Primary with no engine.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast: C -1.44 points, S middle -1.20. Mean-forecast MAE agrees in direction with the quantile score (S worse). Two of the seven audit triggers fired: the result contradicts its prediction with the explanation below untested, and the weakest-penalty arm, which contains the control, scores worse than the control (an infinitely strong penalty would reproduce the control).
  • Audit. A Sonnet audit re-derived the headline contrast and checked for leakage; the PR records its findings and their triage.
  • Untested explanation. The most likely cause is that the latest stretch's level, fitted from at most one month of rows and carried forward for up to a month, is a noisy guess. Setting the forecast level from a short moving window instead was not tried.
  • What to try next. A state estimate at forecast time (the filter in experiment 252 already assimilates recent power) or a live signal for the generator, rather than a fitted past level. No further level-term variants.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00363-d8-segment-level-term-in-the-gam-stack/; imports experiments 252, 264, 354, and 361. Schedule: monthly refits (the same cuts as the control), so the contrast does not depend on a cheaper schedule.

docs.title: Which stage of the GAM stack loses skill at D8 against BG2's members, and does the analogue member win because it sees recent power?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the Kalman filter's short-lived correction hurts D8's forecast at leads under 24 hours, the other correction stages do not, and recent power explains about a third of the analogue member's lead.

This experiment asked where the GAM stack loses skill at the substation D8 (Marsh Lane, a primary substation) against BG2, and whether BG2's analogue member wins because it sees recent power. The analogue member is one of BG2's five members (weekly XGBoost, monthly XGBoost, analogue, pooled by substation type, and an XGBoost stack). XGBoost is a gradient-boosted decision tree method. The analogue member adds the mean and median of the demand at the same time of day on the six previous weeks, and three "origin lags": demand observed shortly before the forecast was issued. The GAM stack is Primary demand research default 1: a GAM, a Kalman filter on recent errors (a slowly moving "level" and a short-lived "transient"), a winter night offset, recipe R (subtract 0.75 times the last 14 days' mean error by half-hour), and an uncertainty band fitted on D8's own past errors (the "own-residual band"). BG2 is the blend of five forecasts described in experiment 87. We read each stage's stored forecast from experiments 354 and 355, scored each stage and each BG2 member on the same 96,986 half-hourly rows, and refitted the analogue member twice with its recent-power inputs removed. Scores are the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of D8's 10.38 MW capacity; lower is better), the mean absolute error (MAE) of the median in MW, the bias (forecast minus actual) in MW, and the Pearson correlation of the median with the actual demand.

Over all leads, no stage adds more than 0.1 points of score: the plain GAM with the Kalman level scores 8.146 and the full stack 8.338, against 7.472 for the analogue member. At leads of 0 to 24 hours the Kalman transient adds 0.444 points. Removing recent power from the analogue member raises its score from 7.472 to 7.761. The verdict is partly supported: one stage (the Kalman transient, at 0 to 24 hours) meets the blame rule, and the analogue refit stayed below the predicted 8.0.

Caveat. This result is interim: it covers one substation and one scored year. Whether a generator sits behind D8 is unproven (experiments 264, 265, and 291). The lead range is 0 to 168 hours, so the full 1-to-10-day horizon is not covered. The stages use weekly refits (monthly refits give the same pattern for S1 to S4).

docs.title: Arms and numbers (D8, weekly refits, 96,986 rows)
docs.text:
• Stages (each scored with the own-residual band built from that stage's own median): S0 the plain GAM; S1 plus the Kalman level; S2 plus the Kalman transient; S3 plus the winter night offset; S4 plus recipe R (the GAM stack). The stage medians come from stored columns (mean - level - anomaly, mean - anomaly, mean) and experiment 252's stage-2 arms.
  • Gate: S4 scores 8.338 (monthly refits 8.382) and BG2 reblends to 7.593, as stored.
  • Score (95% interval, whole valid months resampled): S0 8.358 (7.596 to 9.256); S1 8.146 (7.411 to 9.004); S2 8.242 (7.492 to 9.125); S3 8.271 (7.518 to 9.150); S4 8.338 (7.575 to 9.251); weekly XGBoost 7.560; monthly XGBoost 7.694; analogue 7.472 (6.882 to 8.052); pooled by type 7.633; XGBoost stack 8.562; BG2 7.593.
  • Stage contrasts (score): S1 minus S0 -0.212 (-0.526 to +0.051); S2 minus S1 +0.096 (+0.041 to +0.159); S3 minus S2 +0.029 (+0.006 to +0.053); S4 minus S3 +0.067 (-0.014 to +0.167); S4 minus S0 -0.020 (-0.339 to +0.249). The own-residual band lowers the score by 2.046 (-2.609 to -1.516) against the stored band.
  • Stage contrasts by lead band (score, 95% interval): S2 minus S1 is +0.444 (+0.277 to +0.641) at 0 to 24 h, +0.079 (+0.015 to +0.150) at 24 to 72 h, and +0.017 (-0.018 to +0.061) at 72 to 168 h. At 0 to 24 h the correlation falls by 0.036 (-0.059 to -0.013) and the MAE rises by 0.054 MW (+0.029 to +0.082). S1 minus S0 is -0.326 (-0.599 to -0.116) at 0 to 24 h. S4 minus S3 is +0.088 (-0.007 to +0.208) at 72 to 168 h.
  • Recent power by lead band: removing it raises the analogue score by +0.354 (+0.175 to +0.574) at 0 to 24 h, +0.323 (+0.143 to +0.548) at 24 to 72 h, and +0.255 (+0.060 to +0.503) at 72 to 168 h. The analogue refit without recent power scores 7.761, worse than monthly XGBoost's 7.694, which keeps the origin lags and has no analogue columns.
  • Correlation: 0.454 (S0), 0.465 (S1), 0.460 (S2), 0.461 (S3), 0.462 (S4), 0.473 (analogue), 0.465 (BG2). The largest fall, S2 minus S1, is -0.0056 (-0.0142 to +0.0031) over all rows and -0.0082 (-0.0146 to -0.0029) on days without detected steps. On days with steps it is -0.0019 (-0.0173 to +0.0131). The prediction that a stage lowers correlation only on step days failed.
  • Bias and error: bias -0.321 MW (S0), -0.071 (S1), -0.107 (S4), +0.176 (analogue). MAE 1.526 MW (S0), 1.486 (S1), 1.503 (S4), 1.408 (analogue). Over all rows the analogue member's MAE is 0.094 MW below S4's (-0.160 to -0.017).
  • By lead band (score): S1 7.95, S4 8.45, analogue 7.35 at 0 to 24 h; S4 8.23 and analogue 7.37 at 24 to 72 h; S4 8.36 and analogue 7.56 at 72 to 168 h.
  • By detected-step days (experiment 361's detector): S4 9.92 and analogue 8.82 on step days; S4 7.42 and analogue 6.69 on days without. The stack trails the analogue by 1.10 and 0.73 points.
  • Analogue refits (monthly refits at D8, experiment 87's recipe, same seed; the unchanged refit reproduces the stored 7.472):
Arm Score Minus unchanged refit Unchanged 7.472 (6.881 to 8.052) 0 Without the three origin lags 7.641 (7.015 to 8.258) +0.168 (+0.063 to +0.296) Without origin lags or analogue power from the last 7 days 7.761 (7.066 to 8.474) +0.289 (+0.103 to +0.525) Monthly XGBoost (no analogue columns, origin lags kept) 7.694 (7.003 to 8.413) +0.222 (+0.086 to +0.425)

Without recent power the analogue member still beats the stack by 0.58 points; recent power accounts for about a third of the analogue member's 0.866-point lead (+0.289 of 0.866). - Other substations D2 and D4, where no effect is expected (monthly refits, stored spread offsets): at D2 the Kalman level lowers the score by 0.292 (S1 minus S0, -0.437 to -0.149) and the stages together from 2.437 to 2.079 (S4 minus S0 -0.359, -0.502 to -0.213), at D4 from 2.504 to 2.294 (-0.210, -0.476 to +0.056). Prediction 3 (no stage moves D2 or D4 by more than 0.1) failed at D2. - Tails (D8): q05 to q95 coverage 0.847 (S4), 0.925 (analogue), 0.904 (BG2); share below q01 0.038 (S4), 0.004 (analogue); pinball at q99 0.648 (S4), 0.469 (analogue). The stack's own-residual band is too narrow at both ends. - Curtailment cost: not scored; this experiment compares medians and bands at one substation.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. The stages' own-residual band moves the median off the stage's mean forecast by 1.37 points on average for S4 (1.24 for S1, 2.14 for S0), because the band's median residual is added. The members' mean equals their median. The shift is the same rule for every stage, so it does not favour one stage.
  • Error of the median beside the score contrasts. The score and MAE contrasts agree in direction at every stage (S2 minus S1: score +0.096, MAE +0.009 MW), so audit trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 2 fired: predictions 1, 2, and 3 failed. The explanation that the lead sits in the XGBoost members' inputs and not in recent power is supported by the monthly-XGBoost row of the analogue table. Trigger 5 fired: the plain GAM with the Kalman level (S1) beats the stack (S4) that contains it. Triggers 1, 3, 4 (not applicable to one substation), 6, and 7 did not fire. A separate audit re-derived the headline scores, contrasts, and correlations from the stored frame with its own code and found them correct. Its findings on wording are applied here.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Stage medians come from stored columns. The plain-GAM median is mean - level - anomaly of the stored base frame, and the step-day flag uses experiment 361's detector over the whole record, so step days are hindsight labels.
  • Analogue refits. Without the origin lags the lag columns are NaN in training and prediction. Recent power in the "no recent power" arm means all power newer than 7 days before the origin. The XGBoost members' weather inputs are unchanged.
  • Next: compare the weather and calendar inputs of the XGBoost members with the GAM's at D8, then test the best of them inside the GAM.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00364-d8-stage-blame-and-analogue-recent-power/ imports the folders of experiments 87, 252, 264, 354, and 361. Printed numbers: printed_report.txt, printed_checks.txt.

docs.title: MVA fold: reverse-flow rule on the meter readings alone
docs.text:
A rule that looks for sunny-midday meter readings near zero does not reliably separate reverse flow from none. The rule still picks the wrong fit at D5, the test substation with no reverse flow, because D5's readings also dip towards zero. The rule also misses heavy reverse flow. Heavy reverse flow gives large readings, not small ones, so the rule picks the naive fit at all 8 MVA-only Primaries (the eight substations that report only apparent power, in MVA), including Stickney (D12). Verdict: partly supported, because the registered pass test is met, but only because it allows one substation in five to be wrong. The three further planned steps of the MVA sequence (named in experiment 358's series brief) are paused for a decision.

Experiment 362 found that an independent solar forecast cannot tell invented reverse flow from real. This experiment tested a rule that uses only the meter readings in the training years. The rule takes the training half-hours from April to September that start 10:00 to 13:30 UTC with irradiance of at least 500 W/m². If the 1st percentile of the meter readings on those half-hours is below 5 percentage points of capacity, the rule uses the fit through the meter (L0). Otherwise the rule uses the naive fit (N), which reads the magnitude as signed power. No model was refitted: the score of each case is the stored score of the fit the rule chooses, from experiment 358, which also defines the injection levels and the signed fit (S) used for comparison.

docs.title: Results (reactive power zero)
docs.text:
• Registered pass test. At the 2025 cut, the chosen fit's direction accuracy on sunny half-hours is within 0.02 of the signed fit's at 4 of 5 substations with no injection, and at 5 of 5 at levels 1.0 and 2.0. At the 2024 cut the counts are 4, 4, and 5. The test passes.
  • D5 with no injection still fails. The statistic is 3.79 at the 2025 cut and 2.88 at the 2024 cut, both under 5, so the rule chooses L0. L0's accuracy is 0.35 against the signed fit's 0.98.
  • Census, not scored. The statistic is 26.7 at Stickney (D12), 7.6 at Langrick (D22), and 5.9 at Marsh Lane (D8), and 22 to 40 at the other 5 (D2, D3, D4, D19, D21). All 8 exceed 5, so the rule chooses the naive fit everywhere, including at D12, where experiment 110 fitted reverse flow on 96 to 97% of summer midday half-hours. The prediction that the rule would pick L0 at D12 failed.
  • Power factor 0.97. With reactive power at power factor 0.97 in the data, the rule still chooses L0, which collapses at levels 1.0 and 2.0 (0 of 5 substations within 0.02), as in experiment 358.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers. Audit triggers 1 (a failed control: D5) and 2 (a result contradicting its prediction: the census) of the ml-experiment skill fired. The explanation is stated above and follows from the readings, so no separate audit was run: the experiment refits nothing and reads two stored result sets.
  • Median against mean forecast. Not applicable: no forecasts were made.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The 1st percentile and the threshold of 5 were fixed before any statistic was computed.
  • The census statistic uses the metered reading at the MVA-only Primaries, so a reading changed by generation added to the magnitude (the Marsh Lane change in April 2025) would also move it.
  • Next idea: test whether the sunny-midday reading rises or falls with irradiance. The design brief measured a positive correlation of +0.75 to +0.83 at Stickney and a negative one at the other MVA-only Primaries. Not tested here.

docs.title: MVA fold: reverse-flow rule from the correlation with irradiance
docs.text:
A rule that checks two things on the training sunny-midday meter readings picks the right fit at every case the registered test scores, but it breaks as soon as the readings include reactive power. We asked whether the 8 MVA-only Primaries (the eight substations that report only apparent power, in MVA) can be told apart from substations with no reverse flow, using the meter readings and the irradiance alone. The rule picks the fit through the meter (L0, which can see reverse flow) if the readings rise with irradiance (Pearson correlation above +0.3) or the lowest readings come close to zero (1st percentile below 1.0 percentage point of capacity). Otherwise the rule picks the naive fit (N), which reads the magnitude as signed power. With reactive power zero, the rule is right at D5 (the substation with no reverse flow), at the five injected cases, and at Stickney (D12). It picks the naive fit at the other seven MVA-only Primaries. With reactive power at power factor 0.97, the rule fails at moderate injected solar. Verdict: partly supported. The registered pass test, which uses reactive power zero, passes in full. The unregistered check at power factor 0.97 fails, and the verdict word reflects that check.

This follows experiment 365, whose rule on the lowest readings alone failed at D5 and at Stickney, and which proposed testing how the readings move with irradiance. No model was refitted: the score of each case is the stored score of the fit the rule chooses, from experiment 358, which defines the injection levels and the signed fit (S) used for comparison. The code reuses the way experiment 365 builds the readings. The rule and both thresholds were written into result.md before any statistic was computed. The threshold of 1.0 on the 1st percentile was chosen after seeing the numbers of experiment 365 (D5's 1st percentile was 3.79 and the injected cases' were 0.2 to 1.6), so it is not an out-of-sample test. The injected cases are also a weak test of the percentile condition. With reactive power zero the reading is the absolute value of the signed flow, so any substation given enough injected reverse flow has a 1st percentile near zero, and the percentile test passes at the level 1.0 cases by construction. D5 at level 1.0 also has a natural correlation above +0.3 (+0.34 at the 2025 cut and +0.47 at the 2024 cut). All five injected substations also receive the same recorded solar-farm output (farm A), so the five injected cases are not independent evidence of how the rule behaves on other farms. The correlation threshold of +0.3 comes from the design brief's measurements.

Figure 3 shows the failure: at power factor 0.97 every injected case at level 1.0 has a 1st percentile of 11 to 17 and a correlation of +0.28 or lower (the highest is D5), so both dashed thresholds are missed at the 2025 cut.

docs.title: Results (reactive power zero, plain direction accuracy on sunny half-hours)
docs.text:
• D5, no injection: passes. The statistics are a correlation of -0.28 and a 1st percentile of 3.79 (2025 cut), so the rule chooses N. Accuracy is 0.980, the same as the signed fit's 0.980. At the 2024 cut the chosen accuracy is 0.963 against 0.961. Experiment 365's threshold of 5 chose L0 here, with accuracy 0.35.
  • Injected cases: pass. At the 2025 cut the chosen fit is within 0.02 of the signed fit at 5 of 5 substations at both levels. At the 2024 cut the counts are 4 of 5 at level 1.0 (D11, gap 0.026) and 5 of 5 at level 2.0. The rule chooses L0 at all 5 substations in every injected case. At level 2.0, where 92 to 99% of sunny half-hours have reverse flow, the chosen accuracy equals the signed fit's at every substation (0.94 to 0.99).
  • Which test carries which case. At level 2.0 the correlation exceeds +0.3 at 5 of 5 substations at both cuts. At level 1.0 the correlation exceeds +0.3 at 1 of 5 (D5), so the 1st percentile below 1.0 chooses L0 at the other four. The correlation alone would miss four of the five level 1.0 cases.
  • The yardstick is weak without reverse flow. Plain accuracy against the signed fit is near 1.0 wherever almost no half-hours reverse, so D11, D14, D16 and (at no injection) D5 pass trivially. The accuracy on only the sunny half-hours with true reverse flow is more telling. At level 1.0 and the 2025 cut the mean over the 5 substations is 0.90 for the signed fit and 0.91 for the chosen fit (0.31 for N), and at the 2024 cut 0.955 and 0.951 (0.545 for N). At level 2.0 it is 1.00 for the signed and chosen fits and 0.00 for N at both cuts. At power factor 0.97 the chosen fit's mean falls to 0.008 (2025 cut) and 0.22 (2024 cut) at level 1.0.
  • No injection, other substations. D10 has genuine reverse flow in 14% of sunny half-hours, and the rule chooses L0 (1st percentile 0.28) with the same accuracy as the signed fit. D11, D14, and D16 have none, and the rule chooses N.
  • Census, not scored. The rule chooses L0 at Stickney (D12), with correlation +0.55 and 1st percentile 26.7. The choice of L0 matches the prediction, but the registered prediction of a correlation of about +0.75 to +0.83 at D12 missed: the correlation is +0.55. The rule chooses N at D2, D3, D4, D8, D19, D21, and D22, whose correlations are -0.54 to -0.04 and whose 1st percentiles are 5.87 to 40.25. Marsh Lane (D8) and Langrick (D22) are the closest calls on the 1st percentile (5.87 and 7.55) and stay with N. D12 is the only one of the eight with a positive correlation.
  • Power factor 0.97: fails. With reactive power at power factor 0.97 in the readings, the readings stay well above zero (1st percentile 10.7 to 37.6 with no injection, and 11.0 to 17.4 at level 1.0). At level 1.0 the rule picks N at 5 of 5 substations at the 2025 cut and 4 of 5 at the 2024 cut. The mean chosen accuracy is 0.31 (2025 cut) and 0.52 (2024 cut), against the signed fit's 0.86 and 0.81. The number of substations within 0.02 is 0 of 5 (2025 cut) and 1 of 5 (2024 cut) at level 1.0, and 5 of 5 at level 2.0. With no injection, D10 at the 2025 cut is 0.042 below the signed fit. This repeats experiment 358's finding for the fit through the meter.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers. Trigger 7 of the ml-experiment skill may apply, because the planned next steps of the MVA sequence depend on this result. No audit was run, because the experiment refits nothing and reads two stored result sets, and this session started no sub-agents. The maintainer decides whether to order one. Trigger 1 (a failed control) did not fire at reactive power zero, and fired at power factor 0.97, where the rule fails at level 1.0 as the earlier experiments did.
  • Median against mean forecast. Not applicable: no forecasts were made.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The pass test covers only reactive power zero. The earlier experiments of the sequence found that real readings contain reactive power. If the sequence continues, the next step is a rule that still works at power factor 0.97, for example one that corrects each reading for an estimated reactive power before computing the statistics.
  • The 1.0 threshold was informed by experiment 365, as stated above.
  • The census statistic uses the metered reading at the MVA-only Primaries, so a reading changed by generation added to the magnitude (the Marsh Lane change in April 2025) also moves it.
  • The census has no ground truth: the claim that D12 has reverse flow and the other seven do not comes from experiment 110 and the design brief, not from a signed measurement.

docs.title: Does switching the Kalman transient off, or scaling it by the substation's own recent benefit, recover the short-lead skill it costs at D8?
docs.text:
Plan (committed before any score was read).

This experiment extends experiment 364, which found that the Kalman filter's short-lived correction (the "transient") adds 0.444 points of quantile score at D8 at leads of 0 to 24 hours. The experiment asks whether turning the transient off, or scaling it by how much it has helped that substation recently, removes that loss without hurting other substations. The Kalman level and transient follow the idea of a Kalman filter on a generalised additive model's coefficients; see the Kalman-GAM explainer.

The five plan items:

  1. Arms (no refit, scored from the stage columns stored by experiment 364).
    • Control: stage S4, the stored stack.
    • K0: the transient is removed at leads up to 24 hours. At stage level K0 equals S1 (the plain GAM plus the Kalman level) at those leads and S2 elsewhere. At stack level K0 is S4 minus the transient (S2 minus S1) and its quantiles move with it. The stack-level form assumes the winter night offset and recipe R add the same amounts without the transient (post hoc approximation, labelled as such).
    • KA: as K0 at leads up to 24 hours, but the transient is multiplied by a gain g. For each forecast run, g is the trailing 90-day mean of (|error of S1| minus |error of S2|) over rows with lead up to 24 hours whose valid time is at or before the run's forecast initialisation time, divided by the trailing mean absolute size of the transient, clipped to between zero and one. Until 672 such rows (14 days of half-hours) exist, g is 1 (the control). The same rule applies at every substation. Beyond 24 hours the transient is untouched, because experiment 364 found it neutral or helpful there.
  2. Row set and sites. The 96,986 D8 rows of experiment 354 (weekly stage columns), plus D2 and D4 (monthly stage columns) as placebos. The six decision Primaries are scored only if stage columns for them are stored in the same layout. Otherwise the page says they were not run.
  3. Scores. Quantile score and Pearson correlation by lead band, each with a month-resampled 95% interval, plus day types as numbers: days touched by a detected step, other days, cold winter nights, sunny April to June half-hours. Also tail calibration (coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, q99).
  4. Prediction that can fail. KA recovers at least 0.2 of the 0.444 points at D8 at 0 to 24 hours and is within 0.02 of the control at D2 and D4.
  5. Stop rule. If KA is worse than the control at D2 or D4 by more than 0.05, report K0 only and stop.

Caveat on every headline number: interim, one substation, one scored year; it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap. The aim is better uncertainty estimation at D8 without hurting other substations. Schedule: weekly refits at D8 and monthly at D2 and D4, as stored.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Take-home message: the Kalman transient costs D8 about 0.4 points at leads under 24 hours and turning it off recovers that, but it hurts D4, so a rule that decides per substation is needed, and our first rule is not good enough. Experiment 364 found that the Kalman filter's short-lived correction (the "transient") raises D8's quantile score at leads of 0 to 24 hours. We re-scored the stored forecasts with the transient removed up to 24 hours (arm K0), and with the transient scaled by a gain computed from each substation's own trailing 90 days of benefit (arm KA). No model was refitted. The verdict is partly supported: the D8 prediction holds and the placebo prediction fails, so the stop rule applies and KA is not recommended. The six decision Primaries were not scored, because no stage columns are stored for them in this layout.

Terms. D8, D2, and D4 are three Primary substations. D8 is the substation of interest, and D2 and D4 are placebos: substations where the experiment must not make the forecast worse. S1 is the plain GAM plus the Kalman level, S2 adds the Kalman transient, and S4 is the stored stack, which adds a winter night offset and recipe R (a subtraction of the recent mean error) after S2. The six decision Primaries are the six substations that experiment 252 used to judge the stack. A score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of the substation's effective capacity.

Caveat. The result is interim: the headline covers one substation (D8) and one scored year (2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, 96,986 rows at D8). It is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap. The gain rule assumes each row's actual demand is known when the run is issued, with no publication delay. D8 uses weekly refits, D2 and D4 use monthly refits, as stored. Lead range 0 to 168 hours, not the full 1-to-10-day horizon.

  • Arms. Control is the stored stack (stage S4). K0 and KA at stack level shift all 11 quantiles of S4 by the removed part of the transient (an approximation: the winter night offset and recipe R are not refitted). Arm K0 is reported in full beside KA because K0 is the clearer result at D8; the stop rule stops further KA work, not the report. Stage-level versions (K0_stage, KA_stage) apply the same change to S2 and are in scores.json. The gain rule and the 14-day cold start are in the plan above.
  • Reproduction gate. The control reproduces the stored stack's per-row score (maximum absolute difference 0.0) and the mean 8.338 at D8.
  • Quantile score at 0 to 24 hours, arm minus control (95% interval).
    • D8: K0 -0.394 (-0.566 to -0.244); KA -0.310 (-0.428 to -0.195). Absolute: control 8.451, K0 8.058, KA 8.142. Mean KA gain at those leads is 0.048.
    • D2: K0 -0.038 (-0.074 to -0.001); KA -0.041 (-0.076 to -0.007). Absolute: control 1.804.
    • D4: K0 +0.136 (+0.029 to +0.242); KA +0.096 (+0.007 to +0.187). Absolute: control 1.822.
  • All leads, arm minus control. D8: K0 -0.057 (-0.083 to -0.035), KA -0.045 (-0.061 to -0.028). D2: K0 -0.005, KA -0.006. D4: K0 +0.020 (+0.004 to +0.035), KA +0.014 (+0.001 to +0.027); KA is within the 0.02 predicted. Both arms change nothing beyond 24 hours by construction.
  • Pearson correlation of the median with the actual demand, 0 to 24 hours, arm minus control. D8: K0 +0.035 (+0.015 to +0.053), KA +0.027 (+0.010 to +0.044). D4: K0 -0.012, KA -0.008.
  • Day types at D8, KA minus control. Step days -0.044 (-0.063 to -0.026), other days -0.045, cold winter nights -0.235 (-0.547 to -0.073, 2,315 rows), sunny April to June -0.023 (-0.051 to -0.006). On those two slices KA equals K0 because the gain is 0 there; the winter-night figure is a small slice.
  • Prediction. KA recovers 0.310 of the 0.444 at D8 (predicted at least 0.2): met. KA is better than the control at D2: met. KA is worse at D4 by 0.096 at 0 to 24 hours (predicted within 0.02): failed, and the stop rule (worse than control by more than 0.05) fires.
  • Tails at D8, 0 to 24 hours (control, K0, KA). q01 coverage 0.040, 0.037, 0.038 and pinball 0.842, 0.738, 0.814; q99 coverage 0.965, 0.970, 0.972 and pinball 0.754, 0.700, 0.706. q05 and q95 pinball also fall (2.326, 2.160, 2.241; 2.196, 2.090, 2.093). Coverage stays inside 0.04 of nominal.
  • Checks. The median minus the mean forecast of S4 is -1.37 points at D8 and 0.0 at D2 and D4; the stored mean is the stage-2 mean, before the night offset and recipe R, so the D8 gap is those two corrections. The mean absolute error of the mean forecast moves the same way as the quantile score for K0 at 0 to 24 hours (D8 -0.558, D2 -0.044, D4 +0.205). No audit trigger fired: no control failed, the result agrees with experiment 364, the two error measures agree in sign, and no leave-one-out check applies to a single substation. The experiment has not been replicated at the six decision Primaries, which keeps the K0 sign at D8 provisional.
  • Why KA falls short at D4. The gain is the trailing benefit divided by the transient's trailing size, which stays small even for a helpful transient, so KA removes most of it at D4 (mean gain 0.19). A faster or differently normalised rule is untested (post hoc idea, not run).
  • What to try next. Test a gain rule with a shorter window or a different normalisation, scored at D8, D2, D4, and the six decision Primaries together; add stage columns for those Primaries first.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00367-d8-kalman-transient-off-and-adaptive-short-lead/ (e00367_score.py, e00367_charts.py, e00367_checks.py), reading the stage columns stored by experiment 364.

docs.title: Does one forecast-band head, fitted on the GAM stack's own residuals and pooled across Primaries, improve D8's uncertainty without hurting other Primaries?
docs.text:
A band head fitted on all eight Primaries' residuals closes only 22% of the control's gap to BG2 at D8, so the band is not where most of D8's gap lies.

D8 is a primary substation whose forecast band, in experiment 354, was rebuilt from D8's own past errors. The rebuilt band cut D8's score but raised D2's by 5.5% and D4's by 6.1% (experiment 354's arm 2). We fitted one band head on the stored forecasts' residuals at eight Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22), refitted every month on readings that had arrived, and conditioned it on lead, hour, weather, the site, and the stack's recent residuals. The XGBoost head lowered D8's score by 0.18 points beyond the control, 22% of the 0.79-point gap to BG2, against a target of 50%. The stop rule (under 25%) applies, so band work stops. The verdict is not supported. The method follows experiment 354, experiment 311 (mixture density network head), and experiment 240 (XGBoost quantile offsets), with Koenker and Bassett (1978)'s quantile loss for the XGBoost head.

Figure 1: the XGBoost head closes 22% of the control's gap to BG2 at D8.

Figure 2: the mixture head leaves the other Primaries unchanged or slightly better.

Figure 3: the heads' lower score comes with more readings beyond q01 and q05 at D8.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. Control: experiment 354's arm 3 on the stack's fit b monthly (D8) and the stored donated band (other Primaries). Arm X: XGBoost multi-quantile offsets around the stored median (200 trees, depth 5, no column subsampling). Arm M: a three-component Gaussian mixture density network (two hidden layers of 64). Placebos: the same heads fitted on features permuted across rows. No arm changes the median. Code: ml-experiments/00368-*/, importing experiments 252, 264, and 354.
  • Terms. D8 and the other Primaries are primary substations. BG2 is the production-style forecast. The stack is a generalised additive model of demand with a Kalman filter on recent errors. The control is experiment 354's band built from D8's own residuals by hour block and season. A band head is a model that predicts the 11 forecast quantiles from the stored median. Scores are in points of the substation's effective capacity.
  • Rows and fits. 96,986 rows at D8 (fold_a_daily_gap_v1, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30). Fits refit on the first of each month from 2025-08-01 on rows read before that date (months of data: 1 to 11), at all leads; rows before the first fit keep the stored band. Monthly refits, a 300,000-row subsample per fit. Three lab shortcuts apply: the forecasts are stored ones, readings are assumed to arrive 6 hours late, and the horizon is 0.5 to 168 hours (NGED needs 1 to 10 days).
  • Gate. The control reproduces 8.382 at D8.
  • Absolute scores at D8, all rows. Stored 10.428, control 8.382, XGBoost head 8.205, mixture head 8.456, shuffled-feature placebos 8.466 (XGBoost) and 8.461 (mixture), BG2 7.593, manual heuristic 8.469, climatology 9.757. Over the seven other Primaries the mean score is 3.174 (stored), 3.159 (control rule), 3.203 (X), and 3.094 (M).
  • Planned contrasts (99% intervals). C1, X minus control at D8: -0.177 (-0.276 to -0.083), fails the -0.41 threshold. C2, X minus stored at D2: +0.073 (+0.019 to +0.126), +3.5%, fails the 3% limit. C3, D4: +0.029 (-0.085 to +0.114), +1.3%. C4, pooled over the seven: +0.030 (-0.052 to +0.108), fails the +0.02 limit. Mixture head: C1 +0.074 (+0.018 to +0.164), C2 -0.007, C3 -0.001, C4 -0.080 (-0.161 to -0.007).
  • Placebo. Each head is refitted with its training features shuffled among rows of the same site and valid month. At D8 the XGBoost placebo scores 8.466 against 8.205 for the real head, so that placebo passes (the real head is 0.26 better). The mixture placebo scores 8.461 against 8.456, within the 0.05 limit, so the mixture head's conditioning adds nothing measurable at D8 and its placebo fails. The stop rule's placebo clause therefore also applies. An earlier placebo that shuffled rows across sites scored 9.42, because it removed the site and median information; it was replaced, to match the plan.
  • Tails at D8 (share of readings below q01, below q05, above q95, above q99). Control 3.9%, 8.3%, 7.1%, 2.9%; X 5.8%, 12.0%, 9.4%, 3.4%; M 5.3%, 10.9%, 7.6%, 3.0%; BG2 0.2%, 4.0%, 5.6%, 0.2%. By lead band the X head's score is 8.30, 8.12, 8.19, 8.26 (0 to 24, 24 to 72, 72 to 120, 120 to 168 hours) against 8.51, 8.29, 8.37, 8.42 for the control. Pinball loss at the four tail quantiles and the curtailment-cost metric are not computed here.
  • Caveat. Interim, one substation, one scored year; it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site. The stored mean equals the stored median at every Primary, so the head cannot shift the mean and the check is uninformative. Median error at D8 is 1.505 MW for every head and the control's stored median.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast. Identical across arms (1.505 MW at D8), because no arm changes the median.
  • Audit triggers fired. The trigger for a leave-one-out sign flip: removing D12 turns the XGBoost head's pooled change (C4) from +0.030 to -0.009 (the other six leave-one-out values are +0.023 to +0.075). The trigger comparing quantile-score and mean-error contrasts cannot fire. The verdict rests on the D8 stop rule, which no leave-one-out result changes, so no audit was run.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Look for the rest of D8's gap in the median forecast, for example the stored median's bias on sunny half-hours, because the band cannot move it.
  • The mixture head could replace the stored donated band at Primaries without a gas engine; it scores 0.08 points better pooled (-0.16 to -0.01), a small gain that needs a replication.

docs.title: Does a Primary's rate of generator-like steps predict how much the best-guess stack trails BG2 across the 14 scored Primaries?
docs.text:
A simple step counter does not flag the Primaries where the best-guess forecast trails the production-style forecast (BG2), so the experiment cannot link D8's gap to steps at other sites. We counted, at each of 14 Primary substations, how often the demand drops or rises by at least 1.5 MW for at least 6 hours, using the step detector of experiment 361 unchanged. We then asked whether sites with more steps are the sites where the best-guess forecast (the stack, a generalised additive model with a Kalman filter on its effects) scores worse than BG2. The gap is the stack's mean quantile score minus BG2's, in points of the site's effective capacity; the quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles. They are not: the rank correlation is +0.007, with a 95% interval of -0.683 to +0.594. A post hoc threshold set as a share of each site's capacity changes this to +0.49 to +0.71, so the answer depends on the threshold. Fourteen sites are a weak test. A placebo check also failed: copies of the readings with their days shuffled showed as many steps as the real readings. The verdict is therefore inconclusive.

D8 has the most steps (9.95 per month in the scored year, 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30) and the largest gap to BG2 (+3.619 quantile-score points, as in experiment 252). D12 has a gap of +0.947 and ranks 6th by step rate. D22 has a gap of +0.639 and no detected steps. Caveat for every number here: the result is interim, it covers one scored year, and it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap at D8, the one substation suspected of a nearby generator.

Figure 1: step rate and gap do not line up outside D8.

Figure 2: shuffled copies of the readings show as many steps as the real readings.

  • Arms. No XGBoost, GAM, or neural network is fitted. The detector is experiment 361's detect at 1.5 MW, 6 hours, run once for falls and once for rises over each site's whole history, and a step counts in the scored year if it starts between 2025-07-02 and 2026-06-30. Code reused from experiment 361's folder (the detector) and experiment 252's folder (the site cache, the BG2 reader, and the scorer).
  • Stack and rows. The stack is experiment 252 arm A0 at D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22 (apparent-power sites), and experiment 155 arm C (recipe R alone) at D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 (MW sites), so the two groups use different stack versions. The gap is the stack's mean quantile score minus BG2's on the scored year's rows outside the hand-filtered load-shift events, leads up to 168 hours, in points of effective capacity. The control gate passed: D8's gap reproduces at +3.619.
  • Retraining schedule. None; stored forecasts are scored. The contrast cannot depend on a schedule.

  • P1 (rank correlation at least 0.5): fails. +0.007 over 14 sites (95% interval from resampling sites -0.683 to +0.594); -0.242 without D8; +0.228 over the eight apparent-power sites only.
  • P2 (D8, D12, and D22 all in the top five by rate): fails. D8 is 1st, D12 is 6th, D22 is 14th.
  • P3 (shuffled rate under half the real rate): fails. Shuffling whole days moves the rate to 2.3 to 20.2 times the real rate at the 13 sites with steps. The decision rule says no verdict is drawn from P1 and P2 when P3 fails, hence inconclusive. The shuffle moves summer days next to winter days, so a post hoc placebo permutes days only among days of the same month and day type. It still gives 0.8 to 2.7 times the real rate (D8 1.17, D12 1.35, D2 1.45, D21 0.84). The detector's rate is therefore mostly ordinary demand variation at every site, and no site's rate clearly stands out from its shuffled copies.
  • Size and direction. Median step size is 1.7 to 2.9 MW at every site, and D2 has rises and falls in similar numbers (40 and 33), as ordinary demand swings would; D14 is fall-heavy (17 rises, 35 falls), and D4 and D12 have almost only rises.
  • Capacity-share threshold (post hoc). The gap is in points of capacity, so a fixed 1.5 MW threshold treats sites of 3.2 to 18.2 MW differently (it is 47% of D22's capacity and 32% of D12's). The audit asked for a sweep of 7 thresholds, each a share of the site's effective capacity, on the 14 sites. The plan fixed 1.5 MW, so these rows are post hoc.
Threshold Spearman Without D8 Without D8 and D12 Rank of D8, D12, D22 1% +0.62 +0.52 +0.39 1, 2, 4 2% +0.67 +0.59 +0.48 1, 2, 4 3% +0.71 +0.64 +0.55 1, 2, 3 5% +0.49 +0.36 +0.19 1, 2, 3 8% +0.51 +0.38 +0.22 1, 2, 5 10% +0.56 +0.45 +0.30 1, 2, 5 15% +0.53 +0.41 +0.24 1, 2, 6
  • Reading the sweep. At 1% to 3% every site has 16 to 33 steps per month, and the within-month shuffle gives about 1.0 to 1.3 times the real count at 3%, so those correlations mostly track volatility relative to capacity. At 10% the shuffle gives 1.0 to 2.0 times the real count. The pre-registered threshold stays 1.5 MW.
  • Not covered. The detector threshold is in MW, so a site with a larger capacity has more chance to cross it; no capacity-share threshold was tried. The scored-year window is 12 months, so rates of 0 to 2 steps are single-digit counts. The MVA sites' gaps average over rows that also have climatology and manual-heuristic scores (experiment 252's rows), and the MW sites' gaps over all rows with a BG2 forecast, so the row filters differ slightly between the two groups. The placebos assume the cache is contiguous half-hours from midnight and move data gaps with their days. P3 compares the placebo with the real rate over all history, and D22, with no real steps, cannot be tested.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not applicable, because no forecast was produced here; the gaps are read from stored forecasts that earlier experiments already checked.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile-score gap: not computed, because the gap is only the correlate and the experiment makes no forecasting contrast.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 1 of the ml-experiment skill's audit list, a failed placebo. A Sonnet audit (the manager chose Sonnet only) re-derived the step counts, gaps, Spearman, and placebos from the raw inputs and reproduced them. Mixing experiment 252's and 155's stack arms does not move the ranking (all 14 sites with one arm give -0.011 against +0.007), and counting steps by overlap with the window gives identical counts. The audit also found that the capacity-share threshold changes the correlation, which this page now reports. Leaving out D8 makes the 1.5 MW correlation negative (-0.242), so it rests on D8 alone.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the cause of D12's and D22's gaps directly (D12's apparent-power reading folds reverse flow, per experiment 252; the cause of D22's gap is unclear), because their step rates are low.
  • A detector for D8's multi-day drops needs a placebo it passes before it is used across sites.

docs.title: MVA fold: solar capacity and the eight MVA-only Primaries
docs.text:
If a Primary substation's meter reports only apparent power, a fit that allows for reverse flow finds reverse flow at one of the eight such substations, Stickney (D12), and at none of the other seven. Reverse flow means power flowing from the substation back into the grid, which solar panels cause at midday. A Primary is a substation that steps 33 kV down to 11 kV. Eight Primaries (the "MVA-only" ones) report apparent power in MVA, which has no sign, and six report signed power in MW. We asked two questions. First, does the rule of experiment 366 keep the fitted solar capacity close to that of a fit to the signed series (S)? The rule chooses, for each Primary, between the naive fit (N), which reads the meter reading as signed power, and the fit through the meter (L0), which can represent reverse flow. Second, at which MVA-only Primaries does L0 find reverse flow? For the six signed-MW Primaries, the chosen fit's capacity is within 3.1% of S's, with and without synthetic solar output added to the readings. L0 finds reverse flow at D12 and at no other MVA-only Primary, including Marsh Lane (D8), which NGED's monitor file marks "Yes" for reverse flow. Verdict: partly supported. The capacity result and the D12 result hold. The second half of the hypothesis, that L0 finds reverse flow at the substations NGED marks "Yes" or "Maybe", was refuted. Prediction P3, that L0 would invent reverse flow at the other MVA-only Primaries, failed. The page's predictions P1 to P4 are in the front matter.

Every result holds for reactive power zero only. Experiment 366 found that the rule fails at power factor 0.97, and real MVA-only meters have unknown reactive power. The rule is used as registered and was not tuned. The fits are frozen at the cut on past weather (the scored cut is 2025-07-01 and the replicate cut is 2024-07-01), as in experiment 358, which also holds the injection levels. "Points of capacity" are percentage points of a substation's solar capacity. The fitted capacity is the last season-year's at the cut; the 2025-07-01 cut uses no later rows. D9 is new; D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 reuse experiment 358's cells, and the pin is the pinned solar capacity of experiment 45's frozen vintage as read by pinned_capacity.

docs.title: Results (reactive power zero, scored cut unless stated)
docs.text:
• P1 holds, and level 1.0 is the real test. With no injection the result is mostly a check that the rule does not pick L0 at D5, because N equals S where there is no reverse flow. The chosen fit's capacity is within 15% of S's at 6 of 6 Primaries at level 0.0 (ratios 0.999 to 1.006) and at level 1.0 (0.991 to 1.030). The rule chooses N at D5, D11, D14, D16, and D9 and L0 at D10 with no injection, and L0 everywhere at level 1.0. L0's own ratio at D5 with no injection is 1.30, the placebo failure of experiment 358.
  • P2 holds, narrowly. The pin is within 25% of S's capacity at 4 of 6 at level 0.0: D5 1.07, D10 1.12, D11 1.14, D14 0.92. It is 1.45 at D9 and 1.58 at D16.
  • P3 fails. L0's fitted reverse-flow share of sunny training half-hours exceeds 50% at 1 of the 8 MVA-only Primaries at both cuts. At D12 it is 0.70 (scored) and 0.62 (replicate). At D8 and at the other six it is at most 0.006. At D22 (NGED "Maybe") L0 and N have nearly the same capacity (51.4 and 51.2), and at D8 they are identical, so L0 finds nothing there that N lacks.
  • P4 holds, against a weak comparator. N's fitted capacity at D12 is 0.0 at both cuts, so the gap is "some solar against none". At D12 the rule chooses L0 at both cuts, and L0's reading error on sunny half-hours is 9.3 points of capacity below N's at the scored cut (16.2 against 25.5) and 10.7 below at the replicate cut. At the seven others the chosen arm is N, so its error equals N's by construction.
  • Rule statistics at the eight MVA-only Primaries. D12 has correlation +0.55 and a 1st percentile of 26.7. The seven other MVA-only Primaries have correlations of -0.54 to -0.04 and 1st percentiles of 5.9 to 40.2, which repeats experiment 366.
  • Starting points disagree. The six starting points of L0's fit disagree on capacity by 125 points at D12 and 176 at D4 (11 to 20 at D2, D8, D19, D21; under 0.2 at D3 and D22; scored cut), so a single fit's capacity at D4 or D12 is uncertain.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Trigger 2 fired on P3. P3 failed, and experiment 365 found that L0 fits reverse flow on 96% to 97% of summer midday half-hours at D5. The explanation offered is weak and untested. Experiment 365 reported that figure at the signed-MW sites it checked, including D5, where the readings dip towards zero. The eight MVA-only Primaries have 1st percentiles of the sunny-midday readings of 5.9 or more, against 3.8 at D5. The D5 comparison on sunny half-hours was not computed.
  • Trigger 7 fired. A planned all-16-Primaries experiment depends on this result, which has not been replicated.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet auditor (the series brief allows Sonnet only) re-derived the headline numbers from the stored files and found no error. P1 at level 0.0 is largely true by construction. N's capacity at D12 is zero. D8's statistics move between the cuts. The pin's source at D9 and D16 was not checked.
  • Median against mean forecast. This check does not apply, because the fits are frozen point fits with no quantile forecasts.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• No signed truth exists at the eight MVA-only Primaries. The claim that D12 has reverse flow and the others have little rests on the NGED monitor file and experiment 110. It is unconfirmed whether the fit cannot see reverse flow at D8 or D22 or whether there is none.
  • D8's L0 capacity moves from 32.6 (replicate cut) to 44.4 (scored cut) and its 1st percentile from 24.7 to 5.9, so D8's rule statistics are unstable between the two cuts. The source of the pin at D9 and D16 (vintage or growth prior) was not checked, so the reason for the pin being 45% and 58% high is unknown.
  • The fits are frozen and use past weather, so there is no ensemble forecast, no quantiles, and no Kalman filter.
  • The all-16-Primaries step should run the full forecast stack and must include the power factor 0.97 case, where the rule and the fit are known to fail.

docs.title: Which input group gives monthly XGBoost its lead over the GAM stack at substation D8?
docs.text:
Take-home message: monthly XGBoost beats the GAM stack at D8 mostly because it uses the power measured shortly before the forecast starts. Removing three lagged power values from its inputs raises its quantile score at D8 by 0.550 points (95% interval +0.237 to +0.944), which is 86% of the 0.643-point gap between the two forecasts (the interval spans roughly 37% to 147% of the gap).

What we compared. D8 is the Primary substation at Marsh Lane, one of the substations that step 33 kV or 66 kV down to 11 kV. The GAM stack is the generalised additive model forecast of Primary demand research default 1, refitted weekly (experiment 355). "Monthly XGBoost" is the XGBoost (gradient-boosted decision tree) forecast of one member of BG2, the second best-guess forecast for Primary substations, refitted once a month (experiments 87 and 360). Scores are the quantile score, twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points (percent of the substation's effective capacity, the largest demand it carries; lower is better). Experiment 360 found that monthly XGBoost alone scores 7.695 at D8 against 8.338 for the GAM stack, a gap of 0.643 points. We refitted monthly XGBoost with one group of inputs changed at a time. The three lags are the power observed at the forecast origin (the time the forecast is made), at the same half-hour one day earlier, and at the same half-hour one week earlier, each using only telemetry at least 3.5 hours old. Removing the three lags and the five extra weather inputs together gives 8.339, level with the GAM stack.

Prediction. Written before any score was read: removing at least one input group raises the D8 score by 0.3 points or more, and no group moves the score at D2 or D4 (two other Primary substations used as placebos) by more than 0.1 points. The first half held. The second half failed: removing the lags raises the score by 0.283 at D4 (interval +0.143 to +0.435) and by 0.109 at D2 (+0.052 to +0.164, which includes 0.1).

Caveat. This is interim, from one substation and one scored year, and it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap. The aim is better uncertainty estimation at D8 without hurting other Primaries. The GAM stack's Kalman filter (a recursive correction) also reads recent power, in a different form (experiment 364), so the GAM stack does not simply lack the lags.
