Intervals are 95%, from 20,000 resamples of whole valid months (seed 0). Differences are paired on the same rows, in points. The control scores 2.238 at D2 and 2.398 at D4. D8 has 96,986 rows; D2 and D4 have 121,492 rows each (all stored rows to 168 hours).

docs.title: Decision and results
docs.text:
• Verdict: supported. One group (the origin lags) raises the D8 score by at least 0.3 points with an interval wholly above zero. The stop rule (no group reaches 0.2) did not fire. The placebo half of the prediction failed (see above); the verdict rests on the decision rule, which does not mention placebos.
  • The arms overlap. The D8 effects of the lags (+0.550) and the equal weights (+0.225) sum to more than the 0.643-point gap, so "86%" is the share for one arm, not a partition of the gap.
  • Gate. The refitted control scores 7.695 against the stored 7.694 (tolerance 0.05).
  • Absolute D8 scores. The control scores 7.695, the GAM stack 8.338 (weekly refits, experiment 355), BG2 7.593 (experiment 360), and the GAM-inputs-only arm 8.339. That arm drops the five extra weather inputs (longwave radiation, dew point, surface pressure, precipitation, 10 m wind speed) and the three lags, and keeps temperature, shortwave radiation, solar angles, calendar columns, and lead hours.
  • Lead bands at D8. Dropping the lags raises the score by +0.604 (0 to 24 h), +0.611 (24 to 72 h), +0.523 (72 to 120 h), and +0.487 (120 to 168 h); every interval is above zero. The effect shrinks only slightly at D8, but at D4 it falls from +0.539 to +0.147 and at D2 from +0.175 to +0.054, so it is a D8 pattern.
  • Median error and bias at D8. Bias is the median forecast minus the actual demand, so a positive value is over-forecasting. Without the lags, the mean absolute error of the median rises from 14.02 to 15.13 points of capacity, the bias from +3.43 to +5.87 points, and the correlation with the actual demand falls from 0.447 to 0.390. Equal weights also raise the bias, to +5.34.
  • Recency weighting. Equal weights raise the D8 score by +0.225 and lower the D2 and D4 scores (-0.033 and -0.059), so the 0.5-year half-life helps at D8 and hurts at the other two substations.
  • Retraining schedule. Monthly refits on the whole history with a 0.5-year half-life, 500 rounds, eta 0.05, as experiment 87; the contrast could depend on the schedule, which was not varied.
  • Data. Training rows from the control member of the ECMWF ensemble forecast (ENS) with ERA5 reanalysis past weather, as experiment 87, and 500 boosting rounds at learning rate 0.05; the lags use observed power at least 3.5 hours before the forecast origin.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Mean forecast. The stored forecasts hold quantiles only, so there is no mean forecast to compare with the median. The mean absolute error of the median moves in the same direction as the quantile score for every arm at D8, D2, and D4.
  • Audit triggers. None of triggers 1 to 6 fired: the control reproduced the stored score, the ensemble-mean arm (which should change little) moved D8 by 0.007, inside its interval's 0.017 half-width, no result contradicts experiment 364 (recent power matters), and the mean absolute error of the median agrees in sign with the score for every arm. Trigger 7 (a later experiment's design depends on this result and the result is unreplicated) fires, because the proposed GAM recent-power term depends on it. A Sonnet audit (the manager's decision; no Opus) re-derived the D8, D4, and D2 contrasts from the raw stored forecasts with its own code and reproduced them to within 0.004, found no lookahead and no missing rows, and found that the refitted control matches the stored member at all three substations. It also found that the D8 lag effect is uneven across months: leaving out any one month keeps it between +0.391 and +0.606, but it is large in August 2025 (+2.25) and December 2025 (+1.25) and slightly negative in February 2026 (-0.12). "86% of the gap" is a difference of two scores, and does not show that the GAM stack lacks the lags.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Next candidate. A GAM term that uses the power measured just before the forecast origin. The maintainer decides whether to test it; this experiment did not test which form of the term works.
  • Lags in production. The lags need telemetry within 3.5 hours of the forecast origin, so they are unavailable when telemetry is late, and the degradation rule then applies.
  • Background. No new data-processing finding, so data-processing.md is unchanged.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00371-d8-monthly-xgboost-input-group-ablation/ imports experiment 87's folder (e00087_fit_demand.py, e00087_common.py, e00087_regimes.py, e00087_stack.py) and reads experiment 360's stored frames. Printed numbers are in printed_report.txt beside the scripts.

docs.title: MVA fold: the rule-chosen fit at all 16 Primaries
docs.text:
At the Primary substation D12 (Stickney), the fit through the meter scores 0.57 points better than the naive fit on sunny daylight half-hours, but twelve months of data cannot distinguish that gain from zero. A Primary is a substation that steps 33 kV down to 11 kV. Eight Primaries report apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA), which carries no direction of flow, so reverse flow (power flowing from the substation back into the grid) is hidden. The naive fit treats the meter reading as signed power. The fit through the meter models the lost sign. We asked whether the fit that the rule of experiment 366 chooses scores better than the naive fit. The rule picks the fit through the meter when the training readings rise with irradiance or come close to zero, and it picks the fit through the meter at D12 only. Scores are quantile scores in points of effective capacity (percent of the Primary's capacity). The scored year is 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30. We scored the stored forecasts of experiment 152 over 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, beside BG2 (the production-style forecast), climatology, and the manual heuristic at all 16 Primaries. Verdict: not supported, because the D12 interval includes zero.

Experiment 372 is close to a repeat of experiment 152. It applies no stage-2 correction and makes no claim against the arm A1 of experiment 252. Stage 2 is the correction step fitted on tuning-period forecasts. Experiment 152 did not store those forecasts. Applying stage 2 means re-running experiment 152's engine into a new folder. Every result holds for reactive power zero. The rule fails at power factor 0.97 (experiments 358 and 366).

docs.title: Results (quantile score in points of effective capacity; lower is better)
docs.text:
• P1 fails its interval. At D12, the fit through the meter minus the naive fit is -0.57 on sunny daylight half-hours (-2.42 to +1.31) and -0.30 over all half-hours (-0.76 to +0.18). The point estimate is inside the predicted -1.0 to 0.0, and the interval includes zero.
  • P2 holds by construction. At the seven other Primaries the chosen fit is the naive fit. The fit through the meter and the naive fit also score within 0.001 points of each other at D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22, and differ only at D8 (-0.21 over all half-hours; interval -0.74 to +0.20) and D12.
  • P3 fails. The chosen fit scores worse than BG2 over all half-hours at 4 of 8 Primaries: D8 (+3.36; 2.19 to 4.65), D12 (+0.76; 0.40 to 1.15), D22 (+0.42; 0.17 to 0.68), and D19 (+0.07; -0.01 to +0.15). It is level with or below BG2 at D2, D3, D4, and D21. Pooled over the eight it is +0.56 (0.39 to 0.75), or +0.16 without D8.
  • Sunny daylight half-hours. The chosen fit trails BG2 at all 8 Primaries on the point estimate (pooled +0.73; 0.48 to 1.01), by 0.01 to 1.70 points; the gaps at D19 (+0.01), D3 (+0.10), and D4 (+0.28) have intervals that include zero.
  • Control gate passes. The rescored BG2 scores match experiment 252's stored values (D12 6.47, D2 2.18).
  • D15 and D18. The stack has never run at either. BG2 scores 11.27 at D15 (0.8 months of usable history, 53,525 rows) and 2.74 at D18 (61,463 rows) over all half-hours; climatology scores 35.14 and 12.09, and the manual heuristic 17.02 and 4.04.
  • Hand-filtered half-hours in the scored year. D5 2,107; D18 1,317; D15 1,124; D16 947; D3 456; D14 352; D12 310; D22 209; D10 117; D4 106; D19 106; none at D2, D8, D9, D11, and D21, which have either no event list or no event in the scored year.
  • Six signed-MW Primaries. No stack scores exist on these rows. BG2 scores are in figure 1.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median against mean forecast. This check does not apply, because only quantiles are scored.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 applies to P3, which failed against experiment 252's reading that raw fits trail BG2 at most MVA-only Primaries; the raw fits are level with BG2 (within 0.1 points) at five of eight, and the reason (the lead range and the stage-2 correction) was not tested. No other trigger fired. The pooled contrast without D8 stays positive (+0.16), so leaving out D8 does not flip its sign.
  • Tail calibration (coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, q99) was not computed here; experiment 152 holds it for these fits.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• One scored year and twelve month-blocks give wide intervals.
  • No stage 2, so no comparison with experiment 252's arm A1 or with research default 3 is possible.
  • The rule's choice rests on experiment 366's thresholds, one of which was set after seeing experiment 365's numbers.
  • Re-running experiment 152's engine into a new folder would give stage-2 tuning forecasts at seven Primaries. It needs hours of compute and the maintainer's yes.

docs.title: Does an XGBoost meta-model that weights several worker forecasts by context beat the best single family at D8?
docs.text:
Take-home message: weighting the stored forecasts by context did not help at D8, and whether it helps around holidays is unresolved. We asked whether a second XGBoost model, which we call the meta-model, could give each of seven stored forecasts a weight that depends on the time, and so beat the best of them. The seven are BG2's five members (weekly XGBoost, monthly XGBoost, analogue, pooled by substation type, and an XGBoost stack), the generalised additive model (GAM) stack, and BG2, the best-guess blend of the five members. The meta-model also saw the lead time, the actual power at the forecast's origin, the day of week, the hour, the month, a bank-holiday flag, and each forecast's error over the previous 7 days. We trained it on earlier months and scored it on the next month, from October 2025 to June 2026, at substation D8 (Marsh Lane).

The meta-model's quantile score was 7.406 (percent of capacity; lower is better). The 50/50 blend of the GAM stack and BG2 scored 7.434, and the best single forecast, picked each month using only earlier months, scored 7.405. The meta-model's gain over the blend (0.028) is smaller than the 0.1 the plan required, so the stop rule applies and the experiment was not run at D2, D3, or D4. The verdict is not supported.

The meta-model weighted seven forecasts that were already stored, and no new forecast was made. The members come from experiment 360 (BG2's drop-one ablation), the GAM stack from experiment 355 (weekly refit), BG2 from experiment 87, and the 50/50 blend from experiment 359 (GAM and BG2 quantile blend). The score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in percent of D8's 10.38 MW capacity. A row is one half-hourly forecast of one valid time.

These results cover one substation, one scored year, and lead times of 0 to 168 hours. It is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap at D8.

Figure 1: the meta-model is level with the 50/50 blend overall, and lower on holidays.

Figure 2: the meta-model tracks the 50/50 blend month by month.

Figure 3: the meta-model, the best single forecast, and the 50/50 blend score within 0.03 points of each other.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. Meta-model; meta-model without lagged power; meta-model without calendar context; best single family out of sample; 50/50 blend of the GAM stack and BG2; the GAM stack; BG2; each BG2 member alone; climatology; manual heuristic. Code is in ml-experiments/00373-*/ (e00373_meta.py, e00373_score.py, e00373_charts.py) and reuses the scoring helpers of experiments 252, 264, and 354.
  • Rows. 73,331 half-hourly rows, October 2025 to June 2026 (the first three months only train the meta-model), 0 to 168 hours, fold_a_daily_gap_v1. Intervals resample whole valid months (20,000 resamples, seed 0). The 99% intervals are in scores.json.
  • Gate. The script reproduces the GAM stack (8.338), BG2 (7.593), and each member alone (7.560, 7.694, 7.472, 7.633, 8.562) on the 96,986 rows before any meta-model is fitted.
  • Absolute scores (points, scored months): meta-model 7.406; best single family 7.405; 50/50 blend 7.434; BG2 7.570; GAM stack 7.983; manual heuristic 7.963; climatology 8.836.
  • Contrasts (95%). C1 meta-model minus best single family 0.000 (-0.451 to +0.354). C2 minus the 50/50 blend -0.028 (-0.145 to +0.094). C3 minus BG2 -0.165 (-0.602 to +0.139). C4 minus the meta-model without lagged power -0.008 (-0.017 to -0.001). C5 minus the meta-model without calendar +0.018 (-0.031 to +0.088).
  • Holiday and event days. On 3,765 rows from bank holidays and 24 December to 2 January, the meta-model scores 6.162, against 6.633 for the 50/50 blend (-0.471, -0.759 to -0.211) and 7.282 for the best single family (-1.119, -1.651 to 0.000). On all other days it scores 7.473, against 7.477 and 7.412 (-0.004, -0.115 to +0.119; +0.061, -0.327 to +0.380), so non-inferiority holds against the blend. Against the best single family the interval is too wide to show it.
  • Tails (share of readings below q01 and above q99, nominal 0.01; q05 to q95 coverage, nominal 0.90): meta-model 0.005, 0.013, 0.897; best single family 0.003, 0.001, 0.925; 50/50 blend 0.002, 0.006, 0.926; BG2 0.001, 0.003, 0.890. Pinball loss at q01 / q05 / q95 / q99: meta-model 0.413 / 1.597 / 1.810 / 0.508; best single family 0.366 / 1.845 / 1.714 / 0.453; 50/50 blend 0.410 / 1.702 / 1.732 / 0.444.
  • Serving cost. Serving the meta-model needs every worker to run for every substation, plus one XGBoost fit per refit, for a gain whose interval includes zero.
  • Post hoc. The holiday and event-day slice is not in the decision rule. It holds 18 dates in 4 valid months (December 2,141 rows, January 547, April 528, May 549), so its interval is dominated by December. The meta-model without calendar inputs scores 6.251 on those days (against 6.162 with them and 6.633 for the blend), so the gain does not come mainly from calendar features. In December the meta-model without calendar inputs scores 7.579 against 7.489 with them, although the training data holds no Christmas period. The first run selected BG2 as the best single family every month. BG2 is itself a blend, so the final choice excludes it. The choice is among the six other forecasts, and the analogue member won every month. The exclusion changed only the comparator in C1.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus the 50/50 blend's median, mean over rows (points): meta-model +0.02, GAM stack -1.07, BG2 +1.07, best single family (analogue) +1.63. The stored member forecasts hold no mean, so the median stands in for the mean forecast.
  • Median error beside the score contrasts. Median absolute error (points): meta-model 13.476, best single family 13.418, 50/50 blend 13.631, BG2 13.821. The meta-model is marginally ahead of the blend on score (interval includes zero) and on median error, and is level with the best single family on score and 0.058 worse on median error, so score and median error point the same way at every contrast whose interval excludes zero. The meta-model's median error correlates 0.956 with the blend's.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired: the result contradicts its prediction. The explanation recorded here (worker errors are highly correlated, so context has little to select) was not tested by a further experiment. No other trigger fired: C5's nested control moves the score by 0.018, inside its interval half-width of 0.06; no sister experiment exists to compare interval widths; and no later design depends on this result. No audit was run, because the verdict is negative and the stop rule ends the work.

docs.title: Scope and what to try next
docs.text:
• Not run. D2, D3, D4 (stop rule), the six decision Primaries, and the replicate year 2024-25 (rolling-origin forecasts of every worker are not stored for either).
  • Leads. Weather regime is not an input: the stored frames hold no forecast weather, and their sunny and cold flags are computed from observed weather. A later test with ensemble-driven regime flags is the open version of that idea.
  • What the experiment narrows. A learned weighting showed no gain over a fixed blend on ordinary days at D8. The lower holiday-period score is the one open lead, and it needs a longer history of worker forecasts to test, because the slice holds only 18 dates.

docs.title: MVA fold: stage-two corrections at the eight MVA-only Primaries
docs.text:
The fit that experiment 366's rule chooses, followed by experiment 252's stage-2 corrections, scores no worse than the stack's arm A1 at the eight Primaries that report only apparent power. A1 is the arm of experiment 252's stack that carries stage 2. Over all half-hours, pooled over the eight, the difference is -0.03 points of effective capacity (percent of the Primary's capacity; 95% interval -0.08 to +0.02). The registered threshold was an upper end below +0.10, and the control gate passed. Verdict: supported.

A Primary is a substation that steps 33 kV down to 11 kV. Eight Primaries report apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA), which has no sign, so reverse flow is hidden. The rule of experiment 366 picks the fit through the meter at D12 and the naive fit, which reads the meter reading as signed power, at the other seven. Stage 2 is the correction step of experiment 252: a night offset, recipe R, and a lead-hour spread refitted on tuning-month residuals. The fit through the meter models the lost sign of the flow. D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22 are the eight Primaries' short names; D8 is Marsh Lane, D12 Stickney, and D22 Langrick.

The chosen fit's forecast still trails BG2, the production-style forecast. Chosen fit with stage 2 minus BG2 is +0.53 (+0.35 to +0.73) over all half-hours. The gap sits at D8 (+3.77), D12 (+0.65), and D22 (+0.37). A1 trails BG2 by +0.56 (+0.39 to +0.75), so the choice of fit does not change the gap.

Every result holds for reactive power zero (power factor 1). Experiment 366's rule fails at power factor 0.97 (experiment 358 and 366), and real MVA-only meters have unknown reactive power. The maintainer decided on 2026-10-28 to keep reactive power at zero and to count experiment 366 as a win. The rule is used as 366 registered it and is not tuned on these Primaries. For D8, it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap.

Figure 1 shows the chosen fit and A1 on top of each other at six of the eight Primaries (all but D8 and D12), because their scores differ by 0.01 to 0.05 points there.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Re-run. Experiment 152's engine (arms N, A, and F_fold) was re-run for the tuning, replicate, and scored periods into this experiment's own work folder, with 4 workers of 2 threads. Experiment 152's folder was read and never written. This gives the tuning-period forecasts that stage 2 needs and that experiment 152 did not store.
  • Stage 2. Experiment 252's build_arms was imported unchanged and applied to arms N and A, as experiment 353 did at D8. D8 has no tuning month and borrows the spread of the donor Primaries D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22. The donor spread is taken from experiment 252's stored tuning forecasts of A1, not from re-run chosen-arm forecasts.
  • Chosen arm. The fit through the meter with stage 2 at D12, and the naive fit with stage 2 at the other seven.
  • Scoring. Quantile scores in points of effective capacity over the scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, rows outside the hand-filtered events, with a paired month-resampled bootstrap (20,000 resamples, 95%). Code reused from earlier experiments lives in ml-experiments/00152-*, 00252-*, and 00353-*.

docs.title: Results (quantile score in points of effective capacity; lower is better)
docs.text:
• P1 holds. Chosen with stage 2 minus A1 is -0.03 (-0.08 to +0.02) over all half-hours, inside the predicted -0.30 to +0.30. On sunny daylight half-hours it is -0.10 (-0.33 to +0.11). Per Primary it ranges from -0.29 at D12 (-0.62 to +0.01) to +0.05 at D3 and D21, where the interval excludes zero.
  • P2 holds on the point estimate. At D12, the fit through the meter with stage 2 minus the naive fit with stage 2 is -0.76 (-2.52 to +0.89) on sunny daylight half-hours and -0.27 (-0.61 to +0.04) over all half-hours. The intervals include zero, so one year does not resolve it. Pooled over the eight it is -0.06 (-0.13 to -0.00). The fit through the meter also beats the naive fit at D8 by 0.21 raw and 0.24 with stage 2, and scores the same to two decimal places at the other six (table of absolute scores below).
  • P3 holds. Stage 2 narrows the gap to BG2 a little at D12 (+0.76 raw, +0.65 with stage 2) and D22 (+0.42, +0.37), and leaves D8 at +3.77.
  • P4, the control gate, passes. The re-run raw fits reproduce experiment 372's chosen scores to within 0.04 points at every Primary (exactly at five of the eight; D21 differs by 0.038). The gate compares with experiment 372 (which matched experiment 252's stored values), and no tolerance was registered for the references. They differ from experiment 372's by at most 0.039, because the re-run changes a few scored rows at D8, D12, and D21.
  • Stage 2 against the raw fit (c4). Pooled -0.03 (-0.06 to +0.00). It improves 7 Primaries by 0.04 to 0.14 points and worsens D8 by +0.42 (+0.19 to +0.69). A1 also scores worse at D8 than the raw naive fit (11.43 against 10.95).
  • Absolute scores, all half-hours. Chosen with stage 2, A1, BG2: D2 2.09, 2.08, 2.18; D3 1.46, 1.42, 1.63; D4 2.31, 2.29, 2.39; D8 11.37, 11.43, 7.59; D12 7.12, 7.41, 6.47; D19 2.98, 2.97, 3.05; D21 2.16, 2.11, 2.30; D22 3.93, 3.94, 3.55. Climatology and the manual heuristic are in figure 1.
  • Groups. Chosen with stage 2 minus A1 is +0.02 (-0.08 to +0.05) on cold nights and -0.00 (-0.04 to +0.04) on winter nights. Minus BG2 it is -0.12 (-0.26 to +0.13) on cold nights and +0.28 (+0.16 to +0.39) on winter nights.
  • Tail calibration (share of readings at or below each quantile, mean over the eight; ideal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99). Chosen with stage 2: 0.054, 0.112, 0.916, 0.964 over all half-hours. A1: 0.054, 0.112, 0.917, 0.963. BG2: 0.005, 0.040, 0.957, 0.995. The share of readings below the q05 forecast is 0.112 rather than 0.05, so the stack's low quantiles are too high, and BG2's tails are closer to ideal. D8 shows it most: q05 coverage 0.311 for the chosen fit and 0.040 for BG2.
  • D15 and D18. The stack has never run at either, so only the references are scored. Experiment 372 reports BG2 scores of 11.27 at D15 and 2.74 at D18, and the hand-filtered half-hours at every Primary. The six signed-MW Primaries have no stack scores on these rows either. The step 4 comparison on all 16 Primaries is therefore the eight scored here plus references on the other eight.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median against mean forecast. The median forecast minus the mean forecast is 0.00 at every Primary for both A1 and the chosen fit.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts. The mean absolute error of the mean forecast, in megawatts, is: D2 3.69 against 3.66 for A1; D3 2.49 against 2.39; D4 3.98 against 3.94; D8 15.42 against 15.48; D12 12.34 against 12.89; D19 5.20 against 5.18; D21 3.79 against 3.68; D22 6.32 against 6.34. The direction agrees with the quantile score at D12, D8, and D22. At D3 and D21 both measures put the chosen fit slightly behind A1 (by 0.10 and 0.11 MW), so trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Leave one Primary out. The interval of the chosen-minus-A1 contrast stays below +0.10 in each of the eight leave-one-out runs (upper ends +0.01 to +0.03). Its sign flips when D12 is left out (+0.01, -0.01 to +0.03), so trigger 4 fired for the sign and not for the verdict. Leaving out D8 moves the BG2 contrast from +0.53 to +0.07 (-0.03 to +0.17), so the gap to BG2 is a D8 gap.
  • Triggers. Trigger 4 fired for the sign flip described above, and trigger 5 fired at D8, where the raw fit beats the arm that contains it (stage 2). No Opus audit ran, because the brief for this sequence allows Sonnet only. The verdict does not depend on either: the registered rule uses the upper end of the pooled interval, which is below +0.10 with and without D12 and D8. The explanation for D8, the borrowed donor spread, is untested here. Triggers 1, 2, 3, 6, and 7 did not fire.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• All results are for reactive power zero. Experiment 366's rule fails at power factor 0.97, and real MVA-only meters have unknown reactive power.
  • The rule's 1.0 threshold was set after seeing experiment 365's numbers.
  • One scored year and twelve month-blocks give wide intervals, most of all on sunny half-hours at D12.
  • D8's stage-2 spread is borrowed from six other Primaries, and stage 2 worsens D8.
  • A1 differs from the chosen fit in design (a T-all design, a solar clip, and a 60% clip), so the contrast with A1 mixes the rule's choice with those differences.
  • Averaged over the eight, the stack's lower tail is too narrow, and D8's tails are too narrow in both directions.

docs.title: Does the meta-model over worker forecasts beat a 50/50 blend across the 16 Primaries, not only at D8?
docs.text:
Take-home message: weighting the stored forecasts by context made the forecast worse than a fixed 50/50 blend at most Primaries, so a meta-model is not the architecture to use at every substation. We asked whether the second-level XGBoost model of experiment 373, which we call the meta-model, would beat a fixed average of two forecasts at all 16 Primary substations, not only at D8. The meta-model sees the quantiles of seven stored forecasts (six at D15 and D18), the lead time, the power at the forecast's origin, the calendar, and each forecast's error over the previous 7 days. The fixed average is the 50/50 blend of the GAM stack and BG2. Pooled over the 14 Primaries that have a stored GAM stack, the meta-model's quantile score was 3.288 (percent of capacity; lower is better) against 3.181 for the blend. Its score was worse by 0.107 points (95% interval +0.032 to +0.183). It was lower than the blend at 4 Primaries and higher at 10. The verdict is not supported.

Terms. A Primary is a primary substation of the electricity distribution network, and D2 to D22 are anonymised labels for 16 of them. The GAM stack is a forecast from a generalised additive model with a Kalman filter. BG2 is the best-guess blend of five machine-learning forecasts (BG2's members). A point is 1% of a substation's effective capacity, and a lower quantile score is better. The not supported verdict follows the decision rule in the front matter.

The meta-model reproduces experiment 373 at D8 and fails to generalise. At D8 the meta-model scored 7.406, the blend 7.434, and the best single forecast 7.405, equal to experiment 373's. No forecast was fitted again: the five members of BG2 and BG2 are rebuilt for all 16 Primaries from the stored refit predictions of experiment 87 with the code of experiment 360, and the GAM stack comes from experiments 252, 155, and 355. Only the meta-model is new, and its settings are those of experiment 373 with no tuning.

Figure 1: the meta-model scores worse than the blend at 10 of 14 Primaries.

Figure 2: only in sunny April-to-June half-hours is the meta-model clearly lower than the blend.

Figure 3: the 50/50 blend is the lowest-scoring arm on average, ahead of the meta-model and BG2.

Code is in ml-experiments/00375-*/ (e00375_build.py, e00375_meta.py, e00375_score.py, e00375_charts.py) and copies experiment 373's recipe.
  • Rows. 48,409 to 73,365 half-hourly rows per Primary, October 2025 to June 2026 (the first three months only train the meta-model), leads up to 168 hours, outside the hand-filtered load-shift events at the 13 Primaries whose stack file carries the event mask (D8, D15, and D18 carry none, so no events are removed there), fold_a_daily_gap_v1. Intervals resample whole valid months, the same months at every Primary (20,000 resamples, seed 0); the pooled figure is the mean of the Primaries' means.

  • Leave-one-out. Dropping any one Primary leaves C1 between +0.081 and +0.122, with every interval above zero, so no site drives the result.

The gate passed; the result agrees with the pre-registered expectation that the prediction would fail; the score and error contrasts agree; leaving one Primary out never flips C1; C4 and C5 move the score by less than their interval half-widths; D8's C1 interval (-0.142 to +0.093) matches experiment 373's (-0.145 to +0.094); and no later design depends on this result. No audit was run.

docs.title: Scope and what to try next
docs.text:
• Not run. The replicate year (2024-25), because the rolling-origin worker forecasts of earlier years are not stored for any Primary, and D15 and D18 with a stack, which was never stored there.
  • What the experiment narrows. A learned per-Primary weighting does not beat a fixed 50/50 blend of the GAM stack and BG2 on ordinary days at 14 Primaries, so the next gain in uncertainty is more likely to come from a better single forecast than from a better combiner. The one lead left is sunny April-to-June half-hours, where the meta-model is lower than the blend by 0.143 points (-0.220 to -0.026), a slice chosen after the first look.

docs.title: One GAM stack at all 16 Primaries, with the MVA treatment as an explicit arm
docs.text:
One stack, run unchanged, scores level with BG2 on average at the six Primaries that report signed megawatts. One year of data cannot rule out a gap of 0.13 points. The stack is worse than BG2 on sunny half-hours. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation. The stack is a two-stage additive forecast (a generalised additive model with a correction stage) fitted separately at each Primary. BG2 is the production-style forecast that the stack is compared with. A score is the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles), and a negative difference means the stack is better. Stack minus BG2 over all half-hours, pooled over the six, is -0.02 points of effective capacity (percent of a Primary's capacity; 95% interval -0.17 to +0.13). The pre-registered bar was an interval whose upper end is below +0.10, so the verdict for that group is inconclusive (neither supported nor not supported). The sunny-daylight gap is +0.46 (+0.20 to +0.70). Winter half-hours and cold nights go the other way (-0.29 and -0.44). Every result holds for reactive power zero.

We asked whether the best-guess stack of experiment 252, with stage 2, scores as well as BG2 at every Primary, and how much of the gap at the eight Primaries that report only apparent power (megavolt-amperes, MVA) comes from the MVA treatment. The six signed-MW Primaries are D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16. We ran the unchanged chain of experiment 252 there (its control source), took the eight MVA-only Primaries from experiment 374, and scored all three groups with the rows, metric, and bootstrap of experiment 374.

At the eight MVA-only Primaries the gap to BG2 is a Marsh Lane (D8) gap, and the rule adds 0.03 points. The rule-chosen fit (the fit through the meter at Stickney, D12, and the naive fit elsewhere) minus BG2 is +0.53 (+0.35 to +0.73), and +0.07 (-0.03 to +0.17) without D8. The naive fit at all eight minus BG2 is +0.57 (+0.40 to +0.75). The rule-chosen fit minus the naive fit is -0.03 (-0.08 to +0.01), and it is exactly zero at seven Primaries. At D12 it is -0.27 (-0.61 to +0.04). The rule changes the forecast at D12 only.

docs.title: Results (quantile score in points of effective capacity; lower is better)
docs.text:
• Signed-MW group (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16): inconclusive. Stack minus BG2 is -0.02 (-0.17 to +0.13). Per Primary: D5 +0.14, D9 -0.02, D10 -0.05, D11 -0.15, D14 -0.15, D16 +0.13; every interval includes zero. Stack minus the manual heuristic is -0.70 (-0.96 to -0.44), and minus climatology -0.97 (-1.31 to -0.65).
  • Slices, stack minus BG2, signed-MW group. Sunny daylight +0.46 (+0.20 to +0.70); winter nights -0.17 (-0.30 to +0.03); cold nights -0.44 (-0.95 to -0.00); Economy 7 step -0.06 (-0.16 to +0.04). Registered prediction P1 (between -0.20 and +0.20) holds.
  • Absolute scores, all half-hours (stack, BG2, manual heuristic, climatology). D5 3.52, 3.38, 3.90, 4.26; D9 2.38, 2.40, 2.91, 3.00; D10 3.22, 3.28, 4.13, 4.31; D11 2.35, 2.51, 3.39, 3.55; D14 2.09, 2.25, 2.95, 3.45; D16 2.67, 2.55, 3.15, 3.49.

Chosen fit with stage 2 minus BG2 +0.53 (+0.35 to +0.73); naive fit with stage 2 minus BG2 +0.57 (+0.40 to +0.75); A1 minus BG2 +0.56 (+0.39 to +0.75). By Primary, chosen minus BG2: D8 +3.77 (+2.42 to +5.27), D12 +0.65, D22 +0.37, and -0.07 to -0.16 at D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21. Without D8: chosen +0.07 (-0.03 to +0.17), naive +0.11 (-0.00 to +0.22). P2 and P3 hold.
  • D8 on its own. Chosen and naive fits score 11.37, BG2 7.59, climatology 9.76, manual heuristic 8.47. D8 is the only Primary where the stack trails climatology.

Signed-MW stack: 0.024, 0.072, 0.946, 0.982; BG2: 0.010, 0.041, 0.944, 0.983. MVA-only chosen fit: 0.054, 0.112, 0.916, 0.964; BG2: 0.005, 0.040, 0.957, 0.995. docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control gate. This experiment's stage-2 arm d equals experiment 155's stored arm d to a maximum difference of 0.0 in q50 at all six signed-MW Primaries. The MVA-only numbers reproduce experiment 374's (+0.53, -0.03, +0.07 without D8).
  • Median against mean forecast. 0.00 at every Primary for every arm.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts. Error of the mean forecast against BG2's median, in megawatts: D5 6.01 against 5.88; D9 4.21 against 4.33; D10 5.31 against 5.62; D11 4.21 against 4.48; D14 3.69 against 3.96; D16 4.48 against 4.45. The direction agrees with the quantile score at all six Primaries (at D16 the gap is 0.03 MW).
  • Leave one Primary out (signed-MW). The stack-minus-BG2 interval has an upper end of +0.09 without D5 and +0.11 to +0.17 without any other Primary. The point estimate flips sign without D11 or D14 (+0.01), so trigger 4 fired for the sign. The verdict is inconclusive in all six leave-one-out runs, except that leaving out D5 would meet the +0.10 bar.
  • Triggers. Trigger 4 (a leave-one-out run flips the sign of a contrast) fired as described. Triggers 1 (the gate passed), 3, 5 (no nested arm in the signed-MW group; D8's stage-2 worsening is experiment 374's finding), 6, and 7 did not fire. Trigger 2: P4 contradicts its prediction, and the explanation is untested. No Opus audit ran, because the brief allows Sonnet only and the verdict does not depend on trigger 4: the registered rule uses the upper end of the pooled interval, which is above +0.10 with every Primary except D5.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Reactive power zero only; experiment 366's rule fails at power factor 0.97. For D8, it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap.
  • One scored year and twelve month-blocks give wide intervals. Monthly refits on 24 months were used, not weekly production refits.
  • The signed-MW stack pins the solar capacity to the stored capacity vintages, and the MVA-only stack has no capacity vintage (experiment 252), so the two groups do not share every design choice.
  • The Economy 7 slice is the four half-hours ending at 00:30, 01:00, 07:30, and 08:00 UK local time, defined here.
  • Next: the stack's sunny-half-hour gap to BG2 (+0.46 at the six signed-MW Primaries) is the largest cross-group weakness. A narrower lower tail (q05 coverage 0.07 to 0.11) is the second.

docs.title: The GAM stack, extended to 14 days, scored against BG2 at all 16 Primaries under demand-v1
docs.text:
The stack scores level with BG2 at the six Primaries that report signed megawatts, and trails it at the eight that report only apparent power. The stack beats climatology at all 14 countable Primaries and the manual heuristic at 13 of 14 (D8 is the exception). A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation, labelled D2 to D22 here. The stack is a generalised additive model (GAM) with a correction stage, fitted per Primary, and is "Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 h" with one deliberate gap: it has no two-number solar summary S at any lead, which default 1 includes below 168 hours, so the arm is labelled stack without S below 168 h. The stack is not default 3, because it has no daylight heuristic blend. A score is the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, which equals the continuous ranked probability score, CRPS, up to the estimation from 11 quantiles), in points of effective capacity (percent of a Primary's capacity). A negative difference means the stack is better. BG2 is the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, which production does not run. "MVA-only" Primaries report apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA) and no signed megawatts (MW); every result there assumes reactive power is zero. twCRPS is the threshold-weighted CRPS of the protocol.

Signed-MW six: supported. Stack minus BG2 at days 1 to 10, pooled over the six, is -0.07 (99% interval -0.28 to +0.14, 20,000 resamples of whole months). The registered margin was an upper end below +0.20, and +0.14 is below it. Days 8 to 10 give -0.02 (-0.27 to +0.19), and days 11 to 14 give -0.03 (-0.30 to +0.18). Registered predictions P1 (within -0.20 to +0.20) and P3 (days 8 to 10 trail more than days 1 to 10; true on the point estimates, with overlapping intervals) hold.

MVA-only eight: partly supported. Stack minus BG2 is +0.34 (+0.09 to +0.60) with D8 and +0.18 (-0.02 to +0.39) without. Registered predictions P2 (+0.30 to +0.90 with D8; -0.05 to +0.25 without) holds numerically on both ranges. D8 alone is +1.61 (95% interval +0.52 to +2.85), and removing D8 halves the gap. The point estimate without D8 stays above zero, and its 95% interval (+0.03 to +0.33, leave-one-out below) excludes zero, so the gap is not wholly a D8 gap. The verdict is a judgement, because the decision rule sets no threshold for this group. Days 8 to 10 give +0.34 (+0.05 to +0.67) and days 11 to 14 give +0.46 (+0.09 to +0.92) with D8, so the gap grows with lead.

D15 and D18 (short history, report only). Stack minus BG2 is -0.29 (-1.30 to +0.39) over 6 months. D18 is scorable from 2026-01 and D15 from 2026-03 (the 12-month minimum history), so the intervals cover 4 to 6 months and are wide.

On the 245,463 half-hours that both hold, pooled over the six: default 3 scores 3.276, the stack without S 3.335, and BG2 3.358. Beyond 240 hours and at the other ten Primaries default 3 is not fitted. The comparison crosses a change of training regime, so the 0.06 gap is descriptive.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control gate. Not a row-for-row reproduction, because experiments 374 and 376 stored one fixed fit with one tuning month and no monthly folds. On the headline contrasts, the signed-MW stack minus BG2 in experiment 376 was -0.02 (-0.17 to +0.13, 0.5 to 168 h) against -0.07 here, a difference of 0.05, which is at the limit; the MVA-only gap there was +0.57 (naive fit, 95%) against +0.34 here, which is not within 0.05. Most of the difference comes from D8: here the D8 row is the own-residual arm, and the D8 gap to BG2 is +1.61 against +3.77 in 376.
  • Median against mean forecast. The median minus the mean is 0.00 at every Primary: the stored mean is the corrected mean around which stage 2 centres the quantiles, so the median equals it by construction and no independent mean-forecast contrast exists.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired (P5 failed and the cause is untested). Trigger 7 applies, because the experiment 378 session builds on the stored stage-2 forecasts. Trigger 1 fired in part (the control gate above is not within 0.05 at the MVA-only eight, with the cause given). Triggers 3 (the mean equals the median), 4 (no leave-one-out sign flip), 5, and 6 (no sister experiment at demand-v1) did not fire. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the headline contrasts by its own code from the stored forecasts and reproduced them (signed-MW -0.068, MVA-only +0.344, +0.178 without D8, D8 +1.613). It found no unit error and no lookahead in the stage-2 spread. It found that 55 to 92 rows at D8 and D9 store a missing reading as zero in the stage-2 inputs (under 0.05% of rows, scoring unaffected); this was not fixed.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries. The naive fit of experiment 374 is used at all eight; the rule-chosen fit through the meter at D12 was not run.
  • The stack has no solar summary S below 168 hours, so the stack is not default 1 as the research default log defines it, and the sunny-half-hour gap may be an effect of that absence.
  • The tier-1 daylight blend of experiment 322 (D1) was not tried: its weights are fitted per fold from trailing rows in experiments 317, 319, and 322 and tied to their six-Primary chain.
  • The load-shift detector arm (default 1 with a detector, without, and with the hand labels as an oracle) was not run in this experiment; the load-shift detector arm is a separate follow-up.
  • Missing readings at D8 and D9 enter stage 2 as zeros in under 0.05% of rows (see Checks).
  • Days 11 to 14 are beyond NGED's 1 to 10 day horizon and are descriptive only.
  • The protocol page says D15 and D18 are scored from earlier months than the code allows: with the 12-month rule D18 is first scorable in 2026-01 and D15 in 2026-03.
  • D15 has no pool rows in experiment 103, so a local feature mask supplies its training rows, and its ensemble arrays were built from the production archive read-only (the same extraction as experiment 152, checked against D10's stored arrays with a maximum difference of 0).

docs.title: Primary demand research default 3, ported to all 16 Primaries, scored against BG2 under demand-v1
docs.text:
Default 3 scores level with BG2 at the six Primaries that report signed megawatts, and trails BG2 at the eight that report only apparent power, almost all of that at Marsh Lane (D8). Default 3 is our research demand forecast for a Primary, a 33 kV to 11 kV substation (labelled D2 to D22 here). BG2 is the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, which production does not run. The next paragraph defines the other terms.

Terms.

  • Default 1 and default 3. Default 1 is the generalised additive model (GAM) stack of experiment 377, with the two-number solar summary S added below 168 hours. S summarises the solar response of the 51 ensemble weather members as a mean and a standard deviation. Default 3 is default 1 with S also at 168 to 240 hours, and with a blend towards the manual heuristic's median on daylight half-hours (sun above 5 degrees) at 168 to 240 hours. The "stack without S" is experiment 377's forecast as stored, with S at no lead.
  • Score. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles. It equals the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) up to the error from using 11 quantiles. Scores are in points of effective capacity (percent of a Primary's capacity). A difference below zero favours the first-named forecast. twCRPS is the threshold-weighted CRPS of the protocol, which weights the high-demand tail. The 1%, 5%, 95%, and 99% quantiles are written q01, q05, q95, and q99, and their coverage is the share of readings at or below the quantile.
  • Signed-MW and MVA-only. Signed-MW Primaries report real power in megawatts (MW), with its sign. MVA-only Primaries report apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA), so every result there assumes reactive power is zero. They use the naive fit of experiment 377 (the fit that treats the meter reading as real power), not the rule-chosen fit of experiment 374 (a fit through the meter, chosen by a rule per Primary).
  • D8 spread. D8 has less than 12 months of history, so its forecast spread comes from the residuals of six other Primaries ("donor spread"); experiment 377 also fitted a spread from D8's own past errors ("own-residual spread").
  • Short history. D15 and D18 have under 12 months of history before the scored year, so they are report only and enter no tally.

Signed-MW six: supported. Default 3 minus BG2 at days 1 to 10, pooled over the six, is -0.12 (99% interval -0.31 to +0.06, 20,000 resamples of whole months). The registered margin was an upper end below +0.20, and +0.06 is below it. Days 8 to 10 (168 to 240 hours; BG2 is stored out to 351 hours) give -0.14 (-0.33 to +0.01). Default 3 minus default 1 is -0.03 (-0.06 to -0.02) at days 1 to 10 and -0.12 (-0.19 to -0.05) at days 8 to 10.

MVA-only eight: partly supported. Default 3 minus BG2 is +0.63 (+0.35 to +0.94) with D8 and +0.16 (-0.02 to +0.35) without. The registered prediction (+0.30 to +0.90 with D8; -0.05 to +0.25 without) holds on both ranges. D8 alone is +3.97 (95% interval +2.29 to +5.81). D8 uses the donor spread in every arm here; with its own-residual spread, experiment 377 found +1.61 for the stack without S. Default 3 minus default 1 is -0.02 (-0.05 to -0.004) with D8 and -0.02 (-0.04 to -0.01) without. At days 8 to 10 it is -0.08 with D8 (-0.16 to -0.01), inside the registered range of -0.20 to 0.

D15 and D18 (short history, report only). Default 3 minus BG2, pooled over half-hours, is -0.001 (-0.93 to +0.70) over 6 months at D18 and 4 months at D15. D15 scores worse than default 1 (+0.62, -0.20 to +1.32) because it takes the signed-MW fits of S and the blend, and its 4 months of scored history leave the interval wide.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Rows. Experiment 377's second-stage forecasts at all 16 Primaries on the demand-v1 folds, one fit per fold month on earlier months only. Experiment 378 adds S at 0.5 to 168 hours, and S and the blend at 168 to 240 hours (the band that days 8 to 10 cover).
  • Solar summary S. Each ensemble member's solar response is passed through the Primary's monthly fit of the solar term (experiment 184's code, run on experiment 377's setup; the gate on D5 matched experiment 184's stored values exactly). S is the mean and standard deviation of the 51 responses, with a scale and a spread factor fitted per lead band on the trailing 365 days of runs completed before the fold month.
  • Daylight blend. At 168 to 240 hours the median moves towards the manual heuristic's median with a weight fitted per lead band and season group on the same trailing rows. The blend applies only where the sun is above 5 degrees.
  • Fit groups. The fits are pooled within the signed-MW six and within the MVA-only seven without D8. D8 takes the MVA-only fits, and D15 and D18 take the signed-MW fits. The first fold month has no earlier rows, so S and the blend leave the forecast unchanged there.
  • Intervals. Pooled contrasts use 99% intervals (20,000 resamples), as registered. Per-Primary contrasts use 95% intervals (2,000 resamples) because a single Primary has few months to resample.

These differ from the contrasts against default 1 (-0.03 and -0.02) because default 1 already carries S below 168 hours, which accounts for the extra 0.02 at the signed-MW six.
  • Leave one Primary out (95%). Default 3 minus BG2 at the signed-MW six stays between -0.10 and -0.15 whichever Primary is left out, with intervals that lie wholly below zero only when D5 or D9 is left out. The MVA-only gap stays between +0.62 and +0.74 whichever Primary but D8 is left out, and is +0.16 (+0.02 to +0.30) without D8. Default 3 minus default 1 is negative with an interval wholly below zero in every leave-one-out case in both groups.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrasts (99%). The mean absolute error of the median points the same way as CRPS in every row: default 3 minus BG2 -0.22 (-0.55 to +0.12) signed-MW, +0.41 (+0.01 to +0.80) MVA-only with D8; default 3 minus default 1 -0.04 (-0.09 to -0.01) and -0.04 (-0.07 to -0.01); minus the manual heuristic -1.28 and -0.72.
  • Tail calibration, days 1 to 10 (share of readings at or below each quantile, mean over the group; ideal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99). Signed-MW default 3 0.018, 0.058, 0.947, 0.983; BG2 0.010, 0.045, 0.932, 0.975. MVA-only default 3 0.041, 0.097, 0.918, 0.965; BG2 0.005, 0.042, 0.955, 0.995. MVA-only without D8, default 3: 0.021, 0.070, 0.946, 0.985 (within 0.02 of nominal). D8 alone: 0.183, 0.291, 0.721, 0.826. D15 and D18: 0.034, 0.077, 0.867, 0.947. At the signed-MW six the 1% quantile is too high at D16 and D5: 0.036 and 0.032 of readings fall below it, against 0.01 ideal. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, q99 (default 3 against BG2, signed-MW): 0.245 against 0.222, 0.739 against 0.686, 0.793 against 0.882, 0.262 against 0.323. At the MVA-only eight the pinball loss at q05 is 1.27 against 0.86 for BG2, mostly D8 (4.36).
  • twCRPS, days 1 to 10, mean over the group (default 3, BG2). Signed-MW 0.324, 0.355; MVA-only 0.206, 0.195. Default 3 is better at the signed-MW six and worse at the MVA-only eight, the same split as the CRPS.
  • Replicate months. None: demand-v1 has no replicate period.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control gate. The port reproduces experiment 322's stored default 3 at 168 to 240 hours on experiment 319's own rows at the six Primaries: 3.07596 points against 3.07596 (difference 2e-10, largest single-quantile difference 1e-5), well inside the 0.05-point gate. The gate runs the same replay as the 16-Primary run, on experiment 322's rows and fold structure.
  • Median against mean forecast. The median minus the mean is 0.00 at every Primary: the stored mean is the corrected mean around which stage 2 centres the quantiles, so the median equals it by construction and no independent mean-forecast contrast exists. The error of the median is reported beside the CRPS contrasts above, and agrees in direction in every row.
  • Triggers (the seven audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill). The control gate passed (trigger 1). The registered predictions hold (trigger 2). The error of the median and the CRPS agree in direction (trigger 3). No leave-one-out case flips a sign (trigger 4). Trigger 5 (a nested arm beating the arm that contains it) did not fire. The pooled signed-MW interval is 0.37 wide against 0.42 in experiment 377 (trigger 6). Trigger 7 (a later experiment will use default 3 as its base) applies, and a fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored forecasts by its own code (-0.121, +0.634, +0.158, and -0.034 against default 1, all within 0.01), found no lookahead in the fits and no unit error, and confirmed that the median equals the mean in experiment 377's stage 2. It did not check the bootstrap intervals, the control gate, twCRPS, or the leave-one-out table; the control gate was checked by the gate script above.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries, and the naive fit of experiment 377 is used at all eight. The rule-chosen fit of experiment 374 at 240 hours was not run.
  • D8 uses the donor spread in every arm here, so its row differs from experiment 377's own-residual arm (+3.97 here against +1.61 for the stack without S against BG2). It is unproven whether a generator connected to D8 explains the steps and the gap at D8.
  • The fits of S and of the blend are pooled within a group, so a Primary whose behaviour differs from its group's, such as D15, gets a fit that suits it less.
  • The sunny-half-hour, Christmas, and load-shift slices of experiment 377 were not recomputed here.
  • Experiment 378 reads the second-stage forecasts of experiment 377 and its stored ensemble arrays, so an error there carries into every number above.

docs.title: What does each component of BG2 contribute at all 16 Primaries, out to 14 days, under demand-v1?
docs.text:
Take-home message: a plain weekly-refitted XGBoost model scores within 0.05 percentage points of capacity of BG2 at the six Primary substations whose meters record the direction of power flow, and within 0.02 points at the eight whose meters record apparent power only. BG2 is the five-model blend built in experiment 87, so the blend adds little over its weekly-refitted XGBoost member, and two of its five members add nothing measurable. BG2's upper tail is too narrow at the six signed-MW Primaries: 93.2% of outcomes fall below its 95% quantile, and 97.6% below its 99% quantile. The verdict is supported: no single blend member, the solar offset twins, or the spread factor changes the score by 0.10 points or more.

We asked how much each part of BG2 adds to its score. A Primary substation steps 33 kV or 66 kV down to 11 kV, and the 16 Primaries here carry anonymised labels (D2 to D22). BG2 blends five models: weekly-refitted XGBoost (W), monthly-refitted XGBoost (M), an analogue model (AN), an XGBoost model pooled across substations of the same type (PT), and a frozen XGBoost model with a 14-day error correction (ST). Each model's quantiles are widened about its median by a spread factor of 1.15. At 5 of the 16 Primaries, the models also have twins that include a forecast of embedded solar output (the solar offset twins). We rebuilt BG2 from experiment 87's stored forecasts with no refit, as experiment 360 did at four Primaries. We re-blended BG2 without each member, and scored each member alone. The scoring follows the demand-v1 protocol at all 16 Primaries, at every lead to 14 days. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), estimated from 11 quantiles, in percentage points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of a Primary's capacity; smaller is better). The protocol reports three groups separately. The six signed-MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) have meters that record the sign of the flow. The eight MVA-only Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22) have meters that record apparent power only, so their numbers assume reactive power is zero. D15 and D18 have short histories and are reported without counting in any verdict. The reference forecasts are manual_heuristic (NGED's rule of thumb) and climatology (the average for each month, half-hour, and weekend flag). Production does not run BG2.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are CRPS in percentage points of effective capacity for forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead, unless stated. They cover the 3,660,652 half-hours scored by every arm in July 2025 to June 2026. A negative difference in a drop-one contrast means the dropped part helps. Pooled intervals are 99% intervals from resampling whole calendar months of the forecast origin (20,000 resamples). Per-Primary and leave-one-out intervals are 95% intervals (2,000 resamples).

  • BG2 scores 3.016 at the signed-MW six and 3.788 at the MVA-only eight. Without D8, the MVA-only eight score 3.236, and D15 and D18 together score 7.285. At the signed-MW six, manual_heuristic scores 3.606 and climatology 3.831. At the MVA-only eight they score 4.438 and 4.872. BG2 beats manual_heuristic by 0.589 (0.398 to 0.819) at the signed-MW six and 0.650 (0.504 to 0.823) at the MVA-only eight, and beats climatology by 0.814 and 1.084.
  • The weekly XGBoost model alone trails BG2 by 0.044 (0.006 to 0.090) at the signed-MW six. It scores 3.061. At the MVA-only eight it trails by 0.018 (-0.013 to 0.056) and scores 3.807, and without D8 it trails by 0.025 (-0.006 to 0.063). The gap at the signed-MW six shrinks with lead: 0.080 on day 1, 0.034 on days 5 to 7, 0.019 on days 8 to 10, and 0.014 on days 11 to 14 (-0.024 to 0.066). The weekly XGBoost model alone is within 0.14 points of BG2 at 15 of 16 Primaries; D15 is the exception at +0.617 (0.219 to 1.049). It scores better than BG2 on the point estimate at D4, D5, D8, and D9, with intervals that include zero.
  • Dropping the frozen-stack member (ST) changes the signed-MW six's score most. Dropping ST changes the score by -0.061 (-0.094 to -0.030) at the signed-MW six and -0.010 (-0.039 to +0.025) at the MVA-only eight. Dropping W changes it by -0.037 (-0.067 to -0.012) and -0.031 (-0.065 to -0.003), and dropping AN by -0.031 (-0.052 to -0.011) and -0.023 (-0.035 to -0.013).
  • The monthly XGBoost and pooled-by-type members add nothing measurable. Dropping M changes the score by -0.001 (-0.004 to 0.000) at the signed-MW six and 0.000 at the MVA-only eight. Dropping PT changes it by +0.005 (0.000 to 0.019) and +0.002, so BG2 scores marginally better without PT. PT alone is the weakest member, 0.401 (0.306 to 0.475) behind BG2 at the signed-MW six.
  • The solar offset twins help at the signed-MW six only. BG2 minus the same blend without the offset twins is -0.045 (-0.081 to -0.004) at the signed-MW six, where D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 carry the twins. It is exactly 0 at the MVA-only eight, which have none. At days 11 to 14 the difference is -0.011 (-0.035 to +0.026).
  • The spread factor 1.15 is not shown to matter. BG2 minus BG2 with spread factor 1.0 is -0.023 (-0.053 to +0.004) at the signed-MW six and +0.008 (-0.014 to +0.028) at the MVA-only eight.
  • Experiment 87's build-up of BG2 gains little at each step. The stages are the frozen XGBoost model, the same with a 14-day correction (the stack), monthly refitting, weekly refitting, the blend without offset twins, and BG2. At the signed-MW six they score 3.160, 3.209, 3.122, 3.090, 3.061, and 3.016, so the five steps change the score by +0.049 (-0.012 to +0.116), -0.087 (-0.203 to +0.006), -0.032 (-0.068 to 0.000), -0.029 (-0.066 to -0.002), and -0.045. At the MVA-only eight the six stages score 3.950, 4.023, 3.848, 3.807, 3.788, and 3.788. At D15 the frozen XGBoost model scores 34.366 against 35.178 for climatology, because its median is 0.47 of capacity too low, close to climatology's 0.54. The 14-day correction removes most of this bias. The training window of the frozen model was not checked.
  • Experiment 377's GAM stack, on the half-hours it shares with BG2. The stack is Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 hours. It scores 2.954 against BG2's 3.016 at the signed-MW six (difference -0.062, 99% interval -0.268 to +0.145), and 4.083 against 3.743 at the MVA-only eight (+0.340, +0.108 to +0.577). D8 drives the MVA-only gap: +1.589 (95% interval +0.534 to +2.871). It is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap at D8.

docs.title: Tail calibration
docs.text:
Pinball loss (in points of effective capacity) and coverage at four tail quantiles, and the threshold-weighted CRPS (twCRPS, which weights outcomes above each Primary's 95th-percentile reading more heavily), for forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead. Coverage is the share of outcomes below the quantile, and its nominal value is 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99.

Group Forecast Pinball 1% 5% 95% 99% Coverage 1% 5% 95% 99% twCRPS Signed-MW six BG2 0.222 0.686 0.878 0.321 0.010 0.045 0.932 0.976 0.353 Signed-MW six Weekly XGBoost alone 0.212 0.679 0.905 0.344 0.010 0.041 0.923 0.973 0.372 Signed-MW six manual_heuristic 0.280 0.792 1.011 0.457 0.050 0.070 0.892 0.921 0.413 Signed-MW six climatology 0.222 0.840 1.057 0.396 0.018 0.040 0.904 0.952 0.428 MVA-only eight BG2 0.261 0.863 0.970 0.353 0.005 0.042 0.955 0.995 0.195 MVA-only eight Weekly XGBoost alone 0.258 0.865 0.983 0.357 0.005 0.043 0.954 0.995 0.200 MVA-only eight manual_heuristic 0.413 1.005 1.162 0.476 0.068 0.094 0.903 0.930 0.238 MVA-only eight climatology 0.379 1.160 1.189 0.348 0.045 0.085 0.928 0.968 0.243
  • BG2's upper tail is too narrow at the signed-MW six. The 95% and 99% quantiles cover 0.932 and 0.976, below the nominal 0.95 and 0.99. The weekly XGBoost model alone is slightly worse (0.923 and 0.973).
  • BG2's tails are slightly too wide at the MVA-only eight. The 1% quantile covers 0.005 and the 99% quantile 0.995, against nominal 0.01 and 0.99.
  • The references have worse tail calibration than BG2. manual_heuristic covers 0.050 at the 1% quantile at the signed-MW six, five times the nominal value.

docs.title: Load-shift events, weather slices, and curtailment cost
docs.text:
• During hand-labelled load-shift events, BG2 scores 7.953 at the signed-MW six. The weekly XGBoost model alone scores 8.521 and manual_heuristic 9.040, on 35,150 half-hours.
  • In the 7 days after each event ends, the references beat BG2. BG2 scores 5.022 and the weekly XGBoost model alone 4.566, against 3.933 for manual_heuristic and 4.412 for climatology, on 26,870 half-hours at the signed-MW six.
  • On sunny half-hours from April to June, BG2 and the weekly XGBoost model alone are close. At the signed-MW six they score 3.692 and 3.717.
  • On cold nights (3 °C or below), the weekly XGBoost model alone trails BG2 by 0.33. At the signed-MW six, BG2 scores 4.531, the weekly XGBoost model alone 4.864, and the frozen-stack member alone 4.563.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, scaled limit. The cost is the measure of studies.eval_protocol at a price of £2,000 per MWh. The limit is 0.9 of each Primary's maximum flow before the scored year; the published thermal limit is not used. Summed over the six Primaries for the scored year, the cost is £8.35 million for BG2, £10.59 million for the weekly stage of experiment 87's build-up (no offset twins), £6.11 million for the frozen-stack member alone, £12.66 million for manual_heuristic, and £13.72 million for climatology. D16 drives the frozen-stack member's lead (£3.95 million against £6.05 million for BG2).
  • D15 and D18 (report only). BG2 scores 7.285 across both, the weekly XGBoost model alone 7.610, and manual_heuristic 10.769.
  • We found no replicate period. The stored forecasts start in July 2025, so no earlier year can be scored, and no month is excluded by the 12-month training-history rule.

docs.title: CRPS per Primary, days 1 to 10 (percentage points of effective capacity)
Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary: not available. BG2 and its members store 11 quantiles and no mean, so the check cannot run. The mean absolute error of the median, beside each CRPS contrast, is the substitute below.
  • Error of the median beside each contrast (days 1 to 10, points): the drop-one, offset, and alone-versus-BG2 contrasts have the same sign in the mean absolute error of the median as in CRPS. For example, dropping W changes the CRPS by -0.037 and the error of the median by -0.040. The weekly XGBoost model alone minus BG2 is +0.044 in CRPS and +0.074 in error of the median at the signed-MW six. The one disagreement we found is the spread factor at the MVA-only eight: CRPS +0.008, error of the median -0.016. The CRPS interval for that contrast includes zero.
  • Gates: the re-blended BG2 equals experiment 87's stored BG2 on all 4,099,680 forecast rows of the 16 Primaries (no gap above 0.000005 points). The actuals stored with experiment 87's forecasts equal the readings in the feature cache to 0.0001 MW on the 4,004,653 forecast rows where both exist. The fast month bootstrap of e00379_contrasts.py agrees with the protocol module's headline_month_bootstrap_contrast for BG2 minus BG2 without W at the signed-MW six. Both give -0.03684, and the intervals are -0.0669 to -0.0119 and -0.0659 to -0.0121, which differ only through the random draws.
  • Audit triggers. The ml-experiment skill lists seven. Four fired: trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction: P2, P3, and P4 below), trigger 3 (the CRPS and the error of the median disagree in sign: the spread factor), trigger 4 (dropping one Primary flips a contrast's sign: the step from the frozen XGBoost model to the stack at the signed-MW six, +0.049 in total and -0.002 without D5), and trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm that contains it: BG2 without PT scores slightly below BG2).
  • A fresh Sonnet audit. The audit re-derived the BG2 and weekly-alone CRPS, the drop-W contrast, the exact match between the re-blended and the stored BG2, the absence of leakage in the drop-one blend weights (each month's weights use only earlier valid months), and the unit handling. All were confirmed. It explained P2, qualified P3, and found the zero readings below. It did not check triggers 3 to 5, the tail table, or the curtailment cost. We accepted every finding.
  • Six isolated zero readings are scored. At D9 (5 half-hours, 50 forecast rows) and D16 (1 half-hour, 10 forecast rows), the feature cache holds a reading of exactly 0.0 between readings of 43 to 59 points of capacity, which looks like telemetry dropping out. Experiment 87's stored actual is missing for these rows and this experiment keeps them, so the signed-MW six's absolute score is 3.016 here and 3.014 on experiment 87's rows. The paired contrasts move by well under 0.01.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held: each drop-one change is under 0.10 points (the largest is 0.061).
  • P2 failed (weekly refitting beats monthly by 0.05 to 0.20). Weekly beats monthly by 0.022 (-0.047 to +0.002) at the signed-MW six and 0.041 (0.015 to 0.069) at the MVA-only eight. The audit found that experiment 87's 0.123 is an all-16-Primary figure, carried by D15 and D18 (0.56 to 0.69 each). The same stored forecasts give 0.032 at the signed-MW six and 0.041 at the MVA-only eight under the protocol, and the change of metric explains about 0.02 of the difference.
  • P3 failed (the offset gain is under 0.03 at the signed-MW six). The gain is 0.045. The prediction diluted the offset's effect over 5 of 16 Primaries, but 5 of the signed-MW six carry the twins, and each gains about 0.053. The gain spreads over all hours, including nights, so the contrast is BG2 minus the same blend without the offset twins. It also reflects the blend weights that are re-chosen when the models carry the twins. The audit could not separate those two effects.
  • P4 failed in both halves (each member alone within 0.30 of BG2, except ST, which trails by over 0.50). PT alone trails BG2 by 0.401, above 0.30, and ST alone trails by 0.145, under 0.50.
  • P5 held (BG2's lead over its best single XGBoost model narrows with lead). The gap narrows from 0.080 on day 1 to 0.014 on days 11 to 14.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Add the stack's 14-day error correction to the weekly XGBoost model alone. Compare the result with the five-model blend on cold nights, where the weekly XGBoost model alone trails BG2 by 0.33 points and the frozen-stack member does not.
  • Widen the upper tail of the weekly XGBoost model. Its 95% quantile covers 0.923 at the signed-MW six.

docs.title: Code and data
docs.text:
• Scripts are in ml-experiments/00379-bg2-components-all-16-primaries-to-14-days/. e00379_build.py imports experiment 87's assembly code (e00087_assemble.py and e00087_common.py) from that experiment's folder, and e00379_adapter.py is a copy of experiment 377's adapter.
  • Stored forecasts and scores are in data/ml-experiments/00379-*/work/ (private, never committed). Experiment 377's GAM stack is read from its work/ folder and never written.
  • Refit schedule. BG2 and its members keep the weekly and monthly refits that experiment 87 fixed, and no model was refitted here. The refit schedule is under test: the contrast between weekly and monthly refitting is one of the results.

docs.title: The GAM stack taken apart at all 16 Primaries, and why it is jagged
docs.text:
Two stages of the GAM stack carry its score and two do not. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation. The labels D2 to D22 are the study's anonymised labels, and they are not consecutive because the study covers 16 of the 22 substations in the original numbering. We took apart the forecasting pipeline (the "stack") that experiment 377 scored. Stage 1 is a generalised additive model (GAM) per Primary with a Kalman filter that corrects it from recent errors. Stage 2 is a winter night offset (a fixed correction to winter night-time forecasts), recipe R (a 14-day error profile subtracted from the forecast), and quantile bands whose width is refitted each month on earlier months. We removed one stage at a time and scored what remained against BG2, the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, a blend of five forecasts that production does not run. We also built the stack up from the plain GAM, and asked whether the stack does worse at the Primaries whose demand is less regular.

A score is the quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, which equals the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) up to the estimation from 11 quantiles. The unit is percentage points of a Primary's effective capacity (the capacity its meter can carry), and a lower score is better. "Signed-MW" Primaries are the 6 that report power in signed megawatts. "MVA-only" Primaries are the 8 that report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA); every number for those Primaries assumes reactive power is zero. D15 and D18 have under a year of history and are report only. A "step" is a half-hour change in power above 5% of capacity. In the lists below, "positive: the stage helps" means that removing the stage raises the score.

Verdict: partly supported. The Kalman filter and recipe R earn their place under the thresholds pre-registered in this page's front matter. The winter offset and the per-fold spread do not, apart from D8. The regularity hypothesis is not supported at n = 16, and 16 Primaries are too few to refute it.

docs.title: Results (quantile score, points of effective capacity)
docs.text:
• Arms. full is experiment 377's stack, rebuilt; it reproduces the stored quantiles exactly (largest difference 0.0 at all 16 Primaries). Stages: Kalman filter on stage 1's residuals (K), winter night offset (O), recipe R (R), per-fold spread (F). Not in the stack and not ablated: the solar summary S, the correction network H, and the daylight heuristic blend.
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10, mean over Primaries (full, plain GAM, BG2, manual heuristic, climatology). Signed-MW six: 2.95, 3.32, 3.02, 3.61, 3.83. MVA-only eight: 4.14, 4.87, 3.78, 4.41, 4.86. D15 and D18 (report only): 7.67, 19.98, 8.00, 13.30, 26.65. Pooled full minus BG2 (99%): -0.07 (-0.28 to +0.14) signed-MW; +0.34 (+0.09 to +0.60) MVA-only; +0.18 (-0.02 to +0.39) without D8. The plain GAM minus BG2: +0.30 (+0.07 to +0.54), +1.05 (+0.73 to +1.39), +0.61 (+0.38 to +0.90).
  • Removing one stage (positive: the stage helps), days 1 to 10, 99% interval (signed-MW six; MVA-only eight with D8; MVA-only seven without D8). K: +0.121 (+0.026 to +0.219); +0.465 (+0.179 to +0.821); +0.330 (+0.120 to +0.604). O: -0.002 (-0.011 to +0.008); -0.049 (-0.116 to -0.005); -0.003 (-0.020 to +0.012). R: +0.027 (+0.014 to +0.040); +0.095 (+0.047 to +0.149); +0.079 (+0.043 to +0.120). F (stage 1 tuning-month spread instead): -0.001 (-0.015 to +0.011); +0.270 (+0.138 to +0.420); +0.017 (-0.006 to +0.044). At D8 the per-fold arm is the own-residual spread and the replacement is the donor spread, so the +0.270 is D8's own effect of +2.21 (95% +1.37 to +3.12), averaged over eight Primaries, and not a general spread effect.
  • Thresholds from the plan. K (0.05): earns its place at both groups with D8; at the signed-MW six the point estimate is +0.12 and mostly comes from day 1. O (0.02): does not. R (0.02): earns its place at the MVA-only Primaries (+0.08 to +0.10) and at the signed-MW six (+0.027, just over the threshold, interval +0.014 to +0.040). F (0.02): does not outside D8.
  • Build-up (negative: the added stage helps), days 1 to 10 (signed-MW; MVA-only with D8; without D8). Adding F to the plain GAM: -0.001, -0.266, -0.039. Adding K: -0.328 (-0.466 to -0.193), -0.397, -0.293. Adding O: -0.011 (-0.031 to +0.008), +0.048 (-0.022 to +0.154), -0.022. Adding R: -0.027 (-0.040 to -0.014), -0.095, -0.079. The filter is the largest single step by far.
  • The Kalman filter by lead, filter removed minus full (signed-MW; MVA-only with D8). Day 1: +0.499 (+0.204 to +0.939); +0.646 (+0.340 to +0.963). Days 8 to 10: -0.074 (-0.293 to +0.115); +0.341 (+0.029 to +0.726). Days 11 to 14: -0.154 (-0.455 to +0.087); +0.303 (+0.003 to +0.666).
  • Leave one Primary out (95%). K stays positive and excludes zero whichever Primary is left out (signed-MW +0.075 to +0.150; MVA-only +0.330 to +0.524). R stays positive (+0.025 to +0.030; +0.079 to +0.107). O never excludes zero at the signed-MW six.
  • Slices, days 1 to 10, full against filter removed (signed-MW; MVA-only). Sunny daylight 4.49 against 4.27; 5.68 against 5.72. Sunny April to June 4.38 against 4.20; 5.58 against 5.53. Cold nights 4.18 against 4.94; 3.30 against 4.27. Christmas 4.38 against 4.20; 3.41 against 3.81. The filter makes the sunny-half-hour and Christmas scores worse at the signed-MW six, the slices where the stack trails BG2 (4.00 and 3.72 for BG2 on sunny daylight and Christmas).
  • D15 and D18. Without the filter the mean score of D15 and D18 is 17.2 (7.7 with it): D15 30.7 against 12.8, D18 3.6 against 2.5. Without the filter q95 coverage is 0.32 at D15. The unfiltered forecast there is badly biased and the cause was not investigated.
  • Jaggedness measures (registered in the plan; readings before 2025-07-01, hand-filtered events excluded). M1: share of variance in a half-hour-of-week profile, 0.12 (D15) to 0.65 (D9). M2: extra share explained by binned temperature, 0.01 (D4) to 0.50 (D3). M3: lag-1 autocorrelation of what remains, 0.84 to 0.98. M4: share of half-hour changes above 5% of capacity, 0.03 (D4) to 0.35 (D12). M5 (reverse-flow share, signed-MW six only) is 0.000 to 0.002.
  • Spearman correlation with the gap (stack minus BG2, days 1 to 10), registered sign in brackets. n = 16: M1 -0.02 (-) with permutation p = 0.94; M2 -0.02 (-) p = 0.94; M3 -0.19 (+) p = 0.46; M4 +0.19 (+) p = 0.48; M5 -0.21 (+) n = 6. The decision rule needs M1 at most -0.5 and M4 at least +0.5 with p under 0.025, so H2 is not supported. Leave-one-out ranges: M1 -0.24 to +0.09, M4 +0.04 to +0.39. Post hoc at n = 14 (D15 and D18 dropped): M1 -0.45 (p = 0.105), M4 +0.53 (p = 0.057), leave-one-out M4 +0.45 to +0.74. Both correlations point the registered way, and neither passes the decision rule. D15 (M1 0.12, M4 0.32) and D18 (M1 0.13, M4 0.21) have the stack ahead of BG2 (-0.51 and -0.15), against the registered direction. The gap is large at D8, D12, and D22, which have low weekly-profile shares (0.14, 0.18, 0.16), and at most +0.18 at D3 and D2, which have the highest shares after D9 (0.48 and 0.46); D9, with the highest share (0.65), has zero gap.
  • Placebo. Time-shuffled readings give M1 to M3 near zero (0.003, 0.0002, 0.00) and M4 near 0.82 (every Primary), so the measures read time structure. M1 is inflated on short histories (shuffled M1 is 0.57 at D15, 0.41 at D18, 0.03 at D9), so D15 and D18 are unreliable for M1 and the n = 14 rows are the cleaner test.

docs.title: Tail measures and curtailment cost
docs.text:
• Tail calibration, days 1 to 10, mean over Primaries (coverage q01, q05, q95, q99; pinball q05, q95). Signed-MW: full 0.022, 0.067, 0.946, 0.982; 0.773, 0.815. Filter removed 0.014, 0.046, 0.917, 0.968; 0.725, 0.914. Plain GAM 0.011, 0.036, 0.875, 0.952; 0.756, 1.007. BG2 0.010, 0.045, 0.932, 0.975; 0.686, 0.882. MVA-only: full 0.021, 0.070, 0.944, 0.982; 1.001, 1.124. Filter removed 0.024, 0.074, 0.928, 0.975. Spread removed 0.036, 0.088, 0.918, 0.963 (D8's donor spread and the stage 1 spread are narrow in both tails). BG2 0.005, 0.042, 0.955, 0.995. The stack's upper tail is better than BG2's at the signed-MW six (pinball q95 0.815 against 0.882) and its lower tail worse (q05 coverage 0.067 against 0.045). The full per-Primary table is below.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, limit 0.9 of the earlier maximum, in pounds (full, filter removed, plain GAM, BG2, manual heuristic). All rows: 4.24 million, 10.09 million, 10.59 million, 7.31 million, 10.41 million. Event rows (D5, D10, D14, D16 only; D9 and D11 have no scored half-hour above the limit): 2.81 million, 7.55 million, 7.80 million, 5.24 million, 6.88 million. The 7 days after events: 0.343 million, 0.226 million, 0.234 million, 0.285 million, 0.496 million.
  • At limit 0.5 (same order). All rows: 59.8 million, 85.2 million, 98.2 million, 72.9 million, 104.8 million. Event rows: 7.75 million, 22.99 million, 27.41 million, 11.96 million, 18.28 million. The 7 days after events: 3.25 million, 2.67 million, 3.09 million, 4.07 million, 3.57 million. The filter lowers the cost on all rows and during events. In the 7 days after events it raises the total at both limits, mostly at D16 at limit 0.9 (£45,000 without the filter against £155,000 with it) and with mixed signs by Primary at limit 0.5, which agrees with experiment 367's finding that the Kalman transient adds error after a step.
  • No input is nulled in this experiment, so there are no nulled rows to compare.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control. The arm full equals experiment 377's stored stack: the largest absolute difference in q50 and q95 is 0.0 at all 16 Primaries on the scored year.
  • Median minus mean forecast, per site. 0.0 at every Primary and every arm: the stored mean is the centre of the centred spread tables, so no independent mean-forecast contrast exists.
  • Predictions. P1 failed on days 1 to 10 (+0.12 and +0.47, not under 0.05) and held on day 1. P2 held at the signed-MW six (+0.027) and failed at the MVA-only eight (+0.095). P3 held at the signed-MW six and failed at the MVA-only eight (-0.049, D8; held without D8, -0.003). P4 held without D8 (+0.017) and failed with it (+0.270, D8's donor spread); q05 coverage worsened at the MVA-only eight (0.070 to 0.088) and moved from 0.067 to 0.064 at the signed-MW six. P5 held at the signed-MW six (+0.37) and failed at the MVA-only eight (+0.73). P6 failed.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 2 (predictions P1 days 1 to 10, P2 and P3 at the MVA-only eight, P5 at the MVA-only eight, and P6 failed, and the MVA-only misses are explained by D8 alone only partly); trigger 5 (the arm without the winter offset beats the full stack at the MVA-only eight, and the arm without the filter beats it at days 8 to 14 at the signed-MW six, within noise). Triggers 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 did not fire.
  • Placebos. A permutation placebo (10,000 shuffles of each measure across Primaries) gives the p values above; a time-shuffled-readings placebo gives M1 to M3 near zero.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The stack is experiment 377's, without S, H, and the heuristic blend; stage contrasts may differ in default 3, which experiment 378 builds.
  • The per-fold spread contrast at D8 compares the own-residual arm with the donor spread, so it reports D8's spread choice and not whether refitting the spread monthly helps.
  • D15 and D18 without the filter are badly biased; their contrasts are report only.
  • The regularity hypothesis was tested at 16 Primaries with measures M1 to M4 that are not independent of each other. A larger test would use more Primaries or simulated series with set regularity.
  • Next: a filter that fades out beyond day 7 (signed-MW days 8 to 14 score better without it), and a stack without the winter offset is a simpler release candidate.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
