A fresh Sonnet agent audited the numbers (about 75 quoted numbers, all 384 entries of the per-Primary tail table (16 Primaries, 3 arms, 8 measures), and a re-derivation of four Primaries' scores from the stored arms, which agree within 0.01 and 0.1 at D15) and a second agent reviewed the code. Findings and triage:

  • Accepted and fixed: D8's spread effect was misquoted (+2.21, not +1.6); the D15 score of 17.2 is a mean of D15 and D18; BG2's sunny-daylight score is 4.00; the sign conventions were missing from two list headings; P4 was not scored; the claim that the stack trails BG2 where steps are large, "after day 7" and "day 1 only" overstated the evidence; the offset harm is D8's; the post-event curtailment rise is mostly D16. The permutation p value now adds one to numerator and denominator, and the placebo header names which measure is near zero.
  • Rejected: the claim that D8's fold months were built from D8's own first reading and cover about two months. The control prints 219,674 D8 rows for full and the stored stack alike. The claim that stage 1's spread may be uncentred: the median minus the mean is 0.0 for every arm, including the arms that keep stage 1's spread.

docs.title: A single weekly XGBoost model for Primary demand against the GAM stack
docs.text: A single XGBoost model per Primary, refitted weekly, is as good as the GAM stack at 9 of 14 Primaries and better on average at the eight whose meters hide reverse flow. At the six Primaries with signed readings it is level on average but worse at D11 and D14, and its upper tail is narrower. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation, labelled D2 to D22. The XGBoost model is the weekly member of BG2 (experiment 87), which uses the weather forecast of the 51-member ECMWF ensemble, the local hour and day of week, bank-holiday distances, and the three most recent power readings. We tested seven small changes to it, one at a time, on monthly refits. We then refitted the three changes that helped, together, every week. The GAM stack is "Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 hours" from experiment 377, without the solar summary below 168 hours. All scores are CRPS (the quantile score over 11 levels) in points of effective capacity at days 1 to 10 on fold_a_daily_gap_v1, under demand-v1. A negative difference means the XGBoost model is better. Every MVA-only number assumes reactive power is zero. The XGBoost model is refitted weekly and the stack monthly, so the contrast mixes the model family with the refit schedule.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Hypothesis. Not supported as stated: the XGBoost model is not within +0.05 points of the stack at all 14 countable Primaries. Verdict "partly supported" because it is at 9 of 14.
  • Matches the stack (point estimate within +0.05). D8, D12, D22, D5, D2, D19, D4, D9, D21. The 95% interval lies wholly below zero at D8 (-1.62), D12 (-0.80), D22 (-0.29), and D5 (-0.25), although the audit's alternative bootstrap puts D5 at -0.62 to +0.11. Worse than the stack with an interval above zero: D14 (+0.30; +0.04 to +0.63) and D11 (+0.15; +0.02 to +0.30). Inconclusive: D10 (+0.16), D16 (+0.09), D3 (+0.050, which misses the tolerance by 0.0002). The worst Primary is D14. D15 and D18 are report only: +2.34 (0.14 to 4.24) over 4 months and +0.07 over 6 months.
  • Pooled, 99% interval. Signed-MW six +0.075 (-0.120 to +0.266). MVA-only eight with D8 -0.361 (-0.602 to -0.101), without D8 -0.197 (-0.399 to -0.025). Leaving one Primary out never changes the sign (signed-MW +0.03 to +0.14; MVA-only -0.20 to -0.42).
  • Against the other references. Minus BG2: +0.007 (-0.048 to +0.062) signed-MW, -0.016 (-0.069 to +0.042) MVA-only. Minus the stored weekly baseline: -0.038 (-0.092 to +0.008) signed- MW, -0.034 (-0.063 to -0.004) MVA-only. Minus manual_heuristic: -0.58 and -0.65. Minus climatology: -0.81 and -1.09 (all 99%).
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10 (bundle, stack, BG2, manual heuristic, climatology). Signed-MW: D5 3.83, 4.08, 3.94, 4.35, 4.48; D9 2.51, 2.51, 2.51, 2.92, 2.99; D10 3.43, 3.27, 3.45, 4.16, 4.31; D11 2.58, 2.43, 2.57, 3.41, 3.55; D14 2.51, 2.21, 2.39, 3.01, 3.47; D16 3.29, 3.20, 3.24, 3.80, 4.20. MVA-only: D2 2.28, 2.47, 2.30, 2.86, 2.93; D3 1.72, 1.67, 1.75, 2.11, 2.33; D4 2.42, 2.45, 2.51, 2.80, 2.83; D8 7.61, 9.23, 7.61, 8.31, 9.64; D12 6.72, 7.52, 6.75, 7.92, 8.83; D19 3.17, 3.29, 3.18, 3.79, 3.93; D21 2.36, 2.35, 2.38, 2.77, 2.91; D22 3.81, 4.10, 3.75, 4.71, 5.47.
  • Screening, each change minus the monthly control (99.86% interval, Bonferroni for seven arms). Daily mean shortwave (A2): -0.051 (-0.086 to -0.019) signed-MW, -0.016 (-0.049 to +0.023) MVA- only. 1-year half-life (A5): -0.019 (-0.034 to -0.006) and +0.004. Sunny flag: -0.002 at both groups. Economy 7 input (A1): 0.000 (-0.002 to +0.002). Lead-dependent half-life (A3): +0.007 and +0.025 (worse at MVA-only). 12-month window: +0.043 and +0.024. 0.25-year half-life: +0.072 and +0.039. The refitted control matches the stored monthly member in the median (mean gap 0.02 MW) but not fully in CRPS (up to 0.066 points at D16; see "Audit"). The screening used all 365 daily runs.
  • Predictions. P1 holds (9 of 14 against 9 to 11 predicted). P2 fails: the Economy 7 input moved the Economy 7 step hours by -0.002 (signed-MW) against a predicted -0.03 to -0.10. The local hour is already an input, so a tree can split on the step. P3 partly holds: the solar summary lowers the score on sunny April-to-June half-hours by 0.074 at the signed-MW six and 0.056 at the MVA-only eight. P4 holds (lead-dependent half-life +0.007 and +0.025, both under 0.03). P5 fails: the sunny flag removes about 0.15% of the D12 bias (4.92 to 4.91 points).
  • MVA-only handling. The control under-forecasts demand on sunny half-hours at D12 by 4.92 points of capacity (median minus actual) and over-forecasts it by 6.19 points at D19, 4.75 at D21, and 9.88 at D8. The sunny flag leaves each bias unchanged to within 0.05 points at the 14 countable Primaries. The rule-chosen reverse-flow column of experiments 366 and 374 is off at D12, D2, and D8 (the three checked) when computed from forecast shortwave (correlation +0.21 to +0.28 at D12 against a threshold of 0.3), so that arm equals the control by construction and was not fitted. The signed-MW six serve as controls: the sunny flag moves their bias by under 0.05 points.

docs.title: Tails and curtailment
docs.text:
Measure, days 1 to 10 Signed-MW bundle Signed-MW stack MVA-only bundle MVA-only stack Pinball loss q05 / q95 0.68 / 0.89 0.77 / 0.81 0.86 / 0.95 1.00 / 1.12 Pinball loss q01 / q99 0.25 / 0.36 0.26 / 0.27 0.25 / 0.33 0.28 / 0.33 Coverage q05 / q95 (ideal 0.05 / 0.95) 0.053 / 0.916 0.067 / 0.946 0.068 / 0.938 0.070 / 0.944 Coverage q01 / q99 (ideal 0.01 / 0.99) 0.007 / 0.984 0.022 / 0.982 0.013 / 0.992 0.021 / 0.982 twCRPS 0.372 0.327 0.197 0.226
  • The upper tail is the XGBoost model's weakness at the signed-MW six. Its q95 coverage is 0.916 and its q99 pinball loss is 0.36 against 0.27 for the stack. At the MVA-only eight the XGBoost model has the lower pinball loss at q05, q95, and q01, and the lower twCRPS.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, scored year. At a limit of 0.9 times the maximum observed export, the stack costs less at 4 of 6 (D16 £2.95 million against £6.64 million; D14 £0.54 million against £1.69 million). At a limit of 0.5 the stack costs less at all six. The cost is not defined at the MVA-only eight (reactive power assumed zero).
  • Load-shift events (hand-labelled). Event rows: signed-MW bundle 8.23 against stack 7.35 and BG2 7.96; MVA-only 5.18 against 5.46 and 5.15. The 7 days after: signed-MW 4.55 against 5.11 and 5.07; MVA-only 2.90 against 2.98 and 2.88. No pass or fail is drawn.
  • Lag-missing rows. Only 0.2% of scored half-hours have a missing power lag (3,630 at the signed-MW six, 3,226 of them at D5; 2,238 at the MVA-only eight). Their 5%-to-95% interval is 23.6 points wide at the signed-MW six against 20.1 on rows with lags, and 23.3 against 26.0 at the MVA-only eight. Coverage of that interval is 0.826 and 0.842 on missing rows, against 0.863 and 0.870 on present rows (nominal 0.90). No widening rule was fitted: 3,630 rows, concentrated in one Primary, are too few to fit a factor.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean. Not computed: the stored frames hold quantiles only and no mean. The mean absolute error of the median points the same way as CRPS at the contrasts that matter: D14 4.34 against 3.90 for the stack, D11 4.61 against 4.34, D8 14.06 against 15.94, D12 12.08 against 13.20.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fires: the Economy 7 prediction (P2) was contradicted, and the explanation (the local hour is an input) is structural and was not tested by a removal arm. Triggers 1, 3 to 6 do not fire. The leave-one-out contrasts keep their sign. Trigger 7 does not fire. The Sonnet audit and its triage are listed under "Audit" below.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lead range. The headline is days 1 to 10. Days 11 to 14 are not read here.
  • Schedule confound. The XGBoost model is refitted weekly and the stack monthly. The stack has no solar summary below 168 hours, so it is not the protocol's current research default.
  • Selection. The three changes were chosen on the scored year. The weekly bundle's gain over the stored weekly baseline (-0.04 signed-MW, -0.03 MVA-only) is an upper bound.
  • Next. Give the signed-MW six a better upper tail (a calibration step on the XGBoost quantiles). Try a custom folded-latent loss for the MVA-only reverse-flow bias. GAM partial effects as XGBoost inputs (out-of-fold values per refit) need a separate experiment.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored predictions with its own join and pinball code (report: briefs/e381_audit_report.md in the private data folder). Triage:

  • Headline numbers reproduce. Bundle at D5, D12, and D8 is 3.827, 6.716, and 7.615 (log: 3.829, 6.716, 7.612), and bundle minus stack is -0.253, -0.800, and -1.618 (log: -0.253, -0.799, -1.615). Accepted: nothing changes.
  • The reference gate is only partly met. The refitted monthly control differs from the stored monthly member by up to 0.066 points of CRPS per Primary (D16 breaks the plan's 0.05 gate) and by +0.031 on average at the signed-MW six. The printed gate was a median gap (mean 0.02 MW), not a CRPS gate. A cause such as GPU non-determinism is likely and untested. Accepted: the screening contrasts compare two refits made the same way, so they are unaffected, but the bundle's gain over the stored weekly baseline (-0.04 signed-MW, -0.03 MVA-only) is the same size as this reproducibility gap and is not read as a gain.
  • D5 is borderline. The agent's row-weighted month bootstrap gives -0.62 to +0.11 for D5 against the stack. Accepted: the headline names three Primaries (D8, D12, D22) with clear gains and D5 as borderline.
  • Screening rows. The screening used all 365 daily runs (4,012,330 half-hours), not the registered 292 fold_a_daily_gap_v1 runs. Accepted as a caveat: the final comparison uses the shared rows (2,824,844 half-hours, which BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology limit to the 292 runs, and the stack limits further at D8, D15, and D18).
  • Selection. Almost all of the bundle's gain over the control comes from the solar summary, and the sunny flag is kept on a 0.002-point effect, both chosen on the scored year. Accepted: stated in the caveats.
  • No leakage found. The previous-day shortwave mean is missing on the first day of every run, and every scored run is served by the latest refit at or before its origin. The daily shortwave mean has a negligible train-and-serve difference (half-hours with missing power are dropped from training).
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fires and its explanation holds: the control already has hour_local. Triggers 3 and 4 do not fire. The audit did not compute trigger 6, and did not rerun the tail, curtailment, or load-shift sections.

docs.title: Arms (pre-registered in the plan above)
docs.text: A1 Economy 7 input, A2 daily mean shortwave, A3 lead-dependent half-life, A4 sunny flag (the MVA remedy), A5 recency (0.25-year and 1-year half-lives, 12-month window), A7 rule-chosen reverse-flow column (not fitted, see above), and the bundle of A2, A4, and the 1-year half-life. A6 (GAM shapes as inputs) was not run.

docs.title: Plan as registered
docs.text: Plan (written before any score was read). The question is whether a plain XGBoost model, retrained every week and with no stacked parts, can match the GAM stack at each of the 16 Primaries. The baseline is the weekly member of BG2 (experiment 87), scored under the demand-v1 protocol by experiment 379. The baseline already holds the three recent-power lags (experiment 371 found these carry the gap at D8), the local hour and day of week, the distance to the nearest bank holiday and to Christmas, and lead_hours, so those candidates are in the control and are not tested again.

docs.title: Plan: pre-registered arms
docs.text:
• Control. Experiment 87's n1h recipe, refitted monthly for screening (the stored only_M arm of experiment 379 is the reference; the refit must reproduce it within 0.05 points before any other arm is read) and weekly for the final comparison (the stored only_W arm). colsample_bytree and colsample_bynode stay at 1.0 in every arm, so no arm gains from column subsampling.
  • A1, Economy 7. Adds two inputs: a 0/1 flag for the local half-hours 1 to 6 (the protocol's Economy 7 step hours) and the number of half-hours since local 00:30, clipped to 0 to 12.
  • A2, solar summary stand-in. Adds the mean forecast shortwave over the local day of the valid time (the same ensemble member, the same run) and the mean over the previous local day. It is a cheap stand-in for the GAM's two-number solar summary S.
  • A3, lead-dependent recency. Row weights use a half-life of 0.25 years for rows at leads under 48 hours and 1 year for rows at longer leads, in place of the single 0.5-year half-life.
  • A4, MVA remedy (eight MVA-only Primaries only; the signed-MW six are controls). Adds a sunny flag (forecast shortwave over the Haurwitz clear-sky irradiance above 0.6) and its product with shortwave. A second variant reads the rule-chosen fit of experiments 366 and 374 as an input column if the stored fit exists for the run origins and uses data from before each origin only; the plan records at the start of the work whether it does, and drops the variant otherwise.
  • A5, recency (maintainer, 2026-10-28). Experiments 17 and 34 found that a half-life of 0.5 years beats 2 years by 0.03 to 0.15 points (experiment 34) and that a 12-month sliding window is about as good (experiment 17: -0.92 for the half-life, -0.84 for the window, against an expanding window), while a 6-month window is worse. The control already uses 0.5 years, so the arms test the neighbours: hl025 (0.25 years), hl1 (1 year), and win12 (a 365-day window with the 0.5-year half-life). The half-lives are fixed here and not chosen on tuning months, which lie before the scored year.
  • A6, GAM shapes as XGBoost inputs (optional, only if time allows). Not run in this experiment. It would fit the GAM per fold on that fold's training window only, take its fitted partial effects for time of day, day of week, and temperature and its stage-1 fitted value, and give the training rows out-of-fold values (the GAM refitted with each training month held out in turn) so that no row sees an in-sample fit; the scored rows use the fold's full-window fit. This needs the GAM stack fitted on 12 held-out-month folds per refit, so it is a separate experiment.
  • A7, rule-chosen reverse-flow column (MVA-only eight; added 2026-10-29 at the manager's request, after the A1 to A5 screening). One extra column, no second model: experiment 366's rule recomputed at each monthly refit from that refit's training rows only (sunny midday readings: the Pearson correlation with shortwave above 0.3, or a 1st percentile below 1.0 point of capacity, switches the column on), times the fitted slope of those readings on shortwave, times the forecast shortwave. Prediction: the rule switches the column on at D12 only; the column is a monotone function of shortwave at D12, which a tree can already split on, so the arm moves the D12 score by under 0.02 points and leaves the sunny-half-hour bias at about -4.9 points. A bigger change would mean the shortwave inputs interact badly with the folded meter. Tested monthly at the eight MVA-only Primaries with the signed-MW six as unchanged controls (the rule is off there). A signed-capacity-times-irradiance column from the same fit is the same function again, so it is not run separately.
  • Bundle. The arms kept by the decision rule, fitted weekly.

docs.title: Diagnostics before the arms
docs.text:
• MVA handling. Residuals of the control (median minus actual) on sunny half-hours at D12 (known reverse flow), at the other seven MVA-only Primaries, and at the signed-MW six, by group and lead band, before and after A4.
  • Reference rows. The stack from experiment 377, BG2, manual_heuristic, climatology, and the stored weekly baseline, each reported with its absolute score.

docs.title: Tails and nulled inputs (maintainer, 2026-10-28)
docs.text: Tail pinball loss and coverage at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles are reported per group and per Primary beside CRPS and twCRPS, and the take-home names the tail result. The control and every arm already carry the three recent-power lags, which are missing (NaN) when the telemetry has a gap near the origin. The write-up reports mean 5%-to-95% interval width and coverage on half-hours whose lags are missing against half-hours whose lags are present, and tries one simple widening rule (scaling the quantile distances from the median by a factor fitted on the earlier months of the same fold) if coverage on the missing rows falls short.

docs.title: Avoidable-curtailment cost (maintainer, 2026-10-28)
docs.text: Because the arms feed missing lags on event rows, the write-up reports the protocol's avoidable curtailment cost (studies.eval_protocol) during each hand-labelled load-shift event, in the 7 days after it ends, and across all rows, per group and per Primary, beside CRPS and the tail measures. The cost is defined only for the signed-MW six, so the MVA-only eight carry the label "not defined". The take-home names it.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text: Sonnet only. At most 3 threads and MemoryMax=16G per job. The GPU is shared. Tail calibration, slices, load-shift rows, per-Primary table, leave-one-out, and the D8 own-residual and donor-spread arms follow the protocol page. Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries.

docs.title: Do three recent-power lags, added to the GAM stack as smooth terms, close the gap to monthly XGBoost at substation D8?
Do three recent-power lags, added to the GAM stack as smooth terms, close the D8 gap?
docs.text:
Giving the forecast three recent readings of the substation's power did not help at D8, the substation where the competing XGBoost method leads, and made D8's forecast worse. We asked whether a forecast of electricity demand improves when it is told how much power a substation drew in the hours just before the forecast was made. The extra readings raised D8's forecast error by 0.445 points of the substation's effective capacity (error 9.672 against 9.227). At 12 of the other 13 counted substations the error moved by under 0.05 points; at D22 it rose by 0.096.

The three readings are the newest one available at forecast time, the reading one day earlier at the target half-hour, and the reading one week earlier. Experiment 371 found that monthly XGBoost leads the GAM stack at D8 mainly through these readings. We gave the GAM stack of experiment 377 (Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 hours) the same readings. The stack fits in two stages: the first predicts from weather and calendar for each target time, so it cannot use readings taken before the forecast was made, and the second corrects the first stage's mean forecast. We added the readings to the second stage as smooth terms, each fitted every month on earlier months only. Each reading enters as the reading minus the stack's own forecast for that half-hour.

Scores are the quantile score (CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score estimated from 11 quantiles) in points of effective capacity; lower is better, and a contrast is the arm with the readings minus the stack without them. The "spline arm" is the pre-registered design, the "linear arm" is a sensitivity check, and the "penalised spline arm" was added after the audit. BG2 is the best-guess forecast of experiment 87. D8 and the other labels D2 to D22 are Primary substations. The signed-MW six are the six Primaries that report signed megawatts. The full design is in the plan below.

Results (days 1 to 10, spline minus default, 99% intervals, 20,000 resamples of whole months).

  • D8 (own-residual arm): +0.445 (+0.090 to +0.983); default 9.227, spline 9.672, BG2 7.615.
  • Days 1 to 2 at D8: +0.108 (-0.064 to +0.391). Days 3 to 10: +0.531 (+0.115 to +1.184). Days 8 to 10: +0.695 (+0.162 to +1.489). The harm grows with lead, the opposite of the prediction that the gain would be larger at days 1 to 2.
  • Signed-MW six: -0.019 (-0.052 to +0.008); days 1 to 2: -0.043 (-0.061 to -0.028).
  • MVA-only eight with D8: +0.055 (+0.012 to +0.125); without D8: +0.004 (-0.022 to +0.027).
  • Penalised spline arm (post hoc; smoothness penalty weight 100,000 in place of 10, added after the audit found the pre-registered weight almost zero; not adoptable): D8 +0.080 (-0.012 to +0.154); signed-MW six -0.027 (-0.056 to -0.004); MVA-only eight with D8 +0.004 (-0.018 to +0.023); D2 and D4 -0.026 (-0.054 to -0.003); short-history group +0.016 (-0.019 to +0.063).
  • Placebos D2 and D4 pooled: -0.023 (-0.066 to +0.007). The pooled change is slightly towards a gain, the opposite direction to D8, so neither placebo fails.
  • Per Primary (95%, pre-registered spline): D8 +0.445 (+0.127 to +0.838), D22 +0.096 (+0.037 to +0.159), D15 +0.283 (+0.020 to +0.654, report only), D14 -0.048 (-0.074 to -0.019), D4 -0.048 (-0.095 to -0.010). The spline wins at 10 of 14 counted Primaries. The worst Primary is D8.
  • Linear arm: D8 +0.089 (+0.004 to +0.162); signed-MW six -0.022 (-0.043 to -0.001).
  • D8 by month (days 1 to 10): +1.89 (2025-08), +1.46, +0.50, +0.20, +0.32, +0.03, +0.10, +0.07, +0.15, +0.03, +0.04 (2026-06). Leaving out August 2025 moves the pooled D8 difference from +0.445 to +0.293.
  • Donor-spread arm at D8: default 11.588, spline 12.112 (+0.524).

Tails. At D8 the coverage of the 0.05 quantile is 0.0589 (default) and 0.0583 (spline), of the 0.95 quantile 0.934 and 0.933, and of the 0.99 quantile 0.970 and 0.968, so the lags neither fix nor break the lower-tail undercoverage that experiment 377 found. The printed report holds the pinball loss at the four tail quantiles and the twCRPS per group and per Primary for all six arms. The twCRPS contrast at D8 is +0.050 (+0.011 to +0.118) (the spline is worse); at the signed-MW six it is -0.004 (-0.015 to +0.002).

Nulled rows. A row is nulled when any of the three lags is missing (a gap in the power record). Such rows are under 2% of every Primary: 19 to 3,226 rows per Primary against 55,178 to 172,783 un-nulled rows. Their coverage of the 5% to 95% interval is erratic because the samples are tiny (0.42 to 1.00), and interval width on nulled rows is not systematically wider, since the treatment adds no widening rule. A widening rule was not tried, because nulled rows are under 1% of every Primary except D15 (1.1%) and D5 (1.9%).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The zero-shift gate (no shift reproduces experiment 377's stored stack) was run at D2 only.
  • Median minus mean forecast per site is 0.0 points for default and spline at every Primary, so the spread does not shift the forecast. The mean-forecast absolute error at D8 rises from 15.93 to 16.47 points, in the same direction as the quantile score.
  • Triggers that fired: 2 (the result contradicts its prediction P1, and the only tested explanation is the monthly pattern above, which is post hoc) and 5 (the default arm, nested inside the spline arm, beats it at D8). Triggers 1, 3, 4, and 6 did not fire (the placebos did not fail; the quantile and median-error contrasts agree in sign; leaving one month out leaves D8 positive at +0.293 to +0.489). Trigger 7 does not apply. An independent audit by a Sonnet agent found no lookahead (it corrupted readings after the newest usable one and the anomalies did not change) and no code bug, and reproduced D8's stored forecast exactly. It found that the pre-registered penalty was almost zero and that D8's early fits rested on 21 to 29 independent daily origins per lead band; both are now stated here, and the post hoc penalised arm above was added in response. Not acted on: the missing intercept in the fit (a free constant made D8 worse in the audit's test), and the whole-table cleaning pass that 377 shares.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The terms are stage 2 additive terms, not stage 1 GAM terms and not interactions with the weather inputs. The refutation covers that form only.
  • D8 has under 12 months of history for the whole scored year. Its first scored month rests on one month of history, and its fits use 21 to 29 independent daily origins per lead band in August 2025 (rows per band overstate this, because the newest-lag term takes one value per origin). This departs from the 12-month rule in the plan, as experiment 377's D8 own-residual arm does. The linear and penalised versions stay slightly positive at D8 through spring 2026, so more history alone may not turn the result.
  • Rows before 2024-07 carry no shift in the spread pool of the early fold months, which slightly widens the treated spread there.
  • Next: the lags as origin-dependent inputs to stage 1, or an interaction of the day-lag anomaly with the stack's weather terms, tested at the Primaries with a year of history first.

Reuses experiment 377's folder (e00377s2_common, e00377s2_corrections, e00377s3_stack, e00377_adapter, e00377_score) unchanged, and studies.eval_protocol. Schedule: monthly stage 2 refits, weekly stage 1 fits as stored by 377; the contrast depends on the schedule only through the stage 2 fits. Lag source: the cleaned power the GAM trains on, available at forecast time up to 3.5 hours before the origin.

docs.title: Plan, registered before any score was read
docs.text:
Where the terms enter. The stack's stage 1 GAM predicts from the valid time's weather and calendar and does not depend on the forecast origin, so a lag measured from the origin cannot be a column of its design matrix without re-fitting stage 1 on one row per origin and valid time. The stage 2 correction already depends on the origin (it contains recipe R, a profile of recent residuals), so the terms enter there: one additive shift of the stage 2 mean, then the same fold-by-fold spread. This is a stage 2 smooth term, not a stage 1 GAM term, and the write-up says so in its opening.

The three lags and their anomaly form. For a run with origin o and a row with valid time v, the newest usable reading is the half-hour ending at o - 3.5 h (371's telemetry delay of 3 hours plus the half-hour a reading spans), the day lag is the latest earlier reading with v's half-hour of day, and the week lag is the latest earlier reading with v's weekday and half-hour, all no later than the newest usable reading (the definition of origin_lags in experiment 87). Each lag enters as an anomaly: the reading minus the stack's own corrected mean for that half-hour, taken from the run with the latest origin not after that half-hour (always before o, so it is known at o). The anomaly removes the daily and weekly shape that a raw lag would carry, which a lag-only additive term cannot remove.

No lookahead, and no leaky lags. Every lag time is at least 3.5 hours before o, so no lag is at or after the origin at any lead; the nullification of leaky lags that the feature pipeline does for lags shorter than the lead cannot trigger, and the code asserts that every lag index is at most the newest usable index. A missing reading gives no contribution (the term is zero), so absent data degrades to "default".

Term form. For each lag and each of the six protocol lead bands, a penalised cubic B-spline (8 basis functions, second-difference penalty, weight fixed at 10 before any score is read) of the anomaly, clipped to the 1st to 99th percentile of the fit rows; the shift is the sum of the three terms, fitted by penalised least squares on the residual of the stack's mean, on rows whose origin and valid time both precede the fold month's first instant (the 12-month rule), outside the hand-filtered events. The spread for each fold month is fitted on earlier months' residuals of the treated mean, each earlier month using its own out-of-fold shift. Fits start at cut 2024-07-01 (rows before it get no shift). A band with under 2,000 fit rows gets no shift and is listed. Sensitivity arm, pre-registered: the three terms linear (penalty weight infinite).

Arms. default (the 377 stack as stored, unchanged), default_plus_origin_lags, and default_plus_origin_lags_linear (sensitivity only; at most one pre-registered arm can be adopted, and it is the spline arm). BG2, climatology and the manual heuristic are the references.

Rows and unit. The 16 Primaries of experiment 377; D15 and D18 are report only, D8 follows 377's two-arm rule. Compute: 3 threads.

Tails and nulled inputs. The write-up reports pinball loss and coverage at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles per group and per Primary, beside CRPS and twCRPS, and names the tail result in the take-home. Rows whose lags are missing form the nulled rows; the write-up gives interval width and coverage on nulled and un-nulled rows, and tries a simple widening rule if coverage falls short.

docs.title: Nulled load-shift lags and wider bands in the weekly XGBoost model
docs.text:
Telling the weekly XGBoost model which of its power lags lie inside a load-shift event does not repair its upper-tail forecasts. The XGBoost model forecasts each Primary substation's half-hourly power 1 to 10 days ahead and is refitted every week. A load shift is a period when National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) moves a substation's load onto its neighbours. A power lag is the substation's own power at the forecast origin, at the same time on the latest day, or at the same time in the latest week. We took the hand-labelled load-shift events as known, which is a perfect detector, and tested three fixes on the forecasts whose power lags lie inside an event. The fixes were to set those lags to missing, to switch to a model with no power lags, and to widen the forecast band.

At the six Primaries whose meters report signed megawatts (signed-MW), the model with no power lags lowered the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lower is better), but the interval includes zero and the result rests on two events. At the eight Primaries whose meters report only apparent power (MVA-only), the same model raised the CRPS. The 5% to 95% band should contain 0.90 of the readings. Fixed widening left the signed-MW share at 0.77 to 0.82. Widening by a factor fitted on earlier months raised the share to 0.88 to 0.93, but the factor sat at its cap of 2 in most months, which doubles the band width. Gate O is the pre-registered test of whether perfect labels help enough to justify building a detector. Gate O failed, so the detector arm b2 was not run.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Verdict: not supported. Gate O fails four of its five conditions (listed under Gate O below); the detector arm b2 did not run, as the stop rule requires.
  • Rows: the contaminated-lag rows are rows outside events, days 1 to 10, with at least one of the three lags inside an event: 21,601 at the signed-MW six (6 months) and 22,232 at the MVA-only eight (8 months). They make up 2.2% and 1.6% of the main-score rows.
  • Arms: d, the weekly member of BG2 (experiment 87, stored). c1, event targets dropped, lags inside events set to missing in training and at test time, 30% pseudo-event lag dropout in training. c2, a lagless model (event targets dropped) served on the contaminated rows, d elsewhere. Fixed widening (k = 1.28, tuning-adjacent) and as-of widening (k from earlier months, cap 2) on the contaminated rows. Seed 0, colsample 1.0, weekly refits, ENS control-member training.
  • CRPS on contaminated rows (points of capacity), signed-MW six: d 5.477, c1 5.539, c2 4.153, d plus widening 5.296, c1 plus widening 5.326, c2 plus widening 4.070, BG2 6.095. MVA-only eight: d 3.197, c1 3.292, c2 3.846, d plus widening 3.326, c1 plus widening 3.442, c2 plus widening 3.967, BG2 3.150.
  • Contrasts against d (95% Bonferroni over 6, month bootstrap):
Group Contrast CRPS Tail pinball (mean of q95 and q99) signed-MW c1 + widening -0.15 (-0.86 to +1.06) -0.22 (-0.39 to +0.06) signed-MW c2 + widening -1.41 (-3.12 to +0.32) -0.70 (-2.23 to +0.06) signed-MW widening alone -0.18 (-0.46 to +0.16) -0.34 (-0.89 to +0.06) MVA-only c1 + widening +0.24 (+0.09 to +0.35) +0.11 (-0.05 to +0.25) MVA-only c2 + widening +0.77 (+0.17 to +1.54) +0.18 (-0.03 to +0.51)
  • Tail calibration on contaminated rows, signed-MW six (d, c1, c2, c2 plus widening): q95 pinball 2.29, 2.58, 1.58, 1.19; q99 pinball 0.58, 0.86, 0.43, 0.29; coverage of q95 0.774, 0.709, 0.743, 0.824; coverage of q99 0.917, 0.889, 0.926, 0.972; coverage of the 5% to 95% band 0.705, 0.696, 0.731, 0.820. At the MVA-only eight d already covers 0.882.
  • Nulled against un-nulled rows (signed-MW six, 5% to 95% band): d covers 0.705 on contaminated rows (width 21.7 points) and 0.876 on ordinary rows (20.2). Widening by 1.28 widens the contaminated rows to 27.8 points and lifts coverage to 0.774. c1 and c2 do not widen the band (22.7 and 21.7).
  • Main score, outside events, days 1 to 10, minus d (90% interval): signed-MW c1 -0.015 (-0.032 to 0.000), c2 -0.029 (-0.066 to 0.000); MVA-only c1 -0.004 (-0.018 to +0.009), c2 +0.011 (+0.003 to +0.019). Largest per-Primary difference among the countable Primaries: D12 +0.058 for c2. The report-only D18 is worse by +1.95 (c1) and +1.51 (c2), and D15 by +0.97 (c1).
  • Placebos D2, D9, D11, and D21: arms c2 and widening equal d, bit for bit.

docs.title: Gate O: whether perfect labels justify building a detector
docs.text:
1. The CRPS interval of c2 plus widening includes zero (-3.12 to +0.32), and the tail pinball interval includes zero (upper bound +0.06). Fails.
  2. The 5% to 95% coverage of c2 plus widening on contaminated rows is 0.820, 0.08 under 0.90. Fails.
  3. Main headline per group within 0.02: signed-MW passes; MVA-only c2 plus widening has an upper bound of +0.023. Fails for c2.
  4. No countable Primary worse than 0.05: D12 is +0.058 under c2. Fails for c2.
  5. Placebos identical to d. Passes.

docs.title: Where the c2 gain comes from
docs.text:
• Two events carry most of it. On the contaminated rows attributed to each event, c2 minus d is -3.69 for the D16 event of 17.5 days over Christmas and -4.77 for the D10 event in November. For the 42-day D5 event it is -0.83. Leaving out the D16 event over Christmas moves the signed-MW c2 plus widening contrast from -1.41 to -0.98 (the audit's attribution by lag gives -0.86, and -1.05 without the D10 event, and -0.44 without both). Leaving out the D5 events leaves it at -1.37 and -1.57.
  • The gain grows with time since onset. Signed-MW c2 minus d is -0.57 within 1 day of onset, -0.68 from 1 to 3 days, and -1.85 beyond 3 days. A detector can see events only after about a day (experiment 298), so the first-day rows are the ones it would miss.
  • No contaminated signed-MW rows lie in 20 December to 10 January, because the events that cover that period exclude the rows.
  • D18 is the exception that matters. One D18 event (December, 3 days) has a CRPS of 8.5 for d and 53.0 for c2, a rise of 44 points, and drives the report-only group's loss.

docs.title: Avoidable-curtailment cost
docs.text: The cost is in pounds at the scaled limit of 0.9 times the earlier maximum, over leads of 12 to 36 hours, for the signed-MW six (D9 and D11 have no event rows). No interval has been computed, because the metric returns one total per series. During events D16 costs 7.76 million pounds for d, 9.87 million for c1, 9.56 million for c2, and 7.31 million for d plus widening; D5 costs 241 thousand for d and 236 thousand to 246 thousand for the other arms; D10 and D14 cost about nothing. In the 7 days after events D5 costs 185 thousand for d against 162 thousand for c1; D16 costs 50 thousand for d against 63 thousand for c1 and 39 thousand for c2. Across all rows D16 costs 8.10 million for d and 10.16 million for c1, and no other signed-MW Primary differs between d, c1, and c2 by more than 3%. The D16 numbers come from one site and one long event, so they are a lead for later work, not a result.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed. The stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile score: stored in work/scores/rows.parquet and not tabulated here.
  • Audit triggers that fire: trigger 2 (the c2 gain at the signed-MW six was not predicted, the prediction was no change beyond 0.1 points of CRPS on contaminated rows with W) and trigger 5 (c2 plus widening scores better than c2 at the signed-MW six but worse at the MVA-only eight, and d plus widening is worse than d at the MVA-only eight). An audit by a fresh Sonnet agent re-derived every headline contrast from the stored arms (they reproduce) and found no training leakage; the audit's findings are in Caveats and limits below, and its report is in the private briefs folder.
  • Reproduction gate: a refit of arm d at 4 of 52 weekly refits differs from the stored weekly member by at most 0.0043 CRPS points at the 14 countable Primaries, and by 0.015 and 0.016 at D15 and D18 (GPU subsampling noise). The gate is read at the countable Primaries.

docs.title: Caveats and limits
docs.text:
• The event mask is padded by 24 hours on each side (the feature cache's padding). The audit found that in 54% of the signed-MW contaminated rows and 81% of the MVA-only ones no lag lies inside the unpadded event, only inside the padding. On the 9,864 signed-MW rows with a lag inside the unpadded event, d covers 0.542 (not 0.705) and c2 plus widening minus d is -2.63 (-3.58 to +0.54). The pre-onset padding also tells the oracle arms about an event the forecaster cannot yet know, on 2,040 signed-MW rows; dropping them moves the contrast from -1.41 to about -1.50.
  • The sample is smaller than the group names suggest. The signed-MW contaminated rows come from four series (D5, D10, D14, D16) and the MVA-only ones from five (D3, D4, D12, D19, D22).
  • Arm c2 is confounded. The lagless model drops event targets in training and all three lags together; only c1 isolates the nulling, and c1 shows nothing.
  • Arm d is the stored weekly member; arms c1 and the lagless model are refits. The refit-versus-stored difference was measured at 4 of 52 refits only (at most 0.0043 CRPS points), not at the events.
  • The as-of widening factor is pooled over 11 series, including the report-only D15 and D18.
  • Lead range: days 1 to 10 headline, leads to 14 days scored. NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days.
  • Reactive power assumed zero at the MVA-only eight.
  • The events are hand-labelled and known to the model at forecast time. A live detector sees an event only after about a day, so these numbers are an upper bound on what a detector could give.
  • Fixed widening factor 1.28 is tuning-adjacent: experiment 100 looked at the same year. The as-of factor reached its cap of 2 in most months (the full table is in work/arms).
  • Only 6 months at the signed-MW six hold contaminated rows, so a month bootstrap has wide intervals. Not scored: injected-transfer scoring (aim 2), the second tuning of the lagless model, and arm a.
  • Lag-encroachment sweep not run: the fitted boosters were not saved, because the fit script keeps only predictions, so a synthetic step in the lagged-power inputs cannot be scored.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a widening factor learned per Primary and lead from earlier contaminated rows, applied without any detector (for example on rows whose lag disagrees with the lagless forecast), reaches 0.90 coverage. Experiment 309 tests the disagreement signal.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text:
• Experiment 298's common module imports PyTorch, which a worktree synced without the gpu group lacks, so the neighbour tables were copied instead of imported.
  • pkill -f on a script name also killed the calling shell.

docs.title: What is special about the MVA-only Primaries?
docs.text:
None of the four guesses explains why the GAM stack trails BG2 at the MVA-only Primaries. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation. The labels D2 to D22 are the study's anonymised labels. The "MVA-only" Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22) report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes, and every number for them assumes reactive power is zero. The "signed-MW" Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) report power in signed megawatts. D15 and D18 have under a year of history and are short-history. The GAM stack of experiment 377 trails BG2 by +0.18 quantile-score points on average at the MVA-only Primaries without D8, where 3 of the 7 Primaries are ahead of BG2. It trails BG2 by +1.61 at D8. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity, and a lower score is better. We compared the two metering groups on their size, age, step rate, regularity, price response, and generators, and related each measure to the per-Primary gap by rank correlation (n = 16). Experiment 380's four measures are reused from its stored table: M1 (share of variance in the weekly profile), M2 (extra share explained by temperature), M3 (lag-1 half-hour residual autocorrelation), and M4 (step rate above 5% of capacity). The other measures are new here.

Verdict: not supported. No hypothesis meets the decision rule in this page's front matter. The groups do not differ on any measure except the two price correlations, and that difference has the sign opposite to the one hypothesis C predicts.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Group comparison (difference of medians, MVA-only minus signed-MW, 95% interval from resampling Primaries; Figure 1). Effective capacity: 7.99 against 8.11 MW, -0.12 (-5.27 to +6.41). Peak load: 8.2 against 7.7 MVA, +0.58 (-4.0 to +6.4). Neighbouring Primaries: 5.5 against 7.5, -2.0 (-4 to +2). Step rate above 5% of capacity (M4): 0.118 against 0.117, +0.001 (-0.099 to +0.093). 99th-percentile step: 16.7 against 9.2 points, +7.5 (-10.2 to +19.1). Share of half-hours with a step above 10%: 0.017 against 0.007, +0.009 (-0.035 to +0.037). Weekly-profile share (M1): 0.247 against 0.252. Coefficient of variation: 0.285 against 0.280. Lag-1-hour residual autocorrelation: 0.875 against 0.927, -0.052 (-0.135 to +0.030). Lag-1-day: 0.698 against 0.765, -0.067 (-0.173 to +0.091). Price correlation of the residual: 0.083 against 0.172, -0.089 (-0.233 to -0.003). Correlation of the half-hour change with the price change: 0.091 against 0.158, -0.067 (-0.145 to -0.001). A placebo with the price shuffled in time gives 0.002 against 0.004.
  • Hypothesis A, age: cannot be tested with the files. None of the hierarchy files gives a commissioning or install date. The first power reading is a proxy for the start of the record only: it is 2019-09 (the start of the stored telemetry) for all 8 MVA-only Primaries and for D5, D10, and D11 among the signed-MW Primaries, about 5 weeks later for D14, while D16 starts in late 2020, D9 in 2023, and D15 and D18 in 2024 and 2025. Every Primary with a later first reading is therefore signed-MW, which fits "newer Primaries have megawatt metering". The record start truncates the age of the other 12 Primaries, so the MVA-only group may be older or the same age.
  • Hypothesis B, size: not shown. Median effective capacity differs by -0.12 MW (interval above). Spearman correlation of capacity with the gap: +0.03 (n = 16), -0.30 (n = 14).
  • Hypothesis C, randomness: not shown. M1 to M4, the step sizes, and the coefficient of variation do not differ between groups. At n = 16 the rank correlations with the experiment 377 gap are +0.19 (M4) and +0.19 (steps above 10%), against the +0.4 predicted for M4. At n = 14 (D15 and D18 dropped), the steps above 10% reach +0.57 (p = 0.033, leave-one-out +0.47 to +0.71) and the lag-1-day autocorrelation reaches -0.59 (p = 0.029). About 200 correlations were computed (21 measures, 2 gaps, 5 sets of Primaries), so about 10 would pass p under 0.05 by chance.
  • Within the MVA-only group the gap follows the step rate. Across the 8 MVA-only Primaries, M4 has rho +0.79 (p = 0.031) and the steps above 10% rho +0.79 (p = 0.030); across the 7 without D8, M4 has rho +0.93 (p = 0.007, leave-one-out +0.89 to +0.94). The 6 signed-MW Primaries show rho +0.26 for M4 (p = 0.66) and +0.09 for the steps above 10%. The same relation holds for the experiment 378 gap (default 3 minus BG2, a gap in the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in points, where D8's gap is +3.97): +0.79 for M4 across 8, +0.93 across 7. D12 (M4 0.346, gap +0.76) and D22 (M4 0.210, gap +0.36) have the highest step rates and gaps, and the relation survives dropping any single Primary. D8's own gap (+1.61) does not follow from its step rate (0.128). D8's 99th-percentile step (41.9 points) is the largest of the 16. It is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap.
  • Hypothesis D, embedded generation: not shown, and only partly measurable. The hierarchy files list generators per bulk supply point, not per Primary, and only two bulk supply points (900004 and 900005) carry the 16 Primaries. The count of listed generators at the bulk supply point is 6 for both group medians, and its correlation with the gap is +0.07 (n = 16). The share of each Primary's load that is metered embedded generation cannot be formed from these files, so it is not reported.
  • Price-chasing: not higher at the MVA-only Primaries. The residual's correlation with the Market Index Data price (a proxy for the intraday price) is lower at the MVA-only Primaries and negative at D12 (-0.185) and D4 (-0.073). At n = 14 its rank correlation with the gap is -0.53 (p = 0.055): the Primaries that follow the price most have the smallest gaps.

docs.title: Confounding
docs.text:
• Metering group is confounded with first-reading date (all 8 MVA-only Primaries start at the record start, and the four later starters are all signed-MW) and with the short-history Primaries, which all report MW.
  • Generator counts take only two values within each group, so they cannot be separated from the bulk supply point.
  • Capacity, step rate, autocorrelation, and price correlation are not tied to metering group (Figure 1).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site and the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast: not applicable, because no forecast is made. The audit triggers for forecasting scores do not fire.
  • Measures use readings before 2025-07-01, with the hand-filtered events excluded, so none of them sees the scored year.
  • Placebo: the price shuffled in time gives group medians of 0.002 and 0.004, and rank correlations with the gap of -0.24 (n = 14, p = 0.41) and +0.12 (n = 16, p = 0.66).
  • First reading has no spread inside the MVA-only group, so its within-group correlation is undefined and is left out above.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• The data are 16 Primaries. A rank correlation has to be about 0.5 to reach p = 0.05, so a failure here is "not shown", not "false".
  • The within-group step relation was found after looking at 200 correlations and rests on 7 Primaries (it survives dropping any single Primary). Treat it as a hypothesis to test, for example by adding a step term to the GAM at D12 and D22, or by simulating series with set step rates.
  • Next: ask NGED for the commissioning dates of the Primaries and for the generator capacity behind each Primary, which would test hypotheses A and D directly.

docs.title: Code reuse
docs.text:
• Experiment 380's folder: M1 to M4 and the gap table (jaggedness_table.parquet), read, not rewritten.
  • Experiment 377's folder: e00377_adapter and e00377_score for the feature cache.
  • Experiment 378's folder: score_report.txt for the default 3 minus BG2 gap.
  • Experiment 10's folder: the Market Index Data price (market_index.parquet, provider APXMIDP).

docs.title: Top-down forecasts at four bulk and grid supply points: a GAM stack against a weekly XGBoost model
docs.text: A generalised additive model (GAM) with a correction stage, fitted on the aggregate readings of two bulk supply points and two grid supply points, scores 1.0 to 2.0 points of capacity worse than BG2 and about level with two simple benchmarks. A bulk supply point (BSP) connects the 132 kV electricity network to the 33 kV electricity network, and a grid supply point (GSP) connects the transmission network to the 132 kV electricity network. The four series are D13 and D17 (BSPs) and D1 and D6 (GSPs), labelled as in earlier experiments. "The stack" is the GAM of experiment 377, labelled "stack without S below 168 h": the stack has no two-number summary of solar output below 168 hours and no daylight blend. BG2 is the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, which at these series is its weekly-refitted XGBoost model alone (b_weekly). The two benchmarks are manual_heuristic (NGED's rule of thumb) and climatology (the typical value for the month, half-hour, and weekday type). A score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), estimated from 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity (percent of the series' capacity); a negative difference favours the stack. No research default exists for this family, so nothing is adopted. A simple XGBoost model refitted monthly, with and without the input changes of experiment 381, is scored beside the others (stage D).

docs.title: Results (CRPS in points of effective capacity; lower is better)
docs.text:
• Verdict. Refuted for both groups. Stack minus BG2, days 1 to 10, 99% interval from 20,000 resamples of whole months: BSPs +1.02 (+0.68 to +1.43); GSPs +2.01 (+1.41 to +2.60). The registered margin was +0.20 and both lower ends are above it. The BSPs and GSPs are never pooled together.
  • Per series (95%, 2,000 resamples). D13 +0.55 (+0.11 to +0.98); D17 +1.49 (+1.12 to +1.89); D1 +2.54 (+1.51 to +3.41); D6 +1.51 (+1.04 to +1.94). Leaving out one series leaves every pooled estimate above zero (BSP without D13 +1.49, without D17 +0.55; GSP without D1 +1.51, without D6 +2.54).
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10 (BG2, stack, manual heuristic, climatology). D13 4.68, 5.23, 5.47, 5.62; D17 7.06, 8.55, 8.39, 8.82; D1 14.06, 16.60, 16.97, 16.98; D6 13.68, 15.19, 15.50, 15.55.
  • The stack against the references (99%). Against the manual heuristic: BSPs -0.04 (-0.44 to +0.30), GSPs -0.34 (-1.02 to +0.13). Against climatology: BSPs -0.33 (-0.90 to +0.11), GSPs -0.37 (-1.27 to +0.56). All four intervals include zero. The stack scores better than BG2 at 0 of 4 series, than the manual heuristic at 3 of 4, and than climatology at 4 of 4 (days 1 to 10).
  • BG2 against the references (stage A rows). The references were scored in a first script on the half-hours shared by BG2, climatology, and the manual heuristic; the stack contrasts use the half-hours shared by all four arms. BG2's score differs by less than 0.001 points between the two row sets.
  • BG2 against the references (99%). BG2 minus the manual heuristic is -1.06 (BSPs) and -2.35 (GSPs); BG2 minus climatology is -1.35 and -2.38. All four intervals exclude zero.
  • By lead (stack minus BG2, pooled). Days 8 to 10: BSPs +0.68 (+0.39 to +1.01), GSPs +0.94 (+0.23 to +1.72). Days 11 to 14 (beyond NGED's horizon, descriptive): BSPs +0.62, GSPs +1.14. On day 1 the gap per series is D13 +0.90, D17 +2.39, D1 +4.94, D6 +1.64.
  • Slices (stack, BG2). The stack is worse than BG2 in every slice read, and level at BSP cold nights (5.21 against 5.20): sunny half-hours (BSPs 11.9 against 9.8, GSPs 15.2 against 14.2), winter nights, and Economy 7 steps. The gap is largest at the GSPs on Christmas (22.0 against 15.9) and bank holidays (22.4 against 14.6).
  • Tails, days 1 to 10 (stack; BG2). Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, q99 and coverage at the same quantiles are computed per series by e00386_score_b.py. Coverage at q05 is 0.063 (D13), 0.061 (D17), 0.104 (D1), and 0.055 (D6) for the stack against 0.028, 0.037, 0.042, and 0.044 for BG2; coverage at q95 is 0.935, 0.927, 0.971, and 0.949 against 0.927, 0.960, 0.955, and 0.935. The stack's lower tail is too narrow at D1 (0.104) and a little at D13 and D17; D6 is near nominal (0.055). The stack's upper tail is too wide at D1 (q95 coverage 0.971). BG2's lower tail is too wide at all four.
  • Curtailment cost is not scored: the metric needs the node and generator tables, and the readings here are the aggregates alone.

docs.title: Stage D: a simple XGBoost model, refitted monthly
docs.text:
A plain XGBoost model refitted monthly scores 0.04 to 0.06 points worse than BG2 at the bulk supply points and 0.26 to 0.28 points worse at the grid supply points, and the input changes of experiment 381 add nothing in the pooled groups. The control is experiment 87's n1h recipe (the BG2 weekly member) refitted monthly on the whole history with a 0.5-year half-life and 500 rounds. The bundle adds the daily mean shortwave, the sunny flag, and a 1-year half-life, as experiment 381's best bundle does. Experiment 381 has no forecasts at these four series, so both arms were refitted here (12 monthly refits per series, 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-01; boosters saved as .ubj files under work/boosters/monthly/ in this experiment's private data folder). BG2 is the stored weekly refit of experiment 87, so the control is meant to differ from BG2 in refit cadence only; the training rows, parameters, and half-life are experiment 87's code, which was not diffed against the stored BG2 run.

  • Widening. The stored BG2 has the width of a control widened by 1.15: its mean 90% interval width (q95 minus q05) is 158.5 MW against 137.9 MW for the raw control and 158.6 MW for the control widened by 1.15, which multiplies the distance of every quantile from the median by 1.15. Experiment 87's code applies this factor to its headline arms, and experiment 381's fit script does not. Every XGBoost arm is therefore scored raw and widened by 1.15 about the median (_w), and the widened arms are the like-for-like comparison with BG2.
  • Control minus BG2 (CRPS, days 1 to 10, 99%). Raw: BSPs +0.04 (-0.03 to +0.10), GSPs +0.28 (+0.02 to +0.63). Widened: BSPs +0.06 (+0.02 to +0.11), GSPs +0.26 (+0.05 to +0.49). Monthly refitting lowers the score by 0.04 to 0.06 points at the bulk supply points and by 0.26 to 0.28 points at the grid supply points, over days 1 to 10 (days 11 to 14: +0.13 at the grid supply points, interval -0.02 to +0.30).
  • Bundle minus control. Raw: BSPs +0.005 (-0.057 to +0.064), GSPs +0.013 (-0.190 to +0.298). Widened: BSPs +0.006 (-0.051 to +0.061), GSPs +0.018 (-0.173 to +0.292). The three input changes do not help here.
  • Against the stack. Widened bundle minus stack: BSPs -0.95 (-1.37 to -0.60), GSPs -1.74 (-2.48 to -0.85). Widened control minus stack: BSPs -0.96 (-1.39 to -0.59), GSPs -1.75 (-2.36 to -1.06). Both XGBoost arms beat the manual heuristic by about 1.0 (BSPs) and 2.1 (GSPs).
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10 (control, bundle, widened control, widened bundle). D13 4.72, 4.67, 4.74, 4.69; D17 7.09, 7.15, 7.13, 7.19; D1 14.33, 14.50, 14.36, 14.50; D6 13.97, 13.84, 13.91, 13.80.
  • Tails (widened control; widened bundle). Coverage at q05 is 0.031, 0.040, 0.044, 0.050 (control) and 0.031, 0.042, 0.046, 0.044 (bundle) for D13, D17, D1, D6; coverage at q95 is 0.924, 0.959, 0.952, 0.933 and 0.922, 0.964, 0.948, 0.934. These coverages are within 0.006 of BG2's. The 5% quantile covers fewer than 5% of readings at D13, D17, and D1, so the lower tail is a little too wide, as BG2's lower tail is.
  • Days 11 to 14 (descriptive). Control minus BG2 is +0.005 (BSPs) and +0.130 (GSPs); the bundle's gain over the control is again zero within the intervals.
  • Cadence. The control is refitted monthly and BG2 is refitted weekly. A release claim for either XGBoost arm would need a weekly refit.

docs.title: Lead bands and reverse flow
docs.text:
The stack's gap to BG2 shrinks with lead at all four series, and absolute scores are higher at the grid supply points than at the bulk supply points. CRPS in points of effective capacity on the shared half-hours of the scored year (stack, BG2, manual heuristic, climatology):

Series 0 to 24 h 24 to 72 h 72 to 168 h 168 to 240 h D13 (BSP) 4.92, 4.02, 5.58, 5.71 5.00, 4.20, 5.42, 5.63 5.21, 4.76, 5.44, 5.62 5.53, 5.10, 5.50, 5.61 D17 (BSP) 8.27, 5.89, 8.50, 8.85 8.40, 6.27, 8.33, 8.80 8.58, 7.23, 8.37, 8.80 8.71, 7.78, 8.44, 8.85 D1 (GSP) 15.81, 10.87, 17.11, 17.08 16.67, 12.03, 16.84, 16.92 16.70, 14.34, 16.80, 16.94 16.69, 16.16, 17.23, 17.04 D6 (GSP) 13.53, 11.90, 15.31, 15.37 14.74, 13.15, 15.51, 15.60 15.44, 13.87, 15.34, 15.48 15.73, 14.40, 15.76, 15.69
  • Gap to BG2, 0 to 24 h against 168 to 240 h. D13 0.90 to 0.42; D17 2.39 to 0.93; D1 4.94 to 0.53; D6 1.64 to 1.33.
  • Reverse flow, as a proxy for generation connected to the electricity network below each node. This experiment's data holds no capacity of that generation. Taking a negative reading to mean power flowing out of the node (the sign convention is assumed, not checked here), the share of scored-year half-hours with a negative reading is 50% at D1 (GSP), 16% at D6 (GSP), 10% at D17 (BSP), and 3% at D13 (BSP). The lowest reading is -94 to -101 points of capacity at D1, D6, and D17, and -36 at D13. Reverse flow is more common at the grid supply points, but the share is not a measure of generation capacity.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean. The stack's median equals its mean exactly (difference 0.0 at all four series), because the spread is added to the corrected mean as a centred table. The check cannot expose a shifted forecast here. BG2 stores no mean.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile score. The mean-forecast error was not computed; the error of the median forecast (MAE of the median, days 1 to 10) is printed and agrees in direction with CRPS at all four series (BG2 8.33, 12.62, 25.91, 24.89 for D13, D17, D1, D6).
  • Triggers fired. Review trigger 2 (a result contradicts a registered prediction): the result contradicts its registered predictions P1 and P2 (stack minus BG2 expected at most +0.40 and +0.80). The lead pattern supplies an untested explanation (the stack lacks BG2's recent-power input). No later experiment depends on this result yet. An audit by a fresh agent is requested in the pull request; its findings are triaged there.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Code and reuse. ml-experiments/00386-*/ copies experiment 377's stack (e00386b_* and e00386bs*_*) and experiment 161's input rows; the ensemble arrays are rebuilt from the local ECMWF archive (read only, no fetch), and the rebuild reproduces the stored arrays of another substation (D10) exactly. BG2, climatology, and the manual heuristic are experiment 87's stored forecasts on fold_a_daily_gap_v1.
  • What could not be fitted. The PV capacity is pinned to zero at all four series (no record of when each installation's capacity changed exists), so the stack has no explicit solar term; the stack has no regional wind or solar input, which experiment 36 found helped at GSPs.
  • Protocol. demand-v1 metrics, folds by month, 12-month minimum history (all four series have more than 12 months). The protocol's group table knows only the Primaries, so the scoring script adds the labels BSP and GSP. The stack refits monthly.
  • Stage D rows. Experiment 87's training rows and the daily frames are reused; the cut-offs of every refit follow experiment 87's leakage checks. The bundle of experiment 381 was chosen on Primaries, not on these series.
  • What to try next. A stack with a recent-power term at these aggregates, and a stack with the embedded generation and storage under each node as explicit terms.

docs.title: A folded loss for one XGBoost model at the MVA-only Primaries
docs.text:
The folded loss did not help, and the signed power it reports follows the start we gave the fit, not the readings. At D12, the one Primary substation known to have reverse flow, the folded XGBoost model scored 0.149 points of effective capacity worse than the plain XGBoost model (99.75% interval -0.061 to +0.378, which includes zero), and it left the under-forecast of sunny half-hours unchanged (median minus actual of -5.07 points against -5.04). Across the eight MVA-only Primaries the difference was +0.052 (-0.083 to +0.203), so the experiment cannot tell the two apart on the score. The recovered signed power is negative at sunny midday on 68% to 98% of half-hours at six MVA-only Primaries where earlier experiments found no reverse flow, and on 41% to 97% at six signed-MW Primaries where we added none. A signed MW forecast at an MVA meter therefore needs a structure that fixes the sign. Verdict: not supported (the sunny-bias and sign clauses of the hypothesis fail; the score clause is inconclusive).

The plain XGBoost model under-forecasts sunny half-hours at D12, and a folded loss might fix that. D12 and the other D-codes are anonymised primary substations of NGED, the electricity distribution network operator that supplies the data. At eight of the 16 Primaries ("MVA-only") the meter records apparent power in megavolt-amperes, which has no sign, so reverse flow (embedded solar generating more than the substation's demand) looks like demand. We trained one XGBoost model per Primary to predict a signed latent power l: the power a meter would show if it recorded direction. The loss compares the absolute value of l (smoothed, see below) with the metered reading. We asked whether this lets the model learn the V-shape that reverse flow makes in the readings, with apparent power falling towards zero at midday and rising again, and so give a signed MW forecast. Experiment 381 found the plain model under-forecasts sunny half-hours at D12 by about 5 points. Experiment 365 and experiment 366 supply the known-answer device of discarding the sign of a signed series. Reactive power is assumed zero, apart from a floor Q0 described below.

Each arm refits the plain model's recipe with a different loss, monthly. The recipe is experiment 87's: rows of the ensemble weather forecast's control member from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ENS), a recency half-life of 0.5 years, 500 boosting rounds. Each arm forecasts 73 daily runs (fold_a_every5d_v1) for days 1 to 14, scored under the demand-v1 protocol for days 1 to 10. All scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity, a percentage of the Primary's capacity. The arms are the plain model (XGBoost's built-in quantile loss), F0 (a custom quantile loss with no fold), and F2 (the same loss applied to the folded value sqrt(l² + Q0²), with Q0 of 0, 2, and 4 points). Q0 is a floor for the reactive power that keeps a real apparent-power reading above zero. F2 starts its boosting from the plain model's fit minus a tilt proportional to the forecast shortwave irradiance, which is the "start tilt" below. We did not run F1 (a folded squared loss), F3 (a sign-then-magnitude pipeline), or a weekly refit.

Departures from the plan. The plan scored fold_a_daily_gap_v1, but the fits forecast the 73 runs of fold_a_every5d_v1, so no comparison with the GAM stack or BG2 is made. Contrasts C2, C4, and C5 and predictions P4 to P6 were not tested. The placebo below had no pre-registered threshold, so the conclusion that the sign follows the tilt rests on a control added after the plan.

docs.title: Scores
docs.text:
Absolute scores. The refitted plain model matches experiment 379's stored monthly member (only_M) with a mean absolute gap of 0.0065 MW in the median over 409,968 rows (MW here because the stored member is in MW). F2 (Q0 = 2) is 0.01 to 0.10 points better than plain at D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21, 0.21 worse at D8, and 0.34 worse at D22.

Primary Plain F0 F2, Q0 = 0 F2, Q0 = 2 F2, Q0 = 4 D12 6.860 7.067 7.009 7.009 7.003 D8 7.763 8.218 7.987 7.976 7.995 D22 3.930 4.266 4.280 4.272 4.270 D19 3.290 3.285 3.223 3.226 3.216 D4 2.517 2.500 2.501 2.506 2.500 D21 2.407 2.387 2.338 2.328 2.326 D2 2.328 2.307 2.300 2.294 2.296 D3 1.759 1.702 1.663 1.657 1.659

The folded loss does not lower the score at D12 or pooled. The two confirmatory contrasts use 99.75% intervals (four contrasts, Bonferroni); every other interval on this page is descriptive.

  • C1, F2 (Q0 = 2) minus plain: eight MVA-only Primaries +0.052 (-0.083 to +0.203); without D8 +0.029 (-0.120 to +0.155); D12 alone +0.149 (-0.061 to +0.378). On sunny half-hours: -0.012 (-0.147 to +0.143) pooled and +0.066 (-0.347 to +0.521) at D12.
  • C3, F2 (Q0 = 2) minus F0: eight Primaries -0.058 (-0.087 to -0.030); D12 alone -0.058 (-0.129 to +0.012), the same size as pooled with an interval that includes zero. On sunny half-hours: -0.287 (-0.467 to -0.161) pooled and +0.080 (-0.374 to +0.300) at D12.
  • F0 minus plain (descriptive): +0.110 (-0.026 to +0.253) pooled and +0.207 (-0.012 to +0.439) at D12, so the custom loss alone scored worse in this run, with an interval that includes zero. On sunny half-hours it is +0.275 (+0.111 to +0.530) pooled.
  • Leave-one-out, C1: every 95% interval lay within -0.07 to +0.19, and the point differences were +0.010 to +0.074.
  • Sensitivity to Q0 (descriptive): Q0 = 0 against 2 is +0.004 (-0.001 to +0.009); Q0 = 4 against 2 is -0.000 (-0.007 to +0.006). The floor does not matter at this precision.
  • Sunny-half-hour bias at D12 (median minus actual, so a negative value is an under-forecast): plain -5.04 points, F0 -3.38, F2 -5.07. At D19 the bias is +6.2 for plain and +6.3 for F2.

F2's quantile band is too narrow at all four tail quantiles. Pooled over the eight Primaries (nominal coverage 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99):

Arm Coverage q01 q05 q95 q99 Pinball q01 q05 q95 q99 Plain 0.013 0.071 0.932 0.991 0.248 0.890 0.986 0.331 F2, Q0 = 2 0.024 0.090 0.895 0.965 0.265 0.955 1.042 0.301

F2's q99 pinball loss is 9% lower than plain's, although its coverage is further from 0.99. At D12 the q01 pinball loss is 0.305 for plain and 0.443 for F2. Threshold-weighted CRPS is 0.200 for plain and 0.201 for F2. We did not score the half-hours affected by nulled power-lag inputs or by load shifts, because the avoidable curtailment cost is not defined for unsigned MVA meters.

docs.title: The recovered sign follows the start, not the readings
docs.text:
The known-answer gate was passed, but it was too easy. We took the six signed-MW Primaries, subtracted a synthetic solar plant (a multiple of ERA5 shortwave, sized from the training window only) to create reverse flow, discarded the sign, and trained on the unsigned series alone. Reactive power was added in four settings. With the start tilt at 1.0, F2 recovered the sign of the reverse-flow half-hours: balanced accuracy (the mean of the recall on reverse-flow half-hours and the share of other half-hours correctly left positive) was 0.89 to 0.92, recall 0.89 to 0.98, and the false-reverse rate 0.12 to 0.14, at every reactive setting and at Q0 of 0, 2, and 4. The signed error on reverse-flow half-hours was 5.8 to 6.6 points against 21 to 25 for the plain model. With no tilt the balanced accuracy was 0.50, the same as the plain model's. The gate was too easy because the injected solar has the same linear form in shortwave as the tilt. A rule that sets the plain median negative when ERA5 shortwave exceeds a threshold fitted on the training window scored a balanced accuracy of 0.94 to 0.96 and a false-reverse rate of 0.07 to 0.08, better than F2 on both.

At the MVA-only Primaries the sign is wrong at six of eight. Earlier experiments (experiment 366, a rule on readings and irradiance, and experiment 370, which estimated PV capacity at the eight Primaries) found reverse flow at D12 and at none of the other seven, with no signed truth at any. F2's latent power is negative at sunny midday (ERA5 shortwave above 600 W/m², 10 to 14 UTC, days 1 to 10) on this share of half-hours: D2 0.74, D3 0.68, D4 0.07, D8 0.98, D12 0.17, D19 0.77, D21 0.70, D22 0.98. The share is low at D4 and D12 and 0.68 to 0.98 at the other six, so the readings did not set the sign. The low value at D4 is not explained.

With no injected solar the folded model still reports reverse flow. At the six signed-MW Primaries, with the sign discarded and nothing injected, F2 (Q0 = 2) recovers a negative power at sunny midday on this share of half-hours: D5 0.97, D9 0.41, D10 0.94, D11 0.43, D14 0.64, D16 0.81. True reverse flow (below -1 point) is absent at D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16 and covers 6.5% of these half-hours at D10. Over all half-hours of days 1 to 10 the false-reverse rate is 0.02 to 0.16, and the mean absolute error of the signed power is 8.0 to 11.8 points against 5.4 for the plain model, pooled over the six Primaries. This is the control the gate lacked.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The custom loss and the plain model differ in more than the loss. XGBoost's built-in quantile loss rewrites each leaf value from the residuals, which a custom objective cannot copy, and the custom objective's Hessian is a constant (e00387_fit.py:96), so its leaf values follow a step rule, not a Newton step. F0 and F2 also start from the plain model's predictions on its own training rows and then boost 500 more rounds, so they get 1,000 rounds against the plain model's 500. "F2 minus plain" therefore mixes the fold with a weaker optimiser, and "F2 minus F0" is the cleaner contrast, against a weak reference. An independent audit confirmed the gradient (the finite-difference self-test passes) and these points. The latent's median column is read before sorting, so it could differ from the sorted median where quantile levels cross; the latent is a diagnostic and the crossing rate was not measured.

The mean absolute error of the median points the same way as the score. The forecasts store 11 quantiles, not a mean, so we report the mean absolute error of the median in place of a median-minus-mean check: plain 6.895, F0 7.028, F2 (Q0 = 2) 6.931 points, averaged over the eight Primaries. Scoring uses the folded quantiles of the reading, which are valid quantiles of the metered value; the signed latent is a diagnostic and no score depends on it.

Two review triggers fired. The result contradicted its prediction (we predicted -0.05 to -0.25 points at D12), and the known-answer control was too easy. The checks above and the placebo are the response.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• A signed MW forecast at the MVA-only Primaries needs the sign fixed by structure, for example a latent built as demand minus a non-negative generation term that is monotone in shortwave, with the generation capacity estimated as in experiment 370. Neither the loss nor a tilted start identifies the sign.
  • The fold left the D12 under-forecast of sunny half-hours unchanged (-5.07 against -5.04), although the custom loss alone moved it (F0, -3.38). Look at the ensemble's shortwave spread and at a sunny-day input.
  • Give each arm of a custom-loss comparison the same number of rounds, and compare against XGBoost's built-in quantile loss.

docs.title: Which lagged-power columns improve the simple weekly XGBoost demand model at the 16 Primaries?
docs.text:
Take-home message. None of the five column sets lowered the CRPS of the simple XGBoost demand model. Six weekly analogues made the forecast worse at 12 of the 16 Primaries, and the other column sets either changed nothing or were worse. The verdict is not supported.

We asked whether more columns of past power help an XGBoost model forecast Primary substation demand 1 to 10 days ahead. We refitted the model with each of five column sets on the 1st of each month, scored the forecasts on a year of held-out data, and subtracted the scores of the current model (experiment 381's stored monthly control). A positive difference means the extra columns made the forecast worse. The pre-registered prediction for the weekly analogues (a change between -0.10 and +0.05 points) failed for arm A.

Figure 1. Every arm's CRPS minus the baseline's at days 1 to 10, per group of Primaries. Points to the right of the dashed line are worse than the baseline.

Figure 2. The contrasts at leads of 0 to 24 hours.

Figure 3. The contrasts at leads of 72 to 168 hours.

Figure 4. Lag-encroachment sweep: the share of a plus or minus 5% step that the median follows, for a step on the newest lag reading, the two newest, and every lag.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and recipe. The baseline is the three origin lags (the newest usable reading, the reading at the latest earlier time of the same half-hour of day, and the reading at the latest earlier time of the same weekday and half-hour). A is six weekly analogues (five new columns: the one-week analogue equals the baseline's week lag up to about 6.9 days of lead). B is their mean and median. C is two anomaly columns. E is the baseline without the newest reading. F is E with the day lag replaced by the power exactly 24 hours before the valid time. All arms use experiment 87's n1h recipe with monthly refits (192 fits each), column subsampling fixed at 1.0. Arm D was not fitted, because B and C did not each help alone.
  • Row set and scoring. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, protocol demand-v1, 16 Primaries, valid times from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30, CRPS in points of effective capacity, headline band days 1 to 10. The scorer reads actuals from the shared, unfiltered cache of experiment 103. The check column (below) drops the flagged half-hours.
  • Baseline. Experiment 381's stored monthly control. Its absolute CRPS at days 1 to 10 is in work/score_monthly_final.log; the highest of the 14 scored Primaries is 7.65 at D8 and the lowest 1.75 at D3, and D15 (report only) is 15.60. Baseline minus reference, positive when the baseline is worse (signed-MW six; MVA-only eight): BG2 +0.096 (+0.040 to +0.169) and +0.042 (-0.011 to +0.120); manual_heuristic -0.494 (-0.677 to -0.335) and -0.588 (-0.797 to -0.381); climatology -0.720 (-0.965 to -0.509) and -1.029 (-1.348 to -0.727).
  • Days 1 to 10, arm minus baseline, 99.83% intervals (signed-MW six; MVA-only eight). A: +0.137 (+0.069 to +0.195); +0.047 (-0.104 to +0.125). B: +0.049 (+0.002 to +0.092); +0.002 (-0.092 to +0.057). C: +0.008 (-0.016 to +0.041); +0.002 (-0.020 to +0.019). E: -0.022 (-0.075 to +0.005); +0.001 (-0.012 to +0.024). F: +0.044 (+0.022 to +0.069); +0.096 (+0.052 to +0.146). F minus E: +0.066 (+0.026 to +0.128); +0.095 (+0.060 to +0.133).
  • By lead band. A is worse in every band at the signed-MW six (+0.182 at 0 to 24 hours, +0.131 at 168 to 240 hours). E gains nothing beyond 24 hours in the MVA-only group (-0.007 at 168 to 240 hours) and loses +0.029 (+0.009 to +0.048) at 0 to 24 hours, so the prediction that E would help beyond 24 hours without losing below it failed. F is worse than the baseline at 0 to 24 hours by +0.136 (signed-MW six) and +0.165 (MVA-only eight), and at 24 to 72 hours by +0.108 (signed-MW six) and +0.179 (MVA-only eight). At 72 to 240 hours F's interval includes zero at the signed-MW six (+0.013 and +0.011).
  • Per Primary (arm A, 95% intervals). Arm A is worse at 12 Primaries, with the interval above zero. It is lower at D15 (-1.725, -2.775 to -0.513; report only, 4 scored months) and at D8 (-0.171, -0.499 to +0.035, an interval that includes zero). Leaving out any one signed-MW Primary keeps the contrast between +0.111 and +0.151. Placebos: D2 +0.077 and D4 +0.146, both worse, so the loss is not specific to D8.
  • Tails (days 1 to 10, mean over Primaries; baseline against arm A). At the signed-MW six the 0.95 quantile pinball loss is 0.949 for the baseline and 1.011 for A, the 0.99 quantile pinball loss 0.386 and 0.404, and coverage of the 0.95 and 0.99 quantiles is 0.909 and 0.980 for the baseline against 0.898 and 0.977. Arms C, E, and F are within 0.02 of the baseline's tail numbers; arm B's 0.95 quantile pinball loss is 0.972.
  • Weekly cadence check (descriptive). Refitted weekly with the same code, arm A minus the weekly baseline is +0.145 (+0.069 to +0.231) at the signed-MW six and +0.066 (-0.058 to +0.138) at the MVA-only eight, close to the monthly contrasts. Weekly arm B is partial (384 of 832 fits) and weekly arms C, E, and F were not fitted, so none is scored.
  • Slices (CRPS, baseline against A, E, F). On the event rows (experiment 383's row set) at the signed-MW six: baseline 8.789, A 9.050, E 8.313, F 8.733. On cold nights at the signed-MW six: baseline 4.933, A 5.385, E 4.703, F 4.901. These slices are post hoc and carry no interval. Arm E is lower on both slices.

docs.title: Sweep results
docs.text:
A prediction-only sweep adds a synthetic step of plus or minus 2%, 5%, and 10% of capacity to the lagged-power inputs, then forecasts eight runs, at four Primaries (D8, D4, D10, and D5), for the baseline and arms A, B, and C, to day 10. The runs are served by the refit of 2026-06-23, the latest weekly refit of the scored year, a rule fixed before any score was read. The sweep uses a separate fit of that date, with the trained XGBoost models saved.

  • The median follows only a fraction of the step. For a step of 5% of capacity, the baseline's median shifts by 0.04 of the step when only the newest reading is shifted, 0.20 when the two newest are, and 0.39 when every lag is shifted. Arm C follows more (0.12, 0.28, 0.47). When every lag is shifted, arm A follows 0.44 of the step, arm B 0.39, and the baseline 0.39.
  • No arm widens its band much. The width of the 1% to 99% band stays within 3% of its unshifted width in every arm and lead band up to a step of 5% (arm C reaches 1.029), and within 5% at a step of 10% (maximum 1.047, arm C).
  • The step level usually lies inside the bands. At a step of 5% the level lies inside the 1% to 99% band in 93% to 100% of rows, and q95 (q05 for a negative step) reaches it in 70% to 100% of rows. At a step of 2% the bands cover it in 96% to 100% of rows.
  • Shifting every lag by -5% worsens the CRPS. Against the observed power, the CRPS rises by up to about 1.0 point (0.91 for A, 0.96 for B, 0.97 for C). The full tables are in work/sweep_run.log.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Pre-registered predictions. P1 (arms A and B move the score by -0.10 to +0.05) failed for A (+0.137) and held for B (+0.049, at the edge). P2 (largest gain at 72 to 168 h, near zero at 0 to 24 h) failed: A is worst at 0 to 24 hours (+0.182). P3 (arm C within 0.05) held (+0.008). P4 (no placebo moves unless D8 does) failed: D2 (+0.077) and D4 (+0.146) moved while D8 did not.
  • Median minus mean forecast, per site (points of capacity, baseline). This gap shows whether an arm shifts the whole forecast distribution while leaving its median alone.
