docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Four of the six signed-MW Primaries rarely come near zero, so the folded test has little power. The test cannot run at D12, which reverses flow, because its series is already folded. Experiments 152, 372, and 374 found a fold gain at D12 only, with an interval including zero over a full year.
  • The folded quantiles are the sorted absolute values of the 11 quantiles. This is exact where the whole forecast sits on one side of zero and understates the mass at zero otherwise.
  • No Primary has a stored reactive-power series alongside its active power (the prior-work check searched experiments 79, 110, 152, and 358), so true MVA was not built.
  • One option for a next test is a term for the lowest-demand state at the MVA-only Primaries, where the median forecast is 16.0 points of capacity too high under 10% of peak.

docs.title: Does the ensemble mean or the ensemble spread give the simple XGBoost demand model its gain at all 16 Primaries?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the mean of the 51 ensemble weather members gives the simple XGBoost demand forecast its gain from those members, and the spread of the members adds almost nothing. Here "the simple XGBoost demand forecast" is the monthly-refitted XGBoost model of the half-hourly demand of 16 Primary substations. We gave that model, as extra inputs, only the mean across the 51 members of the temperature and of the shortwave radiation (the mean-only arm), or only their standard deviation (the spread-only arm). The error score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in percentage points of each substation's effective capacity. The mean-only arm lowers it by 0.052 points at the 6 substations whose meters record the direction of flow (the signed-MW six) and by 0.029 points at the 8 whose meters record apparent power only (the MVA-only eight). The spread-only arm lowers it by 0.001 and 0.008 points. Neither input fixes the tails: on cold nights the 95% quantile of the forecast still lies above only 0.77 to 0.78 of outcomes at the signed-MW six, against a nominal 0.95. The verdict is supported: the mean-only arm recovers about 110% of the gain of experiment 389's four-column arm at the signed-MW six and 82% at the MVA-only eight, and the spread-only arm recovers about 1% and 24%.

Experiment 389 found that four extra input columns (the mean and the standard deviation across the 51 members, each for temperature and for shortwave) lowered the CRPS by 0.047 and 0.035 points at the two groups, and that the gain looked like an effect of the mean. This experiment splits the four columns into two arms of two columns each. Both arms use the recipe of the stored monthly forecast of experiment 87 (12 monthly refits at all 16 Primaries). The control is that stored forecast, which receives none of the extra columns. All quantiles are widened about the median by a factor of 1.15, as in experiment 87. Experiment 389's four-column arm is the second comparison. The hypothesis and two predictions (see the front matter) were written after experiment 389's scores and before either arm was scored. The mean-only score was read before the spread-only arm was scored, so the spread-only comparison is not blind.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are in points of effective capacity for forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead on the half-hours of July 2025 to June 2026 that every arm scores (3,844,106 half-hours, a different set from experiment 389's because the arm set differs, so S0M and S1M differ from experiment 389's printed values in the third decimal). Intervals are 99% intervals from resampling whole calendar months, 20,000 resamples. All numbers come from e00394_score.py and e00394_bins.py.

Group Arm CRPS MAE of median q05 q95 q99 Signed-MW six Stored monthly member (S0M) 3.121 5.375 0.034 0.932 0.986 Signed-MW six Four columns (S1) 3.074 5.284 0.037 0.925 0.985 Signed-MW six Mean only 3.069 5.281 0.037 0.926 0.985 Signed-MW six Spread only 3.121 5.373 0.034 0.930 0.985 Signed-MW six BG2 3.016 5.244 0.045 0.932 0.976 MVA-only eight Stored monthly member (S0M) 3.847 6.855 0.043 0.955 0.995 MVA-only eight Four columns (S1) 3.812 6.796 0.049 0.949 0.994 MVA-only eight Mean only 3.818 6.808 0.048 0.950 0.994 MVA-only eight Spread only 3.839 6.847 0.043 0.953 0.995 MVA-only eight BG2 3.788 6.766 0.042 0.955 0.995

The q05, q95, and q99 columns are the share of outcomes below that quantile (nominal 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99).

  • Mean-only arm. Mean only minus S0M: -0.052 (-0.082 to -0.009) at the signed-MW six, -0.029 (-0.044 to -0.013) at the MVA-only eight, and -0.041 (-0.057 to -0.025) at the eight without D8. Leaving out any one Primary leaves each contrast negative with a 99% interval excluding zero (-0.050 to -0.054 at the six; -0.024 to -0.041 at the eight). Mean only lowers the CRPS at 14 of 16 Primaries; it is worse at D8 (+0.058) and D15 (+0.403, report only).
  • Spread-only arm. Spread only minus S0M: -0.001 (-0.011 to +0.013) at the six, -0.008 (-0.014 to -0.002) at the eight, and -0.009 (-0.014 to -0.003) at the eight without D8. The spread-only arm lowers the CRPS at 12 of 16 Primaries (11 if D16, where the change is -0.0005, counts as zero).
  • Mean and spread together. Mean only minus S1: -0.005 (-0.019 to +0.006) at the six and +0.006 (+0.002 to +0.010) at the eight. Spread only minus S1: +0.047 (+0.011 to +0.072) at the six and +0.027 (+0.010 to +0.042) at the eight. The mean-only arm recovers about 110% of the S1 gain at the six (0.052 of 0.047) and 82% at the eight (0.029 of 0.035), so the prediction of at least 70% holds. The spread-only arm recovers 1% at the six and 24% at the eight (0.008 of 0.035), so the prediction of under 30% holds.
  • Tails. A negative change in absolute coverage error means the share of outcomes below the quantile moved towards nominal. Against S0M at the signed-MW six, the change at q95 is +0.006 for the mean-only arm (99% interval -0.006 to +0.012) and +0.002 for the spread-only arm (-0.004 to +0.006). At q05 it is -0.003 for the mean-only arm (-0.005 to -0.001), a small gain from 0.034 to 0.037 towards 0.05. At the MVA-only eight the change at q95 is -0.004 and -0.001. At q99 the intervals include zero except at the MVA-only eight (-0.0004, -0.0009 to -0.0000, and -0.0002, -0.0006 to -0.0000). No arm moves any coverage by more than 0.006.
  • Cold nights. The share of outcomes below q95 at the six is 0.775 (S0M), 0.769 (S1), 0.776 (mean only), 0.769 (spread only), and 0.800 (BG2), over 44,370 half-hours; at the eight it is 0.851, 0.850, 0.855, 0.849, and 0.845. Mean only lowers the CRPS on cold nights by 0.086 (six) and 0.113 (eight) against S0M; spread only by -0.006 and 0.032.
  • Sunny half-hours (April to June). Mean only lowers the CRPS by 0.131 (six) and 0.070 (eight); spread only raises it by 0.011 (six) and 0.017 (eight).

docs.title: Spread terciles
docs.text:
The maintainer expected spread to help when weather uncertainty is high and to calibrate sunny summer half-hours. We cut each Primary's rows, within each of the five lead bands of experiment 389, into terciles of the ensemble's temperature spread at the row's lead, and scored every arm in each tercile. All-hour rows are the stored half-hours of days 1 to 10 with a finite actual (not the scorer's shared set). Intervals resample the calendar months of the valid time (13 months, because leads run past 30 June 2026).

  • High spread does not favour the spread columns. At the signed-MW six, spread only minus S0M at q95 is -0.003, +0.007, and +0.011 points in the low, middle, and high temperature-spread terciles (99% intervals -0.016 to +0.013, -0.004 to +0.023, and +0.002 to +0.022), so it is worse in the high tercile. At the eight it is -0.010, -0.004, and +0.001.
  • The mean's gain is also largest in the low-spread tercile. At q95, mean only minus S0M is -0.023, -0.011, and -0.013 at the six and -0.014, -0.011, and -0.007 at the eight; the interval of every tercile at the six includes zero, as does the high tercile at the eight.
  • q05 and q95 coverage barely moves across terciles. At the six, the share below q05 for S0M is 0.044, 0.035, and 0.036 across the three terciles; the arms move it by at most 0.004. The share below q95 is 0.947, 0.937, and 0.931 for S0M; the arms move it by at most 0.008.
  • June to August sunny half-hours: no arm calibrates them. Sunny means the ensemble-mean shortwave is in the top quarter of all of a Primary's June-to-August rows, night included, so the selection is roughly the brighter half of daytime rows. Terciles cut the shortwave spread within each Primary and lead band. At the six, the stored monthly member's q95 covers 0.98, 0.97, and 0.97 of outcomes in the low, middle, and high shortwave-spread terciles, above the nominal 0.95, and the mean-only arm covers 0.970, 0.966, and 0.965; the q95 pinball loss falls by 0.047, 0.036, and 0.051 points with the mean, and by 0.012, rises by 0.004, and rises by 0.009 with the spread. The scored year holds only 3 June-to-August months (July and August 2025, June 2026), so the intervals resample whole days (99 to 102 days per tercile); they are too narrow to trust as a month-level claim.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not computed: the stored frames hold quantiles and no mean. The mean absolute error of the median falls in step with the CRPS (mean only 5.281 against 5.375 at the six), so the quantile and median contrasts point the same way.
  • Triggers. Audit trigger 2 (a result that contradicts an earlier experiment's finding) fired. Experiment 371 found that an ensemble-mean arm added 0.007 points, and this experiment finds 0.052 and 0.029. A possible explanation is that experiment 371 changed only the prediction inputs while the arms here train on the columns. This experiment did not test that explanation.
  • Audit and review. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the pipeline these arms share with the four-column arm in experiment 389. It re-derived the four-column contrasts from the stored forecasts and found no use of a later forecast run or later weather in the training rows or the prediction rows. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed this experiment's code after scoring had started and found no blocking problem.
  • Leaving one Primary out. Leaving out any one Primary does not flip the sign of the mean-only contrast. For the spread-only arm at the signed-MW six the leave-one-out contrasts range from -0.003 to +0.001, with intervals that include zero, which matches the pooled contrast.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• No fresh S0M refit. The control is the stored monthly member, as in experiment 389; experiment 389's audit found that a fresh refit of it at D5 and D12 (4 of 192 fits) differed from the stored member by -0.002 to +0.004 CRPS, while S1 differed from it by -0.143 to +0.340 at the same refits.
  • Cleaned data and the short-history cut. Experiment 87's pipeline, which these arms inherit, predates the standing practices that clean the power data of substation_zero half-hours and cut D15 and D18 before 2025-03-01, so the result holds for the stored recipe and not for a cleaned one.
  • Four columns, two variables. The mean-only and spread-only arms each hold the columns of temperature and of shortwave together, so the page cannot say which variable carries the gain.
  • Lead range. All scores run to days 1 to 10; days 11 to 14 are in the log.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: The mean of the 51 members carries the gain, which suggests testing the mean of each weather variable the model already uses, and the temperature mean without the shortwave mean, to see which variable carries it. The cold-night under-coverage stays open, because no ensemble input moved it.

docs.title: A level state, a winter re-score, spread bins, a short-history anchor, and lag-event harm, all on stored forecasts
docs.text:
A level filter on the weekly XGBoost model's own residuals closes part of the model's gap to the GAM stack at D14 and widens it at D11, so the filter is not the whole explanation. The weekly bundle is experiment 381's XGBoost model (solar summary, sunny flag, 1-year half-life). The GAM stack is experiment 377's stack without its smoothing stage S below 168 hours. D11 and D14 are two of the 16 Primaries (primary substations) scored here. The filter follows experiment 136's two-state filter, which in turn follows the variational noise filter of de Vilmarest and Wintenberger (2022). Experiment 390 found that a rolling median offset does not copy the filter.

Terms used below. A load-shift event is a labelled period in which load was moved between Primaries. The signed-MW six (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) are the Primaries whose readings are signed megawatts, and the MVA-only eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22) report apparent power only. D15 and D18 have under a year of history and are reported separately. K0 to K4 are the Part A arms. Experiment 383's arm d is the plain weekly member, c1 drops the lags that lie inside an event, and c2 serves a lagless model on rows with a lag inside an event and arm d elsewhere. S0M and S1M are experiment 389's arms (S1M adds the ensemble mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation as columns; S0M does not). Economy 7 is a UK off-peak electricity tariff. An event's depth is its labelled change in load in megawatts, and the padded mask is experiment 390's mask, which extends each labelled event by 24 hours on each side.

Nothing in this experiment is refitted. Every number re-scores forecasts that earlier experiments stored, so the monthly-refit rule does not apply. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of the Primary's effective capacity), for days 1 to 10 unless stated, on fold_a_daily_gap_v1 under demand-v1. Intervals resample whole months, or whole events in Part F. "Raw" means the stored forecast without widening, and _w means widened by the factor 1.15 about the median.

docs.title: Part A: a level state on the weekly bundle
docs.text:
The stack's two-state filter closes 41% of the bundle's D14 gap and widens its D11 gap. K0 is the stored weekly bundle. K1 runs experiment 377's two-state filter (a level plus an AR(1) transient, one filter per hour band, pooled noise settings from e00377_run.noise_hyper) on the bundle's residuals, using readings at least 3.5 hours before the origin. K2 is a one-state random-walk level with a gain and a per-half-hour decay fitted per Primary on an expanding window (prior gain 0.05, decay 0.998 where there is no training data), and K3 pools K2's two numbers across the 16 Primaries.

Primary K0 K1 K2 K3 GAM stack D11 2.577 2.672 2.615 2.679 2.429 D14 2.510 2.387 2.45 2.44 2.209
  • K1 at D11 is worse than K0 by +0.095 points (interval +0.035 to +0.152).
  • K1 closes 41% of the D14 gap, K2 closes 19%, and K3 closes 25%.
  • On the signed-MW six, K0 scores 3.023, K2 3.001, K3 3.000, K1 3.043, and the GAM stack 2.949.
  • On the MVA-only eight, K0 scores 3.721, K2 3.743, and K1 3.804.
  • In the 0 to 24 h band on the signed-MW six, the raw scores are K0 2.564, K1 2.457, K2 2.399, and the GAM stack 2.293 (widened by 1.15: K0 2.584, K2 2.429).
  • Raw cold-night q95 coverage on the signed-MW six rises from 0.736 (K0) to 0.772 (K2) and 0.812 (K1), against 0.880 for the GAM stack (widened by 1.15: 0.773, 0.806 and 0.841).
  • K4 (the GAM stack without its filter, plus K2, on six Primaries) scores 2.898 against 2.954 for the stack on the same rows, so K4 beats the stack by 0.056 points, more than P3's 0.03 band, in the favourable direction. K4 has no interval, and it is worse than the stack at D14 (2.263 against 2.211).

P1 and P2 fail, P3 and P4 hold, so the porting threshold is not met. P1 fails: K1 closes at least half of the gap at neither D11 nor D14. P2 fails: K2 closes under half at D14 and widens the D11 gap. P3 holds: K4 recovers the stack's score within 0.03 points. P4 holds: the 0 to 24 h band improves, so the transient does not hurt it. The porting threshold is not met.

docs.title: Part B: winter re-score
docs.text: Economy 7 columns change nothing, and the ensemble mean and spread columns help cold nights. Against monthly/control, the Economy 7 arm differs by -0.000 on the winter signed-MW six (interval -0.004 to +0.004), and by +0.005 at D14 in winter (+0.001 to +0.012). Experiment 389's S1M (mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation as columns) differs by -0.040 on the signed-MW six (-0.065 to -0.010), -0.031 on the MVA-only eight, -0.058 at D11, -0.032 at D14, and -0.070 (six) and -0.144 (eight) on cold nights. S0M equals the control. S1M closes 36% of the D11 gap and 7% of the D14 gap; the solar arm closes 12% of the D14 gap. Cold-night q95 coverage on the signed-MW six is 0.734 for the control, 0.726 for S1M, and 0.879 for the GAM stack. P5's top-quartile and pooled clauses are not scored here, and S1M's pooled interval excludes zero, so P5 is untested. In winter the S1M difference on the signed-MW six is -0.019 (-0.093 to +0.091), against -0.040 over the year, so winter does not carry the gain.

docs.title: Part C: spread bins
docs.text: S1M's gain over S0M does not rise with temperature spread. Experiment 394's tables were not available, so only the top-decile and regime bins are scored. S1M minus S0M by temperature-spread bin: lower tercile -0.038, middle -0.017, upper -0.020, top decile -0.019 (-0.053 to +0.018). By the share of the 51 ensemble members below 5 °C at the week's coldest day: all warm -0.023, 0 to 25% +0.021, split +0.015, 75 to 100% -0.067, all cold -0.075. The gain therefore sits where the ensemble agrees on cold weather, not where it is split. All-row q95 coverage moves from 0.921 to 0.913, and the ratio of 90% band width to absolute error from 3.74 to 3.62. The intervals are 95%. P6 fails.

docs.title: Part D: short-history level anchor
docs.text: A 7-day level anchor cuts D15's median bias and harms the other 14 Primaries. The anchor is the median of the bundle's own residuals over the previous 7, 14 or 28 days, shrunk by the days of history over the window length. At D15 (4 scored months) the score falls from 15.186 to 13.593 (7 days), 14.071 (14 days), and 14.151 (28 days); the 7-day change is -1.593 (-3.574 to +0.609), and the mean signed error falls from -17.0 to -4.8 points (7 days), -4.7 (14 days), and -5.9 (28 days). D18 (6 scored months) gains nothing. On the other 14 Primaries the 7-day anchor changes the score by +0.101 (+0.049 to +0.153), the 14-day anchor by +0.069 (+0.006 to +0.137), and the 28-day anchor by +0.017 (-0.025 to +0.057). P7's bias clause holds for the 14-day anchor (a 72% cut), and its no-harm clause fails. The 7-day score change at D15 is within its interval. Part A's filters improve D15 more than the anchors do (K0 15.186, K1 13.380, K2 13.445), so the anchor is not the only fix.

docs.title: Part E: lag-encroachment sweep on experiment 391's boosters
docs.text: Shifting lag readings into an event moves the median by up to a third of the step and leaves the band as wide. Experiment 391's stored b0 boosters, 16 Primaries and 86,907 distinct rows per setting (one run on the 15th of each of 12 months), were given lag columns shifted by the event step for k = 1, 2 and 3 of the origin, day and week lags. The median moves by 1.3%, 17.3% and 36.8% of the step. The 90% band is 1.005, 1.009 and 1.008 times as wide as with clean lags. The clean reading lies inside the 90% band on 0.875 of rows at k = 0 and 0.826 at k = 3, and the event-level reading inside it on 0.681 and 0.784. The q95 reaches the event level on 0.701 of rows at k = 0 and 0.812 at k = 3. No lagless booster is stored, no n1 sweep was run, and no real-event comparison was made.

docs.title: Part F: score on unpadded hand-labelled load-shift events
docs.text:
On rows whose target lies outside every event, a power lag inside an event raises the score by about 1 point for the weekly bundle on the signed-MW six, and by 1.7 to 2.0 points for the GAM stack. Events are the 184 merged hand-labelled intervals of briefs/sw_block_detector_label_table.csv, unpadded. No forecast predicts an event, so a median that stays at normal running is the desired behaviour; the harm table therefore scores rows whose target lies outside the event, and coverage inside events is description only. Harm is the CRPS of rows with one to three lags in an event, minus the same Primaries' rows with clean lags; intervals resample whole events (34 events for the signed-MW six, 25 for the MVA-only eight). Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped (filtered, the headline); the unfiltered point estimates differ in the third decimal and the interval bounds by up to 0.1. The baseline is each Primary's overall clean mean. Matching it on Primary, month and lead band gives +1.06 (-0.05 to +2.48) for the bundle and +1.25 (-0.01 to +2.89) for the GAM stack on the six, so the reading that the interval excludes zero is fragile.

Forecast Six: harm (interval) Eight: harm (interval) Six, 3 lags: q95 coverage Weekly bundle +1.03 (+0.05 to +2.32) +0.37 (-0.18 to +1.05) 0.831 Monthly control +0.57 (-0.03 to +1.49) +0.50 (-0.13 to +1.25) 0.818 GAM stack +1.67 (+0.06 to +3.77) +1.97 (+0.46 to +3.80) 0.840 Experiment 383 d +0.97 (+0.08 to +2.10) +0.47 (-0.17 to +1.24) 0.822 Experiment 383 c1 +0.79 (+0.09 to +1.74) +0.44 (-0.14 to +1.19) 0.735 Experiment 383 c2 +0.36 (-0.15 to +1.15) +0.60 (+0.02 to +1.38) 0.779

With clean lags the bundle's q95 coverage is 0.928 on the six.

The median sits about halfway to the event reading when no lag is in the event and nearly at the event reading when lags are (sign-free). The depth missed per event is |median(actual − median forecast)| over |depth|, where 0 means the median reaches the event reading and 1 means it stays at normal running. For the weekly bundle it is 0.50 with no lag in the event (52 events), 0.19 with one or two (27), and 0.16 with three (16). The monthly control scores 0.42, 0.20 and 0.12; the GAM stack 0.63, 0.30 and 0.27; experiment 383's c2 0.39, 0.15 and 0.14. Lag encroachment is therefore consistent with dragging the median into the event. The 90% band stays about as wide (the bundle's median width is 23.1, 26.1 and 24.2 points).

The 24-hour padded mask gives a lower coverage figure. On the bundle's signed-MW six, rows with a lag in the padded mask and a target outside it have q95 coverage 0.786 (interval 0.506 to 0.932, 13 events); the unpadded labels give 0.902 (0.819 to 0.960, 34 events). The two row sets differ (17,111 and 29,631 rows) and the intervals overlap, so the data do not show that padding changes the result. Of 36,718 padded-contaminated rows, 8,485 have no lag in an unpadded event.

Curtailment cost was not re-scored in this experiment. Part H below corrects the label table's sign column; the harm table, coverage and the sign-free depth above do not depend on it. Experiment 390's event-fan figure is redrawn below with the event masks shaded.

docs.title: Part H: the label table's sign convention
docs.text:
In the label table, every "X to Y" row has a positive depth_mw and means that X's power falls. The audit measures, for each labelled event and each Primary it names, the mean cleaned power in the event's first 48 hours (or the whole event if shorter) minus the mean in the 48 hours before the onset. Power is read through studies.power.scan_power, so flagged zeros are dropped. The step is a plain difference of means, with no weather correction. Of the 112 rows with an end time and a depth, 104 are measurable.

  • At X, the measured step is negative in 36 of the 44 measurable "X to Y" rows.
  • In the other 60 measurable rows, the first-named Primary's step has the sign of depth_mw in 53.
  • The rule "X to Y: X falls; any other row: the sign of depth_mw" matches the measured sign in 89 of 104 events. The earlier convention (first-named Primary takes the sign of depth_mw in every row) matched 61 of 104.
  • 51 of 112 signs are corrected: 43 from measurement and 8 from the rule where no step could be measured. The corrected copy is ml-experiments/00395-.../sw_block_detector_label_table_corrected.csv.
  • The measured step has a median of 0.63 times the labelled |depth_mw|. The labelled size is kept, because a 48-hour mean dilutes a drop that deepens later.
  • Among 72 events with a measurable second Primary, the two steps have opposite signs in 44, so load conservation between the pair is only partly visible in 48-hour means.

With the corrected signs, the median follows the event about halfway with no lag in the event and nearly fully with three. The share followed is 1 − (actual − median forecast) / signed depth, where 0 means the median sits at normal running and 1 means it sits at the event reading. Medians over events, for 0, 1 or 2, and 3 lags in the event:

Forecast 0 lags (52 events) 1 or 2 lags (27) 3 lags (16) Weekly bundle 0.52 0.83 0.94 Monthly control 0.60 0.83 0.94 GAM stack 0.40 0.88 0.97 Experiment 383 d 0.63 0.85 0.95 Experiment 383 c1 0.67 0.87 0.92 Experiment 383 c2 0.70 0.85 0.95

The sign-free depth missed in Part F, 0.50, 0.19 and 0.16 for the bundle, becomes 0.48, 0.17 and 0.06 as a share of the depth not followed. With the corrected sign, the median of actual minus forecast has the sign of the event in 90% of events with no lag in the event (it was 69%). Part E does not use labelled depth, so the correction does not change it.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Which actuals the scorer read. Experiment 103's rows.parquet, through the feature cache. It carries no drop_reason filter, so 38 unique scored half-hours of 256,981 (0.015%) are flagged substation_zero, all exactly zero: D21 13, D8 7, D22 5, D9 5, D12 4, D18 3, D16 1. The 622 flagged rows counted elsewhere are the cleaned table's flagged rows over the year, not scored half-hours. Part F drops the flagged rows and also reports the unfiltered numbers. Parts A to E score unfiltered; the 38 rows cannot move a mean by more than their share of the rows.
  • Flagged zeros inside labelled events. 6 inside unpadded events (D22 5, D8 1) and 5 inside the 24 h padded mask (D22 5).
  • Median minus mean. Not computed: the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Error of the mean beside each contrast. Every contrast above carries its interval. Contrasts without an interval are descriptive.
  • Which audit triggers fired. P1 and P2 contradicted the hypothesis, and P7's no-harm clause failed.
  • Verdict. Partly supported: P3 and P4 hold; P1, P2 and P6 fail; P5 and P7 are untested as written.
  • Cadence. Nothing is refitted, so the monthly-refit rule does not apply.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• D15 has 4 scored months and D18 has 6, so Part D rests on very few months.
  • Part C could not be set beside experiment 394's tables, and its spread bins are ranked over all leads before days 1 to 10 are kept (38% lower, 33% middle, 21% upper, 8% top decile of the scored rows). Ranked within days 1 to 10, the bins read lower -0.046, upper -0.012, top decile -0.023. S1M's q95 coverage falls in every bin by 0.005 to 0.013, so P6, which concerns coverage, is judged on CRPS only here.
  • Part F draws no per-forecast chart of coverage by lag count and event length; the tables carry it.
  • The Part F events for D5 overlap in the padded mask, which merges later events.
  • Experiment 391's n1, n0, and o boosters were not swept, and no lagless booster exists.
  • The measured event sizes use 48-hour means, so they dilute drops that deepen later; the corrected table keeps the labelled size.
  • K1's D14 gain (-0.122, interval -0.354 to +0.059) includes zero and sits in winter rows. K2 also worsens D11 slightly (+0.038, +0.000 to +0.074).
  • K3 chose the prior (0.05, 0.998) in all 192 Primary-months, and K2 chose it in 91, so the prior may have been tuned on this same year. The gain grid often hits its lower edge, 0.005.
  • K1's pooled noise settings come from an earlier experiment's fit, whose window was not checked against 2025-07 to 2026-06.

docs.title: Which changes to the weekly XGBoost demand recipe are worth a full year of testing: holiday columns, winter weather columns, hyperparameters, ensemble-summary inputs, or a split by lead?
docs.text:
Take-home: giving the weekly XGBoost demand model the ensemble's view of the weather lowered the forecast error a little in both main test months and at both metering groups, and no other change did so as clearly. Two ways of giving the model that view did best. The first trains the model on the mean of the 51 ensemble members and then applies it to each member (arm E4_em_pool). The second adds the ensemble's mean and spread of temperature and shortwave radiation (arm E1_es2). They lowered the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) by 0.015 to 0.120 points and by 0.026 to 0.072 points of effective capacity, which is 0.4% to 2.7% of the control's CRPS. Two main test months cannot support more than a full-year test. Holiday columns lowered the error on the Easter bank holidays by about 0.5 points, but raised it on all days in January and at the Primaries with signed meters at Easter. The winter weather columns were neutral to worse, 200 boosting rounds was clearly worse than 500, and the window-summary arms of the lag-surprise idea all raised the error. Verdict: partly supported. A screen supports no 99% claim: every number here is a point difference from the control, set against a noise floor from refitting with another seed, in a few test months.

What we asked. We asked which small changes to the weekly XGBoost demand model of experiment 87 lower its CRPS enough to deserve a full year of testing. That model fits one XGBoost model per Primary substation, trained on the control member of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble forecast. We refitted it monthly with each change on up to four test months, and compared each arm with an unchanged control (C0) over days 1 to 10 of the forecast, the horizon that the electricity distribution network operator (NGED) cares about. Primaries split into two metering groups: the signed-MW six (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, whose meters record the sign of power flow) and the MVA-only eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22, whose meters do not). D15 and D18 are scored for the report only. D-codes are anonymised Primary substations. The caveat that matters most for NGED's use: the screen covers days 1 to 10 pooled, and holds no result for any single lead band.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The table lists the change in all-rows CRPS from C0 in the two main test months. Negative is better. The last two rows give C0's own CRPS and the noise floor, the absolute CRPS gap between C0 and a second control fitted with another seed (C1).

Arm 2026-01 signed-MW 2026-01 MVA-only 2026-06 signed-MW 2026-06 MVA-only E4_em_pool -0.120 -0.099 -0.045 -0.015 E1_es2 -0.072 -0.038 -0.047 -0.026 E2_es7 -0.033 -0.058 -0.033 -0.010 E3_em_em -0.044 -0.048 -0.027 +0.003 W7 -0.020 -0.012 -0.028 -0.005 P_hl1 -0.035 +0.003 -0.023 -0.002 H1 +0.011 +0.022 -0.014 -0.020 HT +0.004 +0.001 +0.002 -0.009 HW -0.004 0.000 0.000 -0.002 W1 +0.005 -0.006 +0.026 +0.033 W2 -0.009 0.000 +0.009 +0.020 W3 -0.008 +0.010 +0.011 +0.053 W4 +0.176 +0.388 +0.005 +0.090 P_rounds_r1000 +0.096 +0.021 -0.045 -0.009 P_rounds_r200 +0.237 +0.188 +0.137 +0.117 H0_nocal +0.139 +0.108 +0.077 +0.064 C0's CRPS 4.509 3.823 2.725 3.527 Noise floor 0.015 0.004 0.001 0.002
  • Ensemble-summary arms lowered the error most consistently. E1_es2 (the ensemble's mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation replace the control member's two columns) is the only arm of the first screening tier, other than W7, below C0 in both main months and both groups. E1_es2 gained 0.7% to 1.7% of C0's CRPS. E4_em_pool (train on the ensemble mean of the seven weather variables, then apply to the 51 members and pool them) is the best Tier B arm, and beats E1_es2 clearly only in January (second figure below). E2_es7 (E1_es2's summary for all seven variables) is also below C0 in all four cells, but gains less than E1_es2 in 2026-01 at the signed-MW six, although it holds more inputs.
  • W7 is a small gain. W7 (trailing means of shortwave radiation and the 3-hour change in the clear-sky index) is below C0 in all four cells, by 0.005 to 0.028 points. Each gap exceeds that cell's noise floor, but one gap (0.005 points) is under 0.01.
  • Holiday columns help on bank-holiday days and raise the error on all days in January and at the signed-MW six at Easter. At Easter (2026-04) H1 lowered CRPS on the bank-holiday days by 0.592 points at the signed-MW six and 0.523 at the MVA-only eight. The same arm raised all-rows CRPS by 0.039 at the signed-MW six in 2026-04, and raised the Christmas-slice CRPS by 0.065 and 0.594 points in 2025-12 and 2026-01 at the signed-MW six. H1d (only the signed days to the nearest bank holiday) lowered Easter CRPS by 0.209 at the signed-MW six and 0.344 at the MVA-only eight, and the Christmas slice by about 0.05 at the signed-MW six. Its all-rows changes range from -0.024 to +0.048. In 2026-06, which holds no bank holiday, H1 and H1d lowered all-rows CRPS by 0.014 to 0.020 points; this screen does not explain why. HW did nothing, and HT and HWT raised the Christmas-slice CRPS by up to 0.49 points (third figure below).
  • Winter weather columns are neutral to worse. W1, W3, and W4 raised CRPS in at least three of the four main cells, and W4 (sine and cosine of the day of year) raised it by 0.176 and 0.388 points in January. W2 (the monotone constraint on temperature) helped beyond the noise floor only in 2025-12, by 0.026 and 0.016 points.
  • Boosting rounds. 200 rounds is clearly worse than 500 in every cell (+0.117 to +0.237). 1000 rounds helps in June (-0.045 and -0.009) and hurts in January (+0.096 and +0.021). A half-life of 1 year (P_hl1) lowers CRPS in 3 of 4 cells, by up to 0.035 points.
  • The calendar columns the control holds matter. Removing the hour and weekday columns (H0_nocal) raised CRPS by 0.064 to 0.139 points, so those columns carry real information.
  • Tails. The control's 95% upper quantile covers 78% of readings at the signed-MW six and 90.5% at the MVA-only eight in January (nominal 95%). No arm repairs that. 1000 rounds lowers coverage further, from 0.781 to 0.749 and from 0.922 to 0.881 at the signed-MW six in January and June.

Window-summary arms hurt. The arms WS A1 to A3 (window summaries of the lag surprise of experiment 391) were scored against that experiment's b0 control on 7 Primaries (the signed-MW six and D8), over 1,034,930 scored half-hours at the signed-MW six and 172,780 at D8. All rows, change in CRPS from b0 (b0's CRPS in brackets): at the signed-MW six +0.100, +0.106, and +0.111 for A1, A2, and A3 (3.123); at D8 +0.134, +0.041, and +0.121 (7.684). The second b0 seed differs by at most 0.001 on all rows and 0.010 on the 21,601 event-lag rows outside events, where A1 to A3 raised CRPS by +0.114, +0.250, and +0.275 (b0 4.957). None of the three arms improved on b0 in any group or slice.

The scorer dropped 11 half-hours flagged substation_zero in 2025-12 and none in the other three folds.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (ensemble-summary gains larger in the high-spread tercile): not tested. The spread-tercile slices were not scored. The all-rows gain is small, as predicted.
  • P2 (W1 lowers winter CRPS by 0.05 to 0.15 points and all rows by under 0.03): not confirmed. W1 raised winter CRPS by 0.085 points at the signed-MW six in 2025-12, and moved January by +0.005 and -0.006.
  • P3 (holiday columns lower holiday-day CRPS by 0.3 to 1.0 points and move other rows by under 0.01): not confirmed. H1 lowered Easter CRPS by 0.5 to 0.6 points but moved all rows by up to 0.039 points, and raised the Christmas-slice CRPS.
  • P4 (W4 does not help): confirmed. W4 was worse in 5 of the 6 cells in which it was scored, and clearly worse in January.
  • P5 (at most 3 of 13 hyperparameter settings pass): not tested. Of the 13 settings, 2 ran: the number of boosting rounds (one 1000-round fit scored at 200, 500, and 1000 rounds) and the 1-year half-life. The other 11 did not run, and the go rule needs 4 folds.
  • P6 (four-band split moves CRPS by under 0.03 and shows a jump at a band edge): not tested. The lead-band split was not run.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site, and the error of the mean or median forecast beside each CRPS contrast: not computed for this page, because the page uses only the committed screen table.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 fires: W1 and the holiday columns contradict P2 and P3, and no explanation was tested. Trigger 5 fires: E2_es7 holds E1_es2's inputs and more, and scores worse than E1_es2 at the signed-MW six in 2026-01 (-0.033 against -0.072, a gap above the 0.015 noise floor). No audit has run. Every number here is an interim screen figure.
  • Examples of the forecasts and the avoidable-curtailment cost are not on this page: the committed result files hold neither.

docs.title: What did not run
docs.text:
None of the following is a negative result.

  • Tier D (the lead-band split B4 and B2, W5, W6) and six Tier C settings (P_eta010, P_depth4, P_depth8, P_mcw10, P_sub06, P_lambda10): dropped by the maintainer on 2026-10-31, because they do not feed the model-release or neural-recipe decision.
  • E5 (all51): the other five weather variables hold no per-member data before 2025-07.
  • E6 (ensq): not built. The arm needs a clear-sky helper that W7 gained only afterwards, and the maintainer's list did not include it.
  • Round 2 and stage 2: the folds 2025-10 and 2026-03 and the full-year evaluation of the best three arms were not run, because the manager cut the scope to "write up what exists". The pre-registered go rule (a win in at least 3 of 4 base folds) is therefore not applied. The drop rule can be read on the two main folds: W4, P_rounds_r200, and H0_nocal are worse than C0 by more than the noise floor in all four main cells. The rule drops W4 and P_rounds_r200; H0_nocal is a deliberate ablation of the control's hour and weekday columns, not a candidate. The screen-level reading is that E4_em_pool, E1_es2, E2_es7, and W7 improve all four main cells.
  • Fold coverage. The winter arms W1 to W4 ran on 2025-12 and the main folds, and the holiday arms on all four folds. The ensemble arms, W7, P_hl1, and the rounds fits ran on the main folds only.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Arms. Every arm refits monthly, fits one XGBoost model per Primary per fold on the control member, and keeps colsample_bytree at 1.0. The 17 input columns of the control are the seven weather variables, the solar zenith and azimuth, local hour, local weekday, a lockdown indicator, days_to_christmas, the lead, and the three origin lags. Arms that ran:

Tier Arm Change A C0, C1 Control with seeds 0 and 1; the gap between them is the noise floor A E1_es2 Mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave across the 51 members replace the two control-member columns A H0_nocal Control without hour and weekday columns A H1, H1d Bank-holiday flag, signed days to the nearest bank holiday, and the flags for the days before and after; H1d adds only the signed days A HW, HT, HWT Adds is_weekend, holiday_type, or both A W1 Trailing means of temperature over 6, 24, 72, and 168 hours and the degrees below 15.5 °C of each A W2, W3, W4 Monotone constraint on temperature; W1 plus W2; sine and cosine of day of year A2 W7 Trailing means of shortwave over 3, 6, and 24 hours and the 3-hour change in the clear-sky index B E2_es7, E3_em_em, E4_em_pool E1_es2 with all seven variables; train and apply on the ensemble mean; train on the mean, apply to the 51 members and pool C P_rounds, P_hl1 One 1000-round fit scored at 200, 500, and 1000 rounds; recency half-life of 1 year Separate WS A1 to A3 Window summaries of the lag surprise, scored against experiment 391's b0

Pre-registered rules. An arm is dropped if its days 1 to 10 CRPS exceeds C0's by more than the noise floor in both main folds at both groups. An arm goes to the full evaluation if it beats C0 in at least 3 of its 4 base folds and its pooled gain exceeds the noise floor at either group. Every change here uses little or no extra compute in production, so any gain whose full-year interval excludes zero would be worth porting, and a screen supports no such claim. The committed table holds raw scores only, with no widened (factor 1.15) score.

What the plan found out before fitting. The control already holds days_to_christmas, so the plan dropped the holiday arm H2. Training data start on 2024-04-01, so only the 2026-04 and 2026-06 folds have the full 24-month window. The four screen months in the brief hold almost no bank holidays, so the plan added the two event folds. Only temperature and shortwave exist for all 51 members before 2025-07, which limits E1_es2 to those two variables and made E5 impossible. No national school-holiday calendar exists, so the plan skipped arm H3.

docs.title: Run record and changes since the plan
docs.text:
Fits ran mostly on the CPU, with 4 threads per process. The graphics processor was about three times slower than the CPU for these fits while other sessions shared it. The 2026-01 fold for the first six Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D5, D8, D9) was fitted on the graphics processor, except W1 and W3, which were refitted on the CPU. Every other fit ran on the CPU. For those six Primaries, W1 and W3 are therefore compared with a control fitted on a different device. The seed-to-seed difference between C0 and C1 is at most 0.015 points of CRPS, and the two devices were not compared directly.

The first 8 Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D5, D9, D10, D11) ran first on both main folds, then the other 8. The order let the interim arm table appear after a fraction of the compute.

The code review came after the first fits. A fresh Sonnet review of the arm code ran after the first Tier A fits instead of before them, which breaks the order the experiment skill asks for. The review found that the past half of the trailing temperature windows (W1, W3) stitched the earlier runs together member by member, so the past temperature differed between the 51 members of one run. The past half is now the ensemble mean of the earlier runs' first day, identical for all members. The W1 and W3 fits made before the change were moved aside and refitted, and no result on this page uses them.

Tier C was cut to eight settings, and then to two fit sets. The eight settings were P_rounds, P_eta010, P_depth8, P_depth4, P_mcw10, P_sub06, P_lambda10, and P_hl1. Only P_rounds and P_hl1 ran (see "What did not run").

Cleaned data. The scorer drops half-hours flagged substation_zero in the cleaned power table from the actuals, and prints the number dropped per fold (see "Folds and dropped half-hours").

Window-surprise arms (e00396_surprise.py) reuse experiment 391's stage 2 code, stage-1 tables, refit months, and b0 control, at 150 rounds on the seven Primaries of 391's secondary arms. The printed report is results/window_surprise_scores.txt.

Problems caused by the move: none.

docs.title: Does a plain mixture density network match the simple XGBoost model for Primary demand, and does attention over the inputs help it?
docs.text: Take-home message: a small neural network matches the simple XGBoost demand forecast on five test months, and attention over its inputs does not help. With the XGBoost model's inputs, one network per Primary scores a CRPS (days 1 to 10) of 3.493 points of capacity at the six signed-MW Primaries, against 3.542 for the monthly XGBoost control. One pooled network across the 16 Primaries scores 3.264, and 0.278 points below the control. Attention does not help: A2 (the gate sees the lead, calendar, and holidays) scores 3.288 against 3.320 for A0 (uniform weights), and the gate weights move by under 0.01 over lead time. The verdict is partly supported: the network matched XGBoost, the attention part failed. The tails are the open problem: the networks cover 0.84 to 0.86 of outcomes with their 95% quantile at the signed-MW six, so they are too narrow there. Every number comes from five test months, so all are interim.

docs.text:

  • Stage 2. A2 beat A0 in 1 of 5 folds at the signed-MW six. The stage 2 stop rule fired because the gate was inert.
  • Gate weights (A2). W1 (weather weight falls from day 1 to days 8 to 10): +0.010. W2 (lag weight falls): +0.004. W3 (calendar plus holiday weight rises): +0.004. W6: the largest range of any group's mean weight over lead bands is 0.0095, under 0.05, so the gate is reported as inert.

The networks' q99 pinball loss is lower than XGBoost's (0.41 to 0.44 against 0.49 at the signed-MW six).

docs.text:
• P1 failed in the network's favour. The plain network does not trail S0M raw; it leads it by 0.049 points.
  • P2 failed. The network's q95 and q99 coverage is further from nominal than the XGBoost model's.
  • P3 half held. The one-pass arm is within 0.05 points of the member arm at both groups, but its tail coverage is not better.
  • P4 failed narrowly. A2 minus A0 is -0.033 at the signed-MW six and +0.034 at the MVA-only eight, just outside the plus or minus 0.03 the prediction allowed.
  • P5 not tested. The stop rule fired before the lead-band contrast was read.
  • W1 to W4 and W6 failed, as listed above.

docs.title: Not run
docs.text: The permutation importance of each input group, arm A3, the Primary-embedding ablation, the pinball-loss head, and the full-year runs. The stop rules fired before any of them. The other gate plots are in the experiment's private folder.

docs.title: Deviations
docs.text:
• Early stopping holds out one week in every 12, not every fourth week (see the plan below).
  • The widening of 1.15 about the median on q01, q05, q95, and q99 is applied at scoring.
  • The summary scheme rebuilds the ensemble mean and spread for the training runs of 2024-04 to 2025-06 from the archive, and uses the stored 51-member frames from 2025-07-01. On 2025-07-01 the two routes gave identical values.
  • Every fitted network is saved under work/models/ in the experiment's private folder.
  • Reused forecasts are the stored XGBoost, GAM stack, BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology sets listed below. No XGBoost model was refitted.

docs.title: Plan as committed before any fit
Question
docs.text:
We test whether a small neural network can replace the simple XGBoost model for Primary demand, and whether attention over its inputs helps. Two experiments queued by the maintainer share one network and one scorer, so they run as two stages of one experiment. The maintainer asked for the merge in chat on 2026-10-30.

  • Stage 1: a plain mixture density network against XGBoost. A mixture density network is a neural network that outputs the weights, means, and standard deviations of three Gaussians. Experiment 334's plain network trailed the generalised additive stack but saw different inputs from the XGBoost model, so it could not answer the question. Stage 1 gives the network the XGBoost model's inputs, training rows, and refit schedule.
  • Stage 2: attention over five input groups. The network encodes weather, solar geometry, routine calendar, holidays, and the three origin lags into one 32-wide token each. A softmax gate weights the tokens. The gate sees the lead time in A1, the lead, calendar, and holidays in A2, and the lead, calendar, holidays, and weather in A3, always with the Primary embedding. A0 fixes the weights at 0.2. The design is in briefs/attention_mdn_design_answer.md and its addendum (private).

docs.title: Reused predictions and what is fitted
docs.text:
No XGBoost model is refitted. The references are stored forecasts, read from the private folders of earlier experiments. A fitted network is the only new fit.

  • Experiment 389, arms S0M raw and S1M raw (monthly refits, 16 Primaries, daily origins from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). S0M is the like-for-like XGBoost control for monthly refits. S1M is the same model given the ensemble mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation as extra columns, the fair control for the one-pass arm. Both are raw; the 1.15 widening of the four outer quantiles about the median is applied after loading and both versions are scored.
  • Experiment 381, weekly bundle bundle_solar+sunny+hl1 and monthly control (raw). The weekly bundle favours the control on refit cadence; the page says so wherever it is quoted.
  • Experiments 377, 87, and the manual heuristic and climatology of experiment 87. The GAM stack, BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology, as stored under demand-v2.
  • Experiment 391 (open pull request). Not used: it had not merged when this plan was written.

The scorer restricts each arm and each reference to the half-hours they share, and prints the shared count. The stored rows cover the same 16 Primaries and origins as the networks' rows. A gap would show as a shorter shared count.

docs.title: Inputs and rows
docs.text:
The network sees the XGBoost model's inputs, plus two bank-holiday columns. e00397_prep.py builds them from experiment 87's control-member training rows.

  • Weather. Seven columns: shortwave, longwave, temperature, dew point, surface pressure, precipitation (through log1p), and 10 m wind speed. The member scheme uses one ensemble member's seven columns. The network trains on the control member and, at forecast time, is applied to each of the 51 members, giving a 153-component mixture pooled with equal member weights. The summary scheme uses the ensemble mean and standard deviation of each column (14 columns), computed once per run, and is applied once.
  • Why the summary scheme needs new data. Only the control member is stored for the training months 2024-04 to 2025-06. e00397_prep.py summaries rebuilds the 51-member rows from the archive for those runs with experiment 48's frame builder, and reads the stored 51-member frames from 2025-07-01. e00397_prep.py check compares the two routes on 2025-07-01 before any use.
  • Other groups. Solar geometry (the cosine of the zenith angle, and the sine and cosine of the azimuth), routine calendar (the hour of day at one and two cycles per day, one-hot weekday, the lockdown indicator), holidays (an inside-window flag, scaled signed days to Christmas, a tent function, a bank-holiday flag, and scaled signed days to the nearest holiday clipped at 7 days), and the three origin lags with an is-missing flag and an age in hours for each. The lead enters as the lead divided by 336 hours and its square root, and is never gated.
  • Normalisation. Weather, lags, and scaled day counts are standardised with each fold's training rows only, clipped at 5 standard deviations, and the statistics are saved with the weights. A missing lag is flagged and set to 0 after standardisation. The preparation raises if any weather value is not finite, because the XGBoost frame builder already rejects a valid time that lacks a member. The target is power over effective capacity, standardised with each Primary's training mean and standard deviation, and mapped back before scoring.
  • Training rows. The control member's rows from experiment 87's training table, with the XGBoost model's rule: a fold sees a row only if its valid time is at least 3.5 hours before the refit and its run began at or before the refit, within the 24 months before the refit. Row weights halve every 0.5 years, as for the XGBoost model. Hand-filtered load-shift events stay in the rows, as for the XGBoost control.

docs.title: Folds, refits, and arms
docs.text:
Screen folds. Test months 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. The four months are those of common.md and December is added because none of the four contains Christmas. Each fold trains on the 24 months before its test month and scores that month, with one refit at the start of the month. Monthly refits of the full year follow only for an advancing screen.

Early stopping uses one week in every 12. The design asked for every fourth week with a purge of 14 days before and 7 days after each held-out week. That purge covers every week of a four-week cycle and leaves no rows to train on, so the held-out week comes every 12 weeks. Runs that begin in the two weeks before, or the week after, a held-out week are dropped from training.

Arms.

  • plain_own: one plain network per Primary (arm 2 of the swap brief), 64 hidden units, two layers, three components, six seeds for the chosen setting and three during the screen.
  • plain_pooled: one plain network across the 16 Primaries with an 8-wide Primary embedding (arm 4), fitted in stage 2 as the reference for attention whatever arm 2 shows.
  • A0 to A3: the attention network, pooled with a Primary embedding in the head, and in the gate's query for A1 to A3. A2 without the embedding in the query is the ablation.
  • One pinball-loss head (arm 3 of the swap brief) runs only if plain_own lands within 0.1 points of S0M raw.

Hyperparameters. A pre-registered grid of ten settings (GRID in e00397_fit.py) varies the width (32, 64, 128), layers (2, 3), components (2, 3, 5), learning rate, weight decay, and dropout. Each setting is fitted with two seeds on a validation block (train to 2025-03, validate 2025-04 to 2025-06, which lie before every scored month) and chosen by the lowest mean quantile score at days 1 to 10 over the 14 countable Primaries, with ties to the smaller network. The 51-member frames of the validation months are not stored, so the validation block is scored with the control member's pass. This ranks settings and is not a forecast score. The scored-month score of the chosen setting and the next two is reported, and the ten settings count as the tuning budget. The attention network's token width (16 or 32) and dropout (0 or 0.1) are then tried on A0 with the chosen head, plus the second-best head at token width 32 with both dropouts; A1 to A3 inherit the A0 setting so that tuning cannot favour them.

Loss and optimiser. Mean negative log-likelihood weighted by row age, AdamW at a learning rate of 5e-4 and a weight decay of 1e-3 unless the setting says otherwise, batch 16,384, at most 40 epochs, patience 6. Every network is saved with its standardiser and setting.

docs.title: Checks the write-up reports
docs.text:
• Cold winter nights first, then the pooled score, then cold nights at 3 °C or below, sunny half-hours, the Economy 7 step hours, the Christmas slice, and bank holidays.
  • Tails. Coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99, per group and per Primary, raw and widened by 1.15.
  • Floor. The demand-v2 floor (candidate no worse than manual_heuristic, and within 1.10 times BG2, at each Primary, point estimates), and the median minus the mean forecast per Primary.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost at the signed-MW six, at the scaled limit of 0.9 times the maximum observed export, swept at 0.75 and 0.5.
  • Attention. Gate weights by lead band, hour of day, day type, and per Primary, and the Christmas weeks; token norms beside the weights; and the permutation importance of each group for A0 and A2 (shuffle the group's columns within a month, rescore), because attention weights alone do not show what drives the output.
  • D8 uses the network's own forecast, with the caveat "it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap". D15 and D18 are report-only.
  • Absolute scores of every arm beside the references.

docs.title: Counting towards the demand-v2 stop rule
docs.text: This experiment counts if it ends not supported or refuted. The idea is "a neural network as the main demand model". Experiment 334 (not supported) is the only counted experiment so far, so the count is 1 of 3 and rises to 2 of 3 here. The maintainer named this experiment, which counts as approval whatever the count.

docs.title: Advice followed from earlier experiments
docs.text:
• Followed. Experiment 334: give a neural replacement the past-week information and score cold winter nights before the pooled score (the three origin lags and the cold-night slice here). Experiment 381: compare tails and avoidable-curtailment cost, not only CRPS. Experiment 389: test the ensemble mean and spread as inputs (the summary scheme against S1M).
  • Departed from. Experiment 334 advised testing neural parts as additions to the stack. The maintainer asked for the replacement test, so this experiment tests the replacement.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text: Estimate, to be replaced by a measured time. A pooled fold has about 7 million rows and 46 columns, about 1.3 GB, which fits on the GPU. The design's estimate is 2 to 4 minutes per pooled fit on the GPU and 20 to 40 minutes on three CPU threads. The first task after the slot is granted is to time one fit on each and choose the faster. Fit counts: the grid is 20 per-Primary sets; the stage 1 screen is 5 folds, 3 seeds, 2 schemes; the stage 2 simplest version is 5 folds, 3 seeds, 3 arms (A0, A2, plain_pooled). The slot is 3 threads, the GPU, and MemoryMax=16G.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Experiment 398: do the flagged zero actuals change any published demand score?
docs.text: Dropping 38 faulty zero readings changes none of the conclusions in four earlier demand- forecasting experiments. Experiments 379, 381, 391, and 395 each scored day-ahead to 10-day-ahead demand forecasts for 14 Primary substations (Primaries) against half-hourly power readings. Those readings still contained 38 half-hours that the cleaned power table flags as exact zeros from a faulty meter. We removed those half-hours from the stored per-row scores and recomputed each experiment's headline figures (experiment 381's weekly bundle was rescored from its stored forecasts). The continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, in percentage points of the Primary's effective capacity) falls by at most 0.0023 points at the 6 Primaries that report signed megawatts (the signed-MW six) and by at most 0.008 points at the 8 Primaries that report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA; the MVA-only eight). Within each score file, every forecasting variant (arm) falls by nearly the same amount, so the difference between any two arms agrees with the published difference. The verdict is "partly supported" because the hypothesis was that no figure changes at the printed precision, and the MVA-only CRPS values change in the third decimal place.

docs.title: Contrasts and rankings
docs.text:
• No contrast interval changes sign or crosses zero. We recomputed 86 paired contrasts (5 had no rows, so 81 are compared) (99% interval, 5,000 resamples, month-resampled): experiment 379's 14 arms against BG2, experiment 391's five arms against the control (all rows, lag inside an event, lag outside), and experiment 395's seven monthly arms against the control (CRPS and error of the median), each at the signed-MW six and MVA-only eight. The largest change in a point estimate is 0.0008 points, and in an interval bound 0.0017 points.
  • The weekly bundle of experiment 381 was rescored from its stored forecasts. Bundle minus the GAM stack at the signed-MW six is +0.0749 old and +0.0749 new, at the MVA-only eight with D8 -0.3609 and -0.3612, and without D8 -0.1967 and -0.1966. The bundle's differences from the weekly baseline, BG2, the manual heuristic, and climatology each move by at most 0.0011 points. The largest single-Primary change for the bundle is -0.035 points at D21.
  • No arm ranking changes within experiments 379, 391, and 395 at the headline slice, because every arm of one file loses the same few rows and falls by nearly the same amount.

docs.title: Flagged half-hours per Primary
docs.text:
The flagged keys are the 2,035 substation_zero rows of the cleaned power table between 2024-04-01 and 2026-07-01, each with a power of exactly 0 (build date: the table as read on 2026-10-30). The counts depend on the scored rows of each file, so each file has its own.

File Unique flagged half-hours dropped Per Primary 379 stack and BG2 (rows_stack), 395 (b_rows_*) 38 D21 13, D8 7, D22 5, D9 5, D12 4, D18 3, D16 1 379 components (rows_components) 276 D15 120, D18 119, D21 13, D8 9, D22 5, D9 5, D12 4, D16 1 391 (scores/rows) 15 D8 9, D9 5, D16 1 381 weekly bundle (scored from forecasts) not counted by key its scoring actuals lose 1,179 of 630,528 half-hours across all 16 series and the whole window

At the Primaries that hold the flagged keys, BG2's days 1 to 10 CRPS in experiment 379's stack file falls by 0.035 at D21 (2.377 to 2.343), 0.022 at D18, 0.017 at D22, 0.011 at D9, 0.005 at D12, 0.004 at D8, and 0.003 at D16. The other nine Primaries do not change.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Experiment 379's unit check cannot see the gap. The unit check compares the stored actual of experiment 87 with the cache actual on rows where both are finite, and a flagged actual is a finite 0.0 in both sources, so the maximum difference is zero. The rescore finds the gap because it joins to the production table's drop_reason, not to another copy of the same cache.
  • The median forecast minus the mean forecast and the error of the mean forecast are not recomputed: the experiment changes the scored rows, not the forecasts, and the stored losses already carry the quantile score.
  • Triggers fired: none. No control failed and no nested arm beats the arm that contains it. One prediction, P1 (every headline moves by less than 0.005), was missed: the MVA-only eight moved by up to 0.008. P2, P3 (D21 largest), and P4 held.
  • Compute used: the rescore reads and filters stored per-row scores and recomputes contrasts; no scorer was rerun except experiment 381's own weekly bundle.

docs.title: Caveats and what to do next
docs.text:
• The 38 half-hours are not the whole cache. Experiment 388's scorer, which covers the full scored year for every Primary including D15 and D18, finds 622 unique flagged half-hours, 389 of them at D18 and 196 at D15. Experiments built on that scored set, and experiments 392, 395's Part F, and 396, report their own check columns and are not repeated here.
  • Interval resamples: the 99% intervals use 5,000 resamples, not the 20,000 of the headline protocol, to keep the job inside its time limit. All widths agree with the published figures to the printed precision.
  • A fix in src/studies/dp_features.py or experiment 103's builder (dropping flagged half-hours when the cache is built) would stop new experiments scoring against faulty zeros. We did not make it, because that fix changes the shared cache that open experiments read. The maintainer decides.

docs.title: Does cutting the first months of D15 and D18 help the monthly XGBoost demand forecast?
docs.text:
Cutting the noisy start of D15 and D18 lowers the monthly XGBoost demand forecast's error by about 1%, and cutting 6 months is not safe. We asked whether leaving out the first months of readings, taken while a new substation's meter was being commissioned, gives a better forecast at D15 and D18, the two Primary substations whose history starts after the weather archive does. We refitted the XGBoost model of experiment 381 (refitted monthly) with the first months of each series dropped in six different ways, and scored the forecasts for the months the protocol scores: January to June 2026 at D18, and March to June 2026 at D15. Error is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) of the forecast's 11 quantiles, in points of capacity. The control N0 keeps every row. The six cuts are N3 and N6 (drop the first 3 or 6 months), NS (drop up to the date at which production's settling rule treats the meter as settled), NC (drop every row before 2025-03-01), NCZ (NC, and also drop readings of 0.009 MW or less), and NCR (NC, and also drop runs of 2 or more such readings). The cut to 2025-03-01 (NC) lowered the error at both Primaries by about 1%. A 6-month cut lowered D15's error by 4.4% and raised D18's by 7.2%. The result says nothing about the other 14 Primaries, which have history from before the weather archive starts.

Verdict: partly supported. Prediction P1, that D18 gains 3% or more from NC, failed (NC gained 1.2%). Prediction P2, that no cut gains more than 2% at D15, also failed (N3 gained 2.4%, N6 4.4%). Prediction P3 failed for NCZ at D15, which was 1.28% worse than NC (15.594 against 15.397); NCR (+0.34%) and both removals at D18 (within 0.2%) held.

The decision rule asks for a lower CRPS in two thirds of the scored months and in the pooled figure. At D15 the arms N3, NS, NC, and NCR met it, and N6 and NCZ did not. At D18 no arm met it. The porting threshold is zero, because production already holds a cut date per Primary as the settling rule. Every figure below is a point estimate, because 4 and 6 scored months are too few for an interval.

Figure 1. Each cut's days 1 to 10 CRPS, relative to the control N0 refitted in the same environment (percentages of N0, negative is better).

Arm D15 CRPS D15 months lower D18 CRPS D18 months lower N0, all rows (refitted) 15.606 2.696 N0, stored (experiment 381) 15.599 3 of 4 2.696 3 of 6 N3, first 3 months cut 15.227 3 of 4 2.676 3 of 6 N6, first 6 months cut 14.915 2 of 4 2.891 1 of 6 NS, settling rule 15.439 3 of 4 2.666 3 of 6 NC, cut to 2025-03-01 15.397 4 of 4 2.665 3 of 6 NCZ, NC and near-zero removed 15.594 2 of 4 2.669 3 of 6 NCR, NC and near-zero runs removed 15.450 4 of 4 2.665 3 of 6 GAM stack 12.848 2.499 BG2 13.354 2.646 manual_heuristic 22.590 4.015 climatology 46.195 7.114

CRPS is in points of capacity at days 1 to 10 under demand-v1 (report only), raw (no 1.15 widening). The columns "months lower" count scored valid-time months in which the arm beat the refitted N0. Every arm is the plain monthly control recipe (colsample_* fixed at 1.0), seed 0. The widened rows (1.15) are in the scoring log: N0 15.464 and NC 15.274 at D15, N0 2.753 and NC 2.708 at D18. Widening lowers D15's CRPS and raises D18's, and it reorders arms that are within 0.1 points of each other.

Figure 2. The gain depends on the month, which is why the months-lower counts are low.

At D18 the gain comes mainly from January 2026, the month served by the refit with the shortest history (2.82 for N0, 2.65 for NC). From February on, NC is within 0.1 points of N0 and sometimes worse. At D15 the cuts help most in March 2026 (23.40 for N0, 22.88 for NC and 20.78 for N6) and little afterwards. N6 raises D18's CRPS by 0.45 points in March 2026 and 0.65 in April 2026.

Figure 3. D15's error is a level error that no start cut removes.

At D15 the median forecast of every XGBoost arm is 15.9 to 20.9 points of capacity below the actual, averaged over days 1 to 10 (N0 -20.8, N3 -20.2, N6 -15.9, NC -20.5). The GAM stack's bias is -3.0 and BG2's is -13.1. At D18 the biases are small (N0 -0.66, N6 +1.00). Cutting 6 months removes about a quarter of D15's bias. D15's level stepped up in July 2025, September 2025, and March 2026, so an XGBoost model trained on the earlier months learns a level that no longer holds, and a cut at one date cannot remove that.

docs.title: What each cut needs in production
docs.text: Every arm needs one cut date per Primary. NS needs the settling rule, which production already holds (D15 to 2025-03-20, D18 to 2025-03-04). N3 and N6 need the first reading's date plus a number of months. NC needs the single date 2025-03-01. NCZ and NCR also need a row filter on the power data and on the three origin lags, so they need more work and gain nothing.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• How many near-zero readings were removed. NCZ removed 104 half-hours at D15 and 10 at D18 (readings of 0.009 MW or less, 2025-03-01 to 2026-06-30), all inside the scored year. NCR removed 16 and 2. At D15 most removed readings are single half-hours, so they are real crossings of zero by a series that swings by about 2 MW and exports; this is why NCZ is 1.3% worse than NC at D15. D18's July 2025 dip (1 to 3 July) was left in, as planned.
  • The same rows. Scoring on the rows NCZ keeps (ncz_common) changes each XGBoost arm's CRPS by 0.003 points or less, except N6 at D15 (0.017). D18's values are identical. The two row sets rank the raw XGBoost arms identically.
  • Reproduction. The stored N0 of experiment 381 and the N0 refitted here differ by 0.007 points of CRPS at D15 and 0.0005 at D18. The forecasts differ by a mean of 0.001 (maximum 0.021) of capacity at the median; the uv.lock library versions (xgboost 3.4.1, numpy 2.5.4, polars 2.1.0) are the same, and we did not find the cause. All contrasts use the refitted N0.
  • The settling cut uses later data. new_meter_settling takes each series' capacity from all readings up to 2026-06-30, not up to each refit, so NS's cut dates (D15 2025-03-20, D18 2025-03-04) could move by days if recomputed at each refit. They match the dates the plan quotes.
  • Power source. The training power came from studies.power.scan_power, not from the stored observed.parquet. The two agree on every shared half-hour at D15 and D18, and the training labels agree to 5e-7 MW.
  • Median minus mean forecast, per site. N0: -0.116 MW at D15 and -0.019 MW at D18. NC: -0.124 and -0.030. A cut does not shift the gap.
  • MAE of the median. D15: N0 28.05, N6 26.64, NC 27.62. D18: N0 4.738, N6 5.068, NC 4.732. It points the same way as the CRPS contrast for N6, NC, and NS. For N3 and NCZ at D18 and NCZ at D15 the MAE is within 0.02 of N0, on the other side of it.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 fired: the results contradict predictions P1, P2, and P3. The explanation (the refit with the shortest history gains most, and D15's error is a level error) is in Figures 2 and 3 and in the take-home message. Trigger 7 may apply, because the research default for the other experiments now drops rows before 2025-03-01 (NC); that default rests only on NC being no worse than N0 and on production's existing cut date, and the result is not replicated. No audit has run.
  • Curtailment cost. The scorer returns no cost for D15 and D18, because neither is one of the signed-MW Primaries it defines the cost for.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: The scored months are 4 at D15 and 6 at D18, one seed, one fit per refit. A gain of 1% is larger than the refit noise (0.007 and 0.0005 points) but is not shown to exceed the month-to-month variation. NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days and the headline band covers it. D18 steps up by about 1.5 MW around 2026-07, after the scored year, and no claim is made about that step.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Why D15's median forecast is 16 to 21 points of capacity too low while the GAM stack's is 3 points too low: a level input, a shorter training window anchored on recent months, or the stack's own level term are the candidates. The level anchor of the sister experiment on stored forecasts has not merged and was not added.

docs.title: Experiment 400: blend a forecast with power lags and a forecast without them, by lag surprise
Plan
docs.text:
• Question. Can a smooth, threshold-free weight on a forecast without power lags, driven by how surprising the three lagged readings are, give a forecast that is better around load-shift events and no worse elsewhere? A binary detector reached recall 0.42 with 1.7 false alarms per Primary-year (experiment 391). A forecast that steps loses the trust of NGED's operators.
  • Forecast with lags. Experiment 381's weekly bundle (arm_preds/weekly/bundle_solar+sunny+hl1), stored as fractions of effective capacity, unwidened. It is not experiment 383's plain weekly member (arm d, which is experiment 87's stored weekly member): that member has 64 stored files and cannot cover all rows.
  • Forecast without lags. Experiment 383's raw lagless arm (work/arms/lagless.parquet, 4,099,680 rows, 16 Primaries). Arm c2 of experiment 383 is not used: it applies this arm only on rows with a lag inside an event and arm d elsewhere.
  • Widening. Both forecasts are used raw (no 1.15 widening): experiment 381's bundle carries none and the lagless arm is raw. The 1.15 sensitivity run planned here was not run (see Caveats).
  • Row set. The 2,824,844 rows of experiment 395's Part F slice_table.parquet (16 Primaries, valid times 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30). The plan checks before scoring that both forecasts hold every key and reports any gap. Scoring actuals come from Part F's actual_mw; half-hours flagged in the cleaned power table are dropped from scoring, and the count dropped is reported per Primary.
  • Suspicion score. Experiment 391's surprise_tables/half_hourly/<site>.parquet: u, the normal score of a reading in the lagless stage-1 quantile forecast, at each lag's valid time. A row's three lags (origin, day, and week lags, found with experiment 87's origin_lags) give three own-Primary values. The neighbour surprise uses experiment 391's NGED interconnection list. Leak check. Each u comes from a monthly refit that trained on no row at or after its refit time, and a lag's valid time is at or before the forecast origin, so no u uses information after the origin. The monthly stage-1 tables are indexed by valid time, so they align with the weekly forecasts through the lag's valid time. A lag in the first stage-1 month (2024-10) has u from a model trained on 2024-04 to 2024-09; the scored months start nine months later.
  • Arms. Mixture weight on the forecast with lags: w = 1 / (1 + exp(a + b s + c lead_term)), with lead_term = log(lead hours / 24). B1: s is the largest absolute own surprise over the three lags. B2: s is B1 plus the largest absolute neighbour surprise, as two inputs (b1, b2). B3: the signed own surprise, the sum of the neighbours' positive and negative surprises, and the largest of each sign, as five inputs, so a fit can learn the neighbour sign logic; the rule is not hand coded. Fixed-weight control: w = 0.5. Endpoints: the two pure forecasts. Each of B1 to B3 and the control is scored as a mixture and as a quantile average of the same weights.
  • Fit. The exact CRPS of the mixture (the integral of the squared difference between the mixture CDF and the step at the actual value, with the piecewise-linear CDFs below), plus a ridge penalty of 1e-3 times the squared parameters, minimised by BFGS (at most 60 iterations) on a fixed random subsample of 200,000 training rows (seed 0), with an expanding window: the model for scored month m uses rows whose valid time is before the first of m. July to September 2025 is warm-up and uses w = 0.5; October 2025 to June 2026 is scored. Warm-up months are reported separately. The label table never enters a fit.
  • Reported score. The protocol's CRPS from the mixture's 11 quantiles, so every arm is scored as every earlier experiment is. For a mixture of two well-separated forecasts the 11-quantile score is lower than the exact CRPS, so the report also gives the exact CRPS of the mixture arms.
  • Mixture quantiles. Each forecast's CDF is linear between its 11 quantiles, with the end segments extended to levels 0 and 1 at the slope of the outer segment. The mixture CDF is w F1 + (1 - w) F2, inverted by bisection at the 11 levels.
  • Events. The corrected label table sw_block_detector_label_table_corrected.csv from the head of nged-ml-research PR 49 (112 rows with an end time and a depth), unpadded, with the corrected signs. It is used only to evaluate.
  • Checks are the seven in the brief: the harm table by number of lags inside the event, the cost outside events, the median share of the labelled depth, the tails during events, smoothness at onset and end, avoidable curtailment during events and in the 7 days after (differences against the forecast with lags and the GAM stack), and the cold-night rows separately.
  • Compute. Stored forecasts only: no refit, no GPU, 2 cores, MemoryMax=6G. Chunks of one Primary and one month.
  • Earlier advice followed. Cleaned actuals; both forecasts and the weight named in full in every table; the absolute score beside every contrast. Departures are listed under Caveats.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The blend gives no usable gain, and the surprise scores do not drive the weight. Every number below is for days 1 to 10, valid times from 2025-10-01 (the first scored month), CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) in points of effective capacity. The six Primaries with signed readings are D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16. The eight with MVA-only readings are D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22. Intervals resample whole events (event rows) or months (pooled rows) and are at 95%. The decision rule asked for 99% intervals at k = 12 and a pooled contrast on event-lag rows; neither was computed, so the verdict rests on the failed cost condition below and on the absence of any gain at the eight. The printed reports are in the private folder (work/report.txt and work/curtailment.txt). This page has no figures.

  • Flagged-zero handling. Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped from the scoring actuals and from the fits. The scored rows lose 96 half-hours (D12 8, D18 24, D22 40, D8 24).
  • Widening. Both forecasts are raw. Experiment 381's weekly bundle and experiment 383's raw lagless arm carry no 1.15 widening.
  • Label table. The corrected table sw_block_detector_label_table_corrected.csv from nged-ml-research PR 49: 112 labelled pairs of Primaries (51 with a corrected sign), expanded to 184 per-Primary unpadded events. It is used only to evaluate, never as an input.
  • The weight barely moves around events. In arm B2 the mean weight on the forecast with lags is 0.615 outside events, 0.611 in the first 6 hours of an event, and 0.597 after 24 hours. Its 5th to 95th percentile range is 0.56 to 0.68. The fitted coefficients on surprise and on the log of lead time are both negative, so a larger surprise and a longer lead each raise the weight on the forecast with lags.
  • Absolute CRPS, all 16 Primaries. Forecast with lags 3.867; forecast without lags 4.338; fixed 50/50 mixture 3.938; mixture B1 3.898, B2 3.892, B3 3.886; quantile averages 3.907 to 3.968.
  • Event-lag rows (1 to 3 lags in an event, target outside), arm minus forecast with lags (C1 to C4):
Arm Six with signed readings Eight with MVA-only readings Fixed 50/50 mixture -0.90 (-2.16 to -0.01) +0.14 (-0.04 to +0.31) Mixture B1 -0.77 (-1.83 to -0.03) +0.10 (-0.05 to +0.24) Mixture B2 -0.75 (-1.78 to -0.03) +0.09 (-0.04 to +0.22) Mixture B3 -0.78 (-1.83 to -0.03) +0.08 (-0.05 to +0.20) Forecast without lags -0.93 (-2.49 to +0.26) +0.59 (+0.14 to +1.04)

On event-lag rows, mixture B2 minus the fixed 50/50 mixture is +0.15 (-0.02 to +0.39) at the six and -0.05 (-0.10 to -0.01) at the eight. Outside events it is -0.046 (-0.065 to -0.024) over all 16 Primaries.
  • Cost outside events (C5 to C8, all 16 Primaries, month resampling): fixed 50/50 mixture +0.078 (+0.013 to +0.138); B1 +0.038, B2 +0.033 (-0.013 to +0.076), B3 +0.027 (-0.018 to +0.070).
