The MVA-only eight have no solar term and differ between arms only through their inputs and training noise (0.03 to 0.09 points against A0-doy), the noise floor for networks that differ in nothing relevant to them.
  • Sunny-midday slice (CAMS clear-sky index at least 0.7, 10:00 to 15:00 local time, 88,924 half-hours). Mean CRPS: A0-doy 4.288; C3 4.515; H1 4.515; A0-noirr-doy 4.398. Mean q99 pinball loss: A0-doy 0.314; C3 0.310; H1 0.319; A0-noirr-doy 0.321.
  • Primary contrasts against A0-doy on sunny middays (99.17% month-block intervals, six tests). CRPS: C3 +0.227 (-0.135 to +0.560); H1 +0.227 (-0.043 to +0.471); A0-noirr-doy +0.110 (-0.089 to +0.363). q99 pinball loss: C3 -0.004 (-0.022 to +0.010); H1 +0.005 (-0.008 to +0.023); A0-noirr-doy +0.007 (-0.012 to +0.022). The predictions failed: P1 (H1 minus A0-doy between -0.10 and 0.00) and P2 (C3 minus A0-doy between -0.05 and +0.15) both missed on the point estimate (+0.227), and P3 (C3 minus A0-doy q99 pinball loss lower by 3% to 12%) is a 1% reduction on sunny middays (-0.004 of 0.314) and a 6.6% reduction over all half-hours (-0.020 of 0.304, interval -0.073 to +0.011).
  • All half-hours (secondary), against A0-doy. CRPS: C3 +0.024 (-0.029 to +0.070); H1 +0.001 (-0.023 to +0.022); A0-noirr-doy +0.041 (-0.018 to +0.100). q99 pinball loss: C3 -0.020 (-0.073 to +0.011); H1 +0.007 (-0.001 to +0.014); A0-noirr-doy +0.003 (-0.018 to +0.020). C3 minus A0-noirr-doy: CRPS -0.018 (-0.067 to +0.036), sunny-midday +0.117 (-0.376 to +0.580), all-half-hour q99 pinball loss -0.023 (-0.070 to +0.005). H1 minus C3: CRPS -0.023 (-0.064 to +0.024), q99 pinball loss +0.027 (-0.008 to +0.084). The hybrid shows no gain over the explicit term alone.
  • Tails (days 1 to 10, signed-MW six, mean over Primaries; A0-doy / C3 / H1 / A0-noirr-doy). Pinball q95 0.866 / 0.853 / 0.871 / 0.873; pinball q99 0.304 / 0.284 / 0.310 / 0.307; coverage q95 0.884 / 0.893 / 0.887 / 0.888; coverage q99 0.960 / 0.966 / 0.960 / 0.960; coverage q01 0.014 / 0.013 / 0.015 / 0.014; coverage q05 0.051 / 0.051 / 0.054 / 0.050; threshold-weighted CRPS 0.349 / 0.347 / 0.353 / 0.348. C3 has the lowest upper-tail loss and the highest q95 and q99 coverage, by small margins whose intervals include zero.
  • Log-scale prior arms (added after the inert-prior finding; post hoc). C3p, C3pa, and C3p-weak score 2.993, 2.993, and 2.992 against C3's 2.990 overall, and 4.522, 4.531, and 4.519 against C3's 4.515 on sunny middays. C3p minus C3 is +0.003 (-0.004 to +0.010) overall and +0.007 (-0.018 to +0.032) on sunny middays; C3pa minus C3 is +0.003 (-0.001 to +0.008) and +0.016 (-0.005 to +0.035); C3p-weak minus C3 is +0.002 (-0.003 to +0.009) and +0.004 (-0.018 to +0.038). Their q99 pinball losses are within 0.001 of C3's.
  • Prior share of the log-capacity gradient (2026-06 fold, seed 0). C3: 1.2e-9 at the start (the penalty's gradient is zero at its own centre, where every arm starts), 2.5% at the end. With the capacity shifted 0.7 log units below the centre, the share is 4.4% for C3p and C3pa and 0.46% for C3p-weak. At the end it is 5.0% for C3p, 4.4% for C3pa, and 0.64% for C3p-weak. The prior is about 100 times stronger than C3's per-row scale for C3p and C3pa, and the per-Primary learned capacities are within 0.1 MW of C3's in the first five months.
  • Learned capacity against the studies page (2025/26 season-year, mean over 12 folds and 5 seeds, MW). For C3 the capacities are 1.96 (D10), 2.39 (D11), 2.74 (D14), 2.76 (D16), 3.29 (D5), and 1.29 (D9), against 3.06, 4.21, 4.14, 4.50, 2.19, and 3.11 on the studies page. That is 0.4 to 0.7 of the studies page at five of six Primaries (0.64, 0.57, 0.66, 0.61, 0.41) and 1.5 times it at D5, the same shortfall as in experiment 409. The log-prior arms give capacities within 0.1 MW of C3's at each Primary except C3p-weak (0.1 to 0.2 MW lower), and H1 differs from C3 by 0.1 to 0.6 MW (D5 2.67). The seed ranges are wide (Figure 3).
  • C3 and H1, as run, are effectively an explicit solar term with a free capacity (amendment 3), so these results do not test a regularised capacity.
  • Cleaned data. Flagged substation_zero half-hours are dropped from training, lags, inference, and scoring by experiment 397's matrices, as in experiment 409, and D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01. The count of flagged half-hours dropped per fold was not tallied separately for this experiment.
  • Fits and cadence. Monthly refits, 5 seeds, 12 months. Reused: C3 and A0-noirr-doy seeds 0 to 2 for the five experiment 409 months (a refit of C3, seed 0, 2026-06 reproduced experiment 409's stored forecast to 4e-6). Fitted here: 390 fits (70 in the first stage, 75 log-prior fits on the first five months, and 245 in the extension); 30 fits were reused. Saved networks: data/ml-experiments/00416-mdn-explicit-solar-term-better-powered-follow-up/work/seed_preds/<arm>/<month>_s<seed>.pt.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean of the 11 quantiles, per Primary (MW, all lead times from 0.5 to 336 hours). All arms have a median below the mean-of-quantiles by the same amount: for A0-doy -0.076 (D10), -0.002 (D11), -0.023 (D14), -0.044 (D16), -0.034 (D5), -0.027 (D9). C3 is within 0.02 of A0-doy at each Primary, and the spread does not shift the arms differently.
  • Error of the median forecast beside the quantile-score contrasts (MW, signed six, mean absolute error, all lead times from 0.5 to 336 hours, so the sunny-midday slice holds 132,077 half-hours, not the 88,924 of days 1 to 10). All half-hours: A0-doy 0.439, C3 0.442, H1 0.436, A0-noirr-doy 0.441. Sunny middays: A0-doy 0.628, C3 0.670, H1 0.671, A0-noirr-doy 0.638. The median error points the same way as sunny-midday CRPS (A0-doy best) and the other way from the all-half-hour q99 pinball loss (C3 best).
  • Leave-one-Primary-out, sunny-midday CRPS, C3 minus A0-doy (mean of the six Primaries' own means, so +0.225 here against +0.227 pooled in the headline). All six +0.225; without D5 +0.129; without D9 +0.265; without D10 +0.232; without D11 +0.238; without D14 +0.231; without D16 +0.252. Per Primary: D5 +0.702, D14 +0.192, D10 +0.186, D11 +0.158, D16 +0.086, D9 +0.024. The sign never flips.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 3 fired in a weak form: the q99 pinball contrast favours C3 (-0.020 over all half-hours), while the error of the median forecast favours A0-doy (0.442 against 0.439 overall, 0.670 against 0.628 on sunny middays), and both intervals include zero. No Opus audit was run, because the result is already inconclusive and no later experiment's design depends on its sign. Trigger 4 did not fire (no sign flip). Trigger 5 did not fire (the log-prior arms, which should change nothing, moved the score by at most 0.016 on sunny middays, inside the half-width of 0.02 of the paired interval of C3pa minus C3). Trigger 1 does not apply (no known-answer test). Triggers 2, 6, and 7 did not fire.
  • Data-use caveats. The twCRPS thresholds use history before 2025-07-01, which is the start of the 12 months, so no scored month overlaps them. Half-hours with no CAMS row, or with zero clear-sky irradiance, are outside the sunny-midday slice, for every arm alike.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Keep the free irradiance input in the pooled neural network. A non-inferiority claim for the explicit term needs either a larger margin (about 0.3 CRPS points) or a design with a smaller seed spread, because seven more test months did not lower the minimum detectable effect.
  • Investigate D5, where C3 is +0.70 worse on sunny middays and the learned capacity is 1.5 times the studies page.
  • If an interpretable solar term is still wanted, fix the capacity from the studies page (arm C1 of experiment 409) and test the shape, not the capacity.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
• Plan review. The plan was written and amended before any fit; each amendment is dated and precedes the fits it concerns.
  • Code review (before the first fit). A fresh Sonnet reviewer read the fit and score scripts; 8 findings, all accepted (a 5-seed-average minimum detectable effect added beside the single-seed definition, a key-count check, verdict inputs printed, arm order sorted by input set, a finite check on the clear-sky index, a note that experiment 409 seeds are reused only for its own months, a per-Primary row count, and a memoised per-seed scoring pass). A second fresh Sonnet reviewer read the changed loss (e00416_models.py); 4 findings, all accepted (the start-of-training gradient share is zero for every prior arm, so the shifted-start share is reported; the strength claim is worded as relative to C3; a comment on prior=False; the run recipe names the log-prior arms).
  • Results check (fresh Sonnet). The agent re-derived the absolute CRPS, the sunny-midday and all-half-hour contrasts, the q99 pinball contrasts, the median errors, and the leave-one-Primary-out table from the stored forecasts with its own code. Everything reproduced. It found 7 points, all accepted: the median-error and median-minus-mean checks are in MW over all lead times (labels fixed), the leave-one-Primary-out table uses the mean of the Primaries' own means (labelled), the D5 advice item now says D5's own difference is +0.70, the capacity range in the lessons is 0.4 to 1.5, the noise-floor range is 0.03 to 0.09, and two median-minus-mean values were rounded differently. It did not re-derive intervals, minimum detectable effects, coverage, capacities, or the prior shares.
  • Write-up review (fresh Sonnet, prose). 20 findings. Accepted and applied: the sign convention is stated, the status paragraph is consistent, the lead of "What is asked" defines A0, C3, H1, sunny midday, and minimum detectable effect, the contradictory "only the month-to-month spread" claim is scoped to experiment 409, "no cost in skill" is reworded, "primary contrast" is "pre-registered contrast", the "To be recorded" placeholder is replaced, the next-steps bullet no longer proposes months that have no stored inputs, and several pronoun and fragment fixes. Not applied: linking every earlier experiment mentioned, and rewriting every count as a word or numeral, because the pre-registered plan text is kept as written.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None so far.

docs.title: Can a Primary-level export gate, or labels taken from the zero crossings of the daily reading, stop the signed mixture density network from inventing reverse flow at MVA-only Primaries?
docs.text: Status: done. The stop rule fired: A, A+H, and C all failed the bars on rotation r1, and the day-flip diagnostic (design I) missed its bar. The results sections at the end report the numbers. The plan sections below were written before any fit. This plan follows the Opus design note of 2026-10-30 (private folder: briefs/neural_mva_new_ideas_answer.md), which proposes eight constraints (A to H) against false reverse flow at the eight Primaries whose meter reads apparent power (MVA) only.

docs.title: Question and plan in plain words
docs.text: Some Primaries report only the size of the power flowing, not its direction, so a forecast cannot say whether the flow is demand or solar generation pushing power back up the network. Experiment 412 trained a neural network to infer the direction from the sunshine. With the direction hidden at two Primaries where it is known, the network called reverse flow on 17% of the half-hours that had none, and on 18% to 47% of sunny half-hours when no solar farm was added at all. This experiment tests two constraints that decide the direction with information the network cannot fit from the same readings: one yes-or-no decision per Primary about whether it exports at all, and training labels from the two daily times at which the flow passes through zero.

docs.title: Evidence the plan follows
docs.text:
• Experiment 412 merged as not supported (pull request 69). The capacity prior was inert: 13 nats against a loss over 5.6 million rows moved the capacities by under 0.2 points, and a prior at full weight pulled the capacity to the prior centre and removed the skill with the false calls (balanced accuracy 0.54 to 0.61, within 0.04 of the shuffled sky). This plan adds no capacity prior and keeps the registered, divided prior, whose gradient share the fit script prints in every arm that has it.
  • Experiment 408 is still a draft plan (pull request 64), with an interim block. Its rule-only diagnostics (refit 2026-01-01) show the rule's gate opening on real readings at D10 and D12 only, so it stays closed at D5, and the rule's labels reaching recall 0.64 to 0.79 with a false-reverse rate of 3.8% to 6.1% at level 2.0. Design A copies that rule, so P1's 5% bar sits inside the range the rule already reaches, and the plan says so in the prediction.
  • Experiment 416 is a draft plan (pull request 73). It tests an explicit solar term inside the demand network at the signed Primaries and has no results. Nothing in this plan depends on it.
  • Experiment 409's learned capacities were 0.40 to 0.50 of the studies page at five Primaries (quoted by the design note), so design G (borrowed capacity) is not run.
  • Standing rules of 2026-10-30 applied. Monthly refits only; cleaned data (experiment 397's rows) with the dropped count per fold reported; D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; every fitted network saved as a state file; draft pull request; the seven-step review order (code review before the first fit, results review, write-up review); a day-ahead and a 14-day example forecast are not drawn, because this experiment scores the sign of reverse flow and not the forecast (stated as a departure).
  • Weather inputs are CAMS and ERA5 only, realised, in laboratory conditions; no ECMWF ENS. CAMS gives the unit PV shape u and the clear-sky index k as in experiment 412. ERA5 gives temperature at each Primary (era5_features.parquet of the stage 1 pilot, stamped every 30 minutes to 2026-07-31, interpolated linearly to the half-hour's midpoint), the demand module's only weather input. ERA5 shortwave serves only as a cross-check of CAMS in the diagnostics. The day-ahead behaviour of every design stays untested.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
All code is in ml-experiments/00417-hidden-sign-mva-export-gate-zero-crossing-labels/.

  • e00417_inputs.py copies experiment 412's site_arrays and build_fold, and changes three things. The demand module's input columns are the irradiance-free columns of experiment 405 with every ensemble mean and spread column removed and one ERA5 temperature column added (standardised on the training rows). Setting gains a power factor with demand-driven reactive power, as in experiment 366: the reading is sqrt(P'^2 + (tan(phi) y)^2 + Q^2), with y the Primary's own signed power before the farm is injected and tan(phi) from studies.dp_operator.tan_phi_from_power_factor (power factor 1 is experiment 412's reading). The reactive term follows the demand, so it fills the midday dip, which is what defeated experiment 366's rule. The lags use the same definition. The fold also carries each row's valid time and k.
  • e00417_models.py imports experiment 412's SignedMdn, mixture functions, and quantiles. It adds a negative log-likelihood with a per-row mask for where the folded density applies and an optional signed label for labelled rows.
  • e00417_gates.py holds the Primary-level gate (design A: experiment 366's rule as experiment 408 fits it, a Spearman correlation of the reading with u above +0.3 on sunny summer-midday training rows, or a 1st percentile below 3 points of capacity, which is 1 point above the reactive floor, because every folded reading is at least 2 points and only the correlation branch can fire. The +0.3 comes from experiment 366's results on these same Primaries, so the gate is not a clean out-of-sample choice) and the high-irradiance gate H (u_hi(h) = D_ref(h) / C_max with D_ref(h) the median reading at UTC hour h on overcast summer training rows (k below 0.3) and C_max the largest studies-page capacity (an external figure), in points, among the four signed Primaries that are not hidden, never the hidden pair; the gate is u >= max(0.3, u_hi(h)) with u the scaled shape).
  • e00417_diagnostics.py runs the zero-fit diagnostics of C, D, and E, and the zero-crossing labeller of design C.
  • e00417_fit.py fits and forecasts, e00417_score.py scores (copying experiment 412's metrics and adding the capacity and the prior's gradient share), and e00417_figures.py draws the figures.

docs.title: Zero-fit diagnostics (run first)
docs.text:
The diagnostics read the folded readings at the six signed-MW Primaries before any network is trained. Rows are unique valid times before 2025-07-01 (the window that sets the injection level), with the minimum of k over t0 ± 5 h at least 0.7 on the day for C (a clear day) and k at least 0.7 at the half-hour for D and E. Settings: level 2.0 (reactive floor 2 points), level 1.0, level 2.0 at power factor 0.97, and no injection. The no-injection group is D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16, and D10 is reported on its own, because its 130 real reverse half-hours make it no clean placebo.

  • C, the W-shape score. On each sunny day, with t0 the solar noon: the left minimum is the smallest reading in t0 - 5 h to t0 - 1 h, the right minimum the smallest in t0 + 1 h to t0 + 5 h, and the centre maximum the largest in t0 - 1 h to t0 + 1 h. The score is the smaller of the two differences (centre maximum minus each minimum), in points of capacity. It is positive when the reading crosses zero twice and negative on a day with one smooth midday dip. The area under the curve compares injected days with no-injection days, per Primary and pooled. The labeller calls the half-hours between the two minima reverse flow on days whose score exceeds a threshold, which is the 99th percentile of the score over the no-injection days of the four visible signed Primaries (D9, D11, D14, D16), so the threshold uses no information from the hidden pair. In a fit the threshold is recomputed per refit from the rows build_fold selects (up to the refit minus the cutoff age, inside the 730-day window), and its value is reported per refit. The diagnostics also report the labeller's recall and false-positive rate at that threshold on D5's injected and no-injection days.
  • D, the Sunday-and-holiday contrast. For each clear Sunday or bank holiday, the difference between its midday reading (10 to 14 UTC) and the mean midday reading of clear Tuesdays to Thursdays within 14 days, after removing a linear ERA5-temperature term fitted on those days. The area under the curve compares the differences of injected and no-injection pairs. The sign of the same difference at night (22 to 04 UTC) is reported beside it as a control.
  • E, the sunny-versus-cloudy slope. In each Primary-month, the slope of the midday reading on k after removing a mean for each half-hour of the day and ISO week, with ERA5 temperature as a covariate. The area under the curve compares injected and no-injection Primary-months.
  • Reported with each area: the number of units behind it (days, pairs, or Primary-months), and its 95% interval from a bootstrap that resamples whole days within each Primary (E: Primary-months within a Primary). The bars (0.9 for C, 0.8 for D and E) and the stop rule's 0.8 apply to the pooled point estimate, and the per-Primary areas are reported beside it. D's temperature term is fitted separately for each Primary.

docs.title: Fits (after the code review, with the manager's slot)
docs.text:
Every arm runs on experiment 412's harness: rotation r1 (D5 and D10 hidden), level 2.0 with Q = 2 points, test months 2026-03 and 2026-06, one seed, one GPU process. One arm is 6 fits: injected, no-injection placebo, and shuffled sky, each in both months. The power-factor setting adds 2 fits (injected, both months).

Order Arm What it is Fits 1 S1c-ref Experiment 412's S1c on the CAMS-and-ERA5 inputs 6 + 2 2 A S1c with the Primary-level gate: a Primary whose gate is shut trains and forecasts with X >= 0 (the truncated density everywhere) 6 + 2 3 A+H A with the high-irradiance row gate H on the Primaries whose gate is open 6 + 2 4 C S1c with the zero-crossing labels as signed targets on labelled rows 6 + 2

Design B (demand frozen off the gate) runs only if A passes the placebo and leaves the within-pair false-reverse rate above 5%. Designs D and E enter the fits only if their diagnostics pass and A and C fail. Designs F and G are not run.

  • Gate decisions are printed before any fit. Design A differs from S1c-ref only where the gate is shut, so A at a hidden Primary whose gate is open is the same fit as S1c-ref and its result is copied from S1c-ref (same seed), not refitted. A shut gate at D5 in the no-injection setting gives zero false reverse by construction, which tests the gate and not the network, and the write-up says so. A cannot lower the false-reverse rate at a Primary where the gate is open. A+H differs from A only through the row gate H, and is fitted in full.
  • Gate timing. Design A's gate is computed once per Primary per refit from the folded readings in the training window (rows before the refit), using the real u and k, also in the shuffled-sky arm.
  • Labels. Design C's labels are computed once per Primary per refit from the training window only. Only days whose W score exceeds the threshold are labelled: reverse between the two minima, forward outside them. Labelled rows use the signed density at y' = +-sqrt(max(r^2 - Q0^2, 0)) with no folding. Every other row, including sunny days below the threshold, keeps the folded likelihood with experiment 412's u >= 0.3 gate, so moderate export is never taught X > 0.
  • Compute. Experiment 412 timed a fit at 29 to 83 seconds, 45 seconds to 3 minutes with the fold build, so 32 fits take 25 minutes to 1.6 hours on one GPU process under 8 GB with one feeder core, run as systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p OOMPolicy=continue, with free -g checked before each launch and the run stopped if available memory falls below 12 GB (the manager's limit for this experiment). Refits are monthly. No stored forecast is reused, because experiment 412 read ENS inputs. State files go to models/<arm>/ in this experiment's private folder.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: The scoring is experiment 412's, unchanged: the headline slice is gate-open half-hours (u >= 0.3) with k at least 0.7, a predicted reverse flow is P(X < 0) > 0.5, the false-reverse rate has as its denominator the sunny summer-midday half-hours with no injected and no real reverse flow, and every recall is reported with its half-hour count. The prior penalty's share of the capacity gradient is printed for every arm. Tail calibration (coverage and pinball loss of the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 signed quantiles) is reported per Primary beside the sign scores, and a signed-median-against-truth example is drawn at D5 and D10. The reference's absolute numbers may differ from experiment 412's, because the inputs differ. The first three arms' numbers are interim (two months, one seed, point estimates only).

docs.title: Code review before the first fit
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet reviewer found no leakage and no blocking problem. Accepted: the W-score centre window was ±0.5 h and is now ±1 h as planned (the diagnostics were re-run); bars now scores the registered bars. Noted, not changed: the capacity prior centre is the median studies-page capacity of all six signed Primaries, the hidden pair included, as in experiment 412 (external information, not the hidden sign, and the prior is inert); the ERA5 file is stamped every 30 minutes, so the midpoint interpolation averages two samples; a Primary with fewer than 200 sunny summer-midday training rows gets a shut gate by default, and the row count is stored beside the decision; the bootstrap resamples injected and no-injection days separately although they are paired, and D10 enters the injected pool only; the 1st-percentile branch of the gate does fire (at D5, D8, and D10, whose readings sit at the 2-point floor), contrary to an earlier reading of the plan.

docs.title: Amendment 1 (2026-10-30): a day-level diagnostic, designs I and C merged
docs.text:
The maintainer, through the neural Discuss session, added design I, and an Opus review refined it and merged it with design C into one day-level zero-fit diagnostic (e00417_day_flip.py, run in the first batch beside D and E). Design I as first written (a slope against raw irradiance on sunny half-hours) is superseded, because its clear-sky row filter removes the clouds and ordering by raw irradiance confounds the flip with the time of day.

  • The refined score. Per April-to-September day, on UTC-hour means: regress on the CAMS unit PV shape u (not raw irradiance), keep hours with 0.1 <= u < 0.95, and work on e = r^2 - D^2, where D is a demand profile (the median reading by hour over overcast days of the same 28-day block and day type, plus an ERA5-temperature term fitted on those days). On the morning limb and on the afternoon limb separately, the score is the drop in residual sum of squares from the best non-increasing fit of e on u to the best two-piece line with a positive upper slope, divided by the two-piece sum of squares. The day's score is the smaller limb score, and a day with a daily maximum u below 0.6 is ineligible.
  • Threshold and truth. A day is flagged above the 98th percentile of the other five signed Primaries' no-injection day scores (leave one Primary out; in a fit, the visible four only). A day is positive when at least 2 of its half-hours have signed P' < 0.
  • Arms. Level 2.0 at Q = 2 and Q = 4 points, level 1.0, level 2.0 at power factor 0.97, the no-injection placebo, the shuffled sky, and a clipping arm with the injected farm capped at 70% of its own peak. Two baselines: a day score from its mean midday residual alone (the level baseline), and the shuffled sky. The Haurwitz clear-sky arm and the 2026-03 and 2026-06 test-month reports of the Opus note are not run.
  • Bar for a neural fit (level 2.0, both Q settings): area under the curve at least 0.9, recall at least 0.7 within a 2% false-flag limit at each of D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16, area under the curve above the shuffled sky by at least 0.15 and above the level baseline by at least 0.05, and row labels (a flagged day, with u at or above the day's breakpoint minus 0.05) at balanced accuracy 0.85 with false-reverse at most 5%. Level 1.0 and power factor 0.97 are reported and expected to fail. If the bar is met, arm AHI (S1c with design A's gate and the day gate together, in place of the separate A-plus-H arm; 6 fits plus 2 at power factor 0.97) is fitted, with the day flag reading the test days' observed readings (hindsight, a laboratory condition) and never the signed truth. A fresh Sonnet reviewer reads the new code before any gate uses it.

docs.title: Amendment 2 (2026-10-30): power factor 1, with 0.97 only as a sensitivity check
docs.text: The maintainer's assumption is power factor 1 plus the small reactive floor Q, not 0.97. The farm output is injected at power factor 1 with the 2-point floor, and every fit and every pass or fail rule uses that reading. The two extra fits per arm at power factor 0.97 are dropped from the plan, and the power-factor rows above (prediction P4, the "+ 2" fits per arm, and the diagnostics at power factor 0.97) are sensitivity checks that no rule reads. The reference arm and arm A had already run their power-factor fits when this amendment arrived; those files are labelled sensitivity and no pass or fail rule uses them. The main fits (injected, no-injection, and shuffled sky) had all run at power factor 1, so nothing needs a rerun. A power-factor fit of the remaining arms runs last, only if the machine is idle (e00417_fit.py run --only pf).

docs.title: Departures from the design note
docs.text:
• The H arm is A with H layered on top, not H alone, and the D5 placebo "should still fail with H alone" is not tested.
  • Design C omits the note's CAMS filter that discards a minimum coinciding with a dip in CAMS irradiance. The day filter (k at least 0.7 across t0 ± 5 h) removes cloudy days instead.
  • Design A reuses S1c-ref's fits where the gate is open (see "Fits").
  • Power factor 0.97 uses reactive power proportional to the Primary's own demand, as experiment 366 did, with the 2-point floor kept.
  • Designs B, D, and E run only as follow-ups after the stop decision.
  • Tail calibration and example plots follow common.md; day-ahead and 14-day forecast graphs are not drawn, because the experiment scores the sign.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• The shuffled sky keeps the daylight profile (experiment 405), so it may score above chance; P1 asks for a margin of 0.1 and not for chance.
  • A Primary-level gate decides once, so a wrong decision costs the whole Primary. The diagnostic of the gate at the injected pair and the placebo is reported before the fit.
  • Reactive power at power factor 0.97 raises the readings the likelihood treats as real power, which experiment 366's rule could not survive; the 2 power-factor fits report how far design A and C degrade.
  • The ERA5 temperature is realised weather, available about 5 days late, and the CAMS inputs about 1 day late, so every result is a laboratory result.
  • Moderate export (level 1.0) may give no W shape, so design C may only work at heavy export. Level 1.0 is run in the diagnostics only.
  • Unlogged load-shift events may sit in the readings, as NGED says its logs are incomplete.

docs.title: Results (interim: two test months, one seed, no intervals)
docs.text:
No arm reached the 0.85 pooled balanced accuracy bar. One fit per arm and setting, on rotation r1 (D5 and D10 hidden), level 2.0, power factor 1, reactive floor 2 points.

Arm Pooled BA D5 BA D10 BA False reverse D5 placebo, sunny middays Margin over shuffled sky S1c reference 0.832 0.813 0.857 11.0% 86% 0.25 A: export gate 0.826 0.801 0.858 12.0% 0% (gate shut) 0.25 A + H: hard gate 0.668 0.638 0.703 3.6% 0% (gate shut) 0.13 C: zero-crossing labels 0.823 0.801 0.854 13.9% 85% 0.15
  • Design A passed the placebo by construction and failed the 5% bar, as the plan predicted. The export gate stays shut at D5 with no farm injected, so the density is truncated at zero and nothing reverses. With the farm injected, the export gate opens at both D5 and D10, and the false-reverse rate at the pair was 12.0% (11.0% for the reference).
  • The hard gate H traded recall for precision. Recall fell from 0.77 (A) to 0.37 and balanced accuracy to 0.67, so A+H fails the 0.85 pooled balanced accuracy bar and, at D5 (0.638), the 0.70 per-Primary bar.
  • Design C's labels gave the reference's balanced accuracy and its placebo fault. D5 with no farm still called reverse flow on 85% of sunny middays.
  • The prior penalty stayed inert in every real-sky arm. The penalty's share of the gradient was 0.0001 to 0.0004 (0.002 to 0.005 in the shuffled-sky arms), so no result here comes from a capacity prior.
  • Power-factor 0.97 (sensitivity only). The reference kept pooled balanced accuracy 0.830, and design A's export gate stayed shut at the injected D5, giving balanced accuracy 0.50 there.

Of the zero-fit diagnostics, only the W-shape labeller (C) cleared its bar, and the day-level V in the unit PV shape (design I) did not. At level 2.0 the pooled area under the curve was 0.96 (interval 0.95 to 0.98) for C, 0.59 for D, and 0.75 for E. At level 1.0 the area for C fell to 0.58. The day-level diagnostic (design I), with its regime split and the broken-cloud amendment, reached 0.73 against the 0.9 bar (0.70 when injected days are paired with their own placebo days). Its recall was 0.22 against 0.7. Its false-flag rate was 5.5% at D5 and 8.2% at D10, against the 2% limit. The roughness split put about 99% of days in the broken-cloud class, so the smooth-day area is undefined and the regime comparison could not be made. The registered prediction that one diagnostic stays at 0.8 or above at level 1.0 also failed: C fell to 0.58 and D was 0.59, and E gave an inverted 0.07.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The stop rule fired. A (with or without H) and C both failed on rotation r1, so the signed-MW work stops and the experiment counts as the eighth failed treatment.
  • The export gate showed no measured gain where it opens. Arm A is the reference plus the gate, and was refitted, not copied from the reference. Its pooled balanced accuracy (0.826) was 0.006 below the reference's (0.832), a gap within one seed's noise.
  • Two audit triggers fired. The reference and design C failed the D5 placebo (a failed control), and design C's labels did not lift the fits although its diagnostic passed, against the prediction (P3) that C passes all bars. No Opus audit was requested, because the result is a stop rule firing on registered bars.
  • Four checks were not done. No intervals (one seed, two test months), rotations r2 and r3 not run, the AHI arm not fitted because design I missed its bar, and no figure of signed-median examples was drawn.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Does pretraining the pooled mixture density network on estimates of past weather (ERA5 and CAMS) before fine-tuning on ENS forecasts lower the Primary demand score?
docs.text: Take-home message: pretraining on six years of ERA5 and CAMS weather lowers the pooled neural network's score by about 0.09 points. ERA5 is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' reanalysis (an estimate of past weather), CAMS is the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service's estimate of past sunlight, and ENS is the ensemble weather forecast archive that starts in 2024-04. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at days 1 to 10, in points of capacity; smaller is better. Arm P1 pretrains and then fine-tunes all weights. Arm P2 freezes the second linear layer during fine-tuning. Arm P3 adds forecast-like noise to the pretraining weather. At the six Primaries whose power is signed megawatts (MW), P1 scores 2.847 against 2.908 for the same neural network trained on ENS rows only (difference -0.061, 95% interval -0.100 to -0.030). At the eight Primaries that report apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA) only, the scores are 3.599 and 3.755 (-0.156, -0.242 to -0.088). The verdict is supported, narrowly: the six-Primary interval of P1 ends at -0.0300 and that of P3 at -0.0327, both just below the 0.03-point threshold. P2 and P3 differ from P1 by under 0.015 points at the six. Every interval comes from 12 monthly test folds (2025-07 to 2026-06), resampling whole months.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS at days 1 to 10 over 12 monthly folds, equal weight per Primary, in points of capacity (smaller is better). The arms are scored on every half-hour they share.

Arm Signed-MW six MVA-only eight D15 and D18 ENS only (reference refit) 2.908 3.755 9.498 P1 pretrain, tune all weights 2.847 3.599 9.093 P2 pretrain, second linear layer frozen 2.851 3.610 9.054 P3 pretrain with noise, tune all weights 2.844 3.610 9.094

The reference forecasts cover fewer half-hours, so they are scored together with the arms on the half-hours that all of them share (3.05 million). On those half-hours the ENS-only network scores 2.906, 3.749, and 8.892; P1 scores 2.846, 3.594, and 8.148; and BG2 (weekly XGBoost) scores 3.018, 3.782, and 7.622, at the six, the eight, and D15 and D18. manual_heuristic scores 3.607, 4.437, and 11.267, and climatology 3.833, 4.873, and 24.094.

  • Contrasts (signed-MW six / MVA-only eight, 95% interval). C1 P1 minus ENS only: -0.061 (-0.100 to -0.030) / -0.156 (-0.242 to -0.088). C2 P2 minus ENS only: -0.058 (-0.103 to -0.020) / -0.144 (-0.236 to -0.070). C3 P3 minus ENS only: -0.064 (-0.103 to -0.033) / -0.144 (-0.224 to -0.079). C4 P3 minus P1: -0.003 (-0.022 to +0.013) / +0.012 (-0.003 to +0.026). C5 P2 minus P1: +0.003 (-0.010 to +0.015) / +0.012 (-0.001 to +0.024).
  • Monthly folds. P1 beats the ENS-only network in 10 of the 12 months at the signed-MW six (2025-07 and 2025-10 are slightly worse). The largest gain is in 2026-01 (-0.23).
  • D15 and D18 (report-only). C1 is -0.405 (-0.856 to +0.018) and C3 is -0.403 (-0.735 to -0.086). C4 is +0.001 (-0.163 to +0.206), so noise does not help these two short-history Primaries beyond pretraining itself.
  • Tails. q95 coverage at the signed-MW six is 0.901 for ENS only and 0.906 to 0.908 for the pretrained arms; q99 coverage is 0.965 against 0.971 to 0.973. All stay below nominal (0.95, 0.99), as in experiment 397.
  • Low-data check (C6, four screen folds). With fine-tuning limited to the first 6 months of ENS (2024-04 to 2024-09), P1 minus the ENS-only network trained on the same rows is -1.277 (-2.612 to -0.445) at the signed-MW six and -0.855 (-1.440 to -0.377) at the MVA-only eight. On the full window the same contrast is -0.082 and -0.119. The difference of the two is -1.195 at the six.
  • Screen. On four screen folds (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) all three arms passed the advance rule against experiment 397's stored forecasts: P1 -0.061, P2 -0.059, P3 -0.053 at the six (reference standard error over seeds 0.011), and about -0.14 at the eight.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held at the six and failed at the eight. The signed-MW six gain is -0.061, inside the predicted -0.05 to -0.20. The prediction said the gain would be smaller at the eight, but it is larger (-0.156).
  • P2 held. P2 minus P1 is +0.003 at the six and +0.012 at the eight, within 0.05. Both intervals include zero, so P2 is indistinguishable from P1.
  • P3 failed. The prediction was a gain at days 4 to 10 and a loss on day 1. At the six, P3 minus P1 is -0.002 on day 1 and +0.004 on days 8 to 10, the opposite pattern, and both are far inside the interval. Its q95 and q99 coverage (0.906 and 0.971) are not closer to nominal than P1's (0.907 and 0.972). No band covering days 4 to 10 alone was scored.
  • P4 held numerically. The gain with 6 months of ENS (-1.277) is far more than twice the full-window gain (-0.082), but the ENS-only baseline degrades badly on 6 months of ENS, so the size of the gain reflects a failed baseline as much as the value of pretraining.

docs.title: Input checks and cost
docs.text:
• Row counts. The 2026-01 fold has 4,979,183 fine-tuning rows (520,330 held out) and 7,894,895 pretraining rows (753,275 held out); the 2025-10 fold has 4,185,108 and 7,503,492. Pretraining rows start in 2019-09 and, for D15 and D18, as late as their data begins.
  • Units. ENS and ERA5 or CAMS inputs agree in mean for all seven variables (for example temperature 11.44 against 11.74 degrees Celsius, shortwave 138 against 131 W/m²) on the 2026-01 fold. The within-day spread of ERA5 precipitation is 3 times that of the ENS ensemble mean, as expected of a smooth ensemble mean.
  • Noise against spread. The root-mean-square difference between the ENS mean and ERA5, divided by the median ENS spread, is 1.2 to 3.3 at day 1 for temperature, dew point, pressure, longwave, and wind (1.1 to 1.5 at day 4), and over 40 for shortwave, whose spread is near zero at night. The noise of arm P3 equals the ENS spread, so it is smaller than the real forecast error at short lead.
  • Cost. Pretraining one network took 30 to 63 seconds (40 epochs on 7 to 8 million rows), and one fine-tune took 27 to 55 seconds, against 40 to 83 seconds for an ENS-only fit. The raw pretraining matrices take about 2 seconds per Primary. A production pipeline using pretraining would need ERA5 and CAMS history kept up to date, a pretraining step run rarely, and a monthly fine-tune.
  • Memory. The scoring script held 9 GB of memory while scoring 12 folds of 7 arms at once; the fits peaked below 3 GB.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Training reaches the epoch limit. 56 of 72 pretraining runs and 8 of 24 ENS-only fits stopped at 40 epochs, so a longer schedule might help; this was not tried.
  • The pretrained network sees ERA5 up to the refit in the low-data check. The check therefore measures less ENS, not less data. The 2026-06 fold has 4 months of ENS before 2024-10-01 and the others 6.
  • P3 noise is independent per row and constant over the day. Real forecast errors are correlated across lead times, and the median spread pools all hours of the day, so shortwave noise is non-zero at night.
  • No hyperparameter of the fine-tuning stage was tuned. All arms use one setting and one fine-tuning rate.
  • Low-data check at D15 and D18. The ENS-only network trained on 6 months has too little data at these two Primaries (difference -20.6 points), so the D15 and D18 result of the low-data check is not interpreted.

docs.title: Plan as committed before any fit
docs.text: The sections below are the plan as committed before any fit; counts given as estimates there are measured in "Input checks and cost" above.

docs.title: Design note
docs.text:
Every arm is the experiment 397 pooled plain network with fixed carried components. Names carry the components, so a reader sees what each arm inherits:

  • pooled-emb: one network across the 16 Primaries with an 8-wide Primary embedding, because experiment 406 found the embedding carries the pooling gain.
  • summary: the inputs are the ensemble mean and ensemble standard deviation of each of the seven weather variables (experiment 397's summary scheme), so the network is applied once per run.
  • g09: 64 units, 2 hidden layers, 3 mixture components, dropout 0.1, the setting experiment 397 chose on its validation block. No setting is tuned here.
  • Not carried: the attention gate (inert in experiment 397), the explicit solar term, the lag-trust component, and the D15 and D18 start cut. Each is added in the assembly if it wins elsewhere.

Arms (arm names are <components>_<training>):

Arm Name Training Reference pooled-emb-summary-g09_ens-only Stored forecasts of experiment 397 (plain_pooled, summary scheme), three seeds P1 pooled-emb-summary-g09_era5cams-pretrain_ft-all Pretrain on ERA5 and CAMS, then fine-tune every weight on the ENS rows P2 pooled-emb-summary-g09_era5cams-pretrain_ft-input-head Same pretraining; the second linear layer (net[3]) is frozen, and the first linear layer, the Primary embedding, and the output layer are fine-tuned P3 pooled-emb-summary-g09_era5cams-noisy-pretrain_ft-all As P1, with forecast-like noise added to the pretraining weather means

Pretraining rows. A pseudo-run starts every second day from 2019-09-01 at 00:00 UTC, with the origin 9 hours later (the publication delay of experiment 87). Each pseudo-run has one row per Primary and half-hour for leads 0.5 to 351 hours (the range of experiment 397's rows). Weather is the Primary's ERA5 value at the half-hour stamp (temperature, dew point, surface pressure, longwave, precipitation, 10 m wind speed; the file is already on the half-hourly grid), with CAMS global horizontal irradiance in place of the ERA5 shortwave. Power and the three origin lags come from the dense power grid with experiment 87's origin_lags, so the lags obey the same newest-usable-observation rule as an ENS row. Rows whose power is missing or flagged are dropped, as in experiment 397. The pretraining set holds an estimated 8 to 13 million rows depending on the fold; the build prints the count per fold.

Spread inputs for pretraining rows. ERA5 has no ensemble spread, so the std_* input columns of a pretraining row take the median of the ENS std_* column at that lead band (24-hour bands) over the fold's own ENS training rows. The mean-input and standard-deviation-input distributions then match what the network sees at fine-tuning. This table, the standardiser, and every other fitted statistic use only rows with valid time at least 3.5 hours before the refit, and exclude the held-out weeks.

The noise of arm P3 is the ENS spread. P3 adds independent Gaussian noise to each mean_* input of a pretraining row, in the transformed input space, with standard deviation equal to the median ENS std_* input at that lead band: the noise grows with lead because the ENS spread does. The draw is made once per fold with a fixed seed, shared by all three network seeds, and stored; the standard deviation inputs are not perturbed. The P3-minus-P1 contrast therefore also tests noise as a regulariser. The spread of an ensemble mean is close to its error only for a well-calibrated ensemble, so the build also prints, per variable and lead band, the ratio of the root-mean-square difference between ENS mean and ERA5 to that spread, as a check that the noise is neither far too small nor far too large. The rule stays "noise equals the median spread" whatever the ratio, and the ratio is reported.

Fine-tuning rows. These are exactly the rows of experiment 397's build_train for the fold: ENS rows whose inputs are the 51-member mean and standard deviation of each weather variable, the 24 months before the refit within the ENS archive (from 2024-04-01), one week in 12 held out for early stopping, runs near the held-out weeks purged, and recency weights with a half-life of 0.5 years. The build prints the fold's row count and checks it against the row count of experiment 397's stored fold. The standardiser and the per-Primary target mean and standard deviation of the fold are fitted on those rows and reused unchanged for the pretraining rows, so both stages see the same input scale and the same targets.

Leakage rule. A fold with test month M and refit time R (00:00 UTC on the first day of M) sees a pretraining row only if its valid time is at least 3.5 hours before R and its origin is at or before R (experiment 87's rule). The same rule bounds the ENS rows, the median-spread table, the standardiser, and the CAMS and ERA5 values used. The early-stopping weeks of the pretraining stage are the same absolute weeks as the fine-tuning stage (week index of the origin day, one in 12), and the runs near them are purged from both stages, so a pretraining row never trains on a week the fine-tuning stage validates on. Inference uses ENS only and the same standardiser. The build asserts the valid-time and origin bounds on every array it hands to a network.

Frozen parameters in arm P2 are excluded from the optimiser, so weight decay does not shrink them. Dropout stays active during fine-tuning, as in every arm.

Time and unit alignment. The build pins each convention before any fit. A CAMS timestamp is the end of its hour, joined on (time - 1 µs).truncate("1h") + 1h as the data-processing page says, and the ERA5 timestamp convention is read from experiment 22's loader and matched to ENS's. The build prints, per variable, the mean, standard deviation, and 1st and 99th percentiles of the pretraining inputs beside the ENS inputs of the same fold, and stops if a unit differs by a factor over 3 (precipitation in millimetres per second, shortwave in W/m²). The CAMS swap is applied before the P3 noise.

Training recipe. Pretraining: AdamW at 5e-4, weight decay 1e-3, batch 16,384, at most 40 epochs, patience 6, no recency weights (the purpose is the long history), early stopping on the pretraining held-out weeks. Fine-tuning: AdamW at 2e-4, the same weight decay, batch size, epoch limit, and patience, the experiment 397 recency weights, early stopping on the ENS held-out weeks, starting from the best pretrained weights. Three seeds (0, 1, 2) as in experiment 397; seed s seeds both stages. One pretrained network per fold and seed is shared by P1 and P2.

Scale of the work. The screen is 4 folds, 3 seeds, 2 pretrainings (clean and noisy), and 3 fine-tunings: 24 pretrainings and 36 fine-tunings. Each fine-tune and each pretraining is a 7,305-parameter-scale network on up to 13 million rows, so one fit runs for minutes on the GPU. The resource limits are one GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, and a stop line of 12 GB available memory.

docs.title: Earlier advice, and the replicate
docs.text:
• Four screen folds, registered before any fit. The four months are those of common.md (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). December is left out to save compute, and the maintainer's brief asks for four folds. The stored December forecasts are not read.
  • Advice followed: a pooled network with a Primary embedding (experiments 403 and 406) and no attention gate (experiment 397). Advice that cautions: experiment 1 found ERA5 training of a weather-to-power model helps only up to day 6, and experiment 149 found a longer history inconclusive for the generalised additive model, so a null result is plausible.
  • Replicate: ENS-trained arms have a weak replicate over 2025-04 to 2025-06 at 13 Primaries (evaluation-protocol-demand.md). The screen does not read it, and no adoption is sought.
  • Climatology is refitted per fold on the fold's training window and repeated once per seed.
  • A test checks that the held-out-week phase of origin days before 2024-04 is consistent with the phase of the ENS rows.
  • Pretraining row count: each Primary's first usable power date is printed and the measured row count replaces the estimate of 8 to 13 million.

docs.title: Known limits, registered before any fit
docs.text:
• Low-data check: the fold's 24-month window limits the ENS rows, so the 2026-06 fold holds 4 months of ENS before 2024-10-01 and the other folds 6. The pretrained network has seen ERA5 and CAMS rows up to the refit, including the months the fine-tuning drops, so C6 measures less ENS rather than less data. Row counts are logged per fold.
  • P3 noise: the median spread by lead band pools all hours of the day, so shortwave noise is non-zero at night. The write-up reports this as a limit of arm P3.

docs.title: Planned checks the write-up reports
docs.text:
• Row counts: pretraining and fine-tuning rows per fold, and the number of Primaries and years each contributes.
  • Absolute skill: CRPS at days 1 to 10 for every arm beside BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology, at the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight.
  • Tails: q95 and q99 coverage at both groups, with the lead-band breakdown.
  • Low-data check (C6): the arm with the lowest signed-MW-six screen CRPS among P1 to P3 and the ENS-only network, both fine-tuned (or trained) on only the first 6 months of ENS (2024-04-01 to 2024-09-30), three seeds, on the four screen folds.
  • Production cost: one pretrained network refreshed rarely (the build and fit time measured here), plus a cheap monthly fine-tune (its measured time), and the two weather feeds it needs (ERA5 and CAMS history).
  • Figures first: the headline chart of CRPS against lead for all arms, the gain by Primary, and the coverage by lead band, each with plain captions.

docs.title: What would stop the experiment
docs.text: If a build assertion fails on leakage, the experiment is invalid and stops. If the pretrained network's held-out NLL on ERA5 inputs is no better than the untrained network's, pretraining has failed and the verdict is failed for that arm.

docs.title: Evidence this plan follows
docs.text:
• Follows experiment 403 and experiment 406: one pooled network with a Primary embedding.
  • Follows experiment 397: no attention gate, summary inputs, setting g09, and its tails flagged as the open problem.
  • Departs from the experiment 412 capacity-prior arms, which do not apply here because the pretraining target is the same signed-MW or MVA power as the fine-tuning target.
  • Experiment 413 (differentiable-physics network) did not advance, and experiment 406 found the pooled gain grows with short histories, which motivates the low-data check C6.

docs.title: Do the solar summary, the sunny flag, and a different row-weight half-life, which helped the XGBoost model, also help the pooled mixture density network?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the XGBoost model's solar-summary input did not carry over to the pooled plain neural network, and neither did the shorter half-life, so none of the input changes is adopted.

The solar summary cannot be told apart from seed noise. Adding the daily mean of the ensemble's shortwave radiation (sol) lowered the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at the six signed-MW Primaries (primary substations whose power flows both ways, measured in signed megawatts) by only 0.012 points of capacity (-0.043 to +0.013). The change is one sixth of the minimum detectable effect (0.0738 points, twice the fold-to-fold spread of the difference between two sets of random seeds).

A refit with new seeds moved the MVA-only eight more than the solar summary did. The same neural network refitted with new seeds (ctrl_s3) moved the MVA-only eight (the Primaries measured in megavolt-amperes) by -0.047 (-0.075 to -0.022), about six times as far as sol did there (-0.008). At the signed-MW six the refit moved the CRPS by +0.011, the same size as sol.

The sunny flag with a 1-year half-life, and the 0.25-year half-life, did not help. Adding the sunny flag and a 1-year half-life (bundle) was worse than sol by +0.033 and +0.037. The 0.25-year half-life (hl91r, sol_hl91) raised the signed-MW six CRPS by +0.044 (+0.004 to +0.099) and +0.048 (+0.006 to +0.088) while lowering the D15 and D18 CRPS, as experiment 407's 0.25-year half-life did.

The reference ctrl_w115 stays. Whether a solar summary helps this neural network needs more than three seeds or more than five test months. The verdict is not supported. Every number comes from five test months, so all are interim.

docs.text:
At 0.9 of the limit, arms differ from the reference by up to four times as much as the seed refit does, but no interval is printed. The scorer prices the curtailment avoidable at the scaled export limit (studies.node_curtailment), at 0.9 of the limit and in a sweep to 0.75 and 0.5. The table gives the total over the Primaries for which the scorer returns a cost, in millions of pounds. Several Primaries have no cost in any arm (null in the scorer logs).
