  • Time of day explains the loss. P12 falls from 0.183 (T0) to 0.039 (T1) at the signed six (T1 minus T0: -0.149, interval -0.233 to -0.072) and from 0.130 to 0.020 at the MVA-only eight (-0.066, interval -0.120 to -0.007). P36, which hits the same 17:30 hour, falls from 0.226 to 0.091.
  • The delay itself adds little loss where the network was trained. In T2 and T3 the loss grows by 0.04 points from P6 to P30, P12 to P36, and P24 to P48 at the signed six, so each day of extra delay at a constant hour of day raises the loss by about 0.04 points. P10, off the training grid, loses 0.024, between P6 (0.013) and P12 (0.032).
  • The age inputs do not help. T2 and T2n agree at P6, P12, and P24 (within 0.008 at the signed six). T2 loses more than T2n at W24 (0.054 against 0.025) and W24_P24 (0.098 against 0.066) at the signed six, and less at the MVA-only eight. In absolute terms the two networks score alike at W24 (3.347 against 3.353); T2 improves the fresh-case CRPS by only 0.035, and the improvement does not carry to W24. Feeding T2 a weather age of 9 hours reproduces T2n. Clipping the age to 30 hours changes nothing (both found by the audit described under Checks).
  • Missing readings. T4 loses 0.30 (signed six) and 0.32 (MVA-only eight) points in DROP, against 1.7 to 2.4 and 1.7 to 1.9 for T0 to T3. T4's 90% prediction interval is 1.07 and 1.09 times as wide as for fresh inputs, and its coverage of the 95th-percentile quantile (q95) falls by 0.015 and 0.008 (T3: 0.163 and 0.124).
  • Against the XGBoost S1M model. T3 loses less than S1M at P12 (0.032 against 0.306) and W24_P12 (0.077 against 0.338) at the signed six, and at the MVA-only eight (0.021 and 0.056 against 0.098 and 0.130).

docs.title: Tails and fresh-input score
docs.text:
• Tail coverage holds. At both groups, q95 and q99 coverage fall by at most 0.006 and 0.002 in every arm except DROP, P30, P36, P48, and W48, for every training arm. Fresh-case q95 coverage is 0.892 to 0.896 at the signed six and 0.945 to 0.949 at the MVA-only eight, q99 coverage 0.960 to 0.962 and 0.988 to 0.990.
  • Score on fresh inputs. At the signed six, T1 to T4 score within 0.031 of T0 (T3 minus T0: -0.006, interval -0.045 to +0.037). At the MVA-only eight they score worse by +0.044 (T1), +0.085 (T2), +0.046 (T2n), +0.078 (T3), and +0.109 (T4); only T3 (interval +0.011 to +0.140) and T4 (+0.043 to +0.212) exclude zero. Per-seed fresh means agree (T0 3.905, T2n 3.959, T3 3.989, T4 4.047). The q95 and q99 pinball losses rise by under 0.03 and 0.01 at the MVA-only eight.
  • Seed spread. The standard deviation across the three seeds of one arm's fresh CRPS is 0.01 to 0.05 points. The month-block intervals do not include seed noise. A contrast of two 3-seed averages therefore carries about 0.03 to 0.04 points of extra noise, so the minimum detectable fresh-case contrast is about 0.07 points.

docs.title: Design, data, and caveats
docs.text:
• Recipe. The recipe is experiment 397's pooled plain network (setting g09, three Gaussian components, Primary embedding, ensemble mean and standard deviation of seven weather variables), trained with its training loop, early stopping on every twelfth week (held out), and a 1.15 widening of the outer quantiles about the median. Fits are monthly refits on the 24 months before the refit, for the 5 screen months and three seeds per arm. The 90 fits took 14 to 75 seconds each on the GPU. Code reused from experiments 87, 397, and 410 is imported, not copied.
  • Cleaned data. Flagged substation_zero half-hours are missing in lags and dropped from targets and scoring actuals. The numbers of flagged half-hours in the 5 test months are 153, 11, 0, 3, and 0. In training, 51,600 to 53,200 half-hours per fold are missing: the flagged half-hours, all half-hours before 2025-03-01 at substations D15 and D18, and unobserved half-hours.
  • Rows. Held-out weeks purge 15 days before and 9 days after, because a delay of 24 hours moves a lag a day back. Each random draw (origin hour, delay, weather run, missing lags) is made once per training row and seed, not once per epoch.
  • Reproduction gate. T0's fresh CRPS is 3.324 (signed six) and 3.832 (MVA-only eight) against the stored network's 3.270 and 3.873. The audit could not explain the 0.054 gap at the signed six (1.5 standard errors of a three-seed difference; the MVA-only eight shows the opposite sign). Every contrast here uses T0 and so does not depend on it.
  • Checks. The median forecast minus the mean forecast is -0.23 to -0.27 points at the signed six and -0.39 to -0.47 at the MVA-only eight in every training arm. The error of the median forecast moves with the quantile score: T0 P12 raises the median's mean absolute error by 0.33 points at the signed six (5.81 to 6.14), against 0.05 for T3. Triggers fired: a nested arm beats the arm that contains it (T2 against T2n at W24), a control moves more than expected (T0's DROP loss is 2.4 points against 9.7 for the stored network), and the results contradict Predictions 2, 3, and
  • A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the CRPS of T0, T2, T2n, and T3 in four arms by its own code (largest difference 0.0002), found no leakage in the training-row and scoring code it read, and explained the two anomalies.
  • Audit finding on DROP. The D15 and D18 start cut leaves 9 times as many training rows with all three lags missing in T0 (0.20%) as in experiment 397's rows (0.022%). A refit of T0 without the cut loses 9.1 and 6.4 points in DROP, like the stored network. T0's DROP loss is therefore a side effect of the start cut, and T4's 0.30 should be read against 2.4 (with the cut) and 9.1 (without).
  • Prediction outcomes. Prediction 1 held for P12 (0.039 and 0.020) and P6, and failed for P24 at the signed six (0.053 against 0.05). Prediction 2 failed at W24 (T2's loss is 0.029 above T0's) and held for the delay arms, W24_P12 (0.088), and W24_P24 (0.098). Prediction 2n failed at W24, W24_P12, W24_P24, W48, and DROP at the signed six, and at W48 and DROP at the MVA-only eight. Prediction 3 held for W24 (0.044) and W48 above W24, and failed for W24_P12 (0.077) and W24_P24 (0.088). Prediction 4 held at the signed six (0.043, 0.043, 0.040 in T2) and failed at the MVA-only eight (0.029, 0.029, 0.024). Prediction 5 held at the signed six and failed at the MVA-only eight. Predictions 6, 7, and 8 held. Prediction 9 held (P10 within 0.004 of the interpolation).
  • Decision rule. T3 meets every experiment 410 limit at both groups on point estimates; its W24_P24 upper bound at the signed six is 0.109, above 0.10. The fresh-case score rise at the MVA-only eight (+0.078) exceeds +0.03, so the verdict is "partly supported". T1, T2n, T2, and T4 also meet the limits. The experiment 410 limits were proposed without evidence, and the numbers are given beside them for the maintainer to judge.
  • Caveats. 5 test months give wide intervals. The audit's mechanism for T2's W24 result (age and origin hour are tied in training and decoupled at test) is inferred, not tested. The scored lead range, days 1 to 10, matches NGED's horizon. No XGBoost model was refitted, and P30, P36, P48, and P10 were scored for the neural networks only.
  • Untested next steps. T1 could be tested over the full scored year, and the fresh-case score at the MVA-only eight with more seeds. Training with the three lags sometimes missing (T4) would prepare the neural network for absent readings in production. The weather age could be decoupled from the origin hour in training before the age input is used again. Fits and forecasts: data/ml-experiments/00422-*/work/ (not in git).

docs.title: Does a small calendar encoder, shared by all 16 Primaries, forecast bank-holiday weeks better than the hand-made calendar columns of the pooled mixture density network?
docs.text:
Plan: can the pooled network learn how people use the calendar, instead of being handed it?

Caveat that governs the verdict. The bank-holiday-week rows are 14 days of one Christmas and New Year week and 2 days of Easter week, in three test months. The seed noise on those rows (the minimum detectable effect for six-seed means at the signed-MW six) is 0.343 points of capacity, against the 0.10 that prediction P1 needs. By the plan's own rule P1 is therefore untestable at the five screen folds, and this page reports it as untestable whatever the point estimate. The tested all-rows contrasts (C1, C2, C4) and the descriptive Christmas and Easter scores are what this experiment can answer; the 2026-04 event fold adds six Easter-set days.

docs.title: Design note (Sonnet read of the docs sketches and experiment 396's holiday arms)
docs.text:
• The one encoder sketch we found is TimeEncoder in the production docs' encoders page. It names time of day, day of week, month, bank holidays, Christmas, and Easter, and gives no sizes or training recipe.
  • The pooled plain network gets 18 hand-made calendar columns today (experiment 397, e00397_prep.feature_names): sine and cosine of the hour at 1 and 2 cycles, a one-hot weekday, covid, three Christmas columns, bank_holiday, and two distance columns, from holidays.country_holidays("GB", subdiv="ENG"). It never sees a holiday name, a day of month, or a day of year.
  • Experiment 396 (XGBoost) adds a bank-holiday flag, a signed distance clipped at 7 days, day-before and day-after flags, and a holiday-type code (bank holiday, Easter, Christmas period, New Year, other).
  • Each named holiday has only one or two days in a training window. The window is the 24 months before the refit, clipped at 2024-04-01.
Holiday 2025-10 2025-12 2026-01 2026-03 2026-06 Christmas Day 1 1 2 2 2 Boxing Day 1 1 2 2 2 New Year's Day 1 1 1 2 2 Good Friday 1 1 1 1 2 Easter Monday 2 2 2 2 2 Early May, spring, summer 2 2 2 2 2 All bank holidays 12 12 14 15 16

  • What that limits. An embedding for "Christmas Day" is fitted on one or two days, so it can memorise them and not generalise. A holiday-name encoder can help only by tying holidays together: the five Monday bank holidays share one type with 8 to 10 days. A dates-only encoder cannot follow Easter between years. Any Easter result rests on two days, so the expected gain is small and sits in E1 against E2, and in shared against per-Primary encoders.

  • Experiment 396's holiday columns helped one metering group only. In January they lowered the XGBoost CRPS by 0.046 points at the signed-MW group (interim, unaudited) and raised it at the MVA-only group. The plan therefore scores E1 and E2 separately for the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight in every contrast, and does not expect the holiday-aware encoder to help the eight.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms keep the weather, solar, lag, and covid inputs, the 8-wide Primary embedding, the standardiser (fitted on the training rows; the encoder's integer indices bypass it), the trunk width and depth, the optimiser, the held-out-weeks early stopping grouped by origin day (experiment 397's held_out_weeks), and the row drops of experiments 407 and 419 (e00419_fit.build_train). Only the 18 calendar columns change.

  • R (reference). The 18 hand-made calendar columns; stored forecasts of experiments 407 and 419, not refitted on the five screen folds. R0 is a check: R refitted through the new code path (seed 0, fold 2025-12, and on 2026-04), which must reproduce the stored R within seed noise.
  • E0 (memorisation control). Local half-hour (8-wide embedding) and weekday (4-wide) only; then Linear 32, GELU, Linear 16. Seeds 0 to 2.
  • E1n. E0 plus the two distance columns (nearest_days, nearest_inside) and a bank-holiday flag, with no holiday name.
  • E1. E1n plus the holiday name (12 categories: none, New Year's Day, Good Friday, Easter Monday, early May, spring, summer, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, other bank holiday, substitute day, 24 to 31 December non-holiday; the code lists them from the holidays package) as a 4-wide embedding, and day of month (4-wide) and day of year (366 buckets, 4-wide).
  • E2. The dates only: E0 plus day of month and day of year, with no holiday information of any kind. E2 minus E0 isolates the date columns, and E1 minus E1n isolates the holiday name.
  • E3 (conditional). One E1 per Primary.

Each encoder outputs 16 wide and trains end to end on the same loss. The hour index is the local half-hour, so the clock changes land on the same index.

docs.title: Row sets and folds
docs.text:
Row sets use the local calendar date of the valid time, as in e00396_arms.add_calendar: bank holiday day; bank-holiday week (Monday to Sunday); Christmas set (24 December to 1 January); Easter set (Monday of Holy Week to Easter Monday).

Row set (days in the test month) 2025-10 2025-12 2026-01 2026-03 2026-06 Bank-holiday days 0 2 1 0 0 Bank-holiday-week days 0 10 4 2 0 Christmas set 0 8 1 0 0 Easter set 0 0 0 2 0
  • The five screen folds hold one Christmas and a two-day sliver of Easter week. The event fold 2026-04 (Good Friday 2026-04-03, Easter Monday 2026-04-06) adds six Easter-set days to the two in March; its weather inputs exist, and its results are in the event-fold bullet below.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text:
• Monthly refits on the 24-month window of experiment 397's folds; cleaned data (flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped, counts printed per fold); D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; ENS mean and spread passed once; fitted networks saved under this experiment's private folder; stored forecasts reused (R), which saves 30 fits.
  • Cost. E1, E1n, and E2 times 5 folds times 6 seeds is 90 fits and E0 adds 15, each of 50 to 200 seconds. The 2026-04 event fold adds 21 and R0 adds 6; E3 adds 30 if it runs. One GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The encoder indices are integers, precomputed once per refit.
  • Reference. The reference stays ctrl, because none of experiment 419's input changes won; the Primary embedding and pooling of experiments 403 and 406 are kept.
  • Plan reviewed against the latest evidence (origin/main, 2026-10-31): experiment 419 showed that seed noise moves the six by about 0.011 and the MVA-only eight by 0.047, so the plan uses six seeds and prints the minimum detectable effect; the planned experiments 418, 421, and 422 change the training data or inputs of the same network. Their plans do not mention the calendar columns, except one calendar term in 422's. This experiment's code is merged with theirs after they land.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The calendar encoder did not help. On the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, days 1 to 10, in points of effective capacity), the 18 hand-made calendar columns (R) beat every encoder arm at the six Primaries that report signed power (the signed-MW six). The two arms with date embeddings (E1 and E2) were worse than R in every fold, by 0.04 to 0.71 points. The arms without date embeddings (E0 and E1n) were 0.10 worse than R at the signed-MW six and 0.04 to 0.06 better at the eight Primaries that report apparent power only (the MVA-only eight), which is about the size of the seed noise. The prediction about bank-holiday weeks could not be tested.

Arms. R: the 18 hand-made calendar columns (hour sine and cosine, weekday, Christmas and bank-holiday flags, distance to the nearest bank holiday, and covid). E0: a learned encoder of the half-hour and weekday only. E1n: E0 plus the bank-holiday flag and distance columns. E1: E1n plus the holiday name, day of month, and day of year. E2: E0 plus day of month and day of year, and no holiday information. All five feed the same pooled mixture density network (a neural network that outputs a probability distribution), with the 8-wide Primary embedding of experiment 397.

Design flaw found at the write-up. E1 minus E1n adds the holiday name and the two date embeddings together, so contrast C3 and prediction P1 test "name plus dates", not the name alone. An arm with the name and without the dates is needed to isolate the name.

We asked whether the pooled neural network forecasts better if it learns how people use the calendar, instead of being given the 18 hand-made columns. We replaced the columns by a small learned encoder, shared by all 16 Primaries, and compared four versions with the columns on five test months. This experiment builds on experiments 397, 407, and 419, whose code and stored forecasts it reuses, and on the encoder sketch in the production docs' encoders page.

Verdict: not supported. The hypothesis needed the encoder to help in holiday weeks and to be no worse on all rows. The encoder was clearly worse on all rows.

The example forecasts start on 2025-12-24 and cover D5 (signed-MW) and D2 (MVA-only), both Primaries. At D5 the actuals fall below every arm's median from 30 December. This appears to be a change in the actuals and not an effect of any arm, but the experiment did not check it.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Arms and row set. R is the stored ctrl network (experiment 407, seeds 0 to 2; experiment 419, seeds 3 to 5). E0, E1n, E1, and E2 are as in the plan above; E0 has three seeds and the others six. Five screen folds, monthly refits, cleaned data (flagged exact-zero training rows dropped per fold: 2,155, 2,846, 2,886, 2,899, 2,925; 1,179 scoring half-hours dropped), D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 (report-only). Widened by 1.15. Fitted networks are in this experiment's private work/models folder.
  • CRPS, days 1 to 10 (points of capacity), all rows, signed-MW six / MVA-only eight / D15 and D18: R 3.269 / 3.817 / 8.565; E0 3.375 / 3.762 / 8.744; E1n 3.373 / 3.778 / 8.971; E1 3.539 / 4.075 / 9.026; E2 3.635 / 4.090 / 9.002.
  • Seed noise. The minimum detectable effect for six-seed means (twice the standard deviation over folds of ctrl against ctrl_s3, divided by the square root of two) is 0.052 at the six and 0.047 at the eight; for three-seed means 0.074 and 0.066. On the bank-holiday-week rows it is 0.343 at the six (three folds, two degrees of freedom) and 0.103 at the eight.
  • Tested contrasts (treatment minus reference, interval at 98.75%, month-block bootstrap over 3 to 5 blocks, so read as a range): C1 E1 minus R, all rows: +0.270 (+0.096 to +0.425) at the six, +0.258 (+0.202 to +0.387) at the eight. C2 E2 minus R: +0.366 (+0.167 to +0.596) and +0.273 (+0.200 to +0.399). C3 E1 minus E1n on bank-holiday weeks: +0.353 (+0.020 to +0.384) at the six, +0.390 at the eight; positive in all three folds (+0.384, +0.020, +0.337). C4 E2 minus E0, seeds 0 to 2 both: +0.303 (+0.159 to +0.429) and +0.384 (+0.282 to +0.537).
  • P1 (holiday names help on bank-holiday weeks by 0.10): untestable, the detectable effect is 0.343; the point estimate went the other way (+0.353).
  • P2: failed for E1 and E2, which are outside the noise at both groups; E0 and E1n are 0.10 worse at the six (outside the six-seed noise of 0.052) and about the size of the noise at the eight, where they are better (-0.055 and -0.039 against 0.047).
  • P3 (E2 no better than E0): held, E2 is 0.30 worse at the six and 0.38 at the eight (C4).
  • P4 (does not help the eight): held, no arm beats R at the eight by more than the noise.
  • Christmas set, signed-MW six (one Christmas, descriptive): R 3.676, E0 5.316, E1n 4.238, E1 4.724, E2 5.336. Easter set, signed-MW six (two days in March): R 3.781, E0 3.935, E1n 4.089, E1 4.437, E2 4.765.
  • Event fold 2026-04 (one-seed R0 against encoder seed means; point estimates only): signed-MW six: R0 2.687, E0 2.652, E1n 2.613, E1 3.042, E2 2.932. MVA-only eight: R0 4.161, E0 4.244, E1n 4.102, E1 4.605, E2 4.569. Easter set, signed-MW six: R0 2.937, E1n 2.887, E1 3.284, E2 3.967. E1 and E2 again score worse than R0 at both groups; E0 and E1n do not repeat their 0.10 loss at the six, and the single-seed reference makes this fold a weak check.
  • Tails (widened by 1.15), coverage at q95 and q99 and pinball loss at q99, signed-MW six: R 0.894, 0.961, 0.350; E1n 0.885, 0.953, 0.371; E1 0.907, 0.971, 0.314; E2 0.905, 0.973, 0.295. MVA-only eight: R 0.947, 0.989, 0.255; E1 0.945, 0.987, 0.315; E2 0.946, 0.987, 0.317. The encoders with dates (E1, E2) have a lower q99 pinball loss at the six and a higher one at the eight. Lower-tail coverage at q01 and q05 and the sunny low-demand check are in the scorer's printed report.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site (MAE of the median minus MAE of the mean): within +/-0.17 points at every Primary for every arm except D8 (-0.68 to -0.93) and D15 (+0.82 to +1.66). R shows the same two exceptions (D8 -0.68, D15 +0.82), so the encoders do not shift the forecast at those two Primaries. At D15 the gap grows with the encoders (R +0.82, E1n +1.05, E1 +1.22, E0 +1.52, E2 +1.66), a Primary with a short history and report-only.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside the quantile contrast: this run did not print the MAE of the median or of the mean on its own, only their difference above, so audit trigger 3 (the quantile-score contrast and the mean-forecast contrast pointing in different directions) was not checked directly. The audit's re-derivation of the CRPS contrasts agrees in sign with the scorer's.
  • Audit. Two triggers fired: a result contradicting its prediction (E1 and E2 worse than R) and a nested arm doing worse than the arm it contains (E1 against E1n, E2 against E0). A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the contrasts from the stored forecasts with its own CRPS code and agreed within 0.01 (E1 minus R +0.266, E2 minus R +0.360 at the six). It looked for a bug and found none: training and inference build the calendar indices the same way, the encoder weights train, and the row drops are identical across arms. The held-out validation loss agrees with the test CRPS: E1 ends 0.12 to 0.17 nats worse than E1n, E2 about as far, and both stop after about 10 epochs, against 22 to 36 for the other arms.
  • Reference check. R0 (the hand-made columns refitted through the new code, fold 2025-12, seed 0) reproduces the stored reference to +0.000 at all three groups, so the pipeline differs from the stored one only in the encoder.
  • Triage. The memorisation explanation is consistent with these numbers but untested: the 366-row day-of-year table stays close to its random start, so the encoder may be passing noise into the network, and a zero-initialised or shuffled-bucket placebo would separate the two readings. Accepted, and worded as "consistent with" here. The day-of-year index is the per-year ordinal, so dates after February 2024 sit one bucket later than in 2025 and 2026; this touches only folds 2025-10 and 2025-12 and does not explain the other three folds. Accepted as a caveat. dropped_rows.json holds one value per fold and not per arm; the fit log holds the per-arm counts. No finding changed a number.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The training window holds one or two examples of each named holiday (design note above), so the question of whether names can tie holidays together was tested on little data.
  • Five screen folds are interim. The month-block intervals rest on three to five blocks.
  • Experiment 396's holiday columns helped only the signed-MW group (XGBoost, January, unaudited); here no encoder arm helps either group on all rows.
  • Not run: the per-Primary encoder (E3), because its condition (C1 below zero or C3 at most -0.05) did not hold; a placebo for the memorisation explanation; and the lead-hours bands 11 to 14.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Keep the hand-made calendar columns. The question the experiment leaves open is whether a pooled network with a longer history (the pretraining of experiment 418) can use date embeddings, and a placebo (zero-initialised or shuffled day-of-year) would show whether the dates carry any signal at all.

docs.title: Does the export-gated neural network still forecast signed power better than the plain reading when it sees ensemble weather forecasts instead of recorded weather?
docs.text:
Take-home: with ensemble weather forecasts in place of recorded weather, the neural network with an export gate still forecasts signed power on reverse-flow half-hours much better than the same neural network with the gate shut, although the ensemble forecasts make it less accurate. Signed power is positive for demand and negative for reverse flow, where solar generation exports power up the electricity network. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of a substation's effective capacity), and lower is better. The gate-shut network scores 29.97 and the export-gated network 14.26, a gain of 15.7 points (95% interval 13.8 to 17.4), against 19.2 with recorded weather. The test covers six primary substations with one real solar farm's output added, in spring, summer, and autumn months only.

An unplanned finding: the neural network trained on recorded weather and applied unchanged to ensemble weather scored 5.5 points better (95% interval 4.4 to 6.6) than the neural network retrained on ensemble weather. The pass bars written down before scoring did not test this comparison, and no prediction covered it.

This experiment asks whether the signed forecast of the export-gated neural network survives the step from recorded weather to ensemble weather forecasts. Eight primary substations (the "MVA-only" eight) report only the size of the power that flows, not its direction. Experiment 420 hid the direction at six primary substations where it is known (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 are anonymised labels) and added a real solar farm's recorded output to some of them. It found that a neural network with an export gate, set once per substation to open or shut from a statistic of the substation's readings, forecasts the signed power far better than the same neural network with the gate shut (7.1 against 26.3 points on reverse-flow half-hours). The weather in that test was recorded CAMS irradiance and ERA5 temperature, which a live service does not have at forecast time. This experiment repeats the test with the ensemble (ENS) forecast of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts: the mean and spread across its 51 members of the same weather variables. It trains the neural network on them and scores it on the same rows, in three rotations of which two substations are hidden at a time. The gate still helps a great deal, though less than with recorded weather.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
S1, S2, and S3 pass for A, and the pooled floor is met. All 105 fits and 42 forecast-only runs finished. Values are points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of a substation's effective capacity) of the signed continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), level 2.0 unless stated, with 95% Primary-month block intervals; A is the mean of two seeds and the other arms use seed 0. The minimum detectable effect, written before scoring, was 1.735. All scores are in work/scores_full.json. "Hidden" substations are the six whose direction of flow was hidden from the neural network, and "no-injection" is the setting with no farm added.

Bar Result Passes? S1, gain of A over P0 on reverse-flow rows, pooled 15.72 (13.85 to 17.41), floor 10 Yes S1 by substation D5 5.75, D9 20.67, D10 10.01, D11 16.67, D14 17.84, D16 19.80; every interval excludes zero and clears 1.735 Yes S2, harm at the no-injection substations, pooled +0.009 (-0.003 to 0.023); D9 +0.051, others -0.004 to +0.003 Yes (limits +0.05 pooled, +0.20 single) S3, reading harm at the MVA-only eight, pooled -0.005 (-0.036 to 0.020) Yes (limit +0.05)

The prediction was met on every clause: pooled floors, every hidden substation's interval, S2, S3, and the gate decisions. The label scope in the decision rule gives "inferred, ensemble-tested, gated" at D8 and D12. That label rests on the gate opening in all 21 fits and on the reading check (S3), because those two substations have no signed truth to score.

Unplanned: the network trained on recorded weather and applied to ensemble inputs beat the retrained network. A-applied scored 5.50 points better than A (4.35 to 6.61; 8.76 against 14.26, A as the mean of two seeds), and 21.22 better than P0 (18.42 to 23.77). The plan called A-applied a diagnostic. No bar or prediction covered it, and it contradicts the plan's reason for retraining (a network that has seen ensemble inputs should cope with their bias). A likely explanation, which the stored fits support but no test confirms, is noise in the ensemble inputs. Noise in an input shrinks the fitted coefficient on it. The fitted solar coefficient (the multiple of the unit shape subtracted from demand) was lower and less stable when trained on ensemble inputs: at D9 in seed 0 it ran from 39 to 88 points of capacity across the seven fits, against 98 to 107 with recorded weather. The two seeds of A differ by 2.09 points (0.88 to 3.29) on average, so seed noise is large next to every contrast except S1.

  • Absolute scores on reverse-flow rows: P0 29.97, A 14.26, and for reference the recorded-weather arms of experiment 420: P0 26.26, A 7.05, ref (no gate) 6.99. A-applied scored 8.76.
  • Lead bands (gain of A over P0): days 1 to 2 16.18 (14.25 to 17.90), days 3 to 6 15.86 (13.97 to 17.61), days 7 to 10 15.35 (13.50 to 17.03). The point estimates fall by 0.8 points from the first band to the last, less than the minimum detectable effect, and the intervals overlap. No paired lead-band contrast was computed.
  • Ensemble against recorded weather for A: worse by 7.20 (5.85 to 8.54).
  • Primary-level gates: open at D8 and D12 in all 21 fits and shut at D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22 in all 21, as with recorded weather. The six hidden substations' gates opened in all seven of their fits each.
  • Rotation r1 (stage 1) before the full run: gain 7.79 (6.39 to 9.12) against 8.29 with recorded weather at D5 and D10, floor 4, minimum detectable effect 0.907. Stage 1 passed.
  • Cleaned data: each refit drops 57,531 to 94,724 training rows (summed over the 16 trial-area substations: the six hidden, the eight MVA-only, D15, and D18) that have no usable power reading, including the half-hours the substation_zero rule flags; the counts per fit are in each fit's JSON file. No training row has a missing ensemble unit shape.

With ensemble inputs the sign is called much less well, and the lower tail is too narrow. The numbers are descriptive, level 2.0, seed 0, on the half-hours with the recorded CAMS unit shape at least 0.3 and clear-sky index at least 0.7 (115,040 rows), for every arm.

Measure A (ensemble) A-applied A (recorded weather, experiment 420) Balanced accuracy at P(X < 0) > 0.5 0.600 0.781 0.852 Recall of reverse flow 0.235 0.676 0.859 False-reverse rate, every non-reverse slice row 3.6% 11.5% 15.5% Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.876 0.891 0.930 q01 coverage on reverse-flow rows (nominal 0.01) 0.091 0.118 0.062 q05 coverage (nominal 0.05) 0.308 0.254 not recorded here q95 coverage (nominal 0.95) 1.000 0.987 not recorded here q99 coverage (nominal 0.99) 1.000 0.998 0.998
  • Tail pinball losses (A, ensemble): q01 0.82, q05 3.37, q95 3.11, q99 0.74; P0: 19.20, 20.20, 3.40, 0.79.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus the mean implied by the quantiles, on reverse-flow rows, pooled (trapezoid integration of the 11 quantiles, a rough check): P0 -1.87 points (negative at every substation), A +0.04 (-1.31 at D5 to +0.95 at D11), A-applied -0.10, recorded-weather A -0.14. The spread does not shift A's forecast.
  • Error of the median forecast beside the CRPS contrast (mean absolute error of the median on reverse-flow rows): P0 39.83, A 26.99, A-applied 15.05, recorded-weather A 12.24. The error of the median forecast points the same way as every CRPS contrast, so audit trigger 3 (the two disagree) did not fire.
  • Leave-one-substation-out for A-applied against A: A-applied stays better when any one of the six hidden substations is left out (4.55 when D9 is left out, up to 6.31 when D5 is). D9 carries the most weight. Trigger 4 (leaving one site out flips a contrast) did not fire.
  • Triggers that fired. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own plan) fired in part: A-applied contradicts the plan's reason for retraining, and the explanation is descriptive, not tested. No audit was run, because the S1 to S3 verdicts do not depend on A-applied and the page states the cause as untested. Trigger 5 (a nested arm beats its container) does not apply, because A-applied is not nested in A. Trigger 7 (a later design depends on an unreplicated headline) is met: a live-service port would depend on the 15.7-point headline, which replicates the recorded-weather result on the same injected series. The placebo control held (S2).
  • Mixed seed counts. A is the mean of two seeds in S1, S3, and the A-applied contrast; P0 and A-applied use seed 0. Against seed 0 of A alone the A-applied gain is 6.54 (5.09 to 8.00), and against seed 1 alone 4.45, so the size depends on which seed is read and the sign never changes.
  • S2 pooled excludes D10 (real reverse flow); D10's A-minus-P0 harm is -0.043.
  • Caveats. The reverse-flow rows come from six substations in one rotation each, so rotation and substation are confounded, with 42 blocks. The injected farm is real recorded output added to real demand. The test months are 2025-07 to 2025-09 and 2026-03 to 2026-06, so no winter month is scored. The scored lead range is 0 to 240 hours (days 1 to 10). The 2025-07 refit trains on 15 months, not 24. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so unlogged events may sit in the readings.
  • Not done. Avoidable-curtailment cost (see Departures), a climatology row, a winter example forecast, and a pretrain-then-fine-tune arm (experiment 418's recipe).

docs.title: Plan as registered
docs.text: The sections below were written before any fit or score, and the two minimum-detectable-effect sections were committed before the matching contrasts were read.

docs.title: Evidence the plan follows
docs.text:
• Experiment 420 (merged, pull request 77) found a laboratory gain of 19.2 points (16.5 to 21.5) of the gated network over the gate-shut network, and said most of it comes from allowing negative values, because the ungated reference scored the same as A on reverse-flow rows. The gate matters at the no-injection Primary D5. This plan keeps those caveats.
  • Experiment 418 (merged) found that pretraining on recorded weather and then fitting on the ENS archive helps (about 0.06 points at the six signed-MW Primaries and 0.16 at the eight, over 12 test months), and that an ENS-only fit degrades badly when the archive covers only 6 months. The ENS archive used here covers 2024-04 to 2026-06, so each refit has 15 to 24 months, as in experiment 420. A pretrain-then-fine-tune arm would add a design question, so this plan leaves it as a named next step.
  • Experiments 419 and 423 (merged) found no input change that beats seed noise for the pooled neural network. This plan adds ENS spread columns as inputs, so seed noise is measured here (a second seed of A) before any contrast is read.
  • The data-processing page says ENS irradiance needs calibration against CAMS (shifts of up to 20% in irradiance and 2 K in temperature) and is a 6-hour mean after lead 144 hours. Both facts are why the preferred arm is retrained on ENS inputs, so the network learns the bias, and why an applied-only network is reported as a diagnostic with no bar.
  • Standing practices applied: monthly refits; cleaned data with the dropped count stored per fit (experiment 417's fold drops the flagged half-hours); D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; every network saved as a state file; tails and examples reported; draft pull request. Departures are listed below. Earlier advice followed: score a signed forecast against the ungated network as well as the gate-shut network (reference rows below); label the signed output by what was tested. Advice departed from: none.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The preferred arm is retrained on ENS inputs, and the weather it sees at training time and at inference time is the same ENS mean and spread. Training on realised weather and serving ENS weather would put the network in a distribution it never saw, and the ENS forecast carries known biases. A network applied without retraining is reported as a diagnostic (arm A-applied).

Arm What it is Role P0 Experiment 420's P0 (gate forced shut, plain reading read as signed), trained on ENS inputs Benchmark A Experiment 420's arm A (Primary-level export gate), trained on ENS inputs Candidate A-applied Experiment 420's saved arm A networks (trained on CAMS and ERA5, seed 0), applied to ENS inputs with no refit Diagnostic, reported only, zero fits lab A, lab ref, lab P0 Experiment 420's stored forecasts on CAMS and ERA5 inputs Reported only

What changes in the inputs. Experiment 417's fold is reused unchanged except for three series:

  • PV term and Primary gate. The scaled CAMS unit shape u and clear-sky index k become the ENS-mean unit shape (from the ENS mean shortwave irradiance, divided by the same u99) and the ENS clearness index, taken from experiment 405's extras arrays row by row.
  • Temperature. ERA5 temperature becomes the ENS mean temperature.
  • Spread. Three standardised input columns are added to the demand module: the temperature spread (standard deviation across the 51 members), the unit-shape spread, and the mean temperature itself. The columns are computed once per run, so the network is passed once per row, with no member loop.

Everything else is as in experiment 420: injected farm and reactive floor Q = 2 points at power factor 1, rotations r1 (D5, D10 hidden), r2 (D9, D14), and r3 (D11, D16), the seven test months 2025-07, 2025-08, 2025-09, 2026-03, 2026-04, 2026-05, and 2026-06, 730-day training windows, monthly refits, the same early-stopping weeks, and scoring on leads up to 240 hours (days 1 to 10). Rows are the same rows as experiment 420's, so experiment 420's stored forecasts pair with these row by row.

Settings. Level 2.0 (main) and the no-injection placebo. Level 1.0 is not run, because the question is whether the main result survives ensemble weather.

Weather availability at forecast time. ENS runs are usable 9 hours after their start time (the NWP_PUBLICATION_DELAY_HOURS constant), and each row's ENS values come from the 00Z-run summary that experiment 397 attaches to the row's forecast origin, so no lag-time weather is recorded weather. Before 2025-07-01 experiment 397 builds the ENS mean and spread from the archive (only the control member is stored); from 2025-07-01 it uses the stored 51-member frames. Both arms see this source change, and the month-by-month table shows whether it matters. Rows with missing ENS values stay in both arms with the missing inputs set to zero after standardisation, so the rows match experiment 420's; the count of such rows per fit is stored. The lags in the demand module are power lags, as in experiment 420.

docs.title: Scoring and pass bars
docs.text:
The primary contrast is signed CRPS in points of effective capacity, days 1 to 10, on the hidden-sign rows with reverse flow, A against P0, both on ENS inputs, pooled over the six hidden Primaries. Intervals come from a paired month-block bootstrap (resample whole Primary-months, 20,000 resamples), because each half-hour appears in about 15 runs.

The minimum detectable effect is written down before any arm-against-arm score is read. It is 2.8 times the month-block bootstrap standard deviation of the null difference between A's two seeds (ENS inputs) on reverse-flow rows. Stage 1 fits A's second seed at level 2.0 on rotation r1 so that the figure exists first; the full-run figure uses all three rotations. Each figure is committed to this page before the matching contrast is read. A figure above 0.5 points marks the contrast as underpowered.

  • S1 (gain over P0). A's reverse-row CRPS is below P0's by at least the minimum detectable effect, with the interval excluding zero, pooled and at each hidden Primary at level 2.0. On rotation r1, stage 1 pools D5 and D10 and reads each of the two. S1 also needs a pooled floor, 10 points over the three rotations and 4 points on rotation r1, because experiment 420's minimum detectable effect (0.27 to 0.40 points) is far below every laboratory gain and cannot fail alone. The floors are about half the laboratory gains. A gain above the minimum detectable effect but below its floor is a small gain, not a pass. The minimum detectable effect governs only the contrasts it can resolve (A against A-applied, and A on ENS against A on laboratory inputs); a figure above 0.5 points marks those contrasts, and S1 if it is that large, as underpowered.
  • S2 (no harm where there is no export). Read on the point estimate, with the interval end reported. In the placebo setting, signed CRPS on all rows of D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16 is within +0.05 points of P0 pooled, with no single Primary above +0.20. D10 is left out because it has real reverse flow.
  • S3 (the MVA-only eight). Read on the point estimate. At a Primary whose gate is shut, A's reading forecast equals P0's by construction, so S3 can fail only through the Primaries whose gate opens. Reading CRPS at the eight, from the same fits, is within +0.05 points of P0 pooled.

Reported with no bar: the gain by lead band (days 1 to 2, days 3 to 6 up to a lead of 144 hours, and days 7 to 10 above 144 hours, where the ENS stamps change from 3-hourly to 6-hourly; headline days 1 to 10); experiment 420's laboratory A, ref, and P0 beside the ENS arms, and the paired difference of A on ENS inputs against A on laboratory inputs; A-applied against P0 and against A; q01 and q99 coverage and pinball loss on reverse-flow rows; sign balanced accuracy, recall, ROC area, and the false-reverse rate at P(X < 0) > 0.5 on both denominators of experiment 420; each Primary-level gate decision with its Spearman statistic, with the decisions at the eight set beside experiment 420's (open at D8 and D12, shut at D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22); the dropped half-hours per fit. Experiment 420's caveat is kept in the write-up: most of the gain over P0 is being allowed to go below zero, and the gate matters at the D5 placebo.

Observation made before scoring, and a correction to the gate input. Building the stage-1 training fold for the 2025-07 refit (no fit, no score) first gave a gate shut at D8 and D12. The cause was experiment 417's gate code, which keeps the first row of each valid time. With CAMS every row of a valid time has the same weather, but each ENS row has its own run, and the first row is the longest-lead one (mean lead 333 hours at D5), whose irradiance is a blurred 6-hour mean. The plan therefore computes the Primary-level gate on each valid time's shortest-lead row (e00424_inputs.primary_gates), which is a design choice made before any score. On those rows the gate opens at D5, D8, D10, and D12 in that fold, as in experiment 420. The ENS clearness index is the ENS mean shortwave over 1000 * cos(zenith), not a CAMS clear-sky index, so the gate's k >= 0.7 selects a different, sparser set of rows; the number of rows behind each gate decision is stored.

docs.title: Fits, compute, and stop rule
docs.text:
Batch Fits Stage 1: P0 and A at level 2.0 and the placebo, seed 0, rotation r1, 7 months (28), plus A seed 1 at level 2.0 (7) 35 Full run: all three rotations, P0 and A at both settings (84) plus A seed 1 at level 2.0 (21) 105 A-applied: forecast only, 3 rotations × 7 months × 2 settings 0 fits, 42 forecasts

Stage 1 runs rotation r1 only. If A fails S1 on r1, stop. Otherwise tell the manager and run the remaining rotations (70 fits). Experiment 420 timed a fit at 26 to 83 seconds including the fold build, so stage 1 takes about 30 to 60 minutes and the full run about 1.5 to 3 hours, on one GPU process using about 1.4 GB of GPU memory, one CPU core, systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p OOMPolicy=continue, with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The fit script reads MemAvailable before every fold and every fit and stops if it falls below 12 GiB (the available column of free -g). A fit is skipped when its JSON file exists, so a stopped run resumes. Experiment 420's fits are not repeated: its stored forecasts are the laboratory reference rows. Outputs go to work/fits/<arm>/, state files to work/models/<arm>/, in this experiment's private folder.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
All code is in ml-experiments/00424-neural-mva-export-gated-signed-ens-serving-test/.

  • e00424_inputs.py builds experiment 417's fold with ENS inputs (build_fold) and the ENS model inputs.
  • e00424_fit.py defines the jobs, fits P0 and A, forecasts the hidden pair and the eight, and runs A-applied from experiment 420's state files. It imports experiment 420's arms, gates, training loop, and forecast helpers.
  • e00424_score.py scores S1 to S3, the minimum detectable effect, the lead bands, and the descriptive tables, importing experiment 420's scoring functions.

docs.title: Departures
docs.text:
• Level 1.0 and the shuffled-sky arm are not run. Experiment 420 already showed the shuffled sky is far worse than A on recorded weather, and the serving question needs the main setting only.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost is not computed, for the reason experiment 420 gives: the injected series have no node and generator tables. The q01 coverage and pinball loss on reverse-flow rows stand in.
  • Seed asymmetry. A has two seeds and P0 one, so A's mean over two seeds meets P0's single seed, which lowers A's noise without biasing the contrast. The minimum detectable effect comes from single seeds, so it is conservative for the two-seed mean.
  • No climatology row. The target is a signed series with an injected farm, for which no month-by-half-hour climatology forecaster exists in this repository; experiment 420 had none.
  • No multiplicity correction. S1 to S3 are conjunctive pass bars, each read at 95%; the decision rule needs all three, so the family-wise error of a joint pass is below the level of any one.
  • Figures. The write-up carries a day-ahead example and a 10-day example at D5 with a farm injected, from experiment 420's figure script adapted to these files, and q01, q05, q95, and q99 coverage and pinball loss on reverse-flow rows.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• The injected farm is real recorded output and the weather inputs are ENS, so the test is still a laboratory test of the sign question, although the weather side is now what a live service holds.
  • A wrong Primary-level gate decision makes a whole Primary's forecast wrong. The gate decisions are stored for every fit and reported.
  • ENS irradiance after lead 144 hours is a 6-hour mean, so the unit shape is blurred at days 6 to 10. Experiment 397's summaries do not treat the two stamp spacings differently, and this plan does not change that. The lead-band table, split at 144 hours, shows whether the gain falls there.
  • The scale constant u99 is fixed on one Primary's daylight rows over the whole record, so it also covers the test months. Both arms share the scalar, and it is accepted as negligible.
  • ENS forecast errors that differ by season, lead band, and hour band (experiment 111) may exceed what one retrained network with a lead input learns. The lead-band and month tables show it.
  • Unlogged load-shift events may sit in the readings, as NGED says its logs are incomplete.

docs.title: Minimum detectable effect, stage 1 (written before any arm-against-arm score)
docs.text: On rotation r1 the minimum detectable effect is 0.907 points of effective capacity. The null difference between A's two seeds (ENS inputs) on reverse-flow rows at level 2.0 has a mean of -0.024 (95% interval -0.725 to 0.549; 14 Primary-month blocks, 22,443 rows) and a bootstrap standard deviation of 0.324; 2.8 times 0.324 is 0.907. The figure is above the 0.5-point limit, so contrasts of that size or smaller (A against A-applied, A on ENS against A on laboratory inputs) are reported as underpowered. The figure does not weaken S1, because its floors (4 and 10 points) sit far above it. The figure is in work/mde_stage1.json, which the script refuses to overwrite.

docs.title: Minimum detectable effect, full run (written before the full scoring)
docs.text: Over all three rotations the minimum detectable effect is 1.735 points of effective capacity. All 105 fits and 42 forecast-only runs finished. The null difference between A's two seeds on reverse-flow rows at level 2.0 has a mean of 2.09 (95% interval 0.88 to 3.29; 42 Primary-month blocks, 79,399 rows) and a bootstrap standard deviation of 0.620; 2.8 times 0.620 is 1.735. The two seeds of A therefore differ by a mean of 2.09 points on these rows, and contrasts under about 2 points are underpowered. The 10-point S1 floor is far above that noise. The figure is in work/mde_full.json.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: • The docstrings of experiments 412, 417, and 420 tell the reader to source an env.sh, which does not exist in this repository. PYTHONPATH and DATA_PATH_INTERNAL were assembled by hand; the header of e00424_fit.py lists them. Command that showed it: ls env.sh.

docs.title: Review log
docs.text:
Plan review (fresh Sonnet agent, before any fit). The review gave 12 findings. Accepted: a numeric S1 floor and an outcome for a gain between the minimum detectable effect and the floor; the label covers only the substations whose gate opened; S2 and S3 read on point estimates, with stage 1 testing S2 at D5 only; missing-ensemble rows kept and counted; the 9-hour delay, the archive switch on 2025-07-01, the u99 constant, and the 6-hour-mean limit stated; lead bands split at 144 hours; departures for the climatology row and multiplicity. Not changed: the draft-PR timing, because the brief asks for a draft plan PR.

Code review (fresh Sonnet agent, before any fit). No leakage and no crash on first use. One important finding, accepted and fixed: experiment 417's gate keeps each valid time's longest-lead row, which gave a gate shut at D8 and D12 with ensemble inputs; the gate now uses the shortest-lead row. Minor, accepted: the S1 code was stricter than the plan; the ensemble-minus-recorded interval was dropped; the ensemble clearness index is not a clear-sky index (stated). Not changed: the applied-only fold is rebuilt per job (efficiency only).

Results review (fresh Sonnet agent, from the stored forecasts). Every headline number was reproduced. One discrepancy, accepted: the A-applied contrast used A's seed 0 (6.54) while every other figure used A's two-seed mean (5.50); the page and the scoring script now use the two-seed mean. The Checks above come from this review.

Write-up numbers review (fresh Sonnet agent, against the stored scores). Accepted: four interval ends and one rounding corrected, the claim that the gain "does not fall" across lead bands replaced by the measured 0.8-point fall, "at least 5.7" scoped as a point estimate, the learned-coefficient ranges put on one basis (seed 0), a truncated sentence in the prediction repaired, and a statement that the prediction was met added.

Prose review (fresh Sonnet agent). Accepted: terms defined at first use (primary substation, points of effective capacity, CRPS, hidden, no-injection), the take-home rewritten to be self-contained and scoped, "costs accuracy" replaced, the seed-noise sentence corrected, the lead bands renamed to days 7 to 10, "feeder core" replaced, the results moved above the plan, the audit triggers described, first-person and process-history lines removed from the move section. Not changed: duplication between the headline, lessons, and advice (each must stand alone in the generated tables), the registered-form plan prose, and a split of the long registered sentences in the plan, which would alter the pre-registered wording.

docs.title: Does the pooled mixture density network that combines every component the earlier experiments supported beat its parts and the references?
docs.text:
Pretraining on past weather lowered the forecast error at the six signed-MW and eight MVA-only Primaries, and the Primary embedding mattered far more than pretraining. The continuous ranked probability score (CRPS; lower is better) fell by 0.050 points of effective capacity (the error as a percentage of each Primary substation's effective capacity) at the six Primaries whose meters report signed megawatts (the "signed-MW six") and by 0.124 at the eight Primaries whose meters report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA; the "MVA-only eight"). A third group, D15 and D18, holds the two Primaries with a short history. Removing the Primary embedding raised the CRPS by about 0.85 at both the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight. The MVA-only eight cleared the registered bar, which is the -0.03 threshold written in the plan before any score was read. The interval for the signed-MW six ended at -0.021, short of that bar. The assembled network scored lower CRPS than the monthly XGBoost recipe (S0M) and than BG2 (the production-style blend of XGBoost, analogue, and pooled-by-type models) at the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight, and higher than BG2 at D15 and D18. The verdict is partly supported: the hypothesis that pretraining lowers the CRPS and that removing the Primary embedding or the widening makes it worse held for pretraining at the MVA-only eight, probably held at the signed-MW six, and held for the embedding. Widening did not lower the CRPS. Pretraining is a candidate for a numbered release of the production forecast.

The question was whether combining every component that earlier experiments supported in one pooled neural network beats leaving one out, and beats the reference forecasts. The network predicts 11 quantiles of Primary substation demand for the next 14 days from the weather ensemble (ECMWF ENS, the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts ensemble). The components are one neural network shared by all Primaries with an 8-wide embedding per Primary, summaries of the ensemble's mean and spread, hand-made calendar columns, monthly refits, and a final widening of the bands by 1.15. The one component added here is pretraining, first tested in experiment 418. The mixture density network first learns from ERA5 (a reanalysis, an estimate of past weather) and CAMS (the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, which supplies estimates of past solar radiation), and then every weight is fine-tuned on ensemble rows.

Three networks were refitted at 12 monthly folds and compared with four references. The folds are forecast origins from 2025-07 to 2026-06, each network trained only on data before its month, with five random seeds each. The references were scored on the half-hours that all arms forecast. The three networks are R, trained on ensemble rows only; A, pretrained then fine-tuned; and A-noemb, the same as A without the Primary embedding. The references are the monthly XGBoost recipe (S0M), BG2 (a blend of XGBoost, analogue, and pooled-by-type models), manual_heuristic, and climatology. Scores are the CRPS at days 1 to 10, in points of effective capacity, averaged over the Primaries of each group with equal weight. The signed-MW six are the Primary substations whose meters record the direction of flow. The MVA-only eight are the Primary substations whose meters record apparent power without a sign. D15 and D18 are the two Primaries with a short history, reported separately.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• R (reference network). Pooled plain neural network with the Primary embedding, trained on ensemble rows only, widened by 1.15.
  • A (assembly). R after pretraining on ERA5-and-CAMS rows, with every weight fine-tuned on ensemble rows at a learning rate of 2e-4, widened by 1.15. A_raw is the same forecast without the widening.
  • A-noemb. A built on experiment 406's neural network with no Primary embedding, in both the pretraining and the fine-tuning stage.
  • S0M. The monthly XGBoost recipe, arm S0M of experiment 389, read through experiment 397's references and scored both raw and widened by 1.15.
  • BG2. The blend of XGBoost, analogue, and pooled-by-type models of experiment 87.
  • manual_heuristic and climatology. The two naive forecasts from the project's evaluation code.

Every neural network was refitted with the D15 and D18 start cut and the flagged exact-zero drop. Seeds are 0 to 4 for every fitted arm.

docs.title: Absolute scores
docs.text:
A has the lowest CRPS of the seven at the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight, and BG2 has the lowest at D15 and D18. The table gives the CRPS at days 1 to 10 with the widening of 1.15. All arms and references share 2,922,247 half-hours over leads of 0.5 to 336 hours. The days 1 to 10 subset of those half-hours holds 826,396 at the signed-MW six, 1,103,553 at the MVA-only eight, and 169,766 at D15 and D18, and the table scores that subset.

Arm Signed-MW six MVA-only eight D15 and D18 R 2.878 3.719 8.373 A 2.828 3.594 7.970 A-noemb 3.680 4.431 11.413 S0M (widened) 3.115 3.826 8.291 BG2 3.016 3.774 7.457 manual_heuristic 3.605 4.429 11.112 climatology 3.831 4.866 23.951

The unwidened S0M scores 3.111, 3.818, and 8.309. Figure 2 gives the CRPS per Primary.

docs.title: Minimum detectable effect
docs.text: The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is 0.0368 points, a lower bound. The MDE is the standard deviation over the 12 folds of the difference in signed-MW six CRPS between the mean of R seeds 0 to 2 and the mean of R seeds 3 and 4 (0.0520), divided by the square root of two. A contrast smaller than 0.0368 is inside the noise. Experiment 423 uses twice the standard deviation divided by the square root of two, which would be about 0.074 here (experiment 419 uses twice the standard deviation, 0.0738). The reading that C1 at the signed-MW six (-0.050) is larger than the MDE depends on the lower-bound definition used here. Under experiment 423's convention, C1 at the signed-MW six would be inside the noise.

docs.title: Contrasts
docs.text:
Pretraining lowered the CRPS at the signed-MW six, the MVA-only eight, and D15 and D18, the Primary embedding is worth far more, and the assembly beat the monthly XGBoost recipe. The table gives treatment minus reference, at days 1 to 10, with the month-block bootstrap interval (20,000 resamples, level 98.75%, a Bonferroni correction over four contrasts). D15 and D18 are report-only. C3 is the unwidened forecast minus the widened forecast, so a positive C3 means that widening lowered the CRPS.

Contrast Signed-MW six MVA-only eight D15 and D18 (report-only) C1: A minus R -0.050 (-0.078 to -0.021) -0.124 (-0.219 to -0.048) -0.368 (-0.567 to -0.004) C2: A-noemb minus A +0.851 (+0.723 to +0.999) +0.837 (+0.731 to +0.944) +3.272 (+1.191 to +5.527) C3: A_raw minus A +0.004 (-0.009 to +0.025) -0.011 (-0.016 to -0.006) -0.003 (-0.074 to +0.097) C4: A minus S0M (both widened) -0.287 (-0.402 to -0.171) -0.232 (-0.376 to -0.115) -0.326 (-0.724 to +0.047)
  • C1 is negative in 11 of 12 folds at both the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight. The per-fold differences at the signed-MW six run from -0.102 to +0.018. At the MVA-only eight they run from -0.409 to +0.011.
  • C2 is positive in all 12 folds at both the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight. The smallest per-fold difference is +0.571 at the signed-MW six and +0.557 at the MVA-only eight.
  • The contrasts are pooled over half-hours. The intervals resample months and do not include the variation between seeds.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held. A beat R by 0.050 at the signed-MW six (predicted 0.03 to 0.10) and by 0.124 at the MVA-only eight (predicted 0.08 to 0.20).
  • P2 held. A-noemb was worse than A by +0.851 at the signed-MW six and +0.837 at the MVA-only eight, within the predicted 0.5 to 1.0 points.
  • P3 held at the signed-MW six and failed at the MVA-only eight. Widening the bands by 1.15 was predicted to lower the CRPS by less than 0.03 points and to move q95 coverage (the share of actual values below the 95th-percentile forecast) towards 0.95. At the signed-MW six, widening changed the CRPS by -0.004, inside the noise, and moved q95 coverage from 0.905 to 0.935. At the MVA-only eight, widening changed the CRPS by +0.011, which contradicts the predicted direction. The size is small, about a third of the 0.03 bound. The q95 coverage moved from 0.941 to 0.963, past 0.95.
  • P4 held. A scored lower than S0M by 0.287 at the signed-MW six and 0.232 at the MVA-only eight, both intervals wholly below zero.

docs.title: Tails
docs.text:
Widening by 1.15 moves q95 and q99 coverage towards nominal at the signed-MW six and at D15 and D18, and overshoots at the MVA-only eight. It also pushes q01 and q05 coverage further under nominal. A has lower pinball loss than R at the same widening at all three groups. The tables give coverage (nominal 0.95 and 0.99) and pinball loss at q95 and q99, days 1 to 10, mean over the Primaries of each group. The q01 and q05 coverage of A_raw at the signed-MW six is 0.009 and 0.038, and of A is 0.005 and 0.023, so the widening pushes the lower tail further under its nominal level. The q95 and q99 coverage of A is closer to nominal than that of R at the signed-MW six and at D15 and D18, but not at the MVA-only eight. There A has 0.963 and 0.994 against 0.959 and 0.992 for R, both above nominal.

Signed-MW six (826,396 half-hours):

Arm Cov q95 Cov q99 Pin q95 Pin q99 A_raw 0.905 0.970 0.809 0.279 A 0.935 0.981 0.779 0.260 R_raw 0.903 0.967 0.822 0.290 R 0.933 0.979 0.795 0.269 S0M_raw 0.909 0.980 0.948 0.386 S0M 0.932 0.986 0.928 0.392

MVA-only eight (1,103,553 half-hours):

Arm Cov q95 Cov q99 Pin q95 Pin q99 A_raw 0.941 0.988 0.911 0.243 A 0.963 0.994 0.932 0.253 R_raw 0.936 0.984 0.946 0.256 R 0.959 0.992 0.961 0.258 S0M_raw 0.934 0.991 0.977 0.332 S0M 0.955 0.995 0.987 0.358

D15 and D18 (169,766 half-hours):

Arm Cov q95 Cov q99 Pin q95 Pin q99 A_raw 0.904 0.976 2.231 0.868 A 0.938 0.984 2.126 0.808 R_raw 0.877 0.963 2.630 0.987 R 0.913 0.977 2.427 0.862 S0M_raw 0.866 0.986 2.768 0.717 S0M 0.896 0.990 2.535 0.689

  • On sunny low-demand half-hours the bands are too wide. The q95 coverage of A is 0.995 at the signed-MW six (35,283 half-hours) and 0.987 at the MVA-only eight (46,541 half-hours).

docs.title: Cold winter nights, sunny half-hours, and Economy 7
docs.text:
A has lower CRPS than R in all three slices at all three groups. The table gives the CRPS at days 1 to 10 with the widening of 1.15 for A, R, S0M, BG2, and manual_heuristic. Cold nights are the half-hours the evaluation code flags as cold nights, sunny half-hours are those it flags as sunny, and the Economy 7 step is the overnight cheap-rate tariff switch.

Slice and group A R S0M BG2 manual_heuristic Cold nights, signed-MW six 4.290 4.446 4.953 4.714 6.177 Cold nights, MVA-only eight 3.213 3.315 3.756 3.662 5.022 Cold nights, D15 and D18 5.850 5.934 7.226 5.936 9.291 Sunny half-hours, signed-MW six 3.814 3.831 4.183 4.157 4.824 Sunny half-hours, MVA-only eight 4.979 5.155 5.198 5.158 6.167 Sunny half-hours, D15 and D18 8.966 9.410 9.492 8.611 12.235 Economy 7 step, signed-MW six 2.056 2.115 2.171 2.098 2.552 Economy 7 step, MVA-only eight 2.552 2.622 2.637 2.666 3.036 Economy 7 step, D15 and D18 7.404 7.965 7.654 6.780 10.184

docs.title: Avoidable curtailment cost
docs.text:
At the headline limit, A has the lowest avoidable curtailment cost of the arms with a printed total, about 37% below manual_heuristic. The cost is defined only for the signed-MW six. The definition below comes from the scorer's code. The cost is the cost of a forecast minus the cost of a perfect forecast on the same half-hours, at leads of 12 to 36 hours, scored for each Primary substation separately at a price of £2000 per MWh for curtailed energy. The limit is a fraction of each Primary's maximum flow in the 12 or more months before the scored period. The printed totals below are for the six Primaries together, in millions of pounds over the 12 folds.

Limit as a fraction of earlier maximum A A_raw R_raw S0M BG2 manual_heuristic climatology 0.5 (headline) 66.5 70.8 75.4 84.6 72.9 104.9 112.5 0.75 22.1 25.3 27.7 32.0 24.3 37.4 41.7 0.9 7.62 8.39 9.59 10.2 7.31 10.4 11.1
  • The ranking changes with the limit. At 0.9 BG2 (7.31) is below A (7.62), and A-noemb is lower still (6.37 widened), despite its CRPS being 0.85 worse.
  • The cost of R widened is not shown in the truncated printout, which shows R_raw only.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Independent re-derivation (a fresh Sonnet reviewer, own code). CRPS of R, A, and A-noemb, C1, and C2 reproduce the printed values to three decimals, with seeds paired in all 12 folds and no scored valid time after 2026-06-30.
  • The median-forecast error agrees with the CRPS in sign. This check, the next, and the leave-one-out check come from the results reviewer's own code and are not in the printed report. C1 on the median's absolute error is -0.007 MW at the signed-MW six and -0.020 MW at the MVA-only eight, and C2 is +0.107 MW at both. The stored forecasts hold quantiles only, so the median stands in for the mean forecast.
  • Median minus the mean of the 11 quantiles is small and negative at every Primary of the signed-MW six (-0.014 to -0.091 MW for A), so the spread does not shift the forecast. The largest values for A are at D8 (-0.140 MW) and D12 (-0.166 MW), which are outside the signed-MW six.
  • Leaving one Primary out keeps C1 negative. At the signed-MW six the contrast stays between -0.043 and -0.065 (D10 out: -0.059; D5 out: -0.065), and at the MVA-only eight between -0.113 and -0.141. The gain at the signed-MW six rests on five Primaries: D5 alone is worse with pretraining (+0.023) and D10 is nearly flat (-0.007).
  • Audit triggers. C2's interval does not reach zero, so that trigger did not fire. C3 reverses sign at the MVA-only eight, so that trigger fired there: the page does not claim that the widening lowers the CRPS. No other audit trigger fired.
  • The 11 of 12 negative folds in C1 are not a second test, because the folds make up the bootstrap's resampling units.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• S0M has no D15 and D18 cut and no flagged-zero drop, and comes from experiment 389. Its gap to A is partly a difference in training rows.
  • Flagged zeros among the origin lags still reach the neural network at inference, as in experiment 407. The scoring dropped 1,179 actuals that were flagged exact zeros.
  • The contrast intervals pool half-hours, and the tables average over Primaries, so a table difference and a contrast can differ slightly.
  • The 12 monthly folds (2025-07 to 2026-06) refit every month. The intervals are therefore not interim, but the monthly schedule is not the weekly schedule of production.
  • The lead range of 0.5 to 336 hours covers the 1 to 10 days that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) needs.
  • Training rows dropped per fold. Every fold drops 68,680 fine-tuning rows and 22,769 pretraining rows for a short history at the start. The flagged exact zeros dropped rise from 808 (2025-07) to 2,929 (2026-04) for fine-tuning and from 257 to 1,087 for pretraining.
  • The cut cross-check was not run. No fit without the D15 and D18 cut exists, so the effect of the cut is not sized, and experiment 418's numbers are a guide only.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Candidates to join A are those that beat R on the same 12 folds.
  • Origin-hour training is a candidate robustness variant and was not run. See experiment 422.
  • The export gate of experiment 420 was not tested here. That gate controls whether a signed output is exported at MVA-only Primaries.

docs.title: Data used and where it lives
docs.text:
• Data. The cleaned NGED Primary-substation power series, ECMWF ensemble forecasts for the fine-tuning and the scoring, and ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather for the pretraining.
  • Schedule. Monthly refits at 12 folds (2025-07 to 2026-06).
  • Code. ml-experiments/00425-best-mdn-architecture-assembly-with-ablations/ in this repository.
  • Saved networks. The experiment's data folder, work/models/ (fine-tuned networks) and work/pretrained/ (pretrained networks), under $DATA_PATH_INTERNAL/ml-experiments/00425-best-mdn-architecture-assembly-with-ablations/.

docs.title: Is a graph network over the Primaries, a bulk supply point forecast built from the Primaries beneath it, or neighbour-based outlier spotting worth a fit, compared with simple neighbour statistics? (design note)
docs.text:
Take-home message: in these tests, the recent forecast errors of a Primary's interconnected neighbours predicted none of its day-ahead forecast error. A graph network over the Primaries therefore has no lagged-error signal to pass along, and none was fitted. A scaled sum of the forecasts of the Primaries beneath a bulk supply point also scored worse than a network that sees the node's own readings.

We asked whether three ideas for using neighbouring substations are worth a neural-network fit. The ideas are a graph network over the 16 Primaries, a forecast for a bulk supply point (BSP) built from the Primaries beneath it, and spotting outliers and load-shift events by comparing neighbours. A Primary is a primary substation of the distribution network, and a neighbour is a Primary that NGED's interconnection file joins to it (25 pairs among the 16 Primaries). The first stage fitted no network. It took the stored day-ahead forecasts of the pooled neural network of experiment 397 and asked whether a neighbour's recent forecast error predicts a Primary's own error. It did not. The second stage would have fitted a graph network at 75 fits, and it did not run, so the verdict is not supported. Experiment 404 (plan in draft PR 58) has the arms that test neighbour inputs inside load-shift events (idea 3).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS is not used here, because stage 0 fits no network. The residual is the actual minus the median forecast, divided by the Primary's effective capacity. The signed-MW six are the Primaries D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, whose meters record the sign of the flow. The MVA-only eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22) record only its magnitude, and D15 and D18 are report-only. D13 and D17 are bulk supply points, and D1 and D6 are grid supply points. Stage 0a and 0b use the five test months of experiment 397 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), and 0c uses the four months for which the node network of experiment 415 stored forecasts (2025-12 is absent there). Intervals resample the test months (2,000 draws), so they are coarse. "Reduction" below is the percentage fall in held-out squared error, so a negative reduction is a rise in error.

  • Gate 0a (lagged correlation, signed-MW six, lead 12 to 36 hours). The gate required the interconnected graph's mean correlation to exceed random graphs' by 0.10 and shortest-edge random graphs' by 0.05, in 3 of 5 months. The graph's mean correlation, over the newest reading before the origin and the same time yesterday, is 0.001, -0.002, -0.078, 0.036, and -0.001 in the five months. Random graphs with the same degrees give -0.016, 0.008, -0.016, 0.055, and -0.001. The excess over random graphs is +0.017, -0.010, -0.062, -0.018, and 0.000, so 0 of 5 months pass. At leads 120 to 240 hours the excess lies between -0.031 and +0.011. At the MVA-only eight the graph's means (0.008 to 0.045) are within 0.06 of random graphs' (not gated).
  • Gate 0b (ridge on neighbour lags, signed-MW six). The gate required a reduction of at least 2% against own lags only and at least 1% against each control, on all rows and outside labelled events. On all rows the reduction is 0.01% (-3.05 to +2.61) against own lags only, 1.28% (-0.68 to +3.67) against random neighbours, and 1.46% (-0.75 to +3.79) against shortest-edge random neighbours. Outside labelled events the three reductions are -3.06% (-4.40 to -1.91), -0.87% (-1.75 to +0.41), and -0.69% (-1.61 to +0.65), so the neighbour features raise the error on ordinary rows. The gate failed. At the MVA-only eight the all-rows reductions are -0.33% (-1.15 to +0.57) against own lags, +0.38% (+0.08 to +0.71) against random neighbours, and +0.43% (+0.12 to +0.77) against shortest-edge neighbours; the last two are positive but below the 1% gate. Outside events the eight's three reductions are -0.39%, -0.09%, and -0.06%. D15 and D18 are within 0.3% of zero.
  • 0c (bottom-up bulk supply point, median only). The modelled Primaries beneath D13 and D17 sum to 128% and 171% of the node's mean demand (the node's net flow includes embedded generation, which this experiment did not test), with a half-hourly correlation of 0.73 and 0.71. At D6 the sum is 20% of the node's mean and the correlation is 0.18, and at D1 the sum is 11 times the node's mean and the correlation is -0.23. The 27% and 35% in the registered prediction came from a preliminary look that scaled the cleaned readings by capacity twice, and its rationale was wrong; the 0.7 correlation was right. The mean absolute error of the median (points of node capacity, average of 4 months) is 8.32 (D13), 12.45 (D17), 27.03 (D1), and 25.43 (D6) for the network of experiment 415; 9.02, 13.30, 27.80, and 25.56 for the monthly XGBoost control; 13.35, 18.33, 38.47, and 31.54 for the bottom-up median; and 11.39, 16.64, 35.08, and 29.42 for the bottom-up median plus the node's own three lags. The bottom-up medians are worse than the network in every month at D13, D17, and D1, and in 3 of 4 months at D6. They beat the XGBoost control in 2 of the 16 node-months (D13 and D17 in 2026-01).
  • Idea 3. The label table names one Primary in 31 of its 112 rows, so a neighbour comparison cannot see the other 81 events directly. This experiment did not measure whether neighbours help inside load-shift events. On ordinary rows the neighbour regression found no gain.
  • Predictions. P1 held: the interconnected graph's excess over random graphs was under 0.10 (and under 0.05 against shortest-edge graphs) at lead 12 to 36 hours. P2's first clause held: the reduction against own lags (0.01%) was under 2%. P2's second clause failed on all rows (1.28% and 1.46% against the two controls, above 1%) and held outside events (a loss). P3 held in its first clause (the first bottom-up variant was 60% and 47% above N1 at D13 and D17) and failed in its second: the variant with the node's own lags was 37% and 34% above N1, not within 10%. P4 was not tested.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not computed, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Mean-forecast error. Not applicable: stage 0 scores the median residual and its squared error.
  • Triggers fired. One: the second clause of P3 failed. A likely reason is that the variant was fitted on the children's actual sums and applied to their forecast sums, which makes the child term look more reliable than it is. The reason was not tested. No other trigger fired, and no audit was run.
  • Cleaned data. Forecast rows with no cleaned actual, per fold (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06): 1,520, 719, 0, 248, and 1,349 of about 348,000, of which 1,520, 629, 0, 28, and 264 are D15 and D18 rows before 2025-03-01 or other missing readings. Target rows (lead 12 to 36 hours) lacking one of the two own lag residuals, because the lag falls in a month with no stored forecast: 1,337, 1,314, 496, 1,267, and 1,304 of about 23,700.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Design. Lagged residuals come from the stored forecast with the shortest lead (under 24 hours) for the lag time. Controls are 1,000 degree-preserving random graphs (swap chain, 10 discarded draws, 100 swap attempts between draws) and 1,000 shortest-edge random graphs, chosen from 20,000 draws as the closest in mean edge length. The shortest-edge graphs still have edges up to 1.77 times as long as the interconnected graph's (random graphs: 2.05 times), so the distance control is only partial. Gate 0b used 30 evenly spaced draws of each control and a ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-month-out inside the four training months. The ridge is fitted on four test months and scored on the fifth, so it may use later months to predict an earlier one. Event rows are excluded when the target or a lag time falls inside a labelled event that names the Primary.
  • 0c fitting. The scale, offset, and ridge of the bottom-up variants are fitted on actual readings before the scored month, because no earlier child forecasts exist.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00426-*/e00426_stage0.py and e00426_figures.py. Tables are in this experiment's private data folder, stage0/. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the run and found three blockers (a unit mismatch, an integer-type mismatch in a join, and an unmixed graph sampler), all fixed before the run.
  • Not covered. No network was fitted, so there are no CRPS, tail, curtailment, or example forecast results. Only lagged residuals of one median forecast, a linear ridge, five test months, and the 16 Primaries were tested, so neighbour inputs of other kinds and nonlinear models remain untested.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Read experiment 404's B1 minus B1-nn and B1 minus B1-rw if its batch 2 runs: they test neighbour information inside injected load-shift events, the one place the signal appeared.
  • A regional weather-error input (not a graph) is the other way a neighbour's recent error could help, and stage 0a gives it no support at the day-ahead lead.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Does a whole-day sign labeller, with separate MW and MVA input channels, improve the export-gated neural network's signed forecast at Primaries where the meter hides the sign?
docs.text:
Take-home: a small neural network that reads one whole day of meter readings and marks each half-hour as reverse flow (power exported up the electricity network) or not ranked those half-hours about as well as the forecast network of experiment 420 (arm A), but no better. It also wrongly marked 61.7% of the sunny midday half-hours at Primary substation D5 as reverse flow when no solar farm had been added, so the forecast-network stage did not run. The result is not supported. The same labeller marked 0% at D9, D11, D14, and D16. Its recall (the share of true reverse-flow half-hours it finds) at a 5% false-reverse rate was 0.22 pooled and 0.52 averaged over Primary-months, against a bar of 0.60 and arm A's 0.21 and 0.46. D5 and D10 have a mean sunny-midday reading of 12 to 16 points of capacity (a point is 1% of the Primary's capacity), against 38 to 53 at the four Primaries the labeller trained on. The difference in demand level is the likely cause; a labeller retrained on a wider mix has not tested it.

This experiment asks whether the export-gated neural network of experiment 420 can be improved where it is weakest. Eight Primary substations report only the size of the power that flows, not its direction (signed power is positive for demand and negative for reverse flow). Experiment 420 hid the direction at six Primaries where it is known, added a real solar farm's recorded output to some of them, and found that a neural network with a Primary-level export gate (arm A) forecast reverse-flow half-hours much better than the same neural network with the gate shut. Arm A has three weaknesses: it finds only 52.4% of reverse-flow half-hours when the injected farm is the size of the Primary's typical sunny midday reading (level 1.0), its lower tail is too narrow (the 1% quantile covers 6.2% of reverse-flow rows), and it calls reverse flow on 66.8% of non-reverse sunny summer middays.
