This experiment tested one of two planned ideas, a labeller that reads a whole day of readings and gives each half-hour a probability of reverse flow. The second idea, separate input channels for measured MW and for MVA, was not tested.

Terms used below. Level 1.0 and level 2.0 are the size of the injected farm as multiples of the Primary's typical sunny midday reading. Sunny slice is the half-hours where CAMS solar output is at least 0.3 of its 99th percentile and the clear-sky index is at least 0.7. Pooled means all rows together, and macro-averaged means the mean over Primary-months. Hidden pair is the two signed Primaries whose sign is hidden in a rotation (r1: D5 and D10). L1 and L2 are the two step 0 gate bars. pi is the labeller's probability of reverse flow.

docs.title: Earlier experiments that motivated this one
docs.text:
• The 0.70 area belongs to the hand-made day-flip diagnostic, not to arm A. That diagnostic scored 0.702 in step 0 of experiment 420 and 0.73 in experiment 417. Arm A's own row-level ranking area is 0.930 on the sunny slice at level 2.0. The step 0 bar (an area of 0.85 and a recall of 0.60 at a 5% false-reverse rate) was therefore set against arm A's level-2.0 figures, 0.930 and 0.623, and the result below compares both at level 1.0.
  • Experiment 424 found that arm A survives ensemble weather (a gain of 15.7 points over the gate-shut neural network, against 19.2 in the laboratory test). This experiment kept recorded CAMS and ERA5 inputs, so that every contrast is against experiment 420's stored arm A. No ensemble-weather test was run.
  • Experiment 422 found that training at several origin hours removes most of the loss from late readings. Only the labeller trained on days cut at a random hour, so it can read a day that ends at the newest usable observation.
  • Experiment 417 counted eight earlier treatments of the hidden-sign problem that failed. Its hand-built zero-crossing labeller scored 0.96 on injected against placebo days at level 2.0 and 0.58 at level 1.0, and its hard labels did not lift the fits. The bar here was a probability on every gate-open row, not hard labels.

docs.title: Design as registered (only step 0 was run)
docs.text:
• Step 0: the labeller (105 fits, no mixture density network). One labeller per rotation, test month, and left-out visible Primary: five per rotation and month (one trained on the four visible Primaries, four each leaving one visible Primary out). It reads 48 half-hours of a UTC day: the reading r, y' = sqrt(max(r^2 - 4, 0)), CAMS u and k, ERA5 temperature, a demand reference (median reading by half-hour over overcast days of the same 28-day block and day type), the day type, and a mask. It outputs the logit of P' < 0 and an estimate of P'. The architecture is a width-5 convolution feeding a two-layer bidirectional GRU of 32 units, or a dilated convolution stack of the same width. A pilot on the left-out visible Primaries (rotation r1, test months 2025-09 and 2026-06, level 1.0) picked the one with the higher pooled area.
  • Training copies. Each visible Primary-day is copied with a solar farm injected at power factor 1, at a level drawn from 0 to 2.5 (15% of copies at 0, the placebo days), with Q drawn from 0, 2, and 4 points, capped at 70% of the farm's peak on 30% of copies, and cut at a random hour on 50% of copies. Loss: cross-entropy on the sign (weight 0.25 where |P'| < 2) plus a Huber loss on P'. Every eighth block of seven days is held out for early stopping.
  • No leakage from the hidden pair. Each rotation injects only the farms that its hidden pair does not use (r1: farms B and D; r2: farms A, C, and D; r3: farms B and D). A leave-one-out labeller also drops the left-out Primary's own farm. The hidden pair's signed truth is used only to score. Farms in one region share a sky, so the exclusion protects less than it appears to.
  • Step 0 gate. L1: at level 1.0 on the sunny slice of the hidden pair's test-month rows, the area is at least 0.85 and no more than 0.05 below arm A's on the identical rows, the recall at a 5% false-reverse rate is at least 0.60 and no more than 0.05 below arm A's, and the expected calibration error is at most 0.10. L2: with no injection, pi > 0.5 on at most 2% of sunny-midday half-hours at each of D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16. Counts are rows, pooled over rotations and months, with the Primary-month macro-average beside each.
  • Network stage (planned, not run). The arms were arm A and the plain network (P0, stored), two refits of A, T (A with two channels and a measured flag), TD (T with pseudo-Primaries and MW masking), L (A with the labeller's soft labels and probabilities), TDL (all three ideas), and TDL-perm (TDL with pi permuted across days). The registered rule runs L, TDL, and TDL-perm only if both gate bars hold.

docs.title: Pilot choice, written before the 105 labellers ran
docs.text: On the left-out visible Primaries of rotation r1 (test months 2025-09 and 2026-06, level 1.0, 8 labellers per architecture), the GRU labeller scored an area of 0.945 and a recall of 0.633 at a 5% false-reverse rate; the dilated convolution scored 0.937 and 0.576. The GRU fit takes about 4 seconds, so the GRU is the architecture for the 105 labellers. Both ran all 25 epochs without early stopping, so the labellers may be under-trained; the epoch count was not changed after the pilot.

docs.title: Step 0 result: the gate failed
docs.text:
All 105 GRU labellers ran (about 4 seconds each). Rows are counted, not unique half-hours. Areas and recalls are on the sunny slice of the hidden pair's test-month rows at level 1.0, with arm A scored on the identical rows. No interval is given: step 0 pools 21 labellers, and the macro-average over Primary-months is the spread measure.

Measure Labeller, pooled Arm A, pooled Labeller, macro Arm A, macro Area 0.887 0.880 0.897 0.880 Recall at 5% false reverse 0.223 0.211 0.517 0.457 Expected calibration error 0.072 0.050 0.108 0.095
  • L1 fails on recall. The area (0.887) passes its bar and is no worse than arm A's. The recall at 5% false reverse is 0.223 pooled and 0.517 macro-averaged, both under the 0.60 bar. The pooled figure is low because pooling Primaries with different base rates sets one threshold for all.
  • L2 fails at D5. With nothing injected, pi > 0.5 falls on 64.1% of D5's sunny-midday rows (61.7% of its unique half-hours; the rows repeat each half-hour once per forecast run), and on 0% at D9, D11, D14, and D16 (arm A: 0% at all five). The labeller, trained on D9, D11, D14, and D16, invents reverse flow at D5.
  • Day-level area: 0.903 for injected against placebo days at level 1.0 (325 and 1,001 days), against 0.702 for the hand-made day-flip diagnostic and 0.58 for the zero-crossing labeller of experiment 417. The labeller reads a whole day better than the hand-made diagnostics, but ranks rows no better than arm A.
  • Decision (registered rule): the networks that use the labeller (L, TDL, TDL-perm) did not run. The manager of the experiment queue also decided not to run T, TD, and the two refits of A (128 fits).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: not applicable; step 0 fitted no forecast.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile score: not applicable, for the same reason.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 1 (a placebo control fails: D5 at no injection) and trigger 2 (the result contradicts the prediction that L1 and L2 would pass). An independent audit re-derived every table figure from the stored tables (within 0.005). It found no leakage and no join or window artefact: D5 has no real reverse flow, and its rate is 63.0% in the training window and 61.7% in the test window. Without D5 the pooled recall is 0.656, so D5 causes both failures, but D5 is a hidden test Primary and L2 needs all five.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Train the sign labeller on a mix of Primaries that spans the demand levels of the hidden ones, and test that against arm A first on D5 and D10 with nothing injected. If that also fails, keep arm A as the candidate and run its ensemble-weather test with the laboratory-trained network applied to ensemble inputs beside the retrained one.

docs.title: Can a small convolutional network over whole days of recent power, read by attention, replace the hand-made lagged power inputs and stop the forecast following load-shift events?
docs.text:
Take-home message: reading whole days of raw power did not stop the forecast following load-shift events, but giving the lagged inputs a "surprise" lowered the error on clean and real event rows (and by less on injected harm rows), and that change is the one to carry forward.

A load-shift event moves demand between neighbouring Primary substations for hours or weeks, so the power an hour, a day, or a week ago can be abnormal. A forecast that copies the abnormal power goes wrong. This experiment asked whether a small neural network that reads the raw half-hourly power of whole recent days could learn how far to trust it, in place of the three hand-made lagged readings that today's mixture density network takes. The network could not.

How to read the numbers. Every number is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in percentage points of effective capacity at days 1 to 10 (smaller is better), pooled over four test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), three seeds, and the six Primary substations whose power is metered in signed megawatts, and all are interim. R-inj (the plain neural network with the three lags, trained on clean and injected power) is the reference; it scores 2.947 on clean rows and 2.956 on injected harm rows. A "harm row" is a row whose target is outside every event but whose recent power is inside one. "Injected" rows come from synthetic events added to clean power. "Real event rows" have a target inside an event that NGED (the distribution network operator) logged, and "real harm rows" are harm rows built from logged events. The minimum detectable effect (1.6 times the seed-to-seed standard deviation) is 0.077 on clean rows and 0.071 on injected harm rows.

The day-window network (E3) is worse than the lagged network on every row set. E3 minus R-inj is +0.050 (+0.034 to +0.066) on clean rows (2.997 against 2.947) and +0.042 (+0.029 to +0.056) on injected harm rows (2.998 against 2.956). The experiment predicted E3 minus R-inj of -0.30 to -0.10 on injected harm rows, so the hypothesis is not supported.

No arm followed a smaller share of a step in the recent power, and no arm widened its bands. In the encroachment sweep, a step of 5% of capacity is added to the recent power and the forecast is read 24 to 72 hours ahead. The index k counts how many lagged readings (or, for E3, how many days) carry the step. R-inj and E3 both followed a median 0.125 of the step at k = 3 (the share is read to the nearest 0.05), and every arm's 5%-95% band was 1.00 to 1.01 times as wide after the step as before. E3-surp (E3 plus the surprise channel) followed more, 0.225.

Two attempts to make the bands widen after a step did not work. A path that could only widen the bands (E3-surp-w) learned nothing under the clean-target objective (band ratio 1.019 against 1.018 for E3-surp). A diagnostic arm trained on the injected value did widen after a step (1.069). It also widened every band, so its 95% quantile covered 0.957 of clean readings and its clean CRPS rose by 0.055. The diagnostic arm is not a release candidate.

The one result worth carrying forward is the surprise at the lags (S1). The surprise of a power reading is its difference from the median of the lagless forecast (a forecast that uses no lagged power) for the same half-hour, from experiment 404's cross-fitted table, divided by half the width of that forecast's 5%-95% band. S1 is R-inj plus the surprise at each of its three lags. S1 minus R-inj is -0.083 (-0.096 to -0.070) on clean rows (2.865 against 2.947), -0.060 (-0.076 to -0.044) on injected harm rows (2.897 against 2.956), -0.170 (-0.267 to -0.059) on real event rows (5.687 against 5.857), and -0.007 (-0.035 to +0.024) on real harm rows. The clean gain is only just above the minimum detectable effect of 0.077, and the injected-harm gain (0.060) is below its minimum detectable effect (0.071), so neither result is more than interim.

S1 follows more of a step than R-inj does, which is the trade-off for its clean-row gain. S1's sweep moves the newest and the daily lag together and never the weekly lag, so the like-for-like comparison is R-inj at k = 2. There the mean share followed is 0.141 for S1 and 0.055 for R-inj. The quantile coverage and tail pinball loss of S1 match those of R-inj (the clean 95% quantile covers 0.915 against 0.914).

E3-surp, the same lagless table entering the encoder as a channel, ties R-inj on clean rows and loses on real event rows. E3-surp minus R-inj is -0.011 (-0.033 to +0.010) on clean rows and -0.023 (-0.039 to -0.006) on injected harm rows, and +0.260 (+0.178 to +0.340) on real event rows (6.118 against 5.857). S1 and E3-surp are the headline pair of this experiment: the same surprise, entering as three lagged scalars or as a channel of three day windows.

Smoothing the surprise over 14 days (H-smooth) did not beat S1. H-smooth minus S1 is +0.062 (+0.044 to +0.082) on clean rows and +0.066 (+0.046 to +0.088) on injected harm rows. H-smooth minus R-inj is -0.020 (-0.033 to -0.008) on clean rows, so H-smooth is no better than S1 and is not worth carrying forward.

The experiments with a 14-day convolutional encoder were stopped. On the 2026-01 fold the validation negative log-likelihood of H14-s (a convolutional encoder over 14 days with attention, no lags) was 0.5498 against 0.4777 for R-inj. Three diagnostic fits, each randomly hiding a share (0.1, 0.3, or 0.5) of the day positions, ended at 0.5347, 0.5399, and 0.5650. The pre-registered rule stopped the experiments. The page cannot tell whether the encoder memorised each Primary's history or trained too slowly.

Not done. The avoidable-curtailment cost is not computed, because the injected-world harm rows have no record of which neighbouring substations the shifted load went to. The absolute-skill references (the monthly XGBoost recipe, BG2 the best-guess forecast, manual_heuristic, and climatology) are not drawn. The real-event rows are few, and NGED may have events missing from its logs, so the real-event contrasts undercount.

docs.title: Plan, as registered before any fit
docs.text: The sections below are the plan and the dated design iterations, kept as written.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. The signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight are the two groups of Primary substations by metering (signed megawatt readings, or unsigned megavolt-ampere magnitudes); D15 and D18 are two short-history Primaries.

We test whether a network that reads whole days of raw power can learn how much to trust them. A load-shift event moves demand between neighbouring Primary substations for hours or weeks, so the power an hour, a day, or a week ago can be abnormal. Today's networks take three hand-made lagged readings. Experiment 392 found an XGBoost model follows about 1%, 15% to 20%, and 38% to 41% of a step added to the first one, two, and three lags, with no band widening. This experiment replaces the lags (and every window or surprise statistic built from them) with a small one-dimensional convolutional network over whole days, followed by attention. The idea is the maintainer's (2026-10-31). The attention design follows Bahdanau et al. (2015) (a query scores each position of a sequence) and the convolution follows Bai et al. (2018) (a stack of convolutions as a sequence encoder).

docs.title: Review against the latest evidence
docs.text:
The brief was checked against the pages merged since it was written (experiments 392, 397, 402, 403, 421, 422, 424 and 426, and the open plans of experiments 404, 425, and 427, read on 2026-10-31).

  • The reference is the pooled plain network. Experiment 425's plan names the ENS-only pooled plain network (R) as the reference; and this plan uses the same recipe.
  • Experiment 404's harness has not merged. Its injected-event generator is in the draft PR 58. This plan uses experiment 402's generator (e00402_inject.inject), which is merged and which 404's generator follows. The scripts of experiment 404 are not imported.
  • The sweep's k is defined for whole days (manager, 2026-10-31); see "Encroachment sweep".
  • Standing practices followed. Monthly refits; cleaned data with the flagged and start-cut half-hours dropped (experiment 422's cleaned_arrays), reported per fold; the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01; every network saved in the data folder; stored forecasts reused as references; tails and the avoidable-curtailment cost beside CRPS; example forecasts and event plots; draft PR.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Inputs. The network sees the same weather (ensemble mean and spread, once), solar, calendar, holiday, lead-time, and Primary-embedding inputs as R, and no lag column of any kind. Its only view of recent power is up to three day windows of 48 half-hours:

  • D1, the day before the origin: the 48 half-hours ending at the newest usable reading (the origin minus 3.5 hours, the rule of common.origin_lags).
  • D2, the matching day of week: 48 half-hours centred on the most recent earlier half-hour with the target's day of week and time of day that is at least 3.5 hours before the origin (the weekly lag of R), the half-hours after the newest usable reading masked as unobserved.
  • D3, two weeks earlier: the window of D2 shifted back by 336 half-hours.

Each window position carries five channels: the power over effective capacity (standardised with the training rows' mean and standard deviation, clipped at 5 standard deviations, 0 where unobserved), an observed flag, sin and cos of the position's UTC time of day, and its age before the origin divided by 336 hours. Missing, flagged, and start-cut half-hours are unobserved.

Encoder. Three one-dimensional convolutions (kernel 5, padding 2, widths 16, 32, and 32, GELU) applied to each window with shared weights, giving 48 position vectors of width 32 per window. No pooling, so position survives. A learned day-type embedding (3 vectors) is added to each position vector, so attention knows which window a position is from.

Attention. One head. The query is a linear map of the lead features, the solar, calendar, and holiday columns, the ensemble weather summary, and the Primary embedding. Keys and values are linear maps of the position vectors. A learned "no day" key and value token is always present, so a window set that is entirely unobserved, or distrusted, can be ignored; the softmax runs over all positions of all windows shown plus the token. The context vector (width 32) is concatenated with the query inputs and passed to the same head as R (two hidden layers of 64, dropout 0.1, three Gaussians, g09), so the head is unchanged and only the input route differs. About 13,000 more parameters than R's 8,400.

Training. Experiment 397's loop: weighted negative log-likelihood, AdamW, early stopping on a held-out week in every twelve (experiment 422's purge), monthly refits on the 24 months before the test month. Every arm except R and L0 is trained on injected power: in every epoch each training row draws, with equal probability, the clean series or one of three injected worlds (seeds 100 to 102) for the power in its windows (and for R-inj's lags); the target is always the clean series. Worlds come from e00402_inject.inject over 2024-05-01 to 2026-07-01 at 10% coverage (the generator of experiment 402 with FIRST_DAY moved earlier), with the label table's padded real events excluded as base periods. The event pool uses all labelled events including those after a fold's refit, and each depth is a fraction of the donor's mean absolute power over its whole series; the pool supplies only depths and durations, and both are listed as caveats. Three quarters of the training rows are injected, which is more than real events, so clean-row contrasts partly measure that training mix. Power windows are gathered on the GPU from dense per-Primary arrays, so no window is stored.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text: Arm Recent-power input Trained on R the three origin lags clean power R-inj the three origin lags clean and injected power L0 none (lagless) clean power B-mix fixed 50/50 mixture of R-inj and L0 distributions (not an average of quantiles) no fit E1 encoder over D1 clean and injected E2 encoder over D1 and D2 clean and injected E3 encoder over D1, D2, and D3 clean and injected E3-trust E3 plus experiment 404's trust inputs as extra tokens only if the advance rule is met

docs.title: Encroachment sweep
docs.text:
Prediction-only, on saved networks, on the screen's clean rows. A row is clean when its target is finite and outside the padded real-event mask and the 48 hours after an event, every observed half-hour of its three windows is outside the padded mask, and R's three lags are finite (experiment 392's clean_rows, extended to whole days). Every arm is swept on the same rows: every third daily origin of each test month, leads 0.5 to 240 hours.

  • Steps. Add a step D to the affected half-hours, both signs, of 2.5% and 5% of effective capacity, and of 10% of the Primary's trailing 30-day mean power before the origin. MVA-only readings are clipped at zero after the step, and rows where the clip changed any shifted value are dropped from the share (for all arms alike).
  • k for R, as in experiment 392. k = 1 shifts lag_origin; k = 2 also lag_same_time_latest_day; k = 3 also lag_same_time_latest_week.
  • k for the encoders, two variants. Variant 1 shifts single half-hours, in R's order: k = 1 the newest observed half-hour of D1 (R's lag_origin); k = 2 also the half-hour of D1 at the target's time of day (R's day lag); k = 3 also the centre half-hour of D2 (R's week lag); k = 4 (E3 only) also the centre half-hour of D3. Variant 1 is the like-for-like counterpart of R's three single lags, and k up to 3 is compared with R. Variant 2 shifts every observed half-hour of whole windows: k = 1 shifts D1; k = 2 also D2; k = 3 also D3. Variant 2 is the event that fills a day, and R has no counterpart, so the comparison of variant 2 with R is harsher on the encoders.
  • Raw and widened. The headline is raw (experiment 392's headline); the same table is repeated with the 1.15 widening about the median.
  • Lead bands. 0-24, 24-72, 72-168, and 168-240 hours; the 24-72 hour band is the headline.
  • Reported. The median shift of q50 as a share of the step (+1 is the full step, whichever the sign); the ratio of the 5%-95% band width after the step to the width before; coverage of the clean reading and of the event-level reading (actual plus step) by the 5%-95% band; the attention mass on D1, D2, D3, and the "no day" token, for every k and variant. Three seeds per fold.
  • Lag-masked control. Every arm is also evaluated in evaluation mode (dropout off) with all its recent-power inputs masked, the step added, and the mask applied after the step; the forecast must equal the unshifted masked forecast to within 1e-6 (share 0). A larger difference is a bug.

docs.title: Evaluation rows
docs.text:
• Clean rows (real data, no injection). The scored months' rows whose recent days are outside every padded real event; the benchmark for loss outside events.
  • Harm rows (injected worlds). Test-month rows from three held-out injected worlds (seeds 200 to 202, never seen in training) whose target is outside every event and whose windows contain an injected event; clean rows of the same worlds are reported beside them.
  • Event rows (real). Rows whose target is inside a padded labelled event of the corrected label table, and real harm rows (target outside, windows inside). The unlogged-event caveat applies: NGED may have events missing from its logs, so the clean-lag rows may hold events no label covers and the real-event slices undercount.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text: The fits are 6 arms by 4 folds by 3 seeds, 72 fits, plus a fifth fold if the screen advances. Experiment 397 timed the plain network at about a minute. The encoder is heavier because it reads up to 144 positions per row. A first timing of E3 on the GPU took about 3 minutes per pass over the 4.7 million training rows of the 2026-01 fold, so every arm trains on a random 20% of the training rows in each epoch (up to 60 epochs, patience 8), and early stopping reads a fixed random 200,000 of the held-out rows. A single CPU core was not timed, because the GPU epoch is already the cheaper route. One GPU process under 8 GB with one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, free -g checked before each launch (stop line 12 GB available). Fitted networks are saved under the experiment's data folder. No stored fit is reused, because R's recipe differs (the cut, the injected data). Stored forecasts of experiments 389, 87, and the baselines are read as references only.

docs.title: Second screen: a surprise channel
docs.text: Arm E3-surp gives the encoder a sixth channel, the surprise. The surprise of a half-hour is its observed power minus the median of the cross-fitted lagless forecast for the same half-hour (experiment 404's table, K = 6 blocks, never an in-sample lagless forecast), divided by the width of that forecast's 5%-95% band, clipped at 5, and 0 where either is unobserved. The windows otherwise match E3. It runs as a second screen when experiment 404's table exists, on the same four folds, rows, and seeds, with the prediction written before any score is read: E3-surp minus E3 on harm rows at the signed-MW six lies between -0.20 and -0.03 CRPS points, and E3-surp follows at most half of E3's share of the step in the sweep at k = 3. The table must cover each refit without the scored month; if it does not, the arm waits.

docs.title: Design iterations
docs.text: The maintainer wants at least two design iterations of the tokens and the attention after the first screen, before any separate lag-trust evaluation runs on the saved networks. Each iteration is a change to the encoder (for example a second head, a window of a different length, a learned position code, or the trust inputs of experiment 404 as extra tokens), registered with its own prediction before its scores are read, and scored on the same folds and rows. This page records the first screen only; each iteration adds an arm and a dated section.

docs.title: Design iteration 1 (2026-10-31): a widening-only path, then a 14-day history window
docs.text:
First-screen and second-screen findings set the target of this iteration. In the sweep at step c050 (24 to 72 hours, signed-MW six, raw bands) no arm widens its 5%-95% band after a step in the recent power: the width ratio is 1.00 for every arm except E3-surp (1.018 at c050, 1.026 at m10). E3-surp, whose surprise channel moves with the shifted power, follows more of the step (median share 0.225 at k = 3, against 0.125 for E3 and R-inj). The goal of the programme is a share near zero with wider bands. A wider band lowers the training loss only on rows whose window holds an injected jump, and the network already learns to follow about a fifth of the step there, so the reward for widening is weak.

Arm E3-surp-w adds a path that can only widen the bands. The path takes three numbers from the newest day window (D1): the largest absolute surprise in its last 12 half-hours, its mean absolute surprise, and its largest absolute surprise. Non-negative weights (the softplus of raw parameters that start at -10, so the path starts near zero) map them to one additive term per mixture component. The term is never negative, so the path can only widen. The term is added to the log standard deviations of the mixture. The location outputs and the mixture weights are untouched by the new path. The arm is otherwise E3-surp (same rows, folds, seeds, and training worlds).

Predictions, written before any E3-surp-w score is read.

  • P-I1a (bands): E3-surp-w, pooled over the four screen folds and seed 0, at step c050 (and m10), 24 to 72 hours, signed-MW six, day variant, k = 3, raw bands: band-width ratio of at least 1.05 (E3-surp: 1.018 at c050). We put this at about one chance in three, for the reason above.
  • P-I1b (share): in the same cell, the median share is no larger than E3-surp's (0.225).
  • P-I1c (cost): contrast C9 (E3-surp-w minus E3-surp), CRPS in the units of the other contrasts, on the clean and inj_harm row sets at the signed-MW six, pooled over the four folds: the upper end of the interval is at most +0.02.
  • Result of E3-surp-w (seed 0, four folds): P-I1a failed (width ratio 1.019 against 1.018 for E3-surp at step c050; 1.027 against 1.026 at m10), P-I1b held (median share 0.225 in both arms), and P-I1c held (the CRPS of E3-surp-w is lower than E3-surp's by 0.005 to 0.014 on every row set at the signed-MW six). The widening path did not learn to widen after a jump.
  • Diagnostic, not for release (seed 0, four folds, signed-MW six). The arm DIAG-not-for-release-E3-surp-w-ev (E3-surp-w trained on the injected value wherever the target lies in an injected event) learned to widen only a little more after a step: at step c050 (24 to 72 hours, day variant, k = 3) the band-width ratio is 1.069 (E3-surp-w: 1.019) and the median share is 0.325 (0.225). It also widened every band: the 95% quantile covers 0.957 of clean readings (E3-surp-w: 0.900) and the 99% quantile covers 1.000, and the CRPS on clean rows is 0.055 higher (3.035 against 2.980). The scale path can learn widening when the objective rewards it, and with this objective it learns to widen everywhere.
  • The fallback objective is on hold. The fallback named in the plan (train on the injected world's value where the target lies in an injected event) rewards persistence of the jump, which is the opposite of forecasting the normal running arrangement. It stays unfitted until the maintainer's design session decides. It differs from arm U2 of the uncertainty programme as follows: the fallback keeps the existing transient injected events and lets the target take their value, whereas U2 trains on worlds whose genuine level changes enter the lags and the target together, and keeps the location path blind to the surprise magnitude; U2 also feeds lag ages, missing flags, weather age, and lead into its scale factor and penalises the factor on clean rows. The widening path of E3-surp-w is the clean-target version of U2's scale path.

The 14-day history window (the brief recent_history_encoder_brief.md) follows as its own dated section. Its arms (S1, S404, H-smooth, H-lvl, H14-s, and the other-week control H14-s-ow), its pilot, its leakage check, and its pre-registered rules are those of the Opus design note, with experiment 404's table (frozen at commit 63d3799f, one table per month and seed) as the lagless forecast. They run after E3-surp-w is scored.

docs.title: Design iteration 2 (2026-10-31): a 14-day history window
docs.text:
The question is what level a Primary sits at now, and how to pool the noisy surprise, not which Primary this is. Experiment 421 asked the identity question. This iteration keeps the Primary embedding and gives the network 14 days of history (672 half-hours ending at the newest usable reading, origin minus 3.5 hours) so that it can estimate the Primary's current level against the lagless forecast (aim a) and pool the surprise with learned weights (aim b). The full design, reasoning, and diagnostics are in the design note recent_history_encoder_design_answer.md; this section records the arms, the departures, and the predictions.

Arms, all trained on the injected worlds, on the four screen folds and three seeds.

  • S1: R-inj plus the single-step surprise at each of its three origin lags (reference for aim b).
  • H-smooth: R-inj plus four learned smoothed surprises of the 14-day surprise series. The weights of position j for a target at T are a softmax over the observed positions of a(L) cos(time of day of j minus T) + c(L) cos(day of week of j minus T) minus b(L) times the age of j in days, with a, c, b learned per lead band (days 0 to 2, 2 to 5, 5 to 10, and 10 or more) and b at least 0. The weights never read the surprise values. The observed share of the window joins the inputs. (Aim b.)
  • H-lvl: R-inj plus a level offset and a 4-way soft regime vector per origin. A dilated convolutional network encodes the window, one attention pooling (query: Primary embedding and the origin's time of day) gives a summary, and a second pooling gives the level offset, the weighted mean of power minus lagless median. The three mixture means shift by g(L) times the offset, with g in [0, 1] learned per lead band. The regime vector joins the head. (Aim a.)
  • H14-s: no lags. The same dilated convolutional network encodes the window (eight channels: power, observed flag, lagless median, surprise, sine and cosine of time of day and of day of week), and one attention head with a null token reads it. The score of position j adds three terms to the dot product: a(cos of the time-of-day difference), c(cos of the day-of-week difference), and minus b times the age.
  • H14-s-ow: H14-s with the window read from 28 days earlier (control: identity and season without recency).

Departures from the design note, stated before any score. The bank-holiday channel is omitted (no holiday table is loaded in this harness), so eight channels carry H14-s. Experiment 404's hand-built window statistics (arm S404) are not run in this screen, so aim (b) is decided against S1 only and the comparison with S404 stays open. Window encoding is per row, not per origin: each batch is 2,048 rows and the convolution blocks use gradient checkpointing to stay under 8 GB. The sweep runs the lag variant for the arms that keep R-inj's lags and the whole-day variant on the history (shift the last k days of the history by the step, and any lag that falls in those days), k = 1, 2, 3, for every arm of this iteration, plus the masked control. Experiment 404's lagless table is used for the lagless median and the surprise, one table per month and seed.

More departures, found by the plan and code review. The convolution blocks use a group normalisation (one group) after each convolution, not the layer normalisation of the design note. The three arms that run the convolutional encoder (H-lvl, H14-s, H14-s-ow) take four times as many optimiser steps per epoch as R-inj (batches of 2,048 rows against 8,192, at a fifth of the rows per epoch), so their contrasts with R-inj mix architecture and step count. The sweep has one combined variant, "hist": it shifts the last k whole days of the history and any lag inside them, so at k = 1 both the newest lag and the daily lag move, whereas R-inj's lag sweep at k = 1 moves only the newest lag. The contrasts with R-inj's lag sweep at the same k are therefore not like for like. The design note's P5 comparison with S404, P6b (level offset against real events), the second clause of P8, and P10 are not run in this screen, and sweep variants 1, 2, and 4 are not run. The observed share that H-smooth reads is the share of usable positions (observed power and a lagless forecast). For H14-s-ow the attention class for the newest 6 hours is empty by construction, because the window ends 28 days earlier. The level offset is clipped at 5 standard deviations of the Primary's target.

Pilot result and the H14-s diagnosis (fold 2026-01, seed 0). On the mixed validation worlds the validation negative log-likelihoods were: R-inj 0.4777, E3-surp 0.4591, H-smooth 0.4523 (59 epochs, 286 s), H-lvl 0.4993 (19 epochs, 1,415 s), and H14-s 0.5498 (16 epochs, 1,485 s). The stage-0 rule fires for H14-s (worse than R-inj by more than 0.05), so H14-s and H14-s-ow stop. Before any further convolutional fit, three diagnostic fits of H14-s on this fold read a tenth of the rows per epoch (patience 30): H14-s-diag1 (position dropout 0.1), H14-s-diag2 (0.3), and H14-s-diag3 (0.5). Pre-registered reading, before the diagnostic scores: if the best diagnostic fit reaches a validation negative log-likelihood within +0.01 of R-inj's (at most 0.4877), a four-fold screen of H14-s at that setting is justified; if every diagnostic fit is worse than R-inj by more than 0.03, the 14-day convolutional line stops, and the page says that the window memorised each Primary's history.

Diagnosis result. The three diagnostic fits ended at validation negative log-likelihoods of 0.5347 (H14-s-diag1), 0.5399 (H14-s-diag2), and 0.5650 (H14-s-diag3), each more than 0.03 worse than R-inj's 0.4777, and all three used the 60-epoch limit with the loss still falling slowly. By the rule written above, the 14-day convolutional line stops: H14-s, H14-s-ow, and the four-fold H-lvl screen do not run. The diagnosis does not separate memorisation from slow training at a tenth of the rows per epoch, so the page claims only that three settings of H14-s did not reach R-inj's validation loss.

S1 and H-smooth result (four folds, three seeds, signed-MW six). P4 failed: H-smooth minus S1 on injected harm rows is +0.066 [0.046, 0.088], where the prediction was at or below -0.03. P5 failed in the useful direction: S1 minus R-inj on clean rows is -0.083 [-0.096, -0.070], where the prediction was within plus or minus 0.03. On injected harm rows S1 minus R-inj is -0.060 [-0.076, -0.044]. The minimum detectable effects of R-inj are 0.077 on clean rows and 0.071 on injected harm rows. The learned smoothing of the surprise does not beat the surprise at the three origin lags.

Predictions, written before any score of these arms is read (signed-MW six unless stated; contrast = CRPS difference in the units of the other contrasts).

  • P1: H14-s minus R-inj on clean rows lies between -0.05 and +0.05.
  • P2: H14-s minus R-inj on injected harm rows lies between -0.30 and -0.05.
  • P3: H14-s minus the better of E3 and E3-surp lies within plus or minus 0.05 on harm rows and on clean rows.
  • P4 (aim b): H-smooth minus S1 on injected harm rows is at or below -0.03.
  • P5: S1 minus R-inj on clean rows lies within plus or minus 0.03.
  • P6 (aim a): H-lvl minus R-inj on clean rows, 12 to 36 hours ahead, is at or below -0.03, and the learned g falls with lead (days 6 to 10 at least 0.2 below days 1 to 2).
  • P6c: H-smooth's kernels put at least half their weight within 3 hours of the target's time of day, and their effective number of positions lies between 6 and 100.
  • P7: H14-s-ow minus H14-s on clean rows, 12 to 36 hours ahead, is at least +0.05.
  • P8: on injected harm rows, the mean null-token mass of H14-s is at least 0.15 higher than on the same rows in the clean world.
  • P9: in the whole-day sweep, H14-s follows at most 0.05 of a 5% step at k = 1, 2, and 3, with a band-width ratio of at least 1.10 at k = 3.

Rules. The advance rule, the two aim rules, the choice between the 14-day window and the day windows, the inert and collapse rules, and the stop rules are those of sections 5 of the design note; the screen reports them after scoring. The pilot (one fold, seed 0) runs first and stops the screen if the masked control moves the forecast by more than 1e-6, if a visibility assertion fails, if the attention of H14-s is uniform or sits wholly on the null token, or if its validation negative log-likelihood is worse than R-inj's by more than 0.05.

docs.title: Checks, reviews, and what the page will report
docs.text:
• Departures from experiment 397's recipe, found by the code review. Every arm (R included) trains on a random 20% of the rows per epoch with batch 8,192 (experiment 397: full epochs, batch 16,384, patience 6), and standardises the three lags with one pooled mean and standard deviation of the cleaned targets (experiment 397: one per lag column). Scores use the 1.15 widening; CRPS is the mean of the three seeds' scores, and the tail pinball and coverage are computed from the seed-averaged quantiles. Rows with a valid time on or after 2026-07-01 are not scored.

  • The avoidable-curtailment cost is not computed at the screen. The harm-row sets have no node table; it is computed for the clean rows if the screen advances.

  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviews this plan and then the code before the first fit; a fresh Sonnet re-derives the headline numbers; a fresh Sonnet reviews the write-up and its prose. The PR body records what each found.

  • Reported per group and per Primary: CRPS, q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage and pinball loss, cold winter nights, the avoidable-curtailment cost, absolute CRPS beside every contrast with its interval, and the minimum detectable effect.
  • Figures. CRPS by lead for every arm and the references (headline); sweep share and band ratio against k; attention weight per day and per position; at least six real-event time series plots across both metering groups; a day-ahead and a 14-day example forecast. Generators are anonymised.
  • Audit checks. The median forecast minus the mean forecast per site; the error of the mean forecast beside each quantile-score contrast; which audit triggers fired.

docs.title: What it can and cannot say
docs.text: Four months give wide intervals: the screen can stop the idea or rank it for the queue, and cannot support a claim of benefit. The injected worlds are synthetic; the real-event rows are few. The encoder sees days of raw power at the forecast origin only, so it uses nothing a live service would lack (CAMS and ERA5 are not used at all).

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet auditor re-derived the headline numbers from the stored forecasts and found no fault that changes any headline number. Three audit triggers fired: results contradicted the predictions, nested arms did worse than the arm they extend (E3-surp against E3, S1 against R-inj), and the lag-masked control had to be checked. The auditor matched every CRPS and contrast to 5e-5. The auditor also found no overlap of the evaluation worlds with the training worlds, and found that the rows of the saved lagless table that feed training lie before each refit. The lag-masked control's change in forecast is exactly 0 in all 84 sweep files, as it must be for a control with the lags removed. Four caveats stay open:

  • S1 clears the minimum detectable effect by 0.006 on clean rows. Three of four folds clear it and the 2026-06 fold (-0.053) does not. On injected harm rows S1's -0.060 is inside 0.071.
  • The flags that sort rows into clean, harm, and event rows look only at the three most recent days, not at H-smooth's 14-day history. A real event in days 4 to 14 can sit in H-smooth's clean rows.
  • Training rows take the surprise from cross-fitted lagless forecasts and test rows from the later-fitted lagless forecast, a mild distribution shift that is not a leak.
  • The widening of 1.15 is applied about the median to all 11 quantiles, so every arm's bands are 1.15 times as wide, which keeps arms comparable but is not an arm's own widening.

Checks not run at this screen. The median forecast minus the mean forecast per site, the error of the mean forecast beside each quantile contrast, and the avoidable-curtailment cost were not computed.

docs.title: Which parts of a neural wind-farm forecaster earn their place: passing each ensemble member through the network, a physics power curve inside it, and a head that puts probability mass at zero and at full output?
docs.text:
Take-home: a plain pooled neural network ties Wind farms research default 2, and none of the extra parts earns its place. Default 2 runs a power curve trained on ERA5 weather on each of the 51 ensemble members, then a mixture-density head. "True days 1 to 10" means forecast lead times of 24 to 240 hours, and "kept rows" are the half-hours left after experiment 210's idle-band mask removes those where a farm is idle at low wind. On the kept rows at true days 1 to 10, member_plain scores 10.533 points of capacity against 10.518 for default 2 (difference +0.015, 99.8% interval -0.068 to +0.099). No design beats default 2 by the 0.10-point margin. The 1.5% limit is the share of observations allowed above an arm's q99 (the 0.99 quantile forecast). Every arm leaves 2.2% to 2.8% above it, and the maintainer's rule is that an arm must meet the limit to advance, so no arm advances.

The three farms are W1 to W3. An arm is one design variant: how the ensemble enters the network, whether a physics power curve (the plant) is present, and which head is used. The arms are grouped as A1 (member handling), A4 (physics layer), and A7 (head). The 2 x 2 of plain network against plant, each trained with or without the idle band, is called H-P. Each arm is a pooled mixture-density network, trained five times (seeds 0 to 4) on the daily ensemble hindcast, and scored on 53 Tuesday runs of 2025-07 to 2026-06. Margins (0.10 points, tail harm at most 0.02) were agreed by the maintainer on 2026-10-31. The reproduction gate passed: the shared code reproduces the default's 11.081 kept-row score and 10.518 true-days-1-to-10 score with a per-quantile gap against the stored rows of 0.000 at three decimals.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute scores (kept rows, true days 1 to 10; every lead in brackets). member_plain 10.533 (11.090), member_frozen 10.534 (11.085), member_e2e 10.530 (11.083), one_pass_ms 10.541 (11.126), one_pass_m 10.564 (11.137), memberwise 10.515 (11.109), member_plain_censored 10.551 (11.107). Wind farms research default 2: 10.518 (11.081); research default 1: 10.752 (11.352); climatology: 13.860 (13.842). Seed standard deviations are 0.02 to 0.08 points.
  • A1, member handling: no gain. member_plain minus one_pass_ms is -0.008 points at true days 1 to 10 (99.8% interval -0.093 to +0.076) and -0.002 at true days 3 to 10; both halves of the prediction failed: no gain of 0.10 points, and the q99 pinball loss rose 0.6% instead of falling 5%. Against one_pass_m it is -0.031 (-0.115 to +0.051). The member-wise arm's pooled mixture is -0.026 against one_pass_ms (-0.092 to +0.071). The minimum detectable effect is about 0.08 points, so smaller differences are inconclusive, not null.
  • A4, physics layer: a tie. member_frozen minus member_plain is +0.000 (-0.071 to +0.073); member_e2e minus member_frozen is -0.004 (95% -0.008 to -0.001, within seed noise of 0.05). The plain network is chosen, as the maintainer's rule says.
  • A7, censored head: no better, and the tail is nearly unchanged. member_plain_censored minus member_plain is +0.018 (95% +0.004 to +0.031; 99.8% -0.005 to +0.039). The q99 pinball loss falls 0.6% and the share of observations above q99 goes from 2.46% to 2.35%. The prediction of 1.5% or less failed, and an ad hoc check, not in the stored report, found only 502 of 1,466 exceedances of member_plain's q99 at 99.9% of capacity or above, with a mean overshoot of 7.3 points at a mean q99 of 0.80 of capacity. Censoring was tested on one base arm only.
  • Tails. Observations beyond q99 at true days 1 to 10: 2.15% for the reproduced default, 2.17% to 2.78% for the arms, 1.66% for research default 1 (an XGBoost model), 4.74% for climatology. Beyond q01: 0.6% to 1.25% for the arms.
  • Idle-band results. Scored with and without experiment 210's idle-band mask: training on all rows scores 0.16 points worse at true days 1 to 10 (plain, +0.161, 99.8% +0.043 to +0.290) and 1.74 points better on the idle-band rows (-1.740), and ties on all rows with the idle half-hours scored as zero (plain +0.011 at true days 1 to 10). The scores on cleaned zeros (idle-band observations set to zero, the experiment 210 mask only) are 10.383 for member_plain and 10.374 for the default at true days 1 to 10, and the all-rows arms move ahead of member_plain on cleaned zeros (member_plain_allrows 10.352). The mask's false-keep and false-drop rates need labelled idle periods, which this experiment does not have; experiment 210's own rates are a false-drop rate capped at 5% and misses of 51% to 69% out of sample. In the H-P 2 x 2, trained on all rows, the frozen plant is 0.039 points worse than plain at true days 1 to 10 (99.8% +0.003 to +0.074), 0.038 better on idle-band rows (interval includes zero), and 0.022 worse on cleaned zeros. Trained with the mask, it ties on kept rows (+0.000) and is 0.151 worse on idle-band rows. The prediction that the plant helps on the idle band, and that the gap halves with the mask, failed. The soft cut-in ramp variant and the detector-rule cells are not run.
  • Members as quantile forecasts. The memberwise arm gives each member its own 11 quantiles, and the forecast is the equal-weight mixture of the 51 members' distributions. The mean score of one member's quantiles against the observation is 14.27 points, against 10.52 for the pooled mixture, and 9.8% of observations fall below, and 14.4% above, a member's own q01 and q99. One member's quantiles are therefore narrower than the pooled mixture, whose own tails are also too narrow (2.17% above q99). The maintainer has said production can afford 51 network passes per forecast, and no arm needed them to improve the score.
  • Coherence. Scores use the 51 member paths across W1 to W3 jointly over one run and one calendar day (529 blocks). The Schaake shuffle beats ensemble copula coupling (ECC) from one_pass_ms by 9.3% on the variogram score (99% interval -0.491 to -0.256) and by 0.8% on the energy score. The member route's own plant paths are 5.9% worse than ECC paths from the same arm on the variogram score. Member-wise quantiles taken at ECC ranks are 5.6% better than ECC on the variogram score but 4.2% worse than the Schaake shuffle. The design note's prediction (member route beats ECC by 5% on the variogram score) failed; the 5% margin came from the design note, and the maintainer has not agreed it. ECC beats independent draws by 1.3% on the energy score over a day. It does not beat them on the variogram score. Independent draws score better within the first day of the forecast. Methods: Schaake shuffle (Clark et al. 2004), ECC (Schefzik et al. 2013).
  • Compute. The member route runs 51 network passes per forecast, against one for one_pass_ms. The maintainer has said production can afford 51 passes (2026-10-31).
  • Possible follow-up (not agreed). A soft cut-in ramp on the plant, and the detector-rule cells of the H-P 2 x 2, would need the maintainer's say and the cleaned-zero rows.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate (G0): passed. Kept 11.081 against stored 11.081; true days 1 to 10 10.518 against 10.518, same seeds.
  • Fresh Sonnet reviews: three code reviews before the first fit (they found a missing upper-tail verdict, a lead band that excluded its upper end, a wrong weight-decay setting on the plant, and a wrong member-wise path construction, all fixed). The results, write-up, and prose reviews are recorded in the pull request.
  • Audit triggers: audit rule 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction) applied to A1, A7, and H-P. The A7 explanation (exceedances come from windy half-hours, not the cap) was tested with the exceedance diagnostic. The A1 and H-P explanations are untested.
  • Not applicable: monthly refits and avoidable-curtailment cost (the wind protocol has none), and the 25-second smoke-test numbers, which are not kept.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Seed standard deviations of 0.02 to 0.08 points make differences below 0.08 inconclusive, not null.
  • The member-shifted coherence path keeps the plant's own spread; its comparisons mix in marginal differences.
  • The scored year 2025-07 to 2026-06 follows the training cut-off; three farms is a small sample.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: The maintainer wants one neural design for the demand, wind, and solar forecasters, with each difference between the three justified by an ablation. The Opus review that opens this programme (briefs/unified_forecaster_design_answer.md, private) proposes a shared skeleton: a pooled mixture density network (MDN) with a site embedding, a weather encoder, an optional physics power layer, and a head. This experiment is the wind worker's part: a reproduction gate (G0), then ablations A1 (member handling), A4 (physics layer), and the wind arms of A7 (bounded head), on the three metered wind farms W1 to W3. A second worker runs the solar farms in a separate experiment with its own id.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms share one code path (e00429_model.py): a pooled network with an 8-wide learned farm embedding, two hidden layers of 64, a three-component Gaussian mixture on the farm's output fraction, and the 11-level quantiles read from the mixture's cumulative distribution (experiment 347's recipe). Inputs per case are the lead (sine and cosine of the hour of day and the lead in hundreds of hours, as in 347) and the weather columns of experiment 303's member table (wind speed at 10 m and 100 m, direction sine and cosine at both heights, and temperature). Wind farms in this repository use no lagged power in the 347 head, so none is added.

Arm Member handling (D1) Physics layer (D2) Head (D3) G0 Fixed summary of the plant's 51 powers Frozen stage-3 plant, as 347 Clipped one_pass_ms One pass on the mean and standard deviation of each column none Clipped one_pass_m One pass on the mean of each column none Clipped member_plain Shared encoder per member; mean, standard deviation, p10, p90 pooled none Clipped member_frozen As member_plain Frozen stage-3 plant power as an extra encoder input and as the mixture's centre Clipped member_e2e As member_plain The stage-3 plant as an nn.Module, trained end to end from 347's parameters Clipped memberwise Shared network on each member alone; pooled forecast is the equal-weight mixture of the 51 member mixtures none Clipped memberwise_frozen As memberwise, each member's mixture centred on its own stage-3 plant power Frozen stage-3 plant Clipped member_plain_allrows As member_plain, trained and early-stopped on every hindcast case, idle band included none Clipped member_frozen_allrows As member_frozen, trained on every hindcast case Frozen stage-3 plant Clipped member_<best>_censored As the better of the three member arms as that arm Censored at 0 and 1 ref_347_y2, ref_default, ref_clim stored rows

one_pass_ms is the demand design moved to wind. Arms without a plant centre the mixture on the mean fraction of the training cases, so C3 changes two things at once: the plant power as an encoder input and the plant median as the mixture's centre. A tie in C3 cannot say which of the two failed to help. The trainable plant in member_e2e learns at 2e-4 (the rest of the network at 2e-3) and has no weight decay, so it starts from experiment 347's parameters. The member encoder is a 7-to-16-to-16 network applied to every member; the 51 outputs are pooled and fed to the trunk. The design note suggests training on one random member per row to match the one-pass cost, but pooled statistics need all 51 members, so the member arms use all 51 on the GPU and the cost is stated in the write-up.

The censored head (A7) adds the exact likelihood of an observation at zero or at capacity: for an observed fraction at or below 0.001 the likelihood is the mixture's mass below zero, and at or above 0.999 it is the mass above one. This places point masses at 0 and 1 equal to the Gaussian tails (the design note names point masses fitted by likelihood; the censored mixture is the simplest form with the same effect). The clipped head leaves the likelihood alone and clamps the quantiles, as 347 does.

Carry-forward. The censored arm runs on whichever of member_plain, member_frozen, and member_e2e scores best at true days 1 to 10 (if none beats member_plain by the margin, on member_plain), and the arm name states the choice. If one_pass_ms is within the margin of member_plain (A1 fails), the A4 arms still run on the member route because a power curve needs members (experiment 242); the write-up labels this.

Only the censored arm for the selected base is fitted, so there is one C5. C1 is judged on true days 3 to 10 (lead 72 to 240 hours, kept rows), where the design note's prediction sits; the other contrasts are judged on true days 1 to 10. The tail test is the change in the pooled 0.01 and 0.99 pinball loss at true days 1 to 10. Per-farm tail tables are in the report; the example-forecast figures come from a separate script before the write-up.

docs.title: Added by the maintainer's decisions of 2026-10-31
docs.text:
• Lead ranges. Every table reports true days 1 to 10, the 12 to 36 hour band, and true days 1 to 14 (lead 24 to 336 hours, the part of the row set that exists) side by side.
  • Training data. Wind may use the one year of ENS hindcasts (experiment 303 argued against it; this experiment follows experiment 347 and uses it).
  • Physics layer against idle noise (H-P, A4). The maintainer put the idle-noise 2 x 2 inside this experiment: {plain encoder, frozen plant channel} x {trained on all rows, trained without experiment 210's idle band}. The cells are member_plain_allrows, member_frozen_allrows, member_plain, and member_frozen. The prediction that can fail: trained on all rows, the plant arm beats the plain arm by at least 0.10 points on the idle-band rows and 0.05 on the kept rows, and the gap shrinks by at least half when both train without the idle band. All arms are also scored with and without the idle-band mask; scores on the cleaned-zero rows are added when that row set exists.
  • Members as quantile forecasts (A1). NGED's proposed deliverable is a 51-member power ensemble in which each member is itself a quantile forecast, and production can afford 51 passes. The memberwise arms give each member its own 11 quantiles, and the pooled forecast is the equal-weight mixture of the 51 member mixtures (trained on the pooled likelihood). The report scores each member's quantiles against the observation (averaged over members) beside the pooled mixture's score and the share of observations beyond a member's q01 and q99; the path construction memberwise takes each member's own median as its path.
  • Coherence (A1). NGED runs power-flow models one ensemble member at a time, so the forecast must give 51 members that are coherent across time and across the three farms. The script e00429_coherence.py scores the 51 member paths with the energy score and the variogram score (order 0.5) across W1 to W3 jointly, in two kinds of block: one run and one calendar day (at least 36 shared half-hours), and one run's every twelfth lead across all leads. Four path constructions are compared: ECC (ensemble copula coupling: member k takes the arm's quantile at the rank of its own 100 m wind speed among the 51 at that farm and valid time); the Schaake shuffle (the 51 hindcast runs nearest in day of year supply observed paths, and one historical date orders all three farms and all leads); member-shifted (member k keeps its own stage-3 plant power and adds the arm's median minus the plant's median; this stands for the member route using each member's own path); and independent (no coherence, the lower reference). Experiment 304 found member forecasts correlate 0.95 to 0.97 across farms while errors correlate 0.54 to 0.78, so the Schaake shuffle may beat ECC. The design note's prediction is that the member route beats ECC on the variogram score by at least 5% and on the marginal score by at least 0.10; the 5% coherence margin is the Opus note's proposal, not the maintainer's. The member-shifted construction keeps the plant's own spread and uses no learned encoder, so comparisons across arms mix in marginal differences. It is my reading of "the member route using each member's path", and the write-up says so. The stored default 2 is not path-scored because its stored rows are marginal only.

docs.title: Pre-registered contrasts
docs.text:
Each is the difference in kept-row quantile score at true days 1 to 10 and, beside it, over every lead. All intervals are month-block bootstrap intervals (experiment 347's resampler), 99% level with a Bonferroni correction over these six (level 0.9983).

  1. C1 (A1): member_plain minus one_pass_ms.
  2. C2 (A1): member_plain minus one_pass_m (experiment 343's input choice).
  3. C3 (A4): member_frozen minus member_plain.
  4. C4 (A4): member_e2e minus member_frozen.
  5. C5 (A7): the censored arm minus the same arm clipped.
  6. C6 (A1): memberwise (pooled mixture) minus one_pass_ms.

Reference contrasts, not corrected: each arm against ref_347_y2 and ref_default.

docs.title: Standing practices this experiment follows
docs.text:
• Cadence: one fit per seed on the fixed hindcast, as 347 (not a refit schedule; the wind protocol has no refit loop).
  • Reuse: experiment 347's case frames, stored plant parameters and plant-power summaries, experiment 339's default rows, experiment 324's climatology, and experiment 343's rows are read, not refitted. The scored rows match (the same 53 Tuesday runs and the kept mask).
  • Seeds: 5 per arm (0 to 4); the minimum detectable effect of each contrast is printed from the seed spread and the interval half-width.
  • Models saved: each fitted network's state file under the experiment's data folder.
  • Tails and curtailment: q01, q05, q95, q99 pinball loss and coverage per farm beside the score. No wind-specific curtailment-cost metric exists in the wind protocol, so none is reported.
  • Examples: a day-ahead forecast and a full 14-day forecast for one farm, anonymised.
  • Not applicable: cleaned Primary data, the D15/D18 cut, load-shift events.
  • GPU: one process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The fit slot is requested from the manager before the first fit.

docs.title: Plan review
docs.text: Earlier advice read and followed: 347's reproduction recipe, 339's head, 343's input comparison, and 242's finding about member handling. Departure: the design note's random-member training trick is not used (see Arms).

docs.title: Which of four design differences does a pooled mixture-density network for the six metered solar farms need: ensemble members passed one by one, a PyTorch plant inside the network, ERA5 and CAMS pretraining, and point masses at zero and at capacity?
docs.text:
A one-pass neural network on the ensemble mean and spread is not beaten by any richer design we tested for the six metered solar farms. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters the farms, which are labelled A to F here. A 51-member ensemble weather forecast ("the ensemble") drives every network. We tested four design differences, each against its reference: passing the 51 ensemble members through an encoder (stage A2), adding a plant model inside the network (A5), pretraining on estimates of past weather from the ERA5 reanalysis and the CAMS irradiance product (A6), and adding point masses at zero and at capacity to the output (A7). G0 is the check that the shared code reproduces experiment 345's network. The encoder is 0.22% better at days 3 to 10 over six seeds (99% interval −0.60% to +0.18%), which is inside the seed noise. The plant model is 0.4% worse at days 6 to 10. Pretraining followed by fine-tuning is 0.30% worse (−1.21% to +2.32%), and point masses are 0.002% worse (−1.03% to +1.80%). The A6 and A7 intervals are wider than the 1% margin, so the pre-registered rule selects the one-pass network without either addition. The only difference with an interval that excludes zero on the favourable side is the clear-sky irradiance input column: it improves the score by 0.42% at days 6 to 10 over six seeds (−0.88% to −0.03%), under the margin.

For coherent member paths, a Schaake shuffle of the one-pass network's quantiles beats ensemble copula coupling on the variogram score. NGED's power-flow modelling needs 51 member paths that are coherent across time and across the six farms. The Schaake shuffle ranks the 51 quantiles of each half-hour by 51 observed paths from about a year earlier. It lowers the variogram score by 13.0% (−15.9% to −9.5%) against ensemble copula coupling (ECC, which ranks the quantiles by each member's shortwave radiation), and leaves the energy score over the whole 10 days unchanged (−0.08%, −0.22% to +0.10%). Passing each ensemble member through the network alone gives paths whose energy score is 11.3% worse and whose variogram score is 20.3% worse. Its marginal quantile score is 1.5% worse over all bands (+0.38% to +2.80%).

Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity (lower is better), farm-equal means over experiment 310's scored year. The G0 check passed: g0_onepass matches experiment 345's solar_pooled network to machine precision in every band (differences below 1e-13%), because the shared code with every addition switched off runs the same recipe with the same seeds.

docs.title: Each prediction against its result
docs.text:
• G0 passed. The difference to experiment 345 is below 1e-13% in every band.
  • A2 failed. The encoder beat one pass by 0.57% at days 3 to 10 on three seeds (−1.14% to +0.13%) and by 0.22% on six seeds (−0.60% to +0.18%), against a predicted 2%. The six-seed minimum detectable effect (from the spread between seeds) is 0.58% for this arm. Dropping the spread input (a2_mean_only) changes the score by −0.10% (−0.56% to +0.34%). The member-wise arm is 1.07% worse at days 3 to 10 (+0.08% to +2.14%) and 3.9% worse at day 1.
  • A6 failed. Pretraining followed by fine-tuning is 0.30% worse than the ensemble-only arm over all bands (−1.21% to +2.32%), against a predicted gain of at least 1%. The three fine-tuned seeds spread widely (standard deviation 0.092 points), so the minimum detectable effect is 2.1% (0.18% for the ensemble-only arm and 0.14% for the ERA5-and-CAMS-only arm), and a gain below 2.1% cannot be ruled out. The ERA5-and-CAMS-only arm is 9.99% worse (+5.78% to +13.58%) over all bands and 7.4% worse at day 1.
  • A5 failed. The frozen plant channel is 0.40% worse than a5_plain at days 6 to 10 (+0.004% to +0.76%) and 0.74% worse at day 1 (−0.11% to +1.55%). The trained plant is 0.41% worse at days 6 to 10 (+0.02% to +0.76%), the same as the frozen plant.
  • A7 met its tail-harm limit and did not move the coverage. Against g0_onepass, the 0.01 pinball loss is 0.017 points lower and the 0.99 pinball loss is 0.008 points higher (the limit is 0.02 points). The coverage of the 0.99 quantile rises from 0.9834 to 0.9887 (target 0.99). The coverage of the 0.01 quantile moves from 0.0532 to 0.0513 (target 0.01), so that quantile still covers about 5% of observations. The score is unchanged.

The clear-sky column improves the one-pass network by a little. The a5_plain arm adds the clear-sky irradiance (the radiation under a cloudless sky, from the sun's position) as an input column so that the plant arms differ from it only by the plant channel. The column alone improves on the one-pass network by 0.71% at days 6 to 10 on three seeds (−1.31% to −0.14%) and by 0.42% on six seeds (−0.88% to −0.03%). The six-seed minimum detectable effect is 0.37%, so the estimate is just above seed noise.

The plant result may not be comparable with experiment 313's. Experiment 313 found a 3.4% gain from a plant at days 8 to 10. The audit found two differences. Experiment 430 uses experiment 345's input columns, which have none of experiment 313's plant, plant-spread, or lag columns. Its plant also has one pooled scale at tilt 20 degrees, where experiment 310's has a scale per farm at tilt 35 degrees. The audit also found that the plant is nearly a function of inputs the network already has: the plant's error is only 1% to 3% below that of the ensemble shortwave radiation alone. We did not re-run experiment 313's design, so we cannot say why the gains differ.

docs.title: Coherence of the 51 member paths
docs.text:
The Schaake shuffle lowers the variogram score by 13% on both the one-pass and the encoder marginals. The reference is the one-pass network with ECC. The energy score separates the routes little, because the marginal accuracy dominates it. The variogram score separates them clearly. The energy score is the mean distance of the 51 member paths to the observed path, minus half the mean distance between members. The variogram score compares the observed and the ensemble-mean differences between pairs of half-hours at the same farm up to 6 hours apart, and between farms at the same time.

Arm and route Energy score vs reference Variogram score vs reference One pass, ECC (reference) 0 0 One pass, Schaake shuffle −0.08% (−0.22% to +0.10%) −13.0% (−15.9% to −9.5%) One pass, independent draws +0.26% (+0.11% to +0.47%) +14.3% (+4.8% to +27.7%) Encoder, ECC −0.40% (−1.03% to +0.15%) +0.5% (−0.1% to +1.2%) Encoder, Schaake shuffle −0.48% (−1.08% to +0.12%) −13.0% (−15.9% to −9.5%) Member-wise, own paths +11.25% (+10.43% to +12.21%) +20.3% (+16.3% to +23.9%) Member-wise, independent draws +1.58% (+0.50% to +2.75%) +16.8% (+6.5% to +32.5%)

Rows cover the six farms and 10 days jointly. In each separate day band, the Schaake shuffle lowers the energy score too: by 0.89% at day 1 (−1.06% to −0.73%).

Figure 2. Energy score (with 99% intervals) and variogram score of each route against one pass with ECC, over six farms and 10 days jointly. Negative is better. The variogram intervals are in the table.

  • The member-wise paths score worse than independent draws on the energy score. The energy score is 11.25% worse for the member-wise paths and 1.58% worse for independent draws of the same marginal. On the variogram score the two intervals overlap. Each member is drawn at one fixed quantile level, so a member's path is one level of that member's own distribution and not a coherent trajectory.
  • The encoder does not change the coherence ranking. Its energy-score gain of 0.4% to 0.5% is inside the intervals.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per farm. Averaged over all rows, the median forecast sits 0.39 to 0.83 points of capacity above the mean forecast at each farm, for the one-pass, encoder, a5_plain, and point-mass arms. Averaged by month, the difference for the one-pass arm runs from −3.4 to +3.9 points, with the sign set by the season, so the farm-equal, month-equal mean in the Tail quantiles table is near zero.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile-score contrasts. The mean absolute error of the mean forecast moves in the same direction as the quantile score for the encoder and for a5_plain, farm by farm (scores/checks.csv). One farm moves the other way for one arm, by an amount inside the seed noise.
  • Triggers fired. Of the seven audit triggers in the ml-experiment skill, trigger 2 fired, because every A-stage prediction failed and the plant result differs from experiment 313's. Triggers 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 did not fire, and trigger 7 does not apply. The next section gives the audit findings.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored forecasts with its own code and tried to break the method.

  • Re-derivation: the seven contrasts it re-derived match scores/headline.csv to four decimals, and the G0 check is bit-identical to experiment 345 on all 410,899 rows. Accepted, no change.
  • Seed noise is the main risk. Per-seed A2 contrasts run from −0.87% to +0.94%, and per-seed A5 contrasts from −1.31% to +0.36%. The second seed set was run for this reason, and the six-seed figures shrink both effects. Accepted: the page reports six-seed figures for these two arms.
  • No leakage, misalignment, or clipping fault: training rows end one day before the refit, the standardiser matches a recompute on data before 2025-08-31, the validation window is the last 61 days, ERA5 and CAMS rows stop before 2024-04-01, and all quantiles lie within the farm's ceiling.
  • Plant: it matches experiment 310's NumPy plant at tilt 35 degrees, and a mirrored azimuth scores clearly worse. The plant adds little over the shortwave input.
  • Leave-one-farm-out: no sign flips for A2 or A5. Farms C and E carry most of the A2 gain.
  • Mean-forecast error: no disagreement with the quantile score that matters, so trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Coherence: the pair set, the energy score, and the variogram score match for ECC on one month. The Schaake score differs by 0.016 in energy, from the random fill of about 5% of the missing history, and the Schaake history is at least 340 days old.
  • Not checked by the audit: the other three coherence months, the bootstrap intervals, and experiment 313.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The member-wise route counts the spread twice. The network is trained with the spread input set to zero on one member, and the marginal is then the mixture of 51 member distributions, so the spread enters the forecast twice.
  • The Schaake shuffle's history is partly random for farm E. Farm E has no observed power a year earlier, so its ranks come from random draws, and the shuffle's gain comes from the five farms that have history.
  • The variogram uses pairs up to 6 hours apart at one farm, which misses the gap between one day and the next at night, so it scores the daytime structure only.
  • The a6_* arms have ERA5 rows with a single member. The pretrained network sees no spread there, and the fine-tuning rows are the only ones with a spread.
  • Seed averaging differs between scores. The marginal score averages the quantiles of the seeds, and the coherence scores average the scores of the seeds' paths.
  • The second seed set covers three arms (g0_onepass, a2_member, a5_plain). The other contrasts use three seeds, and their minimum detectable effects run from 0.14% to 2.1%.
  • The trained plant's parameters (tilt, azimuth, scale, and clip) were not logged, so we cannot say whether the network used the plant channel.
  • The A6 arms for wind were not run. Experiment 429's merged code has no pretraining arm, and the manager deferred them.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None so far.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: We test which of four design differences a pooled network for solar farms needs. The Opus design note of experiment 13 proposes one network design for demand, wind, and solar: a mixture density network (MDN) pooled across sites with a learned site embedding, fed the ensemble mean and spread once, and optionally pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS. Each difference between the three forecasters must be justified by an ablation. This experiment is the solar worker's half; the wind worker's half is experiment 429. Here a "farm" is one of the six metered solar farms, labelled A to F.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The four switches are small changes to one network class, and every arm differs from its reference in exactly one switch. The network is experiment 310's MixtureHead: the standardised inputs, two hidden layers of 64, and a three-component Gaussian mixture on the capacity-normalised output. All arms are pooled across the six farms and the six day bands, with experiment 345's 22 input columns (calendar, sun position, ensemble mean and spread of shortwave, beam, diffuse and temperature, the clear-sky index, the lead in hours, and eight further ensemble variables).

  • Member route (A2). A shared encoder (4 channels to 32 to 16) runs on each of the 51 members' shortwave, beam, diffuse, and temperature. The 51 encodings are pooled by mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentile, and joined to the one-pass inputs. The member arm therefore sees everything the one-pass arm sees. All 51 members are used in every training step, which is cheap at this size, so the design note's one-random-member-per-epoch device is not needed.
  • Physics layer (A5). A PyTorch copy of experiment 310's fleet plant adds a power channel (on the member mean for one pass, per member for the member route). "Frozen" fixes tilt 20 degrees (experiment 282 found 15 to 20), azimuth 180 degrees, and a scale fitted by least squares on the training rows; "end to end" also learns tilt, azimuth, scale, and clip. The plain arm adds the clear-sky irradiance as a column so that the arms differ only by the plant channel.
  • Pretraining (A6). Pretrain on the farms' ERA5 and CAMS history before 2024-04-01 (about 153,000 half-hours at five farms; farm E has none), then fine-tune all weights on the ensemble rows with half the learning rate. Columns the history lacks (eight ensemble variables and the spread) are 0 after standardisation, the lead is drawn uniformly from 12 to 252 hours, and every member is the same ERA5 value. One standardiser, fitted on ensemble rows before 2025-08-31, serves every refit of every A6 arm, including the ensemble-only control.
  • Coherent members (A2). NGED's power-flow modelling runs one ensemble member at a time, so the forecast must give 51 member paths that are coherent across time and across the six farms. Four routes give paths. (i) The one-pass forecast with ensemble copula coupling (ECC): the member with the j-th lowest shortwave at a farm and half-hour takes the j-th of 51 quantile levels of that half-hour's forecast. (ii) The same marginals with a Schaake shuffle: the 51 members are ranked in each dimension by the ranks of 51 observed past paths of the same layout (the same farm and offsets from the run, on days within 25 days of the same date one year earlier; a dimension with no history is ranked at random). (iii) The member-wise route: each member is passed alone through the network, which is trained on one randomly drawn member per row per epoch with the spread input set to zero, and path m is the member's quantile function at one level that is fixed for the member across all times and farms (the 51 levels are (j - 0.5) / 51 in a fixed random order). (iv) The independent draw, which permutes the quantile levels at random in each dimension and is the floor. The coherence scores are the energy score and the variogram score of order 0.5 (over same-farm half-hour pairs up to 6 hours apart and same-time pairs across farms) of the 51 paths against the observed path, for the six farms and all leads of one run jointly, and for each day band alone.
  • Per-member quantiles (A2). NGED's proposed deliverable is a 51-member power ensemble in which each member is a quantile forecast (for example the 0.99, 0.95, and 0.90 quantiles). For the member-wise route the experiment therefore also stores each member's own 11 quantiles and scores them two ways: the pooled equal-weight mixture of the 51 members (the marginal forecast, already scored) and each member's quantiles alone against the observation (pinball loss and coverage per level, averaged over members), to show how much of the spread comes from the members and how much from each member's own distribution. Production can afford 51 passes (maintainer, 2026-10-31).
  • Point masses (A7). The head adds two point masses, at zero and at the farm's output ceiling (the 0.995 quantile of its training output, as experiment 310), and truncates the Gaussians to the interval between them. The likelihood is exact, and quantiles invert the truncated mixture.

The stages run in this order, and each uses the winners of the stages before it. G0, then A2, then A6, then A5, then A7. The wind arms of A6 were not run: experiment 429's merged code has no pretraining arm, and the manager deferred them.
