Stage Arms (all three seeds unless stated) Reference G0 g0_onepass, five seeds experiment 345 solar_pooled A2 a2_mean_only (spread dropped), a2_member (pooled encoder), a2_memberwise; paths by ECC, Schaake shuffle, independent draw, member-wise g0_onepass (seeds 0 to 2), ECC A6 a6_ens_only, a6_finetune, a6_pretrain_only (on the A2 winner) a6_ens_only A5 a5_plain, a5_frozen, a5_e2e (on the A2 and A6 winners) a5_plain A7 a7_atoms (on the winners) the same network with the clipped head

docs.title: Pre-registered reading
docs.text:
• G0. Over all bands within 0.5% and in each band within 1.0% of experiment 345's score, five seeds each. Both networks are the same recipe with the same seeds, so the allowed gap is seed and GPU noise.
  • A2. Row set: days 3 to 10. A member arm (pooled encoder or member-wise) is kept if it beats the better of the one-pass and mean-only arms by at least 2% (interval excluding zero). Otherwise one pass is adopted for the marginal forecast. Coherence is read separately: the energy score and variogram score of each route (independent, ECC and Schaake on the one-pass and pooled-encoder marginals, member-wise paths), jointly and per band, with month-block intervals over the 12 months of runs. A route that wins the marginal contrast but is worse than the best route on either coherence score by more than 5% does not advance (the Opus note's proposal).
  • A6. Row set: all bands, and days 6 to 10 separately. Pretraining with fine-tuning is kept if it beats the ensemble-only arm and the ERA5-and-CAMS-only arm by at least 1%.
  • A5. Row set: days 6 to 10 for the gain and day 1 for the harm. A plant arm is kept if it beats a5_plain by at least 1.5% at days 6 to 10 and is within 0.5% at day 1. The end-to-end arm needs to beat the frozen arm by a further 0.5% to be preferred.
  • A7. Row set: all bands, tail metrics. Kept if the coverage of the 0.01 and 0.99 quantiles is closer to 1% and the score and the 0.99 pinball loss are no worse than 0.02 points.

docs.title: Lead range
docs.text: Every contrast is read at days 1 to 10 and, beside it, in the 12 to 36 hour band (day 1). Days 11 to 14 are not scored, because experiment 310's tables stop at day 10 and rebuilding them was judged not worth it for an optional extension.

docs.title: Recipe
docs.text:
• Rows and refits. As experiment 345: training rows have a valid time at least one day before the refit; the last 61 days are the validation set; four quarterly refits from 2025-09; own history only. Monthly refits are not used because the reference forecasts are quarterly.
  • Fit. AdamW, learning rate 2e-3, weight decay 1e-4, 20 epochs, batch 2048, the best epoch by validation likelihood. Seeds 0 to 4 for G0 and 0 to 2 for ablations.
  • Weather at forecast time. Every input is ensemble data of the 00 UTC run, the same as experiment 310. ERA5 and CAMS appear only in pretraining rows, which end before the ensemble store starts. No lagged power enters (experiment 345's solar-only network has none).
  • Reuse. Experiment 345's forecasts are the gate reference and Metered solar farms research default 1's blend (experiment 310) is the absolute reference. Experiment 310's tables are read and never written. This experiment's one-pass arm is fitted here.

docs.title: Compute (as run)
docs.text: About 135 fits: 20 for G0, 36 for A2, 27 for A6, 36 for A5, 12 for A7, plus second seed sets where needed. The smallest network trains in about a minute and the member route in a few minutes on one GPU process under 8 GB with one feeder core, so the whole programme is a few GPU-hours.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
• Plan and code: one fresh Sonnet review before the first fit (leakage, the fit stopping at the refit cutoff, the scoring, row selection, agreement with experiment 345's recipe).
  • Results, write-up numbers, and write-up prose: a fresh Sonnet review each.
  • Unit tests: the PyTorch plant against pvlib and experiment 310's NumPy plant; the head's density and point masses integrate to 1; quantiles stay within bounds.

docs.title: Do idle half-hours at the three metered wind farms look different from genuine low output, and do they follow a weekly maintenance cycle?
docs.text:
Texture separates idle half-hours from genuine low output at Farm B and Farm C, and idle runs at high wind are short except at Farm C. At the same power level, idle readings change by less from one half-hour to the next, and repeat the previous value more often. The level-matched area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) is 0.79 at Farm B and 0.76 at Farm C, so the texture detector D1 stays in the design. At Farm A the two comparison sets share no power level, so texture cannot be tested from power alone. The idle share at high wind is lower on weekday daytimes than at other hours at Farm B and Farm C. A weekday-only result does not settle the whole-farm outage class I2, because maintenance and waits for components can disable turbines for weeks. The run-length test finds idle runs at high wind of up to 5 days at Farm C that low wind cannot explain, and none of 7 days or more at any farm in the stored series. The Farm C result holds at the 1.5-times-cut-in speed only: with the empirical cut-in no run exceeds 44 hours. Verdict: partly supported.

The comparison uses two narrow sets of clear cases and fits nothing. The gate for the whole-farm outage class I2 was changed after the weekday result had been read. We looked at the three metered wind farms (Farm A and Farm C metered in megavolt-amperes, Farm B in megawatts) with no fit. The "sure-idle" set is half-hours with ERA5 100 m wind below 2 m/s and power inside the idle band of experiment 210 (5% to 95% of power at ERA5 wind below 2 m/s, per farm). ERA5 is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts fifth-generation reanalysis, and the cut-in is the wind speed at which turbines start generating. The "sure-generating low-output" set is half-hours with ERA5 wind of at least 6 m/s and power between 3% and 8% of capacity. Both sets are defined by the same ERA5 wind speed that defines the experiment 210 mask, so the test is of texture, not of the mask.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Gate for D1 (texture): best level-matched AUC of a level-free statistic is 0.79 (3-hour rolling standard deviation of first differences, interval 0.75 to 0.83) at Farm B and 0.76 (24-hour centred share of repeated values, 0.71 to 0.80) at Farm C. Both are above 0.65, so D1 is kept. Farm A is untestable: its sure-idle power (0 to 3% of capacity) and sure-generating power (3% to 8%) do not overlap in any 0.5%-of-capacity bin.
  • Level alone separates the sets: unmatched AUCs reach 0.95 (Farm A), 0.93 (Farm B), and 0.85 (Farm C) for level-free statistics, and 1.0, 0.99, and 0.91 for the amplitude statistics. The matched numbers above are the ones that count.
  • Exact zeros and repeats: 43%, 21%, and 43% of sure-idle half-hours are exact zeros at Farm A, B, and C, against none in the sure-generating set (which starts at 3% of capacity). Repeats of the previous value are 36%, 19%, and 33% of sure-idle half-hours and 0.1%, 0.2%, and 1.3% of sure-generating ones.
  • Quantisation step: the smallest non-zero change is 0.005%, 0.011%, and 0.037% of capacity at Farm A, B, and C.
  • Run lengths (I2 gate): with the pre-registered definition (power in the idle band, ERA5 wind above 1.5 times the used cut-in, no gaps), the longest run is 24 hours at Farm A, 28.5 hours at Farm B, and 49 hours at Farm C; 0, 3, and 21 runs exceed 24 hours; none exceeds 7 days. Farm C's longest run is just above the longest spell of ERA5 wind below the cut-in (47.5 hours), a margin of 1.5 hours, and only 1 of its 21 runs over 24 hours exceeds that spell. With the post hoc definition (power at or below the top of the idle band, gaps of up to 3 half-hours), 1, 6, and 81 runs exceed 24 hours. The longest run is 36, 55, and 120.5 hours. The share of high-wind idle half-hours in runs of 1 to 7 days is 6%, 3%, and 19%, and none reaches 7 days. The reference spells with the same gap tolerance are 111, 66, and 66 hours at Farm A, B, and C, so only Farm C's longest post hoc run (120.5 hours) exceeds its reference. With the empirical cut-in as the high-wind speed, no run exceeds 44 hours. So multi-day runs that low wind cannot explain appear at Farm C at the 1.5-times-used-cut-in speed only (marginal under the strict definition, clear under the post hoc one), and not at Farm A or Farm B. No multi-week run is visible in these series.
  • Weekday and hour (secondary check on H2): the idle share of high-wind half-hours on weekday daytimes (08:00 to 17:59 UTC), over the share at other hours, is 1.01 (0.67 to 1.35) at Farm A, 0.77 (0.70 to 0.83) at Farm B, and 0.82 (0.77 to 0.86) at Farm C. The ratio never reaches 1.5, so the weekday cycle gives no support for planned weekday maintenance. This result alone does not settle I2 (see run lengths). With the empirical cut-in of experiment 210 as the high-wind speed the ratios are 1.01, 0.91 (0.55 to 1.42), and 0.72 (0.65 to 1.47), all with intervals that include 1 and none reaching 1.5.
  • Floor by year: the share of exact zeros in the idle floor falls from over 80% in 2019 to 10% in 2026 at Farm A, 7% at Farm C, and 1% at Farm B, and the median floor rises from 0 to about 1.6% (Farm A), 0.7% (Farm B), and 2.5% (Farm C) of capacity. The floor level is not stable across years.
  • Farm B negatives: none before 2020. From 2021 on, 32% to 53% of sure-idle readings are negative. The share is 47% to 61% in the hours 21:00 to 09:59 UTC and 22% to 33% in the hours 12:00 to 18:59, so the negative readings are not a constant offset. The data cannot say why.
  • Farm B against Farm C: at high wind, 10,368 half-hours read idle at both farms, 2,634 only at Farm B, and 20,018 only at Farm C. Of Farm B's idle half-hours at high wind, 80% are also idle at Farm C. A shared ERA5 error or a shared cause (for example a grid event) fits this, and so would an idle band that is wide at Farm C. The data cannot say which.
  • Gallery: up to 60 farm-days per farm (20 sure-idle, 12 at Farm B and 16 at Farm C because fewer days qualify, 20 sure-generating low-output, 20 where the experiment 210 mask and the texture rule disagree), kept private under the experiment's data folder and not published. The disagreement days show flat zero runs at moderate wind that the mask does not cover, and low, noisy readings at low wind inside the mask.
  • Checks: no forecast is scored, so the median-minus-mean, tail, and curtailment checks do not apply. Audit triggers: none fired.

docs.title: Caveats and what the data cannot show
docs.text:
• No outage record. No outage log, availability record, or reactive-power channel exists on disk, so the data cannot say why a half-hour is idle, nor whether the maintainer's reactive-power reading holds. Farm B is metered in megawatts and still has idle half-hours.
  • Window statistics include the half-hour's neighbours. A 24-hour centred window around a sure row can include half-hours outside the set, which dilutes contrast. Constant windows count as autocorrelation 0.
  • Coarse bootstrap. The intervals resample about 8 calendar-year blocks, 2019 and 2026 being partial, and each class-year is capped at 3,000 half-hours.
  • Run lengths depend on the definition. One noisy half-hour breaks a strict run, which shortens runs; the post hoc gap tolerance lengthens them, and both definitions are shown. The data cannot separate a whole-farm outage from an ERA5 error that lasts days, and ERA5's 25 km cell may show high wind while the turbines see calm.
  • The best of 24 statistics scored per farm is quoted, and 17 of the 24 are level-free and gated. The best value is optimistic, though several statistics agree at Farm B (three above 0.77).
  • The high-wind speed is 1.5 times the used cut-in (4.5 m/s at Farm B and Farm C), which is below their empirical cut-ins and dilutes the idle share; the sensitivity run leaves the weekday conclusion unchanged. For run lengths it removes the Farm C result: with the empirical cut-in no run exceeds 44 hours.
  • Sure sets are narrow. Both come from ERA5 wind and a power band, so they cover only the clearest cases; a detector must still be tested on the ambiguous rows.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Build D1 as a level-matched detector, scored within power bins, at Farm B and Farm C, then decide how to test Farm A (its overlap in power is empty on these labels).
  • Decide the I2 class per farm from the run lengths, then test it against any outage record NGED can supply.
  • Look at the disagreement days with the maintainer before the Stage 1 hand labels are drawn.
  • Ask NGED whether a reactive-power channel or an outage log exists, because only that can say why a half-hour is idle.

docs.title: Experiment details
docs.text:
• Code: ml-experiments/00431-wind-idle-data-look/ (e00431_analysis.py, e00431_gallery.py, e00431_runs.py, e00431_charts.py), reading experiment 210's joined.parquet and report.json.
  • Review: one fresh Sonnet code review before the run found a crash in the centred correlation, a level leak that would have passed the gate on power alone, NaN rows dropped in the most idle-like stretches, and an upward bias from folding the AUC; the fixes were applied and the plan was amended before any number was read. The run-length analysis was added after the manager relayed the maintainer's correction, once the weekday result had been read.
  • Cadence, cleaned data, and weather: no fit; the customer-generator series are never flagged by the production cleaning rule; weather is ERA5 100 m wind (research-only, about 5 days late).
  • Data: data/ml-experiments/00431-wind-idle-data-look/ (private).

docs.title: Does scoring the stored wind forecasts against a cleaned-zero target, where the idle half-hours count as zero output, change which forecast ranks best?
docs.text:
Take-home: scoring the idle half-hours as zero output does not change which wind forecast is best, and forcing the forecast to zero below cut-in gains nothing. The zero-below-cut-in arm (experiment 336, x1) lost 0.015 points against raw readings (interval +0.002 to +0.037). Against the cleaned-zero target the same arm ties Wind farms research default 1: the difference is -0.002 points (interval -0.008 to +0.004), because the default already puts its 0.05 quantile at or near zero on 97% of the idle half-hours. The arms with a mixture-density output layer (the mixture-head arms) lead the default by 0.03 to 0.05 points on raw rows, 0.02 on cleaned-zero rows, and 0.23 on masked rows, and every one of those intervals includes zero. The verdict is partly supported: the tie that the hypothesis allowed holds, and the win of at least 0.05 points that the prediction asked for does not.

The question was whether the maintainer's rule changes the ranking of the stored forecasts. The rule is that the forecast says zero where the farm should output zero, and the evaluation never asks the forecast to predict the idle noise. We re-scored 7 stored forecasts on 3 row sets of the same 107,121 half-hours. The ranking hardly moves. The mixture-head arms' lead shrinks because those arms rarely forecast zero on idle half-hours, and the lead disappears when every ERA5-flagged half-hour is scored as zero. Hypothesis H-P (a wind neural network with a physics layer is more robust to the idle noise) is not weakened by this check, and the check cannot support it.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Arm names: "zero below cut-in" is experiment 336's x1. "Head", "head plus rule", and "head on all half-hours" are experiment 339's x1, x2, and x3. "XGBoost on ensemble mean" is experiment 343's M, and "plant plus head" is experiment 347's y2. Scores are the quantile score of experiment 33 (it approximates the continuous ranked probability score) in points of capacity, at true days 1 to 10 with the 3 farms pooled, and intervals resample the 12 test months.

The cleaned-zero row set keeps 65,740 of 66,269 half-hours.

  • Raw: 66,269 half-hours. Masked: 59,861. Cleaned zero: 65,740, which is raw minus the 529 half-hours in outage_suspected runs (the scored year holds 855 of them at all leads).
  • Of the 9,787 low_wind_idle half-hours in the scored year (all leads), 914 (9.3%) had observed power above the farm's idle band (172, 303, and 439 at the 3 farms). Those keep their reading in the cleaned-zero set, and the ERA5-only variant sets all 9,787 to zero.
  • Default scores: raw 10.237, masked 10.752, cleaned zero 10.282, cleaned zero ERA5 10.294.

Zeroing below cut-in ties the default on cleaned zeros and loses a little elsewhere.

  • Zero below cut-in minus default: raw +0.015 (+0.002 to +0.037), masked +0.006 (0.000 to +0.015), cleaned zero -0.002 (-0.008 to +0.004), cleaned zero ERA5 -0.008 (-0.016 to 0.000).
  • Per farm on cleaned zeros: W1 -0.003, W2 -0.009 (-0.017 to -0.001), W3 +0.006 (-0.005 to +0.019). At 12 to 36 hours the pooled value is -0.005 (-0.011 to 0.000).
  • The pre-registered rule reads "cannot tell" for the pooled days 1 to 10 value, so the arm does not "still lose", and H-P is not weakened.

The mixture-head arms' lead depends on the row set and on the label.

Arm minus default Raw Masked Cleaned zero Cleaned zero ERA5 Plant plus head -0.046 -0.234 -0.018 +0.007 Head -0.041 -0.229 -0.017 +0.010 Head plus rule -0.033 -0.224 -0.016 +0.004 Head on all half-hours +0.021 +0.012 +0.028 +0.037 XGBoost on ensemble mean +0.100 +0.081 +0.080 +0.082

Every interval for these rows includes zero. Dropping the mask's rows raises the default's score by 0.515 points and the heads' by about 0.33, which is how the heads' lead grows to 0.23 on the masked rows.

The default forecasts zero on idle half-hours and the mixture heads do not.

  • Share of idle-flagged half-hours (all 107,121 half-hours, all leads) whose 0.05 quantile is at or below 0.5% of capacity: default 0.97, zero below cut-in 0.97, XGBoost on ensemble mean 0.95, head on all half-hours 0.77, head 0.38, plant plus head 0.38, head plus rule 0.35.
  • Observed power falls below the 0.05 quantile on 9.6% to 10.7% of cleaned-zero half-hours for the head, head plus rule, and plant plus head, against 2.1% for the default and 7.1% for the head on all half-hours.
  • The 0.5 quantile is at or near zero on at most 7.2% of idle-flagged half-hours for every arm, so no forecast is a point forecast of zero there.

The mask removes easy half-hours, and the wind speed explains all of the effect.

  • The mask raises the default's score by 0.515 points (kept minus all). Random drops matching farm, month, and hour raise it by 0.12 (5th to 95th percentile 0.10 to 0.14), so all 200 draws fall below the mask. Random drops that also match the wind-speed bin raise it by 0.54 (0.53 to 0.54), so all 200 draws are at or above the mask.
  • The decision rule used the cleaned-zero set only if the mask beats its placebo. The mask beats the calendar placebo and does not beat the wind-matched placebo, so the mask removes easy low-wind half-hours and does not remove hard weather. Arm contrasts on the masked set are therefore comparable with raw contrasts, and absolute masked scores are not.

Zeroing costs most on the half-hours just above cut-in.

  • Conditioned slice (ERA5 speed from cut-in to 1.5 times cut-in, power above the idle band, 810 half-hours, a stress test), minus default: zero below cut-in +0.264 (0.000 to +0.568), head plus rule +0.412 (+0.023 to +0.723), head on all half-hours -0.226 (-0.465 to +0.098).
  • Outcome-free slice (the same speeds, any power, 4,879 half-hours): zero below cut-in +0.085 (+0.004 to +0.193), head +1.28, head plus rule +1.35, plant plus head +1.30 (every interval above +1.0), head on all half-hours -0.080 (-0.296 to +0.157), XGBoost on ensemble mean +0.110.

Tails: no arm is calibrated at the 0.99 quantile. On cleaned zeros the share of observed power above q99 is 1.5% for the default, 1.8% for zero below cut-in, 2.0% for the head, 2.3% for head plus rule, and 1.7% for XGBoost on ensemble mean (nominal 1%). Pinball loss at q99 is 0.595 for the default, 0.616 for zero below cut-in, and 0.625 for the head. The share above q95 is 5.6% to 6.4% for all five.

Ranking. Masked order: plant plus head, head, head plus rule, default, zero below cut-in, head on all half-hours, XGBoost on ensemble mean. Cleaned-zero order: the same, except that zero below cut-in and default swap (a gap of 0.002 to 0.006 points, inside the intervals). On the ERA5-only variant the default ranks above all three head arms. At 12 to 36 hours on cleaned zeros the head arms lead by 0.17 to 0.23 and the interval of every arm but zero below cut-in includes zero.

Pre-registered predictions.

  • P1 (zero below cut-in beats the default by 0.05 or more on cleaned zeros): not met, the arm ties.
  • P2 (the ranking is the same on masked and cleaned-zero rows): met up to one swap inside the intervals. The second clause, that arms with mass at zero move up, is not met: only zero below cut-in moved, by one place, and head plus rule did not.
  • P3 (the mask beats the calendar placebo): met by magnitude (0.515 against 0.14), but the removed half-hours raise the score, and the wind-matched placebo reproduces the whole effect.
  • P4 (the conditioned slice shows zero below cut-in losing, and no forecast differs from the default by more than 0.05 on the outcome-free slice): the first clause holds only at the boundary (lower bound 0.000), and the second fails for zero below cut-in (+0.085), the three head arms with mass away from zero, and XGBoost on ensemble mean (+0.110).

Experiment 429's final quantiles are not stored, so the experiment is not scored. Experiment 429 can report the cleaned-zero row set beside the raw set. It cannot replace the raw set, because the heads' lead on cleaned zeros depends on how the idle half-hours are labelled. Its arms need the same ranking check on the masked and cleaned-zero sets once its quantiles exist.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate: every stored per-row score reproduced to 1e-6. The checked arms are the default, x1 of experiment 336, x1, x2, and x3 of experiment 339, y2 of experiment 347, and M of experiment 343, which was checked against its stored mean score. The experiment 347 arm uses its 5 stored seeds, not the 5-seed mean of quantiles in predictions_y2.parquet.
  • Mask hash (G1, the frozen-mask guard of the plan): sha256 7ab3fe48...5368e4, printed before scoring.
  • Fresh Sonnet reviews: a plan review (it found that low_wind_idle is an ERA5 wind rule), a code review before the first run (it found null-handling crashes and an unchecked arm, all fixed), a results review (it re-derived the default's scores and x1's contrasts from the raw arrays and matched to 6 digits), and a write-up review (it found the lead was overstated, now corrected).
  • Audit triggers: none fires that a re-score of stored forecasts could cause. The cleaned-zero target uses observed power to decide which half-hours become zero. The ERA5-only variant is reported beside it because of that, and the two differ by 0.012 points for the default and 0.014 to 0.038 points for the other arms.
  • Median minus mean forecast per site and the mean-forecast error are not recomputed: the stored forecasts are re-scored on a different target only.
  • Not applicable: monthly refits, saved models, the GPU, avoidable-curtailment cost, and example forecast plots (the brief allows no farm time series to be drawn).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The sample is 3 farms, 2 weather cells, 1 scored year, and 12 month blocks, so intervals are wide. Only the contrasts of zero below cut-in, which differs from the default on few half-hours, are tight.
  • The experiment 210 threshold was fitted on all years, including the scored year. The fit suits a mask for scoring and would leak into a feature.
  • Idle noise at high wind outside runs of 12 hours or more stays in every row set.
  • The headline band is days 1 to 10 of a lead range of 0.5 hours to 15 days. The heads' lead at 12 to 36 hours is larger and is not reduced by cleaned-zero scoring.
  • The conditioned slice selects on the outcome, so it is a stress test and not a gate.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test whether a mixture head with a point mass at zero (experiment 429's censored likelihood) keeps its lead on cleaned zeros. The mixture heads here put little mass at zero, and the other contributors to their losses on idle half-hours are untested.
  • Test an idle detector that does not use wind speed (the texture rules in the wind idle-noise detector design note) with the wind-bin-matched placebo.

docs.title: Plan (as committed before any score)
docs.text: Nothing is fitted. The script reads the stored quantile forecasts of experiments 336, 339, 343, and 347 and the experiment 210 mask, and scores each forecast on three row sets.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
• Forecasts re-scored (seven, all on the same 107,121 rows):
    • the default: Wind farms research default 1 (default.npy of experiments 336, 339, and 343, the same forecast);
    • experiment 336, arm x1: the default with all 11 quantiles set to zero below cut-in;
    • experiment 339, arms x1, x2, and x3: the mixture head, the head plus the idle-floor rule, and the head trained on all half-hours;
    • experiment 343, arm M: the XGBoost model trained on the ensemble mean;
    • experiment 347, arm y2: the physics plant plus the mixture head.
  • Missing: experiment 429's forecasts are not yet stored as final quantiles (only parts/ and models/ exist), so they are not scored here. The script takes a forecast table as input, so the same code scores them once they exist.
  • Idle and outage in the 210 mask: low_wind_idle rows are the idle half-hours (class I1 of the design note), because the flag is set only where ERA5 100 m wind is below cut-in and power lies in the idle band. outage_suspected rows (at least 12 hours in the idle band at ERA5 wind above 1.5 times cut-in) are outages (class I2) and are dropped from the cleaned-zero row set.
  • Guards: G1, the mask file is hashed and its hash is printed before any score. G2, dropped share by month, 1 m/s wind bin, hour of day, and weekday, as a figure of shares. G3, the placebos: random drops with the mask's count in each (farm, month, hour) stratum, and in each (farm, month, hour, wind bin) stratum, 200 draws each. G4, the low-wind slices: ERA5 speed between cut-in and 1.5 times cut-in, with observed power above the farm's idle-band 95% value (chosen on the outcome, as the brief states, so a stress test and not a pass/fail gate) and without that condition. G5, the rank agreement of the arms on the masked and the cleaned-zero row sets.
  • Zero-mass report: for each arm, the share of half-hours whose q05 and whose q50 sit at or below 0.5% of capacity, on idle-flagged and on kept half-hours. A forecast whose 11 quantiles are all 0 scores 0 on a cleaned-zero row, because pinball loss against a zero actual is (1 − τ) times the quantile; against a raw idle floor of 0.3 MVA the same forecast scores τ times 0.3.
  • Standing practices: no model is fitted, so monthly refits, saved boosters, and the GPU do not apply. Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 cut are Primary-substation rules and do not apply to wind farms. Tail pinball loss and coverage at q05, q95, and q99 are reported. Avoidable-curtailment cost is not scored, because no load-shift events are involved. No farm time series is plotted, because the brief allows normalised, aggregated charts only, so the example-forecast and event-plot practices are not followed.
  • Earlier advice followed: reuse stored predictions rather than refit (experiment 336 and 339 rows); score on the same rows in every arm; say plainly that 210's mask uses ERA5 and observed power, so it serves evaluation and training only.

docs.title: Do the six metered solar farms show the wind farms' idle-noise texture when they are not generating?
docs.text:
The six metered solar farms read exact zeros at night, so they do not show the wind farms' idle noise. The question was whether the wind farms' noise while not generating, which the maintainer suspects is reactive power on an MVA meter, also appears at the metered solar farms. The solar farms do not show it. The TimeSeriesMetadata table lists all six farms in MW, not MVA, and 95.8% to 99.9% of night readings (solar elevation below -6 degrees) are exact zeros at five of the six farms (91.8% at Solar B). The wind farms' idle floor in experiment 210 held 19% to 41% exact zeros and a median above zero at the two MVA farms. The result narrows the next step: no solar detector, and no cleaned-zero scoring for solar, unless the outage check below finds a reason.

Solar B meets the pre-registered "the same noise" label, but only through the rule's negative-readings clause, which is a flaw in the rule. For a farm that is nearly all zeros, criteria 1, 2, and 4 pass trivially (zeros count as repeats, zeros lie on any lattice, and the season ratio is 0/0, taken as 1), so criterion 3's clause "at least 5% of night readings negative" alone decides, and Solar B passes it with a lower bound of 5.3%. Separately, and Solar B's 91.8% zeros also satisfy the "not the same" clause (at least 90% zeros). The rule listed "the same noise" first. Solar B's other readings are 8.1% negative (interval's upper end 10.9%), and across all hours of the record its negative readings have a median of -0.010 MW and a minimum of -0.192 MW; its night median is zero. Read post hoc, the pattern is consistent with a small import, for example station load, and is not a floor above zero. The year-by-year negative share moves between 0.1% in 2019 and 15.6% in 2023 (Figure 2), which does not by itself establish either reading. Solar E shows the same pattern at 4.1% negative.

Idle runs on clear days are short, except at Solar D and Solar E. Of the half-hours with CAMS clear-sky index at least 0.7 between 10:00 and 15:00, 2.8% to 14.4% read near the night floor (3.2% at Solar F). Whole idle days form runs of at most 4 days at Solar A, B, C, and F, 24 days at Solar D, and 17 days at Solar E. No farm has a run longer than 24 days, and no farm has the pre-registered outage class (at least 50% of idle half-hours in runs over 24 hours; the highest share is 41.6%, at Solar E). At every farm except Solar E, most idle half-hours lie outside whole idle days. Runs over 7 days hold 29.3% of Solar E's idle half-hours and 6.9% of Solar D's.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Prediction. Night median under 0.1% of capacity and non-zero repeats under 20%: holds at all six farms (prediction asked for five).
  • Pre-registered labels. Solar A, C, D, E, and F "not the same"; Solar B "the same noise" (flawed rule, above). Overall verdict supported (five or more "not the same").
  • Texture statistics (summary.csv): non-zero repeats are 0.01% to 0.14% of night readings. The quantisation step is 0.001 MW at three farms and 0.011 to 0.035 MW at the other three (private table), so each farm reports on the meter's own lattice, zero included. Lag-1 autocorrelation of night first differences is -0.51 to -0.03. Median rolling standard deviation of first differences is zero at every farm.
  • Season. Summer and winter night medians are both zero at every farm, so the season criterion holds trivially (season.csv). Zero shares differ by under 1 point between seasons.
  • Flags. The cleaning table flags 0 night half-hours at these six customer-metered series. The night statistics use all rows.
  • Share touched. Where the label was "the same noise" (Solar B), night half-hours are 39.3% of all half-hours and 71.9% of half-hours with the sun up; the negative ones are 8.1% of those.
  • Daytime idle (daytime_runs.csv, daytime_run_bins.csv): a day needs at least 3 qualifying half-hours. The run test sees only whole idle days; partial-day idling is counted in the idle share and not in a run.
  • Agreement between farms (pair_agreement.csv): of the four pairs within 10 km, Solar A and Solar C share 5 idle days of 20 on either (Jaccard 0.25) and Solar B and Solar D share 3 of 21 (0.14); Solar A with Solar E, and Solar C with Solar E, share none. Idle days are mostly farm-specific, not weather.
  • Weekday profile (daytime_weekday_hour.csv): a secondary table; the weekday table decides nothing.
  • What the data cannot show. No MVAr channel, outage log, or curtailment record exists, so idle days cannot be told from curtailment or a station fault. CAMS clear-sky index is hourly and satellite-derived, so cloud inside the hour can make a "clear" half-hour dark. Rolling statistics are degenerate when readings are all zero. Gallery PNGs (20 farm-days per farm) are in the private data folder, not published.
  • Audit triggers: the result contradicts nothing it predicted; the one flawed label (Solar B) is reported as pre-registered and read post hoc. No control or leave-one-out check applies.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Check Solar D's 24-day and Solar E's 17-day idle runs against NGED's records for outages or export limits.
  • Decide Solar B's small negative readings with NGED (station import), only if the solar scores show a farm-level bias at night.

docs.title: Which re-ordering of the stored demand forecast's 51 sample paths, by ensemble member rank or by past observed paths, makes the paths coherent across the 16 Primaries and across leads?
docs.text:
Re-ordering the 51 values by temperature or by past paths does not make the paths clearly more coherent overall, because ordering by temperature helps across leads and hurts across Primaries. The stored forecast of experiment 425's arm A gives 11 quantiles per Primary substation (a substation feeding the distribution network from the transmission network) and half-hour. This experiment drew 51 values from them and assigned the values to 51 sample paths in five ways, then scored how well the paths match the observed dependence, with no fit. The scores are in points of capacity, meaning percentage points of each Primary's effective capacity. The five orderings are defined in the first bullet below. The joint variogram score (the gating block; the variogram score penalises wrong differences between pairs of half-hours or Primaries) moved by 1% or less between independent draws, temperature ranks, shortwave ranks, and the Schaake shuffle. It moved by 11.4% for the comonotone ordering, so the score can see dependence. The Schaake shuffle did at least as well as temperature ranks (the second claim of the hypothesis), but neither beat independent draws by the 5% margin. The registered verdict is not supported: P2, P3, and P4 failed and P1 failed in its second half.

  • Arms. ECC-T (ensemble copula coupling: the coldest member gets the highest value), ECC-SW (the darkest member gets the highest value), SCH (the Schaake shuffle: the values follow the ranks of the 51 past observed paths nearest in day of year), IND (independent draws), and CO (comonotone: every Primary and lead takes the same rank, the strongest dependence possible). The energy score is the other coherence score, the distance of the paths from the observation. The signed-MW six are the Primaries whose meters report signed megawatts, the MVA-only eight report only apparent power, and D15 and D18 are the two with short histories. Every arm holds the same 51 values at each Primary, half-hour, and run.
  • Rows. 12 monthly folds (2025-07 to 2026-06), 16 Primaries, daily runs at 09:00 UTC, scored on the half-hours with a cleaned actual (4,004,653 rows); 1,179 flagged exact-zero actuals are dropped from the whole scoring cache. Forecast: experiment 425's arm A, seeds 0 to 4 averaged in quantile space and widened by 1.15, stored in data/ml-experiments/00425-best-mdn-architecture-assembly-with-ablations/work/seed_preds/A/. Code reused by copying: experiments 87, 377, and 381 (scoring context); the page's scripts import those three folders.
  • Joint variogram score, days 1 to 10 (mean of 12 folds, points of capacity): IND 1.7657, ECC-T 1.7752, ECC-SW 1.7679, SCH 1.7669, CO 1.9667. Against IND: ECC-T +0.5% (+0.3% to +0.8%), SCH +0.1% (-0.3% to +0.5%), CO +11.4% (+10.4% to +12.2%). At 12 to 36 hours the joint contrasts were +0.7% (-0.0% to +1.4%) for ECC-T, -0.4% (-1.0% to +0.1%) for SCH, and +7.0% (+5.9% to +7.9%) for CO. No ordering other than CO moves the joint score by 5%.
  • Across Primaries (spatial), days 1 to 10: IND 1.6045, ECC-T 1.7115, ECC-SW 1.6694, SCH 1.5984, CO 1.7440. ECC-T against IND +6.7% (+4.7% to +9.1%; the interval straddles +5%). SCH against IND -0.4% (-1.7% to +1.0%); SCH against ECC-T -6.6% (-7.6% to -5.5%). The spatial block is secondary and has no verdict. The energy score agrees (ECC-T +6.2%, +5.5% to +6.8%).
  • Across leads (temporal), days 1 to 10: IND 1.6335, ECC-T 1.6050, ECC-SW 1.6268, SCH 1.5757, CO 2.1539. ECC-T -1.7% (-2.8% to -0.7%), SCH -3.5% (-6.3% to -0.9%), and neither reaches the margin. At 12 to 36 hours: IND 1.3914, ECC-T 1.2122, ECC-SW 1.3278, SCH 1.1778; ECC-T -12.9% (-17.0% to -9.0%), SCH -15.3% (-20.9% to -9.2%), SCH against ECC-T -2.8% (-5.7% to +0.2%).
  • Shortwave ranks (C4). ECC-SW against ECC-T: -0.4% (-0.6% to -0.2%) jointly, -2.5% (-4.3% to -1.1%) across Primaries, and +1.4% (+0.5% to +2.3%) across leads at days 1 to 10. In the half-hours scored as daylight, ECC-SW beat ECC-T by -0.2% (-0.7% to +0.2%) across Primaries and -0.8% (-1.6% to +0.0%) across leads. In cold-night half-hours across Primaries ECC-SW beat ECC-T by -6.4% (-8.4% to -3.6%), the opposite of P4, because the radiation is zero at night and the ranks there are random, which is independent draws.
  • Marginal check. The 51 values give the same CRPS for every ordering, so the marginal contrast is zero by construction and the 0.03-point margin applies only in step 2. The CRPS of the 51 values was 3.597, 4.608, and 10.604 at the signed-MW six, the MVA-only eight, and D15 and D18 (days 1 to 10), against 2.829, 3.598, and 8.431 from experiment 425's 11-level estimator, so the second half of P1 failed. The gap is the estimator: on one run (2025-10, fourth run) the same 11 quantiles scored 3.487 with the 11-level formula and 4.558 with 51 even levels (e00434_estimator_check.py). The two numbers are not comparable, and the page makes no claim about discretisation loss beyond that.
  • Tails. The share of actuals above the largest of the 51 values (days 1 to 10) was 2.43%, 0.90%, and 3.66% at the signed-MW six, the MVA-only eight, and D15 and D18; below the smallest it was 0.70%, 0.69%, and 0.30% (a calibrated 51-value ensemble gives 1.92% each way). The ordering does not change these shares.
  • Slices. The cold-night slice has actuals in only 5 to 7 of the 12 folds (the other months have no cold nights), so those contrasts are interim. The spatial daylight and cold-night slices keep the half-hours where at least half of the Primaries with an actual are flagged; the temporal slices use each Primary's own flags. Daylight is the local mid-day band, not the sun's elevation.
  • Caveats. The 2026-06 fold has 29 or 30 runs in some blocks instead of 30, because the actuals end on 2026-07-01 and a late-June run's vector loses components past that date; every arm has the same rows in each block. The marginal means and tail shares are taken per Primary over all its rows, then averaged within the group. The Schaake pool starts on 2025-03-01 (so that D15 and D18 have data), holds 89 to 346 dates per run, and uses the 51 dates nearest in day of year, which are mostly consecutive days. Experiment 425 gave the 2025-07 fold only March to mid-June dates. A past path of 14.6 days overlaps its neighbours, so the 51 paths are less varied than 51 independent years would be. The Primaries are scored together, not by group. The temperature sign (colder member, higher demand) was fixed in the plan and could not be checked against an observation per member. No per-member quantiles exist in the stored forecasts: arm A ran one pass on the ensemble mean and spread, so the member-wise comparison is not scored here.
  • Checks. No model was fitted, so median-minus-mean and mean-error checks do not apply. Every arm was verified to hold the same 51 values at every run (the script stops otherwise), and the score code matches a brute-force version on random inputs. One planned check failed: the second half of P1, which the estimator check explains.
  • What to try next (the manager decides). A step 2 that runs the 51 members through the neural network could compare it against SCH and ECC-T on the spatial and temporal variogram scores, because the joint score cannot separate them. A longer Schaake pool would need Primary data from before 2025-03-01 for D15 and D18, or the pool could use the 14 Primaries with long histories.
  • Problems caused by the move to the nged-ml-research repository. None.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet plan review (10 findings; the tails, verdict rules, pool, ties, missing-actuals rule, and scaling were added to the plan), one Sonnet code review before the first run (no score-changing bugs; NaN and permutation checks added, wording of the spatial slice and n_dim documented). Results and write-up reviews: see the pull request.

docs.title: Do simple input bundles that did not help XGBoost (thermal lag, solar gain, look-ahead, and calendar, tariff, and national signals) lower the error of the pooled mixture density network?
docs.text: This experiment tests, on four folds, whether windows of weather and a few calendar and national signals lower the error of the pooled neural network that experiments 397 to 425 built. The network predicts 11 quantiles of Primary substation demand from the ECMWF ensemble mean and spread at one valid time. Experiment 419 gave it a centred daily mean of shortwave and found -0.012 (-0.043 to +0.013), one sixth of its minimum detectable effect. Trailing and forward windows of temperature and shortwave were never given to the neural network, although the maintainer asked for them on 2026-10-31.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Reference. R and A of experiment 425: the pooled plain network with the 8-wide Primary embedding, 3 Gaussian components, setting g09, and the ensemble mean and spread inputs, trained on ensemble rows only (R) or pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS rows and fine-tuned at a learning rate of 2e-4 (A). Same rows, the D15 and D18 start cut at 2025-03-01, the flagged exact-zero drop, held-out weeks, row weights, 1.15 widening, and monthly refits. The stored seeds 0 to 2 of both arms on the four screen folds are the controls. A check (e00437_fit.py check) proves that a fold built here without extra columns equals experiment 425's fold, bit for bit.
  • Arms. Each arm appends columns to the 46 inputs and changes nothing else. Bundles:
    • T, thermal lag (8 columns). Trailing means of the ensemble-mean temperature over 3, 6, and 24 hours; the temperature change over 3 and 6 hours; the minimum and maximum over the local day of the valid time; and the days since the trailing 24-hour mean last exceeded 5 degrees C, capped at 10.
    • S, solar gain (6 columns). Trailing means of the ensemble-mean shortwave over 3, 6, and 24 hours; the 3-hour change in the clear-sky index (shortwave over Haurwitz clear-sky shortwave, held at its last daylight value overnight; the helper of experiment 396 arm W7); and the realised CAMS irradiance of the last complete UTC day before the origin (its mean in W/m2 and its ratio to CAMS clear-sky). CAMS publishes the previous day at midnight UTC, so production can read both.
    • F, look-ahead (6 columns). Forward means of ensemble-mean temperature and shortwave over the 6 and 24 hours after the valid time, taken from the same run only, and the share of each window the run covers (windows are truncated at the end of the 14-day horizon).
    • C, calendar, tariff, and national signals (14 columns). The Economy 7 step as a UTC half-hour indicator and that indicator times degrees below 15.5 C; five Lincolnshire school-term columns from experiment 11's calendar (term flag; signed days to the nearest term start and end; signed days from the year's first working day; a window flag); and seven signals of the local day before the origin: the mean, maximum, and 16:00 to 19:00 mean of the Elexon market index price, a Demand Flexibility Service flag, and the day's mean national demand, embedded solar, and embedded wind (NESO historic demand). All 16 Primaries lie at 52.9 to 53.3 degrees N, 0.2 degrees W to 0.3 degrees E, inside the box that experiment 11 found to be Lincolnshire, so one county's calendar applies to every Primary.
  • Pretrained form. T, S, and F are also run as T_pre, S_pre, and F_pre: pretrained on experiment 418's ERA5-and-CAMS pseudo-run rows with the same columns computed from the dense weather, then fine-tuned on ensemble rows at 2e-4. C has no pretraining form, because the pretraining rows carry no school or national columns. A pretrained network is fitted for each bundle, fold, and seed, and cannot be shared across folds: the pretraining rows end 3.5 hours before each fold's refit, so a network pretrained for a later fold has seen the earlier fold's test month.
  • Window construction. A trailing window ends at the valid time. For half-hours at or before the forecast origin (09:00 UTC) the series holds the ensemble mean of the previous run that covers them (leads of about 9 to 33 hours); after the origin it holds this run's own ensemble mean. ERA5 is not used, because it arrives about 5 days late and a column built from it could not be served. e00437_features.py check rebuilds sample runs with every later run deleted and requires identical columns. In the pretrained form the windows come from the dense ERA5-and-CAMS series, which is the same stand-in the pretraining rows use for the valid-time weather.
  • Known mismatch in the pretrained form. check-pretraining printed each column's standardised mean and spread in the pretraining rows and the ensemble rows for the 2026-01 fold. The weather windows agree to within 0.25 standard deviations in the mean and 0.07 in the spread, except csi_change_3h, whose spread is 2.6 in the pretraining rows against 0.9 in the ensemble rows. CAMS irradiance changes more over 3 hours than the mean of 51 ensemble members does, the same smoothing gap that affects the shortwave input itself. The write-up reports it as a caveat for S_pre.
  • Dismantling. A bundle that advances is split into halves and refitted in the same form: T_means/T_rest, S_means/S_rest, F_temperature/F_shortwave, and for C C_tariff/C_school/C_national. A combination of the winning bundles (T+S+F, with or without C) is fitted once at least two bundles advance. These are descriptive.
  • Fits and compute. 4 bundles by 4 folds by 3 seeds is 48 ensemble-only fits (about 75 seconds each including the forecast) and 36 pretrained fits (about 55 seconds of pretraining and 40 of fine-tuning each, plus a pretraining-row build of about 2 minutes per fold and bundle). That is about 1.0 plus 1.8 GPU-hours before dismantling, and up to 2 more GPU-hours for the halves and the combination. One GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, 8 GB of host memory, one BLAS thread.
  • Standing practices followed. Monthly refits; cleaned data (flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped, counts printed per fold); the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01; every fitted network saved under work/models/; stored controls reused; tails, the avoidable-curtailment cost, and the example forecasts reported; four-fold screen with every number labelled interim.

docs.title: Caveats registered before the fits
docs.text:
• Window seam at the origin. The ensemble-mean summaries hold no half-hour at or before the run's own origin, so half-hours between 00:00 and 09:00 on the origin day come from the previous run (leads of about 9 to 33 hours). Trailing windows therefore mix two runs at 09:00.
  • T is partly a look-ahead bundle. The daily minimum and maximum temperature use the later hours of the valid time's local day, which the run already forecasts. F isolates pure look-ahead.
  • Publication latency of the previous-day signals. The CAMS, Elexon price, and NESO demand columns use the whole local or UTC day before the origin date. The brief states that CAMS arrives at midnight UTC; the latency of the Elexon and NESO files at 09:00 UTC was not measured, and the training values are the final revised ones. The write-up states both as open points for serving.
  • Forward windows in the pretrained form come from ERA5 and CAMS, which do not degrade with lead, while the ensemble-mean forward windows do. The write-up reports this as a caveat for F_pre.
  • Economy 7 is on the UTC clock, as the brief and experiments 121, 137, and 281 define it. The protocol's economy_7_step slice is on local half-hours, so during British Summer Time the two differ by one hour. The write-up reports C on that slice and states the offset.
  • Bundle C has no pretrained form. The brief asks for the weather bundles in both forms; the pretraining rows hold no school or national columns, so C runs ensemble-only.
  • No summer fold. The four folds are autumn, Christmas, winter, and spring; 2026-06 is not included, so a solar-gain effect in summer cannot show.
  • Data searched for bundle C. On disk and used: Lincolnshire County Council term dates (experiment 11, 2021-22 to 2025-26), Elexon market index prices (p3-price-download), NESO historic demand and embedded generation (experiment 185), and Demand Flexibility Service requirements (experiment 177). A school calendar for another county is not needed, because all 16 Primaries lie in Lincolnshire. No download is made.
  • Reported beside CRPS: the 12-to-36-hour band, tail calibration per group and per Primary, the cold winter night slice, the avoidable-curtailment cost, and the dropped half-hours per fold. Load-shift plots and load-shift row sets do not apply. Experiment 396 arm W7 has no result yet; the write-up cites it if it lands.
  • Process, in order. Draft pull request; plan review (fresh Sonnet); code review (fresh Sonnet) before the first fit; fits; results review with the audit triggers; write-up; prose review.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
No bundle lowered the CRPS by the registered bar, so no dismantling or confirmation run is planned. The best arms lowered the CRPS at only one group, by less than 0.03 points, in 2 of 4 folds. The next step is to leave these bundles out of the pooled plain network and, if the question returns, to test the thermal-lag bundle T on more folds.

Arm key. R is the ensemble-only pooled plain network, and A is its pretrained form; both are the controls. T adds thermal-lag columns, S solar-gain columns, F look-ahead columns, and C calendar, tariff, and national-signal columns (C_tariff adds only the 2 tariff columns of C). A _pre suffix marks the pretrained form of a bundle, whose control is A. "The six" and "the eight" are the 6 signed-MW Primaries and the 8 MVA-only Primaries.

docs.title: Contrasts
docs.text:
CRPS at days 1 to 10 in points of capacity, four monthly folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03), seeds 0 to 2. A positive difference means the arm is worse than its control. Intervals are the descriptive month-block bootstrap at the 99.69% level, which with four blocks spans the fold range; the decision rests on the fold counts.

Arm (control) Signed-MW six MVA-only eight Verdict T (R) +0.016 (-0.078 to +0.081) -0.022 (-0.071 to +0.007) 2 of 4 folds at the eight S (R) +0.043 (-0.037 to +0.136) +0.002 (-0.069 to +0.099) tail harm at q95 C (R) +0.059 (-0.054 to +0.163) +0.038 (-0.057 to +0.170) worse C_tariff (R) +0.047 (+0.005 to +0.165) +0.021 (-0.041 to +0.045) worse F (R) +0.042 (-0.002 to +0.086) -0.000 (-0.047 to +0.049) no change T_pre (A) +0.025 (-0.036 to +0.089) -0.029 (-0.094 to +0.015) 2 of 4 folds at the eight S_pre (A) -0.016 (-0.086 to +0.078) +0.011 (-0.115 to +0.107) below the bar F_pre (A) +0.026 (-0.041 to +0.084) +0.020 (-0.002 to +0.036) tail harm at q95

Controls: R scores 3.404 and A 3.341 at the six, 3.917 and 3.764 at the eight. The group of Primaries D15 and D18 is report-only; every arm except T_pre (-0.176) is worse than its control there, by 0.14 to 0.66 points.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (solar gain S helps most on cold sunny days) is not supported. S was worse than R on cold sunny days (+0.308 at the six) and better on cold overcast days (-0.236), the opposite order.
  • P2 (thermal lag T helps at both groups, most on cold winter nights) is not supported. T was worse at the six (+0.016). The small gain of T at the eight came from two folds, 2025-12 (-0.071) and 2026-01 (-0.025); 7 of 8 Primaries improved.
  • P3 (look-ahead F helps at the eight) is not supported. F changed the CRPS at the eight by -0.000.
  • P4 (calendar, tariff, and national signals C help on the Economy 7 step) is not supported. C was worse on that slice at the six (2.985 against 2.805 for R).
  • P5 (the pretrained form gains at least as much over its control) is not supported. For each bundle, the gain over the control of the pretrained form beat that of the ensemble-only form at one group and lost at the other. The gain of S_pre over A beat the gain of S over R by 0.059 at the six and lost by 0.009 at the eight. For F_pre against F, the figures are 0.016 better at the six and 0.020 worse at the eight. For T_pre against T, they are 0.009 worse at the six and 0.007 better at the eight.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Fold-by-fold differences, per-Primary CRPS, tails, and the cold-night, sunny, Economy 7, and cold sunny-versus-overcast slices are in the figures below; the slice intervals are not shown because few half-hours (769 and 911 on cold overcast days) make them unreliable.
  • A fresh reviewer re-derived the pooled CRPS of R, A, T, and S_pre from the raw forecast files and matched the scorer to three decimals. The median-error and CRPS contrasts agree in sign in all 16 arm-and-group pairs. Leaving out any one Primary flips no verdict.
  • The new columns are not degenerate: their standardised spread is near 1 and the first layer of the neural network uses them. The ensemble-only fold without extra columns equals experiment 425's fold bit for bit.
  • C_tariff (2 columns) beat C (which contains them) by 0.012 at the six. Both differences from the control are inside the noise.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The screen is too coarse to show "no effect". The minimum detectable effect is 0.064 points against R and 0.045 against A, which is 1.5 to 2 times the 0.03 bar, and fold-to-fold differences swing by more than the bar.
  • The four folds hold no summer month, so the second example is spring and S cannot be judged in summer.
  • The hyperparameters were tuned at 46 inputs and reused at 48 to 60. Extra inputs at fixed capacity may explain the worse scores of C and S, and a bundle might help with another setting.
  • The scorer does not compute P1 and P4 as single numbers, and it pairs by fold, not by fold and seed. The slice contrasts above were read by hand.
  • The pretraining mismatch for csi_change_3h registered above applies to S_pre.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Test bundle T on more folds, since it is the only bundle that lowered the CRPS at the eight with both controls (R and A).

docs.title: Data used and where it lives
docs.text:
• Data. The cleaned NGED Primary-substation power series, ECMWF ensemble forecasts, ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather for the pretrained arms, and the on-disk school, price, and national-demand series for bundle C.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00437-neural-demand-thermal-lag-solar-gain-and-tariff-feature-bundles/.
  • Saved networks and forecasts. $DATA_PATH_INTERNAL/ml-experiments/00437-neural-demand-thermal-lag-solar-gain-and-tariff-feature-bundles/work/.

docs.title: Background for experiment workers
docs.text: Read this page, and the pages it links, before you plan an experiment. The pages state what earlier experiments established about the data sets and about the scoring rules, in short bullets, and link the page that owns each fact. The pages exist because several mistakes that cost an experiment a re-run were facts that an earlier experiment had already found and filed on a page the planner did not open.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. This page: the reading order and the update rule.
  2. NGED power telemetry: series, units, tables, timestamps.
  3. Weather inputs by product: which weather exists when.
  4. Row sets and scoring: row sets, metric, intervals, gating.
  5. Substation information fields: metadata, hierarchy, capacity.
  6. Metered generators and anonymisation: farms, caps, labels.
  7. Market and other data: prices, PV_Live, DFS, null results.
  8. Problems and the best forecast: baselines, best guess, scores.
  9. Adopted and open questions: what is settled, who owns the rest.
  10. Data processing: steps every experiment applies to the data.
  11. Glossary: terms the experiment pages use without defining.

The reference page What is on disk says where each data set sits under data/ and how to read it.

docs.title: Three facts that have cost experiments time
docs.text:
• The TimeSeriesMetadata table has 33 rows, and 32 series carry data. Count 32 series; do not change 32 to 33 (NGED power telemetry).
  • ERA5 reaches the forecast about 5 days late. Any ERA5 value used at a lag time is a ceiling. Name the weather source at lag times in every write-up (weather inputs).
  • Read power through studies.power.scan_power. The raw table holds rows that cleaning flags (NGED power telemetry).

docs.title: Update rule
docs.text:
• The experiment that learns or overturns a fact about the data fixes the page. Edit the bullet in place so that the page describes the present, and change its "last checked" line.
  • Add or correct at most five bullets per experiment. Write the bullet where a planner would look first, and link the experiment or page that owns the evidence. If nothing changed, write "background: no change" in the pull request body. The merger checks the pull request body for the list of changed bullets or for that sentence.
  • End every factual bullet with an evidence tag in the form (exp 179; 6 farms, one year; provisional): the experiment ids, the scope of the evidence, and a status of established, provisional, or overturned by N. A bullet about code or disk layout says (code) or (disk). A bullet that digests a linked docs page says (docs), and that page owns the evidence. A bullet whose evidence nobody has traced says (unchecked).
  • Mark a bullet established only when it states a count or a definition, or when a second experiment or row set reproduced the finding. Every other bullet is provisional.
  • Check a tag before you rely on it. Open the result.md of each cited experiment and confirm that the experiment supports the claim, that the scope matches, and that the status fits. Replace (unchecked) with a traced tag whenever you find the owning source.
  • A later experiment may overturn a bullet. The overturning experiment changes the status in the tag to overturned by N, where N is its id, and rewrites the bullet to state the present fact.
  • Do not copy a rule from a page that owns it. Link the owner page instead.

Last checked against experiment 321.

docs.title: Adopted and open questions
docs.text: No experiment result is adopted in production, a set of results are candidates for the next model release, and each open question belongs to one theme. This page gives one line per item and links the theme that owns it. A planner checks here before proposing an experiment that a theme already holds as settled or planned. Evidence tags follow the update rule.

docs.title: Adopted
docs.text: • Nothing is adopted. The release log lists no numbered model release, and no result.md carries production_status: adopted (model releases) (docs).

docs.title: Candidates for the next release
docs.text:
• Primaries and supply points: weekly refits, and a five-member blend at Primaries (experiment 87). Owner: production reference and best guess (docs).
  • Retraining: weekly refitting without the 14-day correction (experiments 34, 48, 81). It holds at 16 Primaries on two sets of runs, but 3 series carry much of the gain. Owner: retraining and training history (exp 34, 48, 81; 16 Primaries; provisional).
  • Solar and wind farms: the pooled mixture over ensemble members, the solar spread factor, and the wind power-curve base margin (experiments 2, 16, 20). Owner: calibration and uncertainty (docs).
  • Solar offset: a forecast of the unmetered solar output as an XGBoost base margin at Primaries with a clean capacity estimate (experiments 64, 78). Owner: solar disaggregation (docs).
  • Physics-based demand model: the convex model with a Kalman filter (experiment 111), a recent-error correction recipe (experiment 155), and a correction neural network with a two-number solar summary (experiment 220). Owner: differentiable physics: forecast engine (docs).

docs.title: Open questions by theme
docs.text:
• Do the spread factor, the blend, and the solar offset hold on a second validation year? The first year chose their settings. Owner: production reference and best guess (docs).
  • Which training source suits solar and wind farms, the ERA5-trained mixture or the ensemble's own history? Needs more than 6 solar and 3 wind farms. Owner: production reference and best guess (docs).
  • Does weekly refitting beat the stack on an unscored year and with the full ensemble, and why do older training years score worse? Owner: retraining and training history (docs).
  • Do old years of history help the physics-based demand model? The answer changed sign between two scored years. Owner: differentiable physics: long history and drift (docs).
  • Does one model pooled across Primaries match a model per substation, and does pooling hold at hundreds of series? Owners: hierarchy and pooling and differentiable physics: pooling across substations (docs).
  • Does a calibrator that sees recent power help solar and wind farms, and does a missing-lag flag widen the band where a lag is missing? Owner: calibration and uncertainty (docs).
  • Does lagged power help once the 14-day correction is in place? No experiment has combined them. Owner: lagged power and error correction (docs).
  • Does the live Met Office UKV feed give wind farms the gain the research archive did? Owners: generator forecasting and weather products and blending (docs).
  • Does a better sunshine forecast close the gap to the true-sunshine oracle? Owner: solar disaggregation (docs).
  • Which extra inputs help Primary demand beyond the calendar and solar set? A heating term gave 0.14 points in cold hours on one winter, under its 0.3 target. Owner: demand inputs (docs).
  • Does any forecast curtail less than another once about 2,500 series are scored, and are the forecast tails too narrow in general? Owner: curtailment cost (docs).
  • What physical plant reproduces each metered solar farm's output, and how much rooftop solar sits behind each substation? Owners: metered solar farms and differentiable physics: embedded generation (docs).
  • Does the physics-based demand model, driven by ensemble weather, forecast Primary demand up to 7 days ahead as well as BG2? Experiment 111 could not tell them apart. Owner: differentiable physics: forecast engine (exp 111; 5 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • How should the physics-based demand model combine its daily profile with holiday, heating, and solar terms? Owner: differentiable physics: demand, calendar and weather (docs).

Last checked against experiment 225.

docs.title: Market and other data
docs.text: Experiments hold public price, demand, solar, and carbon data, and no experiment has yet found a source that improved a forecast of NGED's series by more than the experiment's decision threshold. This page lists each source, what it is for, when its values become known, and where it sits on disk. The price series are described in full on the GB price data page and in the data sources page.

docs.title: What each source is for
docs.text:
Source Folder under data/studies/downloads/market/ What it is Known when Imbalance system price elexon_system_prices Price paid for energy short or long in a half-hour About 19 minutes after the period ends Market index price elexon_mid_apx Short-term exchange price, half-hourly During the half-hour Day-ahead price neso_n2ex_day_ahead Hourly auction price The morning before delivery Demand outturn, generation by fuel elexon_demand_outturn, elexon_fuelhh National demand and generation Demand: about 30 minutes after the half-hour; generation: at publish_time Demand and wind forecasts elexon_ndf, elexon_tsdf, elexon_windfor National forecasts, every publication kept At publish_time Frequency elexon_frequency 15-second values and a half-hourly summary Not checked Bid, offer, and notification data elexon_bod, elexon_boalf, elexon_pn, elexon_mels Per Balancing Mechanism Unit Within minutes, for gate-closed periods Carbon intensity carbon_intensity National forecast and actual, grams per kWh Forecast up to 2 days ahead PV_Live pv_live, pv_live_gsp Sheffield Solar's estimate of solar generation Revised after first publication; updated_at gives the last revision Octopus Agile octopus_agile_east_midlands Half-hourly import tariff, East Midlands The afternoon before the delivery day

The "known when" column digests the publication table and the folders' READMEs (docs, disk). Nothing we hold says when the frequency series is published.

docs.title: Timestamps and coverage
docs.text:
• The market tables mark the start of each period, in UTC, whereas the NGED power feed marks the end of each half-hour. Shift one side by 30 minutes before joining (data sources; docs).
  • PV_Live labels each half-hour by its end. The stored time column is PV_Live's datetime_gmt minus 30 minutes (disk).
  • Most market folders cover one year, 2025-09-01 to 2026-09-30. The two exceptions are pv_live_gsp, which runs from 2019-01-01 to 2026-10-14 for the Walpole and Bicker Fen grid supply points, and octopus_agile_east_midlands, which runs from 2025-08-31 to 2026-09-01 (disk).
  • Experiments 177 and 185 keep the system prices for longer spans in their own public/ folders, under data/ml-experiments/00185-*/public/system_prices (disk).
  • The demand flexibility service (DFS) has no page of its own. The NESO service-requirement archive ends on 2026-03-27 and is stored as dfs_service_requirement.csv under data/ml-experiments/00177-*/public/ (exp 185; 1,231 days with a record; disk).
  • Each licence's attribution wording applies wherever the data is shown (docs).
  • Elexon's indicated demand and generation reach at most 42 hours ahead, and the study found no table that maps their regions to NGED's licence areas, so neither is a ready input (study; docs).

docs.title: Price features tried
docs.text:
• A price at the target half-hour lowered the pooled error by 0.52 points of capacity in the selection year and 0.18 in the confirmation year (interval included zero), and a price from another week matched about 0.45 of the 0.52 (exp 15; pooled series, two years; provisional).
  • Lagged prices gave no gain that survived the confirmation year. A shuffled price from another week reproduced most of the selection-year gain at the one battery-affected substation (exp 10; 2 listed substations, two years; provisional).
  • Adding price changes to the price level lowered the error by 0.037 and 0.050 points of capacity, and by 0.039 and 0.047 against changes taken from another week. The verdict was small gain, under the 0.1-point threshold, and the demand-inputs theme does not adopt it (exp 25; Primaries, two years; provisional). See the demand inputs theme.
  • National system price, DFS events, national demand, wind, solar, and interconnector flow each explain under 1% of the day-to-day variation in the best-guess forecast's loss. Giving the Kalman filter the signal in hindsight made the score slightly worse (exp 185; 5 substations, 1,683 substation-days of one scored year; provisional).
  • Modelling a price-following asset in the history did not improve the forecast at D8 or D14. The ceiling with the true price gained 0.6% at D8 (exp 191; 2 Primaries; provisional).
  • PV_Live lags at the two grid supply points gave no resolved gain (-0.03 points of capacity; exp 27; 2 GSPs; provisional). A PV_Live-based solar forecast gave -0.14 with an interval that included zero, and the true PV_Live value gave -0.50, almost all at leads of 7 to 15 days (exp 28; 2 GSPs; provisional).
  • Add a placebo twin to every price input, a copy with the right level and the wrong timing (exp 10, 15; Primaries; provisional).

Last checked against experiment 218.

docs.title: Metered generators and anonymisation
docs.text: NGED meters 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, and 3 other generator or storage series in the trial area, and the output of every one of them may leave the private data store only under an anonymous label. This page lists the series, the export-cap record for the one generator under active network management, and what a plot or pull request may show. Public data about generators is treated differently, and the last section says how.

docs.title: The series
docs.text:
• The 32 series that carry data include 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, and 3 other generators or storage units. The three are one battery energy storage system, one biofuel generator, and one series of type "Other (Generation)" (disk).
  • Of the 3 wind series, 1 is metered in MW and 2 in MVA (disk).
  • A type of "Other (Generation)" need not be solar. Do not assume a daylight profile (exp 182; one farm behind D8; provisional).
  • Read a farm's cleaned series from cleaned_solar_farms.parquet in data/ml-experiments/00179-*/ and keep rows with a null drop_reason. The file has no site column, so join studies.pv_dataset.pv_sites() on time_series_id for the label, the coordinates, and the capacity (exp 183; 6 farms; provisional).
  • Farms miss 7.6% to 27.6% of their half-hours. Check coverage before comparing farms (exp 179; 6 farms; provisional).
  • About 3.0% of the daylight half-hours of the six solar farms read exactly zero. Count a zero actual as inside a quantile forecast only by a rule stated in advance: the share at or below the 0.01 quantile (3.3% to 3.5% for research default 1) counts them, and the share strictly below it (1.2% to 1.4%) does not (exp 321; 6 farms; provisional).
  • A flat top in a farm's output is not proof of clipping. The cause is not settled (exp 179, 183, 218; 6 farms; provisional). See the metered solar farms theme.
  • A near-zero reading at a wind farm is not always low wind. Of the half-hours above 1.5 times cut-in wind speed, 1.6%, 13%, and 30% sit in the idle band at W1, W2, and W3, and ERA5 wind speed finds only part of them (exp 210; 3 wind farms; provisional).
  • UKV wind lowered the error of the three wind farms by about 0.2 points of capacity at 24 to 54 hours ahead, using a research archive and not the live feed, so the gain is an upper limit (exp 54; 3 wind farms; small gain; provisional). See the generator forecasting theme.

docs.title: Active network management and the curtailment feed
docs.text:
• One generator in the trial area is connected under active network management (ANM), and NGED has confirmed there are no others. A generator with no cap record therefore ran free (network page; docs).
  • Two records exist and they are different quantities. The setpoint history is one row per change of the export cap, in MW. The curtailment/ feed on NGED's S3 bucket is a derived volume of MW lost (data sources; docs).
  • The setpoint history is the one to use. The cap's sign, its start date, and the month the scheme goes live are on the network page (docs).
  • The export sits in data/studies/downloads/observations/NGED-ANM/, and studies.export_cap joins it onto an experiment's grid. It drops capped hours from training and keeps them at scoring (disk).
  • The clamp uses the cap in force, which a day-ahead forecast does not have, so it is an upper bound on what the cap could buy (code).
  • Curtailment at substations is scored by cost, not by this feed. The scoring code is a worked example on 2 bulk supply points and could not rank forecasts at the headline limit (exp 84; 2 BSPs, one scored year; provisional). See the curtailment cost theme.

docs.title: What may be published
docs.text:
• Never publish an NGED metered generator's time series with its name or identifier. The rule covers charts, tables, leaderboards, dashboards, reports, and issue and pull request bodies. The full rule is in CLAUDE.md (docs).
  • Use the labels from studies.anonymise: "A" to "F" for the solar farms and W1 to W3 for the wind farms. site_labels_for assigns them under a fixed seed, and it raises on a different count of generators (code).
  • Put no calendar dates on the axis of a generator's time series, and publish no output in MW. Normalise by the generator's own capacity. The dataviz skill's anonymisation section and the study skill's anonymisation section own the rest (docs).
  • Keep any plot of one farm's time series, and the cleaned series, under data/ml-experiments/. The private tables stay there (docs).
  • D1 to D22 label demand-side series, not generators in general. The glossary defines them, and substations may be named (docs).

docs.title: Public generator data
docs.text:
• Time series from public sources may be named. The settled output of Balancing Mechanism Units in Elexon's published data may be shown with names, in MW, on calendar dates. A study that mixes public and NGED generators anonymises the NGED ones (docs).
  • The public-data studies are the solar BMU census and the solar BMU disaggregation. (docs)

Last checked against experiment 218.

docs.title: NGED power telemetry
docs.text: The power readings are half-hourly telemetry from 32 time series in NGED's trial area, and several of their properties change how an experiment must read them. This page lists the properties that have cost experiments time. The processing steps themselves are on the data-processing page, and the context of the network is on the network page.

docs.title: The series
docs.text:
• There are 32 series that carry data. They are 16 Primary substations, 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, 2 grid supply points (GSPs), 2 bulk supply points (BSPs), and 3 other generators or storage units (home page) (disk).
  • The TimeSeriesMetadata table has 33 rows. One row has no data. Count 32 series, and do not change 32 to 33 (disk).
  • "32" also counts something else on the network page. The 41 connected hydro sites sit across "32 distinct primary substations" (network page). That is a count of Primaries across all four licence areas and has no link to the 32 trial series (docs).
  • The time_series_type column does not say what a generator is. A type of "Other (Generation)" need not be solar, so do not assume a daylight profile (exp 182; one farm behind D8; provisional).
  • Label the generators "Solar farm A" to "Solar farm F" and similar outside the private data store. studies.anonymise holds the labels. Substations may be named. The D codes (D1 to D22) that the write-ups use are anonymised labels of the demand-side series, defined in the glossary (code).

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
• A series is metered in MW (signed active power) or in MVA (apparent power, never negative). Read the unit from the units column. Eight of the 16 Primaries are metered only in MVA, so solar output behind one of them appears as demand in daylight (disk).
  • Use an MVA Primary for demand only on dark rows. The rule, its evidence, and the row counts are in the data-processing page (exp 103; 8 MVA Primaries; established).
  • A negative value at an MVA series is a fault between the meter and us, not an export (PowerTimeSeries field description) (code).
  • GSPs and BSPs are not clean demand. The GSPs are dominated by generation, and the BSPs sum the trial Primaries (data-processing page; exp 103; 2 GSPs, 2 BSPs; established).

docs.title: Raw and cleaned tables
docs.text:
• Two Delta tables hold the power: data/NGED/power_time_series.delta (raw) and data/NGED/cleaned_power_time_series.delta (cleaned). The cleaned table holds every raw row plus a nullable drop_reason column that names the cleaning rule that flagged the row (code).
  • Read power through studies.power.scan_power. scan_power keeps only the rows with a null drop_reason. A study must not name the raw table; a test enforces this (code).
  • Read the raw table only when the question is about availability. The raw table is what NGED delivered, and it holds the rows that cleaning flags (exp 182; series 32 and 33; provisional).
  • One cleaning rule exists today: substation_zero. It flags a reading of exactly 0 from a Primary, BSP, or GSP (nged_data.cleaning) (code).
  • substation_zero drops real zeros for a switched-out transformer. Switching experiments that need those rows must treat the flagged rows as kept (zero-reading entry; exp 132; switching log, few events; provisional).
  • For time_series_id 32 and 33, the cleaned and raw tables hold identical rows (exp 182, e00182_check.py; 2 series; provisional).

docs.title: Timestamps
docs.text:
• The time column marks the end of the half-hour that the reading covers. Do not shift it. Power timestamps show no 30-minute error on either side of NGED's fix of 2026-03-26 08:30 UTC (data-processing page; exp 103; 6 metered solar farms, with the Primaries only weakly tested; provisional).
  • Before that instant, the ingest moves NGED's stamp 30 minutes earlier (PowerTimeSeries.correct_late_timestamps). A study must not shift the stamp a second time (code).
  • Join hourly power to a weather product that stamps the end of its hour on (time - 1 µs).truncate("1h") + 1h. The evidence is on the data-processing page (exp 103; CAMS and 6 metered solar farms; provisional).
  • Assume a power reading reaches the forecast 3.5 hours after the half-hour it covers. No experiment has measured the delay on live telemetry (exp 87, 104, 106; assumption; provisional).

docs.title: Gaps, ramp-up, and regime changes
docs.text:
• Count a series' history from its first unflagged row. Only five Primaries hold long histories: D5, D10, and D11 from 2019-09, D14 from 2019-10, and D16 from 2020-12. The late starters begin between 2023 and 2025 (exp 103; 16 Primaries; established).
  • The start cuts and the fixed lockdown window are on the data-processing page. See trim the start of each series and fixed windows (exp 6, 102, 103, 173; established).
  • Some series changed regime. D8's weekday daytime demand fell from about 9 MW to about 3 MW between 2023-10 and 2025 (exp 103; D8; provisional).
  • A residual-only segmentation dates D8's break exactly but finds only about half of 10% steps. At a penalty low enough to date the 2023-08-15 break it also finds 2 to 3 false regime changes per Primary-year, and a penalty that keeps false changes under 1 labels 42% of 14 to 60 day load shifts as states (experiment 295; 14 Primaries, injected steps; provisional).
  • D8's multi-day drops coincide with a gas-engine detector's running states. The detector flags 27 of the 28 drops that began after the engine left D8's reading, against about 1 in 5 comparable stretches. The link between the drops and the engine is not proved, because the drops and the detector both read D8's residual (experiment 291; D8; provisional).
